title: CLI: edit rejects unknown options instead of writing an unchanged copy (#133)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #133.

## Cause

`edit`'s argument loop matched the options it knew and had `_ => {}` for everything else, so a misspelled option such as `--rotat 1:90` was silently skipped. With no edits collected, the command opened the file, saved it and exited 0 — a byte-identical copy of the input presented as a successful edit. The loop also advanced one argument at a time, so an option's *value* was itself re-examined as an argument on the next pass.

## Fix

`apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/main.rs`: every argument is parsed before the file is opened, and nothing is written for a command line that is rejected.

- An unknown `--option` fails with `edit: unknown option "--rotat" (expected one of: --out, --password, --full, --rotate, --delete, --move, --insert-blank, --title, --author)`.
- An option without its value (`--rotate` as the last argument) fails with `edit: --rotate needs a value` instead of reading an empty string.
- A second positional argument is reported (`one input file, then options`).
- `--out`, `--password`, `--full` and the edit options behave as before; `--full` is read from the parsed flag rather than re-scanning `args`.

`apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/edit.rs` (new): a misspelled option fails and leaves no output file; an option without its value fails; a second input file fails; the documented options still edit and save (rotation checked on the written file).

## Tested

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cli` — the misspelled-option test fails on `upstream/main` (exit 0, output written) and passes here
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo check -p pdfcraft-cli --no-default-features`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- Rebased on current `main` (827c61b)

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Split: keep only the resources each part draws (#204)
author: itsmunzir
body:
Closes #204

In a book whose pages share one `/Resources` dictionary, every split part carried every XObject the source listed — so a part saved out at the source's size although its pages drew a fraction of the images.

- `extract_pages` (the path behind Split and Extract Pages) now walks each part's content streams, records every XObject name drawn with `Do` — descending into form XObjects — and removes the `/XObject` entries no page of that part names. Pages that share a dictionary keep the union of what they draw.
- The garbage-collecting rewrite on save then drops the now-unreachable objects, so the part shrinks.
- `organize` gains the downward dependency on `pdfcraft-content` for the operator parser.

## Tests

- A one-page part must lose the other page's image and save smaller than the whole document.
- A part holding both pages must keep the union.

title: XFA: run the forms' JavaScript: calculations, validation, rows, visibility (#60)
author: ysrdevs
body:
Towards #60, after #121. Laid-out XFA forms had their fields but none of their behaviour: totals didn't compute, "Add row" buttons did nothing, subforms a check box should reveal stayed hidden, and validation messages never showed. Now their JavaScript runs.

## What changed

**`pdfcraft-js`: the XFA scripting object model** (`js/src/xfa.rs`), native boa objects over a snapshot of the form tree. Nodes are Proxies (scripts address children by name): `xfa.form` navigation, SOM resolution (absolute, relative with the containing-subform search, `..` descendants, indexes and `[*]`), `rawValue`/`presence`/`access`, instance managers (`_name`, `addInstance`, `removeInstance`, `setInstances`, `count`), `xfa.host` (messageBox, resetData, print, setFocus, gotoURL), `xfa.layout` page numbers, `xfa.event`, `app`, `console`, `util`, and unqualified sibling names as XFA resolves them. `this` is the node; the completion value is returned (a calculate script's result). Everything a script changes or asks for comes back as effects.

**`pdfcraft-xfa`: the live form** (`script.rs`): the instance tree with values, presence and access, the event table from the template (click, change, exit, initialize, calculate, validate with its message), presence and access overrides kept on the AcroForm (`/PCXfaOverrides`, so undo, redo and reopening keep them), row instances added and removed in the datasets packet through the existing merge pipeline, and `rerender`. Only single-statement button idioms (reset, print, save as, launchURL) stay native PDF actions; anything else is a script.

title: CLI: text fails when the document cannot be opened (#132)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #132

**Root cause.** `PageRenderer::new` stores a failed open (missing or wrong password, unparseable file) as `None`, so `page_count()` returns 0. `text` without `--page` then iterates `0..0`, prints nothing and exits 0 — a protected PDF looked like an empty one. #131 only covered an explicitly selected page.

**Fix** (`apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/main.rs::text`). When the renderer has no pages, call `pdfcraft_render::inspect` with the same password and propagate its error (`text: the document is protected by a password` / `text: the password is incorrect` — the wording `info` already uses). If `inspect` reports pages but the renderer still has none, fail with `text: the document could not be parsed`. A genuinely 0-page document still succeeds.

**Tests** (`apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/text.rs`): a fixture is protected with `run --script` (`doc_protect` with `open_password`); `text protected.pdf` must exit non-zero, mention the password and print nothing; `--password openme` must still print every page. `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test -p pdfcraft-cli` are green.

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: switch87
body:
## Why

The desktop app never installs a logger, so `log::warn!` / `log::error!` records (recovery, rendering, i18n) are discarded, and the panic hook and start-up messages go to `eprintln!` only. A launch from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so an ordinary user has nothing to attach to an issue, and `RUST_LOG` can't help them.

We ran into this in the sister project PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#1143): a window that stayed empty on Linux took an hour of `WAYLAND_DEBUG` and `gdb` to understand, while the app had already logged the relevant decision to nowhere. A log file next to the settings would have shown it in the first minute.

## What

`apps/pdfcraft/src/logging.rs`, no new dependency (`log` was already a workspace dependency; the app crate now uses it directly):

- **Two sinks:** standard error and `logs/pdfcraft.log` in the app's settings directory, next to `app.ron` (`eframe::storage_dir("PdfCraft")`: Linux `~/.local/share/pdfcraft/logs/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/PdfCraft/logs/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\PdfCraft\data\logs\`). A small `settings_dir()` helper makes sure both use the same directory.
- **Rotation:** each launch moves the previous log to `pdfcraft.1.log` (and that one to `.2`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start.
- **Bounded:** the file stops at 16 MiB with one note; records logged before the file is attached are buffered (max 512, with a "N earlier lines dropped" note).
- **Levels:** `info` for `pdfcraft*` targets, `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` replaces this with env_logger-style directives; a trailing `*` matches a prefix.
- **Never crash:** no `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing; an unusable directory or a failed write keeps standard error only; lock poisoning is handled.

`main.rs`: the logger is installed first; the panic hook now reports through `log::error!` (falling back to standard error when errors are filtered out), so a panic lands in the file. The start-up `eprintln!`s (app icon, control …

title: Automation: doc_info reports annotation and link rects in displayed-page coordinates (#129)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #129

## Root cause

`info()` in `crates/automation/src/lib.rs` serialised `annotations[].rect` and `links[].rect` straight from `DocInfo` (the PDF `/Rect`, user space), while the module's convention — and `comment_list` / `link_list` for the same objects — report rectangles with the origin at the top-left of the displayed page. The MCP `info` resource dispatches through `doc_info`, so it returned the same values. Reusing a `doc_info` rect in `link_edit` moved the link; on rotated pages the mismatch was more than a y flip.

## Fix

Convert both through the page's `user_to_view` (the `rect_to_view` helper `comment_list` already uses, now `pub(crate)`), looked up with `pages.get(page)` so an annotation that points at no page keeps its raw rect rather than panicking.

## Tests

`doc_info_rects_are_displayed_page_coordinates` in `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs` builds the issue's fixture (note + link on an unrotated page and on a 90°-rotated page), saves and reopens it, asserts `doc_info` agrees with `comment_list` / `link_list` on both pages (and with the input geometry), then feeds the `doc_info` rect of the rotated-page link back into `link_edit` and checks the link did not move. Fails before the fix with `[72, 672, 200, 692]` vs `[72, 100, 200, 120]`.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Automation: doc_protect restrictions need a permissions password — say so, and refuse them without one (#134)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #134

## Root cause

`doc_protect`'s schema described `printing` / `changes` / `copy` / `accessibility` and their defaults unconditionally. The engine, like Acrobat, only enforces `/P` behind an owner password (`Protection::permission_bits` returns `-1` without one), so `open_password` alone encrypts the document and leaves every operation allowed — and an explicit `copy: false` / `changes: "none"` in that call was silently ignored while the tool reported success.

## Fix

- `crates/automation/src/tools.rs`: the tool description and the four permission properties now say the restrictions and their defaults apply only with `permissions_password`, and that `open_password` alone restricts nothing. `open_password` / `permissions_password` get descriptions too.
- `crates/automation/src/lib.rs`: passing any restriction argument without `permissions_password` is an `InvalidArgs` naming the argument and what is needed, rather than an unrestricted file (AGENTS.md §3: errors an agent can act on). `open_password` on its own, and the existing engine behaviour, are unchanged.

## Tests

`protecting_with_an_open_password_alone_restricts_nothing` in `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs`: each of the four restriction arguments is refused without a permissions password and leaves the document untouched; `open_password` alone saves, reopens with the password and reports copy/modify/high-quality printing allowed (page deletion works); and the schema text for the tool and each permission property mentions `permissions_password`.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation` (65 + 4), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #253: `comment_add` anchors note and attachment icons at the displayed top-left on rotated pages
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #253

## Root cause

`comment_add` converted a note's or attachment's `at` — documented as the icon's top-left in displayed-page coordinates — as a single point through `PageInfo::view_to_user` and passed it to `Shape::Note { at }` / `Shape::Attachment { at }`. The engine's `rect_for` (`crates/annot/src/lib.rs`) builds the `/Rect` as `[at.x, at.y - NOTE_SIZE, at.x + NOTE_SIZE, at.y]`, so `at` is the **user-space** top-left of the square. On an unrotated page that is the same corner as the displayed top-left; under `/Rotate` it is a different corner, and the icon extended away from the requested point in the wrong direction — one icon width (20 pt) off in x at 90°, in both axes at 180°, in y at 270°.

## Fix

`icon_anchor` in `crates/automation/src/comments.rs` converts the whole displayed square `[x, y, x+20, y+20]` to user space and takes that rectangle's `[x0, y1]`, so the resulting `/Rect` covers the requested square whatever the rotation; both the `note` and the `attachment` branch use it. `PageInfo::view_rect_to_user` (render) is added as the normalized-rectangle counterpart of `view_rect_to_quad`, and `NOTE_SIZE` is re-exported from `pdfcraft-engine` so automation does not reach into the annot crate.

Unrotated pages produce byte-identical results. The desktop canvas converts a click the same way (`PageCx::to_user` → `Shape::Note`), but what a click on a rotated page should mean for the icon is a UI call I have not made here.

## Tests

Before the fix it fails on the 90° page (`[180, 300, 200, 320]` for the attachment, `[52, 72, 72, 92]` for the note).

title: Issue #248: `pdfcraft-cli render` writes the format its `--out` name says (.png, .jpg, .tif or .pam)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #248

## Root cause

`render` in `apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/main.rs` always wrote a netpbm PAM stream (`P7 … TUPLTYPE RGB_ALPHA`) to whatever path `--out` named — the comment said PAM kept the tool dependency-free, but the CLI already links `pdfcraft-engine`, whose `export` module encodes PNG, JPEG and TIFF (`png` 0.18, `image` 0.25). So `--out p1.png` produced a file no PNG reader could open, and the usage line still said `--out x.pam`.

## Fix

The output format follows the `--out` extension (case-insensitive): `.png` → PNG, `.jpg`/`.jpeg` → JPEG (quality 90), `.tif`/`.tiff` → TIFF, `.pam` → the raw RGB_ALPHA stream exactly as before. Any other name is refused before the page is rendered — `render: --out p1.bmp: use a .png, .jpg, .tif or .pam name` — rather than silently writing something the name does not describe. The module doc's usage line now reads `--out x.png (.png, .jpg, .tif or .pam)`.

`pdfcraft_engine::export::encode_image(width, height, premultiplied, ImageFormat)` wraps the three existing encoders so the CLI and `Exporter::image` share one match (both call sites were already `pub` functions; this only adds the dispatcher).

## Tests

New `apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/render.rs`, driving the built binary on a one-page Letter PDF at 36 dpi:

- `a_png_name_gets_a_png`: the file starts with the PNG signature and its IHDR says 306×396, matching the size the command reports. Fails on `main` with `not a PNG: [80, 55, 10, 87, …]` (`P7\nW…`).
- `jpeg_and_tiff_names_get_those_formats`: `.JPG` starts `FF D8`, `.tif` starts `II*\0`/`MM\0*`.
- `a_pam_name_still_gets_the_netpbm_stream`: the P7 header and `306×396×4` bytes after it.
- `an_unknown_extension_fails_and_writes_nothing`.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cli` (18 pass), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cli -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are green.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #249: `pdfcraft-cli split` creates `--out-dir` when it does not exist
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #249

## Root cause

`split` in `apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/main.rs` joined each part's name onto `--out-dir` and wrote it with `std::fs::write`, never creating the folder. A folder that did not exist yet therefore failed on the first part, with that part's path and the raw OS error (`…\101-linux-commands-light-p1-300.pdf: The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)`), which reads as the split itself failing.

## Fix

Once the parts have been computed, the folder is created with `create_dir_all` before any part is written. A folder that cannot be created (for example a file in the way, or no permission) is reported as `split: --out-dir <dir>: <error>` — the folder's problem, not the first part's. Existing folders behave exactly as before.

## Tests

New `apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/split.rs`, driving the built binary on a 3-page PDF:

- `a_missing_out_dir_is_created`: `--out-dir parts/nested` where neither level exists succeeds, every `report-pN.pdf` is on disk and listed on stdout. Fails on `main` with `No such file or directory (os error 2)` on `report-p1.pdf`.
- `an_out_dir_that_cannot_be_created_is_reported_as_such`: `--out-dir` pointing at an existing file fails, the message names `--out-dir` and the folder rather than `report-p1.pdf`, and the file is untouched.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cli`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` are green (one unrelated `tests/text.rs` case flaked once under a parallel build and passed on re-run).

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #189: each document tab keeps its own scroll position
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #189

## Root cause
The page view's `ScrollArea` in `canvas::document_area` had no id of its own, so egui derived it from the parent `Ui` — the same for every document. All tabs therefore shared **one** scroll offset in egui's memory: switching to another document showed it at wherever the previous one had been scrolled to (clamped to its length), and switching back showed the first document at the other one's offset — usually the top, which is the "resets to the beginning" in the report.

## Fix
Salt that `ScrollArea` with the document's `DocId` (`id_salt(("page-view", view.id))`), so egui keeps one offset per tab. Navigation (`goto`, zoom anchors, auto-scroll) is unchanged: it already went through the same scroll area builder.

## Tests
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs::each_document_keeps_its_own_scroll_position` — with a 5-page and a 2-page document open at Fit Width: scroll a.pdf to page 4, switch to b.pdf (must be at its own top) and scroll it to page 2, then switch back and forth (a.pdf still on page 4, b.pdf still on page 2). Before the fix it failed at the first switch: b.pdf opened on page 2, inherited from a.pdf's offset.
- Cited as evidence on the `view.document-tabs` parity entry; `cargo xtask parity` passes.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` all green; `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. Run on a Linux (WSL) build host without a GPU adapter, so GPU-only tests skip.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #185: arrow keys and Page Down / Up move through a scrolling document
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #185

Also covers item 1 of #224 (Page Down / Page Up move by the content on screen rather than a whole page).

## Root cause
`canvas::shortcuts` only handled → / ← and Page Down / Page Up in single-page view, or with ⌘ held; ↓ / ↑ were not handled at all. In the continuous (default) and two-page views the page view relies on egui's `ScrollArea`, which has **no keyboard scrolling of its own** — so without a modifier the keyboard could not move through the document at all (reproduced headlessly: every one of the six keys left the view on page 1).

## Fix
As in Acrobat ("Previous/Next page: Left/Right Arrow", "Scroll up/down: Up/Down Arrow", "Previous/Next screen: Page Up/Page Down"):
- → / ← go to the next / previous page in **every** layout (a whole spread in two-page view, through the existing `step_page`).
- ↓ / ↑ scroll a line (40 pt, a desktop mouse-wheel line); Page Down / Page Up scroll a screen less one line where the pages scroll.
- ⌘ + those keys, and plain Page Down / Page Up in single-page view, keep their page steps (unchanged).

The scroll is queued on the `DocView` (`key_scroll`) and applied by the page view's `ScrollArea` in the same frame, beside the middle-button auto-scroll; `document_area` takes it at the top, so it never lingers into a later frame (organize grid, empty document). The shortcuts list shows `← / →` beside `⌘← / ⌘→` (no new translatable string), and the `view.page-navigation` parity entry cites the new test (`cargo xtask parity` passes).

## Tests
`crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs::arrow_and_page_keys_move_through_a_scrolling_document` — continuous view at Fit Width: → / ← turn pages; ↓ and Page Down each take several presses to reach page 2 (↓ more than Page Down, since a fit-width page is taller than a screen), and ↑ / Page Up come back to page 1; → moves a spread in two-page view; Page Down still turns the page in single-page view. It failed at the first → before the fix (page 1 instead of 3).

title: macOS: every file picker is non-blocking (Save As, exports, folders, Browse…)
author: AutoHenry
body:
Follow-up to #145. That PR moved File ▸ Open, Combine, Insert, Replace and OCR ▸ multiple files to non-blocking pickers. This one does the same for **every other native file picker**: Save / Save As, save-on-close, exports, folder pickers, attachments, stamps, images, signing, print to PDF, and the Browse… buttons. These still ran the blocking `rfd::FileDialog`. On macOS that's the same `-[NSSavePanel runModal]` nested run loop inside winit's event handler, and it aborts the app (`panic_cannot_unwind`) when you click in the window while the panel is open. Save As on a new document was the most likely way to hit it, and it takes every open tab's unsaved work down with it.

After this PR, `rg 'rfd::FileDialog' crates apps` finds only a doc comment.

## Mechanism

`pickers.rs` is generalised from "pick → `PickFor`" to "ask → closure":

- `Ask::{File, Files, Folder, Save}(rfd::AsyncFileDialog)`.
- `PdfCraftApp::ask(ask, target, then) -> bool` creates the rfd future on the main thread. A worker waits on it with `pollster`, queues the result and requests a repaint. `then(&mut app, paths)` runs in `process_picked` on a later frame. `ask_one` is the single-path version.
- **One picker at a time.** The claim is held from `ask` until the pick's closure *starts*, not just until the panel closes. A closure that asks again (Merge data files → save the CSV; Run action → results folder) therefore always gets its picker. A request that is refused because another picker is open tells the user, and `ask` returns `false`.
- **Each closure runs inside `pdfcraft_engine::guard`**, as commands do (AGENTS.md §4). This work used to run inside the guarded command; a panic in it is now reported and the app keeps running.
- A cancelled pick runs nothing.
- **`target: Some(doc)`** drops the pick with a notice if that document is no longer active, or has been edited since the picker opened. Page and object positions captured at ask time are only valid while the document is unchanged. Used by: ad…

title: Issue #188: page steps in two-page view take every spread when several fit on screen
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #188

## Root cause
In the scrolling views the current page is the page with the largest visible height (`document_area`), and next/previous page (`step_page`) start from it. When more than one row of pages is **wholly** on screen — a book with a portrait cover and landscape two-page spreads, at Fit Width or Fit Page — those heights are equal except for sub-point rounding after the scroll offset is applied, so "current" became whichever wholly visible page rounding happened to favour. Instrumented: after ⌘Page Down to page 4, rows 4–5 and 6–7 both showed 347 pt, and page 6 won. The next step then started from the wrong spread: from the cover ⌘Page Down went 2–3 → 6–7 → 10–11, skipping spreads; with the rounding the other way it stays put after the cover, which is what the report describes. Uniform portrait documents never have two wholly visible rows at those fits, which is why the existing spread test passed.

## Fix
- Visible heights within half a point count as equal, and the topmost page wins.
- The page navigated to stays current while no page shows more of itself, so the next step starts from it.

Scrolling by wheel or keys is unaffected: the current page still changes as soon as another page shows more of itself.

## Tests
`crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs::page_down_steps_every_spread_when_several_fit_on_screen` — a 12-page book (portrait cover and back, landscape spreads) in two-page view with a cover page, at Fit Width, Fit Page and Fit Height: ⌘Page Down visits pages 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and ⌘Page Up 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1. Before the fix, Fit Width gave 2, 6, 8, 12, 12, 12. Cited on the `view.cover-page` parity entry (`cargo xtask parity` passes).

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` all green (328 passed); `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. Run on a Linux (WSL) build host without a GPU adapter, so GPU-only tests skip.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

author: AutoHenry

title: render: guard degenerate annotation appearance transforms
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

ISO 32000-2 §12.5.5 maps an annotation appearance onto the annotation in three steps: transform the form's `/BBox` with its `/Matrix`, take the upright box around the result, then scale and translate that box onto `/Rect`. The vendored hayro-interpret computes the scale as `/Rect` width ÷ transformed-box width (and the same for height) with no check.

When `/BBox` has zero width or height, or `/Matrix` has a zero row or column, the transformed box is a line or a point and that division is by zero. The resulting infinite or NaN matrix is pushed onto the graphics state, and every path, clip and glyph the appearance draws reaches the device with non-finite coordinates.

On current `main` the hayro rasteriser happens to discard that geometry, so the page *looks* right, but nothing guarantees it: any device (the raster device, `TextDevice`, or the planned DisplayList device) receives NaN/∞ from untrusted input. AGENTS.md §4 asks for division by zero and NaN/∞ to be guarded where they arise.

## Fix

After computing the mapping, skip the appearance unless the transformed box is finite with positive width and height and the mapping matrix is finite (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/mod.rs`, marked `PdfCraft patch:`, +13 lines). No fallback geometry is invented:

- Clipped to a collapsed `/BBox`, the appearance shows nothing anyway, so skipping it doesn't change what's drawn.
- MuPDF (`mutool draw`) and Poppler (`pdftoppm`), run as external black-box oracles on the same fixtures, draw nothing either.

Valid appearances take exactly the same path as before.

## Fixture and regression test

`raster::tests::degenerate_annotation_appearances_are_skipped` builds the PDFs in code: a `/Square` annotation with `/Rect [10 10 60 40]` whose `/AP /N` form fills `0 0 20 20` and shows text (`/F1` Helvetica). The cases are:

| Case | Form dictionary |
|---|---|
| zero-width `/BBox` | `/BBox [0 0 0 20]` |
| zero-height `/BBox` | `/BBox [0 0 20 0]` |
| point `/BBox` | `/BBo…

title: render: synthesize missing Highlight appearances
author: cyfung1031
body:
This changes only the rendering fallback for imported Highlight annotations that lack a usable normal appearance stream. Existing `/AP` appearances remain authoritative, and the PDF is not modified: nothing is written back to the document.

## Problem

A Highlight annotation (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.10) carries everything needed to draw it: `/QuadPoints`, `/C` and optionally `/CA`. Many older or generated PDFs omit the `/AP` appearance stream. The vendored hayro-interpret only draws annotations through `/AP /N`, so PdfCraft showed these highlights as nothing at all. MuPDF, Poppler and PDFium (black-box oracles) all draw them.

## Architecture check

- **Reusing `pdfcraft-annot`'s builder from the renderer** would need a `render → annot` edge. Both crates are L3, and that sideways edge isn't on the allow-list in `xtask/src/layers.rs`.
- **The builder works on `pdfcraft_cos::Dict`**, while hayro walks `hayro_syntax::Dict`.
- **Fix location:** a small read-only fallback in the vendored interpreter's annotation loop, next to where `/AP /N` is drawn. It follows the builder's semantics, so imported and PdfCraft-made highlights look alike.

## Fix

`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/mod.rs`, marked `PdfCraft patch:`:

```
if a usable /AP /N form exists  → draw it (unchanged)
else if /Subtype is /Highlight  → draw_highlight_without_appearance
else                            → nothing (unchanged)
```

`draw_highlight_without_appearance` does three things:

- **Geometry:** it builds one path from the `/QuadPoints` quads. Corners go in the Z order Acrobat writes and `pdfcraft-annot` reads (UL, UR, LR, LL).
- **Paint:** it sets the fill colour space and colour from `/C` (gray, RGB or CMYK), the fill alpha from `/CA` (clamped to 0–1, default 1), and the Multiply blend mode.
- **Drawing:** it calls the interpreter's own `fill_path`, so the device sees an ordinary fill in page space, with the same paint, layer and soft-mask handling as content-stream fills.

title: fonts: keep later widths and the embedded font when /Widths or /FirstChar is malformed
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Every simple font (TrueType, Type 1, Type 3, standard 14) gets its widths from `read_widths` in the vendored hayro-interpret (`font/true_type.rs`). Three defects there, each checked on synthetic files against MuPDF (`mutool`), Poppler (`pdftoppm`), PDFium (`pypdfium2`) and pdf.js (`pdfjs-dist` 4.10), run as external black-box oracles:

| Input | Before (main) | MuPDF / Poppler / PDFium / pdf.js |
|---|---|---|
| `/FirstChar 4294967295 /LastChar 4294967295` | one `Width::Missing` pushed per code below `/FirstChar`: 50,000,000 already took 276 MB RSS (`pdfcraft-cli render`); `4294967295` asks for 34 GB, and a larger value aborts on allocation | render normally |
| `/Widths [null 600]` or `[/W 600]` (`/FirstChar 65`) | the array ends at the bad entry, so code 66 loses its width and `BBBA` piles onto one spot | skip that entry; the B glyphs advance 600 |
| `/LastChar` below `/FirstChar`, or `/FirstChar` so large the count overflows | `read_widths` returns `None`, the font fails to load, and a **standard font stands in** for the embedded program (TrueType) or Type 3 procedures | keep the embedded font, with no widths from the array |

The first row is a never-crash issue (AGENTS.md §4: cap allocations sized by the file). It is the simple-font counterpart of the `MAX_CID` patch (7). The other two rows are compatibility issues: malformed metadata makes PdfCraft lay out or draw text differently from every renderer I tried.

## Fix

`read_widths` now builds a 256-entry table (simple-font codes are single bytes). It fills it from `/Widths` for codes `/FirstChar ..= min(/LastChar, 255)`. An entry that isn't a number leaves its code `Missing`, which falls back to `/MissingWidth` as before. A reversed or overflowing range yields no widths instead of failing the font. About +10/−13 lines, marked `PdfCraft patch:`.

Valid `/Widths` arrays produce the same lookups as before; every consumer indexes the table with a `u8` code. **Explicit zero widths stay zero.** I checked…

title: render: map annotation appearance boxes onto /Rect corner to corner
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

ISO 32000-2 §12.5.5, step 2: a matrix **A** "scales and translates the transformed appearance box to align with the edges of the annotation's rectangle", mapping its lower-left and upper-right corners to those of `/Rect`. So A(x) = sx · (x − box.x0) + Rect.x0, and the translation term is **Rect.x0 − sx · box.x0**.

The vendored hayro-interpret uses **Rect.x0 − box.x0**. That is only right when the box starts at the origin or the scale is 1. Any other appearance is shifted by (sx − 1) · box.x0, likewise in y, and drawn partly outside its `/Rect`.

The test fixtures, with `/Rect [10 10 60 40]` (device x 10..59, y 60..89 at 72 dpi):

| Appearance | PdfCraft `main` | MuPDF / Poppler / PDFium / pdf.js |
|---|---|---|
| `/BBox [10 10 30 30]` | x 25..74, y 55..84 | x 10..59, y 60..89 |
| `/BBox [0 0 20 20] /Matrix [1 0 0 1 10 10]` | x 25..74, y 55..84 | x 10..59, y 60..89 |
| `/BBox [0 0 20 20]` (control) | x 10..59, y 60..89 | same |
| `/BBox [100 100 150 130]` (as large as `/Rect`; control) | x 10..59, y 60..89 | same |

The oracles were run locally as external black-box processes: `mutool draw`, `pdftoppm`, `pypdfium2` and `pdfjs-dist` 4.10. Real files hit this whenever an appearance's `/BBox` is offset and its size differs from `/Rect`, for example a stamp or form XObject reused at another size, or a `/Rect` resized without regenerating `/AP`.

I found this while preparing #271, and kept it out of that PR so #271 stayed a pure robustness change.

## Fix

`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/mod.rs`, marked `PdfCraft patch:`: the scales are computed once, and the translation becomes `Rect.x0 − sx · box.x0` and `Rect.y0 − sy · box.y0`.

- **Unchanged:** appearances whose box starts at the origin, or whose box is as large as `/Rect`. That includes everything `pdfcraft-annot` and `pdfcraft-forms` generate, since they use `/BBox = /Rect`, origin boxes or note-icon boxes.
- **Degenerate boxes from #271:** a box that collapses to a line still yields a non-finite …

title: Issue #166: Save, Print and Export include the text still being typed in a form field
author: AutoHenry
body:
Fixes #166: Save omitted the text still being typed in a form field. Desktop had the same bug; this fixes both.

## Cause

A text field's editor keeps what you type in a draft (`view.forms.focus.text`). It becomes a `SetFieldValue` edit only on Enter, Tab or losing focus. That edit is queued on the tab and applied on the next frame, and only for the active tab. Shortcuts that work while typing (⌘S, ⌘P, ⌘W…) ran first, so Save wrote the document without the text, and the field still showed it.

Typing also didn't count as an unsaved change. Closing the tab or quitting while typing didn't ask, and a draft left in a tab you'd switched away from was dropped by Close All.

## Fix

- **`commit_form_typing() -> bool`** acts on the active tab only. It applies an edit still queued on the tab, then commits the open field's draft, closing the editor as clicking away would.
  - If the field rejects the value (a validation script or format), it keeps the editor open with the text and returns `false`.
  - The caller then stops: nothing is saved, printed, exported or signed without the value, and the field's own message explains why.
- **It runs where the document is actually read, not on every command.** That covers:
  - Save, Save As (including its later callback) and save-on-close;
  - Print;
  - Export (pages, Office, form data);
  - Reduce file size and Optimize;
  - Sign;
  - Extract, Split and Copy pages;
  - button scripts, which read the fields.

  Changing the theme, zooming and other unrelated commands leave the field alone.
- **Shortcuts pressed while a form field's editor is open now run one frame later.** The field takes that frame's typing and Escape first. So "type x, ⌘S" in one frame saves the "x", and "Escape, ⌘S" still discards the draft.
  - A delayed shortcut runs only in the document it was pressed in.
  - It is dropped if a save prompt opened, or a field refused its value, in the meantime.
  - The delay depends on the field's editor being open, not on egui's…

title: V, H and Space pick the Select and Hand tools
author: wstock
body:
Reported in https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/261#issuecomment-6061599357 (and on #273): "The Select (V) and Hand (H) toolbar commands are not working".

## Root cause
The quick toolbar's tooltips promise `Select (V)` and `Hand (H)` (`canvas.rs`), but no handler listened for either key. The only way to change tool was to click. Not platform-specific.

## Fix
As in Acrobat:
- **V** selects the Select tool, **H** the Hand (from any tool, like clicking the toolbar button).
- **Space held** pans with the Hand and goes back to the previous tool on release.

They're plain letters, so `PdfCraftApp::tool_keys` skips them while a text field (find bar, comment editor…), a form field, a dialog or the palette has the keyboard, and when a modifier is held (so ⌃⌘H, Read mode, is untouched). It runs beside the existing ⌘A handling, before `canvas::shortcuts`. A Space released while typing still gives the tool back.

The shortcuts dialog lists `V` and `H / Space (hold)`, reusing the already-translated tooltip strings (no new catalog entries), and the `view.hand-tool` parity entry cites the new test.

## Tests
`crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs::v_h_and_space_pick_the_quick_tools`: H → Hand, V → Select (also from Crop); Space held → Hand, released → back to Crop; Shift+H does nothing; H and Space typed in the find bar keep the tool. It failed at the first H before the fix (`Select` instead of `Hand`).

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui` all green (361 passed); `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask parity` clean. Run on a Linux (WSL) build host; the reporter's platform (Windows 11) wasn't available, but nothing here is platform-specific.

title: M14: Arabic and Hebrew file names render in the tab strip, recent files and Properties
author: samehelhawary
body:
## Problem

A document with an Arabic file name (for example `واحد اثنين.pdf`) showed replacement boxes in the tab strip, while the OS-drawn window title was fine.

Two causes:

1. **No glyphs.** The interface font stack (Inter, JetBrains Mono, egui's defaults, the craft-fonts `Jpan`/`Hans` faces) has no Arabic face.
2. **No right-to-left ordering.** egui 0.36 shapes each font-face run, so the letters of an Arabic word join, but it places the runs in logical order. With glyphs alone the two words would appear swapped.

## Change

- **Fonts**
  - The interface takes `Arab` faces from the craft-fonts build input (`pdfcraft_fonts::ui_arabic_fonts`), also on wasm.
  - On desktop, one font already installed on the machine is added as the last fallback of every family (`crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs`). It only draws characters no embedded face has. It is read at runtime and never embedded; `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` turns it off, and `cargo xtask screenshots` sets that.
  - `theme::font_definitions_for` stays embedded-only, so the existing font tests are unchanged.
- **Order**
  - `bidi::visual` puts single-line text in display order with a left-to-right base (the extension stays at the end, as in the window title). It uses `unicode-bidi`, which was already in `Cargo.lock`.
  - It is applied to the painted tab label and hover text, the Home recent-files name and path, and the Properties File and Location rows. Accessibility names keep the logical text.

## For maintainers to decide

- **`AGENTS.md` §1.4 gains a rule.** It allows reading an installed font at runtime as a last interface fallback, never embedded, shipped or shown in published screenshots. §1.2 lists system fonts as forbidden assets and did not mention runtime use, so this needs a maintainer's agreement. If you would rather not have it, the system-font part can be dropped and the craft-fonts part still stands.
- **The release pin is not moved.** craft-fonts already has Noto Sans Arabic at its current head…

title: M3: find text in mixed horizontal and vertical PDFs
author: midasdf
body:
Fixes #126.

The extractor currently treats an upright Type0 vertical font's x axis as its reading direction. Japanese vertical columns consequently get grouped across columns as horizontal lines, so matching text is missed when a horizontal heading is present.

Expose the CMap writing mode through the vendored OutlineGlyph and use negative glyph-space y for WMode 1. Group each of the four writing directions independently, retaining the existing upright-frame layout and mapping highlight boxes back to page coordinates. Document the small vendored API patch and update the existing Find parity evidence.

The synthetic mixed horizontal/vertical PDF regression fails on unchanged main ("日本語\n文日\n章本\n語"), then passes with the fix. It checks two occurrences, right-to-left columns and vertical highlight geometry; no font or PDF binary fixtures are added. Both Identity-V and the issue's UniJIS-UCS2-V encoding are exercised.

This remains geometric text extraction: arbitrary interleaving of separate horizontal/vertical blocks is not a complete logical reading-order implementation. It adds no text-creation controls or vertical PDF editing feature.

Validation: render package tests 43 passed; strict package Clippy, layers/assets/parity and the full 29-crate wasm gate passed. Stock `cargo xtask ci` stops at an existing `clippy::collapsible_match` in unchanged `crates/optimize/src/images.rs:57`. The full workspace CI is not claimed green.

End-to-end: `pdfcraft-cli run --script ... --root ...` opened a locally generated mixed-writing PDF with embedded OFL BIZ UDMincho. `text_find` returned `count: 2` and separate horizontal/vertical rectangles; `page_render` output was inspected. The local PDF/image are not included in the patch.

title: Issue #159: open .p12 files with trailing whitespace, PEM armour or base64
author: Mawfyy
body:
Fixes #159

## Problem

`pkcs12::open` demanded clean DER at the first byte, so a `.p12` with one extra newline, PEM armour or a bare base64 body — the shapes OpenSSL wraps, editors append and government portals emit — was refused **before any crypto ran**, with `malformed data: PKCS #12: not a PKCS #12 file` and no reason (the exact parse failure was swallowed at the `map_err`).

## Change

- `normalize()` before the strict parse: trim ASCII whitespace → `-----BEGIN` takes the base64 body between the armour markers (byte offsets, so a marker glued to the body line works too) → a bare base64 body is decoded. A real DER PFX always contains bytes outside the base64 alphabet, so the DER fast path can't swallow a valid file; `der.rs` stays strict, all leniency is at the `open()` boundary.
- The error keeps the familiar `not a PKCS #12 file` wording and now carries the exact reason (`… not a PKCS #12 file: trailing bytes after DER element`).
- Truncated and empty files still fail, now saying why.

## Test

`crypto.rs::opens_wrapped_pkcs12_files_and_still_rejects_broken_ones` — a wrapped copy of `rsa-aes.p12` yields the **same certificate** through trailing whitespace, PEM armour and bare base64; truncated and empty inputs error with the reason in the message. All three wrapped forms failed before the fix.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign` — green (all suites)
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- End-to-end: `pdfcraft-cli run --script` → `sign_document` with a newline-appended `.p12` produces a signed PDF

## Notes

- BER indefinite-length files (`30 80`) are still rejected with a clear reason; if the reporter's file turns out to be BER that's a follow-up.
- Full `cargo xtask ci` runs in CI (local machine couldn't take the load).
- @baobabprince / @rodrivva: if your original FNMT file still fails after this, please attach `xxd certificado.p12 | head -3` on #159 — it tells us which encoding the file actual…

title: XFA: run FormCalc scripts
author: ysrdevs
body:
## XFA: run FormCalc scripts

FormCalc is the default scripting language of XFA forms made with older versions of Designer (a script element without a `contentType` is FormCalc). Until now those scripts were detected and reported ("FormCalc scripts don't run yet"), so forms written in it never calculated, validated or reacted to buttons.

This adds a FormCalc interpreter in the `js` crate (`crates/js/src/formcalc.rs`), written in Rust against the XFA 3.3 FormCalc specification (part 8), and runs it from the engine next to the JavaScript path.

### How it fits

* **One object model, one set of effects, one set of budgets.** The JavaScript model's form table (`XHost`/`HNode`), SOM resolution, instance manager operations and effect recording are now shared (`pub(crate)`), with Context-free `add_instance`/`remove_instance` that the boa wrappers call. FormCalc records the same `XfaEffect`s, so the engine applies them with the same rules: merged and capped effects, message boxes and console lines; print/save/links/focus from clicks only; one datasets rewrite per event; the same loop/recursion limits and per-activity time budget; a runaway script abandoned and the form's scripts turned off.
* **Engine**: `Runner::run` picks `run_formcalc_within` or `run_xfa_within` by the event's language; everything after that (results of calculate/validate, effects, re-layout, undo, datasets) is unchanged.

### Language covered

* Expressions with FormCalc's operators (`+ - * /`, `== <> < <= > >=` and `eq ne lt le gt ge`, `& | and or not`, unary `- + !`), coercions (strings as numbers where numeric, null as 0 in arithmetic and null in comparisons), `;` and `//` comments, `""` escapes, newline-separated statements, case-insensitive keywords.
* `var`, assignment to fields and to `presence`/`access`/instance counts, `if/elseif/else/endif`, `while/do/endwhile`, `for … upto/downto … step … do … endfor`, `foreach … in (…)`, `func … endfunc` (with recursion), `break`, `continue`, `return`, `exi…

title: Issue #173: a failed ?file= startup fetch is reported in the app
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #173.

## Problem
When the browser app's `?file=` URL couldn't be fetched (an HTTP 404, a network or CORS failure), `apps/pdfcraft-web/src/main.rs` logged the error with `console::error_1` and did nothing else. The user saw the ordinary welcome screen, with no sign that the requested PDF had been tried.

## Fix
- `PdfCraftApp` gets a `failed_inbox: FailedInbox` (`Arc<Mutex<Vec<(name, error)>>>`) next to the existing `inbox`.
- The startup fetch queues `(name, error)` there when it fails, and requests a repaint in both cases. The console line stays for developers.
- On the next frame, the app reports each failure once with the notice it already uses when a delivered file won't open, e.g. "Couldn't open missing.pdf: HTTP 404". The message is translated through the existing catalog entry.

## Tests
- New `pickers::a_failed_startup_url_is_reported_in_the_app` covers it. It checks that the notice names the file and the error, that no document opens, and that each failure is reported once.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo check -p pdfcraft-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` builds.

title: Security: create save staging files with create_new (follow-up to #164)
author: jcl-bit
body:
Follow-up to #164, as suggested there: create the staging file with `create_new(true)`, so a file or link planted at the staging path can't redirect the write. No issue was filed.

**Automation and CLI (`write_atomic`)**

Every save staged at the fixed name `.<name>.pdfcraft-tmp` and wrote it with `fs::write`. That follows a symbolic link and writes through a hard link. So in a folder someone else can write to, a link planted at that name sent the bytes into whatever file it pointed at, and the rename then moved the link into place.

Now:
- **A random name.** The staging file gets a random 64-bit suffix from std's `RandomState`, which is keyed from the operating system's random source. No dependency is added, and the name can't be planted in advance.
- **`create_new`.** The file is opened with `OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true)`. That fails if anything already has the name: a file, a hard link, or a symbolic link, even a dangling one. title: Issue #157: the Windows portable zip keeps settings, logs and recovery beside pdfcraft.exe
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #157.

The Windows portable zip had no `portable.txt`, and the app had no portable mode. It always created `%APPDATA%\PdfCraft` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PdfCraft\Recovery`, even when the user added `portable.txt` by hand.

Now `portable.txt` (or `PdfCraft.portable`) next to `pdfcraft.exe` turns on portable mode, as PhotoCraft already does. The settings, log files, crash-recovery autosaves and new digital IDs then go in a `PdfCraftData` folder beside the executable, and the old PrintCraft folders are not migrated. The portable zip now includes `portable.txt`. If `PdfCraftData` can't be written, for example on a read-only drive, the app uses the per-user folders and shows a message saying why. Tested by unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/portable.rs`. They cover: no marker, each marker name, reusing an existing data folder, a folder named like a marker (not treated as a marker), an unwritable data folder (falls back and gives the reason), and no executable folder.

title: D5: READMEs for cos and engine
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

Thirteen crates have no README, although `CLAUDE.md` step 2 tells every session to read the README of the crate it is touching. These are the two that matter most: `cos` is where every hostile file lands first, and `engine` is the whole API surface a frontend gets.

title: Issue #263: combine, extract and split keep the PDF/X output intent and identification
author: Fazmin
body:
Fixes #263.

## Problem
Combine, extract and split build a new document from copies of the pages. They also carry over bookmarks, form fields, layers, attachments and four Info keys. Nothing copied:
- the catalog's `/OutputIntents`;
- the `GTS_PDFXVersion`, `GTS_PDFXConformance` or `Trapped` Info entries;
- the XMP `pdfxid` identification.

So a PDF/X file stopped being one, and a RIP or preflight lost the intended output condition.

## Fix
A new `organize::pdfx` module reads what a document declares about its print standard and writes it into the new document.

**Extract and split** (one source) carry:
- `/OutputIntents`, with their ICC profiles. They copy through the same object map as the pages, so a profile the pages already use isn't stored twice.
- `GTS_PDFXVersion`, `GTS_PDFXConformance` and `Trapped` in Info. The version comes from Info, or from the XMP when only the XMP has it.
- A new XMP packet with `pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion` (and conformance), `pdf:Trapped` and `dc:title`. It's written only when the source had XMP, so a PDF/X-1a:2001 file (PDF 1.3) doesn't gain one.

**Combine** carries the same, taken from the first source, only when every source declares the same version, trapping and output intents (`/S`, `OutputConditionIdentifier` and the decoded profile bytes). Otherwise the result claims nothing, as before.

The new document gets a fresh XMP packet instead of the source's because the source packet can claim standards the new file no longer meets. Extract doesn't copy the structure tree, so carrying `pdfuaid` (or a PDF/A level-a claim) over would be false. A test checks this.

## Not in this PR
- **A warning when combine's sources disagree**, as the issue suggests. That needs a new return value through `Session::combine` / `combine_ranges` to the CLI, the `doc_combine` tool and the Combine UI, and #321 is reworking that UI. The parity note records the gap. For the same reason I didn't take the issue's other suggestion of keeping the first source's ou…

title: Security: refuse mailto attachments, show link hosts in punycode (follow-up to #104)
author: jcl-bit
body:
Follow-up to #104, as suggested there: refuse `mailto:` addresses that ask the email app for a local file, and show international hosts in punycode in the link prompt. A third commit closes a gap in #104 itself that turned up while reviewing this: an address the URL parser rejects was opened as a local file. No issues were filed.

**Refuse email links that attach or insert a local file**

A document's `mailto:` link could ask the email app to attach a file from the user's computer, so one click on "Open email app" drafts a message carrying, say, an SSH key. The parameter names below come from the clients' own source:

- Evolution (`e-msg-composer.c`, `handle_mailto`): `attach` and `attachment`, compared without case.
- KMail (`commandlineinfo.cpp`, messagelib `parseMailtoUrl`): `attach` and `attachment`.
  - Names are percent-decoded and lowercased.
  - The query starts at the first `?`, even after a `#`.
  - `&` is read as `&`.
  - RFC 2047 encoded words are decoded across the whole address before it is read.
- Claws Mail (`scan_mailto_url`): `attach`, plus `insert`, which reads a local file into the message body.
- xdg-email isn't on PdfCraft's path (links go to `xdg-open`/`gio` through the `webbrowser` crate), but other Linux tools use it. It hands `attach` to Thunderbird (Mozilla bug 1613425). It reads `mailto:a@example.org&attach=…` with no `?`, and copies the subject into Thunderbird's comma-separated `-compose` argument.

These parsers disagree with each other, so `document_url` doesn't imitate any one of them. It refuses a `mailto:` address (new `BlockedLink::MailFile`) when any word that starts with `attach` or `insert`, in any case, is followed by `=`, wherever that word appears. The check repeats after each layer of percent-decoding, which covers `%61ttach` and `%2561ttach`. It also refuses (new `BlockedLink::MailEncodedWord`) any `=?…?=`, because KMail's lenient RFC 2047 decoder could turn one into `attach`, and a backslash before a digit or `x`, bec…

title: Security: print jobs, new digital IDs and the --control file no longer write through planted links
author: jcl-bit
body:
Three more writes of the same kind as #319, which listed them under "Not in this PR". You didn't ask for these, so here is the risk for each, plainly. Every one needs **another local user account on the same machine** (a shared workstation, a lab or terminal server, a multi-user Linux box), or a folder that someone else can write to. None of them can be reached from a PDF or over the network. One commit per fix, so any of them can be dropped.

**1. Printing on macOS, Linux and FreeBSD (`print::spool::submit`)**

Risk: another user on the machine could read every document you print, or swap in their own file so a different document is printed.

How: each job was written to `<temp>/pdfcraft-print-<pid>/job-<time>.pdf` and passed to `lp` by name. In a shared `/tmp`, that folder name can be guessed from the process id. It was made with `create_dir_all`, which accepts a folder someone else created first and follows a symlink planted at that name. The job was then written with `fs::write`. The folder was also never removed.

Fix: the job is piped to `lp` on stdin, so nothing is written to disk. `lp` prints stdin when given no file; the job options are the same as before.
- `lp_args` no longer takes a file argument.
- The job is fed on its own thread while `lp`'s output is collected, so neither side can block on a full pipe. If the thread can't be started, `lp` is stopped and an error is returned rather than a panic.
- When `lp` refuses a job before reading it (an unknown printer), the user sees `lp`'s message, not a broken pipe.
- CUPS ends its reply for a stdin job with "(0 file(s))", which would read in the "Sent to …" notice as if nothing was sent. That suffix is dropped.

**2. Configure New Digital ID ▸ Create (`sign_ui`)**

Risk: the new ID's private key could be written to a place another user chose, or be readable by them.

How: the code found a free name with `!p.exists()` and then wrote the `.p12` with `fs::write`. That is check-then-write: a file or link planted…

title: D1: pin and verify the pdf.js corpus
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

`xtask corpus` cloned `mozilla/pdf.js` at **HEAD**, with no commit pin and no content check, and the corpus tests `return`ed early when the directory was missing. Three consequences:

- the corpus sweep measured a **moving target** — a file changed upstream silently shifts our numbers;
- `xtask/baselines/pdfjs.json` was compared against whatever upstream happened to be that day;
- a damaged, partial or tampered checkout produced **green** results.

AGENTS.md §2 asks for shared fixtures "fetched pinned by commit and sha256-verified". This does that.

## How it verifies

Two layers. The **commit** fixes which tree we ask for. The **manifest digest** fixes what actually landed on disk: one `<sha256>  <path>` line per file, sorted by path, then one sha256 over that text. Git's own object ids are SHA-1, so the manifest is what makes this a sha256 check rather than a SHA-1 one.

Pinned at `5d923c9`, **1455 files** — which independently matches what the GitHub tree API reports for `test/pdfs` (124,609,164 bytes).

### The platform trap

The checkout sets `core.autocrlf=false` and `core.eol=lf`. This repository has `autocrlf=true` **globally**, so without that git would rewrite line endings on checkout and the same commit would hash differently on Windows than on Linux — a pin that means different things on different machines is not a pin. Confirmed `autocrlf=true` on this machine before adding it.

### No more silent skips

A successful verification writes `corpus/pdfjs/.pdfcraft-corpus.json`. The corpus tests now skip **only** when nothing is fetched, and fail loudly when a checkout exists without that stamp. `xtask check` verifies before sweeping, so the baseline is never compared against an unknown tree.

The corpus itself stays git-ignored and is never committed; only the pin is.

## How it was verified

End to end on a real fetch, not reasoned about:

- [x] The unrecorded-pin guard refuses to fetch and says what to run
- [x] `--update-pin` fetches and…

title: D2, D3: fuzz every tool's arguments, and prove root confinement
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

AGENTS.md §3 and §4 treat tool arguments as untrusted — they are the MCP attack surface, and an agent can send any JSON at all. But nothing fed hostile arguments to the tool table: `xtask fuzz` mutates **PDFs** only.

And `tools::check_args` validates **shape alone** — that the arguments are an object, have no unknown keys, and that required keys are present and non-null. **Types and ranges are not checked there.** So a string where an integer belongs, `i64::MIN` where a page number belongs, or a 100,000-character path all reach the handler, and each handler had to cope on its own with nothing verifying that they all did.

## Two tests

**`no_tool_panics_on_hostile_arguments`** — every tool, called with a zoo of wrong types, numeric extremes (`i64::MIN`/`MAX`, `u64::MAX`, `1e308`, `-0.0`), empty and 100,000-character strings, NUL bytes, a right-to-left-override filename, format specifiers, emoji, and mistyped or 64-deep nested containers. **19,299 calls over 132 tools.** Each must return `Ok` or a readable `ToolError` — a panic is a crashed MCP server or CLI.

**`no_tool_escapes_the_root`** — the D3 audit, mechanized. Every path argument (`path`, `paths`, `folder`, `out_dir`, `file`) is tried with `..` traversal, absolute POSIX paths, Windows drive and UNC paths, and a **planted symbolic link** pointing out of the root. **451 attempts, all refused**, plus a filesystem diff as a second net.

Reading the code says every handler resolves its own paths and that no tool dispatches another internally — so the hole PhotoCraft found (an allowed command internally running another and skipping the check) **does not exist here**. A test keeps that true as tools are added; a written finding would not.

## Both were proved to fail before passing

Per `execution-plan.md` §1.3, by actually injecting defects rather than reasoning:

- An out-of-bounds index in `page_rotate` is caught and reported as `page_rotate panicked on {"degrees":-1,"doc":1}: index out of bound…

title: Update image signatures live during resize and movement
author: remesis
body:
Resizing or moving an imported image signature currently updates the selection frame while the image stays at its old geometry until release. Update the embedded image on every pointer frame. During movement, hide the frame and resize handles, then restore them immediately on release.

Prepare a read-only background of the page without the selected signature and cache it alongside the embedded image texture. Pointer frames transform the image without changing the PDF. The final preview stays visible until the committed page raster arrives. This preserves page content beneath the old image, image alpha and annotation opacity, including zoom, document/view rotation and reopened PDFs. Each completed gesture still uses the existing move/resize edit and creates one undo step. Escape cancels the gesture before egui's synthetic drag release can commit it.

Corner resize handles preserve the embedded image's original aspect ratio and keep the opposite corner anchored. Edge midpoint handles stretch width or height independently. The live preview and committed rectangle use the same constraint, including rotated pages and reopened signatures that were previously stretched by an edge handle.

Add the corresponding engine preview API and read-only `comment_image_preview` tool. The tool selects `background` or `image` and returns one PNG per call, so CLI clients can save both layers separately. Image decoding and the UI background raster are bounded; encrypted previews retain the render configuration. Update crate documentation, signature parity evidence and the roadmap.

title: F1 + F2: exact standard-14 metrics, and code-to-Unicode completeness
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

`pdfcraft_fonts::helvetica_width` was a fifteen-line guess by character class, and **seven crates generate appearance streams through it** — `annot`, `edit`, `forms`, `ocr`, `redact`, `sign`, `xfa`. Times was Helvetica × 0.9, bold × 1.05, Courier a flat 0.6.

Against the published metrics, a Times capital `A` is **722**. The estimate said **600** — a 17% error on a single letter, compounding across every line of generated text.

`Std14` now carries the real advance widths for all fourteen faces, indexed by character code: WinAnsiEncoding for the twelve text fonts (what we actually write into appearance streams) and their own built-in encodings for Symbol and ZapfDingbats.

## What moved over

- `helvetica_width` delegates to the table, so **every call site gained exact Helvetica with no change**.
- The three places that faked another face by scaling Helvetica now select the right face: `Family` in `edit::added`, the paragraph measure in `edit::text`, and the redaction overlay fonts.
- `Metrics::width` in `fonts::pdf`, which measures *existing* document text when a font carries no `/Widths`. That path feeds redaction's glyph removal, where a wrong width means **cutting the wrong glyphs** — the most consequential of the four.

The local four-way `Std14` enum in `pdf.rs` collapsed bold and italic together; the real one does not, so `Times-Bold` is no longer measured as `Times-Roman`.

## Verification

Tests **spot-check the table against values typed in from the specification by hand**, so it is verified against the spec rather than against whatever generated it. Helvetica `A`=667 `W`=944 `space`=278 `@`=1015; Times `A`=722 `space`=250; Times-Italic `A`=611; Courier 600 throughout. Plus: Courier is fixed pitch at every defined code, every text font covers printable ASCII and Latin-1, Symbol and ZapfDingbats are not WinAnsi, `/BaseFont` aliases and subset prefixes resolve (`ABCDEF+Helvetica-Bold`, `Arial,BoldItalic`, `TimesNewRoman,Bold`), and hostile t…

title: Create PDF from scanner (#312)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #312

Adds File ▸ Create ▸ PDF from Scanner: select a scanner, colour preset, flatbed or feeder (including duplex), resolution and paper size, then open the scanned pages as a new unsaved PDF. Flatbeds can collect more pages; optional OCR makes the PDF searchable.

title: render: apply W/W* clipping after every path-painting operator
author: cyfung1031
body:
Part of #260 (pages 3, 5 and 9: "pdfcraft needs to support clipping").

## Problem

ISO 32000-2 §8.5.4: `W` / `W*` mark the current path to become the new clipping path *after* the path-painting operator that ends it has painted it, under the old clip. `n` is only one such operator. Any of `S s f F f* B B* b b*` may end a clipping path.

The vendored hayro-interpret committed a pending clip only in `EndPath` (`n`). With any other operator:

1. **The clip was never applied.** Everything painted afterwards ignored it.
2. **The clip stayed pending.** The next unrelated `n`, even after `Q`, used it to clip with a different path, so visible content disappeared.

#260's test file ends its clips with `W* S`:

- **page 3:** `… circle … W* S /Sh0 sh`. The axial shading meant for the circle floods the whole page and hides everything drawn before it.
- **page 5:** `… rounded rectangle … h W* S`. The image meant for the rounded rectangle is drawn unclipped, over its border.
- **page 9:** two `W* S`. The nested circle ∩ rectangle clip spills its gradient bands across the page.

Page 4 uses `W n` and was already fine. Upstream `LaurenzV/hayro` `main` has the same `EndPath`-only code. PDF-XView needed the same fix: it delays the clip until after whichever operator follows.

## Fix

`apply_pending_clip` takes the pending rule and, if the path isn't empty, pushes the clip. `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/path.rs`, marked `PdfCraft patch:`.

- **Where it runs:** after painting, before the path is cleared, in `fill_path`, `stroke_path` and `fill_stroke_path`. These cover every painting operator, including the closing variants. `EndPath` uses the same helper.
- **Leftovers:** the pending rule is cleared every time, so it can't leak. The now unused `Context::clip` getter is removed.

## Test

`raster::tests::clipping_path_applies_after_any_painting_operator`. On a 100×100 page, `q 0 0 1 RG 4 w 0.8 g 20 20 40 40 re {W|W*} {op} 1 0 0 rg 0 0 100 100 re f Q` runs for each of `n S s f …

title: View: page rasters map texel for texel onto the screen (sharp text at any zoom)
author: cyfung1031
body:
Part of #260 (page 9: "pdfcraft needs to render better text anti-aliasing with zooming").

## Problem

The rasters themselves are fine: `pdfcraft-cli render` output matches MuPDF, PDFium and Poppler. The softness comes from how the desktop view puts the raster on screen, through two mismatches:

1. **Render scale.** `DocView::render_scale` rounded the device scale to 1/64, to spare re-renders on tiny fit-width changes. At 87 % on a 2× display the exact scale is 2.32000, but the page was rendered at 2.31250, 0.32 % too small for its rectangle.
2. **Placement.** The texture was stretched onto the page's layout rectangle, whose corner usually doesn't fall on a whole physical pixel (scroll offset, centring).

Either mismatch makes the GPU resample every texel linearly, which softens lines and glyphs.

Measured with the headless `shot` example: #260's `pdf_engine_test.pdf`, page 9, compared at 2 px per point against a direct render at the exact scale.

| Zoom | Before: mean diff / max | Before: sharpness | After: mean diff / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| 87 % | 6.30/255 / 123 | −7.9 % | **0.00 / 1** |
| 137 % | 2.66/255 / 88 | −1.7 % | **0.00 / 0** |
| 150 % (quantizes exactly) | ≈ 0 | 0 % | ≈ 0 |

## Fix

All in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:

- `render_scale` is the exact device scale.
- Tags resolve 1/65536 of a scale step (`scale_tag`) instead of 1/1000, so a raster at a different scale is recognised as stale.
- Each page rectangle starts on a whole physical pixel (`snap_to_pixels`). Overlays move by at most half a pixel along with it.
- A raster at the current scale, whole page or tile, is drawn at its own pixel size from that corner (`PageXform::texel_aligned`). Each texel covers exactly one screen pixel, in every view rotation.

Unchanged: a raster from an older scale (mid-zoom, before the new one arrives) and the low-resolution backdrop under tiles still stretch to the page, as before.

Trade-off: a fit-width zoom that changes by a fraction of a percent (window resi…

title: render: draw non-embedded Japanese CID fonts with a craft-fonts face
author: cyfung1031
body:
Part of #260 (page 2: "pdfcraft needs CJK font support").

## Problem

#260's test file shows Japanese text in a CID font the PDF does not embed:

- `/Type0 /BaseFont /HeiseiMin-W3 /Encoding /UniJIS-UCS2-H`
- descendant `CIDFontType0` with `/CIDSystemInfo << /Registry (Adobe) /Ordering (Japan1) >>`

PdfCraft drew nothing for it, both in PrintCraft 0.2.1 and on current `main`. MuPDF, Poppler, PDFium and Acrobat draw it in a Mincho face.

Most of the machinery is already there:

- When a CID font isn't embedded, hayro builds a `FallbackFontQuery` that carries the `character_collection`.
- Given a substitute font, hayro maps CIDs through the Adobe-Japan1-UCS2 CMap to Unicode and then to the face's cmap (`font/cid.rs`, `map_via_unicode`).
- Release builds have embedded craft-fonts' Japanese faces all along.

But `pdfcraft-render` never installed a font resolver. hayro's default resolver answers every fallback query with a Latin standard-14 font, which has no Japanese glyphs, so the run was blank.

## Fix

`RenderConfig::settings` installs a resolver. For a fallback query whose collection is **Adobe-Japan1** it returns a craft-fonts face:

| Font name | Face |
|---|---|
| Mincho names (`HeiseiMin`, `KozMin`, `Ryumin`, `MS-Mincho`, `HiraMin`) | Shippori Mincho, via `document_japanese_font` |
| Gothic names (`…Gothic…`, `HeiseiKakuGo`, `KozGo`, `…Maru…`) | BIZ UDPGothic, Regular or Bold |
| anything else | by the descriptor's serif flag |

Every other query keeps hayro's default. There is a single construction site, so the page view, printing, export, the CLI and text extraction all get it.

**Without craft-fonts nothing changes**, as CLAUDE.md requires: there is no face to return. Building with craft-fonts is what release workflows and the Linux CI job already do.

**Japanese only, on purpose:**

- The craft-fonts commit PdfCraft pins (`abb83316`) has only Japanese faces.
- craft-fonts' later Simplified Chinese face is Noto Sans CJK SC. AGENTS.md §1.1 forbids it ("do not …

title: M11: Optimize PDF and Reduce File Size run in the background with a progress bar
author: mlkonrad
body:
## Why

Advanced optimization and Reduce File Size did all their work on the UI thread. On a large file the window stopped repainting until they were done, so it looked as if the app had crashed (on GNOME the "not responding" dialog appeared). On a 60-page, 328 MB file of 600 ppi images the run takes about 27 s.

## What

Both commands now run in the background, following the pattern OCR and Export already use: a worker thread, shared progress state, polling each frame, and `run_inline` for tests and the web.

- **`pdfcraft-optimize`:** `optimize_with_progress` reports each image and the clean-up. Returning `false` stops with `OptimizeError::Cancelled`. `optimize` is unchanged for existing callers.
- **engine:** new `optimizer` module.
  - `Session::optimize_job` captures a copy of the document and the choices.
  - `OptimizeJob::run` reports each `OptimizeStage` (removing user data, images, cleaning up, merging, writing) with a `fraction()`. It stops on request with the new `EditError::Cancelled`.
  - A panic is turned into an error (`guard`), so the worker always reports back.
  - `optimized_bytes` is now the job run in place.
- **ui:** both commands call one `start_optimize`.
  - A card at the bottom centre shows the stage ("Optimizing… image 14 of 40"), a bar that eases towards the fraction with a soft light sweeping across it, the percentage, and **Cancel**.
  - The card uses the same inverted style as the toast, in light and dark. Toasts stack above it, using its measured height.

- The headless `doc_optimize` and `doc_reduce` tools stay synchronous.

title: Comments without an appearance stream are drawn (display only, never saved)
author: cyfung1031
body:
Part of #260 (page 7: "pdfcraft needs to render the same styling for solid background overlay annotation block"; also the Ink path, which #260 calls the "curve annotation lnk path").

## Problem

#260's page 7 has these annotations, none with an `/AP` appearance stream:

- a FreeText (`/DA (/Helv 10 Tf 0 0 1 rg) /C [.85 .47 .02] /Border [0 0 1]`)
- a Text note
- a Highlight
- an Ink stroke

Acrobat, MuPDF, PDFium and Poppler draw them from their dictionaries. PdfCraft drew only the Highlight, via #274's renderer fallback.

`pdfcraft-annot::appearance::build` already draws every one of these types: it's what PdfCraft uses for its own comments. The renderer can't call it, though. `render` and `annot` are both L3, and the builder works on `pdfcraft-cos` objects while hayro reads `hayro-syntax`. Re-implementing FreeText (fonts, wrapping, `/Q`, callouts) inside the vendored interpreter would duplicate it.

## Fix

**`pdfcraft_annot::with_missing_appearances(&Document) -> Option<Document>`** returns a copy of the document in which each annotation without `/AP /N` gets the appearance `build` draws from its dictionary. That covers every type `build` handles, including FreeText, Ink, Text, FileAttachment, standard stamps, shapes, lines and markup.

- Links, form fields and pop-ups are left alone, as is anything `build` declines (it returns `None` rather than draw something worse).
- An existing `/AP` is never replaced.
- It returns `None` when nothing is missing, so there's no copy.

**`pdfcraft-engine`** gets a new `Document::display: Arc<Vec<u8>>`:

- **What it holds:** the working bytes plus, in memory only, an incremental update with those appearances. When nothing is missing, or the document can't be edited, it is `bytes` itself (same `Arc`).
- **Who reads it:** the page view's render pool (pages, thumbnails, find), the `page_render` automation tool, and page images via `export_source`.
- **When it's rebuilt:** wherever the renderer is rebuilt: open, `refresh`, `refresh…

title: Ink strokes are drawn as smooth curves through their points
author: cyfung1031
body:
Part of #260 (page 7: "pdfcraft needs to render the curve annotation lnk [ink] path").

## Problem

#260's screenshot of page 7 shows Acrobat drawing the Ink annotation's `/InkList` (five points) as a **smooth curve through the points**. It crosses the page's own straight zig-zag drawn at the same points.

`pdfcraft-annot`'s appearance builder draws ink as straight segments between the points. MuPDF, Poppler and PDFium do the same, but PdfCraft targets Acrobat. The builder draws:

- every ink comment PdfCraft creates (Comment ▸ Pencil);
- signatures drawn with Fill & Sign;
- with #371, the display-only appearance for ink that has no `/AP`.

## Fix

`crates/annot/src/appearance.rs`: a stroke of **three or more points** is drawn as a Catmull-Rom spline through every point, written as cubic Béziers (`smooth_segments`). The curve leaves each point parallel to the chord between its neighbours, and an end uses itself as the missing neighbour. This is a standard construction, not taken from any other implementation. Two points stay a line, and one point stays a dot.

A curve can swing a little beyond its points: on a sharp turn, by up to about a sixth of a neighbouring chord. A Bézier stays within its control points, so `rect_for` now grows a new ink annotation's `/Rect` over the control points as well as the points. Before, it used only the points plus the line-width margin, so a curve could have been clipped by `/BBox = /Rect`.

## Test

`annot` `tests::ink_strokes_are_smooth_curves_through_their_points` checks:

- **Three points** (0,0) (10,10) (20,0) give exactly `0 0 m  1.667 1.667 6.667 10 10 10 c  13.333 10 18.333 1.667 20 0 c S`. **Before:** `10 10 l 20 0 l`.
- **Two points** give `l`, and **one point** gives the existing dot.
- A stroke rising to (20,20) and dropping to (21,0) gets a `/Rect` that holds its curve. Its control point is at y 21.667, so the top must be ≥ 23.667. **Before:** 22.

title: Linux: accept file:// URI args so desktop launchers recognise pdfcraft as PDF default
author: bunakalya
body:
## Summary
- GNOME Files (and other freedesktop-spec launchers) only register an app as the default handler for a mimetype if its `.desktop` `Exec` accepts URIs (`%u`/`%U`), not just paths (`%F`). pdfcraft's entry used `%F`, so even after `xdg-mime default ai.storyteller.pdfcraft.desktop application/pdf`, double-clicking a PDF in Files silently fell back to another installed viewer (confirmed via `Gio.AppInfo.get_default_for_type("application/pdf", must_support_uris=True)` returning the other viewer, `False` returning pdfcraft).

- `apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`: added `path_from_arg`, which decodes a `file://` URI argument back into a plain path before it reaches the rest of the app (which only ever opens paths). Other schemes (`https://`, `mailto:`…) and plain CLI paths pass through unchanged.

title: Home: pin folders and list their newest PDFs
author: amitabhthakur
body:
Home gets a **Folders** section. File ▸ Pin folder to Home… (or **Pin a folder…** on Home) pins up to 8 folders, and each lists its newest PDFs with how long ago and their size. One click opens a file (or focuses the tab already showing it), and **Unpin** removes the folder from Home without touching its files.

## Why

Scans and synced documents land in a folder: where a scanner saves, or a cloud drive's local sync folder (iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox). Today, reaching them means File ▸ Open and navigating there each time, and Recent only knows files that were already opened. Acrobat offers connected storage accounts on Home; the parity entry `misc.connected-storage` is `na` with "use OS file dialogs and synced folders". This is the local-first version: a pinned folder is read through the file system like any other path, never through a provider's API, and nothing leaves the machine.

## How

`crates/ui-egui/src/folders_ui.rs` (new) holds the pinned folders, the listing and the Home section.

- **Never blocks the frame.** Folders are listed on a worker thread (inline under `run_inline` in tests), at most every 5 s while Home shows, so new scans appear without reopening anything and a slow or offline synced folder can't stall the UI. If a worker ends without a result, `Arc::strong_count` detects it and the next listing retries.
- **What is listed.** Only PDFs directly in the folder (extension, case-insensitive); hidden files, subfolders and other files are skipped. At most 20,000 directory entries are read and 100 PDFs kept (newest first, files without a modified time last), 8 shown until **Show N more**.
- **Unavailable folders.** A folder that can't be read stays pinned and says so ("It may have moved, or its drive or cloud sync is offline"), then lists again once it's back.
- **Locations in words.** Each folder is described by where it is instead of its full path, so two folders called "Scans" can be told apart: "iCloud Drive", "OneDrive · Contoso", "SharePoin…
