title: Security: fix three audit findings in redaction and signature validation
author: JeremyYao
body:
## What this changes

Three security fixes found by an audit of `main`, one commit each. In all three the operation reported success while the saved file, or the verdict shown, was wrong.

**1. M8: redaction unlinks removed images and forms from inherited and shared resources**

Apply Redactions and Remove Hidden Information give a rewritten page its own pruned `/Resources`. The dictionary the page drew through before could still name the removed image or form, and a full-rewrite save keeps whatever is still referenced. The removed image samples and form text stayed in the saved file when:

- the page inherited `/Resources` from a `/Pages` node;
- several pages shared one resource dictionary object;
- a form without `/Resources` drew the image through the page's dictionary.

Pages with their own `/Resources` (the case #1099 fixed) were not affected.

The interpreter now records the original object behind every XObject it drops or replaces. After the page loop, each page-tree resource dictionary that still names one loses that entry, unless a page drawing through that dictionary still draws the name. A dictionary that loses an entry is replaced by a private copy on its node, so a dictionary object shared with other nodes is left alone for them. If a page's use of a name cannot be told, the operation fails closed.

**2. M9: a cross-reference entry the reader sets aside is never an unchanged signed object**

`pdfcraft-cos` judges post-signing changes; the renderer draws the page. They resolve some cross-reference entries differently. A revision appended after signing could redefine a page's content stream and give the object an entry the reader sets aside while the renderer follows it (an in-use entry at offset 0, or a second entry for the same object in one section). The classifier compared the signed object with itself and reported the signature Valid while the page showed the new content.

`pdfcraft-cos` now records the entries it does not take at face value (`Docum…

title: M1: Share PDF parsing and bound background document opening
author: LabDennis

## What this changes

Refs #307. Reuse the unmodified source parse during document inspection and bound background PDF preparation to the next result the UI can accept. Later paths stay unread while a prepared result, password prompt or other modal interaction waits. Up to 64 requests remain accepted.

The desktop enables background opening before startup files and session restoration. title: M4: copied pages keep the resources they list only up the page tree
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Part of #1628: this is a cause that produces exactly the reported symptom, but I could not confirm it is the reporter's without their file.

The Combine list's thumbnails are drawn from each source file, where hayro looks a resource name up the page's own `/Resources` and then up the page tree. Some files rely on that: the page lists its font, and the images or forms it draws are listed only on a `/Pages` node. When pages are copied, `import_pages_mapped` keeps the page's own `/Resources` whole and only falls back to the inherited one when the page has none, so the copy loses everything listed up the tree and draws an empty page. That is the "fine in the list, blank after combining, blank when exported" in the issue. Copied pages now get their own dictionary plus the names only their ancestors list (the page's entry wins, then the nearest ancestor). Pages with complete resources are copied as before. Strictly speaking a page's `/Resources` replaces the inherited one (ISO 32000-2 §7.7.3.4), but our own reader shows these files, so the copy should keep what the user saw. Happy to switch if you'd rather follow the spec here.

I couldn't get the reporter's file, so this is the cause I could rebuild from the description: a one-page file with the form on the `/Pages` node renders in the list and comes out blank from Combine on main. Combine, Insert from File, Extract and Split all go through this function, so all four are fixed.

Fixes #1640.

In a PDF, a CMYK JPEG's samples are ink amounts, inverted only when the image's `/Decode` says so; that's how the page renders it. The export decoded these JPEGs with the `image` crate, which follows the convention for standalone JPEG files instead (Adobe-style CMYK, stored inverted). It also ignored `/Decode` on JPEGs. So the CMYK/YCCK images in the attached file, which have a soft mask and go through the PNG path, all came out as negatives. Now CMYK JPEGs are decoded to their raw CMYK samples with `zune-jpeg` (already in the tree through `image`; YCCK gets converted to CMYK), and `/Decode` inversion applies to JPEGs like it does to every other image. A CMYK JPEG with no mask is still written as is when its `/Decode` inverts it, since an image viewer reads that file correctly. Without the inversion the viewer would show a negative, so it's written as a PNG. Happy to switch that last part if you'd rather keep every unmasked JPEG byte for byte.

Validation:
- `cmyk_and_ycck_jpegs_export_in_the_colours_the_page_shows` (synthetic 8×8 CMYK and YCCK JPEGs, with and without a mask and an inverting `/Decode`): fails on main (cyan ink exported as black, `CMYK: [0, 0, 0, 255]`), passes here
- the attached `example_pg59.pdf`: the red banner and the other CMYK images now export in their real colours
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create --lib -- jpeg image mask cmyk`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: XFA: decode BMP and TIFF pictures
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1644.

BMP and TIFF pictures in XFA templates and data were left out with "not a JPEG, PNG or GIF". They're now recognised by their bytes (the declared type is ignored, so `image/tif` and `image/x-ms-bmp` work too), sized from their headers, and decoded the same way as GIF. That means the same `Limits`, 8-bit samples plus a soft mask when there's alpha, and only the first page of a TIFF. A TIFF is turned and flipped as its Orientation tag says, in its layout size and in its pixels, so a picture tagged as shot sideways comes out the way viewers show it. `crates/xfa` turns on the `bmp` and `tiff` features of `image`. Both were already in the workspace, so `Cargo.lock` doesn't change.

The engine had an exhaustive match on `Kind` for image fields, so it needed two new arms. A BMP or TIFF picked for an XFA image field is now kept in the data as `image/bmp` / `image/tiff`. Before this it was refused, because the layout couldn't show it.

title: control: cap line length before auth
author: SteamSmith
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1259, as @echelon suggested there: before auth, `BufReader::lines()` has no limit on line length.

`serve` in `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` now reads lines with a bounded read (`take(max + 1).read_until(b'\n', …)`):

- **Before `auth` succeeds**, a line may be at most `MAX_AUTH_LINE` = 4 KiB. The auth request (`pdfcraft-cli` sends `{"token": …}` with a 32-hex token) is about 100 bytes. A longer line gets a `-32600` error and the connection is closed, after reading at most `MAX_AUTH_LINE + 1` bytes of it. No newline is needed for the limit to apply.
- **After `auth`**, lines are read whole, as before. Authenticated clients can still send large requests.
- End of stream, read errors and non-UTF-8 input end the connection exactly as they did with `BufRead::lines`; only an overlong line gets the error reply.

The reader returns `LineRead::{Line, End, TooLong}`, keeping "too long" distinct from I/O errors.

## Tests

New, in `control::transport_tests`:
- `lines_are_read_up_to_the_limit`: line at the limit accepted, CRLF stripped, final line without newline, end of stream, and an overlong line reported as `TooLong` with only limit+1 bytes consumed
- `an_overlong_line_before_auth_is_refused`: `MAX_AUTH_LINE + 1` bytes with no newline → `-32600`, then the connection closes
- `long_lines_after_auth_are_still_read`: after `auth`, a 16 KiB line is parsed (`-32700` for non-JSON) and the connection stays open

On Windows (rustc 1.99.0):
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --no-fail-fast`: all green, identical to `main` plus the 3 new tests (lib 344 vs 341).
- `tests/control.rs` passes in full (46 tests).
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo xtask wasm` (31 crates ok) are clean.

title: Render: a soft mask shrunk below its size is filtered, so thin strokes drawn through it survive
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1649.

The body text in that PDF isn't text: Word saved each line as a 2×2 black image whose `/SMask` is a 1-bit bitmap of the glyphs at about 600 dpi, so the mask alone carries the text. The mask has no `/Interpolate`, and since #624 a minified mask without it is nearest-sampled. At 100–200% that keeps one mask sample in three to six, so the thin CJK strokes fell between the samples and came out broken and aliased (the CLI render shows the same thing as the screenshot, so it's the renderer, not the UI). Now a soft mask of a different size than its image is filtered when it's shrunk, whatever its `/Interpolate`, which only asks for smoothing when the mask is enlarged. Images whose mask matches their size, and every #624 case, are unchanged.

## How you verified it

- `raster::tests::shrunk_soft_mask_larger_than_its_image_keeps_thin_strokes`: fails on main (the one-column stroke disappears, `[255, 255, 255, 255]`), passes here
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib minif` and `--lib image_resampling`: the #624 and resampling tests stay green
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -p hayro --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- rendered the issue's PDF with `pdfcraft-cli render` at 96 and 177 dpi: the text now looks like the other viewer's
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

The change only covers masks that differ in size from their image (the Word case). A mask-sized-like-its-image or a plain 1-bit scan of text minified without `/Interpolate` still takes the #624 nearest path; I left it alone because #624 asked for exactly that, but filtering any shrunk soft mask would be a one-line widening, happy to switch. The patch is recorded as (15) in both hayro rows of `vendor/README.md` (the table has the row twice on main).

title: Embed craft-fonts by default via .cargo/config.toml [env]
author: sblount2025-design
body:
A plain `cargo build --release` from a clean clone silently produces a CJK-blind binary. build.rs warns and carries on:

```
warning: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese text will render as empty
boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts next to this repo and
rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo exactly as the warning asks, the build *still* needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand on every invocation. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten, and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

**This is not a new convention — it mirrors `deckcraft/.cargo/config.toml`, which already ships this exact block.** The other craft apps that read `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` don't, which is the inconsistency this closes.

Properties:

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.
- No `force`, so a `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` already in the environment still wins for a one-off build against a different font set.
- If craft-fonts is **not** cloned beside the repo, behaviour is unchanged — build.rs warns exactly as it does today.
- The existing `[alias] xtask` entry is untouched.

## Verification

Built with the variable explicitly removed from the environment, so only the config could supply it:

```
env -u CRAFT_FONTS_DIR cargo build --release
```

The crate recompiled and the "no craft-fonts embedded" warning did not appear. Tested on macOS (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, against craft-fonts at its current main.

title: fix(organize): Document Properties also change the XMP title and author
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`doc_set_info` (Document Properties ▸ Description) changed `/Info` only. Files that also carry the values in their XMP packet (`/Root /Metadata`; LibreOffice exports, every PDF/A file) kept the old `dc:title` and `dc:creator`, so the file disagreed with itself after the edit:

- viewers that prefer XMP kept showing the old title (Firefox's built-in viewer does, in its tab title);
- `doc_info` reported the new `/Info` values, so an agent believed the change was done;
- on a PDF/A file, our own preflight then reports "The title in the metadata and the document information differ" (6.6.3).

The comment above `set_info` said XMP sync would come with the `model` crate. This does the small part now: when the catalog has an XMP packet, `set_info` changes the matching property as well, with the pairing PDF/A uses (ISO 19005-1 §6.7.3, the same one `pdfcraft-preflight` writes):

| Info key | XMP property |
|---|---|
| Title | `dc:title` (`rdf:Alt`, `x-default`) |
| Author | `dc:creator` (`rdf:Seq`) |
| Subject | `dc:description` (`rdf:Alt`, `x-default`) |
| Keywords | `pdf:Keywords` |
| Creator | `xmp:CreatorTool` |
| Producer | `pdf:Producer` |

The packet is edited as text (`crates/organize/src/xmp.rs`): an element is replaced where it stands (so it keeps its description's namespace declaration), a simple value written as an attribute is rewritten in place, a missing property gets an `rdf:Description` of its own (same `rdf:about`) before `</rdf:RDF>`, and an empty value removes the property, as it removes the `/Info` key. The rest of the packet (other schemas, unknown properties, padding) stays byte for byte. The stream is written unfiltered and keeps `/Type /Metadata /Subtype /XML`, so `/EncryptMetadata false` still applies to it.

Nothing changes for files without XMP (none is added), for other keys, or for packets this can't edit safely: not UTF-8, no `rdf:RDF`, or larger than 16 MiB decoded.

title: Open: opening an already-open document focuses its tab (#1620)
author: edurbs
body:
Fixes #1620.

Opening a document that is already open now focuses its tab instead of opening a duplicate — on every open path: File ▸ Open, drag-and-drop, double-click in the file manager (single-instance forward), the command line, Open Recent / Home, and the control channel's `ui open`.

**What changed**

- `open_path` checks `view_showing(path)` before reading the disk — paths compared after `std::path::absolute` normalization (the same semantics as session restore: no symlink resolution, no Windows `\\?\` prefix). - `open_recent` delegates to the same lookup, so every open path shares one dedup.
- Programmatic callers get an honest contract: `open_path` returns `Opened | Focused | Failed`. `ui open` replies Ok with `"focused": true` when the document was already open (Err only on real failures), and a document-needing tool picked from the palette with no active document still runs when the picked file was already open.

- Pathless documents (attachments, recovery snapshots, earlier revisions, converted images/text, the web build) still open multiple copies.

- No reload-if-changed-on-disk when focusing.

title: M1: edit finds the pages a damaged file's readers find
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1656.

The file in the issue has two problems. The reader handled both and `edit` handled neither. Its newest xref section's `/Prev` points into a zeroed region. The reader rebuilds from object headers when that happens, but cos kept the newest section and silently dropped everything only the older section located, including two of the three pages. And the catalog's `/Pages 172 0 R` points at one of the zeroed objects, so even with every object found there is no page tree to walk. The reader finds the pages by scanning, organize found none, and `--rotate 1:90` became "page 0 does not exist".

So now:
- cos treats an unreadable older section as damaged cross-reference data and rebuilds from object headers. That's the path it already takes when the newest section is unreadable. The "older cross-reference section ... is unreadable" line stays in the repair log.
- `pdfcraft_organize::recover_page_tree` gathers the `/Type /Page` objects into a new page tree, in file order. At open the engine writes that as one more revision and reopens it, the way the XFA layout is applied, so the document opens unmodified. It keeps the result only if the reader then shows the same pages as before: same count, sizes and rotation. The scanning reader takes any dictionary with `/Contents` as a page, so it can skip a blank page or show an annotation as a page. When the two disagree, nothing is rebuilt. Page edits then fail with "the document's page tree lists no pages: the file is damaged" instead of touching a page the user doesn't see.
- On a signed document the page tree is never rebuilt. Edits to a signed file that was rebuilt from object headers are refused with the existing `SignedRewrite` error, because saving such a file is always a full rewrite and would invalidate the signatures. Before this, that save fell back to a full rewrite without saying so.

## How you verified it

- `pdfcraft-cli` `tests/edit.rs`:
  - `a_document_whose_page_tree_is_missing_edi…

title: Keep the full final spread reachable with unequal page heights
author: FredApps
body:
When the last page is shorter than its partner in the final two-page spread, using only that last page's bottom underestimates the scrollable content height. The taller left page cannot be scrolled fully into view. A synthetic four-page document at 200% zoom left 372.67 screen points below the viewport at maximum scroll.

Use the greatest bottom among the laid-out page rectangles, plus the bottom margin. The one-line correction preserves zero content height for an empty document.

Five regressions drive synthetic wheel events through the viewer and check the final spread's bottom and margin:
- taller left page;
- taller right page;
- equal-height pages;
- an unpaired final page;
- a taller left page with cover mode enabled.

Related to #187, with partial scope only: this reproduces unreachable tall-left content, not the reporter's original flash of a page from 30 pages back. That report remains open.

Validation on the approved tree based on 0a098648:
- Full workspace: 2,866 passed, 0 failed, 13 ignored, with the CI-pinned craft-fonts input.

title: Text selection: dragging to the top or bottom edge of the view scrolls it
author: marcoarnulfo

Part of #1670.

A text-selection drag never scrolled the view by itself: egui's ScrollArea doesn't autoscroll a drag, so with the button held at the bottom of the window the selection stopped at whatever was on screen. title: Edit text & images: a dragged image's pixels follow its frame instead of waiting for the release
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1671. The handle half was already fixed on `main`, so this covers the preview.

The first half, where the corner handle misses even though the resize cursor is showing, is already fixed on `main` by #1116 (6d843a8e). In 0.6.0, a press between 2 and 8 px outside the corner showed the resize cursor, but the object marquee still took it and deselected the image. `image_owns_pointer` now keeps that press for the image. I checked this with a throwaway kittest that pressed and dragged from every offset within 8 px of the corner at 100%, 120% and 200% zoom. Current `main` misses none of them. What's left is the preview. While a corner (or the whole image) is dragged, only the blue frame moves, and the image pixels stay where they were until release. title: fix(sign): render Unicode characters in visible signatures using bundled Inter font
author: PINYOPATTANAWASANPORN
body:
## What this changes

Enables visible signature appearances in `pdfcraft_sign` to render Unicode characters (specifically Latin Extended-A / Central European characters such as `č`, `ć`, `ž`, `š`, `đ`) by embedding the bundled `Inter-Regular.ttf` font with `/Identity-H` encoding and a `/ToUnicode` CMap when the signer name, labels, reason, or location contain non-WinAnsi text.

When all text is within `WinAnsiEncoding`, the existing zero-byte overhead behavior (using standard `/Helv`) is preserved.

## Why

Visible digital signature appearances previously drew text exclusively using `/Helv` (standard-14 Helvetica Type 1 font with `WinAnsiEncoding`). Signer names containing valid European characters outside Windows-1252 (e.g. Slavic / Central European names like `Luka Petravić` containing `č` U+010D and `ć` U+0107) either failed during signature appearance generation with `SignError::Unsupported` or resulted in placeholder characters.

`pdfcraft_fonts` bundles `Inter-Regular.ttf`, which covers Latin Extended-A and provides full OpenType glyph mappings. By dynamically selecting between `/Helv` and embedded Inter:
1. Standard ASCII / WinAnsi signatures remain compact with zero embedded font overhead.
2. Signatures with Central European / Slavic names render accurately and cleanly.
3. Unsupported scripts (outside Inter's coverage) still return a clear `SignError::Unsupported`.

## Verification

- **Unit tests added:**
  - `pdfcraft_fonts::inter_width_measures_latin_extended_and_ascii`: verifies advance width measurement of Latin Extended characters against `skrifa`.
  - `visible_appearance_draws_central_european_characters_with_embedded_font`: signs a synthetic document with signer `"Luka Petravić"` and Slovenian metadata, validates zero `?` in appearance stream, confirms `/PCFull0` font dictionary is embedded, and validates cryptographic signature validity with `signatures(&doc, ...).status == Status::Valid`.

title: fix(ui): a tool chosen with no document runs once the picked file opens
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
## What this changes

Since #1493, a running app opens files on the background worker. `open_then_run` (a tool chosen with no document open, e.g. Export ▸ Text) still checked for the new tab right after `open_path`. By then the file hadn't opened yet, so it opened a frame or two later and the tool never ran. `a_tool_chosen_with_no_document_asks_for_one_and_runs_on_it` has been red on `main` since then.

The fix reuses `PendingOpen.then`, which already carried the command through the password prompt. `open_path` becomes `open_path_then(path, None)`, and `open_then_run` calls `open_path_then(path, Some(command))`:

I also checked the other `open_path` callers that look at `views.len()` straight afterwards. `control.rs` already handles a pending open. `reopen_last_files` runs before the first frame, so it is always inline. title: Text selection: a drag after a double- or triple-click extends by whole words or lines
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1685.

A double-click selects the word as an anchor/head run, but the drag that follows moved the head to the nearest glyph, so it extended letter by letter, and dragging left kept only the first glyph of the clicked word (the anchor). Now, while the drag belongs to a multi-click, the selection grows by the same unit the clicks chose: whole words after a double-click, whole lines after a triple-click. The clicked word or line always stays selected, and the anchor switches to its far end when the drag goes backwards, as in Acrobat and browsers. The word/line/page lookup the press and release paths already shared is now one small `click_unit` helper, reused by the drag.

Validation:
- `a_double_click_drag_extends_by_whole_words_both_ways` (tests/ui_group/text_select.rs): fails on main (`"quick bro"` dragging right, `"uick b"` dragging left), passes here

title: fix(render, ui): form-heavy documents draw and fill fast (spot-colour images, widget placement, Fields panel)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Fillable forms felt much slower than in Acrobat, both on opening and on every field filled. Profiling a real fillable character sheet (2 pages, 274 text fields, not committed) showed the fields cost almost nothing: the engine opens it in 0.04 s. The time goes into **drawing the page background**, plus two things that grow with the number of fields.

**1. Spot-colour images convert once per pixel value, not once per pixel** (vendored hayro-interpret patch 28, `f9a4b9f7`).
The sheet's background art is a 3304 × 4105 8-bit `/DeviceN [/Black] /DeviceCMYK` image whose tint transform is a PostScript calculator (Type 4) function. `decode_raster` ran that program once per pixel (13.5 million times a page) and collected four `f32`s a pixel on the way. Each page took 3.8 s and 430 MB to draw; Poppler takes 0.27 s. Because every field edit replaces the `RenderPool`, the same cost came back after each field was filled. Patching only the images' colour space to `/DeviceGray` (same fields) brought it to 0.12 s, which confirmed the cause.

An image whose pixels hold at most 16 bits of samples (8-bit Separation/DeviceN, 1/2/4-bit gray, indexed, 4-bit RGB…) now converts through a table of every possible pixel value (`rgb_via_lookup`). The table is used only when the image has more pixels than it has entries. Each sample is decoded by the same `decode_sample` the per-pixel path now shares. `fix_image_length`'s rules for short and overlong data are kept: pixels past the data are converted exactly as before.

**2. Widgets without `/P` are placed in one pass** (`f8916d37`).
`Inspector::find_widget_page` searched every page's `/Annots` for each such field (O(fields × annotations)), so a form of 8,000 such fields took 1.17 s to open instead of 0.27 s. The pages' `/Annots` are now read once, lazily, into an annotation → page map (the same pattern as `named`). A widget that two pages list is now placed on the first, as `pdfcraft-forms` places it; before, it went to whi…

title: Print: choose paper by PDF page size (#1103)
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Refs #1103 (the "Automatic (PDF page size)" option; #1212 covers the fixed default and this change is independent of it).

## What changes for users

Acrobat's **Choose paper source by PDF page size**, as a checkbox under Paper in the Print dialog, on by default and kept across restarts:

- With a **Size** layout (Fit, Actual size, Shrink, Custom), each page prints on the standard sheet it matches: A4 pages on A4, Letter on Letter, in either orientation (the same 0.5 pt match as *Match page at 100%*). Pages of a size no sheet matches print on the paper chosen in the dialog.

- **Match page at 100%** becomes a checkbox, on by default, so a page prints 1:1 on its own sheet rather than shrunk by Fit's 18 pt margin. With paper by page size it is always on offer and only sets the scale (Actual size, Auto orientation; off means Fit). Without it, it works as the button did: enabled when the viewed page matches a sheet, and it picks that sheet.
- Off: the old behaviour, except that the dialog now starts at Actual size instead of Fit.
- `doc_print` takes `paper: "auto"` for the same thing (documented in its schema; the error for an unknown paper lists it). Its default scale stays `fit`.

The print-ready PDF carries the sheet sizes; craft-print already spools it at the PDF's page sizes (CUPS with `fit-to-page=false`, Windows per page), so which tray a driver takes a sheet from stays the driver's decision.

title: Save to a mounted volume that cannot rename (#981)
author: muraa-p
body:
Fixes #981.

A Cryptomator FUSE mount, a network share or a container overlay can refuse a rename its own
filesystem could have done, answering `EXDEV` or "not supported". Every save then failed with an
error the user could only act on by saving somewhere else, and closing the app right afterwards
surfaced the same failure again.

Both the staging file and the target live in the same folder, so a rename normally succeeds and
stays atomic. Where it cannot, this copies the finished bytes across and drops the staging file:
the save lands on the volume, at the cost of the replacement no longer being atomic, which is the
most such a filesystem allows. Every other rename failure still reaches the user untouched.

The fallback is deliberately narrow — only `ErrorKind::CrossesDevices` and `ErrorKind::Unsupported`
are retried as a copy — so a genuine permission or read-only failure is not disguised as a save
that worked.

Tests cover both halves: the ordinary rename still moves the staging file rather than copying it,
and a failure the copy cannot stand in for is still reported.

title: Scroll with the wheel while selecting, and at the viewport edge (#721)
author: muraa-p
body:
Fixes #721.

## Why the wheel stopped working while selecting

`egui::ScrollArea` only reads the wheel when no widget owns a drag — its `is_hovering_outer_rect`
requires `ctx().dragged_id().is_none()`. So once the button was held to select text, every notch
was swallowed and the page sat still until the button came up.

A trackpad still worked because its precise deltas already bypass the ScrollArea (the path added
for #759). A coarse wheel had no such path, and egui's easing cannot fill the gap either: it is
the ScrollArea that applies the eased delta, and the ScrollArea is what has already decided to
ignore the wheel.

## The fix

- A coarse notch under a drag is converted to points and applied through the existing
  un-animated scroll path, using egui's own line and page factors (`input_options.line_scroll_speed`,
  and the viewport height for a page) so a notch moves as far here as anywhere else.
- The eased tail is dropped while the drag holds, so releasing the button cannot jump the document
  by a leftover notch.
- Dragging a selection off the top or bottom edge now scrolls too, so a long selection can be made
  without letting go. Only a selection drag does this: the Hand tool pans by its own drag delta,
  and a middle-button gesture already owns the scroll.

Single-page view still turns pages rather than scrolling vertically, and the change is inert when
no drag is under way.

## Test

`the_wheel_scrolls_the_document_while_a_selection_drag_is_held` drives a real harness, presses and
drags the pointer, asserts the drag is actually under way (`dragged_id().is_some()`), then turns
the wheel and reads the page's position on screen back. It fails against the old behaviour.

title: Scroll a selection drag at the viewport edge (follow-up to #1514, #721)
author: muraa-p
body:
The half of #721 that #1514 left open. It builds on the `selection_drag` flag that PR added for a drag that began on text.

Reaching the top or bottom of the window with a held text-selection drag used to stop the selection there, so a long selection had to be made in pieces. Now the drag scrolls the page itself.

The scroll is linear in how far the pointer has crossed into a 40-point band at the edge, and capped at that band's worth of it (16 points per frame), so it speeds up towards the edge but cannot jump when the pointer leaves the window entirely. Back in the middle of the viewport it stops altogether.

Two details worth calling out:

- **The band is measured on screen.** The closure passed to `show_viewport` receives `viewport` in *content* coordinates — its minimum is zero until the user scrolls — so a band measured against it drifts by a whole scroll offset and goes out of reach at the window's edge. The code therefore measures against `visible`, the same rectangle translated into screen coordinates, which is what `page_screen_rect` and the rest of this function already work in.
- **The pointer is allowed to leave the viewport.** Dragging past the edge is exactly the gesture this serves, so there is no `contains` gate; only the overshoot into the band is measured, and the clamp caps the rate however far out the pointer goes.

The tests cover the edge and the steady state: a held drag at the bottom edge scrolls the document down — the page's screen top rises, the same way a negative wheel delta does — while the same drag parked in the middle of the viewport does not drift.

title: M5: Fill & Sign text reads across on rotated pages
author: alexanderalber
body:
## What this changes

Typed text in Fill & Sign (text and dates), comment text boxes and the headless `fill_sign_add` tool ignored the page's `/Rotate`. On a page stored sideways, which is common for scanned forms (a user report: an office's photo-scanned registration form), every piece of typed text came out sideways.

- The box is laid out along the displayed axes, with its displayed top-left at the click (new `pdfcraft_engine::text_box_at` / `displayed_offset`, built on the existing `signature_image::upright_box`).
- When a `TextBox` or `Typewriter` is added to a turned page, the annotation records the turn in `/PCTextRotate`. Its appearance draws the text upright in the displayed box and maps it into `/Rect` with a form `/Matrix` (`view_matrix_for`), the same way rubber stamps (`/PCStampRotate`, #1398) and image signatures (`/PCPictureRotate`) already do. Flattening honours the `/Matrix`.
- Callouts are unchanged: their leader line and box stay in user-space axes.
- Contributor credit: adds my own `contributors/people.toml` entry (separate commit).

## How you verified it

title: Edit text: the four-way arrow wherever a drag moves, and a sharp page while editing
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Follow-up to #1600 (#1520, #1623): moving text works, but nothing said so.

## Problem

In Edit text & images the pointer over a closed paragraph was the text cursor, and a drag showed the closed hand. So the two ways to move a paragraph (drag it while closed; since #1600, drag the frame of the open one) went unnoticed: a user clicks, gets the typing box, drags inside it and selects text instead.

A second thing showed up while testing this: with a paragraph open, the rest of the page goes soft once zoomed past about 1.2x on a Retina display. The page around the editor is drawn from one raster, `TextBackground`, capped at the 2048 px backdrop side.

## Change

- **The four-way arrow wherever a drag moves** (`edit_text_ui.rs`, `object_ui.rs`): over a closed paragraph, on the frame band of the open one (4 px outside its outline), over a selected object group, and throughout a move of a paragraph, an image or a group. The open paragraph's text keeps the text cursor, a paragraph's left and right edges keep the rewrap cursor, image corners keep the resize cursors. This matches Fill & Sign, where a placed mark already shows `CursorIcon::Move`.
- **A sharp page while editing**: the editing raster is asked for at the tiling threshold (`TILE_THRESHOLD`, 4096 px, now `pub(crate)`) instead of `BASE_SIDE`, sharp to about 2.5x on Letter or A4; a GPU with a smaller `max_texture_side` still caps it. Worst case 64 MB for one raster, the same order as the tiles it stands in for.

title: macOS: the standard About panel shows the website and Discord links (#1287)
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Closes #1287

## Cause

PdfCraft > About PdfCraft is AppKit's standard About panel: winit's default macOS menu calls `orderFrontStandardAboutPanel:`. That panel shows the icon, name, version and `NSHumanReadableCopyright` from Info.plist, and under them whatever `Credits.rtf` (or `.html`/`.rtfd`) the bundle carries in `Contents/Resources`. The bundle carried none, so the panel had no website.

## Change

`packaging/macos/Credits.rtf`, copied into `Contents/Resources` by `package.sh` before signing, with the lines the in-app Help > About has: the one-sentence description, the licence, and clickable links to getartcraft.com and the Discord. Plain RTF with `HYPERLINK` fields, which the panel renders as links. No code change; the native menu bar (#80, #904) is untouched.

## Tests

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `textutil -convert txt Credits.rtf` | the five lines, no stray markup |
| Ad-hoc bundle (debug binary + Info.plist.in + Credits.rtf, `codesign -s -`), PdfCraft > About PdfCraft | the panel shows the five lines under "Version 0.7.1 (0.7.1)" (read back through Accessibility); the links are the `HYPERLINK` fields TextEdit writes, which the panel renders as links |
| `package.sh` | not run (needs the release build and signing); the added line is a plain `cp` next to the icon's |

Observed on macOS 26 (Apple Silicon, German system).

title: M6: detect form fields on scanned pages (#1721)
author: alexanderalber
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1721. Prepare a form ▸ Detect form fields found nothing on scanned forms: it read only text-layer words and drawn paths, and a scan is one picture.

- **When:** a page that images cover at least half of, and whose content draws no lines or boxes, takes the new path. Every other page is detected exactly as before (a born-digital form over a background picture still uses its vector shapes).
- **Shapes from pixels** (`pdfcraft_forms::detect::raster::shapes`, pure, L3, no new dependencies). The page is rendered at 144 dpi (long side capped at 3000 px, input capped at 12 MP). Ink is a pixel clearly darker than its local mean, so uneven paper still counts as paper. Lines are nearly solid horizontal or vertical runs of ink (≥ 4 pt, gaps ≤ 1 pt bridged). Boxes are enclosed patches of paper (flood fill) that are close to rectangles. A box with a small printed label gets its largest empty band of rows, or failing that of columns, as the writing area (common in German official forms). Rules are the horizontal lines with an open end; lines closed by verticals at both ends are box, table or frame edges. The result goes into the existing pure `detect()` unchanged.
- **Labels:** from the text layer (an earlier Recognize Text), else from OCR when the models are installed. Recognised "words" under 4 pt tall are dropped, because noise read as text made a box look filled. Without models the fields are still created, with default names (Text1, Check Box1).
- **Rotation:** detection runs in the displayed frame, so a scan stored sideways and turned with `/Rotate` reads like any other page. Fields on a turned page get `/MK /R` equal to the page rotation (with the rect pinned so `set_props` doesn't swap it), so typed text reads upright.
- `form_detect_fields` description and `parity` `form.auto-detect-fields` notes updated.

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-forms`, `pdfcraft-engine`, `pdfcraft-automa…

title: M14: Print on File Explorer's PDF menu (#1695)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1695. Also fixes #2082: Outlook Classic's Print Immediately runs the file type's `print` verb, which this adds.

When PdfCraft is the default PDF app on Windows, File Explorer's right-click menu has no **Print**. The `PdfCraft.Document` ProgID registered only `open`. This PR:

- **MSI** (`packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs`): adds `PdfCraft.Document\shell\print\command` = `"pdfcraft.exe" --print "%1"`.
  - It sits in the `PdfcraftApp` component next to `open`, so uninstall removes it.
  - Windows shows the canonical verb in the system language, and on Windows 11 it's under "Show more options".
- **`pdfcraft --print <files…>`** (`apps/pdfcraft/src/print_verb.rs`): prints each file on the system default printer without creating a window, then exits.
  - Settings are the Print dialog's defaults: all pages, Fit, document and markups. It prints one copy and uses the driver's own two-sided setting.
  - Paper is the standard sheet the first page matches (A4, Letter…, via `print::matching_paper`). Otherwise it's the page's own size, sent with `Scaling::ShrinkToFit` so the spooler shrinks it onto the printer's default paper. The dialog's US Letter default would be wrong for A4 users, with no dialog to fix it.
- **Fallback, never silent**: a file that can't be printed unattended opens in the app instead, with the new `--dialog print` option. The reason goes to the log. This covers:
  - a missing file or one that isn't a PDF;
  - a file that needs a password;
  - permissions that forbid printing (enforced by `Session::print_pdf`);
  - no default printer, or a job the spooler refuses.
- **`--dialog print`** (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`): opens the Print dialog through `open_print()`, the same path as the menu. With no document open, it does nothing.

title: M2: Make literal text search linear and tolerate missing layout metadata
author: LabDennis
body:
## What this changes

Literal page search used to retry an entire query at every character. Long repeated prefixes made the work grow with both page and query length. The new private search module uses a prefix table (KMP), keeping matching linear while preserving Unicode case folding, whitespace normalization, whole-word boundaries, non-overlapping accepted matches, glyph ranges and result limits. Rejected whole-word candidates still allow overlapping later matches.

The same path no longer panics when a PageText has incomplete layout metadata: absent word/line metadata adds no inferred separator, while known separators remain effective. GUI find and the existing automation search tools share this implementation; no new API or dependency is introduced.

## How you verified it

Windows, upstream base `7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a`:

- All 269 renderer library tests and four new integration tests pass. The missing-metadata regression was run against the original implementation and failed with an out-of-bounds panic before the fix.
- 32,000 deterministic differential comparisons against a simple reference matcher cover multi-character/empty glyphs, Unicode, word and line gaps, case options, whole-word boundaries and result limits. Dedicated cases cover rejected overlapping candidates and long repeated prefixes.
- Existing automation tests `open_inspect_render_and_find` and `redaction_search_respects_case_and_word_boundaries` pass.
- Strict all-target renderer Clippy passes on Rust 1.99.0. Formatting, assets, layers, and WebAssembly renderer checks pass (four existing WASM warnings in untouched code). Tests and benchmarks used Rust 1.95.0.

The included `search_bench` example measures the public PageText search, including normalization and glyph mapping. Same machine/profile, seven measured runs after warmup per revision:

title: fix(ui): drop tests open the dropped PDF inline, not racing the open worker
author: Erry91
body:
## What this changes

Two UI tests fail intermittently since #1493 moved preparing a PDF opened after the first frame
onto the open worker:

- `ui::dropping_a_pdf_on_the_window_opens_it` failed in 3 of 4 runs of the `ui` suite on `main`
  (7437bde3), on macOS, and also failed when run alone.
- `editing::files_dropped_outside_the_page_grid_still_open_as_documents` fails when the
  `editing` suite is busier. With one unrelated test added to the suite, it failed in 5 of 10
  runs.

Both tests drop a PDF and then check for its tab after three frames. The worker often isn't done
by then. #1493 kept startup and test flows inline ("this also preserves deterministic inline
startup and test flows"), but a drop arrives after the first frame, so these two tests ended up
on the worker.

The tests are about where a drop goes (a tab, not the page grid), not about the worker, which
`open_worker_tests.rs` covers. So both now set `run_inline`, the switch documented for
background jobs in tests and already used by several test setups. The drop then opens in the
same frame. This removes the race instead of waiting longer for it, and adds no time to the
suite.

**Related:** these are two of the UI test failures since #1493 that are listed in #1691. #1681
fixes another one with the same cause.

title: M1: a save that doesn't reopen is refused before it replaces the file (#1698)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1698 (point 1: write before verify).

`doc_save` wrote the new bytes with `write_atomic` and only then called `mark_saved`, which is where a rewrite that doesn't reopen gets caught, so by the time the error came back the original file was already gone. This adds `Session::check_save`, the same reopen check `mark_saved` relies on (the cos parser with the reopen password, then `check_pages` against the open document's page count), and runs it before the write in `doc_save` and in the desktop `save_doc_to`. If it fails, the save returns the usual "could not be reopened" error (on desktop, "Couldn't save …") and the file on disk is untouched. Checking the page count is slightly stricter than `mark_saved`, which would accept a readable rewrite that lost pages; refusing that seemed in line with not losing work, but happy to switch to a plain reopen check.

Point 2 (`write_full` dropping the page tree reconstructed when a damaged file was opened) isn't touched here; #1664 rebuilds that page tree as a revision at open time and should cover it. This PR doesn't depend on it.

Validation:
- `a_save_that_does_not_reopen_leaves_the_file_as_it_was` (synthetic file whose catalog `/Pages` is `[ 0 ]`, so the reader finds its one page by scanning and a full rewrite drops it): fails on main (the file is replaced by 500 bytes that don't reopen, as in the report), passes here
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test automation save`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine --lib save`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-automation -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: M2: Fix image anti-aliasing
author: wilcley
body:
## What this changes

Black-and-white scans look broken when zoomed out. Thin lines (staff lines, serifs, table rules) break up or disappear, and text turns jagged.

**Cause:** images without `/Interpolate` (most scans; it's the PDF default) were shrunk by nearest-neighbour, which keeps one source pixel in N. On a 1200 dpi 1-bit scan shown at 60 dpi, that is one pixel in 20 per axis, so any line thinner than that is usually skipped. Found on a scored-music PDF: 1-bit CCITT pages of 10718 × 13701 with no `/Interpolate`. Most staff lines on a page vanished or broke up.

**Fix** (in `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`):

- Images without `/Interpolate` are now shrunk by **exact area averaging**: each device pixel is the coverage-weighted mean of the source area it covers. A thin black line becomes a gray line instead of disappearing, and edges are anti-aliased.
  - Integer arithmetic in units where a source pixel is `target` long and a target pixel `source` long, so every overlap is exact.
  - Streams source rows once each. Memory is one source row plus two target rows of `u64` sums plus the output, all allocated with `try_reserve`. No filter plan or tables, so it has none of the Catmull-Rom planning limits.
- Soft-masked images and `/ImageMask` stencils are averaged **premultiplied**, straight into target RGBA. This replaces `nearest_premultiplied_rgba`, so a clear pixel adds no colour to its neighbours and no full-size RGBA copy is made.
- Shrunk non-interpolated images now **snap to whole device pixels** (`snap_minified_image`), as interpolated ones already did, so the averaged raster is drawn 1:1 and not nearest-sampled a second time.
- `/Interpolate true` is unchanged (Catmull-Rom). Enlarging is unchanged.

**#624 still holds.** That fix stopped Catmull-Rom from blending hard edges across neighbouring pixels. Area averaging only mixes what falls inside one target pixel, so grid-aligned flat colours shrink to exact palette colours. `non_interpolated_images_are_not_smoot…

title: Edit text & images: alignment guides while moving a paragraph or image (#1714)
author: ch0kemeister
body:
Closes #1714. Stacked on #1717 (the cursor and sharpness change); the first commit here is that one, the next two are this.

## What changes for users

While a paragraph or image is dragged in Edit text & images, its edges and centre snap to the edges and centres of the other paragraphs and images on the page, and to the page's own edges and centre, within 6 screen pixels. Where it snapped, a magenta line runs across the page and a small "Shift drags freely" label sits beside the box; both vanish on release. Shift drags freely. The nearest line wins on each axis. The open paragraph dragged by its frame, and a group selected with Shift-clicks or a marquee, snap the same way as one box. Arrow-key nudges stay exact, as before.

Second commit: the paragraph's pixels travel with the frame. Until now only an empty frame moved and the text stayed where it was until release. The page raster's picture of the paragraph is now drawn into the preview over a blank where it was, closed by its box, open by its frame, and for a selected group; the same approach #1677 takes for images, which this doesn't touch. No render during the drag; the edit renders it properly on release.

## Code

`edit_text_ui.rs`: `snap_to(moving, others, page)` returns the snapped rect and the guides; `draw_guides` paints them and the label. The paragraph drag (`BlockDrag`, `Grip::Move`) and the image move (`ImageSelection::drag` without a corner) feed their preview rect through it, so the applied `MoveObjects` / `ImageEdit::Move` carries the snapped offset. `object_ui.rs`: the selection gesture carries a `snap` offset and its guides, measured on the selection's union, applied to the preview and to `object_move_offset` on release. Candidates come from the page's paragraph rects and image frames (`view.edit_lines`, `view.edit_images`), measured on the text itself rather than its 2 px padded box so text, images and the object selection all line up alike. Rewrap handles and corner resizes don't snap.

title: Issue #1676: put fallback faces on the interface baseline
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1676: in a Chinese interface, Chinese next to Latin in one label ("扫描和 OCR", "欢迎使用 PdfCraft") no longer sits above or below the Latin, and icons line up with their Chinese labels again.

**Cause.** In epaint 0.36's `text_layout`, a glyph from a fallback face is positioned at

```
face_ascent + 0.5 * (font_height − font_face_height)
```

This centres the fallback's line box (ascent − descent + gap) on the primary face's line box instead of lining up their baselines. Relative to Inter, the fallback's baseline therefore moves down by

```
((ascent_f + descent_f) − (ascent_Inter + descent_Inter) + gap_Inter − gap_f) / 2   (em)
```

The amount depends entirely on whichever Chinese face is installed. Measured with skrifa, the metrics egui uses:

| Face | Shift under Inter |
|---|---|
| Microsoft JhengHei (`msjh.ttc`, zh-Hant on Windows) | +0.047 em (down) |
| Microsoft YaHei (`msyh.ttc`, zh-Hans on Windows) | +0.034 em |
| SimSun | −0.075 em (up) |
| JetBrains Mono (the monospace primary) | −0.004 em |

**Fix.** Each fallback face gets a `FontTweak::y_offset_factor` that cancels its own shift. The factor is computed from that face's vertical metrics, read with the same skrifa version and call egui uses (`metrics(Size::unscaled(), LocationRef::default())`), so any face lands on Inter's baseline: PingFang, JhengHei, YaHei, WenQuanYi, and the craft-fonts faces.

- `theme::on_interface_baseline` is applied in `system_fonts::read`, which covers the installed Chinese, Devanagari, Telugu and general fallbacks, and to every embedded non-primary face in `font_definitions_for_platform`, which covers craft-fonts.
- A face that doesn't parse is left as it is.
- The primary faces' tweaks are unchanged (`windows_hinting_changes_only_the_jetbrains_symmetric_rendering_field` still passes).
- `skrifa` moves from the native-only dependencies to all targets. egui already brings the same version to wasm, so nothing new enters the tree.

title: M7: fold repeated image transforms into one cm instead of nesting q
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Moving, resizing, rotating or flipping a figure wrapped it in a fresh `q cm … Q` on every edit. Twenty drags therefore left twenty nested graphics states and twenty `cm` operators around one `Do`. The content stream grew with each edit and moved the figure toward the nesting limit that viewers enforce (PDF 32000-1 Annex C recommends 28 levels).

When the placement already sits alone in a `q cm … Q`, `transform_image` and `translate_images` now change that `cm` in place. That wrapper can be the image's own placement or one an earlier edit added. Either way the CTM inside is `local · cm · outer` (ISO 32000-1 §8.3.4, §8.4.4), so the rendered result is the same.

These cases still get the wrapper, but only once:
- a bare `cm Do` with no `q`
- a clip shared with other content
- a scope that holds any other content

title: M7: Edit text keeps each run's style when restyling a mixed region or editing it in several places
author: Arakmar
body:
## What this changes

Two Edit text bugs in regions that mix styles (e.g. a 24 pt title, a red heading and 12 pt body lines).

**1. Restyling a region collapsed it.** Clicking Bold, Italic or a font family rewrote the whole region in the first run's size and font, merged into one rewrapped block. Font and weight changes always took the single-style rewrite path.
- **Styled rewrite:** these changes now use the styled rewrite. Each run keeps its size and colour, and standalone rows (titles, dates) keep their break and alignment. Paragraph lines reflow within the region, and if a paragraph grows the lines below it move down.
- **Per-run Bold/Italic:** with no selection, Bold and Italic toggle only the weight or slant of each run. This adds a new `BlockStyle::italic`, also accepted by `text_edit`.
- **Own font resource:** a chosen weight or slant gets its own font resource, instead of overwriting the shared substitute that other paragraphs may use.
- **Caret:** the inline editor's caret is as tall as the row it is on, instead of the region's first size.

**2. Two separate edits in one draft restyled the text between them.** Adding a letter to the red heading and another to the black line below it, before applying, turned the text between them red and bold. `TextBlock::edited_spans` matched the draft to its source runs with a single common prefix and suffix. A bounded Myers diff now keeps each unchanged character in its own run, and an inserted character takes the run of the character before it.

title: M7: keep the source operators of rows a text edit doesn't reach
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Changing one character in a paragraph used to rewrite every row of that paragraph from its text state, which caused three problems:
- A row whose width came from `TJ` kerning or justification gaps was squeezed back to that width with a `Tz` stretch.
- The `TJ` gaps became literal double spaces, so copying and searching saw `justified  text`.
- Fixing a typo in the last line of a justified paragraph stretched the glyphs of every line above it.

`rewrite_styled_block` now compares each output row with the source row at the same position. A row keeps its original operators, byte for byte, and only the other rows are drawn again, when all of these hold:
- every character in the row comes from the source unchanged;
- no style range covers it;
- the paragraph-wide formatting, width and position are untouched.

The new drawing goes where the first rewritten row was. The existing `ET`/`BT` split then restores the text matrix for the rows kept after it.

Rows are rewritten as before in these cases:
- An earlier row wrapped and pushed them down, so they no longer line up with a source row.
- A rewritten row used `'` or `"`. Its move to the next line is something the rows after it depend on.
- The first rewritten row is drawn in a different space from the paragraph's first row.
- A source run contains a line break, so editor rows can't be paired with visual rows.

Changing the whole paragraph's formatting, width or position still rewrites every row. Formatting a selection rewrites only the rows it covers.

This only changes the styled path that the inline editor uses (`rewrite_styled_block`). The `Tz` calibration still applies to rows that are rewritten.

title: M7: draw new characters with the source font's own embedded program
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

A PDF that embeds the complete TrueType/OpenType program of a simple WinAnsi font can encode only 256 characters through that font. The program itself usually has many more glyphs. Typing a character that the encoding lacks, such as `ő` (or Arabic in a face that has it), ignored the program and sent the edit to the Type 3 fallback, so:
- official builds drew the character with the Japanese face's Latin glyph;
- builds without craft-fonts refused it with *"this text needs PdfCraft's Japanese fallback font"*, even for a Latin letter.

The row editor now tries the paragraph font's own program after these sources and before the fallback:
- the source encoding;
- same-face resources;
- matching craft-fonts faces.

When the program has the glyph, it is embedded once per edit as a Unicode Type 0 font, the same embedding a loaded font gets. The new character therefore keeps the source face. A paragraph whose new characters only that program can draw now takes the row editor's path.

The program is used only when both of these hold:
- **The font is not a subset** (no `ABCDEF+` tag). A subsetter can keep a character's mapping after dropping its outline.
- **`embedding::validate` accepts it.** That includes the OS/2 `fsType` check, so a font licensed only for preview & print, or with restricted embedding, is not reused for editable text.

When no face has a non-Japanese character, the error now names that character and points to **Load font…** and **Installed fonts…**. Japanese text keeps its current message.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: Automation: tell a tool name or an unknown id from a command without a tool in command_run
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1759.

`command_run`, which `command_batch` calls for each step, gave the same message for every id that had no mapped tool: "command X has no headless tool". That was true only for real commands. A tool name such as `page_rotate` and a plain typo got the same message, which suggests the command exists. Now the error covers three cases. For a tool name, it gives the matching command id (`page_rotate` -> `page.rotate`) or says to call the tool directly. An id the registry doesn't know gets "unknown command id". A real command with no tool keeps the old message. Thanks @stobados for the clear report.

I kept tools out of `command_batch`. Steps still take command ids only, so the batch contract and the param filtering in `command_run` stay as they are. If you'd rather have `command_batch` accept tool names too, I'm happy to switch.

Validation:
- `command_batch_tells_a_tool_name_from_an_unknown_or_toolless_command`: fails on main (all four steps say `command "…" has no headless tool; see command_list`), passes here, also alone with `--test-threads=1`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test automation command_batch` and `--features mcp ... conventions_` (the existing batch/conventions tests) pass
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- No assets, parity entries or docs touched (no doc quotes the old message)
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(automation): say when a command id is a tool name or unknown (#1759)
author: MrPranklin
body:
Fixes #1759.

`command_run` and `command_batch` resolved a step's `id` only through `tool_for_command`, so every id that isn't a command with a headless tool got `command "…" has no headless tool; see command_list`. That's right for a registered command like `file.open_recent`, but for a tool name such as `page_rotate` (or a typo) it reads as if the command exists and only lacks a tool.

The lookup in `conventions.rs` now tells the three cases apart:
- a registered command without a tool keeps the existing message;
- a tool name says so and names its command id, e.g. `"page_rotate" is a tool name, not a command id; use command id "page.rotate" or call the page_rotate tool directly`, or says the tool has no command id;
- anything else is `unknown command id "…"; see command_list for ids such as "page.rotate"`.

The issue also suggested accepting tool names as aliases. I went with the clearer error instead, because it keeps `command_*` to the command registry and doesn't add a second way to spell every step. If you'd rather accept tool names, it's a small follow-up.

Validation:
- `command_ids_that_are_tool_names_or_unknown_say_so` checks `command_batch` and `command_run` with a tool that has a command, a tool without one (picked from `tools()`), an unknown id, a registered command without a tool, and a real command that still runs. It fails on main (`command "page_rotate" has no headless tool; see command_list`) and passes here.

title: M8: redacting part of a scanned (JPEG) page keeps the rest of its picture (closes #1771)
author: magdale76
body:
Closes #1771.

Redacting part of a page made from images removed the whole picture: `image::clear` only handled lossless filters, and a `DCTDecode` image (every scan and camera photo) was removed whole, leaving a white page with black boxes.

**Change** (`crates/redact/src/image.rs`)
- A grey or RGB JPEG (`/Filter /DCTDecode` or `[/DCTDecode]`) is decoded with `image` (zune-jpeg, already in the tree through `pdfcraft-optimize`), the covered pixels are cleared with the same pixel walk, and a new JPEG (quality 90) is written **from the cleared pixels only**. Nothing of the original stream is carried over: no covered pixels, no APP segments such as an EXIF thumbnail. The original object is untouched for other pages, as before.
- Still removed whole (fail-closed): CMYK JPEGs, a colour space whose component count disagrees with the JPEG, data the decoder can't read, more than 64 Mpx, and JPX/JBIG2/CCITT.
- The pixel walk moved into `clear_pixels`, shared by both paths, and uses `get_mut` instead of indexing.
- README and the `protect.redact-area` parity notes say what is still removed whole.

**Tests** (`crates/redact/src/tests.rs`)
- `a_scanned_jpeg_page_keeps_its_picture_around_the_redaction`: a page-sized RGB JPEG redacted in its left half. One image cleared, none removed; the copy is still DCT, the left half is black and the right half white.
- `a_jpeg_that_can_not_be_cleared_safely_is_still_removed`: grey colour space over an RGB JPEG, and non-JPEG bytes, are removed whole; a grey JPEG in a `[/DCTDecode]` array is cleared.
- By hand on Windows 11: a PDF of photographed pages, with areas redacted and applied, then saved and reopened. The page kept its picture with only the marked areas blacked out; before the change it came out blank.

title: M5: draw FreeText text outside WinAnsi with craft-fonts Type 3 glyphs (#506)
author: tuat-yate
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #506 for FreeText: text boxes, callouts and Fill & Sign text. Builds on @kogasura's closed draft #975.

Text outside WinAnsi (Japanese, Greek, Cyrillic, Central European) used to be drawn as `?`. It is now drawn with Type 3 fonts built from the craft-fonts Japanese faces, each with a ToUnicode map, so it saves, flattens, searches and copies as typed. Nothing is embedded. Text that is entirely WinAnsi is drawn byte for byte as before.

- **`pdfcraft-fonts`: new `type3.rs`.**
  - `type3_glyph` and `type3_font` replace the editor's copies, which this PR removes. This also fixes the editor's ToUnicode maps, which wrote up to 240 entries in one `beginbfchar` block; the limit is 100.
  - `type3_plan` picks one face for a whole text and decides once which characters it draws, so measuring, reporting and drawing agree.
  - Characters that `needs_shaping` (combining marks, RTL, Indic, Thai, …) are never planned, so they are reported rather than set apart or out of order.
- **`annot`.**
  - `appearance::build` now returns an `Appearance`: the form plus the plan of the fonts it names.
  - `Appearance::store` adds those fonts as indirect objects when the appearance goes into a document. This happens in `apply_appearance`, which both the saved path and the display-only path (`with_missing_appearances_cached`) go through, so nothing is written inline and fixed up later.
- **Interaction with #1112.** The FreeText branch of `undrawable_text` uses the same plan as the drawing. Drawable text is no longer marked (`PCUndrawn`), `fill_sign_add` no longer warns about it, and flattening isn't refused for it. Measurement labels, stamp by-lines and redaction overlays are unchanged, because they are still Helvetica-only.
- **Box sizing.** `text_measure` / `text_wrap` measure with the advances the text is drawn with. They are used in `fitted_box`, `ui-egui`'s `text_box_rect` and `fill_sign_add`.

Not in this PR:
- CJK line breaking and kinsoku. Lines still break on…

title: docs: keep one copy of the catalog paragraph in localization.md
author: feraremag2680
body:
## What this changes

`docs/localization.md` carries the "Dialogs, panels, menus, notices and history labels" paragraph three times. This deletes two of them and keeps the current one **exactly as main wrote it**. No rewording, nothing else touched: one file, two lines removed.

The copies this deletes:

- one ends `Czech and Turkish cover the menus so far` — stale since #1057 completed the Turkish catalog;
- one stops at Slovenian and says only Czech covers the menus — it predates Kazakh, Polish, Greek, Turkish, Lithuanian and Vietnamese.

Both are superseded by the paragraph #1712 wrote, which covers every shipped language and the CLI/MCP exclusion.

### Why there are three

Main had two copies until 15 October. At 06:21 #1712 replaced both with the single current paragraph — the same cleanup this PR originally proposed, done independently. At 06:54 #2320, branched before that, added its two back, so main carries three again.

Neither author did anything wrong. A language addition edits the paragraph its branch has, and the merge keeps both sides. It is the same mechanism that produced the duplication #1525 fixed in the **Auto** paragraph.

### It will happen again

29 other open PRs touch this file, nearly all adding a language. Any of them branched before 15 October restores its copies when it lands.

This PR only cleans up the current state. Stopping the recurrence is a separate, structural question, and #1712's "and others" is most of the way there: once the paragraph names no languages, a language addition has no reason to edit it, and the per-language facts already live in [localization-parity.md](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/main/docs/localization-parity.md). title: M7: reuse a page's font resource and program when embedding again
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Every call to `embed` or `embed_mapping` wrote a new set of font objects under a new `PCFull{n}` name:
- a Type 0 font;
- a CIDFont;
- a descriptor;
- a ToUnicode map;
- a glyph map.

Editing a paragraph that needs a full face therefore added another set of font objects to the page on every apply, even when the text was the same. That covers a completed subset, shaped Arabic, or a loaded font. The program itself was shared only when it sat among the first 8192 objects of the document. On larger files, each edit also copied the whole font program, which is often several megabytes.

`embed_mapping` now checks the page's own `PCFull` resources first:
- **Same embedding.** If one has the same font name, program, glyph map (`CIDToGIDMap`, or the CFF encoding CMap) and ToUnicode map, it is returned as is and nothing is written.
- **Same program.** Otherwise, if one of them already uses this program, the new resource shares it, wherever that program sits in the document. The existing document-wide search still runs after this.

Programs are compared by the length they were written with (`Length1`) before their data is decoded. Streams are compared decoded, so a file that another writer has compressed since is still recognised.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: M7: read the page once per keystroke when measuring a text draft
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

The inline editor calls `text_edit_layout` on every keystroke to size the frame. Each call interpreted the page's content four times:
1. `text_blocks`, for the paragraphs;
2. `text_lines` again, for the untouched runs;
3. once more inside `rewrite_block`, on the clone, which was still unchanged;
4. and finally for the rewritten draft.

The first three read the same, unchanged page.

Now `text_edit_layout` reads the page's lines once and groups the paragraphs from them. It then hands those lines to the rewrite through a new private `rewrite_block_from`. `rewrite_block_with_limit` also uses that function, after reading the lines itself, so `rewrite_block` behaves exactly as before. The draft is still read back once after the rewrite.

I measured this on a page of 120 runs in 80 paragraphs: 50 keystrokes in a release build took **0.87 ms each, against 1.25 ms before**. Those are the fastest of three runs each, from a throwaway timing test that is not part of this PR.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: M11: merge image fragments, and the Standard and Mobile optimizer presets (closes #1783)
author: magdale76
body:
Closes #1783. Related: #490.

Some PDF printers draw a page picture as thousands of images one pixel row high. Reduce File Size and the PDF Optimizer couldn't touch such a page: a one-row image can't be resampled, and every JPEG strip repeats its headers. On one real 4.3 MB page they saved 2 bytes. This PR puts the strips back together first, as Acrobat's optimizer does, and adds the optimizer's Standard and Mobile presets.

## Results on the real page (private, measured locally; one A4 page, 3,300 strips)

| | Size | Mean abs. pixel difference vs the original at 96 dpi |
|---|---|---|
| Original | 4.3 MB | |
| Acrobat, Mobile | 147 KB | 8.3 |
| **This PR, Mobile** | **161 KB** | **6.9** |
| **This PR, Standard / Reduce File Size** | **231 KB** | **6.6** |
| main | 4.3 MB | |

## Changes
- **`pdfcraft-optimize::fragments`** (new; `Settings::merge_fragments`, on by default). A run is consecutive `q … cm /Name Do Q` groups with nothing else between them, each drawing an upright image (no rotation, skew or flip). The images are 8-bit grey or RGB in one colour space, have no masks and no decode array that changes anything, and use a codec PdfCraft decodes. They share their left and right edges and are stacked edge to edge, at least four of them. Failing that, the rows drawn one under the other up to a gap count as a run. Each run becomes one Flate image at the finest resolution of its fragments; JPEG and Flate strips of different widths are resampled to the widest. The image settings then resample and recompress it as usual, and Clean Up drops the strips. A page whose content stream doesn't parse cleanly (`skipped > 0`) is left alone.
- **Presets** (`Preset::{Standard, Mobile}`). Standard is `Settings::default()`. Mobile resamples colour and greyscale images above 144 ppi to 96 ppi, JPEG high (80). Values were read off Acrobat's dialog; no assets or strings copied.
- **UI:** the PDF Optimizer has a Settings menu (Standard, Mobile, Custom once an option changes) and a Me…

author: edurbs

Layer A of PDF → PostScript/EPS export: `create.export-ps` / `create.export-eps` to `partial`, per docs/gaps.md §8.

Tracks #1561 (Layers B/C/D remain open there).

title: M10: Add reviewable scan-line cleanup
author: LabDennis
body:

title: M7: rewrap Chinese and Japanese text between characters
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Rewrapping a paragraph broke rows only at spaces. Chinese and Japanese are written without spaces between words, so a rewritten paragraph in either language stayed one overlong row and ran past its frame.

A row may now also end between two characters when either one is an ideograph, kana or full-width form (Unicode line breaking, UAX #14, class ID). The line-start and line-end rules of JIS X 4051 ("kinsoku") still apply:
- **A row never begins with:**
  - closing punctuation (`、。，．！？`);
  - closing brackets and quotes (`」』）】`);
  - small kana (`っゃョ`);
  - the prolonged sound mark and iteration marks (`ー々ゝ`);
  - the ideographic space.
- **A row never ends with:**
  - an opening bracket or quote (`「『（【`);
  - a currency sign before an amount (`￥$€`).

Those characters move with their neighbour. A Latin word inside Japanese text, such as `PDF` or `￥100`, is never split. Korean is written with spaces between words, so it keeps breaking only at spaces. So does Thai, whose words need a dictionary to find.

The rule lives in a new private module, `crates/edit/src/linebreak.rs`. Both rewrite paths use it:
- `wrap` in `text.rs` cuts each word into breakable pieces and joins pieces of one word without a space;
- the word scan in `rewrite_styled_block` ends a word at those same points.

No new dependency and no fonts. Which face draws a character is unchanged.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: M7: justify paragraphs whose font shows the space with another code
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

A justified paragraph stretches its spaces with word spacing (`Tw`). But `Tw` applies only to the single-byte code 32 (ISO 32000-1 §9.3.3). Two kinds of font show a space with some other code:

- **A composite source font** (Type 0, two-byte codes). Justify was turned off for these, so the paragraph came out left-aligned, with no message.
- **The generated Type 3 fallback** (Japanese or Hebrew text the source font lacks). Its codes are numbered from 1, so code 32 is whatever the 32nd different character happens to be. Justify set `Tw` anyway. That widened that one character and left the spaces as they were, so the rows didn't reach the right edge.

Now `rewrite_block` checks whether word spacing reaches the font's space: does the space encode as a single-byte code 32?
- **Yes:** nothing changes, and `Tw` stretches the spaces as before. That covers simple fonts and the standard-14 substitute.
- **No:** a stretched row is shown up to and including each space. Each space is followed by a `TJ` adjustment of the same amount (`-1000 · extra / size`), and `Tw` stays 0. The space glyph is still drawn, so the text reads back unchanged.

Underlines keep the stretched width, as before.

title: M9: sign with PKCS#11 tokens and smart cards
author: berkeleyinc
body:
## What this changes

Adds a third external-key backend beside the macOS Keychain and the Windows store, so PdfCraft can
sign with a PKCS #11 token or smart card on Unix. Flips parity `sign.pkcs11` to `shipped`.

- `crates/sign/src/pkcs11.rs` (new, gated `#[cfg(all(unix, not(target_arch = "wasm32")))]`): loads
  a PKCS #11 module at run time — `PDFCRAFT_PKCS11_MODULES` (colon-separated), else a
  `p11-kit-proxy.so` — and never links one. RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 and DER-encoded ECDSA P-256/P-384 with
  SHA-256/384/512, through `PrivateKey::external` / `ExternalKey::sign`, the same shape as
  `keychain.rs`.
- Certificates are read **pre-login** (`CKO_CERTIFICATE`); a leaf is matched to its key by `CKA_ID`
  via the private key object or its public counterpart (private keys are hidden until login on
  SoftHSM and cards). Signing logs in with the PIN the caller set once per signing session, never
  guessed; a token with a protected-authentication-path (keypad) passes none.
- Certificates that can't sign — no private key, an unsupported key type, or a key usage without
  `digitalSignature`/`nonRepudiation` — are reported with the reason (greyed in the picker,
  `unusable` in the tool), not silently dropped, as `windows.rs` does.
- `pkcs11:<token label>:<SHA-256>` reference for agents (`sign_pkcs11_ids`, `sign_document`) and a
  PKCS #11 label in the desktop ID picker; the PIN rides the existing `password` argument.
  `pkcs12::write` now refuses a key that lives outside PdfCraft rather than emit a `.p12` with an
  empty key bag.
- i18n: three new UI literals translated in every catalogue, with `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes
  refreshed.

title: M12: View ▸ Line weights, Ctrl/Cmd+5 strokes every path one device pixel wide
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1828.

Thanks @eranco7 for the clear request. The renderer always stroked with the graphics state's own line width, so there was nothing to toggle yet. This adds View ▸ Line weights (Ctrl+5, Cmd+5 on macOS), a checkbox that's on by default. Turned off, it sets a new `InterpreterSettings::thin_lines` flag, and hayro-interpret's stroke path then sets the width to one device pixel from the CTM. That way it holds at every zoom, and inside pattern cells and Type 3 glyphs too.

It is one app-wide setting, as @eranco7 asked, wired like Reading colours: `PdfCraftApp::set_thin_lines` applies it to every open document, and every document opened afterwards starts with it (opened files, created documents, revisions, the signed version, and a file reloaded from disk after it changed; the reload now reapplies Reading colours too, which it used to lose). It's saved with the other preferences (`thin_lines` in the settings file), so it survives a restart, and a value that isn't a boolean keeps line weights on. Underneath, the engine keeps it per document through `RenderConfig` and `Session::set_thin_lines`, with a `view_line_weights` automation tool so `page_render` can show it. It is display only: print previews ignore it, `Document::export_source` clears it so Export ▸ Image, `doc_export_images` and Print as Image draw the real widths, and print itself never goes through the setting. The vendored patch is listed as (35) in `vendor/README.md`, and the parity entry `view.line-weights` is now shipped.

Choices that are yours, happy to switch:
- Stroked text (render modes 1/2) keeps its width. Only paths and `re` rectangles get thinned.
