title: XFA: flatten a form into a plain PDF, or convert it to a static form
author: ysrdevs
body:
## XFA: flatten a form into a plain PDF, or convert it to a static form

Follow-up to #121, #230, #301, #414, #1175, #1355 and #1589. This closes `form.xfa-flatten`, the last XFA parity entry that was still planned.

### The problem

Flattening the fields of a laid-out XFA form baked them into the pages but left the XFA in the file. Adobe's viewers see the packets and `/NeedsRendering`, lay the form out again from the template over the baked pages, and show a live form; every other viewer shows the flattened pages. The "flattened" PDF was two different documents depending on the viewer.

### What changes

* **`pdfcraft_xfa::strip`** takes the XFA out of a document: the packets (template, data, config, everything), `/NeedsRendering` on the catalog and the AcroForm, the layout mark, the overrides, Reader usage rights (`/Perms /UR3`, which changing the form voids anyway), and the private keys PdfCraft put on every field down the Kids tree (`/PCSom`, `/PCXfaClick`, `/PCXfaImage`, `/PCItems`). The packet streams are freed so an incremental save carries no unreachable copy of the data. Each field dictionary is walked once (a seen-set checked before pushing, and a cap); a document without XFA is left untouched.
* **Nothing goes in silence.** `strip` reports what the packets held beyond the fields: the packets by name, data values no field showed (counted against the fields' data paths), buttons that ran XFA scripts and image fields (inert from now on), the layout mark's own warnings (now permanent), the usage rights. The engine turns the report into document warnings prefixed `XFA removed:`, adds a count of fields whose value differed from the form's data (data PdfCraft could not read into them, now lost), and shows them in the app's warnings and the tools' output. On undo the XFA's own warnings apply again and the strip's go.

title: M1-M9: audit run-4 medium fixes: signature verdicts, fail-closed redaction and sanitizing, bounded work
author: JeremyYao
body:
## What this changes

The medium-severity findings of a defensive security review of the codebase (synthetic fixtures only, no personal data), one commit per finding, each with the red-before-fix evidence in its message. The high-severity findings are in #1916; this branch is based on `main` independently of it, so whichever merges second needs a rebase (both touch `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs` `classify_changes`, the sign README and the parity notes).

**Signatures (M9).** An OCSP responder carried in a response is a delegate by how it was found, whatever subject name it copies. A certificate trusted for signing is not thereby a time authority: a timestamp token is trusted time only from a certificate with id-kp-timeStamping. The byte range must exclude exactly the `/Contents` of the object carrying the signature dictionary, so a second field borrowing a genuine signature's range and value is invalid. Defining an object the signed revision referenced but never defined is page content. Form changes after signing are judged by what changed, not by where: a field is form fill only when nothing but its value and what is regenerated from it changed, a new field or widget is a comment-level change unless it is a signed signature field, and under P=1 the one signature change permitted is a document timestamp. A field the signer locked (FieldMDP references, else the signed field's `/Lock`, which signing now writes as a reference) may not be filled in afterwards.

**Scripts (M6).** Source a script builds at run time for `eval()` or `Function()` is screened as the script itself was (boa `HostHooks::ensure_can_compile_strings`).

**Apply Redactions (M1/M8), fail-closed where it guessed before.** Streams are decoded strictly and as the document declares them (an indirect `/Filter` or `/DecodeParms` is resolved; truncated or corrupt data, an out-of-range predictor, `/F` or `/DP` on the dictionary are errors — `Stream::filters_in` and `Stream::decoded_strict_in`, additive). title: feat(cli): page lists take ranges, and a missing page is named as typed (#1923)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1923, in two parts.

**Ranges.** `page_list`, which parses `extract --pages`, `split --before` and the page lists of `edit --rotate/--delete/--move`, accepted comma-separated single pages only, so `--pages 1-2` failed with `bad page number "1-2"`. **The off-by-one.** On current `main` the message is already right: `pdfcraft-cli extract two.pdf --pages 3` says `page 3 does not exist` (I ran the issue's commands against a build of `main`). title: M2: bound ASCII85 decoding by the stream's output limit (#1796)
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1796

The vendored hayro-syntax gives every filter an output limit. But ASCII85 never got it. `Filter::apply` called `ascii_85::decode(data)` without the limit and the decoder wrote every group and every `z` with no check. Since each `z` turns one byte into four, a Flate stage that's already at its 256 MiB limit can be pushed another 4x past it.

Now the limit is passed through and ASCII85 handles it the same way RunLength, LZW and Flate already do which is it writes only what fits stops with a warning once it hits the limit and caps its starting buffer at the limit. I also added ASCII85 to the patch notes in `vendor/README.md`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` (ran it on the whole workspace)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render`, 269 passed

hayro-syntax isn't a workspace member so I put the test where the earlier bomb fix (#411) put its tests. `decompression_bombs_stop_at_the_stream_limit` in `crates/render/src/raster.rs` now has a fifth stream, `[/FlateDecode /ASCII85Decode]` a Flate stream of `z`s that decodes to more than 256 MiB.

I reverted the fix and checked that the test fails what turned out that it decoded 301,989,892 bytes against the 268,435,456 limit. With the fix it stops at `MAX_DECODED_STREAM`.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests
- [x] No input derived indexing. The remaining space is computed with `saturating_sub`, and the allocation is capped at the limit
- [x] No `unsafe`
- [x] Regression test added (see above)

## Provenance

- [x] No assets, no fonts
- [x] No GPL/AGPL code
- [x] Behaviour follows the existing `decode_limit` convention in this crate

title: fix(redact): phone pattern no longer matches the tail of longer numbers (#1884)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #1884

## Summary

The phone pattern matched the tail of longer digit strings: in a 21-digit IBAN-style run it matched starting at digit 11, so `redact_mark pattern=phone replacement=X` redacted only the last 11 digits while the identifier head (`DE44 5001 0517`) stayed visible — half-redacted output for a redaction tool. The same applied to SIRET and NIR numbers holding a phone-shaped tail.

## Changes

- `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs` — `is_valid_phone_candidate` now rejects a candidate that is immediately preceded by a digit plus separator (space/dot/dash) or immediately followed by a separator plus a digit, i.e. a candidate that is actually part of a longer number. Standalone international (`+33 6 12 34 56 78`), parenthesized (`(202) 555-0123`), dotted and dashed numbers are unaffected, and the existing digit-only whole-run length cap (15) is unchanged.
- Regression test `phone_does_not_match_tail_of_longer_numbers` using the issue's exact IBAN fixture, negative guards for SIRET/NIR lengths, and positive guards for standalone numbers in space, dot and dash layouts.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact patterns` — 11 passed, 0 failed (30 filtered out), including the new regression test.
- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-redact -- --check` — clean.

title: M4: write each page label dictionary as an indirect object
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Refs #1763.

This is an interoperability change; the labels PdfCraft wrote were already valid. `set_page_label_ranges` in `crates/organize/src/labels.rs` put each label dictionary straight into `/Nums` (`/Nums [0 << /S /D /St 324 >>]`), which ISO 32000 allows. Some readers only accept a label dictionary that is its own object, the way Acrobat writes them (`/Nums [0 9 0 R]`). pdfannots2json, which the Obsidian Zotero plugin uses to extract annotations, is one of them: it skips a direct dictionary and falls back to the physical page number, which is what the reporter saw. Each label dictionary is now added as an indirect object and referenced from `/Nums`. The keys (`/S`, `/P`, `/St`) and the tree itself are written as before, and the reader already took both shapes.

I'm saying "Refs" rather than "Fixes" because I haven't run pdfannots2json on a file saved with this branch, so I can't confirm the reporter's case end to end. The labels need to be saved again with this build for the file to change. Happy to switch to "Fixes" if someone can confirm it, or if you'd rather close the issue with this.

Validation:
- New `page_labels_are_written_as_indirect_dictionaries` in `crates/organize/src/tests.rs` sets three ranges, saves, reopens the saved bytes, and checks that every `/Nums` value is a reference to a dictionary with the expected `/S`, `/P` and `/St`, and that the labels read back the same. On main it fails with "the label of page 0 is not an indirect object"; here it passes.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize --lib page_label` passes, and `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-organize --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:

title: M6: auto-size text fields shrink and wrap typed text on screen, as on the page
author: dsskaggs-ai
body:
## What this changes

Auto-size text fields (`0 Tf`, often inherited from the AcroForm `/DA`, as in InDesign-exported forms) already fit their value to the box in the **page appearance**. The **in-place editor** and the **preview shown before the page re-renders** (`paint_unbaked_widget`) ignored auto size. They used a fixed guess from the box height (`h × 0.6`, 6–12 pt), never shrank to the width and never wrapped multiline text. So while you typed a long value it ran past the box and was clipped, unlike Acrobat/Reader, where the text shrinks (and wraps, for multiline) to fit.

- **One fit for both.** The sizing loop moves out of `appearance.rs` into `appearance::auto_text_size_by(width, height, multiline, line_width, wrapped_height)`, with `auto_text_size(text, …, width_of)` as the Helvetica/`wrap_with` convenience. The page appearance output is unchanged. The engine re-exports it as `field_auto_text_size_by`.
- **The screen measures in the font it draws with.** `forms_ui::field_text_size` passes egui galley measurements, because the interface font is wider than Helvetica and breaks lines differently. With Helvetica metrics on screen, the editor still overflowed by a line (caught by the new test).
- **The editor wraps at the width the size was fitted to** (box less 3 pt per side, scaled), so the fit holds at every zoom.
- **Explicit sizes are unchanged** and still clip, as in Acrobat.

Related but separate: #1888 / #1912 change the default size of *newly created* fields. This PR is about filling existing auto-size fields.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-forms`, `pdfcraft-engine`, `pdfcraft-ui-egui` (`--all-targets`)
- [x] tests: `pdfcraft-forms` 68/68, `pdfcraft-engine` all pass, `pdfcraft-ui-egui --test forms` 23/23

title: fix(test): wheel-after-Point test expects half a wheel line, so it passes on macOS
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What this changes

`selection_mouse_wheel_resumes_after_point_scrolling` (crates/ui-egui/tests/viewer.rs, from #1514) asserts that one `Line` wheel notch after a `Point` scroll moves the view more than 50 points. `ScrollSpeed` (#514) makes a wheel line 40 points on macOS and 100 on Windows and Linux, so on macOS the notch scrolls exactly 40 and the test fails on every run:

```
Point-to-Line delay=16: point=30, line=40
Line input must resume after Point: 84 -> 44
```

The test now expects more than half of `ScrollSpeed::Normal.line_points()`: 50 on Windows and Linux, as before, and 20 on macOS. It still fails if the Line notch is swallowed after Point input, which is what it is there to catch. Test-only; no behaviour changes.

## How you verified it

On macOS (Apple silicon), on `main` at 7437bde3:

title: fix(automation): no top-level oneOf in form_set_props input schema (#1961)
author: andreero0
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1961.

`form_set_props` was the only tool whose `input_schema` had a top-level `oneOf` (`field` or `fields`, added in #650). Anthropic's tool API rejects a request when any tool's input schema has `oneOf`, `anyOf` or `allOf` at the top level, so attaching `pdfcraft-cli mcp` to a Claude-based client (Kiro, Claude Code, Claude Desktop) made every prompt fail with:

```
tools.N.custom.input_schema: input_schema does not support oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level
```

The `oneOf` is dropped and the tool now uses `.with(schema(...))` like its neighbours. Nothing is lost: the handler in `forms.rs` already rejects both-or-neither with "give either field or fields, not both", and the descriptions of the tool, `field` and `fields` already say to use one or the other.

`tool_table_is_well_formed` now also checks that no tool has a top-level `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`, so this cannot come back unnoticed.

title: Desktop: show an opening indicator during PDF preparation
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Problem

Preparing a large PDF can take long enough to leave a visible pause even when it runs in the background and the UI thread remains free. While preparation is underway, PdfCraft shows no opening feedback, so the Open action can look ignored and users cannot tell whether the document is still being processed. This makes the app feel unresponsive and gives users no confirmation that their request was accepted.

This PR shows an opening indicator as soon as the native open request is queued and keeps it visible until preparation succeeds or fails. It addresses feedback during the wait; it does not speed up PDF preparation or change CPU or memory use.

Check the request-to-feedback lifecycle: once a native open request is queued, the opening card should appear while background preparation runs, show the pending filename, and clear on success or failure. It should coexist with the optimization card and toast, and respect reduced-motion settings. The indicator is deliberately indeterminate because the parser exposes no meaningful progress fraction.

## Summary

Add localized opening feedback immediately when a native PDF open is requested. The existing background loading path is unchanged. The spinner requests repaints at most 12.5 times per second when motion is enabled. This is a UI feedback change; it does not claim faster opening or lower CPU or memory use. Refs #307.

title: CLI: run --script --report prints one JSON document for the run (#1891)
author: vangel76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1891.

`pdfcraft-cli run --script` printed each step's result as its own pretty-printed object and a failure as one text line on stderr, so a caller could not parse stdout as one document or see which step failed from stdout alone. New opt-in flag `--report` prints one JSON document at the end of the run:

- Exit codes unchanged: the first failing step ends the run, the report is printed, stderr gets the same message, exit 1. Later steps are listed as `skipped`.

title: Issue #1910: Organize opens on the current page
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1910. Opening Organize Pages from the viewer now selects, highlights and scrolls to
the page the user was reading. Before, the grid always opened at page 1, and a selection
left from an earlier visit stayed highlighted instead of the current page.

Three separate things produced that symptom, which is why the diff touches five entry points
and the grid's click handling rather than one line:

1. **Nothing scrolled the grid.** Entering Organize was a bare `view.organize = true`,
   written in five places (tool panel, `page.organize`, the `--organize` option, the
   open-document path when the Organize tool is already chosen, and Create Multiple).
   The scroll offset was whatever egui's `ScrollArea` remembered. A new
   `DocView::open_organize()` is now the only way in; it records the page to reveal and the
   grid scrolls to it on its next frame. The cell is computed from row and column rather than
   looked up, because the grid is virtualized and rows outside the clip are never laid out.
   Each of the five call sites is changed so that no bare assignment remains to reintroduce
   the bug.

2. **A stale selection won the highlight.** The grid highlights `selected` when it is
   non-empty and falls back to the current page only when it is empty. `open_organize`
   therefore drops a selection that does not contain the current page. A deliberate
   multi-selection that includes it is kept, so "select pages in the Pages panel, then open
   Organize to act on them" still works.

3. **The viewer undid the grid's page.** A thumbnail click set `view.current` directly, and
   the continuous viewer recomputes `current` from its scroll position every frame, so the
   value was lost as soon as the grid closed. That made a selection the user just made in the
   grid indistinguishable from a stale one. Grid clicks now call `go_to_page`, as the Pages
   panel already does, so the picked page is also where the document is when the grid closes.

title: Redact: mark text by caller-supplied regex (#1886)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1886

**Root cause.** `redact_mark` only knew literal text, a rect, or five built-in patterns; any other identifier format could not be marked without the caller extracting the text itself.

**What changed**
- `redact_mark` takes `regex` (one of the exclusive selectors, same `pages` scoping as `find`/`pattern`) and optional `validate` (`luhn`, `mod97`, `iban`; keeps a match only if its checksum holds, spaces and hyphens ignored). Schema and tool description updated.
- New `crates/redact/src/user_regex.rs` (separate file, no change to `patterns.rs`). The expression is untrusted: it runs on the `regex` crate (linear-time, no backtracking, no look-around/back-references), compiled with limits: 1024 bytes source, 1 MiB compiled size and DFA cache, nesting 32. Empty expressions and ones that match the empty string are refused with `InvalidArgs`; at most 10 000 matches per page. Char/byte offset mapping is checked, no indexing.
- New dependency: `regex` 1.x with `default-features = false, features = ["std", "unicode"]` (pulls `regex-automata`, `aho-corasick`; MIT/Apache-2.0). `Cargo.lock` also re-unified some `windows-sys` entries on resolve.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml`: new entry `protect.redact-regex` (headless only, missing parts listed); ROADMAP.md progress line.

**Tests / commands run**
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact user_regex`: multibyte offsets, validators, hostile input (empty, too long, unclosed, back-reference, empty match, oversized repetition, deep nesting, `(a+)+$` on 50 000 chars returns at once).
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation` (new `redacting_with_a_caller_regex_through_tools`: errors, two ID numbers marked and applied, Luhn keeps only the valid card).

title: Optimize: optional target_bytes for doc_optimize (#1889)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1889

**Root cause / gap.** `doc_optimize` runs one fixed set of settings, so a caller with a size limit has to guess and retry by hand.

**What changed**
- `doc_optimize` takes an optional `target_bytes` (integer >= 1; 0 or negative is `InvalidArgs`).
- If the first copy (the caller's settings, exactly as before) is larger, it retries with up to 5 stronger image steps, applied to colour and grey images: downsample to at most 110 / 96 / 72 / 54 / 36 ppi with JPEG quality at most 45 / 35 / 28 / 20 / 12. The caller's own ppi/quality are kept when already stronger. It stops at the first copy that fits.
- Result adds `target_bytes`, `target_reached`, `attempts` (max 6) and `target_settings` (`step`, `max_ppi`, `max_jpeg_quality`; step 0 = caller's settings). When nothing fits, the smallest copy is written and `target_reached` is `false`.
- Every attempt runs on the open document through the existing `optimized_bytes`, which never modifies it, so failed attempts change nothing. The output path is resolved through `--root` as before. Without `target_bytes` the output is unchanged (no new keys).
- Schema and tool description updated; `parity/` note on `optimize.optimizer` (headless-only extension, not an Acrobat feature).

**Tests**
- `optimizing_to_a_target_size` in `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs`: no target gives no new keys; a target just below the default result is met by a stronger step; an already-met target stops at 1 attempt; target 1 is not reached after 6 attempts and writes the smaller copy; the open document is unchanged afterwards; target 0 refused; path outside the root refused. Seen failing with the retry loop disabled (`target_reached: false`, `attempts: 1`).
- Run: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test automation optimiz` (3 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-automation -- --check`.

**Not done**

Fixes #1924

## Root cause
In Single Page view the wheel pager only ran when the whole page fit (`fits && ...`). Zoomed in, the wheel went to the `ScrollArea` only and stopped at the page edge.

## What changed
- `canvas.rs`: when the page is taller than the window, wheel events go to a new `DocView::single_page_wheel_edge`. It turns only when the view is at the edge the motion pushes against (bottom for scrolling down, top for up), using the same `single_edges` state the arrow keys already use (#273). Forward shows the next page at its top; backward shows the previous page at its bottom (`goto` fraction 1.0, as the arrow keys do).
- The turn frame was laid out for the old page, so the new page's placement is applied on the next frame, and egui's eased copy of the notch is suppressed for 0.25 s so it doesn't scroll the new page away from its edge.
- `wheel_pager.rs`: `feed_edge`. Choice against accidental turns from momentum: a smooth gesture (touch phases or a phase-less burst) that panned the page first never turns; the fingers must lift (or the burst pause 0.15 s) and a new swipe must start at the edge, then move one notch's worth (40 pt), one page per gesture. A wheel notch at the edge turns at once (no momentum there). Fitting pages behave as before.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml` (view.layout-single-page notes + evidence) and a ROADMAP.md log line.

## Tests
- `wheel_pager::tests::edge_paging_needs_a_gesture_that_did_not_pan` (unit)
- `view.rs::single_page_wheel_at_the_bottom_edge_turns_to_the_next_page_top_and_back`, `single_page_swipe_that_reaches_the_edge_does_not_turn_but_a_fresh_one_does` (kittest, 200% zoom)

title: Draw: a released pen stroke stays on screen until the page raster has it (#1858)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1858

**Root cause:** on release the live gesture overlay is dropped and the annotation is committed, but the page raster that draws it is rendered afterwards. Until it arrives the stale raster (without the stroke) is shown, so the stroke vanishes for as long as the render takes.

**What changed**
- `CommentView` remembers released drag drawings (pen, line, arrow, rectangle, oval) and paints them from their points (same style as the live preview) until a fresh raster of that page (whole page, or the last stale tile) is received.
- Cleared on undo/redo/document-wide invalidation, on any edit other than adding an annotation, and after 20 s as a fallback so a failed render leaves no ghost. At most 16 are kept.
- `paint_gesture` split into `paint_gesture` + `paint_draw` (shared by live and settling strokes).

**Verified**
- Tests (`crates/ui-egui/tests/comments.rs`): the stroke stays pending after release and clears once the raster arrives; undo before the raster leaves nothing. Both fail with the `settle` call removed. `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test comments`, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt pass.
- In the real app on Linux (control channel, synthetic 1.5M-path page whose re-render takes several seconds): on `upstream/main` a screenshot right after the pen release (render pending, Comments panel already shows the drawing) shows no stroke; it appears only once the render finishes. With this branch the stroke is visible in the same in-between frame and after settling. Two strokes in a row, the second released while the render was pending: both visible in the in-between frame and after settling.

**Not done / unverified**
- Not tried on Windows or with the reporter's file or a mouse.
- Polygon, polyline, cloud and callout tools are not covered (they commit on click/double-click).

title: M7: select and edit vector paths; align, distribute and arrange page objects (#1540)
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
Fixes #1540.

## What this changes

Edit text & images can now select and edit vector paths, the lines, shapes and fills a page draws, alongside text and images. Page objects can also be aligned, distributed and brought forward or sent backward. Parity: `edit.vector-edit`, `edit.align-distribute-objects` and `edit.arrange-objects` go from planned to shipped.

**In the Edit tool**
- A click on a path's painted shape selects it, not its empty box. A drag moves it.
- Shift-click and the marquee add paths to a selection of text, images and added items. A path covering most of the page (a background) stays out of clicks and plain marquees.
- With one path selected, corner handles resize it.
- Delete or Backspace removes the selected paths and images.
- The arrow keys nudge the selection (#1600) now that paths are part of it.
- Right-click opens a menu for the selection:
  - **Arrange:** Bring to front, Bring forward, Send backward, Send to back.
  - **Align:** left, centre, right, top, middle, bottom.
  - **Distribute:** horizontally, vertically.
  - **Delete.**
- The left panel shows Fill colour and Stroke colour swatches for selected paths.
- Every change is one undo step.

**For scripts and agents** (`AGENTS.md` §3)
- `object_list` now reports path rows with their fill and stroke colours and line width.
- `object_move` accepts `path` references.
- New tools: `object_align`, `object_resize`, `object_recolour`, `object_delete` (destructive) and `object_arrange`.
- New engine edits: `Edit::AlignObjects`, `TransformPath`, `RecolourObjects`, `DeleteObjects` and `ArrangeObjects`.

**How it edits the PDF.** Every change is a byte-preserving splice of the page's content:
- Only the content streams it touches become new objects.
- Each edit runs on a copy and is checked again before it is swapped in, so a refusal leaves the document exactly as it was.
- Move and resize wrap the path in `q cm … Q`. A private clip moves with its path.
- Recolour wraps the path in `q rg/RG … Q`.

title: Show release notes and compatible downloads in Check for Updates
author: mjshfrvstj-sys
body:
## What this changes

Check for Updates currently compares numeric version tuples and sends users to a GitHub release page to choose a package themselves. This change uses SemVer precedence, shows release notes and download sizes, and opens an exact GUI-package link when the installation context is identified. Unknown contexts retain the official release-page fallback, while confirmed managed installations receive software-manager guidance.

**This PR does not implement automatic downloading, installation, or restarting.** Package links open in the user's browser, installation remains manual, and update checks remain explicitly user-initiated. “Remind Me Later” dismisses the dialog; no reminder scheduler or background checks are added.

- Correct prerelease ordering, including `rc.2 < rc.10 < stable`; optional leading `v`/`V`; build metadata does not manufacture an upgrade, malformed versions are rejected, and older releases are not offered. The existing stable channel is preserved.
- Bounded, plain-text release notes; installed/available versions; selected package and size; retry, up-to-date, missing-package and ambiguous-package states. New labels use existing modal/theme/accessibility conventions and all 22 translation catalogues.
- Exact asset selection by platform, running-build architecture and installation type. Windows x86/x64/ARM64 MSI/portable names, macOS universal DMGs, and Linux AppImage names are covered. CLI/web/checksum/zsync assets are never guessed as installers.
- Shared metadata and selection policy in `pdfcraft-platform`, reusable without GUI or network dependencies. The read-only `update_release_info` automation tool evaluates supplied metadata/context offline, without file or network access; it does not perform an update check or install.

title: Forms: simplified field notation written as real JavaScript, not AFMakeNumber(0)
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What this changes

When a field's Calculate is simplified field notation, `forms::af::calculate_js` wrote

    /** BVCALC (Unit\ Price * Qty) / 2 EVCALC **/ event.value = AFMakeNumber(0);

PdfCraft reads the comment back (`parse_calculate`) and evaluates it natively, so it looks right here.
But a viewer that runs the script instead of reading the comment, Acrobat among them, sets the field
to 0. Acrobat itself writes its translation after the comment. `notation_js` (new, public) now does the
same: each field name becomes `AFMakeNumber(this.getField("name").value)` (`\` escapes in names
honoured, as Acrobat writes them), numbers, operators and parentheses kept:

    /** BVCALC (Unit\ Price * Qty) / 2 EVCALC **/ event.value = (AFMakeNumber(this.getField("Unit Price").value) * AFMakeNumber(this.getField("Qty").value)) / 2;

The comment is unchanged, so `parse_calculate` still recognises it and PdfCraft's own evaluation is
unchanged.

title: Edit: crop an existing page image with its handles
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What this changes

`edit.image-crop` was partial ("for added images: trim each side, clipped"). Images already on the
page can now be cropped too:

- `ImageChange::Crop([f64; 4])` (`edit/src/images.rs`): the part to keep, in user space, becomes a
  `m l l l h W n` clipping path - the box's corners mapped by the inverse of the scope's matrix - placed
  just inside the scope that holds the image (the private-crop scope from #1269), or a new `q … Q`
  around the `Do`. A clipping path already at the scope's start (the picture's earlier crop) is
  replaced, so a crop can grow back. The pixels are never scaled, and a later move or resize wraps the
  scope, so the crop travels with the picture.
- Engine `ImageEdit::Crop` (undo label "Crop image"); tool `image_edit` action `crop` with `rect`
  (top-left-origin points, the part to keep).
- Window (`edit_text_ui.rs`): right-click a selected picture ▸ Crop Image puts it in crop mode
  (`CropMode`, exported): eight handles trim (the inside pans), the part that goes is dimmed, Enter or
  Done applies, Esc or Cancel leaves; Remove Crop (enabled when the picture is cropped) shows the whole
  picture again.
- Rows for the three new labels in all 21 languages, with their checksums in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`; parity

title: ui: route window close through craft-quit on macOS (fixes #2006)
author: zachshallbetter
body:
### Summary

Fixes #2006.

On macOS, closing the window allowed `eframe` to drop the root window while AppKit's run loop was actively running. In subsequent display cycles, AppKit's Touch Bar observation or view hierarchy observers attempted to remove KVO observers from the deallocated view (`-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]`). This triggered an uncaught Objective-C exception and caused macOS CrashReporter to display an "unexpectedly quit" dialog upon exit.

### Solution

1. Added `craft-quit` (with feature `egui`) from `storytold/craft-libs` as a workspace dependency.
2. In `PdfCraftApp::logic` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`), called `craft_quit::on_close_request(ctx)` immediately following `self.guard_quit(ctx)`.
3. When close is requested:
   - If unsaved documents exist, `guard_quit` emits `egui::ViewportCommand::CancelClose` to keep the window open for user confirmation. `craft-quit` sees the cancellation and does not intervene.
   - If documents are clean or discard was confirmed, `craft-quit` intercepts the close request, cancels the raw viewport drop via `CancelClose`, and dispatches `-[NSApplication terminate:]` on the main queue.
   - AppKit then cleanly runs `applicationWillTerminate:`, invoking `eframe`'s normal exit handling and terminating cleanly with status 0.
4. Added unit test `quit_intercept_preserves_dirty_documents_and_forwards_clean_close` in `crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs` exercising both clean close and dirty document prompt preservation.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib quit_intercept`: pass (1 passed)
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test control`: pass (47 passed)
- `cargo fmt --check`: pass
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo check -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`: pass

title: fix(ui): wrap long filenames and metadata in Document Properties (#2011)
author: Osaym
body:
Closes #2011

### Summary
When opening **Document Properties** (`⌘D` / `File ▸ Properties…`) on PDFs with long filenames (such as academic papers, books from the Internet Archive, or legal filings with descriptive titles), the modal dialog was previously forced to expand horizontally far beyond the viewport boundaries because `egui::Grid` row labels defaulted to unwrapped single-line layouts.

This PR wraps text values in Document Properties rows within the 420 pt content column, ensuring the dialog card maintains its intended fixed width (640 pt) and remains properly centered on screen regardless of filename or metadata length.

### Changes
1. **Bounded Multi-Line Wrap in Properties Rows**:
   - In `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs`, wrapped row values inside a scope with `ui.set_max_width(420.0)` and `.wrap()`.
   - Allows long file names and metadata to wrap cleanly onto multiple lines without stretching column 2 or blowing out the modal card width.
2. **Regression Test**:
   - Added `document_properties_long_filename_does_not_overflow_card` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/dialog_chrome.rs` to verify that opening a document with an extreme filename keeps the modal card bounded within the expected width.
3. **Quality Gates**:
   - `cargo fmt --check`: Clean.
   - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: 0 warnings.
   - `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`: All unit and integration tests passed.

title: Encrypt with certificate: public-key security for recipients (/Adobe.PubSec)
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What this changes

The catalog listed **Protect ▸ Encrypt with certificate** as planned (M8). This makes it work: the document is
encrypted for the holders of certificates (ISO 32000-2 §7.6.5), and each opens it with their own private key.

- **sign**: CMS EnvelopedData (`envelope.rs`): RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport and AES-128-CBC content when
  writing; AES-192/256 and 3DES envelopes are read too. A recipient is matched by issuer and serial or by
  subject key identifier. `new_seed()` takes the file key's seed from the operating system's random generator.
- **crypt / cos**: a second security handler, `/Filter /Adobe.PubSec` with `/SubFilter /adbe.pkcs7.s5`, AESV2
  (Acrobat 7) or AESV3 (Acrobat X), with per-recipient permissions. A file that needs a certificate reports its
  envelopes (`CosError::NeedsCertificate`), and `Credential::Certificate` opens it.
- **engine**: `Edit::ProtectWithCertificates`. The session keeps the person's digital IDs and tries them on a
  file's envelopes when it opens. The renderer and inspector read a decrypted copy; saves stay encrypted, and
  signatures are still checked over the file's own bytes.
- **ui**: the **Encrypt with Certificate** dialog. Recipients come from certificate files (.cer, .crt, .pem,
  .der) or from your own digital ID files. Each has "All permissions" (the default for your own IDs) or the
  dialog's restrictions (printing, changes, copying, screen readers). It also has compatibility (AES-256 or
  AES-128) and all contents or all but metadata. It warns when none of the recipients is you. Opening such a
  file asks for a digital ID file and its password, in the same place the password prompt appears.
- **automation**: `doc_protect_certificates` and `identity_add`.
- Rows for the new labels in all 21 languages, with their checksums in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`. Parity
  `protect.certificate-encryption` and `protect.recipient-permissions` move from planned to partial.

title: Highlight the selected text when adding a comment, instead of a sticky note
author: lepotatoguy
body:
## The problem

When I selected a sentence and added a comment, PdfCraft didn't mark the sentence. It dropped a small sticky-note icon at the end of the line, and that was it. Coming back to the PDF later, you couldn't tell which words the comment was about.

Acrobat highlights the selected text and attaches the comment to that highlight. That's what I expected, and it's what this PR does.

## What changed

- **Commenting on selected text now highlights it.** Select some text, click "Add comment", and the text gets a yellow highlight. The Comments panel opens with that comment's card ready for you to type into.
- **The "Add a comment" box in the panel does the same** when text is selected. With nothing selected it still makes a sticky note, like before.
- **A small toolbar shows up over a selected highlight**, with Reply, Colour and Delete. Delete is greyed out if the comment is locked or the PDF doesn't allow commenting. It also works on underline, strikethrough and squiggly comments.

The cause: the "Add comment" button opened the sticky-note editor, and the panel box always made a sticky note. The PDF engine already knew how to save a highlight with a comment attached, so I didn't touch the engine or the save code. Everything is in `crates/ui-egui`.

## Before and after

Both screenshots use the same small test PDF and the same steps: select the first sentence, click "Add comment", type "hi".

**Before (`main`):** a sticky note at the end of the line. The sentence isn't marked.

![Before: sticky note at the end of the line](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lepotatoguy/pdfcraft/5cccad14/pr-1/before.png)

**After (this branch):** the sentence is highlighted, the toolbar sits above it, and the comment shows in the panel.

title: Native macOS menu bar, and an optional Discord button
author: RiccardoTancredi
body:
## Native macOS menu bar, and an optional Discord button

### What
- A real macOS menu bar (**PdfCraft, File, Edit, View, Go, Pages, Window, Help**), built with `muda`, driven by the existing command registry (`pdfcraft_engine::commands`) so labels, enablement, shortcuts and i18n all come from one source. Go collects page navigation; Window and Help use the standard AppKit roles.
- A **`show_discord`** preference (off by default) that hides the title-bar Discord button and the Home community card. Help ▸ Join the ArtCraft Discord stays either way. Added to Preferences, persisted, with translations.

### Why
On macOS the app had only the in-window menu; this adds the system menu bar users expect. The Discord toggle is opt-in and changes no default behaviour for people who want the button.

### How it stays safe
- Menu items carry **no key equivalents**: the keyboard keeps flowing through egui, so text fields, form fields and the `⌘W` rule in `registry_shortcuts` are unchanged — a menu never steals a key.
- The menu bar is macOS-only (`#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`); other targets are untouched. No `unsafe` (muda wraps AppKit; `objc2` only for `MainThreadMarker`).
- `show_discord` is persisted outside the `json!` macro because that macro was already at the recursion limit.

### Tests
- `native_menu_tests`: every enabled menu command runs on a document (nothing is dead or unknown), and the bar names only registered commands.
- Discord toggle: round-trips through persist/restore, and is hidden by default; the title-bar layout test opts the button back in.

### Notes for maintainers
- Happy to **split into two PRs** (menu bar / Discord toggle) if you prefer — they're independent.
- Branched from `7437bde`; `main` moves fast, so I'll rebase on request.
- New dependency: `muda` (macOS target only), already pulling the same `objc2`/`objc2-app-kit` as the tree.

title: Support PDF page paper sizes and refresh CLI extraction fixtures
author: YouseifUS
body:
## What this changes

Print can use the current PDF page as its paper size, including custom label/envelope sizes. **Match page at 100%** selects Actual size and Auto orientation; `doc_print` exposes the same choice as `paper: "page"` using the first selected page. One paper size applies to the job. This is a partial implementation of #1931; physical printer validation and per-page printer-media selection remain outstanding.

The refresh retains main's raster printing, label layout, A6 presets and localized paper names. Custom PDF paper no longer sends the previous preset's CUPS media override; matching media must be selected in the driver. Its regression failed before this correction and passes afterward.

CLI extraction fixtures express required xref spaces inside escaped strings. The generated PDF bytes were independently compared against main for page counts 0 through 8 and are identical.

## Why the branch was refreshed

title: M2: clip intersection starts its row walk at the first shared row
author: cyfung1031
body:
## What this changes

`clip::intersect` in `vendor/vello_common/src/clip.rs` starts its row walk at the earlier of the two paths' first rows (`min`), so every path walks every row from the top of the clip down to its own rows. A row where one path has no strips produces no output, and the comment above the walk already says rows outside either path's bounds are ignored. The change starts the walk at the later of the two first rows (`max`). It is one line. The rows it skips contain no strips from either path, so the strips and the pixels are unchanged.

The vendored crate is vello_common 0.0.8, which `hayro`'s `vello_cpu` pins. Upstream releases 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 already start at the later row (`let mut cur_y = path_1_start_y.max(path_2_start_y);`, line 366 in both), so this backports their fix. Upgrading `vello_cpu` would be a larger migration, which this PR does not attempt.

On the A1 sample from [storytold/pdfcraft#623](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/623), the walk was most of the stroke rasterization: in one sampled full-page render, `clip::intersect` accounted for 513 of the 690 samples taken in the stroke path.

The crate is vendored as the other patched crates are: the PR adds the whole vello_common 0.0.8 source tree (45 files, about 15.8k lines, upstream licence files unchanged), so most of the diff is that copy. Besides the one-line change, the PR adds a test-only row counter and the test that reads it, the `vendor/README.md` row for the crate, the `ATTRIBUTION.toml` entry for the crate's reference image (see Provenance), and the path entry for `vello_common` in `Cargo.lock`.

## How you verified it

**Setup.** macOS on an 8-core Apple-silicon Mac, release builds without debuginfo, 7 render workers (the engine's count). Input: `demo_heavy_engineering_A1.pdf` from #623, page 1. The timing harness is [storytold/pdfcraft#2042](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2042). It replays the requests the canvas makes: fit width, backdrop, thumbnail,…

title: fix(render): a Multiply highlight inside a transparency group keeps the text (#1968)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1968.

The highlight appearance Foxit and other editors write is a transparency group (`/Group << /S /Transparency >>`, not isolated) whose content is filled with `/BM /Multiply`. Every `/Group` form got a vello layer of its own, so the Multiply blended with that layer's transparent backdrop instead of the text, and the layer was then composited over the page as an opaque yellow block.

Vendored hayro-interpret patch (28), `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/x_object.rs`: a group that is neither isolated nor knockout composites its elements with the backdrop already on the page (ISO 32000-2 §11.4.7). When such a group is entered at full opacity, with no soft mask and Normal blending, a layer has nothing to add, so its content is drawn straight onto the page and a blend mode inside it sees the page. `/I` and `/K` are now read from the group dictionary (both default false). An isolated group starts from a blank backdrop by definition and keeps its layer; so do a knockout group and a group entered at partial opacity, under a soft mask or with a blend mode on the group itself (for those, elements still composite against a blank backdrop, an approximation that `parity/` now states).

This fixes the group, not the highlight: the same appearance drawn from page content with `Do`, or any other annotation (a stamp, a free text) that multiplies inside a non-isolated group, draws the same way. #2025 takes a different route for the same issue, wrapping every Highlight annotation's appearance in a Multiply group from the annotation code; the two are independent and the maintainer can pick either.

title: fix(engine): Save writes a repaired file in full even without edits (#1937)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1937.

A damaged file is repaired on open (the cross-reference index rebuilt from object headers, as Document Properties ▸ Repairs reports), but Save wrote the file back exactly as it was: `Session::save_bytes` returns the bytes as opened whenever nothing was edited, and a repair is not an edit. So the "repaired" file on disk was still the damaged one, and opening it again repaired it again.

- `pdfcraft-engine`: `save_bytes` writes a reconstructed document in full even when it has no edits. `write_incremental` already does that rewrite for a reconstructed document (there is no cross-reference chain to append to); the short cut in front of it was what skipped it.
- `pdfcraft-cos`: `Document::reconstructed()` names the condition (no revision chain: rebuilt from object headers, or built from scratch with `new_empty`), and `write_incremental` uses it too, so the writer and the engine agree on one definition.
- `parity/`: `core.repair-broken-files` cites the tests and says that a repair still does not count as an unsaved change, so closing the document does not offer to save the repaired file.

title: M2: copy Flate back-references in runs
author: cyfung1031
body:
## What this changes

The streaming Flate decoder in the vendored `hayro-syntax` decodes the page content stream. It copied each back-reference one byte at a time, through a checked index and a push per byte. It now copies in runs of up to the reference's distance. The bytes written are the same: a run reads only bytes already in the output, and a reference whose source does not exist still writes nothing.

Effect on `demo_heavy_engineering_A1.pdf` (the synthetic A1 sheet from https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/623, page 1; the timing harness is storytold/pdfcraft#2042), against `origin/main` 3f044b62:

- Fit-width page: 9.72 s to 9.63 s, faster in 7 of 7 pairs (p = 0.016).
- Thumbnail: 6.35 s to 6.21 s, faster in 6 of 7 pairs (p = 0.125, not significant).
- Peak memory: unchanged within noise (about 43 MB for the tile, 568 MB for the fit page).

The gain is modest because inflate is one part of a request's fixed cost. It is taken without changing the output.

title: Linux/BSD: open files from later launches in the running PdfCraft (#1726)
author: tydude001
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1726. The single-instance handoff from #282 and #715 only runs on Windows. On every other platform `claim()`
returns `Claim::Alone`, so on Linux each `xdg-open` or file-manager open starts another process with its own window.
@chilllla traced this in the issue.

Linux and the BSDs now use the same exchange: the same request line and `ok` reply, the same election lock for launches
that start together, and the same stale-socket recovery. The socket comes from `std::os::unix::net`, so there's no new
dependency for it, and only the Windows code still uses `uds_windows`.

- **Where the socket lives.** `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pdfcraft/instance-<display>.sock`. That folder is the user's own
  (mode 0700, per the XDG base directory spec), so no other account can listen there or send files in. Without
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` the launch keeps today's behaviour, and the socket never falls back to `/tmp`.
- **One socket per display.** The name comes from `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, else `DISPLAY`, so a launch on another seat, a
  nested compositor or a forwarded X display opens its own window there, the way the Windows socket is kept per session.
- **Flatpak.** All runs of the app share its `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, and the socket is a file, so the handoff works
  without `--share=network`, which the manifest leaves out on purpose. This matters for the second report in #1726.
- **Bringing the window forward.** winit's `focus_window` does nothing on Wayland, so on a native Wayland window the
  handoff also sends `RequestUserAttention(Informational)` (an xdg-activation request). Desktops show that in the
  taskbar. X11 still gets `Focus` only. Telling Wayland and X11 apart uses `raw-window-handle`, which is already in
  the tree through winit and eframe; it's added under `cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))`.
- macOS is unchanged (Apple events), as are `--new-window`, any other option, launches with no files and every
  failure path.

title: fix(forms): read each JavaScript name tree node once
author: Dev-next-gen
body:
## What this changes

`document_scripts_named` walked the `/Names /JavaScript` tree by resolving and deep-cloning every kid onto its stack before looking at it. The 10,000 cap counted nodes taken off the stack, not what went on it, so a node whose `/Kids` lists itself 1000 times pushed 1000 full copies of itself per visit. On a 6.5 KB file, `pdfcraft-cli run` (`doc_open`, then `js_document_scripts`) used up an 8 GB address space in 8 seconds and aborted with `memory allocation of 48000 bytes failed`. The same walk runs when a field edit sets up the script runner, and an allocation abort is not caught by `catch_unwind`. A tree that lists a leaf twice also returned its script twice.

Kids now stay unresolved on the stack and references already read are skipped, as the `/Dests` walker in `organize/src/outline.rs` does. The cap stays.

## How you verified it

- New test `document_scripts_read_each_name_tree_node_once`: fails before the fix (the `init` script comes back thousands of times), passes after.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms --lib`: 68 passed.
- The 6.5 KB file through `pdfcraft-cli run`: aborted after 8 s before, returns one script instantly after.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests
- [x] Recursion is bounded
- [x] No `unsafe`
- [x] Any crash this fixes has a small synthetic regression test

Found by a defect-hunting pipeline I build and run ([Dev-next-gen](https://github.com/Dev-next-gen)), using Claude Code with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5.

title: feat(ui): the tab strip as the title bar on Windows, by preference
author: rolim-gabriel
body:
## What this changes

On Windows the system title bar sat above the tab strip, a row carrying nothing but the window buttons. GNOME on Wayland already gets the strip as the header bar (`window_controls`); Windows now gets the same when Preferences ▸ Use system title bar is turned **off**. It stays **on by default** there, so nothing changes for anyone until they ask.

- The buttons take the shape of Windows' caption buttons: flat, 46 px wide, the strip's full height, flush with the window's edge, the close button red on hover (`window_controls::Style`). Adwaita's circles stay for GNOME.
- winit keeps the styles an undecorated window needs for Aero Snap, caption drag and edge resizing, and egui-winit turns the undecorated shadow on, so the app's hairline border is left off on Windows.
- The launcher now reads the saved preference from `app.ron` before it creates the window, so the window opens with the right frame on every platform instead of switching on its first frame. (On Windows, with the system frame as the default, every launch would otherwise have switched. GNOME users with Use system title bar on get the same fix.) This adds `ron` to the app crate, which eframe already pulls in.
- The preference's tip states the one thing that needs the system title bar: the Windows 11 Snap Layouts flyout over the maximize button.

author: rolim-gabriel

With the strip standing in for the title bar (GNOME, and Windows after #2043 or with `PDFCRAFT_TITLEBAR=app`) a window carries no name at all, as a browser's does not. Preferences ▸ **Show in the tab strip** puts one back for those who want it: Nothing (the default), Logo, Name, or Logo and name, at the strip's left end before Home. The logo is PdfCraft's own icon unless the user chooses a PNG or SVG file of their own; the name is PdfCraft unless they type one. Works on every platform, whatever draws the frame.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/brand.rs`: the preference, its JSON (`"brand": {show, name, logo}`, one key, because `json!` in `persist` is at the compiler's recursion limit), and the loading. A user's logo is read once and kept as a texture; a file that cannot be read or decoded leaves PdfCraft's own logo in place and logs why, so a broken path never leaves a hole. PNG decodes through the `png` crate already in the tree (any colour type, capped at 2048 px a side, format detected by content not extension); SVG through egui's loader.
- The widgets sense nothing, so the strip's drag passes through them; a wide logo is capped at six times the strip's height so it cannot push the tabs away; the name is cut at 60 characters.

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

The `pdf()` fixture in `crates/automation/tests/batch.rs` now builds its document on a fixed clock (`Session::with_clock`, as the engine tests do).

With the system clock, every call to `pdf()` stamps the current second into the file's dates, so two calls a second apart differ by one byte inside the compressed object stream. Two tests compare a batch output with a *fresh* `pdf()`:

- `explicit_file_can_write_a_numbered_copy_beside_its_source` (`batch.rs:114`)
- `batch_output_collisions_are_safe_under_concurrent_writers` (`batch.rs:209`)

Whenever a second boundary falls between writing the fixture and the comparison, they fail. That happens on the slower Windows runner: `test (windows-latest)` was red on these two tests in #1943 (run 38490938111), and the same tests failed in runs 38478046165, 38473911806 and 38468313812 of other PRs. The failing byte arrays in those logs are identical except for one byte of the object stream and its Adler-32 tail, which is a one-digit change in a date.

No product code changes.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation -j 2 --test batch` (8 passed)

**Proof of the cause.** A probe test that calls the old `pdf()` twice with a 1.1 s sleep in between fails with `assertion left == right failed` and the same single-byte difference as the CI logs; with `with_clock(|| 1_700_000_000)` the same probe passes. (The probe is not committed: a test that sleeps for a second has no place in the suite; the fix is in the helper every test shares.)

title: fix(fill-sign): place image signatures at the physical size their PNG states
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2061.

Thanks for the very precise report and the measurements. `SignatureImage::from_bytes` re-encoded the imported image without its PNG `pHYs`, and `SignatureImage::rect` always fitted it into the 150 x 32 pt box (24 pt for initials), so a 10 mm and a 50 mm seal both landed at 32 pt. Now the normalized PNG keeps the density (rescaled when a large source is scaled down to the 4-megapixel limit, and carried through the white-background clean-up the signature pad applies), so saved signatures keep it across restarts too, and `rect` places such an image at its physical size, scaled down in proportion when it is bigger than the page. Aspect ratio and alpha are unchanged. Images that state no density (no `pHYs`, a `pHYs` in unknown units, or a JPEG) keep today's 150 x 32 pt box: that is the documented fallback, written in the `rect` doc comment and in the parity notes. GUI and `fill_sign_add` share `rect`, so both get it.

Two things I left out on purpose, happy to add either:
- an explicit "original size" on/off choice in the Image tab, in case you'd rather keep the box as the default;
- JPEG JFIF/EXIF density: `pdfcraft-create` already parses JFIF, but many cameras and editors write a default 72 dpi there, which would place a phone photo at a very large size, so it felt like your call.

One visible change to call out: many tools write a default pHYs of 72 dpi, so a large PNG saved that way is now placed at 1 px = 1 pt (scaled down to fit the page) instead of going into the envelope. If you'd rather be safe there, I can treat 72/96 dpi as "no real density" and keep the envelope for those, or put the physical size behind an explicit option.

Rebased on main. `form.fill-sign-signature` in `parity/acrobat-features.toml` currently has `evidence` and `notes` twice on main (left by a merge), which is where this conflicted; the rebase keeps one merged pair, the same text #2419 (mtlcl410) proposes for it, so whichever lands second rebases trivially. `cargo xtask parity…

title: M3: draw Chinese file names with installed Hans/Hant faces on every language
author: zsy-arch
body:
## What this changes

Chinese PDF file names showed boxes for Simplified-only characters on every non-Chinese interface language (简历v5.pdf drew □□v5…). File names and document titles are content, not interface text, but the installed Han faces were only loaded when the interface language itself was Chinese — and the embedded craft-fonts faces are Japanese-only (the Hans face is barred, AGENTS.md §1.1), so Simplified-only characters had no face at all. The craft-fonts Hans face itself remains gap 5, and machines without an installed Chinese face — Linux, Flatpak — still need it.

Now the installed Hans and Hant faces join every font stack whatever the interface language is:

- the interface language's own region sits **before** the Japanese faces (one baseline per line for interface text);
- the other region sits **after** them and only draws characters they lack;
- with a `Hans` craft-fonts face embedded, Simplified is covered and only the Traditional face is added;
- the general installed face (`Need::Other`, Arabic probe) now only ends stacks, instead of sometimes being a Han face.

author: haisondb35-blip

Text that WinAnsiEncoding can't hold (Vietnamese `ạ ế ơ ư đ`, Central European, Greek, Cyrillic) used to be refused by Add Text ("only Western European characters can be written there for now"). title: M3: full screen shows one fitted page at a time, as Acrobat's Full Screen Mode (#1459)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1459. Refs #379, #1353.

Full Screen Mode (⌘L / Ctrl+L) now behaves like Acrobat's: the page on black and nothing else, one page at a time fitted to the screen, turned by a click or the keys. Before, full screen only hid the window chrome and kept the layout as it was, so a slide deck in continuous view scrolled past with the quick tools still on top and the page not filling the screen (#1459).

- In full screen: the backdrop is black, the quick tools are not drawn, a click on the page goes forward and a shift-click back (unless the click opened a link, or a double-click selected a word), and Space, Enter and Backspace turn pages alongside the arrows and Page Up/Down that already did where nothing scrolls. Esc leaves as before.
- `parity/`: `view.full-screen` cites the new tests and says what is still missing; `view.full-screen-presentation` becomes partial (click to advance); `docs/ui-parity.md` and the ROADMAP progress log updated.

title: M4: read page transitions and display times (/Trans, /Dur) into DocInfo
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #379 (the transitions it asks for) and #2070 (full screen as a presentation).

Reads each page's presentation settings from the file, ISO 32000-2 §12.4.4: the `/Trans` dictionary (style, `/D` duration, `/Dm` dimension, `/M` motion, `/Di` direction, `/SS` Fly scale, `/B` backdrop) and the `/Dur` display time. This is the data a full-screen presentation needs to play transitions and auto-advance; playing them is a later PR on top of #2070, and the dialog that sets them later still.

- `pdfcraft-render`: `DocInfo::transitions`, a `PageTransition` per page that carries `/Trans` or `/Dur` (in page order), with `TransitionStyle` for the twelve styles of table 164. Lenient as the rest of `inspect` is: an unknown style is `R` (the spec's default), a non-numeric or negative `/D` the default second, a `/Di` outside 0/90/180/270/315 falls back to 0, a bad `/Dm` or `/M` to horizontal/inward, a negative `/Dur` means no display time. Bounded by the page count; an indirect `/Trans` is resolved like any other dictionary.
- `pdfcraft-automation`: `doc_info` lists them under `transitions` (1-based `page`, `style` null for a display time alone); the tool description names them.

title: fix(render): whole-word find matches inside Chinese, Japanese and Thai text
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Find with **Whole words only** never matched inside Chinese, Japanese or Thai text: a word boundary was "the neighbouring character is not alphanumeric", and Han, kana and Thai letters are alphanumeric, so `台北` was not found in `台北市` and `PDF` not in `的PDF檔`. Those scripts write no spaces between words, so a neighbouring letter of theirs says nothing about where a word ends. Acrobat finds `台北` in `台北市` with the option on.

- `pdfcraft-render` `PageText::find_opts_limited`: a neighbour bounds the match only when it is a letter of a script that puts spaces between words. `unspaced_script` names the others by Unicode block: CJK ideographs (unified, extensions A to G, compatibility, radicals, 々〆〇), hiragana, katakana (including halfwidth and phonetic extensions), bopomofo, Thai, Lao, Myanmar, Khmer, Tibetan. Latin neighbours behave as before: `cat` is still not a whole word in `category`.
- The find bar, the Search panel, `text_find` and the redaction word search all go through this function, so they agree.
- `parity/`: `view.find-options` says so and cites the test.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render -j 2 --lib` (272 passed)

**Test** `text::tests::whole_words_ignore_neighbours_in_scripts_written_without_spaces`: one run `台北市的PDF檔案` then `category`, and a second page with Thai and kana. With whole words on: `台北` → `0..2`, `北市` → `1..3`, `PDF` → `4..7`, `pdf檔` → `4..8`, `category` found, `cat` not; `ไทย` inside `ภาษาไทย`, `カタカナ` inside `ひらがなとカタカナ`. With the boundary rule reverted to plain `is_alphanumeric`, the test fails at its first assertion (`台北` finds nothing).

title: M4: custom document properties through the engine and the tools
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Custom document properties (Acrobat's Document Properties ▸ Custom: name/value pairs kept in `/Info` beside the standard entries), through the engine and the tools. The dialog's Custom tab is a follow-up, after #2012 lands on `dialogs.rs`.

- `pdfcraft-organize`: `custom_info` lists every `/Info` entry whose key the spec does not name (`STANDARD_INFO_KEYS`, table 349) and whose value is text, at most 256. `check_custom_key` applies the rules Acrobat applies to a custom name: not a standard name, not empty, at most 127 bytes (the name length every reader must accept, Annex C), and none of whitespace, the delimiters `()<>[]{}/%` or `#`, so the name reads the same everywhere. `set_info` runs that check for any non-standard key, so a custom entry is set and cleared exactly as Title and Author are (and undone as one step, labelled "Change {key}" as before).
- `pdfcraft-render`: `DocInfo::custom`, the same list from inspection, so an opened file shows its custom entries at once.
- `pdfcraft-engine`: `Document::custom_info`, and the metadata refresh after an edit keeps `info.custom` current.
- `pdfcraft-automation`: `doc_info` lists them under `custom` (`name`, `value`), and `doc_set_info`'s description says custom names are accepted and how they are checked. `pdfcraft-cli info` adds a `custom_properties` count.
- `parity/`: `organize.custom-properties` becomes partial with what is still missing (the Custom tab; mirroring into XMP `pdfx:` as Acrobat does).

## How you verified it

title: M12: the geometry of page transitions (ISO 32000-2 table 164)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #379 (fades and transitions in full screen), #2070 (full screen as a presentation), #2074 and #2083 (reading and setting `/Trans`).

The geometry of page transitions, ISO 32000-2 §12.4.4 table 164, as a pure module `pdfcraft_render::transition`: given an `Effect` (a style with the entries it reads) and a progress `t` from 0 to 1, `frame` returns which parts of the outgoing and the incoming page to paint, where, and how opaque, in page fractions. Nothing here touches pixels, time or the UI; the full-screen presentation will paint from it when it plays transitions (a later PR on top of #2070), and `Effect::from_parts` is the bridge from a read `/Trans` dictionary.

title: M9: sign every page with one digital signature, repeat Fill & Sign signatures, trust Windows roots
author: mendax-iitm
body:
## What this changes

Three signing additions, aimed at people who sign every page of a document, as is common with Indian DSC USB tokens (ePass2003, ProxKey, mToken) and as Foxit's paid tier does.

1. **One digital signature shown on a page range.** The Sign as dialog gets **Show on other pages too**, with the existing page-range control (all pages / from–to / odd / even). It creates **one** signature, with one CMS and one PIN prompt. The signature field gets one widget per page (`/Kids`, each with `/Parent`), and every widget shares the same `/AP /N` stream. Each extra widget sits in the same place relative to its page's crop box and keeps the size of the first one. Without the option, the single-page output is byte-for-byte the same merged field-and-widget as before.
   - `pdfcraft-sign`: `SignOptions::also: Vec<(usize, [f64; 4])>`. It skips repeated pages and the signed page itself, refuses pages that don't exist, refuses an invisible signature, and refuses an existing field.
   - `automation`: `sign_document` takes `also_pages` (1-based).
2. **Fill & Sign: Repeat on pages.** After you place a signature or initials, both the Fill & Sign tools panel and the toolbar menu offer **Repeat on pages**. It places the same saved signature in the same place, relative to the crop box, on a page range. All the copies are one `Edit::Batch`, so one Undo removes them.
3. **Windows trusted roots for validation.** At start, the desktop app reads Current User > Trusted Root Certification Authorities and validates signatures against those roots. Before this, a DSC whose CA the token driver installed into Windows always showed as "unknown". The engine now keeps the user's trusted certificates and the OS roots in separate lists. `trusted_certificates()` still returns only the user's list, which is what gets persisted, so OS roots are never saved. The Sign dialog's ID chooser also gets a **Refresh** button, which lists a token that was plugged in after the dialog opened.

title: fix(preflight): don't read font programs or ICC profiles as colour operators
author: CartoDrone
body:
## What this changes

`pdfa_convert` and `pdfa_verify` wrongly report **DeviceCMYK** for any PDF that embeds a TrueType font. As a result, `pdfa_convert 2b` refuses to add the sRGB output intent ("DeviceCMYK is used: it needs a CMYK output intent (not added automatically)"). The output declares PDF/A-2b but isn't compliant: veraPDF fails it on 6.2.4.3 because DeviceRGB is used with no output intent.

**Cause:** `uses_device_colour` (in `crates/preflight/src/lib.rs`) scans every stream without `/Type` or `/Subtype` for `g`/`rg`/`k` tokens. Embedded font programs and ICC profiles have neither key, so stray `k`/`K` bytes inside a font program count as CMYK operators. veraPDF finds no DeviceCMYK anywhere in the affected files. Seen on:
- reports printed to PDF by Chromium (`FontFile2` with `/Length1`);
- PDFs written by WordCraft through krilla (`FontFile2` **without** `/Length1`).

**Fix:** such streams are no longer scanned. They're recognised in two ways:
- by their keys (`/Length1`–`/Length3`, `/N`);
- by reference: whatever a font descriptor's `/FontFile`, `/FontFile2` or `/FontFile3` points at, or an `[/ICCBased …]` colour space. This is needed because some writers omit `/Length1`.

The reference walk is depth-bounded, and nothing in it can panic.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-preflight --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-preflight`, 12 passed
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` / `assets`: not applicable (no crate boundaries or assets touched)

**Tests.** There are two new regression tests, and I checked that each fails without its part of the fix:
- `font_programs_and_icc_profiles_are_not_content` (streams marked by their keys);
- `referenced_font_and_icc_streams_are_not_content_without_marker_keys` (streams found by reference). It also checks that the same bytes in a real page content stream are still detect…

body:

title: fix(organize): keep page labels on their pages when pages are deleted
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2091.

`delete_pages` rebuilds the page tree but never touched `/PageLabels`, whose ranges are keyed by page index. After a delete every range kept its old start, so the labels slid onto other pages and persisted in the saved file, which is why reopening didn't help. A 10-page document labelled `i ii iii 1 2 3 4 A-1 A-2 A-3` read `i ii iii 1 2 3 4 A-1` after deleting pages 5–6. Now each range moves back by the number of deleted pages before it and keeps its first number, so the numbering runs on over the gap (`i ii iii 1 2 A-1 A-2 A-3`), as Acrobat does. A range whose first page was deleted starts on the next page left, and a range left with no pages gives way to the one after it. A label tree that can't be read is left alone, so it never blocks the delete. Insert and move don't touch the labels either; I've kept this PR to deletion, which is what the issue reports.

This only calls `set_page_label_ranges` to write the result, so it doesn't overlap #1959, which changes how that function writes each range.

Validation:
- `organize::tests::deleting_pages_keeps_the_label_ranges_on_their_pages`: fails on main (`["i", "ii", "iii", "1", "2", "3", "4", "A-1"]` after deleting pages 5–6), passes here. It also covers deleting a range's first page and deleting a whole range, each checked again after a full save and reopen
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-organize --lib label`, `--lib delete`, `--lib replace`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-organize --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

I couldn't reproduce the exact `5, 6, 6, 6, 7` from the issue without the original PDF; the test reproduces the labels sliding onto other pages after a delete, which is the cause I found. Insert and import go through a different path and aren't touched here.

title: fix(comments): show comment dates in local time
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2096.

New comments are stamped in UTC (`D:20261014073000Z`), which is a valid PDF date, but `pretty_date` only reformatted the digits and dropped the zone, so the Comments panel and the Properties dialog showed UTC: 8 hours off for the reporter in UTC+8. `pretty_date` now converts a date that carries an offset (`Z`, `+HH'mm'`, `-HH'mm'`) to the local zone before formatting; a date without one is shown as written, since PDF leaves its zone unknown. The conversion lives in `pretty_date_at(s, offset)` so the test can pin it to +08:00 whatever the machine's zone. The local offset comes from `chrono::Local`, like the engine's `local_utc_offset()`. On wasm `pretty_date` has no zone of its own and shows UTC; the browser offset that `Session::with_wall_clock` now injects isn't reachable from `render::inspect`, where comment dates are formatted on open. Threading it through would change `inspect`'s signature, so I left that out; happy to do it as a follow-up if you want wasm to match.

I left the writing side alone: storing UTC with `Z` is correct, and Acrobat shows those in local time too. If you'd rather also write the local offset like Acrobat does (`+08'00'`, as `signing_date` already does), happy to switch.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib inspect::tests::dates_`: `dates_are_shown_in_local_time` fails on main (`2026-10-14 07:30` instead of `15:30`), passes here; ignoring the date's own offset makes it fail again

title: fix(ui): check boxes over text should show the pointing hand, not the I-beam
author: alehel
body: ## What this changes Hovering a check box or radio button that sits on page text showed the text-selection I-beam instead of the pointing hand (Foxit shows the hand). author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2001.

The Print dialog kept its choices only while the app was open (`open_print` rebuilds the draft with `..keep`), and `persist`/`restore` saved none of them, so an office that always prints two-sided or in grayscale set the same options again for every document, worst where another program opens each PDF in a fresh PdfCraft. Following the split proposed in the issue:

| Remembered across restarts | Starts fresh for each job (as before) |
|---|---|
| Two-sided (off / long edge / short edge) | Copies |
| Grayscale | Pages to print (all / current / range / selected) |

title: fix(print): Properties… reads CUPS driver options off the GUI thread, with a deadline for lpoptions (#1818)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1818.

Properties… in the Print dialog (CUPS) called `spool::printer_options` on the GUI thread, and that runs `lpoptions -p queue -l` with `Command::output`, which waits with no deadline: a CUPS that has stopped answering froze the window. Two changes:

- **The read runs off the GUI thread.** The click records a request (`PrintDraft::read_options_for`); `poll_print` starts a thread on the next frame (`read_options_in_background`), the panel says "Reading the printer's settings…" meanwhile, and the options are picked up when they arrive. A read that dies leaves the panel with "This printer offers no settings of its own." rather than waiting; a read a later click superseded is dropped. `PdfCraftApp::options_source` lets a test stand in for the spooler, like `printer_source` does for the printer list.
- **`lpoptions` is given ten seconds.** `spool::output_within(command, limit)` spawns the command with its output on a pipe read by a thread of its own, polls `try_wait`, and at the deadline kills and reaps it, returning `TimedOut`; its output is capped at 4 MiB (the rest drained). `printer_options_via_within` takes the limit, and on a timeout the PPD's own defaults stand, so the dialog still offers the driver's choices. The `printer_options` tool goes through the same path.

Discovery (`lpstat`) is unchanged: it was already read in the background (#1236), and craft-print bounds its own spooler calls.

One UI string, in the 21 catalogues (the literal-coverage tests require it), with `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes updated. `crates/print/README.md`, the parity note on `print.printer-selection`, and the `ROADMAP.md` log.

title: M6: detect a row of comb boxes as one comb text field
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1887.

Detection looked at each drawn box on its own, so a row of comb cells either fit no rule (18 x 22 cells: too tall for a check box, too narrow for a text box) or became one check box per cell (16 x 20). `detect()` now first groups boxes into rows of touching cells of the same size and proposes each row as one field, `Kind::Comb { cells }`, labelled like any text field. When the fields are added, the comb flag and `MaxLen` = cell count are set in the same undoable batch (through `set_props`, which already handles comb), and `form_detect_fields` reports it as `kind: "text"` with `comb: <cells>`. A lone square, squares with a gap between them, and touching squares of different sizes stay check boxes. Thanks @erwanpaccard for the clear repro, and to #93 for already flagging comb boxes as the gap; I also moved them out of "Not yet" in the parity notes.

Rebased on main's scanned-page detection (#1721/#1722): scanned pages go through the same `detect()`, so rows of comb boxes read from the pixels are grouped too, but the tests here cover drawn forms only (boxes found from pixels may not come out exactly the same size). A field on a turned page gets its rotation and the comb flag in the same `SetFieldProps`.

Choices that are yours to make, happy to switch:
- Two touching cells are enough for a comb, since CERFA-style dates split into JJ / MM groups of two. A row of check boxes drawn edge to edge would now become a comb; 3 or 4 would avoid that at the cost of the two-cell date groups.
- A cell is 5 to 30 pt wide, 8 to 40 pt tall and at most 1.2 times as wide as tall: comb cells are square or taller than wide, and this keeps an empty table of wider cells (an attendance sheet of 24 x 18 or 28 x 20 pt cells) out, which the test pins. An empty grid of square cells would still read as one comb per row.
- A row with text inside any of its cells is not a comb (same rule as empty boxes), so its cells fall back to the old behaviour.
