title: fix(sign): a signed page's resources are page content whatever keys a later revision writes (#1787)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1787.

`classify_changes` already judges a signed page and the trailer's `/Info` by the role they held when signed. Everything else a later revision changed went through `change_kind`, which reads the keys of the *new* version: a dictionary carrying `/FT`, `/DR` or `/T` + `/Kids` is a form fill, `/Subtype /Widget` too, `/Type /Annot` + `/Rect` a comment. So an incremental update could rewrite a signed page's indirect `/Resources` dictionary (or its `/Font` dictionary, a font, a graphics state, an XObject), change what the page shows, add `/FT /Tx`, and be reported as a permitted form fill under P=2, P=3 or an approval signature.

- **Roles from the signed object graph** (`signed_page_resources`): from each signed page's `/Resources` (its own or inherited), the resources dictionary and its category dictionaries (`/Font`, `/XObject`, `/ExtGState`, `/ColorSpace`, `/Pattern`, `/Shading`, `/Properties`) are *containers*; everything their entries reach (fonts and their files, XObjects and their own resources, graphics states and soft masks, colour spaces, patterns, shadings, optional-content properties) is content the page draws. The walk is over the signed revision, stops at signed pages and the catalog (back-references), and is bounded by depth (32), objects visited (50,000) and inheritance steps (64); past a bound the rest is judged as before.
- **Classification**: a changed object the page draws is `page content`, whatever keys its new version carries, before any other rule (the DSS rule included: naming a font in `/Certs` does not help). A container that kept every entry it had and only gained names changes nothing the signed content draws (a name unchanged content never uses), so it is judged as before; one that lost or changed an entry is page content.
- Four existing tests rewrote the page's font or its drawn Form XObject and expected the generic `other changes`; they now get the more specific `page content`, still refused at every lev…

title: #1449: open CAdES signature envelopes (.pdf.p7m) read-only, with extraction
author: edurbs
body:
Closes #1449.

A `.pdf.p7m` file — a DER/BER CMS `SignedData` envelope wrapping a whole PDF, the attached CAdES format used for Italy's *firma digitale* — currently falls into the lenient reader's repair path: the `%PDF-` header is found inside the envelope, `startxref` is not, and the user sees "file is broken and repaired" for a perfectly valid document. Worse, the envelope's signature is invisible, so an edit + save silently discards it.

## What this changes

- **Open:** the engine's single open path sniffs the DER envelope (allocation-free, decided from the first bytes — a PDF starts with `%`, DER with a SEQUENCE, so the two are structurally disjoint) and opens the embedded PDF directly. **No repair messages.** One code path serves the GUI, drag-drop, CLI and MCP. On current main's two-phase open model the sniff sits in `OpenContext::prepare_open`, so background opening takes the same branch.
- **Read-only, by construction:** the embedded document has no editor and no path — every edit command refuses with the reason, and Save can never write over the `.p7m` (a read-only document with a path is saved in full to that path, so the path is dropped). The envelope's own bytes are never rewritten.
- **Identified:** a notice bar shows the signer, signing time, and a content-digest check, worded as integrity ("the content matches what was signed") with trust explicitly **not** checked; v1 does no chain/revocation validation. Properties ▸ Advanced lists the details, including how many SignerInfos the envelope carries (one is shown). The inner PDF's own signature banner yields to the envelope bar (that signature stays in the Signatures panel), and inner damage surfaces on the envelope bar through the standard warnings channel.
- **Extract:** `File ▸ Extract the original PDF…` and the notice bar's button open the embedded PDF as a new, editable, unsaved document — `extract_original` in the engine, `doc_extract_original` in the automation table (with optional atomic `out` …

title: fix(render): a soft mask fades a gradient fill again
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2128. Fixes #2200 (same cause, a Word export).

The faded shapes in these slides are gradient fills (axial shading patterns) painted through a luminosity soft mask. Since axial and radial shadings are drawn as native gradients (#1061), vello_cpu 0.0.8 takes its fast path for an opaque gradient on fully covered tiles and copies it straight over, skipping the mask (and a non-Normal blend mode too), so the fade came out solid. Images already dodge the same fast path by declaring themselves transparent while a mask or blend mode is set, but a gradient can't be flagged that way, so in that case the shading is now sampled as a texture, as it was before #1061. Unmasked shadings keep the native path. vello_cpu 0.1 checks the mask in that fast path, so this can go away with the upgrade. Happy to switch to another approach if you'd rather handle it differently.

Validation:
- `raster::tests::soft_mask_applies_to_a_shading_pattern_fill` (a red shading pattern through an alpha mask covering the left half): fails on main (`outside the mask: [255, 0, 0, 255]` instead of white), passes here
- the reporter's file renders both slides like Chrome and macOS Preview now
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib` filtered on gradient / soft_mask / shading, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -p hayro --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: OCR: Downsample to shrinks a page box given in pixels
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1848.

Thanks @ihsanmokhlisse for the detailed write-up, the diagnosis pointed straight at the line. `OcrJob::run` reads a scan at its own resolution clamped to `[1 px/pt, dpi/72]`. When the page box is the image's pixel size (one point per pixel, here 2263 x 3200 pt), 1 px/pt is already the full image, so every "Downsample to" choice gives the same bitmap. The scale now lives in `OcrJob::scale`, and a page larger than a sheet is measured as if it were shrunk to fit one. Floor and cap both scale by `842 / long side`. Pages up to A4 or letter size come out exactly as before, the 1 px/pt floor included. A 2480 x 3508 pt page (A4 at 300 dpi, stored in pixels) now renders at about 595 x 842 at 72 dpi, 1240 x 1754 at 150 dpi, and stays at full size at 300 and 600 dpi. That matches the same scan stored at its real A4 size.

Two choices are yours to make, and I'm happy to switch either one:
- The reference sheet is A4's long side (842 pt) rather than letter's (792 pt) suggested in the issue. With 842, an A4 300 dpi scan stored in pixels keeps its full resolution at the default 300 dpi, and a 1 px/pt A4 page is never shrunk.
- The change only applies to pages with images. A large page without images, such as outlined vector text, still renders at the chosen dpi on its real size, as before.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine --lib ocr::tests::downsample_shrinks_a_page_box_given_in_pixels`: fails on main (`72 dpi, page 0: 2480x3508`), passes here. Dropping the `min(1.0)` on the sheet factor makes it fail again (`72 dpi, page 1: 651x842`, the low-resolution letter page is enlarged)
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine --lib ocr::tests::`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: fix(render): honour soft masks and blend modes on opaque gradients
author: alehel

## What this changes

PowerPoint-exported slides that fade a gradient out through a luminosity soft mask rendered as hard, opaque blocks: the left-hand white-to-blue fade on a title slide became a rectangle, and a white fade over a photo became a grey panel that hid the photo, a banner and icons behind it. title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `pdfcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: pdfcraft`;
  - `conflicts: pdfcraft, pdfcraft-bin, pdfcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.pdfcraft`, not `pdfcraft`.** The AUR already has `pdfcraft`, `pdfcraft-bin` and `pdfcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.7.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `pdfcraft-0.7.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.
- `pacman -Qip` reads the package, and `.PKGINFO` has the expected name, version, x86_64 arch, packager, depend…

title: fix(ui): Preferences ▸ Graphics can start with OpenGL, for displays where Direct3D 12 flickers (VRR)
author: garpu-ng
body:
## What this changes

On Windows, the PdfCraft window flickers on displays with G-SYNC, FreeSync or another variable refresh rate (VRR), most visibly on OLED and VA panels. The flicker follows the pointer, and screen recordings don't show it. Refs #1560, #1719, #1868 (and the same reports on Discord: turning G-SYNC off stops it).

**Cause.** wgpu presents through a Direct3D 12 (DXGI flip-model) swap chain, and the GPU driver gives the focused window that presents through one the display's variable refresh rate. The panel's refresh rate then follows PdfCraft's presents. PdfCraft draws only when something changes, so the rate jumps between almost nothing and the full rate on every pointer move, and these panels change brightness with their refresh rate.

**Fix.** A new **Preferences ▸ Graphics: Auto / OpenGL** setting, which applies from the next start.
- **Auto** keeps today's behaviour: wgpu, with OpenGL as the fallback when wgpu can't start.
- **OpenGL** starts with eframe's glow renderer, which doesn't flicker.
- The renderer has to be chosen before the window exists. `apps/pdfcraft` therefore reads the preference from eframe's `app.ron` (the app's JSON under `pdfcraft`, or the legacy key) before `run_native`. That needs `ron` 0.12, the version eframe's `persistence` feature already pulls in.
- `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER` still wins over the preference. A value that names no renderer leaves the preference in charge.
- The control channel sets it as `renderer` (`auto` or `gl`).
- It is hidden in the web build.

Observed on an RTX 5080 with an AW3425DW QD-OLED (240 Hz, G-SYNC Compatible), running PdfCraft 0.7.1. The same matrix is in `docs/development.md`:

| Renderer | Flicker |
|---|---|
| wgpu, Direct3D 12 (the default) | on every pointer move |
| wgpu, D3D12 through DirectComposition (`WGPU_DX12_PRESENTATION_SYSTEM=visual`) | as much, or more |
| wgpu, D3D12 drawing every frame (a test build) | all the time while the window has focus |
| wgpu, D3D12 without `DXGI_SWAP_C…

title: fix(fonts): keep a subset Type 0 font for glyphs /W leaves to /DW
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1388.

Thanks to @AMJ1308 for the Chrome files, which showed the cause. In a subset Type 0 font, `Metrics::has_glyph` (`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs`) treated every CID without a `/W` entry as missing. Skia leaves out every CID whose width equals `/DW`, though. In the `BAAAAA+ArialMT` subset that covers `x` and `y`, so "Germany" or "Norway", even after deleting words only, went to Helvetica. `/W` alone can't settle the question. PyMuPDF keeps a ToUnicode for the whole face after subsetting, so trusting ToUnicode for unlisted CIDs would draw `.notdef` there instead. For a subset CIDFontType2, a CID that `/W` doesn't list now counts as present when the embedded TrueType program has outline data for its glyph (through `/CIDToGIDMap`). Subsetters keep glyph ids and empty the glyphs they drop: in the attached file, `x` and `y` have outlines and the dropped glyphs are empty.

This fixes the Chrome/Skia case. I don't think it explains the original Georgia report: those PyMuPDF files carry no subset tag, so the rule changed here never applied to them. So this is "Part of" rather than "Fixes".

The program is decoded once per `Metrics::from_dict` call, and only for subset composite fonts. Happy to make it lazy if that matters on large CJK subsets.

Possible follow-ups from the issue that I left out, since they're product choices: embedding a metric-compatible face (Arimo/Tinos/Cousine) instead of non-embedded Helvetica when a substitute is unavoidable, and a persistent note on the edited paragraph saying which font it is set in.

Validation:
- `a_subset_keeps_its_font_for_glyphs_left_to_the_default_width` (fixture built in the test: Skia-style `/W` and `/DW` over the bundled Inter program): fails on main (`substituted: Some("Helvetica")` for "Germany"), passes here. Its `z` case (a ToUnicode entry with no glyph in the program) still substitutes, and fails if unlisted CIDs are trusted on `/DW` alone.

title: fix(ui): a second file dialog waits for the open one instead of being refused
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2150.

Thanks @AMJ1308 for the precise report. `PdfCraftApp::ask` refused any picker request while another panel was open, and the refused request took its closure with it: the reduced bytes from Reduce File Size, Split's folder follow-up, and so on. Now the request waits in a small queue on `Pickers`, with its closure and its document target taken at request time, and `process_picked` shows the next one as soon as the current pick has been handled. A picker asked from a pick's own closure (Merge data, then save the spreadsheet) still comes first, as before. The toast now says the dialog will follow ("Another file dialog is still open. This one will open when it closes.") instead of asking the user to retry.

title: feat(ui): select text across pages by dragging or ⇧-clicking (#527, #2110)
author: Mawfyy
body:
Fixes #527
Fixes #2110

A run of selected text may start on one page and end on another: the anchor stays where the press went down and the head follows the pointer onto whatever page it crosses, so a drag that walks off the bottom of a page keeps selecting, and ⇧-click lands the head on another page. The drag now starts where the press went down rather than where the pointer sits on the frame egui counts it a drag, so a fast flick across the gap in one frame still selects.

Copy, the floating action bar and `ui.state.active.selected_text` carry every page of the run in document order, one line per page break. Marking follows the selection: highlight, underline, strikeout and redact cover every page it spans as one undo step (one Batch edit); a note and a replacement land on the selection's last page, where their composer shows the quads involved. Text layers for every page of a run stay pinned so a selection still copies after scrolling away, and a page changed under it clears it.

Holding a selection drag at the top or bottom edge of the screen pulls the document along (#2110), ramping to full speed at the edge; the wheel already scrolled during a drag (#721) and keeps doing so.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`: all targets green (ui_group 69/69, control 57/57), including new drag/⇧-click/one-undo-marking tests and a control-channel headless drag.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: 0 warnings.
- `cargo xtask parity`: exit 0.
- Docs updated: ROADMAP progress line, `docs/ui-parity.md`, `parity/acrobat-features.toml` (`view.text-select`, `view.copy-text`).

## Notes
- The drag-start hoist to the press origin is a behavior fix in its own right: a fast flick that crosses the page gap in a single frame previously never started the selection.

body:
## What this changes

**Add comment on selected text now highlights the text.** Before, "Add comment" in the text-selection toolbar opened the sticky-note composer and dropped the selection's quads, so the selected text was never marked and a large note icon was placed beside it instead. Acrobat's Comment on a text selection highlights the text and keeps the note on that highlight. It is a fixed 14 px on screen at any zoom, so it covers as little of the surrounding text as possible. The marker is drawn by the viewer only and is not written to the PDF.

- A **single click** on commented text or its marker opens the comment for editing (the existing Edit comment composer). Plain highlights still only select on a click, and sticky notes and other comments keep opening on a double click as before.
- A **right click** on commented text or its marker gives the existing comment menu (Edit text, Reply, Set status, Colour, Delete, Properties…).

title: Save As to another file writes a clean copy without earlier revisions
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2165.

`save_doc_to` took `save_bytes` for Save As too, so the copy was the original file plus one more revision, and a page removed with Delete Pages (or text replaced with Edit Text) was still there in the first one. Save As to a different file now goes through `save_full_bytes`, which already exists and is what `doc_save` in automation does for a new path. Signed documents stay incremental so their signatures keep covering the file, and Save on the same file is unchanged. Thanks @oracola91 for the precise report. `docs/architecture.md` already listed Save As among the full rewrites; I made that line say "to another file, unless the document is signed".

I kept plain Save (⌘S) incremental even for a document that has never been saved, so only an explicit Save As changes; happy to switch it to "any new path" like `doc_save` if you prefer. Options 2 and 3 from the issue (`require_full_save` after removal edits, or a note when the file has earlier revisions) are product calls I left out. The web build's Save As (download / host) is unchanged too.

Validation:
- `save_as_to_a_new_file_drops_earlier_revisions` (tests/editing.rs): fails on main (two `%%EOF`, the deleted page's content still in the file), passes here

title: M1: every PDF leaves the engine checked, and every writer uses one staging-file writer (#2166)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2166 (its second part; the first, comparing the file on disk before Save, the "already open" tab and the recovery store's lock, is a separate change).

Only Save and Save As ran the #1698 check (the saved bytes reopen with their pages) before replacing a file, and only the app and the rooted tools wrote through a staging file. The other writers did neither: Sign & save and the OCR batch in the app, `pdfcraft-cli edit`/`combine`/`extract`/`split` (plain `std::fs::write`, which truncates first, so `--out` naming the input plus a failed write left no good copy), and automation without `--root`.

- **Nothing leaves the engine unchecked.** `write_new`, which every new file goes through (Combine in its three forms, Extract, Split, Create from blank/images/text), now reopens the bytes and checks they show the pages they were built from; `sign`, `timestamp_document` and `embed_ltv` run `check_save` on their output; `ocr::recognize_file` does too. So the app's Sign & save and OCR batch, `doc_sign` and the CLI commands get the check without each caller remembering it. Split by size still measures a part's size with an unchecked write (`write_unchecked`), since nobody writes those bytes.
- **One staging-file writer.** `pdfcraft_platform::staging::write_atomically` (and `write_atomically_with` for tests, with the suffixes and the flush injectable) is the writer; it keeps the macOS fallback to `fsync` where a volume refuses `F_FULLFSYNC`. The desktop app's `write_atomically` and the tools' `write_atomic` are now thin wrappers that keep their staging-name forms, their folder checks and their error wording, so their existing tests (planted names, refused flushes, the dirty-after-failure retry) still hold. The CLI writes its PDFs through it (`write_pdf`), and `edit` runs `check_save` first.

title: fix(ui): mirror the macOS title bar when the traffic lights are on the right (RTL system languages)
author: Yousef-Dev921
body:
## What this changes

On macOS with a **right-to-left system language** (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, …) AppKit lays the traffic lights out from the **right** end of the title bar. That happens even though PdfCraft has no right-to-left localization, and whatever PdfCraft's own interface language is (I checked 0.8.0 in English on an Arabic system: same result). The integrated tab strip (#789 / #1055) always kept its clearance on the left. So:

- the lights covered the **theme** and **keyboard-shortcuts** buttons and crowded **Discord**, so they couldn't be clicked;
- Home sat beside an empty 70 pt gap where the lights would have been.

Before (0.8.0, Arabic system language):

| | Strip |
|---|---|
| Expected left-to-right design | `[● ● ●] [Home] [tabs…] [+ Open] ……… [Discord] [?] [theme]` |
| 0.8.0, RTL system | `[ 70 pt gap ] [Home] [+ Open] ……… [Discord] [?][theme] under [● ● ●]` |
| This PR, RTL system | `[theme] [?] [Discord] ……… [Open +] [tabs…] [Home] [● ● ●]` |

The fix:

1. **Ask the window which side the lights are on** instead of guessing from a language: `NSWindow.windowTitlebarLayoutDirection`, which Apple documents for apps that use `titlebarAppearsTransparent` and put controls under the title bar ("the layout direction may be RTL even in applications that do not have a RTL language localization"). Safe `objc2-app-kit` calls only (same approach as `drag_pointer.rs`), on the main thread, cached in `PdfCraftApp::titlebar_lights_right` once a window has answered. The new features (`NSApplication`, `NSResponder`, `NSWindow`, `NSUserInterfaceLayout`) are already in the tree through winit/rfd, except the empty `NSUserInterfaceLayout` feature.
2. **Mirror the strip** when they are on the right, so the existing design holds with the lights at the other end: Home beside the lights, the tabs reading from the right (the first tab beside Home), then Open; Discord, shortcuts and theme at the far end, in mirrored order. The scroll arrows keep their visual sides.

title: M8: Extract, Split, the first change to a signed document and Remove security say or ask first (#2168)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2168: three prompts before a surprise.

1. **Extract and Split of a protected document say that the new files aren't protected.** Combine already noted it in its list; Extract's toast now ends with "The extracted pages aren't protected: the original's security settings don't carry over." (the separate-files path says it as its own toast), and Split says the same for its parts. Only when the source is encrypted.
2. **The first change to a signed document asks first.** `apply_edit`, the one path every change in the app goes through, keeps the edit in `pending_signed_edit` and opens `Dialog::SignedEdit` when the document has a signed signature and this document's changes haven't been confirmed yet: "This document is signed. A change adds a new version: the signatures stay valid for the version they signed, and viewers will show that the document was changed after signing." A certified document adds what its certification allows (no changes / filling in forms and signing / forms, signing and commenting, from the strictest signed `/DocMDP` P). **Change anyway** makes the change and marks the document (`signed_edits_confirmed`), so its later changes aren't asked about again; **Cancel** (or closing) drops it. Rewrites that would break a signature are still refused by the engine as before; this only comes earlier. Headless tools are not affected.
3. **Remove security asks first.** `protect.remove` opens `Dialog::RemoveSecurity` ("The passwords and the restrictions are removed when you save."); the dialog applies the edit and shows the existing toast. A restricted document still asks for its permissions password first, then this.

title: M9: harden .p12 digital IDs (#1847)
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Part of #1847 (item 4: digital ID files).

## What this changes

- New .p12 files use **600,000** PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 rounds instead of 2048 (OWASP) for the key and the MAC. Existing files still open.

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341). Fixes #1472.

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How you verified it

PdfCraft 0.7.1's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `pdfcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.7.1 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `pdfcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: fix(edit): keep the runs of untouched text between two edits
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2198.

`TextBlock::edited_spans` decides which source run each character of the draft comes from, but it only knew the common prefix and suffix of the old and new text. With two edits in one session (heading, then a paragraph further down, without leaving the editor), everything between them fell in the "changed" middle and inherited the run just before the first edit, so the body took the heading's font and colour on save. Now the texts are aligned word by word with Myers' diff first; each changed stretch keeps the old prefix/suffix rule, so a single edit gives the same result as before (except where repeated words make the alignment ambiguous, and both readings match the text), and untouched words keep their own runs. The diff is bounded at 64 changed words: past that it falls back to the old one-change behaviour, so rewriting a long sentence plus another edit in the same session can still show the bug. The bound keeps it linear, which matters because the inline editor calls this every frame. Happy to switch to a different bound or granularity if you prefer. The editor's live preview uses the same function, so it shows the right styles too.

Validation:
- `unchanged_runs_between_two_edits_keep_their_styles` (edits "About" and "footer" in the mixed-style block in one `replace_block`): fails on main ("Plain bold text." comes back as Courier-Bold in the heading's blue), passes here; with the bound set to 0 it goes red again
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib` filtered on style/region/run/mixed/rich/block/edit/text/line/paragraph/row: all green
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Forms: fields that share a name take the same value
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2214.

Fields duplicated with Duplicate (one parent, several widgets) already shared their value. What didn't work is the other shape the issue describes: separate field dictionaries that repeat the same name, as many writers save "the same field on every page". `set_value_with` filled only the first field with that name, so the other copies kept their old `/V` and appearance in the app and in the saved file. ISO 32000 §12.7.3.1 treats fields with the same fully qualified name as one field, so now the value the first one takes (after its keystroke/validate scripts, which run once) is copied to the other same-named fields of the same type: `/V` (and `/I` for choices) on each field dictionary, and each one's widgets redrawn with its own `/DA`. Check boxes switch to each copy's own on state.

I left two things alone, happy to change either: same-named fields of a different type are not touched, and fields are still listed separately on load rather than merged into one (merging would change `Field.obj` for every consumer, so it felt like a bigger call than this fix).

Validation:
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms --lib fields_sharing_a_name_take_the_same_value`: fails on main (the second `ClientName` field has no `/V` after filling), passes here. It also checks after save and reopen that all three widgets draw the value and both `Agree` check boxes are on.

title: M3: Save asks before writing over a changed file, one tab per file, locked autosaves (#2166)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2166 (its first part; the second, every writer checked and atomic, is #2182).

- **Save asks before writing over a file it did not come from.** The watcher already knew the version PdfCraft last read or wrote, but also recorded a version it found and did not apply (the document had unsaved changes). A separate `basis` stamp now records only the version the document came from (open, reload, Save, Save As), and Save in place compares the file against it, watcher on or off. When something else wrote the file meanwhile, `Dialog::OverwriteChanged` asks: "“{name}” changed on disk after it was opened or last saved. Saving now replaces that newer version with this one." **Save anyway** writes (and what was to follow the save, closing the tab or quitting, follows); **Save as…** keeps the file on disk and asks where to put this version; **Cancel** drops the save. After our own write the file is the document's version again, so the next Save does not ask.
- **The changed-on-disk notice says what each button does:** "Reload shows the new version and drops your unsaved changes; Save replaces it with this version."
- **One file, one tab.** `open_path` (File ▸ Open, drag and drop, the command line, Open Recent, a link to a file) brings the tab already showing that file to the front instead of opening it again, however the path is spelled (`same_file`: equal, or equal once absolute). The tool it was opened for still runs. A file still being opened by the worker is left to that.

The n…

title: fix(cos): find objects a broken cross-reference table leaves out
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1628.

@megaz90 traced their blank pages to a cheap converter: the files show cross-reference warnings, and rewriting them with `qpdf` fixes Combine. Those are files whose xref table leaves objects out. A common case is a subsection numbered one too low (`0 5` followed by the entries of objects 1 to 5), which leaves the last object, often the page's image, with no entry. Another is an in-use entry at offset 0, which the reader sets aside. `Document::load` reads an object with no entry as `null`. The preview still looks right because hayro (like MuPDF and Poppler) rebuilds the table by scanning, but Combine copies the `null`, so the page comes out blank and stays blank after export. #1635 fixed a different cause of the same symptom.

When the table shows one of these inconsistencies (object 0 in use, or an entry set aside with nothing else for its object), `open` now scans the file once for `N G obj` headers. That is the scan `reconstruct` already did, moved into a shared function. Numbers with no entry take the location of their last header, and the repair log says how many were filled. The same index answers entries whose offset is wrong, which before searched the whole file once per object (in the off-by-one case, that is every object). Existing entries are never replaced, so an object freed by an incremental update stays freed. Files with a consistent table don't get scanned. A number that no section lists isn't treated as a sign of damage, because valid files have those (an oversized `/Size`, or xref streams whose `/Index` skips free numbers) and §7.3.10 reads them as null. Only gaps are filled. Free entries stay null even when a body with that number is still in the file. Happy to switch if you'd rather go further.

The opposite off-by-one is handled too (the `free-entry-image.pdf` @jpeskov attached to #1628, which @LabDennis found this PR didn't cover): a subsection that says `1 7` but opens with object 0's free-list head (`0000000000 65535 f`), so ever…

title: fix(redact): size image clearing with checked arithmetic (#2177)
author: atahabilder1
body:
## What this changes

Fixes part 2 of #2177 (Redact: image row sizing). Part 1 (Optimize) is #2178.

Applying a redaction that **partly** covers an image decodes it and clears the covered pixels (`crates/redact/src/image.rs`). The image's `/ICCBased` `/N` comes from the file, was cast with `as usize`, and was multiplied unchecked into the row size:

- `/N 2^60` overflowed `w * ncomp * bpc`. A debug build panics at `image.rs:70`. A release build wraps the row size to 0, truncates the buffer to empty and then indexes `data[0]` out of bounds.
- A negative `/N` wrapped to a huge `usize` the same way.

After this change:
- `/N` must be 1, 3 or 4 (ISO 32000-2 §8.6.5.5). It is read with `usize::try_from`, not `as`.
- `bits_per_pixel`, the row size, the byte total and the bit total (`bytes * 8`) are computed with `checked_mul`. Every bit index in the clearing loop is below the bit total, so the loop arithmetic cannot overflow.
- The pixel writes use `get_mut` instead of `data[byte]`.

An image that fails any check returns `None`. The caller already treats that fail-closed and removes the whole image, as the module doc says it does for images it can't clear. A fully covered image is unaffected: it was already removed without being decoded.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact -j 2`: 41 passed
- [x] `cargo xtask layers` (no violations) and `cargo xtask assets` (ok)

**Tests.** New regression test `a_hostile_icc_component_count_is_refused_not_multiplied_into_a_crash` in `crates/redact/src/tests.rs`. It builds a synthetic 2×1 image whose ICC stream declares `/N` 2^60, -1 or 2, marks half of the image, applies the redaction, and asserts `(images_removed, images_cleared) == (1, 0)` and that the `Do` is gone.

**Seen failing before the fix:** with `image.rs` reverted to `main`, the test panics with `attempt to multiply with overflow` at `crates/redact/src/im…

title: fix(forms): open a text field on press so dragging over it selects text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2213.

A text field's editor only opened on a completed click (`forms_ui::page_input` waited for `resp.clicked()`), so a press that turned into a drag never opened it: the gesture stayed with the page and field 1 got neither focus nor a selection. Text fields now open on the press. The editor didn't exist when the press happened, so on its first frame it puts the caret where the press landed and takes over the drag (`set_dragged_id`); from then on egui's own drag-to-select extends the selection, as in Chrome's PDF viewer and Acrobat. A side effect: a plain click now puts the caret where you clicked instead of at the end, which is also what those viewers do. Happy to switch if you'd rather keep the old caret placement for clicks.

Since the press now commits the previous field, the release of the same gesture must not commit it again, or a value its validation script refuses is validated (and alerted) twice. The click no longer commits or opens a text field when the press already did. It only keeps the new editor focused, because egui can't hit an editor until a frame has laid it out. A refused field that reopens on the press also stays open when that release lands elsewhere.

Validation:
- `forms::dragging_over_another_fields_text_focuses_it_and_selects_from_the_press` (egui_kittest: type into `name`, focus `city`, drag over `name` from inside its first word to past its end): fails on main (focus stays on `city`), passes here; without the caret placement or the drag hand-off it goes red again
- `forms::pressing_another_text_field_validates_the_refused_value_once` (a `qty` field whose script refuses values over 100, then a press and release on another field): one alert, and `qty` stays open with the typed text; committing again on the release turns it red

title: M14: add Catalan interface and date localization
author: guillemvela
body:
## What this changes

Adds Catalan (`ca`, Català) as an interface language and as a date language (Preferences ▸ Interface language / Date format ▸ Language).

- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/ca.tsv`: a 2,592-entry catalog written clean-room from the meaning of the English labels, in standard Catalan computing vocabulary. title: M9: cargo xtask trust-lists builds the EU Trusted Lists file
author: thorstenhirsch
body:
## What this changes

`cargo xtask trust-lists [--out FILE]` builds the file that `sign_trust {"eu_trusted_list": "<path>"}` loads (#622): the certificates of the **granted qualified CA services** (`CA/QC`) of the 30 national EU Trusted Lists, concatenated as DER and sorted, so a rerun with the same lists gives the same bytes. Today that is 875 certificates, 1.4 MB, written to `dist/trust/eutl-qualified-ca.der` (git-ignored).

Refs #775, #87, #824 (qualified signatures show Unknown): with this file loaded through #622, the PDF attached to #775 is Valid.

- CAs that issue only certificates for web site authentication (QWAC CAs, 113 of 977 granted services) are left out: they issue no signing certificates. A service that says nothing about it is kept.
- The UK's frozen list is left out by its scheme territory, not by its address.
- Deterministic, HTTPS only (a list pointed to with `http://` is fetched with `https://`; Slovakia's does), every download capped at 64 MB through a bounded read (whichever curl is installed), each of up to three tries a fresh curl with a fresh buffer, a failed list stops the run and writes nothing.
- Every certificate of an accepted service must be valid base64 and one DER SEQUENCE (what #622's loader requires of an entry), or its list fails, naming the service: the file is complete or not written, and the loader can't call it damaged.

**Order:** this is independent of #622 to build and review, but the file is only useful once #622 (trust lists in `sign_trust`) has landed. Whichever of the two lands second should update the `sign.eutl` entry and the gap-10 wording in `docs/`; I left them alone so the two PRs don't conflict.

title: M8: measure fonts without /Widths with their embedded program (#2130)
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #2130

## What this changes

**Bug:** Find & Redact could leave the last letters of a line on the page and in the saved file.

**Why:** if a font has no `/Widths` it  draws its boxes with the real font's widths but redaction guessed the widths from the font's name. When the guess was too wide. The last letters seemed to fall outside the mark so they were kept. The verify step used the same guess, so it didn't notice.

**Fix:** with no `/Widths`, `Metrics` now reads the widths from the embedded font the same way the renderer does (`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs`). Fonts that have `/Widths` are unchanged.

Two new tests, both using the existing Inter asset. Without the fix, both fail:

- `redact`: only 14 of 21 letters are removed and apply still says OK.

I also checked 13 synthetic PDFs through `pdfcraft-cli`. All now redact the whole phrase.

title: fix(ui): type right-to-left text in display order, keeping typing order (#2101)
author: Mawfyy
body:
Fixes #2101

The line editor, the Add text box and the Fill and Sign type box showed right-to-left text in logical order, left to right: typing `مرحبا سلام` read backwards, and text placed where the words appeared on screen landed somewhere else once the file was saved. The saved PDF already wrote bidi correctly, so the screen and the file disagreed.

egui lays text out left to right and its caret works in the buffer's character order, so the editors now hand it the display-ordered string from a new buffer (`VisualText`) that maps every insertion, deletion, selection, copy and cut back to the paragraph's logical text; the format panel's range styles the logical span it covers. The paragraph editor keeps its per-source-line look by walking the display string with the line each character came from.

`bidi::visual_with_order` is the order map: UAX #9 display order as a strict permutation — bidi controls kept, brackets mirrored, no character gained or dropped.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`: all targets green, including new unit tests (permutation invariants, mid-sentence insert, a selection crossing a run, selection slices/spans) and two control-channel tests that type an Arabic sentence into the real Add text box and Fill & Sign, put the caret at the visual start and retype, asserting the logical text.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: 0 warnings.
- `cargo xtask parity`: exit 0; `edit.add-text`, `edit.rtl-cjk-editing`, `misc.rtl-ui` and `misc.prefs-language` entries updated, ROADMAP progress line added.
- Live app smoke: typing `ا ببببب` draws the logical-first word at the right edge, and the committed, engine-rendered page shows the Home-caret `Z` between the two words.

## Notes
- Hebrew still has no face to draw it in a box: craft-fonts ships no "Hebr"-covering face (separate work, fonts epic).
- Comment composer and interface fields (search, dialogs) keep logical-LTR display; tracked in `misc.rtl-ui`.

title: fix(forms): Tab and Space reach check boxes and radio buttons, and a click focuses them
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2223.

Check boxes and radio buttons were click-only. The form overlay built its Tab order from text, combo and list fields alone and had nothing to show for a focused box, and a click on one (`forms_ui::page_input`) cleared the field focus, which also dropped the text still being typed in the field before it. Now every fillable field is a tab stop, in the same `/Tabs` order. A focused check box or radio button gets the blue focus ring the text fields already have, and an invisible focusable widget over it holds egui's keyboard focus, so Space toggles it and the arrows step through its radio group (selecting as they go, wrapping, and following the group to another page like Tab does) instead of turning the page. The other page keys (Page Up/Down, Home/End, and the arrows on a check box) keep working: `canvas::shortcuts` no longer stands aside for that widget, only for real text input. A box scrolled out of view lets go of the focus (there is no draft to keep), so scrolling back with the arrows doesn't change a radio choice and doesn't pull the keyboard from the find bar. A click toggles the box and focuses it, so Tab goes on from there. When the click also commits typed text, the text edit is applied first and the toggle follows on the next frame; if the field refuses the text, it reopens and the box is left alone. A focused box also draws its new state while the page re-renders (the unbaked overlay used to be skipped for the focused widget).

Two choices that are easy to change: each radio button is its own tab stop, as text fields with several widgets already are (browsers stop once per group), and Space only selects a radio button, as in browsers, while a click on the selected one still turns it off unless the group sets NoToggleToOff. Happy to switch either.

#2213 (my PR for drag-selecting in text fields) touches the same file, in the text-field press and commit code; this one stays out of those paths, so they shouldn't conflict beyond a rebase.

title: Refuse header/footer Bates numbers that would overflow u64
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/edit/src/lib.rs:445` (no existing issue): Header/footer Bates numbering panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' when the start number is near u64::MAX.

## Cause
`add_header_footer` computed each page's Bates number as `bates0 + k as u64`. `bates0` can be any u64 parsed from the template, so a start near u64::MAX with two or more pages overflowed. That panics in debug builds and wraps to 0 in release builds. Page numbers were already checked before drawing, but Bates numbers were not.

## Fix
Before any marks are removed or drawn, `add_header_footer` now checks with `checked_add` that the last selected page's Bates number fits in a u64. If it doesn't, it returns `EditError::Invalid` and leaves the document unchanged. The per-page add also uses `checked_add` instead of a plain `+`.

## Verified
- Regression test `header_bates_start_that_would_overflow_is_refused_without_drawing`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib header_bates_start_that_would_overflow_is_refused_without_drawing`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Page-number handling and the Bates token parsing in `bates_start` are unchanged.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: fix(preflight): read device colour from content operators, not whitespace-split bytes
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

`pdfa_verify` and `pdfa_convert` decide which device colour spaces a document uses by reading its content streams. Until now they found those streams by their dictionaries (no `/Type`, no `/Subtype` other than `/Form`) and split their bytes on whitespace, looking for `g`/`rg`/`k` tokens. That missed real CMYK content and made some up, so a CMYK document could be given an sRGB output intent and pass verification, and an RGB one could be refused it. Fixes #2259.

Now:

- **Content streams are found by role:** the pages' `/Contents` and Type 3 glyph procedures, which only a reference identifies; form XObjects, including the `/Type /XObject` ones that used to be skipped; and streams with a `/BBox` and no `/Subtype`, which covers appearance streams that leave out `/Subtype /Form` and tiling patterns. Mesh shadings carry a `/BBox` too, so they are excluded. Type 3 fonts are found inline in resource dictionaries too, with a depth bound.
- **Each content stream is read with `pdfcraft_content::parse`,** operator by operator: `g`/`G`, `rg`/`RG`, `k`/`K`, `cs`/`CS` with a device space name, and inline images' `/CS` or `/ColorSpace` (`/G`, `/RGB`, `/CMYK`, the full names, or `[/I <base> …]`). The abbreviations only count in inline images; anywhere else `/CMYK` is a resource name.
- **Strings, comments, inline image data, font programs, ICC profiles and shading data are never read as operators.** That also covers what #2089 fixes for font programs and ICC profiles (see below).

`pdfcraft-preflight` now depends on `pdfcraft-content` (L2 → L4, allowed; `cargo xtask layers` passes).

title: M3: screen resolution and ruler calibration for Actual size (#739)
author: aalbertiarchitecte
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #739, and adds a way to measure the right value instead of guessing it.

Actual size and every fixed zoom percentage now scale from a **screen-resolution basis** instead of a fixed 96 dpi. Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ **Screen resolution**:

- **Standard (96 ppi)**: the default and today's behaviour, so nothing changes for anyone who doesn't touch it.
- **Custom: N ppi**: Acrobat's Custom Resolution, in device pixels per inch.
- **Calibrate…**: three lines (the window's whole, half and quarter width, so a short ruler can measure one). The user measures one or more and types the length in their unit; several readings are averaged, and readings more than 2% apart are flagged.

Once calibrated, Actual size shows a page at its real size on the glass (checked on Windows 11: a 100 mm line in a PDF measures 100 mm), and percentages scale from that basis, as measured in #739 (`logical px per PDF point = ppi / 72 × zoom`). Fit modes still fit the window.

**Design.** The resolution is stored as a physical density and divided by the current pixels-per-point when drawing, so a page keeps its size when the OS display scaling or PdfCraft's interface size changes. That differs from Acrobat for a typed Custom value (Acrobat's is a logical ppi); I chose the physical one so a calibration survives a scaling change, and I'm happy to follow your call there.

`canvas::PT` stays the standard basis; `DocView` gains a `pt` field that the app sets every frame from `screen_ppi::basis`, and the eight fixed-percentage uses in `canvas.rs` read it. Setting `screen_ppi` (null = Standard), control option `screen-ppi` (`standard` or a number), dialog `calibrate-screen`.

title: Make a missing external oracle loud instead of a silent pass
author: tanish2k09
body:
## What and why

Every test that wanted an external oracle probed for it by hand and chose for itself what to do when it was missing. The common choice — print a line and return — **reports as a pass**, so a suite with no oracles installed looked exactly like one in which every oracle agreed. 16 such probe sites across 7 files, in three different conventions.

That was not hypothetical. **No CI runner installed `qpdf`**, so `cos/tests/encryption.rs::qpdf_agrees` had never executed on a runner, while `README.md` said saved output was "independently checked with qpdf". For R2–R4 that test is the *only* check of owner-password authentication (Algorithm 7) that does not go through our own code.

This is the same failure class the repo has been bitten by twice before: the confinement test that passed with path resolution switched off, and a background monitor that ran silently for 30 minutes because `jq` was missing.

## What this does

- **`crates/oracle`** (`Class::Testkit`, dev-dependency only) holds the probes — `qpdf()`, `pdftoppm()`, `pdftotext()` — and one rule: a missing oracle is a **declared skip or a failure, never a silent pass**.
- **`PDFCRAFT_ORACLES_REQUIRED`** picks which, on the same convention as the existing `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED`. CI installs `qpdf` and sets it, so a skip notice on a runner is now a red build.
- All four live probe sites migrated: `cos/tests/encryption.rs`, `cos/tests/writer.rs` (×2), `xtask/src/gates.rs::text_oracle`, `organize/src/tests.rs`.
- `README.md`'s two verification claims made precise, and the `core.write-validity` parity note updated — it said "skipped when qpdf is absent", which is no longer how it behaves on CI.

The crate has **no panicking path of its own**; `or_skip!` expands its `assert!` into the caller, which is test code.

## Verification

**The qpdf tests were run against real qpdf (12.4.2) for the first time — they pass.** So the README claim is now both enforced and true, and this PR should not turn CI red.

title: fix(filters): preserve output-limit errors in raw Flate fallback
author: MMexicann
body:
## What this changes

Raw deflate that begins with bytes resembling a zlib header triggers the existing Flate fallback. If that retry exceeds the caller's output budget, the old code replaces its `LimitExceeded` error with the first attempt's corruption error. Strict decoding reports the wrong failure; tolerant decoding accepts an empty partial stream. For example, a one-byte raw stream decoded with a zero-byte budget currently returns `Ok([])` through `Stream::decoded_within`.

Preserve the retry's limit error. Keep the original corruption diagnostic when both attempts are corrupt, and keep successful raw fallback unchanged. The allocation cap already worked; this fixes error propagation and prevents silently accepting an over-budget stream as empty content.

Discovered while reviewing current upstream `9931329b`; no existing issue is linked. Open issues, open PRs (including contributor PRs), and recent commits were checked for overlap. No feature, dependency, asset, or contributor-name record is added.

It catches one today: `clipboard-win` 5.4.1 (through `arboard` and `egui-winit`, on Windows) is yanked; 5.4.2 and 5.4.3 came out on 2026-10-23. The second commit moves `Cargo.lock` to 5.4.3 with `cargo update -p clipboard-win`, which changes only that package.

This PR used to also add `--locked` to the Clippy, test and CLI steps of `ci.yml`. No Rust code changed.

- Rebased on `main` at c894928e.

- `cargo metadata --locked`: `Cargo.lock` matches the manifests.
- Not built on Windows here; `clipboard-win` is a patch release within 5.4.

title: One way to write a synthetic PDF fixture
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Stacked on #2266** — base is `feat/oracles-must-run`, because the layering fix in `c965a7df` is what lets `cos` dev-depend on a `Class::Testkit` crate at all. GitHub will retarget this to `main` when #2266 merges. Review the last commit only.

## What and why

55 files hand-rolled the same serialiser — number the objects, record each one's offset, emit a classic cross-reference table and a trailer — **111 times over**. The object *bodies* are properly the business of the crate under test. The envelope around them is not, and every copy is a place for a fixture to be quietly wrong in a way that makes a test prove less than it appears to.

`docs/gaps.md` gap 12 names "synthetic fixtures" as something the fidelity harness needs, and there was no shared way to make one.

title: redact: clear a scanned page's JPEG image in place instead of blanking the page (#2246)
author: skylartaylor
body:
Fixes #2246.

## Root cause

A scanned page (Brother scanner, ocrmypdf/Tesseract output) is **one full-page `/DCTDecode` (JPEG) image** plus an invisible OCR text layer. `redact`'s in-place image clearing only supported Flate/LZW/ASCII85/ASCIIHex/RunLength (`crates/redact/src/image.rs` allowlist), so a partly-covered JPEG fell through to the fail-closed path in `interp.rs` that **removes the whole `Do`** — and since the one image *is* the whole page, the page comes back blank while the redaction box and (invisible) text layer remain.

## Fix

- A plain `/DCTDecode` image is decoded (via the `image` crate's jpeg feature, already in the tree), the pixels whose centres fall under a redaction region are zeroed, and the result is re-encoded as a **new JPEG** object; the `Do` is repointed at the cleared copy. Everything outside the mark survives.
- Shared pixel-hit helpers now drive both the raw and JPEG paths — `get_mut` + a `MAX_PIXELS` cap, no indexing on input-derived values.
- Fail-closed behaviour unchanged for everything else: JPX/JBIG2/CCITT, CMYK/YCCK JPEG, non-plain filter chains, non-identity `/Decode`, undecodable streams → image removed whole (no residue).
- `/SMask`/`/Mask` preserved.

## The privacy question from the issue

**The OCR text under the mark was already removed** by the text path (`show()` cuts covered glyphs out of `Tj`/`TJ` with an equivalent `TJ` displacement) — verified empirically on the reporter's file: `text_find` of the marked title → 0 matches after apply+save, `text_extract` over the marked rect → empty, raw scan of every decoded stream for the redacted glyphs' codes → no residue, while text right of the mark still matches. So there was no second defect; the new regression test pins the invariant anyway.

## Evidence

- Red/green: with `image.rs` reverted to 0.8.0 and the new test kept, the test fails with exactly the reporter's symptom (`images_removed: 1, images_cleared: 0`); with the fix it passes.
- Reporter's file: pre-fix save = …

title: Measure rendering against Poppler, and turn the pixel test on
author: tanish2k09
body:
## Why

`docs/gaps.md` gap 12: **until rendering is measured, every claim about its quality is a judgement.** Text extraction had an oracle (word-F1 vs `pdftotext`) and written output got qpdf in #2266. Rendering had nothing.

## The metric is the point

A raw pixel-for-pixel comparison is useless here. Two correct renderers disagree on every glyph edge — antialiasing coverage, hinting, subpixel stem placement — so a strict comparison reports a perfect page as badly wrong, and the number tells you nothing about whether a shading is missing.

`pixels::compare` counts a pixel as differing only when it differs from **every** pixel in the other image's 3×3 neighbourhood by more than a tolerance. A one-pixel shift finds a near match next door and is forgiven; a glyph that isn't there has no near match and is counted. It runs in **both directions** and takes the worse, because the one-directional form flatters whichever renderer is blurrier.

## First reading

`cargo xtask render-oracle`, 250 corpus files, page 1, 72 dpi, tolerance 8:

```
229 compared: median 0.89%, mean 2.16%, p90 5.35%
25 within 0.1%; 15 size mismatches, 5 we could not render, 4 Poppler could not
worst:
  84.22%  bug1552113.pdf
  20.11%  bug1743245.pdf
  13.36%  bitmap-refine-template1-tpgron.pdf
  13.01%  bitmap-refine-tpgron.pdf
  12.39%  22060_A1_01_Plans.pdf
   8.79%  ZapfDingbats.pdf
```

It **reports rather than gates** — the corpus isn't fetched on CI, and a first reading of a borrowed renderer is a baseline to improve on, not a bar to clear.

The worst results cluster on JBIG2 `bitmap-*` files (`hayro-jbig2` carries 3 local patches) and on ZapfDingbats. That aims the renderer work at something specific for the first time, which is the whole point of having the number.

## Verification

The metric's correctness lives in unit tests, and they were written to fail first:

- `a_one_pixel_shift_is_forgiven` — a shifted stem scores 0 but still reports `max_delta` 255, the honest signal
- `missing_cont…

title: redact: clear a DCT scan's pixels instead of removing the whole image
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Redacting a scanned PDF blanked the page: the page image is DCT (JPEG) coded, the pixel-clearing path only decoded lossless filters, and its fail-closed fallback removed the whole image. The fix decodes DCT images with the same `image` crate the create path already uses, clears only the pixels whose centres fall under the mark, and writes the result as a Flate image, keeping every other pixel of the scan. DeviceGray and DeviceRGB JPEGs are covered; a JPEG whose size or component count disagrees with the dictionary, or a CMYK JPEG, is still removed as before. A regression test builds a JPEG-backed page, marks the middle, and asserts the image is cleared rather than removed, the page still draws it, the marked pixels are zero, and the border survives.

Fixes #2246

title: render: average a minified 1-bit mask instead of picking strokes away
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A 1-bit source minified by between 1:1 and 2:1 was drawn by picking single source samples, so a one-pixel stroke vanished (Type 3 image-mask glyphs, fax-era and OCR fonts). Decoded image data now carries a `one_bit` flag, set for `/BitsPerComponent 1` images and stencil masks, and a minified 1-bit source and its mask are area-averaged into premultiplied RGBA instead of picked; interpolated and continuous-tone images keep the existing paths and #624's crisp-screenshot rule. The regression test renders a 10×1 `/ImageMask` and a 1-bit DeviceGray image with a one-pixel stroke across 6 device pixels (1.67:1) and requires the stroke to appear as a mid-tone.

Fixes #1700

title: organize: split a combined field/widget so every copied page owns its widget
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A widget that doubles as its own field (`/Subtype /Widget`, no `/Parent`) was copied once and shared between both copies of a repeated page, so only the last page could identify it (its `/P`) and per-page annotation edits were impossible. Page import now splits such a widget into a parent field holding the field keys (name, value, flags) and a widget child holding the annotation keys (rectangle, appearance, page), registers the parent in `/AcroForm /Fields`, and gives every later copy of the page its own widget child in the parent's `/Kids`. The repeated-page independence test no longer exempts own-field widgets, and a new test requires distinct widgets, correct `/P` per page, and one shared parent/value after save and reopen.

Fixes #1810

title: Say what the render-oracle score does and does not mean
author: tanish2k09
body:
Follow-up to #2286, from doing the first thing the new instrument asked for: looking at its most extreme reading.

## The 84% file is Poppler's bug, not ours

`bug1552113.pdf` was the worst of the first 250 at **84.22%**. The cause is Poppler. The file is a 250×50pt page with two lines of Times-Roman and a link annotation whose `/Border` width is **112**. Poppler paints that as a band across the whole page:

| ours | Poppler |
|---|---|
| both lines of text legible, no link border | a solid band over the text, only `isible.` showing |

The fixture is named **"Bug 1552113 - this text should be visible."** In our rendering it is.

So the first correction this PR makes is to the documentation of the number itself: **a high score is a disagreement, not a verdict on us.** Anything at the top of the worst list needs a person to look at both images before it is treated as our bug. That caveat is now in `docs/gaps.md` and the crate README.

## A plausible change the measurement rejected

Poppler synthesises an appearance for an annotation that has none; we draw only what the document carries. (`view.render-annotation-appearances` already records *"Link borders without /AP and printing are not covered yet"* — the oracle independently rediscovered a documented gap, which is a decent validation of it.)

That made `-hide-annotations` look like the obvious way to measure page content alone. So I measured it over the same 250 files:

| | annotations shown | hidden |
|---|---|---|
| median | 0.89% | 0.89% |
| mean | **2.16%** | 2.18% |

title: feat(plugins): sandboxed WebAssembly plug-in host (ABI v1)
author: bonjourjules
body:
## Summary

Adds a generic, sandboxed WebAssembly plug-in system to PdfCraft — the extension mechanism requested in #336 — so third-party authors can ship document tools that users install from a release build, with no repository, terminal or native binary involved.

This deliberately does **not** try to host native Acrobat plug-ins: that needs Adobe's C SDK and unsafe FFI into arbitrary machine code (as noted on #336), and cannot work in the browser build.

## The format follows PhotoCraft / VectorCraft, not a new one

PhotoCraft established a plug-in convention and VectorCraft explicitly follows it. This PR adopts the same arrangement so authors and users see one system across the Craft apps:

- **One `.wasm` file per plug-in**, manifest embedded in the module (no package format, no PdfCraft-specific file extension)
- Same manifest fields (`id`, `name`, `version`, `kind`, `author`, `description`), same `wasmi` sandbox and limits: no host imports, a fresh instance per call, 32 MiB module cap, fuel budget
- Export prefix mirrors the siblings (`pc_*`, `vc_*` → `pdf_*`): `pdf_abi_version`, `pdf_manifest`, `pdf_alloc`, `pdf_run`
- Where PhotoCraft declares a `filter` kind and VectorCraft an `effect` kind, PdfCraft declares `command` (plus its `commands` list): the plug-in receives a JSON document context and answers with a message and host-interpreted actions (`show_message`, `set_document_info`, `open_document`). The host validates everything; the guest cannot touch the document directly.

## What's in the change

- `crates/plugin` — discovery in the per-user `Plugins` folder, install (validated before anything is written, same-id installs replace), uninstall, enable/disable persisted in `disabled.json`
- `crates/plugin-sdk` + `examples/plugins/hello` — a small guest SDK and a generic example plug-in (reports document facts, stamps document info). Its `build.sh` refreshes the checked-in test fixture, the same arrangement as PhotoCraft's example.
- UI — **Menu ▸ Plugin…

title: Pin that every JBIG2 conformance fixture decodes to the same picture
author: tanish2k09
body:
Acting on the render oracle's top finding — and it inverted.

## The JBIG2 cluster is Poppler's bug, not ours

Four JBIG2 fixtures sat at the top of the oracle's disagreement list (13.4%, 13.0%, and a group at exactly 6.86%). `hayro-jbig2` carries local patches, so the obvious reading was that we were wrong.

The 96 `bitmap-*.pdf` corpus files are a **conformance suite**: one small drawing encoded through every corner of JBIG2 — each generic-region template, custom AT pixels, TPGDON and TPGRON, refinement, halftone with and without skip, symbol dictionaries with Huffman tables, MMR, composition operators, random access, unknown-height segments. Those features change how the bytes are *compressed*, not what the picture *is*.

**So a correct decoder renders all 96 identically — a real test with no reference image and no oracle. The suite checks itself.**

| | distinct images across the 96 |
|---|---|
| **ours** | **1** |
| Poppler | **8** |

Poppler draws a **blank page** for the seven halftone-skip and symbol fixtures, and its output *changes when TPGRON is switched on*, which a correct decoder's cannot. Roughly a fifth of its JBIG2 output is wrong.

Confirmed visually on `bitmap-halftone-skip-grid.pdf`: we draw the picture, Poppler produces an empty page.

## What this adds

`crates/render/tests/jbig2_invariants.rs` pins the invariant. It needs no external tool, so it is immune to the oracle problem it was written to resolve. It is `#[ignore]`d and corpus-gated on the existing `pdfcraft-cos` pattern — including that an *unverified* corpus is a failure, not a skip.

On failure it names the odd files out rather than reporting a count, since that is the whole value:

```
JBIG2 coding features must not change the picture, but 1 of 97 fixtures decoded differently:
  1 file(s): ["bug1552113"]
```

That output is from **watching it fail** — I admitted one unrelated file to the set to prove the detection works. My first attempt at a failing probe (treating `-grid` as a codi…

title: edit: commit the open paragraph when a click switches text boxes
author: midasmatterhorn
body:

title: The fonts README still called the standard-14 widths an estimate
author: tanish2k09
body:
Found while orienting for the font work.

F1 replaced the character-class approximation with the published standard-14 metrics, and `helvetica_width` has delegated to `Std14::Helvetica` ever since. The README kept describing it as PdfCraft's own estimate — and, more importantly, said:

> No metrics file or font program from any vendor is bundled

That stopped being true when the generated tables landed. They **are** Adobe-authored non-visual technical data: the item `AGENTS.md` §1.1 permits, carried in `std14_metrics.rs` with `adobe_data = true` in `ATTRIBUTION.toml`.

A contributor reading that README would have concluded there was no vendor data in the crate at all. That is the one kind of error that actually matters in a provenance claim, and it is mine — I left it behind in F1 when I moved the table.

Now says what *is* bundled and what still is not: widths and encodings, never a font program or a typeface.

`fonts` 65 · `fmt` clean. Documentation only.

title: Read WinAnsi 0xAD as a hyphen, so search and redaction can see it
author: tanish2k09
body:
**Needs your reading of the spec before merging — I could not settle it, and the implementations disagree.** Everything else about it is verified.

## The problem

A page that draws a discretionary hyphen through WinAnsiEncoding's `0xAD` extracts, in our map, as **U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN**. That character is invisible. So text the reader can plainly see does not match a search for it, and **`redact`'s pattern matching — which runs on exactly this map** (`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs:1060` says so) — does not match it either.

That is the same silent-failure shape as reading Symbol as Latin in F2: the text is there, the tool cannot see it.

Found by running the text oracle, which has never been run in this repo. `XiaoBiaoSong.pdf` scored word-F1 **0.231** against `pdftotext`, and the entire gap was this one character, 104 times — our output and Poppler's were otherwise character-for-character identical.

## The change

Annex D.2 gives codes `0x2D` and `0xAD` the same glyph name, so the byte a Windows codepage calls a soft hyphen draws, and should extract as, an ordinary hyphen.

Reading table only. **Writing is unaffected**: `win_ansi_byte` maps `0xA0..=0xFF` by identity, so `'-'` still takes the canonical `0x2D` and a caller holding a literal U+00AD still writes the `0xAD` byte — which is the one that draws a hyphen anyway.

The existing round-trip test could no longer hold for that code, since two codes now mean one character. It states the aliasing explicitly rather than asserting a bijection.

## Why it needs you

The evidence is **not unanimous**:

| source | reading |
|---|---|
| a PDF library's docs, citing ISO 32000-1 Annex D.2 | glyph name at `0xAD` is `hyphen` |
| Poppler | extracts **U+002D** |
| vendored hayro | table says `173 => "sfthyphen"`, reports **U+00AD**, normalises to `hyphen` *only* for glyph lookup |

So two implementations disagree, and I cannot read the normative Annex D.2 table from here. The behavioural argument favours U+002D — a redaction tool tha…

title: M10: open Office documents as PDFs through an optional local LibreOffice
author: ArturFaleiros
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft can now open Word (`.docx`, `.doc`), PowerPoint (`.pptx`, `.ppt`), Excel (`.xlsx`, `.xls`), OpenDocument (`.odt`, `.odp`, `.ods`) and `.rtf` files as PDFs. This is the `create.from-office` parity entry ("Create PDF from Office documents (LibreOffice sidecar)").

- **Desktop:** File ▸ Open gets a *Word / PowerPoint / Excel / LibreOffice* filter. The open worker converts in the background, and the result opens as a **new unsaved PDF tab**. The source file is never written, and Save As picks the destination.
- **Automation:** `doc_convert_office { path }` does the same headlessly and returns a new document id, like `doc_create` (CLI `run` and MCP share the table).
- **Converter:** a separately installed LibreOffice. Nothing is bundled, downloaded or started at launch. Standard Windows / macOS / Linux install paths are detected, and `PDFCRAFT_LIBREOFFICE` (an absolute path) overrides them.

How the external process is contained (`crates/platform/src/office.rs`):
- The input is checked by extension *and* magic bytes (OLE2 / ZIP / `{\rtf`), then copied into a fresh temporary directory under a fixed name (`input.<ext>`). The user's filename never reaches the command line.
- Each run gets a fresh `-env:UserInstallation` profile with macro execution off, active content off, untrusted referer links blocked, and Writer/Calc automatic link updates off. `TMP`/`TEMP`/`TMPDIR` point into the temporary directory.
- Limits: 128 MiB input (read with `take`), 256 MiB output, a 120 s deadline. On timeout or drop, the whole process tree is killed (Unix process group / `taskkill /T`). The output must start with `%PDF-`, and it then goes through the normal engine open path, which validates it.
- `--root` sessions refuse the tool **before** resolving or reading the path, because an external program can't inherit the path resolver. The web build returns "requires the desktop app".

The project CI does not install LibreOffice, so the rea…

title: The text oracle scored us zero for honouring a no-copy document
author: tanish2k09
body:
## The problem

A PDF can forbid copying its text. `pdfcraft-cli text` honours that and refuses, naming the owner password as the way through. **pdftotext ignores the flag and extracts anyway.** So the oracle compared our refusal against its text and scored **0.000** — measuring obedience, not quality.

`bug1815476.pdf` is the case: a one-page Spanish form we **render perfectly** but decline to extract. It sat at the bottom of the worst list looking like a font bug, which is exactly what sent me investigating it.

## The fix

Those files are skipped and **counted**, not scored, and the count is printed rather than passed over in silence — the same rule `pdfcraft-oracle` exists for: *a comparison that did not happen must not look like one that succeeded.*

```
text oracle: 19 files with text; median F1 0.991, mean 0.854, p10 0.231
  1 skipped: the document forbids copying its text, which we honour and pdftotext does not
```

Before / after over the first 250 corpus files:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| files compared | 20 | 19 |
| median | 0.991 | 0.991 |
| **mean** | **0.811** | **0.854** |

The gain is entirely the removal of a false negative — no extraction changed.

## Design notes

Permissions come from **`Document::permissions()`**, not from matching our own error string, so the check does not break when the message is reworded. That meant a new `pdfcraft-cos` dependency for `xtask`; `xtask` is `Class::Exempt` so the layering gate is unaffected, and it passes at 37 crates.

A file that cannot be opened at all counts as *permitted*. That is a different problem, and dropping it quietly would hide it.

## Verification

Demonstrated by the before/after run above — the file that motivated the change is gone from the list and accounted for. `xtask` 48 · clippy clean · `fmt` clean · `layers` 37 crates.

title: fix(engine): give a host with no clock or time zone a real one (Session::with_wall_clock)
author: bonfim6P
body:
## What this changes

On `wasm32-unknown-unknown` the engine has neither a clock (`Session::now()` is empty) nor a time zone (`local_utc_offset()` is `0`). In a browser build that means Fill & Sign stamps **1 Jan 1970** and `/ModDate` is never written.

The only way to inject a clock today is `with_clock`, which is a test shortcut: it takes the injected instant **as local time** and zeroes the zone. A host that knows both the UTC time and its zone (a browser does: `Date.now()` and `getTimezoneOffset()`) therefore cannot use it. Inject only the clock and you get either the local dates or the UTC ones wrong by the zone's offset — 21:30 in São Paulo (UTC-3) is already the next day in UTC.

This adds `Session::with_wall_clock(clock, utc_offset)` (and `Automation::with_wall_clock` forwarding to it):

- `clock` is the **UTC** instant in seconds — what the file records (`/M`, `/ModDate`, the signing time).
- `utc_offset` is the local zone's seconds east of UTC, **asked on every use**, because the zone changes with daylight saving.
- `today()`, `signing_date()` and `stamp_by_line()` read the offset through one helper (`local_offset`) instead of three copies of `if self.clock.is_some() { 0 } else { local_utc_offset() }`. The precedence is: an injected zone, else `0` under the test clock (already local), else the system's — so **nothing changes for a native build or for `with_clock`**.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine a_wall_clock` — passes. It pins the contrast at 21:30 on 14 Oct 2026 in São Paulo: the stamped day is the 14th, `signing_date` is `D:20261014213000-03'00'`, `now_secs()` stays `00:30Z` on the 15th, a UTC zone gives the 15th, and the plain test clock still answers the 15th (which is why it can't serve a browser).

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: feat(automation): Automation::render_pixels returns a page as RGBA, without the PNG round trip
author: bonfim6P
body:
## What this changes

`page_render` only returns PNG. A host that paints the page straight onto a canvas (a browser, a GPU texture) encodes a PNG only to decode it again, on every scroll.

`Automation::render_pixels(doc, page, scale)` returns the page as `(width, height, Pixels)` — RGBA, four bytes a pixel — using the same renderer and the same per-document cache as `page_render`. `scale` is pixels per point (1.0 = 72 dpi). `Pixels` is re-exported from the crate root so a caller can name the type. It validates exactly as the tool does: a finite scale within the tool's dpi limit, a 1-based page that exists, a document that is open.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test automation render_pixels` — passes. It checks the size agrees with `page_render` at 72 dpi, that the buffer is RGBA and not blank, that doubling the scale doubles the width, and each refusal (scale `0`, negative, `NaN`, infinite, past the dpi limit; page `0`, past the end; a document that isn't open).
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] tests pass on the crate I changed
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` / `assets` — not touched

**Tests.** The behaviour is new, so there is no "red before the fix"; the refusal cases are the part that pins the validation.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests
- [x] No input-derived indexing; the page count is checked before the page is used; the scale is rejected unless finite and in range, so no NaN/inf reaches the renderer
- [x] No `unsafe`

## Provenance

- [x] No assets, no GPL/AGPL code

## Security
