title: feat(automation): an in-memory disk behind a vfs module, so the tool table runs on wasm32 (RFC)
author: bonfim6P
body:
> **This is a draft, and a request for direction before polish.** It is the most invasive of the three small changes I'd like to upstream (the others are #2317 and #2318), and I'd rather hear whether you want it, and in what shape, than have you review 600 lines you'd have asked me to redo.

## What this changes

On `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `std::fs` compiles and then fails on every call: there is no disk. `pdfcraft-automation`'s tool table reads and writes files in about 40 places (`doc_open`, `doc_save`, `page_insert_file`, the export outputs, the review sidecars…), so a browser host can't use it.

This routes those calls through a new `vfs` module that picks one of two backings:

- **the real disk** (`std::fs`, unchanged) — every native build, by default;
- **an in-memory disk** (path → bytes) — always on for `wasm32`, and, so the layer can be tested natively, behind the `memfs` feature.

A browser host puts the PDF on the in-memory disk, calls the tool, and reads back what it wrote. The whole table works without touching tool by tool. I run the engine this way in a WebAssembly build.

Every call site is a one-for-one swap of `std::fs::*` for `vfs::*`, so a native build behaves as before. Two things that need a real folder switch themselves off on the in-memory disk, with a message that says why: `doc_batch` and `Automation::with_root`. `write_atomic` is a single write there.

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --features memfs --lib vfs` — 3 tests: names and bytes round-trip, `.` and `..` resolve by name and can't climb above the root, a folder isn't overwritten by a file, a file can be removed.

title: fix(optimize): reject hostile image dimensions safely
author: earlvanze
body:
## Problem and fix

Optimize could panic when a PDF image declared hostile dimensions: its pixel byte count multiplied unchecked, and conversions could truncate dimensions. Reject invalid, oversized, or unrepresentable dimensions and use checked byte counts before reading image data. The shared pixel reader also protects the image-fragment optimizer, and malformed soft masks leave their parent images unchanged.

Fixes #2178.

## Validation

- Reproduced the original hostile-dimension regression against current main: integer-overflow panic; it passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize --profile low-disk --locked -j 2` (25 tests passed).
- Strict Clippy for all optimizer targets, workspace formatting, and the optimizer WASM check passed.
- `xtask layers`, `xtask assets`, and `xtask parity` passed.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of images and soft masks with invalid, excessively large, or overflowing dimensions, preventing unsafe decoding and preserving affected content during optimization.

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a right-hand panel in PDFCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the panel says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside PDFCraft and names this app's world — pages and their order, extract/split/combine/rotate, forms and their fields and tab order, redaction that removes content for good, OCR, headers/footers/watermarks, bookmarks and annotations, PDF/A, compression and export — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (organize pages plan, form field advice, redaction checklist, PDF/A and standards advice, compress and export) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent menu or panel names — and redaction's irreversibility is said plainly. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

title: fix(oracle): take clippy's as_chunks hint in decode_pam_gray
author: Hathor875
body:
## What this changes

Unblocks CI on `main`. Clippy 1.99 adds `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, and CI runs `-D warnings`, so the ubuntu and windows test jobs have been failing at the **Clippy** step and never reaching their tests. This affects every PR into `main`, including ones that never touch `pdfcraft-oracle`. It landed with the oracle crate itself (`f988cf87` / `0754740f`).

`decode_pam_gray` is the only `chunks_exact(constant)` in the workspace. Taking the suggested `as_chunks::<4>().0` also lets the pixel be destructured as `&[r, g, b, a]` rather than indexed four times through `?`. Those four unwraps were unreachable — `chunks_exact` only yields full chunks — so the new pattern is infallible rather than merely unlikely to fail. `wanted` is `width * height * 4`, hence a multiple of four, so no remainder is dropped and the output is byte-identical.

This is a behaviour-preserving lint fix only. No test, no parity change.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean (reproduced the failure first, then confirmed it gone)

## Never-crash

title: feat(automation): accessibility_tags lists tags a page at a time, with filters
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`accessibility_tags {doc}` returns every structure tag in one result. On tagged guides printed by Chromium (`page.pdf({tagged: true})`), 20 to 21 pages give 400 to 630 tags and 70,000 to 124,000 characters of JSON, more than an MCP client accepts in one tool result (Claude Code refused it and spilled it to a file). Open PR #1496 adds each tag's text to the listing, so results will grow.

`bookmark_list` already pages. `accessibility_tags` now does the same, and can keep only the tags an agent is after:

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `offset` | where the page starts, from 0 (the previous page's `next`) |
| `limit` | tags in the page, 1 to 1000, default 200 |
| `types` | only these types, as listed in `type` (`["H1", "H2", "H3"]`) |

title: feat(edit): flattening form fields can keep the signature fields
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

A common form workflow: fill it, flatten it so the answers can't be changed, then sign it in the signature box the form already has. `doc_flatten` flattens either every comment or every form field, so the empty signature field goes with the rest, and signing it afterwards fails:

```text
doc_flatten {doc}                          -> fields "name" (text) and "signature" (signature) both gone
sign_document {field: "signature", ...}    -> there is no signature field "signature"
```

The workaround is to note the field's page and rectangle before flattening and sign with `page` + `rect`, which creates a new field.

`doc_flatten` gets `keep_signature_fields` (boolean, default `false`, so nothing changes for existing callers). With it, widgets of signature fields stay on the page and in `/AcroForm /Fields`, and every other field is flattened as before. A widget counts as a signature field by its own `/FT /Sig` or one inherited from its parent fields (followed at most 64 levels). Signed signature fields are kept too: flattening one would drop the signature anyway.

Plumbing:

- `pdfcraft_edit::FlattenOptions` and `flatten_with`; `flatten(doc, pages, comments, fields)` keeps its signature and calls it.
- `Edit::Flatten` gains `keep_signature_fields`; the Action Wizard steps and the interface's Comments ▸ Flatten and Forms ▸ Flatten pass `false` (two one-line changes in `ui-egui/src/commands.rs`).

title: Connect MCP tools to the running PdfCraft window
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli mcp` currently owns a separate engine session. An agent cannot fill the form a person already has open in PdfCraft. `mcp --connect FILE` uses the existing authenticated `--control FILE` channel and runs the same automation table on the window's own session. Document ids, resources, edits and Undo refer to the tabs the person sees. New documents open behind their active tab; rendering and stale selections refresh after changes.

The CLI reuses its control-file ownership/permissions checks and sends tokens only to loopback. Both control and MCP remain opt-in. A lost reply is not replayed automatically, because an edit may already have run; the next call reconnects and rereads the control file. Replies are bounded and checked for matching JSON-RPC ids.

MCP adds read-only `ui_state`, `ui_inspect` and `ui_screenshot`, including in compact mode. It does not expose UI input, which would bypass root confinement and human signing consent. The window refuses tools while a text/comment draft or edit dialog is open. MCP inspection uses protected `tool.inspect`; private signing/password views cannot be inspected or captured through the bridge; password-node values are omitted.

The agent prepares, the person signs. Connected tools refuse all `sign_*`, signature/initials placement, reusable signature-image export, redaction application and tab closure, also through command wrappers. Signing credentials are rejected before relay and again at the window dispatch boundary. Signature fields, ordinary text/dates and redaction marks may be prepared; the person signs or confirms redaction in the app. Existing headless signing remains unchanged.

The automation runner is supplied by the desktop binary, preserving crate layering: ui-egui has no dependency on automation. No provider client, model key, new listener or automatic MCP registration is added.

title: feat(automation): bookmarks and links say where on the page they go
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`bookmark_list` and `link_list` say which page a bookmark or link goes to, but not where on it. An agent checking a table of contents, or rebuilding bookmarks after an edit, can't tell "top of page 2" from "the heading halfway down page 2", and a link through a named destination only gives the name.

Each bookmark row and in-document link now carries `destination`:

| Destination | `destination` |
|---|---|
| `[page /XYZ left top zoom]` | `{"fit": "XYZ", "left", "top", "zoom"}` |
| `/Fit`, `/FitB` | `{"fit": "Fit"}` |
| `/FitH top`, `/FitBH top` | `{"fit": "FitH", "left": null, "top"}` |
| `/FitV left`, `/FitBV left` | `{"fit": "FitV", "left", "top": null}` |
| `/FitR` | `{"fit": "FitR", "rect"}` |

Positions are in points from the top-left of the displayed page, like every `rect` the tools return; `null` where the destination leaves a value unspecified (`/XYZ 72 500 0` keeps the reader's zoom, so `zoom` is `null`). A link whose target is a named destination now resolves it as the viewer does: `to_page`, `destination` and `named: true`, instead of only `other`.

Plumbing: `pdfcraft_organize` reads the explicit destination array behind an explicit, `/D` or named destination (`explicit_dest`, replacing `page_of_dest`) and keeps its type and numbers in `Bookmark::view`; the engine passes it through `BookmarkRow`.

title: fix(engine): a new or recovered document stays unsaved through undo
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**Narrowed after #1435.** This PR first fixed #1310, #1311 and #1312. #1435 (bartalos86) landed a fix for the same three issues today, and three of this PR's four tests pass on `main` as it is, so I've dropped that part. #1310–#1312 can be closed against #1435.

What's left is the case #1435 doesn't cover, and it can lose a whole document:

- **A new or recovered document became clean after undo.** `sync_dirty` calls a document clean when its bytes are the ones last "saved". For a new document (Combine, Extract, Create) or one restored from recovery, those are the bytes it was opened from, which were never written where the document belongs. So edit → Undo made it clean: Close didn't ask to save, and autosave stopped keeping it, so the whole combined or recovered document could be discarded without a prompt.
- **The fix.** `Editor::unsaved_file` is set by `open_new` and `mark_recovered`, and cleared by `mark_saved`. While it's set, the document stays unsaved whatever undo or Revert brings back. Revert now derives `dirty` from the same rule instead of always clearing it.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-engine -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pdfcraft-engine -j 2`
- [x] New `undo_never_makes_an_unsaved_document_clean`. A combined document stays unsaved after edit + Undo (and still gets a recovery snapshot) and after Revert. A recovered document stays unsaved after edit + Undo. Once saved, undo back to the saved state is clean.
- [x] Seen to fail: with `unsaved_file` left out of `sync_dirty`, the first assertion fails.

## Never-crash / Security

- [x] No new `unwrap`/indexing; one boolean on the editor.

title: fix(ui): on macOS, dragging a tab moves the tab, not the window
author: tisca26
body:
## What this changes

On macOS, dragging a document tab to reorder it (#1551) moved the whole window instead. The tab reordering itself worked; the drag just never reached the app. It happens with a held click and with three-finger drag on the trackpad, in v0.8.0.

**Cause.** On macOS the tab strip is the title bar: a transparent title bar over a full-size content view (`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`). For a press in that band, AppKit asks the view under the pointer whether it can move the window (`mouseDownCanMoveWindow`), and NSView answers YES for any view that isn't opaque. winit's `WinitView` doesn't override it, so AppKit started a window drag before egui saw the event. #1551 was verified on Windows, where this doesn't apply.

**Fix.** `vendor/winit` now answers `mouseDownCanMoveWindow` with the window's own `movable_by_window_background` attribute: NO unless an app asked for it (PdfCraft doesn't). PdfCraft already moves the window itself when the drag starts on the strip's empty background (`ViewportCommand::StartDrag` in `chrome.rs`), so that keeps working, and so does double-click to maximize. The value is passed to the view the same way `accepts_first_mouse` is, so it needs no `unsafe` call. Documented as winit patch (12) in `vendor/README.md`.

## How you verified it

On macOS 27.0.1 (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, on `ac89a11`:

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft -j 4 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft --test winit_macos_title_bar_drag` passes, and fails with `vendor/winit` reverted
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` (no crate boundary or asset touched)

By hand with three PDFs open: dragging a tab (held click and three-finger drag) reorders it and the window stays put; dragging the empty part of the strip still moves the window.

**Tests.** `tests/winit_macos_title_bar_drag.rs` follows the other vendored-winit tests: it keeps the patch in the build so a re-vendored winit can't silently br…

title: crypt: authenticate against encryption numbers qpdf wrote (plus one hand-derived vector)
author: amoisttowe1
body:
Test-only. Adds `crates/crypt/tests/qpdf_literals.rs`: three tests, seven vectors. Six quote encryption
dictionaries written by qpdf core 12.2.0 through pikepdf 9.11; the seventh is hand-derived from
ISO 32000-1 at revision 3 with `/Length` 40. Nothing else in the repository changes — this commit is
comments plus one assertion message, its parent is the reviewed head `cdbce8a`, and the push is a
fast-forward.

**Why it matters.** `create()` and `open()` share one key derivation, so a wrong-but-self-consistent
implementation round-trips cleanly. Deleting Algorithm 2 step f from `crates/crypt/src/lib.rs:393` leaves
all 17 unit tests green (`rc=0`) and fails these rows instead, with `#2358`'s property failing alongside
them. Outside numbers test conformance; round trips test only self-agreement. Every R3/R4 vector already
in the repository uses a 16-byte key, so `/Length`/n truncation is invisible in all of them; the
metadata-plain pairing shows step f's four `FF` bytes from outside, and it is the only such case here.

**Reproduction.** One blank 200×200 page, `Encryption(owner=OWNER, user=USER, allow=Permissions(extract=False), R=n)`
then `save(static_id=True)`; read `/Encrypt`. Below R=4 both `aes=False` and `metadata=False` must be
forced — pikepdf checks metadata first (`Cannot encrypt metadata when R < 4`), then AES. Revisions 2 and
3 reproduce as whole files, byte-identical across two days (`63f2d95b…`, `39afbdd5…`). Revision 4
reproduces all eight dictionary fields; its file differs by exactly one 32-byte stream, a fresh AES-CBC IV
(ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4). Revision 6 reproduces structurally, with fresh salts per run; the fixtures its two
rows were copied from were overwritten before archiving, so those rows rest on internal consistency plus
this record. A re-captured pair with retained artifacts can be added on request.

decrypt. No assertion pins crypt-filter nam…

title: Fix util.printd panic on an escaped multi-byte character
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/lib.rs:785` (no existing issue): util.printd panics on a backslash-escaped multi-byte character in the format string.

## Cause
In `util.printd`, the `\` escape branch copied only the first byte after the backslash (`b[i + 1] as char`) and always moved forward by 2 bytes. With a multi-byte UTF-8 character such as 'é' or '€', this wrote the wrong character and left the index in the middle of the character. The next `fmt[i..]` slice then panicked, so the script stopped with an internal error.

## Fix
The escape branch now reads the whole character after the backslash, pushes it, and moves forward by `1 + ch.len_utf8()`. A regression test covers escaped 2-byte, 3-byte and ASCII characters.

## Verified
- Regression test `printd_escapes_multibyte_chars`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js --lib printd_escapes_multibyte_chars`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The other format branches of `printd` and the default branch, which already handles multi-byte characters, are unchanged.

title: Reject impossible dates such as Feb 30 in FormCalc Date2Num and Parse
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:1916` (no existing issue): FormCalc Date2Num accepts impossible dates such as Feb 30 and rolls them into the next month instead of returning 0.

## Cause
FormCalc's `parse_date` only checked that the day was between 1 and 31, without comparing it to the length of the month or allowing for leap years. `Date2Num`, `IsoDate2Num` and `Parse` therefore accepted dates like 2023-02-30, and `days_from_civil` moved the extra days into the next month (2023-02-30 became 2023-03-02) instead of returning 0 or null.

## Fix
`parse_date` now checks the day against a new `days_in(y, m)` helper, which matches the one in the AcroForm date parser and handles leap years. Impossible dates now make Date2Num return 0 and Parse return null, while real month ends like 2024-02-29 still work.

## Verified
- Regression test `date2num_rejects_days_past_the_end_of_the_month`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js --lib date2num_rejects_days_past_the_end_of_the_month`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The AcroForm date parser in crates/forms/src/af.rs already rejects these dates and was not changed. `days_from_civil` and the date formatting code were also left alone.

  **One sheet per page** (Page 1, Page 2…). Export asks where to save, as Word's does. It needs
  the copy permission, like the other exports.
- **Tables become cells.** The tables the Word/HTML export already detects (`tables()`) become
  rows of cells; a cell that spans columns is merged across them; column widths follow the
  table's grid. Paragraphs become rows with their text in column A, in reading order. Size, bold,
  italic and colour become cell fonts. Images are left out.
- **Values Excel can compute with** (`crates/export/src/cells.rs`), shown exactly as on the page:
  plain numbers (grouped thousands, decimals kept in the format); dollar, euro and pound amounts,
  negatives in parentheses or with a trailing minus, and percentages, each with a number format
  that shows the same text; ISO dates and dates with an English month name become real dates.
  Anything that could be read two ways stays text: leading zeros (codes), more than 15
  significant digits (card and account numbers, which Excel would round), and numeric dates such
  as `03/04/2026`.
- **Excel's limits:** a sheet past 1,048,576 rows goes on on a new sheet; columns past 16,384 are

title: Issue #2364: an incremental save of a PDF with bytes before its header counts offsets from the header
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2364

## Root cause
A file with bytes before its `%PDF-` header counts its cross-reference offsets from the header: Acrobat, qpdf, Poppler and MuPDF all read such a file that way, and so does the file's own `/Prev`. `write_incremental` wrote the new objects, the new section and `startxref` as absolute file positions next to that header-relative `/Prev`, so qpdf reported `xref not found` and Poppler `Syntax Error: Illegal character`, and both rebuilt the table. Our own reader tries both conventions, which is why the saved file still opened here.

## Fix
`Document::offset_base` is the header offset for a file that has a cross-reference chain (0 for most files); `write_incremental` subtracts it from every offset it writes, for a classic table and for a cross-reference stream. A full save is unaffected (it writes a new file without the prefix).

## Tests
`crates/cos/tests/writer.rs::incremental_save_of_a_prefixed_file_counts_offsets_from_the_header`: a 128-byte prefix before a one-page file with a classic table, and before the same file saved in full with a cross-reference stream. After an Info edit and an incremental save, `startxref` + prefix lands on the new section, the new entry for the Info object + prefix lands on `3 0 obj`, `/Prev` is the original `startxref`, and the result reads back with two revisions and the edit. Fails on `main` at the `startxref` assertion. The saved files from both cases also open in Poppler (`pdfinfo`) with no warning; before the fix Poppler reported `Syntax Error (725): Illegal character '>'`.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos` (74 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean, on a Linux (WSL) build host.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #2365: a rebuilt file keeps the /Info and /ID of its cross-reference stream
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2365

## Root cause
The fixture is two PDFs concatenated: the second is cut off before its own cross-reference data, so no `startxref` is within reach of the tail and the file is rebuilt from object headers. The rebuild takes its trailer from the last `trailer` dictionary with a usable `/Root`, and a file written with cross-reference streams has no `trailer` keyword at all, so it fell through to "the catalog alone": `/Info` (and `/ID`, `/Encrypt`) were dropped. That is why Document Properties showed the fields empty before the save and a full save wrote only the edited `/Subject` and `/ModDate`.

## Fix
`reconstruct()` remembers the offset of every scanned object whose dictionary mentions `/XRef`, parses those, and treats each `/Type /XRef` stream dictionary with a usable `/Root` as a trailer candidate alongside the `trailer` dictionaries; the one latest in the file wins, as before. The keys a cross-reference stream's dictionary carries for itself (`/Type`, `/W`, `/Index`, `/Filter`, `/DecodeParms`, `/Length`) are dropped from the rebuilt trailer, as the chain readers drop them (a save writes its own).

## Tests
`crates/cos/src/document.rs::reconstruction_takes_the_trailer_from_a_cross_reference_stream`: a full save with object streams (its only trailer is a cross-reference stream), then a second file of 5 KB appended without cross-reference data. Opening rebuilds; `/Info` and `/ID` are in the trailer, the Info `/Title` reads, and a full save after setting `/Subject` keeps `/Title` and `/Creator`. On `main` the trailer has only `/Root`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`openpreserve-format-corpus/jhove-errors/PDF-HUL-138/6.2017-0960.pdf`, SHA-256 `a299…22`): before, the rebuilt trailer was `<< /Root 254 0 R >>`; after, `/Info 284 0 R` resolves to Creator `Word`, Producer, CreationDate and ModDate, and a full save after a `/Subject` edit keeps them all.

title: Issue #2367: an object stream whose entry cannot place it is found by its header
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2367

## Root cause
In qpdf's `xref-compressed-in-compressed.pdf` the cross-reference stream says object stream 69 (which holds the outlines, object 70, and the page labels, 82) is itself compressed inside stream 81. The format forbids that, and 81 does not exist. `Document::objstm` loaded a container only through its cross-reference entry, so the lookup failed, every object inside read as `Null`, and a full save (which rewrites the reachable objects) wrote `/Outlines null /PageLabels null`. An incremental save copies the original bytes, which is why it kept them; MuPDF recovers them by scanning.

## Fix
When the container's entry cannot load it as a stream, `objstm` finds it by its own `N G obj` header with `scan_for`, the same last resort a plain object with a wrong offset already has (decrypted the same way). Nothing changes for files whose entries work.

## Tests
`crates/cos/src/document.rs::an_object_stream_marked_as_compressed_is_found_by_its_header`: a hand-built file with a cross-reference stream whose row for the object stream says "in stream 99" (nonexistent) and whose catalog's `/Outlines` lives in that object stream. Opening reads the chain without repair; object 4 is the Outlines dictionary, and a full save reopened still resolves `/Outlines` to it. On `main` object 4 reads as `Null`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`qpdf/qtest/qpdf/xref-compressed-in-compressed.pdf`, SHA-256 `c990…c2`): before, objects 70 and 82 were `Null` and the full save had no outlines or page labels; after, 70 is the Outlines dictionary (Count 6), 82 the PageLabels tree (12 ranges), and a full save keeps both.

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos` (75 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-cos --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean, on a Linux (WSL) build host.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #2366: a trailer whose /Prev is a reference still reaches the earlier sections
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2366

## Root cause
`JA3-1998-PDF.pdf` (and `JA1-1996-PDF.pdf`; both `tiff2pdf` output, JHOVE's PDF-HUL-157 cases) ends its first trailer with `/Prev 297298 0 R`: the offset of the earlier cross-reference section written as a reference. `read_xref_chain` took `/Prev` as an integer only, so the chain ended after the first section without a note, and every object of the earlier section — pages 2–4 (objects 1, 4, 7) and their images — read as `Null`. That is the "one page where both readers find four" in the report. A full save then wrote the three missing kids as `null` (`/Kids [5 0 R null null null] /Count 4`), which is what MuPDF reports as a page-tree cycle and Poppler renders as 1×1 (Poppler: `Kid object (page 2) is not an indirect reference (null)`). The incremental control kept the original bytes, so other readers could still reconstruct them.

## Fix
`prev_offset`, used by both chain readers (`read_xref_chain` and `read_xref_chain_materialized`, since #1505): a reference-valued `/Prev` is read as the offset it names, with a repair-log note (`the trailer at 119 gives /Prev as the reference 297298 0 R; reading it as offset 297298`); the section there is still validated as before, so a wrong value just ends the chain. Any other non-offset `/Prev` is noted too instead of being dropped silently.

## Tests
`crates/cos/src/document.rs::a_prev_written_as_a_reference_still_reaches_the_earlier_sections`: a one-page file with an incremental update whose trailer says `/Prev <offset> 0 R`, against the same update with a numeric `/Prev`: both open with two revisions, the page of the first section has the same entry and reads as a Page, the update's Info reads, and the reference form leaves one repair-log line. On `main` the reference form has one revision and the page is `Null`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`openpreserve-format-corpus/jhove-errors/PDF-HUL-157/JA3-1998-PDF.pdf`, SHA-256 `51b1…2d`): four pages read; after a `/Subject` edit and a full save, `pdfinfo…

title: Issue #2368: flattening keeps a NoRotate widget upright on a rotated page
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2368

## Root cause
An annotation with the `NoRotate` flag (`/F` bit 5) is shown upright on a page with `/Rotate`: its appearance turns with the page about the rectangle's upper-left corner (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.3), and that is how MuPDF and Poppler draw it. `flatten` placed every appearance with Algorithm 8.1 alone (bounding box → `/Rect` as it lies in user space), so on the fixture's `/Rotate 90` page the flattened `NoRotate` widget came out turned with the page and in a different place, while its two neighbours without the flag (drawn the same way before and after) looked unchanged.

## Fix
When the annotation has `NoRotate` and the page (with inherited attributes) has a `/Rotate` of 90, 180 or 270, the placement matrix is followed by that turn about `(x0, y1)` of the rectangle (`upright` in `flatten.rs`). Nothing changes for other annotations or unrotated pages.

## Tests
`crates/edit/src/tests.rs::flattening_keeps_a_no_rotate_widget_upright_on_a_rotated_page`: a plain widget and a `NoRotate` widget sharing one appearance (bbox 100×50 onto a 100×50 rect at (100, 500)) on pages rotated 0, 90, 180 and 270. The plain one is always drawn with `1 0 0 1 100 500 cm`; the `NoRotate` one with the same on 0 and with `0 1 -1 0 150 550`, `-1 0 0 -1 100 600` and `0 -1 1 0 50 550` on 90/180/270 (each keeps the appearance's upper-left corner at (100, 550) and turns it with the page). On `main` all four draw `1 0 0 1 100 500`.

Verified on the issue's fixture (`qpdf/qtest/qpdf/manual-appearances.pdf`, SHA-256 `d1da…cf`), page 2 (`/Rotate 90`, widgets 7 and 8 plain, 9 with `NoRotate`): after flattening the fields and a full save, Poppler's render at 36 dpi differs from the unflattened page by 80 pixels (anti-aliasing of the drawn appearances; the dark-pixel bounding box is identical), against 648 pixels before the fix, when widget 9's box moved.

title: Issue #2352: a CCITT image whose /Rows is 0 decodes to its height, not to nothing
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2352

## Root cause
The scanner writes each page's Group 4 image with `/DecodeParms << /K -1 /Columns 1656 /Rows 0 >>`. `/Rows 0` means "use the image height" (ISO 32000-2 Table 11: the default, 0, means the image's rows are not known in advance; viewers take the image's `/Height`). The vendored `hayro-syntax` (`src/filter/ccitt.rs`) read `/Rows` as written and only fell back to the image height when the key was absent, so it decoded zero rows: an empty image, a white page, both in the app and in `pdfcraft-cli render`, as the reporter found (and confirmed by blanking the key).

## Fix
PdfCraft patch (17) to hayro-syntax: when the image's height is known it takes precedence over `/Rows`, as other viewers do and as upstream hayro's `decode` now does (its `rows` is the image height, else `/Rows`), so the patch goes away at the next bump. `vendor/README.md` records the patch and its test, as the other patches are.

## Tests
`crates/render/tests/ccitt_rows.rs::a_ccitt_image_whose_rows_is_zero_decodes_to_its_height`: an 8 × 4 Group 4 strip made by ghostscript's `tiffg4` device (left half black), drawn as a 1-bit `DeviceGray` image over a page of its size, with `/Rows 4`, `/Rows 0` and no `/Rows`; rendered through `PageRenderer` at 1:1, pixel (1, 1) is black and (6, 1) white in all three. On `main` the `/Rows 0` case fails ("the left half is black": it renders white).

`cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --test ccitt_rows`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean, on a Linux (WSL) build host.

Developed with AI assistance (Claude Code); reviewed and tested locally.

title: Issue #2385: audit finds thick strokes, black highlights and white boxes over text
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2385

## What was missed
`pdfcraft-cli audit` took covers only from `re` rectangles and rectangular `m`/`l` paths filled with an opaque non-stroking colour, and from `/Redact` annotations. The report's three other ways of hiding text that a reader sees as redacted were reported clean (`count: 0`, exit 0) while the text stayed extractable:

| cover | now |
|---|---|
| `0 G 20 w 70 705 m 400 705 l S` (thick black stroke, "marker") | `covered-text`, rect `[70 695 400 715]` |
| `/Subtype /Highlight /C [0 0 0]` annotation over the text | `covered-text` |
| `1 g 70 695 330 20 re f` (white filled rectangle) | `hidden-under-white` (new kind) |

## Fix
- `cover.rs`: the walker also tracks the stroking colour (`G`/`RG`/`K`), the line width (`w`) and the stroking alpha (`/CA`). A single `m`/`l` segment along one axis, stroked opaquely (`S`, `s`, or `B`/`B*` with the fill), counts as the rectangle it paints: the segment widened by half the line width each side, the width taken through the CTM's scale. Slanted or bent strokes and stroked rectangles (outlines) are not covers; the module docs say so.
- `lib.rs`: the annotation pass reads `/Highlight` annotations too (colour from `/C` in gray/RGB/CMYK, `/CA` default 1, Hidden and NoView skipped); an opaque one whose contrast against the text is below the existing 3.0 threshold is a `covered-text` finding, like a filled rectangle would be. Yellow or translucent highlights are not flagged.
- A new `FindingKind::HiddenUnderWhite` (`hidden-under-white`): an opaque cover painted after the text whose relative luminance is ≥ 0.9 (white is 1.0; the `0.9 g` table shading of the existing test is 0.79 and stays unflagged) hides dark text as completely as a black one, the way forms are whited out. It is reported apart, as the report suggests, so callers can decide; a white marker stroke falls under it too.
- The `doc_audit_redactions` tool description lists the new covers and kind; the automation audit test still passes.

title: fix(preflight): follow colour spaces to the device space they draw in
author: guillehr2
body:
## What this changes

`pdfa_verify` and `pdfa_convert` now follow a colour space to the device space it actually draws in. Before, a device space that reached the page through a colour space, rather than through an operator or a bare `/ColorSpace /DeviceCMYK`, was missed. A spot colour with a DeviceCMYK alternate or an indexed image over DeviceCMYK was given an sRGB output intent and then passed verification. Fixes #2411.

This is the follow-up #2260 listed as out of scope, rebased on `main` now that #2260 has landed.

- **One function follows colour spaces** (`colour_space`): a device name is marked; an Indexed or Pattern space follows its base, and a Separation or DeviceN space its alternate. The depth is bounded (`MAX_SPACE_DEPTH`), so a cyclic or absurd chain of references stops. `[/DeviceRGB]` written as an array counts too. CIE-based and ICC-based spaces are not device colour.
- **It is applied wherever a colour space appears:**
  - an image's or a shading's own `/ColorSpace`. This replaces the bare-name check, so `[/Indexed /DeviceCMYK …]` and `[/Separation … /DeviceCMYK …]` images and shadings now count;
  - an inline image's `/CS`. This replaces the `[/I …]` special case;
  - a `/ColorSpace` resource entry, once content selects it by name with `cs`/`CS` or an inline image's `/CS /CS0`.
- **A resource entry counts only once something selects it.** Content collects the names it selects. After the content pass, those names are looked up in every resource dictionary. A space the resources merely list is not used.
- **The reading behind Separation/DeviceN alternates (ISO 19005-2 §6.2.4.3–6.2.4.4):** a device alternate needs the same output intent as the device space used directly. §6.2.4.3 limits every use of a device space and makes no exception for alternates. §6.2.4.4 requires same-named Separations to agree on their alternate, which treats the alternate as part of the colour's definition. title: CI: run cargo xtask parity, so a parity file that no longer parses fails the merge (#2416)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #2416

## What changes
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` but not `cargo xtask parity`, so a merge that leaves `parity/acrobat-features.toml` invalid passes every check — which is how `main` ended up with the duplicate keys of #2415. The Linux job now has a `Parity` step after the assets check that runs `cargo xtask parity`, the same gate `cargo xtask ci` already applies locally (it parses the file and rejects `shipped` claims whose commands, tools or tests don't exist).

On today's `main` this step fails exactly as #2415 describes (`TOML parse error at line 2625 … duplicate key`, exit 1) — that is the check doing its job. It goes green once #2419 (the merged keys) lands; merging this one after it keeps `main` green.

title: fix(engine): PNG export writes opaque pages as RGB at deflate level 3 (3–5× faster, same size)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft_engine::export::encode_png` wrote every raster as RGBA at the `png` crate's default level (zlib level 6). A rendered page is always opaque (it's drawn on white), so the alpha channel only made the file bigger and slower to write. An opaque raster is now written as **RGB at deflate level 3** with adaptive filtering; a raster with translucent pixels is still RGBA with straight alpha, exactly as before.

Same file size, 3–5× faster to write (release build, Linux):

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 300-dpi scan drawn at 220 dpi | 805 ms, 4.46 MB | 167 ms, 4.47 MB |
| Text page at 220 dpi | 70 ms, 0.85 MB | 40 ms, 0.89 MB |
| Annual-report page at 150 dpi | 179 ms, 1.41 MB | 64 ms, 1.38 MB |

This is the encoder behind Export ▸ Image (PNG), `pdfcraft-cli render` and Print as Image. `pdfcraft-automation` had its own copy (`page_render` and the other page previews, MCP included); it now calls the engine's, so there is one encoder, and `png` is only a dev-dependency of the automation crate.

title: fix(render): read each object stream's index once (vendored hayro-syntax patch 22)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

`XRef::get_with` (vendored hayro-syntax) parsed an object stream's whole index of `objnum offset` pairs again for **every object it fetched** from that stream, so reading all of a stream of N objects took N² steps. Most producers cap object streams at 100–200 objects (PdfCraft's own writer at 100), but some don't: the pdf.js corpus file `bug1978317.pdf` (Firefox, 65,542 objects in one stream) took 37 s to draw and 40 s to extract its text, and was a known timeout in the robustness baseline.

The parsed index is now kept per stream (`ObjectStreamIndexes`), beside the decoded stream data it indexes, and like that data never cleared (a repair keeps it too). A malformed index is remembered as malformed; `/N` or `/First` that can't be read (a reference that can't be followed while another stream loads) is not remembered. An offset past `usize` is now malformed instead of wrapping. Vendored hayro-syntax patch (22).

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bug1978317.pdf` render | 37 s | 0.5 s |
| `bug1978317.pdf` text | 40 s | 1.9 s |
| 40,000 pages in one object stream, open | 54 s | 0.2 s |

(Release build, Linux.) `bug1978317.pdf` now passes `pdfcraft-cli check`, so its `timeout` entry leaves `xtask/baselines/pdfjs.json`, as `cargo xtask check` asks for a newly fixed file.

## How you verified it

title: Fix text selection across narrow article columns
author: guillerpsanchez
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2387.

Ordinary text selection could cross both article columns because a narrow gutter was treated as a word space before reading-order grouping. Detect a gutter repeated across three nearby baselines and split those runs before grouping, so selection and extraction read each column in order. Isolated large word spaces and Alt/Option rectangular selection retain their behavior.

The optional detection pass has a fixed lookback and capped, fallible flag allocation, with the previous heuristic as fallback. Adds synthetic layout regressions for narrow gutters, ragged lines and redraws, plus a pointer-drag regression covering both columns in both directions. title: Fix GPU startup requests exceeding adapter limits
author: Bortlesboat
body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft now clamps egui-wgpu's requested device limits to the selected adapter's capabilities before enabling its full 2D texture extent. The reported V3D adapter supports 15 inter-stage shader variables while the default request asks for 16, so device creation rejects the request.

The existing wgpu clamp handles both maximum limits and reversed minimum-alignment limits. Compatible defaults and the existing HiDPI texture-extent behavior are preserved. The required roadmap records describe the candidate without changing milestone estimates.

title: fix(render): faster sampled functions, image decodes across zoom levels and patch meshes (vendored hayro-interpret patches 31–33)
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Three vendored hayro-interpret patches found by profiling the release build against the pdf.js corpus, a public annual report (#1584) and synthetic scans. One commit each:

_Rebased onto main at 99941daa: #1557 took hayro-interpret patch (29) for its annotation hooks and 13e3154a took (30) for the Annex D.2 alias codes, so these patches are now numbered 31–33 (code comments, `vendor/README.md`, commit subjects). The code is unchanged._

**Patch 31: sampled functions index a flat sample array.** A Type 0 function kept its samples in a `HashMap` keyed by each point of its `/Size` grid (two `SmallVec`s per key, SipHash), and the renderer builds a shading's functions again on every paint, so each paint did one hashed insert per sample. The samples now stay in stream order in one `Vec`, found by strides. The interpolation keeps the same recursion and arithmetic, so results are bit for bit the same; a point the stream ended before still gives no value. Also fixes `2_u32.pow(32)` overflowing (a panic with overflow checks on) at 32 bits per sample.

**Patch 32: one decode of an image serves every size it is drawn at.** The decoded-image cache (patch 24) keyed every decode by the size the image is drawn at, but only JPX decodes a reduced resolution for a size; every other filter decodes the whole image. So a JPEG or Flate scan missed the cache at every zoom step, was decoded again, and was kept once per zoom level. The key now carries the target size only when JPX decodes the image, its `/SMask` or its `/Mask`. `InterpreterCache::decoded_image_decodes()` (new, public) counts the cache's decodes.

**Patch 33: patch meshes copy their vertices' colours less.** Coons and tensor patches are drawn as 722 triangles each, and every vertex's colours were produced or copied up to five times (each grid cell interpolated its four corners itself, cloned all six vertices, and the sampler cloned each again to move it into device space). Each grid point is now interpol…

title: fix(search): match Arabic across presentation forms, tashkeel, tatweel and alef/yeh variants
author: jadhamandi
body:
## What this changes

Find (Ctrl+F, `text_find`) compared Arabic code point by code point, so typed Arabic often found nothing:

- **Presentation forms** (U+FB50–FDFF, U+FE80–FEFC), which many older PDFs and Office exports map their glyphs to: `ﻣﺤﻤﺪ` was not found by typing `محمد`.
- **Tashkeel and tatweel**: `مُحَمَّدٌ` and `مـحـمـد` were not found by `محمد`.
- **Alef / yeh spelling variants**: أ / إ / آ / ٱ vs ا, and ى vs ي.

A new `text::fold_arabic` maps presentation forms to letters via NFKC (so ﺅ → ؤ, not waw + a hamza mark), drops harakat, their spacing forms and tatweel, and folds the alef/yeh variants. Search applies it in both case modes, since Arabic has no case. Text outside Arabic script is unchanged. It adds `unicode-normalization`, which is already in the tree through `stringprep`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`)

The randomized comparison against the reference search (`tests/search.rs`) now folds the same way, and its alphabet gains Arabic presentation-form, lam-alef, haraka, tatweel and hamza pieces. Reverting the fix in `search.rs` turns the Arabic search test red.

title: M9: PKCS #11 signing, checked with CloudSigner (mSzafir) on macOS
author: marcintrojnacki
body:
## What this changes

Signing with PKCS #11 devices (smart cards, USB tokens, remote signing services), checked end to end with KIR's **CloudSigner for mSzafir** qualified signatures on macOS, from the packaged app and from the CLI.

Addresses #85, #1578, #2224 and #318 (PKCS #11 part). There are other open PKCS #11 PRs (#1593, #1837, #1896, #2215). What this one adds that they don't, as far as I can see:

- **CloudSigner (mSzafir) support.** The module is found where its macOS installer puts it. No PIN is asked for, because CloudSigner takes its OTT code in its own window and the approval happens in the mSzafir app. A token signs on a worker so the app goes on while the signer approves on the phone.
- **One approval for a batch.** A `Transaction` holds every document's `C_Sign` until all of them are ready, then releases them together. CloudSigner gathers up to 20 signatures into one transaction: one OTT code and one approval. The automation tool is `sign_documents`.
- **The chain embedded in a signature is the signer's path, not every certificate on the token.** CloudSigner lists a TLS server certificate (`*.szafir.kir.pl`) and an unrelated root beside the signer's, and neither issued it.
- **The hardened runtime let the release app load the module.** Library validation refused every vendor's PKCS #11 library ("mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs"). This PR adds `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` to the app and to the CLI, which `package.sh` now signs with the same entitlements. #1593 has the same entitlement for the app.

Engine: `pdfcraft-sign::pkcs11` on the `cryptoki` crate.

- Keys sign with `CKM_RSA_PKCS` over a DigestInfo, or with `CKM_ECDSA`.

title: macOS: bring the window forward when a file is opened in the running app (fixes #1928)
author: manchitmr
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1928.

Opening a PDF from Finder (double-click, Open With, a Dock drop) while PdfCraft was already running opened the tab but left the window where it was: behind Finder, minimized, or full screen on another Space. Nothing seemed to happen, and focus stayed on Finder.

`OsEvent::Open` is where every file handed to the running app arrives: Apple events on macOS, and the single-instance handoff on Windows and Linux. After opening the files, it now sends `ViewportCommand::Minimized(false)` and `ViewportCommand::Focus`. - **After:** same steps. macOS switched to PdfCraft's full-screen Space, with the new PDF as a new tab in the existing window.
- **Manual:** Open With from Finder with the app already running opens a new tab and brings the window forward. Clicking the Dock icon with the window behind Finder also brings it forward.

Addresses #1777. `edit.find-replace` was planned. This adds it in Edit text mode, through the
paragraph rewrite Edit text already uses, so a replaced word keeps the paragraph's font, size and

title: Connect MCP tools to the running PdfCraft window
author: CouchRiv
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli mcp` currently owns a separate engine session. An agent cannot fill the form a person already has open in PdfCraft. `mcp --connect FILE` uses the existing authenticated `--control FILE` channel and runs the same automation table on the window's own session. Document ids, resources, edits and Undo refer to the tabs the person sees. New documents open behind their active tab; rendering and stale selections refresh after changes.

The CLI reuses its control-file ownership/permissions checks and sends tokens only to loopback. Both control and MCP remain opt-in. A lost reply is not replayed automatically, because an edit may already have run; the next call reconnects and rereads the control file. Replies are bounded and checked for matching JSON-RPC ids.

MCP adds read-only `ui_state`, `ui_inspect` and `ui_screenshot`, including in compact mode. It does not expose UI input, which would bypass root confinement and human signing consent. The window refuses tools while a text/comment draft or edit dialog is open. MCP inspection uses protected `tool.inspect`; private signing/password views cannot be inspected or captured through the bridge; password-node values are omitted.

The agent prepares, the person signs. Connected tools refuse all `sign_*`, signature/initials placement, reusable signature-image export, redaction application and tab closure, also through command wrappers. Signing credentials are rejected before relay and again at the window dispatch boundary. Signature fields, ordinary text/dates and redaction marks may be prepared; the person signs or confirms redaction in the app. Existing headless signing remains unchanged.

The automation runner is supplied by the desktop binary, preserving crate layering: ui-egui has no dependency on automation. No provider client, model key, new listener or automatic MCP registration is added.

title: M7: fold repeated group moves of a cropped image into one clip cm
author: komo1iddin
body:
Follows storytold/pdfcraft#1746, which folds repeated image transforms into one `cm`. That change covers an image moved on its own. This one covers the other case: a group move of an image that carries its own crop.

## What this changes

Some images carry their own crop: `q re W n cm Do Q`. When an image like that was moved as part of a group, a fresh `cm` went in before the clip path on every move. Twenty moves left twenty `cm` operators in front of one `re`. The nesting never got deeper, but the content stream grew with every drag.

`translate_images` now checks whether a `cm` already sits right before that clip. That `cm` may come from an earlier move or from the file itself. If it does, the move replaces it with the product of the new matrix and the old one. The CTM at the clip is `c · prev · outer` either way (ISO 32000-1 §8.3.4, §8.4.4).

Two cases keep the old behaviour and insert a separate `cm`:
- the previous `cm` has a value that is not finite;
- the product has an entry larger than 1e12.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

  - `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test automation`: 173 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are `a_save_that_does_not_reopen_leaves_the_file_as_it_was` and `signing_with_translated_labels_through_tools`. Both also fail on `main` at afa8e184 on this macOS machine, and neither involves images.

**Test.** `repeated_group_moves_of_a_cropped_image_change_one_clip_transform` crops an image smaller than itself and moves it twenty times as part of a group. It checks that:
- the image and its visible crop both moved by the full offset;
- the operator count stays at its value after the first move;
- the caption drawn after the image is untouched.

title: M7: show a shaped run in one text object instead of one per glyph
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

`rewrite_styled_block` writes shaped text (Arabic, Indic, Latin with combining marks) glyph by glyph, and each glyph got a text object of its own:
- `BT`;
- the whole text state: `Tf Tc Tw Tz TL Ts` and the colour;
- an absolute `Tm`;
- one `Tj`;
- `ET`.

A row of 15 glyphs took 15 text objects, and a long Arabic paragraph took thousands of operators. Other viewers also saw every glyph as a separate piece of text when selecting or searching. Only ActualText kept copying working.

Now each shaped run is one text object:
- **One state and one `Tm`.** The state is written once and the run's start is set once.
- **Glyphs in `TJ` arrays.** Each glyph is preceded by an adjustment. It moves the glyph from where the glyph before it ends to where shaping put it. "Where it ends" is the glyph's width in the embedded font's `/W` (ISO 32000-1 §9.4.3, §9.4.4). So kerning and mark offsets come out exactly as shaped.
- **Marks above or below.** A mark shaped above or below its letter is raised with `Ts` (§9.3.7), and the rise is reset after the run.
- **Spacing.** Character and word spacing are already part of each glyph's position, so `Tc` and `Tw` are 0 inside the run.
- **Long runs.** A `TJ` array holds at most 4096 elements; a longer run continues in the next one.

On a test row of 15 glyphs, the content stream went from 392 tokens and 15 per-glyph text objects to 90 tokens and one text object. The ActualText span around the run is unchanged.

title: fix(content): an inline image ends at its own EI, not a later one
author: luigiPinna
body:
Fixes #3157.

**Update.** The fix itself landed on `main` through #3983 (`6bb89022` merges `04697ad4`), and #2456 is closed. What this PR carries now is the follow-up its tests needed. Since #3438, an unfiltered inline image ends at its computed length before the `EI` look-ahead runs, so the two #2456 tests, built on an unfiltered 1×1 `/DeviceGray` image, passed on `main` with the fix reverse-applied. Both now use a filtered image (`/F /AHx ID 00> EI`), whose length isn't known up front, so the look-ahead decides again. Test-only, +6/−4. Checked on `main` at `9a0ec645`: with the `mod.rs` change reverse-applied the old tests pass and the new ones fail; restored, the new ones pass; `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render -j 2` (366), fmt, clippy, `layers`, `assets` and `parity` pass. #4011 had the same commit and is closed in favour of this one. The description below is the original one, for the fix.

---

## What this changes

A page draws and extracts nothing after an inline image when the content that follows holds a byte above 0x7F before the next `E` `I` pair (#2456). Both halves are everyday content: WinAnsi text with ä ö ü ß in a string, or the two-byte codes of any Type 0 font, and a capital "EI" in a later word (EINGANG, BEI, KLEIN). Reported on five real scanned documents with an OCR text layer, where 40 of their 275 pages returned no word at all.

**Cause.** In `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/content/mod.rs`, the end-of-data look-ahead takes an `EI` with whitespace around it as a candidate, then searches for the next `EI` or `BI`. If that was an `EI` and any byte in between was non-ASCII, the candidate was rejected ("binary data in-between, so we for sure have not reached the end") and the search went on. When the candidate is the real end, though, those in-between bytes are the content stream that follows the image, and a content stream carries bytes above 0x7F inside its strings. No later candidate qualified, so the image data ran to the end of the stream.

title: M7: drop the fallback fonts a text edit leaves unused
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Some edits draw Japanese or Hebrew characters that the page's fonts lack. Each such edit generates new Type 3 fallback fonts (`PCJp…`, `PCHe…`) holding the outlines of every character it draws. These fonts are never reused, so editing the paragraph again generates a fresh set. The old set stayed in the page's resources and in the saved file. As a result, every edit added another set of glyph outlines.

After `replace_line` and `rewrite_block` succeed, the page's generated fallback fonts that no `Tf` selects any more are removed from the page's own font dictionary. A generated fallback font here means a Type 3 font with `/Name /PCJapanese` or `/PCHebrew`.

**What counts as "selects".** Every `Tf` in content that can name the page's fonts:
- the page's content streams;
- every form XObject the page can reach that has no `/Resources` of its own. Such forms use the page's resources, however deeply they are nested (ISO 32000-1 §7.8.3);
- the glyph procedures of Type 3 fonts without `/Resources`. The generated fonts are left out, because their procedures are outlines only.

**When nothing is removed:**
- any of that content can't be decoded strictly, since a partly read stream might name the font in the part that wasn't read;
- the page doesn't own its resources (a rewrite gives the page its own);
- more than 4096 form XObjects are reachable.

**What is never touched:**
- registered and embedded full faces (`PCFull…`), which `text_fonts` lists for later edits;
- the file's own fonts, even one whose name starts with `PCJp`.

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean

title: feat(print): pass orientation options to spooler for landscape printing
author: emre-clk91
body:
## Summary
While PdfCraft provides orientation selection (`Auto`, `Portrait`, `Landscape`) in the Print dialog UI and composes sheets with matching dimensions, it did not forward the requested orientation options to the CUPS spooler (`lp`).

On Linux/CUPS systems, printers default to portrait (`orientation-requested=3`). Without explicit orientation options passed to `lp`, print queues will treat landscape documents as portrait and rotate or clip them.

## Changes
- Added `auto_landscape` tracking in `PrintDraft` initialized from the document layout and kept up to date during sheet layout and print submission.
- Added `is_landscape()` on `PrintDraft` to determine if the job is landscape (`Landscape`, `Booklet`, or `Auto` with landscape sheets).
- In `PrintDraft::job()`, append `orientation-requested=4` and `landscape=true` for landscape jobs, and `orientation-requested=3` for portrait jobs.
- Added unit tests in `print_ui.rs` and updated integration test in `tests/print.rs` asserting orientation spooler options.

title: M7: keep the text blocks cache after the document is edited
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

`Editor::text_blocks` caches a page's text blocks. Opening a paragraph and applying its edit both need them, and grouping a long page isn't cheap. The cache was keyed by the document's source identity, and it was only used while the document was unmodified, because edits keep that identity. So after the first edit it never hit again, and every call grouped the page again. After an apply the panel and the canvas each call it, and automation's `text_paragraphs` calls it as well.

This adds `pdfcraft_cos::Document::read_state()`. It returns a `ReadState`: what the document reads as, made of:
- its source identity;
- its trailer;
- every object changed since it was opened.

Changed objects are compared as allocations (`Arc::ptr_eq`). The state holds them, so a later object can't take the address of one of them. As a result:
- a clone of the document, or a snapshot that undo restores, has the same state;
- every `set`, `add`, `free` or trailer change makes a different state, even when it sets the same value again.

The engine cache is now keyed by this state instead of `(!is_modified, source_identity)`. So it keeps hitting after edits and can never return another state's blocks.

**Measurement.** On a page of 120 rows, `Document::text_blocks` after an edit took 0.215 ms per call before and 0.006 ms now. That is a release build, best of three runs, with a throwaway timing test that is not part of this PR.

title: Ctrl+V pastes a picture from the system clipboard onto the page
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2494.

In the page view nothing read a picture from the system clipboard: ⌘V / Ctrl+V only pastes pages in Organize Pages, and when the clipboard holds just an image (a screenshot, a picture copied in a browser) egui-winit sends no `Paste` event and swallows the key press, so only the release of V reaches the app. A plain V press always comes through, so a release of V with no press before it is the shortcut, even when Ctrl was let go a moment before V. On that release this reads the clipboard image (the same arboard read Create ▸ Clipboard uses) and places it through `add_image`, the path Add Image takes: on the current page, centred, at its natural size shrunk to fit, selected, one undo step. Text fields, form fields, Prepare Form (where ⌘V pastes copied fields, see #1629), dialogs and Organize Pages keep ⌘V as before, and a clipboard with only text does nothing, as today.

Choices that are yours to make, happy to switch:
- It lands in the middle of the current page, like Add Image, rather than under the pointer.
- The web build is unchanged: it has no clipboard image read yet.

This overlaps with my #1625, which pastes a picture copied inside PdfCraft. Its ⌘V listens for `Event::Paste`, which never fires for an image-only clipboard, so if both land the two paths should become this one release-based handler: the system clipboard image first, else the picture copied inside PdfCraft.

Validation:
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/content.rs::a_picture_on_the_clipboard_is_pasted_onto_the_page`: fails on main (`left: 0, right: 1` at the ⌘V step), passes here, also run alone. title: fix(sign): fill typed signature outlines with non-zero winding (#1786)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

In `Inter-Regular.ttf` (the fallback font for typed signatures when `DancingScript.ttf` lacks a glyph), the Serbian Cyrillic letters `Ђ` (U+0402, `uni0402`) and `ћ` (U+045B, `uni045B`) are TrueType composite glyphs built from two overlapping clockwise contours (`T` + `largerighthook` in `Ђ`, and `h` + `crossbar` in `ћ`), whereas `Ћ` (U+040B) and `ђ` (U+0452) are single merged contours. Filling `script_outline` contours with the even-odd rule punched a transparent hole where those same-direction contours cross on the stem (`winding == ±2`). Fill typed-signature outlines with the non-zero winding rule in `script_preview`, Stamp `/PCOutline` appearances (`f` instead of `f*`), and `pdfcraft_sign::Graphic::Outlines::draw` (`f` instead of `f*`), matching the Type 3 glyph emitters in `crates/edit`.

Fixes #1786

## How you verified it

Tested on commit `5f642e11`:

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot -p pdfcraft-sign -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings` — 0 warnings

title: feat(ui): split view: two panes, one document or two
author: regendorf-ux
body:
## What this changes

Addresses the split-view half of #1683 ("Move tab to new window and split-view", which also
gathers #2032's side by side or stacked) and #2036 (split screen on one file):

- **Split view.** **View ▸ Split** (⌘\ / Ctrl+\, `view.split`) splits the current document into
  two panes, and ends split view again. A tab's right-click menu gains **Split right** and
  **Split down**: the tab the main pane shows gets a second view of its document (page 2 beside
  page 40); another tab moves beside it (two documents side by side). A tab dropped on the right
  half of the page area splits right with it.
  - Each pane has its own tab strip (the second pane's is small), scroll and zoom. A tab dragged
    from one pane's strip onto the other pane moves there.
  - The divider drags (15–85 %).
  - The pane last clicked is the active one: menus, keys and the side panels act on it, and a
    thin accent line marks it.
  - Closing a pane's last tab, or Split again, ends split view.
- **One document, two views, one undo.** The same document in both panes is two `DocView`s with
  one `DocId`. The document, its edits and its undo history stay the session's, so an edit made
  in one pane shows in the other (the other view follows it as after a reload, keeping its
  place) and Undo is the document's. Both views render through the document's one render pool;
  a request both ask for is rendered once. Closing one view never closes the document and
  doesn't ask about the document's edits; it asks only about typing that view holds of its own

title: Export Data as CSV keeps formula-like cells as text, like the merge report
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Export Data (CSV) writes field names and values as they are, only quoting a cell that holds a comma, a quote, a tab or a line break. A spreadsheet runs a cell that starts with `=` or `@`, or with `+` or `-` when it isn't a number, as a formula, quoted or not. So a value in a form someone sent you can run as a formula when you export the form data and open the CSV.

#4101 fixed this for Merge Data Files into Spreadsheet and left Export Data alone "because PdfCraft re-imports it, so its round trip is unchanged". This covers Export Data and keeps that round trip:

- `merge_csv`'s rule moves unchanged into `runs_as_formula`. The merge report's output is the same byte for byte.
- Export Data uses the same rule: such a cell gets a leading `'`. A value that already starts with `'` in front of a formula character gets one more.
- Import Data takes exactly that one `'` off again, so Export Data then Import Data gives back every value unchanged.

This replaces the earlier version of this PR, which had its own rule and also changed `merge_csv`.

I couldn't find in Adobe's public help or forums how Acrobat writes such a cell, so this doesn't claim to match it. It follows the rule #4101 chose for the merge report.

title: fix(cos): an incremental save of a file with bytes before its header counts from the header
author: cortenburg28-arch
body:
## What this changes

Some files have bytes before `%PDF-`, and their offsets count from the header instead of from the first byte. We already read such files: when a section isn't at its absolute offset, the reader retries it relative to the header. The incremental writer, however, appended a section whose object offsets and `startxref` were absolute, while its `/Prev` kept the header-relative value. qpdf reported "xref not found" and reconstructed the file, so a save that reported success left a broken-looking update.

- `Revision` gains `header_relative`, set when the reader found that section by counting from the header. `Document::header_offset()` exposes where the header is.
- `write_incremental` counts the new section the same way as the section its `/Prev` points to (the newest revision). This applies to classic tables and cross-reference streams alike, because both take their offsets from the same `base`.
- A file whose offsets already include the prefix keeps absolute offsets. A second test pins that case so the fix cannot overcorrect.

Fixes #2364

title: M7: keep a blank line as a paragraph break (#2517)
author: ihsanmokhlisse
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2517.

Two paragraphs with one blank line between them were grouped as one paragraph. Rows joined while the baseline gap was under 2.5 times the font size. A blank line at ordinary leading is 2 times 1.2, which is 2.4 times the size, so it fell under that limit. Editing the first paragraph then deleted the second.

Once a paragraph already has two rows, a later row joins only when the gap stays within 1.5 times that paragraph's own leading. A paragraph that still has one row joins ordinary leading and double spacing (up to 2.05 times the size) and stops before a blank line. Growing the first paragraph by one row no longer pulls in a neighbour that started three sizes below.

title: fix(ui): the last session comes back to the place on the page, not only the page
author: cortenburg28-arch
body:
## What this changes

#2310 asks for a PDF to come back where the reader stopped: the same page **and the same place on that page**. "Reopen the files from the last session" (#442) already brought back the page; the place on it was still missing (listed in `core.reopen-last-session` as "scroll position within the page (#418)"). This adds it.

- `DocView` notes, each frame it is drawn, where the window's top is within the current page as a fraction of the page's height: the inverse of the existing `goto` jump. `DocView::position_in_page()` returns it (a jump not yet drawn counts as done).
- The last session keeps it per file as `top` next to `page`, and reopening a file goes to `(page, top)` instead of the page's top.
- Settings are untrusted: `top` must be a finite number and is clamped to one page above or below; anything else, and settings written before this change (no `top`), reopen at the page's top as before. The file list stays capped at `MAX_FILES`.
- A fraction of the page height rather than points, so it still lands near the same line when the window or zoom differs between sessions.

Fixes #2310 together with #2195: #2195 remembers the page, zoom and layout per file for files opened again outside the last session (recent files, double-click, command line), so this PR deliberately does not duplicate that. `DocView::position_in_page()` is the piece #2195 (or a follow-up) can store per file to bring back the place there too.

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2447.

Remove Hidden Information (links, comments, attachments) and Sanitize take the annotations off the page's `/Annots`. In a tagged PDF, the structure tree also points at each link and comment it tags through an object reference (`/OBJR /Obj …`). That reference kept the annotation reachable, so the full rewrite these operations force wrote it out again, **with the link's URL or the comment's text**. Meanwhile `link_list` reported no links.

- `remove_hidden` now collects every annotation it removes on every page, the pop-ups of removed comments included.
- New `tags::drop_object_refs` walks the structure tree, with the same seen-set and size bound as `tags::clean`, and drops the elements' `OBJR` kids pointing at those annotations. It handles an `OBJR` given directly or by reference, in a `K` array or as `K`'s only kid. The elements and their marked content stay, so the tagged text is unaffected.
- The `ParentTree` entries keyed by the removed annotations' `StructParent` point at structure elements, not at the annotations, so they don't keep anything alive and are left alone.
- Parity: `protect.remove-hidden-information` notes and evidence; `ROADMAP.md`.

title: fix(redact): redaction removes Info entries and XMP that repeat the redacted text (#2448)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2448. `redact_apply` removed the glyphs under the marks, but the same words often sit in the document information dictionary (`/Title`, `/Subject`, `/Keywords`…) and in the XMP that mirrors it, so they survived the redaction in the saved file.

- **Collecting the removed text** (`interp.rs`). While applying, each removed glyph's text (`ToUnicode`/encoding, as for search) is gathered into runs by position, not by operator: a glyph that starts where the last one ended continues the run, a small gap makes a space, and a jump (another mark, another line) or any glyph that stays starts a new run. Text shown one character per operator still makes one word, and two marks don't join their words. Bounded (100,000 runs, 64 KiB each).
- **Scrubbing** (new `metadata.rs`), after verification succeeds:
  - each run (two or more letters or digits) and each of its words of three or more becomes a term, compared without regard to case or spacing;
  - an `/Info` entry whose text contains a term is removed (the others stay), whether `/Info` is direct or an object of its own;
  - the catalog's and each page's XMP stream is removed whole when its text contains a term. "Text" is element content, attribute values (XMP keeps simple properties as attributes) and CDATA, with entities and character references decoded; tag names and comments are left out, so redacting "title" doesn't hit `dc:title`. Editing the XML in place could leave it malformed or keep the term in another spelling, so the stream goes whole.
  - fail-closed: unreadable XMP, a packet over 16 MiB, or text too large to search against every term counts as matching.
- `Report::metadata` counts what went. README, `protect.apply-redactions` notes and evidence, and ROADMAP updated.

**Not in this PR:** XMP on other objects (images, fonts), bookmarks (#1141/#1145) and attachments. #162 also handles Info/XMP, by removing all of it as part of a larger hardening; this is the narrow fix for the issue and doe…

title: A save keeps the permissions of the file it replaces
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1790.

On Unix, saving over an existing file wrote a new staging file with the default mode for a new file (usually `0644` with a `022` umask) and renamed it over the original. A PDF that was `0600` became readable by other local users after a save.

Now `write_atomically_with` reads the permissions of the file it replaces. The staging file is created owner-only (`0600`) and given those permissions before anything is written to it, so it is never more open than the original, even while it is empty. A new file still gets the usual mode for a new file. Desktop Save, the CLI and the automation tools all write through `pdfcraft_platform::staging::write_atomically_with`, so one change covers all three. `create_staging` keeps its signature and behaviour.

Windows is unchanged: #1790 leaves ACLs to a separate look, and so does this PR.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-platform --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-platform -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings` on macOS, and the same with `--target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-platform -j 2`: 14 passed

title: M6: dynamic forms work: radio/check box actions, /Next chains, click targeting, image fields
author: khemchan-Seenanan
body:
## What this changes

Acrobat-style "dynamic" forms, where choosing a radio option reveals follow-up questions, captions or whole sections, did nothing in PdfCraft. A real 5-page, 250-field application form (made with Acrobat PDFMaker) exposed four separate causes. Each is its own commit:

1. **Check box and radio button actions run on click** (`M6: run check box and radio button actions on click`). Only push buttons read a mouse-up action. Each `Widget` now carries its own action (`Widget::action`: the widget's `/A` or `/AA /U`, else the field's), and a click sets the value first, then runs the action, as Acrobat does. Without that order, the show/hide edit replaced the queued value edit and the button stayed unselected.
2. **Clicks reach the topmost field that responds** (`M6: clicks reach the topmost responsive field; image picks survive typing`). The hit test took the first field in form order. On real forms, read-only caption boxes overlap radio buttons ("Text14 is read-only"), and a text field revealed by one option covers the next option. Widgets now record their `/Annots` position (`Widget::stack`); the click goes to the topmost widget, skipping read-only ones (which don't respond to clicks, per the ReadOnly field flag) unless nothing else is there. The same commit applies the queued edit (e.g. typing in the field being left) before **any** button's action runs, so an image field's file picker no longer finds the document changed and silently drops the chosen picture.
3. **`/Next` action chains are followed** (`M6: follow /Next action chains...`). The form uses 1,843 chained actions ("hide the photo box, then show its caption"; one choice reveals ~30 fields). Only the first action ran. `ButtonAction::Chain` holds the whole chain (ISO 32000-2 §12.6.2: one action or an array per `/Next`; at most 256 actions, each object once, so cycles end). On click, the chain's show/hide steps are applied together as one undo step, then its other steps run.

author: khemchan-Seenanan

## What this changes

Adds Acrobat's dynamic-field JavaScript: `this.addField(cName, cFieldType, nPageNum, oCoords)` and `this.removeField(cName)`, for forms with "Add row" style buttons.

- **`js` crate:** both are document methods in the sandbox. `addField` takes positional arguments or one object (`{cName, cFieldType, nPageNum, oCoords}`), validates them (field type, page, four finite coordinates, at least 4 pt each way, a non-empty name without a period, a name not in use and not a parent of other fields), and returns the new field's object, usable at once in the same script (`value`, `readonly`, `checkThisBox`, …). title: Print: start on the printer's default paper; keep the dialog on screen
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What this changes

Three problems in the Print dialog, seen on macOS with a CUPS queue whose default paper is A5:

- **Paper follows the printer.** The dialog always started on US Letter and sent `media=Letter` with the job, so a queue set up for A4 or A5 was asked for Letter paper unless the user changed it each time. It now starts on the printer's default paper:
  - on CUPS, the destination's `media` default (PWG self-describing names such as `iso_a5_148x210mm`, or a PPD size name);
  - otherwise, the PPD's current `PageSize`, measured with its `*PaperDimension`.

  `spool::default_paper` reads this once per listed printer, not every frame, and only until the user picks a paper or uses "Match page at 100%". Each time the dialog opens it starts from the printer's default again, as system print dialogs do. Unknown sizes, unlisted destinations and Windows keep the previous behaviour.
- **The dialog scrolls when it is taller than the window.** With Properties… open on a laptop screen (1280 × 740 points), the centred modal ran off both edges. The printer row and the Print and Cancel buttons could not be reached. It now scrolls like Preferences. `min_scrolled_height` keeps the modal at window height instead of settling at the height it had when scrolling began.
- **Properties: "Reset to printer defaults" gets a row of its own.** In longer translations, such as Bulgarian («Възстанови настройките по подразбиране на принтера»), the right-to-left button row ran over the panel's title.
