title: M10.5: keep colour print previews in colour
author: xoincare
body:
## What this changes

In the Print dialog the preview was **always grey**, even with *Print in grayscale* off.

`GRAYSCALE_TAG` in `ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` and `PRINT_TAG` in `render/src/raster.rs` were both `1 << 60`. Every print-preview request carries `PRINT_TAG`, so on receipt `tag & GRAYSCALE_TAG != 0` was always true and every preview raster went through `grayscale()`.

- `GRAYSCALE_TAG` moves to the free bit `1 << 59` (`scale_tag` uses only the low bits).
- A `const` assertion keeps it disjoint from `PRINT_TAG`, `THUMB_TAG`, `TEXT_TAG` and `GRID_TAG`.
- The preview tag is now built by `print_preview_tag(scale, grayscale)`, which a unit test pins.

Only the preview was affected. The print job's ticket already asked for colour (`psk:Color` in the validated ticket on a Brother MFC-T910DW).

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib print`: 14 passed
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` / `assets`: not applicable (no crate boundary or asset touched)

**Tests.** `canvas::tests::a_colour_print_preview_is_not_made_grey` checks that a colour preview tag has `PRINT_TAG` set and `GRAYSCALE_TAG` clear, that a grayscale tag has `GRAYSCALE_TAG` set, and that the scale round-trips. I reverted `GRAYSCALE_TAG` to `1 << 60` (with the const assertion commented out) and watched it fail, then restored it.

## Never-crash

- [x] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests
- [x] No input-derived indexing or arithmetic changes
- [x] No `unsafe`

## Provenance

- [x] No assets, fonts or copied code; the fix comes from reading this repo's own tag constants.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Bit 59 is unused across `ui-egui` and `render` today. The const assertion turns any future collision with the listed tags into a compile error.

title: M7: never encode typed text with CID 0 (#3223)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3223.

Editing a line in a PDF exported from Microsoft Word drew a box at every space once the editor closed. The reporter's file shows the cause. Its Type 0 font (`BCDEEE+TimesNewRomanPSMT`, Identity-H, `/CIDToGIDMap` stream) has a ToUnicode CMap that maps **both** CID 0 and CID 7 to U+0020: `<0000> <0002> [<0020> <004D> <00E1>]`. It also gives CID 0 a width in `/W` (`0 [778]`). CID 0 maps to GID 0, `.notdef`. The real space is CID 7, which maps to GID 3 `space`.

`Metrics::encode` keeps the lowest code that shows a character. `has_glyph` accepted CID 0 because `/W` lists it. So every typed space became `<0000>`. The reporter's Modified.pdf has 10 of those in the rewritten line and no `<0007>`. Each one draws the `.notdef` box at 778 units instead of a 250-unit space. That is also why the line got condensed (`87.08 Tz`), which looks like a different font.

CID 0 is `.notdef` in every CIDFont, and a code that a CMap leaves unmapped lands there too. So `has_glyph` now refuses CID 0 for composite fonts. Decoding is unchanged: existing text that uses CID 0 still extracts as a space.

## How you verified it

- New unit test `composite_fonts_never_encode_with_cid_0` mirrors the Word font: CID 0 and CID 7 both map to space, and CID 0 has a width. Without the fix it fails with `Some([0, 1, 0, 5, 0, 0, …])` against the expected `[… 0, 7 …]`. With the fix it passes.
- The property test `lookups_match_the_expanded_mappings` models the reverse map, so its model now leaves code 0 out too.
- End to end on the reporter's Original.pdf, replacing page 1 line 6 through `text_edit`:
  - 0.9.0 (d8b27058) writes 10 × `<0000>` and 0 × `<0007>`;
  - this branch writes 0 × `<0000>` and 10 × `<0007>`;
  - `pdftotext` reads both the same, because the ToUnicode maps both codes to a space. The difference only shows when the page is drawn.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`-p pdfcraft-fonts --all-targets`)

title: M8: phone pattern finds slashed and labelled unseparated numbers (#3205)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the first part of #3205: `pattern=phone` missed three Italian formats.

| Text | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tel. 0426/123456` (landline, slash) | missed | marked |
| `cell. 3451234567` (mobile, no separator) | missed | marked |
| `cell. +393451234567` (+39, no separator) | missed | marked |

- **Slash.** `/` now counts as a separator when it sits between two digits. It only counts in a number whose area code starts with a trunk 0 (the national rule). A North American or `+` number with a slash still doesn't match. So reference numbers such as `prot. 2024/123456` stay unmarked, and slashed dates stay with the date pattern.
- **No separators.** The pattern used to require at least one separator, so that plain numbers (ids, VAT numbers, table values; #1884) never match. That rule stays. The one exception is a number right after a phone label: `tel`, `cell`, `fax`, `phone`, `mobile`, `telefono`, `cellulare`, `telefon`, `téléphone`, `móvil`, `gsm` and a few others, in any case, followed by up to four spaces, colons or dots. `id 0211123456`, an unlabelled `+4921511234567` and `hotel 3451234567` still don't match.

The second part of #3205, telling the user which numbers were not marked, is not in this PR.

- New test `slashed_and_labelled_unseparated_phone_numbers`. It uses the reporter's eight lines (all now marked whole) plus `Fax: 0211123456` and `Telefono 0426/123456`. title: M3: extract text from glyph names outside the Adobe Glyph List (#3169, #3170)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3169 (fixes its glyph-name case B; A is left open, see below) and #3170 (not fixed by this PR any more, see below).

A simple font without a usable `/ToUnicode` gets its text from glyph names. When a name was not in the Adobe Glyph List, the glyph was dropped from the extracted text even though the page drew it.

**Full AGL mapping** (`glyph_name_to_text` in hayro-interpret). This follows the [Adobe Glyph List Specification](https://github.com/adobe-type-tools/agl-specification): drop everything from the first `.`, split the rest on `_`, and map each part through the list or as `uniXXXX…` / `uXXXX`–`uXXXXXX` (uppercase hex only, as the specification says). `f_i`, `f_l` and `hyphen.case` now read as `fi`, `fl` and `-`. It applies to Type 1, CFF, non-embedded standard and embedded TrueType simple fonts.

**Removed after review:** an earlier version also read names that only number the glyph (`C39`, `c251`) as the code's character in StandardEncoding. @ahmadmuj showed that this invents characters: in embedded CFF and Type 1 fonts where byte 233 selects `/C1`, it extracted `Ø` for a glyph drawn exactly like `/eacute`. Such names say nothing about the character, so they read as nothing again, as on `main`.

What that costs:
- **#3170** (the 821-page book set in fonts with `C`-numbered names) gets back to extracting almost nothing. With the fallback it extracted 1,895,402 characters against 4,058 on 0.9.0; that gain came from the guess, so the issue stays open. A fix needs something that knows the glyph, such as its outline or a `/ToUnicode`, not its code.
- **#3169 case A** (`c251` small caps) likewise reads as before.

**Unit test** `text::tests::glyph_names_outside_the_glyph_list_still_read_as_text` (pdfcraft-render), one glyph per line. `/Differences` with `f_i`, `f_l`, `hyphen.case`, `C39`, `c251`, `C174`, `uni00660069`, `a12`, `foo`, `C39.sc` and `/C1` at 233 reads as `fi fl - fi`: the numbered names, `a12` and `fo…

title: Box Type 3 glyphs by their own bounds so lines set in bitmap fonts stay apart (#3171)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3171.

## Cause

The cause is the one the issue suggests. `draw_glyph` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` gives every glyph the -200..800 em box in 1000-unit glyph space, so the box is as high as the font size. A Type 3 font's size is only nominal, though. The fixture sets its bitmap fonts at 58 pt, but the glyphs are about 5 pt high and the lines are 8.4 pt apart. Each glyph box was therefore about 58 pt high and overlapped the lines above and below. The layout then joined the six lines that start at x = 371.1 into one line and ordered their glyphs by x ("EDTwIS...").

## Fix

- `Type3::glyph_bounds` (vendor patch in `hayro-interpret/src/font/type3.rs`) reads the glyph's `d1` bounding box from its glyph procedure. If there is none (a `d0` glyph), it uses `/FontBBox` when that is non-empty. It maps the box through `/FontMatrix` into the same 1000-unit glyph space that `draw_glyph` uses. `Type3Glyph::vertical_bounds` exposes it, next to the existing `advance_width` patch.
- `draw_glyph` uses those vertical bounds for Type 3 glyphs. When they are missing or empty (for example `/FontBBox [0 0 0 0]` with no `d1`), it keeps the old em box. Outline glyphs are unchanged.

## Test

`type3_lines_are_boxed_by_their_glyphs_not_by_the_font_size`: a synthetic Type 3 font set at 58 pt with `/FontBBox [0 0 0 0]` and glyphs 100 units high (5.8 pt), and two lines 8.4 pt apart that start at the same x, like the fixture. The test expects `"ab\ncd"`. With the old em box, the two lines overlap and merge.

body:
Fixes #3172.

The issue reports two problems on the same cover headline. Both are fixed here, in `crates/render/src/text.rs`:

- **Blanks inside `1.4GB` and `1GB`.** The white sentence is a second text run drawn over the big digits, with blank glyphs where the digits sit. The runs only interleave (they do not collide by `RUN_COLLISION`), so `place_glyphs` keeps them in x order and the blanks came out between the digits. The new `drop_covered_blanks` runs after `place_glyphs` on segments with two or more text runs and removes a blank glyph when more than half of its width is covered by the ink of other glyphs on the line. A blank that stands in a gap is kept. A single-run segment is not touched, because only another run can draw over a run's blanks. Dropping a glyph from the output works the same way as the existing "fake bold" redraw filter.
- **`50FREE`.** The word-gap test used the segment height, which is the tallest glyph on the line (the 39 pt digits), so the 5.3 pt gap after `50` was under the limit. The limit for each gap now uses the smaller height of the two glyphs on either side of it. It is capped at the old line limit, so a gap that was a word break before stays one. The line's typical letter gap (tracking) is still added as before.

Test: `blanks_under_a_number_and_a_word_gap_next_to_big_digits` builds two big digit pairs and a smaller sentence drawn over them with blanks where the second pair sits. Before the fix the output keeps the blanks between `1` and `4` and joins `50` to `FR`. With the fix it is `50 FR 14 CD`.

Not in scope: the missing hyphen in `PLUG-INS` (a glyph with no Unicode, #3169) and the leader-dot word gaps in #3086.

title: Drop a glyph redrawn at the same place by a later pass, not only within 4 glyphs (#3173)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3173.

The page in the issue is drawn once per column, each pass inside its own clip. A glyph that crosses the clip edge is drawn by both passes at the same place: the R of WORLD and the s of illustrated. Text extraction kept both copies, so it gave `WOR RLD` and `illusstrated`.

**Cause**

The fake-bold filter in `arrange` (`crates/render/src/text.rs`) only compared a glyph with the 4 glyphs drawn just before it. Here the second copy comes thousands of glyphs later. The run-level redraw check does not help either, because it only looks at runs of 2 or more glyphs, and the second copy starts a different run (`RLD`, `strated`).

**Fix**

- The 4-glyph check stays as it is.
- In addition, each kept glyph is recorded in a map keyed by its text (an FNV-1a hash, new `text_hash`) and its grid cell (square cells, a fifth of the glyph height wide). A new glyph also looks up its own cell and the 8 neighbouring cells. If the latest kept glyph there has the same text and passes the same position test as before, the new glyph is dropped. This is the same grid-cell lookup that the run-level redraw check below already uses.
- The position test is the same as before, so the condensed-text rule from #1467 still applies. Only the drawing-order distance changes.

With the second R gone, `LD` starts right where the first `WOR` ends, so no word break is forced. The `RUN_OVERLAP_SPACE` code from the issue does not need a change.

**Tests**

`a_glyph_redrawn_by_the_other_column_pass_is_dropped` draws `WOR` and `illus`, then 100 other glyphs, then the second pass: `R` at the same place followed by `LD`, and `s` 0.01 pt to the left followed by `trated`. It checks that the lines read `WORLD` and `illustrated`. Without the fix both duplicates are more than 4 glyphs back, so they are kept. The existing fake-bold and condensed-text tests (`fake_bold_duplicates_are_removed`, `condensed_double_letters_are_kept`) still cover the near case.

title: Keep a subscript or superscript in its line when extracting text (#3174)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3174.

In `CO2-Emissionen` the `2` is a 4.698 pt glyph on a baseline 2.67 pt lower than the 8.1 pt `CO`. `arrange` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` starts a new segment unless the em-box centres of two neighbouring glyphs are less than half the *smaller* glyph's height apart. For `O` to `2` the centres are about 3.7 pt apart and the limit was 2.35 pt, so the `2` became its own segment. The same-baseline merge (`h * 0.3`) and the block step (size ratio) did not join it back, so the `2` came out on its own line and the sentence read `CO -Emissionen`.

**Fix**

When the next glyph starts right next to the previous one (horizontal gap smaller than the smaller glyph's height), the centre test uses half the *taller* glyph's height instead. A sub- or superscript is off the line by more than half its own height but by less than half the height of the full-size glyph beside it, so it now stays in the segment, and so does the `-` after it.

Nothing else changes: for two glyphs of the same size the limit is the same as before, and glyphs with a larger gap use the old limit. The merge, block and word-gap steps are untouched. The heuristic list in the `layout` doc comment now mentions sub- and superscripts.

**Test**

`subscript_stays_in_its_word` builds `CO2-E` with the sizes and offsets from the issue (8.1 pt `CO` and `-E`, a 4.7 pt `2` 2.7 pt lower) and checks that `plain_text()` is `CO2-E`. Without the fix the `2` is a separate segment and a separate block, so the text is not `CO2-E`.

title: Draw a note without an appearance as a fixed-size icon at the corner of its Rect (#3175)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3175.

A `/Text` or `/FileAttachment` annotation with no `/AP` gets a 20 × 20 icon appearance from PdfCraft (`NOTE_SIZE`). Both the renderer and `doc_flatten` (Algorithm 8.1, `placement`) map that box onto the whole `/Rect`. So the icon was stretched over a large `/Rect`, and in a `/Rect` with no width (LaTeX `pdfcomment`) it was scaled to nothing, while flatten still counted it as drawn and deleted the note.

**Fix:** when `apply_appearance` stores a built icon on a Text or FileAttachment note, it also sets the note's `/Rect` to a `NOTE_SIZE` box at the upper-left corner of the old `/Rect`. That is where MuPDF and Poppler draw the icon. PdfCraft's own notes already use this box (`rect_for`), so nothing changes for them.

`apply_appearance` is the one place where all these paths store the appearance, so one change covers both points of the issue:

- **Large `/Rect` (render):** the display copy from `with_missing_appearances` gets the 20 × 20 `/Rect`. The source document is not changed.
- **Large and zero-width `/Rect` (flatten):** `doc_flatten` builds the missing appearance through `set_appearance`, so the icon is baked in at its real size and position and is no longer lost.

The same applies when a foreign note is restyled or imported from XFDF and PdfCraft redraws it: the new appearance is always 20 × 20, so its `/Rect` now matches it. Notes can't be resized (`set_rect` refuses them), so no user-chosen size is lost. Notes that keep their own `/AP` are not touched.

**Tests**

- `annot`: `a_note_without_an_appearance_is_shown_at_icon_size`: the display copy gives the issue's large `/Rect`, a zero-width `/Rect` and a FileAttachment with a reversed `/Rect` a 20 × 20 box at the upper-left corner. The source document keeps its rectangles.
- `edit`: `flattening_a_note_with_a_zero_width_rect_draws_a_fixed_size_icon`: flattening a zero-width note and a large note bakes both icons in at scale 1, at the upper-left corner.

Both tests fail without the fix (unchanged r…

title: Shading patterns use the stroke or fill alpha current at paint time (#3176)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3176.

`Pattern::new` ran at `scn`/`SCN` and copied `graphics_state.non_stroke_alpha` into `ShadingPattern::opacity`. That caused two bugs:

- A `gs` after the pattern colour operator (`/Pat2 scn /GS2 gs ... f`) had no effect, so the fill came out opaque.
- A stroked pattern never used `/CA`, because `SCN` also read the fill alpha.

The fix:

- `Pattern::new` no longer captures alpha. `ShadingPattern::new` starts at opacity 1.0.
- `get_paint` already picks the stroke or fill paint data. It now sets the pattern's opacity from `data.alpha` at paint time, the same way solid colours use it. This covers paths, text and stencil masks, which all go through `get_paint`.
- Tiling patterns are not changed.

Test: `shading_pattern_uses_the_alpha_current_at_paint_time` in `crates/render/src/raster.rs` renders a page in the same layout as the issue's fixture: a pattern stroke with `/CA 0.25` set after `SCN`, and a pattern fill with `/ca 0.25` set after `scn`. It checks that both come out as red at 25% over white, about (255, 191, 191). Without the fix both are opaque (255, 0, 0). The test sits next to the existing render test for a soft mask on a shading pattern (#2128).

  * Shading patterns now correctly respect opacity settings applied after the pattern is selected, for both fills and strokes.

title: xtask models: PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE serves the OCR models to a build box without network
author: zberry
body:
## Why

When the Craft apps are built from source on a machine without network access, PdfCraft is the only app whose tar packaging reaches the network: `stage_models` (`packaging/env.sh`) runs `cargo xtask models DEST`, which `curl`s the two ocrs models and their licence text (#103). Pre-placing the files does not help, because `package.sh` wipes `$WORK` first and the xtask writes straight into the stage. Today we serve those downloads through a `curl` shim on `PATH`; this change makes that unnecessary without touching how releases are built.

## What

- `fetch_all` reads `PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE`. For each `[[fetched]]` file (and its `<file>.LICENCE.txt`), `fetch_verified` first looks for a file of that name in the cache directory and copies it into place; otherwise it downloads as before. Either way the bytes land in a `.part` file, are verified against the manifest's SHA-256, and are renamed only then. A cached file that fails its hash is an error, never a silent fallback to the network.
- `cargo xtask models "$PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE"` on a connected machine lays the cache out exactly as the xtask expects, so seeding it is one command. The failed-download message now says so.
- Comments in `packaging/env.sh` and the `Needs:` headers of the Linux, FreeBSD and Windows packaging scripts, plus `docs/releasing.md`, no longer say packaging needs the network unconditionally.
- Unset or empty `PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE` behaves exactly as before, so CI and releases are unaffected.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 52 passed (three new tests: cache hit copies without downloading, a corrupt cached file is refused, empty setting is ignored).
- `cargo fmt --check -p xtask`, `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask assets`: clean, with Rust 1.99.1.
- End to end: seeded a cache with `cargo xtask models DIR` online, then ran `xtask models` under `unshare -rn` (no network) with `PDFCRAFT_ASSET_CACHE` set: both models, both licence texts and `ATTRIBUTION.txt` …

title: fix(content): accept inline image EI without preceding whitespace (#3108)
author: Ozt-y
body:
### Summary

Fixes #3108.

When parsing content streams in `crates/content`:
- In `unfiltered_image_end`: accept `EI` immediately at the computed sample length `end_data` (i.e. `separator == 0`), while maintaining the existing fallback heuristic when the preceding byte inside the computed span is whitespace (which signifies short/damaged payloads followed by `\s+EI`).
- In `end_of_image`: accept `>` as a valid preceding delimiter character before `EI` (`data[i - 1] == b'>'`), allowing ASCIIHex (`>EI`) and ASCII85 (`~>EI`) inline images to be delimited without intervening whitespace.

#### Diff Sketch & Call Tree
```text
Content::parse(stream)
  └── inline_image(data, pos)
        ├── unfiltered_image_end(data, begin, dict)
        │     - Computes exact end_data from W, H, CS, BPC
        │     + Accepts separator == 0 when preceding byte is non-whitespace
        └── end_of_image(data, begin)
              + Matches EI preceded by whitespace OR '>'
              + Preserves end_data = i (including '>') for ASCIIHex/ASCII85
```

---

### Evidence

#### Before
Running `cargo test -p pdfcraft-content` with inline images ending directly with `EI` (`2060A0E0>EI`, `ab()EI`, `ab[]EI`):
```text
thread 'tests::inline_image_terminator_without_preceding_whitespace' panicked at crates/content/src/tests.rs:406:9:
assertion `left == right` failed: operators after inline image must be preserved: BI /W 4 /H 1 /BPC 8 /CS /G /F /AHx ID 2060A0E0>EI Q BT /F1 18 Tf (After) Tj ET
  left: [[66, 73]]
 right: [[66, 73], [81], [66, 84], [84, 102], [84, 106], [69, 84]]
```
All operators following the inline image (`Q`, `BT`, `Tf`, `Tj`, `ET`) were swallowed into the inline image byte buffer.

title: fix(fonts): embedded CFF fonts declare their CMap and map glyphs through the charset
author: kouros7376
body:
## Summary

Editing text with an imported **CID-keyed OpenType (CFF) font** produced a page Acrobat refuses to parse
and, independently, the wrong glyphs for some characters. Both defects are in the CFF branch of
`crates/fonts/src/embedding.rs::embed_mapping`; the TrueType (`glyf`) branch is unaffected. One file
changed, one new test.

## Root cause

1. **Embedded CMap stream missing required entries.** For CFF fonts the Type0 `/Encoding` is an embedded
   CMap stream. It was written as a bare stream with no `/Type /CMap`, `/CMapName` or `/CIDSystemInfo`,
   all three of which ISO 32000-2 Table 118 ("Additional entries in a CMap stream dictionary") requires.
2. **CID-keyed CFF charset not applied.** A `CIDFontType0` selects glyphs by CID, and for a CID-keyed
   CFF the CID of each glyph is given by the CFF `charset` (GID → CID). The code wrote the GID as the CID
   in both the encoding CMap and `/W`. Whenever the font's charset is not the identity, the viewer drew
   a different glyph than the one measured and intended. Name-keyed CFF fonts (CID = GID,
   ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.2) were correct and stay unchanged.

## Symptoms

- Acrobat (Pro 2022) rejects the edited page: `getPageNumWords` on it fails with
  *"error parsing a form, Type 3 font or pattern"*, so its words cannot be extracted, and exporting the
  document as PNG images leaves that page out.
- Characters whose GID ≠ CID are drawn with other glyphs (in our case `(800` came out as `●00`, and `)`
  as a circled digit).

## Reproduction

1. Take any PDF with a paragraph of text.
2. `text_font_import` a CID-keyed OTF whose CFF charset is not the identity (for example Pretendard,
   OFL-1.1, `Pretendard-Regular.otf`).
3. `text_edit` the paragraph with that font, including digits and parentheses, and save.
4. Open in Acrobat: the page fails to parse (`getPageNumWords` error above) and the digits are wrong in
   other viewers. After this fix the page opens, its words are extracted, and the glyphs are right.

title: fix(edit): preserve annotation optional-content membership in marked content (#3213)
author: Ozt-y
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3213.

In `crates/edit/src/flatten.rs`, annotation flattening previously baked appearances into page streams without transferring optional-content (`/OC`) membership. This meant that annotations belonging to optional-content groups (OCGs) or membership dictionaries (OCMDs) lost their layer association once flattened, preventing viewers from toggling layer visibility dynamically.

This PR implements marked-content membership transfer and fail-closed structural validation:
- **Marked-Content Wrapping**: When an annotation has a transferable `/OC` entry, flattening registers `/PCFlOC{n}` in the page's `/Resources /Properties` dictionary (allocating collision-safe keys via `checked_add` and non-destructively cloning shared/inherited resources) and emits `/OC /PCFlOC{n} BDC ... Do ... EMC` around the appearance invocation.

- **Shared Appearance Isolation**: Annotations sharing a single Form XObject appearance stream keep separate per-call `/OC` marked-content blocks without mutating the shared appearance dictionary or stream bytes.

title: Audit text drawn inside form XObjects for faux redactions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3218

## Cause
`audit_redactions` got its text only from `pdfcraft_edit::text_lines`, which doesn't follow `Do` into form XObjects. So text drawn in a form was never checked against the covers or the `/Redact` marks, even though covers inside forms were found. Also, every rectangle inside a form was stamped with the position of the outer `Do`, so paint order inside a form couldn't be told apart.

## Fix
A new `pdfcraft_edit::form_text_lines` walks a page's form XObjects at any depth and returns their text lines in page space, each with a lexicographic paint path (page `[stream, op]` of the `Do`, then the operator index in each nested form). It fails instead of leaving text out when the depth or visit limits are reached. The audit now checks these lines next to the page's own lines, and the cover scan records the same kind of path for each rectangle, so 'painted after the text' works inside and across forms.

## Verified
- Regression tests `text_inside_form_xobjects_is_audited`, `box_before_form_text_is_not_a_cover`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-audit --lib form`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`text_lines` (Edit text) still leaves form text out (#2964), and the cover kinds the audit recognises are unchanged (#3117). Covers are now scanned before text, so the existing too-deep and cycle errors keep coming from the cover walk.

title: M10: Export ▸ Image shows the estimated size of the files (#2819, #3137)
author: SulejmaniRodrigo
body:
The Export to Image dialog now says what the files will take before exporting, in KB or MB, and the same estimate is reachable headlessly through the new read-only `doc_export_size` tool.

`Exporter::estimate` draws and encodes up to three pages — the first, the middle and the last — at the export's own resolution and format, and scales their bytes per pixel to each page's pixel count. A page whose render would exceed 16 megapixels is sampled smaller, which reads a little high because bytes per pixel fall with resolution, so the estimate errs on the large side rather than the small. On blank pages the estimate is the file's exact size; across differing pages it stays within a quarter.

The dialog measures on a worker thread with cancellation and no stale results, and only once the settings settle, so dragging the quality slider does not start a worker per frame. The strings are translated in every bundled catalog.

title: Lay out vertical (Identity-V) text as columns in the edit layer
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3216

## Cause
The edit layer's `interpret` in `crates/edit/src/text.rs` never checked the font's writing mode. Every glyph moved the pen to the right, so a vertical column got a wide, short box starting at its first glyph. Neighbouring columns then overlapped and seemed to share a baseline, so `coincident_ops` took a nearby column as a copy of the edited line and deleted it.

## Fix
On each `Tf`, `interpret` now reads the writing mode through `vertical_encoding`. For `WMode 1` fonts it moves the pen down by `/DW2`'s vertical advance (default −1000), treats TJ offsets as vertical, gives each run a tall box centred on the pen, and never joins vertical runs into horizontal lines. If the writing mode can't be read (a broken, cyclic or invalid embedded CMap), the error is passed up and listing or editing that page's text is refused instead of guessing a direction.

## Verified
- Regression tests `vertical_text_lines_are_columns_and_editing_one_keeps_its_neighbour`, `text_whose_cmap_writing_mode_cannot_be_read_is_not_edited`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib -- vertical_text_lines_are_columns_and_editing_one_keeps_its_neighbour text_whose_cmap_writing_mode_cannot_be_read_is_not_edited`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Per-glyph `/W2` vertical metrics are not read: every glyph uses `/DW2`'s advance. Group moves still refuse vertical text, as before.

author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2658 (the creation-date row). Every save goes through `pdfcraft_platform::staging::write_atomically_with`: a staging file beside the target, flushed, then renamed over it. So the file's creation date became the time of the save, on macOS (as reported) and on Windows (reproduced below).

Before the rename, the staging file now takes the replaced file's creation date. That uses `File::set_times` with `FileTimesExt::set_created` from std, on Windows and macOS, where a program can set it. It is best effort: a volume that can't store the date leaves the new file's own date, as before. A new file keeps its own date. Linux has no settable creation time, so nothing changes there.

Not in this PR (the other rows of #2658):

- read-only files: #2699, merged;

title: Find and edit images whose Do or cm spans two content streams
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3113

## Cause
The image layer of Edit a PDF (`page_images`, `reading_images`, `change_image`, `translate_images`) parsed each `/Contents` piece separately. An operator whose operands end one piece and whose keyword starts the next lost its operands: a split `Do` drew an image that was never listed, and a split `cm` was dropped. The image was then reported in the wrong place, and moving it wrote a transform built from that wrong placement.

## Fix
Images are now read from the page's streams joined (`Pieces::join`), as text editing already does, and are addressed by the `Do`'s index among the joined operators. Delete, replace, transform, crop and group moves rewrite the content with `splice`/`rewritten_contents`, which rewrite every piece a split operator spans and copy every other byte unchanged.

## Verified
- Regression test `an_image_whose_operator_starts_the_next_stream_can_be_selected_moved_and_deleted`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib an_image_whose_operator_starts_the_next_stream_can_be_selected_moved_and_deleted`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Nothing outside the image layer: text editing already joins the pieces, and Form XObject contents are still parsed as their own single stream.

title: Renderer: sample a mesh shading over its triangles alone, not the whole path
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Zooming into a dense CAD page could hit the render watchdog: "page 57 took longer than 20 s and
was skipped; the page may be damaged or extremely complex". The page (BricsCAD, 3370 × 1524 pt,
251,000 single-segment strokes, 310 one-triangle type 4 shadings painted with `sh` at 50% alpha)
took **2 s per 1024 px tile at every zoom** and 7.9 s fit-to-width, while a 16 px tile of it took
65 ms: neither parsing nor the strokes were the cost. `sh` fills the whole canvas with the
shading, and `Renderer::set_paint` sampled the mesh texture over the whole path, one hash lookup
and one texel per canvas pixel, 310 times per tile.

- hayro-interpret patch (35): `EncodedShadingPattern::extent`, the device-space pixels a mesh's
  triangles touched when it was encoded (`None` for shadings that paint everywhere, and for a
  mesh with a `/Background`, which paints between its triangles).
- hayro patch (19): `set_paint` intersects the texture with that extent, pads instead of
  repeating it (the pixel ring around the triangles stays transparent), and returns
  `PaintSetup::Nothing` for a mesh with no triangle on the canvas, which the fill, stroke, rect
  and stencil callers skip.

`vendor/README.md` rows updated (note: upstream has the hayro and hayro-interpret rows
duplicated; both copies were edited alike).

## How you verified it

- `page_timing` (release) on the page: fit 7864 → 880 ms; a 1024 px tile 2030 → 85 ms at 100%
  and 2030 → 70 ms at 400%; the 16 px tile unchanged (65 ms: the page's re-interpretation, paid
  per tile). **Output hashes identical** before and after for
  all four scenarios, so no pixel changed.

title: M7: work out each font's space width once per paragraph rewrite (#2616)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #2616 ("every letter added or deleted freezes the program").

Each keystroke in Edit text rebuilds the paragraph's draft (`text_edit_layout` → `rewrite_styled_block`). Inside, the per-character `advance` measurement calls `source_space` for every character. When the source font can't show a space, `source_space` scans every font on the page and builds a `Metrics` for each, which includes decoding the font program. That is common: LaTeX- and Sphinx-made subsets space words with `TJ` kerning and have no space in their ToUnicode. So the draft did a page-wide font scan once per character.

The space width of each font is now worked out once per rewrite, before the per-character pass. The three call sites in `text_regions.rs` read it from that table. Results are identical; only the repeat work goes away.

## How you verified it

**Measured** with `text_edit_layout`, which is what each keystroke runs. Release CLI built with craft-fonts, 10 keystrokes appended one by one, on page 20 of NVIDIA's public *Virtual GPU Software User Guide* (Sphinx output; its body font maps no space):

| paragraph | `main` per keystroke | this PR per keystroke |
|---|---|---|
| 383 characters, with `▶` bullets | ~460 ms | ~71 ms |
| 199 characters, plain ASCII | ~255 ms | ~16 ms |
| 78 characters | ~125 ms | ~16 ms |

The JSON output of all 30 layouts is byte-identical between the two builds. Text left unchanged was already fast, ~11 ms, so the cost was in the rewrite.

**Regression test** `a_long_draft_in_a_font_without_a_space_works_out_the_space_width_once`. The page is a two-row paragraph in a Type0 subset whose ToUnicode has no space. The test lays out a 380-character draft and counts `source_space` calls through a test-only thread-local counter.
- With the fix: 1 call.
- With `text_regions.rs` put back to `main`: it fails with "worked out 1055 times for 380 characters", and takes 1.39 s instead of 0.02 s.
- A first version of this test, on a one-row paragraph…

title: Read doubled-sign integers like --280 in the COS lexer
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3111

## Cause
`Lexer::number` tolerated a doubled sign (`--280.0`) only in its real-number branch. The integer branch passed `--280` straight to `parse::<i64>` and `parse::<f64>`, which both fail. That raised a syntax error, so a `TJ` array containing `--280` didn't parse and the whole operator was dropped by the edit layer, the export and redaction.

## Fix
The integer branch now collapses a leading doubled minus sign to a single one, as the real branch already does, before parsing. `--280` reads as `Int(-280)`, and `[(Hello) --280 (World)] TJ` parses.

## Verified
- Regression test `doubled_sign_integer_reads_like_the_real_form`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-cos --lib doubled_sign_integer_reads_like_the_real_form`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I didn't change the real-number branch or any other lexer behavior. I didn't change the content, edit or redaction crates, because they pick up the fix through the shared lexer. The regression test is at the lexer level and does not run the full repro PDF through Edit text, export or redaction.

title: Read /ActualText from named property lists in edit text and export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3110

## Cause
The edit layer's content interpreter (`interpret` in crates/edit/src/text.rs) read `/ActualText` only when the second `BDC` operand was an inline dictionary. When that operand was a name (`/Span /MC0 BDC`), it was never looked up in the resources' `/Properties`, because the interpreter received only the `/Font` dictionary. So Edit text and the Office export showed the glyph text instead.

## Fix
The interpreter's `logical_text: bool` flag is now `Option<&Dict>` and carries the current resources' `/Properties`: the page's in `text_lines`, and the page's or form's in `reading_lines`. A name operand is resolved there before `/ActualText` is read, with the same 4 MB size limit as before. Named lists that have no `/ActualText`, and names that are missing, still keep the glyph text.

## Verified
- Regression test `actual_text_from_named_property_list`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib actual_text_from_named_property_list`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`clear_block` and `translate_blocks` still pass `None`, so they do not read `/ActualText`, as before. The reading path (`pdfcraft-cli text`, Find) and the renderers already handle named lists and are unchanged.

title: fix(engine): undo past a security change saves in full (#3276)
author: skylartaylor
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3276. Undo past a save that changed security now appends the restored state to the newest earlier save with its security, instead of to the last saved file.

**Bug.** After undo restores a snapshot from before the last save, `Session::save_bytes` reopens the saved file and appends the snapshot as an incremental update. When the two use different encryption — undoing a saved protect, remove-protection, password change or rekey, or a compaction that renumbered `/Encrypt` — the update is read with the wrong key. Every round trip reopened with blank pages, and remove → save → undo → save left the plaintext revision inside a file that reports itself encrypted.

**Fix.**
- `Document::output_security_identity` is what a save encrypts with: the security dictionary and, below revision 5, the first `/ID`, which together determine the key. Passwords, authentication level and where `/Encrypt` lives (object number or inline) are not part of it.
- `Session::save_bytes` compares the snapshot's identity with the saved file's, recorded at `mark_saved`. When they differ, the snapshot goes onto the newest file of this session that has its security and continues its source (at worst that source), opened with the snapshot's key. Earlier saves in the same security stay in the chain; revisions in the other security, all undone, are dropped, as saving any security change already does. An unedited snapshot that is its target is saved as those bytes unchanged, so a restored signature stays valid.
- `overlay_changes_from` returns `Ok(false)`, changing nothing, when security differs or the target has a pending security change. Otherwise it takes the snapshot's `/Encrypt` place for writing only, so undo past an optimized save still appends to it, and it writes again any unchanged object packed in an object stream whose number the snapshot reuses or lacks; those read back as `null` before.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warni…

title: Keep text rows in other layers, gs states or Tz out of a paragraph
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3115

## Cause
Edit text joined rows into one paragraph by position and font alone. A rewrite then wrote every row in a single row's place and state, so a row inside an `/OC` marked-content sequence, after a `gs`, or at another `Tz` lost that state, or passed it on to the edited row (for example, a visible row moved into a hidden layer).

## Fix
The text interpreter now records, for each run, the `/OC` optional content groups around it and the `gs` resources applied before it (a new `Paint` key). Runs and rows whose key differs are no longer joined into one line or paragraph, and rows with a different horizontal scale no longer join. Editing one row now leaves the others' operators and state as they were.

## Verified
- Regression test `editing_a_row_keeps_the_layer_opacity_and_scale_of_the_rows_around_it`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit --lib editing_a_row_keeps_the_layer_opacity_and_scale_of_the_rows_around_it`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Text hidden by an OFF layer still appears in Edit text as its own paragraph. This change does not evaluate optional content visibility. A row inside a form XObject drawn within an `/OC` sequence does not inherit that layer. Two rows with different horizontal scales on the same baseline can still join.

title: fix(organize): prune named destinations without recursive calls
author: PerchAnton
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3309. Deleting a page from a deeply nested `/Names /Dests` tree could overflow the call stack. Pruning now uses an explicit stack and a seen set, visiting shared and cyclic indirect nodes once while retaining destinations for surviving pages.

Following [review feedback](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/3311#issuecomment-6254879404), there is no name-count traversal budget: valid documents with 60,000 named destinations remain editable. The former budget-refusal tests and documentation are removed. `delete_pages` documents its existing nontransactional low-level error contract; callers needing atomic edits use a working clone. A code comment distinguishes this complete cleanup walk from the depth-limited bookmark lookup.

The synthetic regressions inspect every destination target after deletion, undo, redo and save/reopen, including a 16,384-node chain and a 60,000-name document. Undo restores the deleted page and its names; redo removes them again and preserves surviving targets. Tests assert the actual full/incremental save modes, the incremental prefix, unsaved metadata, unchanged source bytes and rendered pixels. Shared/cyclic-node and inline-root coverage remains; the organize regressions are grouped with page-deletion tests. Roadmap/parity records describe the final behavior with unchanged estimates.

title: M2: a fax image with fewer /Rows than its /Height is decoded to its height (#3308)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3308.

## Cause

The steel schedule table in the reporter's drawing (`pdfplot16.hdi`, AutoCAD's plotter driver) is a 2418 × 2920 Group 4 fax image in an `/Indexed` space. Its `/DecodeParms` say `/Rows 2418`, which equals `/Columns` and not the image's `/Height` of 2920. The CCITT filter decoded only `/Rows` rows, so the bottom 502 rows stayed zero, which is index 0 (black). That's the black block under the table in the screenshot. MuPDF and the reporter's other viewer draw all 2920 rows. Patching a copy of the file to `/Rows 2920` makes PdfCraft draw the whole table as well.

## Fix

Vendored hayro-syntax patch (18) in `filter/ccitt.rs`: a non-zero `/Rows` below the image's `/Height` no longer cuts the image short, and the decoder decodes to the height. When the data really ends sooner, the existing lenient path still returns the rows it decoded. `/Rows 0` keeps patch (17)'s meaning.

## Tests

- `raster::tests::group4_fax_with_rows_below_its_height_decodes_to_the_image_height`: an 8 × 4 Group 4 image with `/Rows 2` and `/BlackIs1 true` (so the decoded rows are white and undecoded rows show black), through `/DeviceGray` and `/Indexed`, plus a `/Rows 4` control. It fails without the fix: `[/Indexed …] /Rows 2: image row at y 27 is decoded`, left `[0, 0, 0, 255]`.
- The reporter's file, rendered at 72 dpi with this branch: the whole table shows.
- Gate: fmt, clippy `-p pdfcraft-render -D warnings`, render tests 310 passed, xtask layers/assets.
  - Standalone `hayro-syntax` has 2 failures, `pdf_version_header` and `pdf_version_catalog`. They are the same on `main`: those tests read fixture files that aren't vendored.

title: The recovery folder is owner-only on Unix
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

Recovery snapshots are unsaved copies of open documents. `RecoveryStore` made its folder with `create_dir_all`, so the folder got the default mode (usually `0755` with a `022` umask), and the first snapshot file got the default mode for a new file (#2544 keeps the mode only of a file that is replaced). On a shared Linux or macOS machine, other accounts could list the folder and read the snapshots of documents that are not encrypted. Encrypted documents were already safe, since they are stored encrypted.

Now `RecoveryStore::create_dir` makes the folder and, on Unix, sets it to `0700` when it is open to group or others. `claim` (when an instance starts) and `write` (each autosave) both go through it, so a folder an earlier version made is tightened at the next start. This follows `image_pick::write_clipboard_file`, which keeps its folder `0700` the same way. With the folder owner-only, the files inside are out of reach whatever their own mode, so `write_atomically` is unchanged.

Windows is unchanged: `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is already per-user.

title: Render weekday letters in FormCalc date pictures
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:1929-1957 (format_date), with DateFmt returning "EEEE, MMMM D, YYYY" at :2333` (no existing issue): FormCalc Num2Date/Format ignore the weekday letters in a date picture: DateFmt(4) gives a literal "EEEE".

## Cause
`format_date` only handled the Y, M and D letters and copied every other character into the output. `DateFmt(4)` returns "EEEE, MMMM D, YYYY", so `Num2Date` and `Format` printed the literal text "EEEE" instead of the weekday.

## Fix
`format_date` now handles runs of `E`. `EEEE` gives the full weekday name, `EEE` the three-letter name, and `E` or `EE` the weekday number (1 = Sunday). The weekday is worked out from the day serial, where 1900-01-01 was a Monday.

## Verified
- Regression test `date_pictures_render_the_weekday_letters`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-js date_pictures_render_the_weekday_letters`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`Format` still decides that a picture is a date picture only when it contains `YY` or `DD`, so a picture made only of `E` letters is still treated as a number picture. `parse_date` (used by `Date2Num`) is unchanged. Other letters in a picture still pass through as literal text.

* **New Features**
  * Date formatting now supports weekday tokens: `E` and `EE` display a numeric weekday, `EEE` displays an abbreviated name, and `EEEE` or more displays the full weekday name.

title: M6: Treat AcroForm /MaxLen 0 as unlimited
author: djmushin
body:
## Summary

Fixes an AcroForm text-field compatibility issue where a field
specifying `/MaxLen 0` could incorrectly reject text input.

The fix treats an explicit `/MaxLen 0` as an unlimited character
length, including when the field inherits a positive maximum
length from a parent field.

This improves compatibility with existing PDF forms without
changing the behavior of fields that specify positive limits.

## Background — Follow-up to PR #3168

This change was originally submitted as part of #3168, which
combined AcroForm performance optimizations, text-field
compatibility improvements, and optional profiling instrumentation.

Following maintainer review, the contribution was separated into
independent pull requests to simplify review, testing, and merging.

The performance optimizations have already been submitted
separately as #3318.

This PR contains only the `/MaxLen 0` compatibility fix,
its regression tests, and supporting documentation.

Optional profiling instrumentation has been excluded.

The compatibility branch was independently rebased onto
upstream `main` at commit `932bf9c6` and validated.

This restructuring directly addresses the scope concerns
raised during the review of #3168.

## Problem

Some existing PDF forms explicitly define `/MaxLen 0` on
text fields.

Previously, PDFcraft could interpret this value as a maximum
length of zero characters, preventing users from entering text.

This could also occur when a field explicitly specified
`/MaxLen 0` while inheriting a positive limit from a parent.

In these cases, the explicit zero value should represent
an unlimited field rather than preventing input.

## Changes

- Treats explicit `/MaxLen 0` as unlimited.
- Preserves positive maximum-length restrictions.
- Ensures an explicit zero overrides an inherited positive limit.
- Adds regression coverage for the affected behavior.
- Updates the forms documentation and Acrobat feature-parity records.

title: Rail: scroll the panel buttons above the page navigation in short windows (#3282)
author: majidninja
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3282.

The right rail puts its panel buttons (Comments, Bookmarks, … Tags) top-down and the page navigation cluster (page field, view history, prev/next, zoom, fit, rotate, page display, zoom in/out) bottom-up in the same space. Nothing stops the two from meeting, so in a window that isn't tall enough for both they get drawn on top of each other. That's what the screenshot in the issue shows: the page number field sits over the Tags icon.

Now the navigation cluster is its own `Panel::bottom` inside the rail, and the panel buttons go in a vertical `ScrollArea` in whatever height is left above it. In a tall window nothing looks different. In a short one the buttons clip above the navigation and scroll with the wheel. That's intended: it's a plain egui `ScrollArea` with the default scrollbar, nothing rail-specific.

The diff in `chrome.rs` looks big, but it's only the two blocks swapping places plus the two wrappers. `git diff -w` shows the real change. The navigation code itself is unchanged.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`, all green)

New test: `short_window_rail_buttons_scroll_clear_of_page_navigation` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui.rs`. It opens a document in a 1000×560 window and checks that the first rail button is above the page field and that Tags starts out below it, so the window really is too short. Then it scrolls the rail and checks that Tags ends up fully above the page field while the field stays where it was. I reverted the `chrome.rs` change and the test fails on the Tags check, as it should.

title: Render: a five-point polyline is no longer painted as its bounding box
author: Hamza0101
body:
A PDF holding a five-point open polyline whose ends reach the corners of its own bounding box renders as a rectangle: the middle disappears and the open side comes out closed.

## Measured with `pdfcraft-cli`

Content stream, nothing else on the page:

```
0 0 0 K  2 w
80 38 m  80 21.75 l  60.571 29.875 l  40 21.75 l  40 38 l  S
```

`pdfcraft-cli render … --dpi 72`, reading the pixels back:

| | peak drawn near (60, 30) | dark pixels along the bounding box's top edge |
|---|---|---|
| **before** | **no** | **36** — a straight edge the file does not contain |
| after | yes | 0 |
| six-point zigzag (control) | yes | 0 |
| real rectangle (control) | no | 36 |

## Cause

`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/context.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) fn path_as_rect(path: &BezPath) -> Option<Rect> {
    // One MoveTo, three LineTo, one ClosePath
    if path.elements().len() != 5 {
        return None;
    }
    …
    if corners[0] && corners[1] && corners[2] && corners[3] { Some(bbox) } else { None }
}
```

The comment names the shape it means to match. `len() != 5` also admits **one `MoveTo` and four `LineTo`** — a five-point open polyline — and the corner test only asks whether all four bounding-box corners were *visited by some point*, never whether *every* point is a corner. Both call sites in `interpret/path.rs` then call `device.draw_rect(&rect, …)`.

The zigzag slips through because its ends and the points beside them land on all four corners, and (60.571, 29.875) — the peak — is simply ignored:

| point | corner |
|---|---|
| (80, 38) | max x, max y |
| (80, 21.75) | max x, min y |
| **(60.571, 29.875)** | **none — the peak** |
| (40, 21.75) | min x, min y |
| (40, 38) | min x, max y |

The condition is narrow, which is why only some art is affected: 3, 4 or 6 points are fine, and `s` (closepath + stroke) escapes it because the `ClosePath` makes six elements. So the same drawing survives if its author happened to close the path.

`push_clip_path` skips a clip whose rectangle cover…

title: cli: info names the standard a document declares
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes the verifiable half of #3319, "PDFcraft does not recognize a PDF/A file".

## What I could check

The report has no sample file, and the bot has asked for one. But one part of it is objective, so I built a file that declares PDF/A — `pdfaid:part` 2 and `pdfaid:conformance` B in the catalog's XMP metadata stream — and inspected it:

```
$ pdfcraft-cli info declares-pdfa.pdf
{ … "encrypted": false, "tagged": false, "javascript": false, "layers": 0,
      "xfa": null, "pdf_version": "1.7", … }      # 24 fields, no mention of PDF/A
```

Detection is not the problem: `pdfcraft_preflight::declared` reads that declaration, and the app's Standards panel renders it as "PDF/A-2b". It is `info` — the documented "document summary" — that left it out, so anything driving the CLI, and anyone checking a file without opening the app, is told nothing about the standard.

## Change

`info` gains three fields, from the same `declared()` call the Standards panel makes, so the CLI and the panel agree by construction instead of parsing the metadata twice:

```
declares-pdfa.pdf    "pdfa": "2B",  "pdfua": null,  "output_intents": []
a plain PDF          "pdfa": null,  "pdfua": null,  "output_intents": []
```

`pdfa` is the part and conformance together (`"2B"`, `"3A"`), which is how the level is written and spoken; `pdfua` is the part; `output_intents` lists the condition identifiers the panel already shows. Nothing else in the summary changes.

**Where it is read.** In the CLI, not in `pdfcraft_render::Inspect`. `xtask layers` puts `render` at 3 and `preflight` at 4, so the summary struct cannot reach the declaration, while an app may depend on any layer. The document is opened once more through `pdfcraft_cos::Document::open_with_password`, with the password `info` was given, and a file that fails to parse there simply declares nothing rather than failing the command.

## Tests

`apps/pdfcraft-cli/tests/info_standards.rs`:

- `info_names_the_declared_pdfa_level` — a declaring file …

title: Drop U+FFFE and U+FFFF from XFDF/XML form-data export
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs:192-209 (esc), used by export_xfdf (:445) and export_data XML (:594-612)` (no existing issue): XFDF/XML form-data export writes U+FFFE/U+FFFF, so the exported file is not well-formed XML.

## Cause
`esc()` in the xfdf crate escaped `& < > "` and dropped C0 control characters, but it passed the XML 1.0 noncharacters U+FFFE and U+FFFF through as raw text. A field value, comment or attribute containing one produced an export that is not well-formed XML, and roxmltree rejects it on import.

## Fix
`esc()` now leaves out U+FFFE and U+FFFF, as it does for C0 controls. This matches the XFA data writer and the Office exporter, and covers both `export_xfdf` and the XML `export_data`. The regression test exports a value with both characters, checks the XFDF and XML parse, and checks the value comes out as `abc`.

## Verified
- Regression test `xml_exports_drop_xml_noncharacters`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf --lib xml_exports_drop_xml_noncharacters`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The other `export_data` formats (FDF, CSV) and the XFA and Office writers are unchanged.

title: M10: put image pages on a chosen paper size (#3273)
author: saad-mughal435
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3273.

A photo becomes a page as large as its pixels, so a 4000 × 3000 phone picture with no stored resolution gives a 4000 × 3000 pt page (about 1.41 × 1.06 m), and a set of photos of different pixel sizes gives pages of several different sizes, none of them a paper size. The `dpi` option added for #190 changes the scale but not that.

`doc_create` (`from: "images"`) and `doc_create_multiple` (both `combine` and `separate` modes) now take:

- **`page_size`** — a paper name (`A4`, `Letter`, `Legal`, `Tabloid`, `A0`–`A6`, `ARCH A`–`E`, `ANSI C`–`E`) or `[width, height]` in points. The image is scaled to fit and centred.
- **`page_turn`** — turn the sheet to match each image's orientation, so a landscape photo gets a landscape page. Default `true`; a square image never turns the sheet.

The shape the issue asked for, as `pdfcraft-create::ImagePage`:

```rust
pub enum ImagePage {
    #[default]
    Image,                                        // today's behaviour
    Fixed { width: f64, height: f64, turn: bool },
}
```

Nothing is cropped or stretched: the scale is `min(pw/w, ph/h)`, so the aspect ratio is kept and an image smaller than the sheet is enlarged to fill it rather than left in a corner. Pixels are still never resampled.

**Two things worth noting about where the code went:**

- The paper-name match moved out of `doc_print` into `printing::paper_named`, so Create and Print answer exactly the same names instead of growing a second list. `pdfcraft-print` owns the table and is `create`'s own layer, so the name is resolved at L7 and `create` takes plain points — no new same-layer dependency.
- `ImagePage::Image` is the default and every existing entry point delegates to it, so `from_images`, `from_images_with_resolution` and `convert_to_pdf` are unchanged for their callers. A test asserts the default path writes a byte-identical file.

title: M10: exported TIFF and JPEG pages record the resolution they were drawn at
author: MortenHusted
body:
## What this changes

Pages exported as TIFF or JPEG now say the resolution they were drawn at. TIFF exports are LZW-compressed, as `encode_tiff`'s comment already said they were.

The bugs, both on `main`:
- **No resolution.** A page exported as TIFF said `1 × 1` with no unit, whatever the dpi, and a JPEG said nothing (JFIF aspect ratio 1:1). Other programs fall back to a default, usually 72 dpi, so a 300-dpi Letter page opens and prints as a 35 × 46 in poster.
- **No compression.** The TIFF was written uncompressed, although the comment says "LZW-compressed by the encoder's default". `image`'s `TiffEncoder` doesn't compress. A Letter page at 300 dpi came to 25 MB.

`pdfcraft-cli render --dpi 300` on page 1 of a 426 × 485 pt PDF, read with `tiffinfo`:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Resolution | `1, 1 (unitless)` | `300, 300 pixels/inch` |
| Compression | None | LZW |
| Size | 10.8 MB | 65 KB |

What changed:
- **Resolution.** `encode_image`, `encode_jpeg` and `encode_tiff` take the dpi to record: TIFF `XResolution`/`YResolution` in inches, the JFIF density in dots per inch.
  - `Exporter::image` records the resolution the page was actually drawn at (`dpi_used`). A page too large for the renderer at the asked resolution says the lower one, which is the one `doc_export_images` reports in `lower_dpi`.
  - `pdfcraft-cli render` records `--dpi`. It refuses oversized pages, so that is the resolution drawn.
  - This reaches File ▸ Export ▸ Image, the `doc_export_images` tool and `pdfcraft-cli render`.
- **TIFF writing.** `encode_tiff` uses the `tiff` crate directly, because `image`'s `TiffEncoder` can set neither the resolution nor the compression. `tiff` 0.11 is already in the graph through `image`, and `pdfcraft-create` depends on it the same way.
- **LZW** is a commit of its own, so it can be dropped on its own (see the last section).
- The third commit adds my own `contributors/people.toml` entry.

title: fix(export): omit hidden-layer text from Office output (#3211)
author: robertobulltech
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3211. HTML, RTF, DOCX and PPTX exports, and Edit text, omit text hidden by the PDF's default optional-content configuration. This covers nested marked content, OCG/OCMD membership policies and bounded visibility expressions, and forms' own `/OC`. Hidden text still advances the text state, and editing visible paragraphs preserves hidden source operators. ActualText around hidden content or forms cannot reintroduce hidden text; non-form replacements retain their behavior.

The review findings are addressed:
- Redaction auditing reads retained page glyphs, including default-hidden layers, through a dedicated reader. It ignores ActualText substitutions so accessibility strings cannot conceal retained glyphs. Both covered text and unapplied marks are still reported.
- Visibility uses a depth counter and the first hidden scope's depth, with constant memory and no 256-level visibility cutoff. Paragraph/ActualText metadata remains bounded, with excess closes matched correctly.
- Referenced OCG/OCMD results are cached across operators and form visits, up to 65,536 entries per read. XObject resources resolve once per interpreter invocation, and the redundant form visibility check is removed.

Rebased onto `main` at `ec0a9650`, preserving upstream clipping-path safeguards, named ActualText handling, joined content streams, form traversal budgets and truncation reporting, plus the unrelated upstream automation tests and parity evidence.

title: #2922: on Windows, draw with Direct3D 12 only, not wgpu's OpenGL backend
author: benandez
body:
Fixes #2922.

## Cause
@KNUFFIXX's stacks in #2922 show the print thread hanging in `StartPage`, inside the Kyocera KX v3 driver. The driver calls `EnumWindows` and then `GetWindowTextA` on every top-level window. One of PdfCraft's windows is wgpu-hal's hidden `wgpu Device Class` window (GL backend, `gles/wgl.rs`). Its thread blocks in `drop_rx.recv()` and never pumps messages, so `WM_GETTEXT` never returns, and the job stays at Spooling with 0 bytes. With `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` that window is gone and the job prints. Upstream: gfx-rs/wgpu#10504 and #10505.

## Change
- `configure_gpu`: on Windows the instance backends go from `DX12 | GL` to `DX12`.
  - A machine where wgpu can't start still gets OpenGL through the existing glow retry in `main`. glow creates no hidden wgpu window.
  - A GPU with no D3D12 driver now draws through WARP instead of wgpu's GL backend. `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl` gives it hardware OpenGL.
- The test now asserts that GL is not among the Windows backends, and `docs/development.md` is updated.

## Testing
- On Linux: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p pdfcraft gpu_backends`.
- The new assertion only runs on Windows, so CI's Windows job covers it.
- Not yet tried with a Kyocera printer. @KNUFFIXX, could you try a build of this branch?

title: Create from images: put each image on a paper size
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3273.

## The problem

A phone or camera JPEG carries 72 dpi, or no resolution at all, so a 4000 × 3000 photo becomes a 4000 × 3000 pt page — about 1.41 × 1.06 m. The `dpi` choice from #190 changes that size, but a set of photos with different pixel sizes still gives pages of different sizes, and none of them is a paper size.

## Change

`pageSize` — a paper name — or `pageWidth` and `pageHeight` in points put every image on a page of one size, scaled to fit and centred:

```
default                400×300 pt       (a page per image, unchanged)
pageSize=a4            595.28×841.89
pageSize=letter        612×792
pageWidth/pageHeight   300×300
```

Taken by `doc_create from:"images"`, `doc_create_multiple` and `doc_combine` — the three the ticket names. Omitting them leaves today's behaviour exactly as it is.

Placement is a fit, not a stretch or a crop. A 400 × 300 pt image on a 300 × 300 pt page draws as:

```
q 300.000 0 0 225.000 0.000 37.500 cm /Im0 Do Q
```

— 300 × 225, proportions kept, centred 37.5 pt up.

## Four decisions worth your eye

- **One list of paper sizes.** Names resolve through `pdfcraft_print::PAPERS`, the 20-size table Print already uses, so "a4" cannot drift from Print's A4. `create` and `print` are both layer 4 and cannot see each other, so the lookup lives in `engine` (layer 6), which already depends on both. `"letter"` and the table's own `"US Letter"` both work, case-insensitively.
- **No signature churn.** `convert_to_pdf` and `as_pdf` have twenty-one callers between them, so `convert_to_pdf_on_pages` and `as_pdf_on_pages` sit beside them and the existing calls are untouched.
- **"Scaled to fit" scales both ways.** A small image fills the page rather than sitting small in the middle of it. I first wrote it capped at 1:1 and my own test caught the contradiction; filling the page is the plainer reading of the request and gives pages that look alike, which is the point. title: fix(windows): name the single-instance socket by the session id, so a launch without SESSIONNAME finds its session's window (#3338)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3338.

## Cause

As @halr9000 traced it: on Windows, the single-instance socket was named after `%SESSIONNAME%` (`instance-Console.sock`, `instance-RDP-Tcp3.sock`). Task Scheduler, services and some remote shells start a process without `SESSIONNAME`. Such a launch looked for `instance.sock`, never found the window opened from Explorer, and opened a second one.

## Fix

The socket is now named by the **session id** in the process token: `instance-s<id>.sock`.
- The id is read through `winsafe`'s `HACCESSTOKEN::GetCurrentProcessToken().GetTokenInformation(SessionId)`, with the `advapi` feature added. No `unsafe` is needed.
- A scheduled launch runs in the user's session, so it gets the same id as the window opened from Explorer, and hands its files to it.
- Each session has its own id, so a launch in one session never hands files to a window in another. This answers @earlvanze's review: the first version of this PR fell back to the console's name, which could have sent a file from a Remote Desktop session to a console window.
- `SESSIONNAME` names the socket only if the id can't be read.

## Tests

- **Naming.** `each_windows_session_gets_its_own_socket_name`: the same id gives one name with or without `SESSIONNAME`, different ids give different names whatever `SESSIONNAME` says, and the `SESSIONNAME` fallback applies only without an id.
- **Windows only.** `this_process_has_a_session_id`: the token gives an id, and the socket path uses it.
- **A real scheduled task (Windows 11).**
  - Setup: PdfCraft opened on `A.pdf`, then an interactive `schtasks … /IT` task launched it on `B.pdf`. The task's environment had no `SESSIONNAME`.
  - `main`: 2 processes, both in session 1, and the first window still showed `A.pdf`.
  - This PR: 1 process, and the first window switched to `B.pdf`.
- **Mutation batch.** Five mutants, all killed: ignoring the id, `session_id()` always `None`, the socket path ignoring the id, a restored "Console" default, and one name for every id.…

title: M5: Fill & Sign panel shows "Flatten Fill & Sign when saving" (#2149, #3339)
author: benandez
body:
Refs #2149, #3339.

## Problem
Fill & Sign saves text, marks and signatures as annotations by default (`flatten_fill_sign_on_save: false`). The only way to lock them into the page is a checkbox in Preferences, which people filling a form don't find (#2149, and #3339 today).

## Change
- The Fill & Sign panel shows the same **Flatten Fill & Sign when saving** checkbox under *Sign yourself*, with the explanation from Preferences. It's bound to the existing setting, so it persists, shows in Preferences, and works the same through `ui.state` and settings.
- Both strings already exist and are translated, so the catalogues don't change.

title: Clamp the zoom-anchor scroll to the content so zooming out no longer jolts the page (#3266)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3266.

**Cause.** While zooming, `document_area` keeps the point under the pointer still by setting the scroll offset to `point - rel` from `view.zoom_anchor`. That offset was only kept above zero, never below the maximum scroll. Zooming out beside a page that becomes narrower (or shorter) than the window asks for an offset past the end of the content. egui clamps the offset only after the frame is drawn, so every zoom frame showed the page shifted to one side, and when the zoom stopped it snapped to where it belongs. The further the pointer is from the centre, the larger the requested offset and the bigger the jump, as the issue says.

**Fix.** A small `anchored_scroll` helper clamps the anchored offset to `0..=content - viewport` on both axes, the same bound the `goto` branch right below already applies ("egui clamps only after drawing ...") and the Hand-tool pan uses. The pointer zoom and the generic "zoom changed" fallback both set `zoom_anchor`, so this one place covers them. Inside the scrollable range the offset is unchanged, so zooming in still keeps the point under the pointer.

**Test.** `zoom_anchor_scroll_stays_within_the_content` checks an offset past the end, before the start, inside the range, and content smaller than the viewport.

title: M2: a tiling pattern drawn once shows its cell at full scale (#3349)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3349.

## Cause

The network-switch pictures in the reporter's slides (Acrobat PDFMaker 11 for PowerPoint) are picture fills. PDFMaker writes each one as a tiling pattern meant to be drawn once: `/PaintType 1 /TilingType 3 /XStep 2147480100 /YStep 2147480100`, with a matrix that flips y, and a single image in the cell. The fill is a rectangle the size of the cell.

Vendored hayro patch (3), `tiling_cell_scale`, keeps a cell pixmap within 3000 px a side by lowering the cell's scale to `3000 / step`. With a step of about 2.1 × 10⁹, that is a scale of about 1.4 × 10⁻⁶, so the 183 × 17 picture was drawn far smaller than a pixel and disappeared. MuPDF and Acrobat draw it. Across the 19 pages, the pages with such fills (1–4, 8, 10, 17) differed from MuPDF in 10k–22k pixels at 72 dpi; with this fix they differ in about 6k–8k, which is antialiasing noise, about the same as on the untouched pages.

## Fix

Vendored hayro patch (20), in `renderer.rs` (`set_paint`, tiling branch). When the step is too large for a cell pixmap and the painted area can only meet the first cell, the cell's `/BBox` is drawn at full scale into a pixmap with a 1-pixel transparent border, and sampled with `Extend::Pad` instead of `Repeat`. So the cell shows once and nothing repeats or smears.

`shows_one_cell` decides "only the first cell". It maps the path's device bounds (grown by the stroke's width for a stroke) into pattern space, and checks that the cells one step away (k = ±1, in x and y) can't be reached. Every other path keeps today's behaviour, including the 3000 px cap.

## Tests

- `a_tiling_pattern_drawn_once_shows_its_cell`: PowerPoint's step and a flipped matrix, with the cell in the middle of the page. Filled and stroked, the cell shows, and nothing appears left, right, above or below it. An ordinary step of 20 still tiles.
- `a_large_step_still_tiles_where_the_next_cell_shows`: steps of 3100 at scale 1, just over the cap. The cell to the right, left, above and below still shows …

title: fix(a11y): join and splice page content streams with cross-stream rules (#3217)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #3217

### Problem
When a page's `/Contents` is an array of streams, ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2 specifies that they represent a single concatenated stream where tokens can be split across stream boundaries and a `%` comment at the end of one stream without a newline continues into the next stream up to its first end-of-line.

In `pdfcraft-a11y`:
1. `autotag::content_bytes`, `alt::page_content`, and `content::page_content` joined `/Contents` streams with `b'\n'` instead of `b' '`, prematurely ending any trailing `%` comment at a stream boundary so commented-out operators at the start of the next stream were parsed and emitted as live content.
2. `alt::artifact_marked_content` (`mark_decorative`) parsed and re-serialized each stream in isolation with `pdfcraft_content::parse` + `serialize_ops`, dropping operands of operators split across two content streams and stripping trailing cross-stream comments.

### Solution
- Join `/Contents` streams with `b' '` in `autotag::content_bytes`, `alt::page_content`, and `content::page_content` (matching `pdfcraft_content::Pieces::join`).
- Rewrite `alt::artifact_marked_content` to join the page's content streams with `pdfcraft_content::Pieces::join`, parse operators across the joined stream via `Pieces::parse`, and splice only matching `BDC` operator spans to `/Artifact BMC` via `Pieces::splice` so split operators and cross-stream comments stay intact.

### Testing
- Added `crates/a11y/tests/cross_stream.rs` covering:
  - `autotag_keeps_text_commented_out_across_stream_boundary_hidden`
  - `mark_decorative_preserves_shape_split_across_content_streams`
  - `mark_decorative_and_mark_artifact_keep_cross_stream_comment_hidden`

title: M2: a JP2 image in a colour space the decoder refuses is drawn by its component count (#3306)
author: mtlcl410
body:
Fixes #3306.

## Cause

As @jpeskov traced it: the veraPDF fixture's JPX image has no `/ColorSpace`, and its JP2 header's colour specification (`colr`, METH 1) names enumerated colour space 19, CIEJab. `hayro-jpeg2000` 0.3.5's `get_color_space` handles only CMYK, CIELab, sRGB, greyscale, sYCC, e-sRGB and ROMM-RGB, and returns `Unsupported` for every other enum. So `Image::new` failed, the filter returned `None`, and the image was skipped: a blank page. `hayro-jpeg2000` isn't vendored, so the fix sits in the vendored `hayro-syntax` JPX filter.

## Fix

Vendored hayro-syntax patch (20), in `filter/jpx.rs`. The normal path is unchanged. Only when `Image::new` fails, and the JP2 header has a `colr` box naming an enumerated space outside the decoded set, is the image decoded again from a copy. In that copy those `colr` enums name the space the decoder assumes when there is no `colr` box: greyscale, sRGB or CMYK for 1, 3 or 4 components (`ihdr`). Other component counts, ICC `colr` boxes and anything unreadable are left alone. The box walk is bounded and uses checked arithmetic, and handles 8-byte (`LBox` 1) and to-the-end (`LBox` 0) lengths.

Why sRGB for this file: I rendered the fixture with the enum rewritten to sRGB (16) and to sYCC (18), and compared each with MuPDF at 72 dpi.

| | mean abs diff vs MuPDF | pixels > 40 |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (blank) | 25.39 | 56,721 |
| as sYCC | 11.46 | 71,135 |
| **as sRGB (this PR)** | **0.61** | **349** |

## Tests

- `raster::tests::a_jp2_image_in_a_refused_enumerated_colour_space_is_drawn`: a 1×1 JP2 with every sample 128. It draws mid-grey with CIEJab (19) and YPbPr (22) for 3 components and bilevel (15) for 1, and with sRGB (16) as a control. On `main` the first three draw nothing.
- `filter::jpx::tests` in `hayro-syntax` (run with `--manifest-path vendor/hayro-syntax/Cargo.toml`):
  - `refused_enumerated_colour_spaces_become_the_component_counts_default`: the replacement by component count, several `colr` boxes (only refuse…

title: fix(preflight): identify PDF standards by XML namespace
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

PDF/A identification currently depends on the literal `pdfaid` prefix. A valid XMP packet using another prefix, or a default namespace on its elements, is therefore not recognized in Standards and is reported as lacking identification by PDF/A verification. Resolve PDF/A and PDF/UA identification by namespace URI and local name, for attributes and elements, and reject misleading prefixes bound to another namespace. Metadata decoding is bounded to 8 MiB before allocation; the XML parser disallows DTDs and bounds metadata size (8 MiB), nesting (1,024), nodes (100,000), attributes per element (128), and total attributes (4,096). Namespace declarations count as attributes; over-limit packets are not identified.

This addresses one possible cause related to #3319; the reporter's file has not been supplied, so it does not claim to resolve that report.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-preflight --profile low-disk --locked -j 2` (16 passed); the namespace regression fails on the original implementation, and the attribute-limit and metadata-decode regressions fail when their guards are removed, and a compressed oversized fixture is rejected during decoding.

title: fix(sign): offer only certificates that may sign documents from the Windows store
author: Tomcatt
body:
## What this changes

A DoD Common Access Card (and other PIV smart cards) puts several certificates into the Windows Current User store under the same name: one for signing, one for encryption, one or more for Windows logon / card authentication. All of them have a private key, so the digital ID picker listed them as identical, selectable entries. Only the signing one produces a signature that validates. With the others, validation says "unknown" because the key usage or EKU doesn't allow document signing. In practice this means picking the right entry by trial and error.

`pdfcraft-sign` already knows whether a certificate may sign (`Certificate::signing_problem`). This PR runs that check during Windows store enumeration, *after* the private-key check. A certificate that can't sign is now greyed out in the picker and marked `unusable` in `sign_windows_ids`, with its reason (for example "it is not issued for signing documents (…)"), the same way the store already handles a key CNG can't open. Certificates without a private key are still left out entirely, as before.

`Certificate::signing_problem_clause` rewords the existing diagnostic so it follows the certificate's name in a list.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`, on Linux and on `--target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2`: all pass

**Test:** `crates/sign/tests/chain.rs::a_smart_cards_certificates_that_may_not_sign_say_why_in_id_lists` builds four CAC-shaped certificates: encryption (keyEncipherment + emailProtection), logon (smartcardLogon + clientAuth), PIV card authentication (2.16.840.1.101.3.6.8), and signing (digitalSignature + nonRepudiation, emailProtection + documentSigning). It checks that the first three get a reason and the signing one gets none. With the clause stubbed to `None`, the test fails (`left: None`).
