title: Clear image pixels intersected by redaction marks
author: earlvanze
body:
A redaction mark can intersect part of an image pixel without containing its center. Previously that pixel was left unchanged, and if no centers were covered the original image remained in the saved PDF. For example, a narrow mark over one edge of a 2-pixel image left both original samples recoverable after apply and save.

Clear every pixel whose transformed footprint's bounding box overlaps a redaction region. The bounding box is conservative for rotation and shear, so it can clear neighboring pixels as well. Unsupported image codecs and masks still follow the existing fail-closed removal path; this does not solve the whole-page JPEG removal tracked in #283.

Validation:
- The synthetic full-save/reopen regression failed on main (`images_cleared == 0`) and passes after the fix for unrotated and rotated images, checking that the original image resource is removed and only the intersected sample is cleared.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact --profile low-disk --locked -j 2`: 73 passed, one ignored timing probe.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact --all-targets --profile low-disk --locked -j 2 -- -D warnings`; wasm32 check for pdfcraft-redact; fmt, layers, assets and parity checks passed.

title: fix(render): text extraction keeps the word gaps between Hangul words
author: kouros7376
body:
## Summary

Extracted text (`text`, `text_extract`, search, copy) ran Korean words together whenever the producer
drew the word gap by position alone, with no space glyph. Hangul was counted among the scripts written
without word spaces (Han, kana), so a gap narrower than half the line height between two Hangul words
was never a space. One function changed in `crates/render/src/text.rs`, one new test.

## Root cause

`is_cjk` (used only by the word-gap rule in `arrange`) covered the Hangul syllables (U+AC00–D7AF),
Hangul Jamo (U+1100–11FF) and compatibility Jamo (U+3130–318F) along with Han and kana. The rule
"two CJK glyphs with a gap under `0.5 × h` are one word" is right for Chinese and Japanese, which are
written without word spaces, but Korean is written with them, and a Korean word gap (about a quarter em)
is well under that limit. Producers that draw each word with its own `Td`/`Tj` (HWP exports and
scanned-and-OCR'd documents among them) therefore lost every word boundary.

## Fix

`is_cjk` now covers Han, kana, bopomofo and their compatibility and fullwidth forms, and not Hangul, so
Hangul word gaps are judged by the same position-relative threshold as Latin ones (`typical letter gap +
0.15 × h`). Han and kana keep the no-space rule.

## Before / after

A page drawn with `drawString` per word (a space-width gap, no space glyph), `pdfcraft-cli text`:

```
before: 복합문화센터건립공사설계설명서제3장
        도면번호 A-101 축척 1/200 검토자박검토
after:  복합문화센터 건립공사 설계설명서 제3장
        도면번호 A-101 축척 1/200 검토자 박검토
```

Lines drawn without a gap (`복합` `문화` `센터` butted together) still read as one word, and `建築` `設計`
with the same gap still read as `建築設計`.

## Test

`text::tests::hangul_word_gaps_are_spaces_and_han_gaps_are_not`: a quarter-em gap between two Hangul
words is a space, the same gap between two Han words is not. Fails on `main` with
`left: "복합문화센터", right: "복합문화 센터"`.

## Checks

- `cargo test -p …

title: fix(windows): present Direct3D 12 through a composition visual, so resizing doesn't stretch (#2738)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2738. On Windows, Direct3D 12 now presents through a DirectComposition visual (`wgpu::Dx12SwapchainKind::DxgiFromVisual`) instead of a swap chain made on the window itself.

With the window's own swap chain, wgpu creates it with `DXGI_SCALING_STRETCH`. While the window is being resized, Windows stretches the last frame, still at the old size, to the new window size until a new frame arrives. The text shimmered and the left panel's width bounced for as long as the drag lasted. A visual's last frame is shown at its own size instead, so the panel stays put. `WGPU_DX12_PRESENTATION_SYSTEM=hwnd` still selects the old path. It is now documented in `docs/development.md`.

A script drags the window's right edge back and forth with the real mouse, 240 frames per run. In each frame it compares the left 450 px of the window with a still reference. That region doesn't depend on the window's width, so a frame that differs there was drawn stretched.

| Build | Presentation | Stretched frames / 240 |

| this branch | default (visual) | 0, 0 |

author: pedrocaluiz
body:

PDFs from **Microsoft Reporting Services** (bank statements, invoices, report exports) write `stream` followed by a space and then the line break: `stream \r\n`. title: Control channel: keep a covered or minimized window working on macOS
author: mateogasme
body:
## What this changes

An agent driving PdfCraft through `--control` stops working as soon as the user goes back to
another app on macOS. Once the window is covered or minimized, every `ui.click`, `ui.key` and
`ui.screenshot` times out with "the window is not being drawn". Two things cause it:

- winit reports the window `Occluded(true)` (or `is_minimized()`), so eframe's
  `ViewportInfo::visible()` is false and it runs no egui pass at all, so injected input never runs.
- Even when a pass runs, wgpu-hal's Metal surface skips acquiring a covered window's drawable on
  purpose (`CurrentSurfaceTexture::Occluded`, the workaround for gfx-rs/wgpu#8309), so
  `paint_and_update_textures` returns before the screenshot capture, and no screenshot arrives.

This keeps the control channel usable while the user works in another app, still only while
`--control` is on:

- **vendor/winit, patch (14):** `platform::macos::set_keep_drawing(on)`. While it's on, a
  covered or minimized window reports `Occluded(false)` and `is_minimized() == Some(false)`.
- **vendor/egui-wgpu, patch (3):** `winit::set_keep_drawing(on)` turns on the winit switch as
  well. While it's on, a requested screenshot whose surface texture can't be acquired
  (`Occluded`/`Timeout`) is drawn off screen into the capture texture and read back, and nothing
  is presented. `CaptureState::new_for`, `update_for` and `copy_to_buffer` make that texture from
  a size and format, since there is no surface texture to copy them from.
- **apps/pdfcraft:** `--control` calls `eframe::egui_wgpu::winit::set_keep_drawing(true)`.
  Without `--control` nothing changes.

The surface is still not presented while covered, so this adds no 1-second `nextDrawable` hang
(the reason wgpu skips it). A covered window runs egui passes only when something requests a
repaint, as a visible one does.

Measured on macOS 26.6.2 (Apple M4), v0.9.0 with and without this patch, window fully covered by
another app's maximized window, rounds of "click Nex…

title: Keep save shortcuts behind other dialogs

body:

title: M6: a date typed without separators fills a yyyymmdd field
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A date typed without separators is now accepted by a date field whose format writes its fields side by side, such as `yyyymmdd`. On `main`, such a field refuses **every** date: typing `20261018` into a `yyyymmdd` field gives

> Invalid date/time: please ensure that the date/time exists. Field [ … ] should match format yyyymmdd

so the field cannot be filled at all, whether by typing, by `form_fill`, or from a value the calendar is asked to read.

**Why it matters.** `YYYYMMDD` is the date format of US Army forms. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, published by the Army Publishing Directorate) is a dynamic XFA form with 76 date fields, 70 of which show their date as `date{YYYYMMDD}`; its own field help asks for "today's date in Y Y Y Y M M D D format". `date_pattern` (`crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`) turns `date{YYYYMMDD}` into the `yyyymmdd` format, so on `main` each of those 70 fields refuses every date, as does any form field with `AFDate_FormatEx("yyyymmdd")`. I found this while filling that form in PdfCraft 0.9.0. There is no existing issue (searched for yyyymmdd, undelimited, AFDate and parse_date).

### Cause

`parse_date` (`crates/forms/src/af.rs`) splits the typed text into numbers at every non-digit, then gives one number to each field of the format. `20261018` is a single number: the year takes it, nothing is left for the month, and `it.next()?` returns `None`. The widths the format's letters define were never consulted.

### Fix

- `order()` now returns a `Part` per field of the format, with
  - its fixed width when typed run together: 4 for `yyyy`; 2 for `yy`, `mm`, `dd`, `HH`, `MM` and `ss`; 0 where the width varies (`m`, `d`) or the field is a name (`mmm`);
  - `joined`: the next field follows with nothing in between (`yyyymmdd`, `HHMM`).
- `parse_date` keeps runs of digits as text. A field joined to the next takes only its own width from a longer run and leaves the rest for the next field, **but only when fewer runs were t…

title: M6: the date picker follows a whole date typed while it is open
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

The date picker now moves to a date as soon as the field's text becomes one. On `main` it takes its month once, when it opens, so typing `03/14/2025` into a field whose calendar is showing October leaves it on October; the typed date only shows after leaving the field and coming back.

### Cause

`calendar()` (`crates/ui-egui/src/forms_ui.rs`) reads the field's text only while `Focus::calendar` is still `None`, on the first frame. From then on it reuses the stored month every frame, which is what keeps the ‹ › arrows working, but it also ignores everything typed afterwards.

### Fix

- `Focus` gets `calendar_text`: the text the calendar last saw.
- Each frame, if the text has changed since then **and** now parses as a whole date in the field's format, the calendar moves to that month. Otherwise it keeps the month it shows.
- So half a date (`03/1`) leaves it where it is, a whole one (`03/14/2025`) moves it, and after the arrows turn to another month it stays there until the text changes again.
- Opening the calendar and picking a day work as before. `parse_date` is unchanged; the calendar reads the text exactly as the field's format and keystroke check do.

No existing issue. This came up while filling DA Form 31 by hand.

## Screenshots

The real shell, rendered headlessly with egui_kittest: the `crates/ui-egui/tests/data/form.pdf` fixture plus a date field in its default `mm/dd/yyyy` format. I click the field and type `03/14/2025`, without leaving it.

author: earlvanze
body:

title: M12: XFA dates are written and read in the field's data picture
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA date values are now written to, and read from, the form's data in the field's **data picture** (`<bind><picture>`). On `main`, PdfCraft always writes a date into the datasets packet as ISO (`2026-10-18`) and reads it back as ISO, whatever the field's data picture says. A form whose date fields bind as `date{YYYYMMDD}` therefore gets `2026-10-18` from PdfCraft but `20261018` from other XFA viewers. Data those viewers wrote is shown in PdfCraft exactly as stored, not in the field's own pattern.

The XFA spec separates the pictures: the `<ui>` picture is how a date is typed and shown, the `<bind>` picture is how it is kept in the data, and ISO is only the default when a field has no data picture. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*) is a real-world case: 70 of its 76 date fields bind as `date{YYYYMMDD}`. This was found while filling it.

No existing issue (searched for bind picture, data picture and XFA dates). #2993 also touches `crates/xfa/src/data.rs`, in `iso_to_pattern` and `pattern_to_iso` (month and weekday names). This PR only calls those two functions, so the two changes combine without conflict (checked by merging #2993 onto this branch).

### Cause

- `parse_field` keeps only the `<ui>` picture (`Field::picture`); `<bind><picture>` is dropped.
- `wanted` (`crates/xfa/src/data.rs`, writing the datasets) turns a typed date into ISO and writes that.
- `values_at` (reading values for a form laid out before) and the `DateTimeEdit` branch of the layout (`crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`) both take the data to hold ISO.

### Fix

- `Field` gains `data_picture`, parsed from `<bind><picture>`.
- **Writing:** a typed date is read in the field's own pattern and turned into ISO, as before. When the field has a date data picture, the ISO date is then written in that picture (`20261018`). A field without one still gets ISO.
- **Reading:** on layout and in `values_at`, a stored value is read through the field's data picture first. A value that …

title: Share compatible text field names
author: earlvanze
body:
## Problem

Preparing a form currently rejects a text field name already used by another field. This draft supports a subset of repeated-name text fields by keeping their widgets under one logical field, so they share a value and appearance.

## Changes

title: M12: laying out a dynamic XFA form takes off the usage rights it voids
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

When PdfCraft lays out a dynamic XFA form that carries **usage rights** (`/Perms /UR3`), it now takes them off the catalog in the layout revision and says so in the layout report (the notice bar and `doc_info`). It no longer saves a file whose usage rights are void.

Usage rights are a signature over the form as it was published (ISO 32000-1, 12.8.2.3). PdfCraft's layout revision replaces the placeholder pages and adds the fields, so the rights no longer match the form. On `main` they stay in the file anyway. Every save carries the layout revision, so every saved copy holds rights that no longer match its form. A widely used free viewer then opens the form **with every field locked**: the person PdfCraft's user sends the form to can't fill in a single box.

`strip` (taking the XFA out) already removes usage rights for the same reason, with a note. This PR moves that code into one helper, `drop_usage_rights`, and calls it from `write_form`, the one place that rewrites a laid-out form's pages and fields. Both the open-time layout (`render_into`) and a script-driven re-layout (`rerender`) go through `write_form`.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case. It is a dynamic XFA form with usage rights, and this was found while filling it. No existing issue (searched for usage rights and UR3).

### Cause

- `write_form` (`crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs`) rewrites the page tree and the AcroForm, and leaves `/Perms` alone.
- The layout is one appended revision (`prepare_open_unguarded`, `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`), and every save, incremental or full, includes it.

### Fix

- **`drop_usage_rights(doc, catalog)`**: removes `/UR3` (and the older `/UR`) from `/Perms` and keeps everything else, such as a certification's `/DocMDP`. An indirect `/Perms` is rewritten where it is rather than copied into the catalog. An emptied `/Perms` is removed. It returns whether anything was removed.
- **`write_form`** calls it and repo…

title: M6: a secured form's notice bar still says it is a form
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A secured form's notice bar now still says it is a form. On `main`, the bar on any secured document (opened without the owner password, with changes or page assembly withheld) shows only *"This document is secured. Some changes are restricted by its security settings."* For a secured fillable or XFA form, that message *replaces* the form's own notice, and with it:

- the **Highlight fields** button, the only one-click way to see where the fields are;
- *"This document contains N interactive form fields."*, or for a dynamic XFA form *"Dynamic XFA form laid out from its template: …"* with **every layout note** PdfCraft recorded (pictures left out, fields drawn with `?`, and so on);
- *"This is a dynamic XFA form, which PdfCraft can't display yet…"*, the one warning that tells a user the page in front of them is a placeholder.

Secured forms are common. Government and corporate forms are routinely encrypted with filling allowed and changing withheld. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is one, and this was found while testing #3401 on it: the layout note that PR adds never appeared, because the bar showed only the security notice.

No existing issue (searched for secured, notice bar and Highlight fields).

### Fix

`notices` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) first works out what the document is as a form (XFA layout, XFA placeholder, static XFA, or interactive fields), using the same messages as before, then:

- **Secured and a form:** the bar shows the form's notice followed by the security sentence. **Highlight fields** stays, next to **Security settings** and **Unlock…**. The icon is the form's.
- **Secured and not a form:** unchanged (the lock icon and the security sentence alone).
- **Not secured:** unchanged.
- A form whose scripts were turned off still takes the bar first, as before.

Both sentences are existing translated strings, so the catalogs need no new entries.

title: M12: an XFA script that fails partway keeps what it changed before the error
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

An XFA script that fails partway now keeps what it changed before the error. On `main`, `Runner::run` (`crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`) returns as soon as a script reports an error, before `apply_effects`. So a script that set ten values and then threw changes nothing. JavaScript doesn't work that way: every statement before a `throw` has run, and its assignments stand. Other XFA viewers follow it, so forms are written, and tested, against that behavior.

It matters because real forms trip over their own stale references. A form is revised, a field is renamed or removed, and a script written for the old version still names it. In the viewer it was tested in, the script's earlier lines do their work and the error only shows in the console. In PdfCraft the error undoes that work, so the form stops working.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, and this was found while filling it:

1. Checking **8. CHARGEABLE** runs that box's change script. Its first part opens the leave-type boxes (`access = "open"` on *Annual (Ordinary) Leave* and eleven others) and shows the chargeable sections.
2. About 200 lines later it sets `this.resolveNode("Non_Chargeable_Section_9_and_10_Subform.Non_Chargeable_Total_Days_Requested").rawValue`. No such field exists in the template, so `resolveNode` returns `null` and the assignment throws a `TypeError` in any viewer.
3. On `main` that error discards step 1. The leave-type boxes stay protected, so nothing after them can be filled: 10a, 10b and the requestor's signature never appear.

The 10a script has the same kind of reference (`Chargeable_Total_Days_10b`, also absent from the template).

No existing issue (searched for script error, partial and effects).

### Fix

- `Runner::run` records the error as before (the JavaScript console and the error list still show it), then applies the effects the script recorded before it failed, re-laying the form out when they show or hide…

title: Honor single-page redaction selections
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

`redact_mark` silently ignores `page` for text, word, pattern and whole-page marks. For example, searching for matching text with `page: 1` marks every matching page, and applying those marks can remove content from unintended pages.

Honor `page` for each selector, reject simultaneous `page` and `pages`, and reject `pages` for rectangle marks. Document the selection rules in the tool schema.

## How you verified it

- The new two-page synthetic regression failed on main (two marks instead of one) and passes with the fix. It covers all four selectors, invalid selections without added marks, and application preserving the other page's text.

- `cargo clippy --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked --profile low-disk -j 2 -p pdfcraft-automation`
- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`

## Reviewer note

Calls that previously supplied both selectors, or supplied `pages` with `rect`, now fail rather than silently discarding one selector. Existing `pages` selection and the default of all pages remain supported.

## What this changes

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; strict clippy for `pdfcraft-render --all-targets` and `hayro-interpret --lib`; `cargo xtask layers`; `cargo xtask assets`.

title: Respect unspecified Type 3 glyph bounds
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

An all-zero Type 3 `/FontBBox` means the font does not specify glyph bounds. PdfCraft currently treats it as a zero-sized clip for shaded glyphs, so they disappear. Carry the enclosing page or clip bounds into the glyph context in that case; a missing box follows the same existing fallback. Nonzero font boxes still use their transformed bounds.

title: Speed damaged xref recovery with a bounded candidate index
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

When many in-use cross-reference entries have stale offsets, recovery currently scans the whole file once per requested object. Build a shared candidate-position index on the first fallback lookup, and check candidates newest first with the existing parser. The index is capped at 500,000 candidates; if it exceeds the cap, recovery uses the existing scan. Valid offsets do not build the index, and freed xref entries remain freed.

Refs #3414. This addresses a measured recovery cost, not the whole report: a stalled open can still block the single background worker, and the reporter's original PDF and Windows handoff have not been tested.

title: Let a later document open while one preparation stalls
author: earlvanze
body:
## What this changes

A stalled background PDF preparation currently holds the only open worker, so later files cannot open. Two bounded workers now share the existing 16-entry FIFO queue. One stalled preparation can coexist with a later successful open; if both workers stall, later jobs still wait.

A later successful ordinary open keeps focus if an earlier ordinary open finishes afterwards. A later failed open does not suppress the earlier successful open. A delayed document-bound tool still activates its own document before executing; converted files also respect the background focus decision. Password prompts and tool dialogs continue to hold other ready results until the interaction finishes.

Refs #3414. This does not cancel a stalled parse, establish the cause of the reporter's file, or make progress when both workers are occupied. Documents can complete and appear in a different order from the requests; that tradeoff needs review.

title: M10: Office export follows forms 50 deep and up to 50 000 a page and says where it stops (#3120)
author: Faabyy
body:
Export to Word, PowerPoint, HTML and RTF stopped at 12 nested forms and 4 096 forms a page and left the rest out silently, while the renderer, `text` and Find read 50 levels. A page that draws a label or table cell as a form more than 4 096 times lost the text of the later ones.

Export now follows forms 50 deep and up to 50 000 a page (the renderer's budget for nested paints). title: fix(render): use unfiltered inline image byte length before EI heuristic (#3107)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Closes #3107

### Problem
When an unfiltered inline image (no `/Filter` / `/F`, or `null` / `[]`) contains the byte sequence `EI` followed by whitespace and bytes that happen to parse as a text-showing or content operator inside its sample payload, hayro-syntax's `UntypedIter::next` cut the inline image at that internal `EI` and executed the remaining image sample bytes as page content operators. As a result:
- Only the prefix of the inline image before `EI` was decoded, distorting rendered pixel values.
- Any operators embedded in the remaining image bytes (such as `BT ... (Injected) Tj ET`) were executed during rendering, text extraction (`plain_text()`), and `find()`.

Meanwhile, `pdfcraft-content` (`crates/content/src/lib.rs`) already computes the exact byte length of unfiltered inline images (including row byte padding) before falling back to heuristic `EI` scanning.

### Fix
- Teach hayro-syntax's inline image reader (`UntypedIter::next` in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/content/mod.rs`) to compute the deterministic sample byte count of unfiltered inline images (`/DeviceGray`/`/G`, `/DeviceRGB`/`/RGB`, `/DeviceCMYK`/`/CMYK`, 4-element `[/Indexed ...]`/`[/I ...]`, and `/ImageMask`/`/IM`, respecting full/abbreviated key consistency) and check for whitespace + `EI` at that exact offset before falling back to the `find_ei` heuristic.
- Align `/L` policy with `crates/content`: deterministic layout dimensions (`/W`, `/H`, `/CS`, `/BPC`, row padding) directly determine the unfiltered payload length, so a conflicting or crafted `/L` cannot force an early cut and inject operators. (Named resource color spaces like `/CS /CS0` remain a known follow-up gap as stream tokenizers do not resolve against parent resource dictionaries).

title: fix(sign): judge every object changed after signing by its signed role (#1787 follow-up)
author: LetoCoder26
body:
## What this changes

This follows up #1787. That fix made a signed page's resources page content whatever keys a later revision writes. Any other dictionary changed after signing was still classified by keys in its *new* version. Signature objects were permitted to change under every DocMDP level. As a result, documents changed after signing still validated as **Valid**, including under P=1. The new tests cover these cases:

- **A rewritten signature dictionary.** A new `/Reason` or `/M`, or an emptied `/Reference` (dropping a P=1 certification) followed by a comment.

title: Edit text: refuse a rewrite of text that is a clipping path
author: Hamza0101
body:
Refs #3429 — the Edit text half, which is the part that destroys files.

Credit where it is due: @RavenCrowe666 reported it with the Photoshop source and @mtlcl410 traced it to `clear_block`'s existing guard. They converged on exactly this fix; I have implemented and measured it.

## Reproduced

A page whose only text is a `7 Tr` mask with a red rectangle painted through it, edited through `text_edit` and rendered either side:

```
before:  red pixels  1,521   (3.4% of the page — the fill shaped by the letters)
after:   red pixels 45,000   (100% of the page — a flat rectangle)
```

`doc_save` reported success with `"undo": "Edit text"`, and the file reopens without a warning. So the loss is silent.

## Change

`replace_line` and `rewrite_block` refuse render modes 4 to 7:

```
text used as a clipping path cannot be edited: its glyphs mask the artwork behind them
```

`clear_block` has refused these since before this PR — *"text used as a clipping path cannot be previewed for editing"* — so the editor already knew they were unsafe; the two rewrite paths simply did not ask. There were exactly two `render_mode` guards in `crates/edit/src/text.rs` and neither covered a rewrite.

```
clipping text   refused, no file written, document untouched
normal text     still edits → "EDITED"
```

## Tests

- `rewriting_clipping_path_text_is_refused_for_every_clipping_mode` — all four modes (4, 5, 6, 7) against both entry points, and after each refusal the page still has its one line reading `MASK`, so the assertion is that the document is *untouched* rather than merely that an error came back. Without the guard it fails.
- `painting_modes_are_still_rewritten` — modes 0, 1 and 2 still rewrite, so the guard cannot quietly widen to text that paints ink.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

title: Render: a glyph shown in a clipping mode clips even with no outline
author: Hamza0101
body:
A glyph shown in a clipping render mode (`4 Tr` to `7 Tr`) adds its outline to the clipping path, and that clip applies to everything painted after `ET` until the enclosing `Q`. When the glyphs shown have no outline — a space, say — the clip they contribute is empty, and an empty clip admits nothing.

`interpret_window` applied a clip only once a glyph had contributed an outline, so such a text object applied **no** clip and whatever followed painted unmasked:

```
q BT 7 Tr /F1 24 Tf 4 10 Td ( ) Tj ET  1 0 0 rg 0 0 40 40 re f  Q
```

filled the whole page where nothing should paint through the empty clip.

### Measured

Red pixels of a page filled red behind the text object, in this renderer and in two others:

| page | pdfcraft before | pdfcraft after | Preview (CoreGraphics) | Firefox (pdf.js) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a space shown in `7 Tr` | 100% | **0%** | 0% | 0% |
| no glyph shown in `7 Tr` | 100% | 100% | 0% | 100% |
| no text object | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| a space shown in `0 Tr` | 100% | 100% | 100% | 100% |

The two independent readers agree on the first row and disagree on the second, and pdf.js's `endText` is explicit about where the line is: `pendingTextPaths` exists only once a glyph has been shown in a clipping mode, so no glyphs shown leaves the clip alone, while glyphs shown with empty outlines are clipped with an empty `Path2D`. This change draws the same line — `clip_shown` is set in `clip_glyph`, not when `Tr` selects a mode.

A glyph whose outline is unavailable (Type 3) leaves the real clip unknown, so that case stays unclipped as well.

### What this is not

An earlier version of this PR also clipped for a text object that shows no glyphs at all, and I described it as the root cause of #3123 and #3429. That was wrong, and review caught it: editing a clipping title away leaves a text object with no glyphs, which is exactly the case that must not clip, so the flood those reports describe is the edited file's own meaning. #34…

title: fix(engine): a reload keeps reading colours and hidden comments (#3443)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3443. Not `Fixes`: this closes the one path I could reproduce, and I have not confirmed it is the path the reporter hits on macOS.

`Session::reload` handles a file that changed on disk. It used to open the new bytes with a default render config, so a document shown in reading colours, or with its comments hidden, went back to the file's own look. The UI re-applies the reading-colour preference only on open (`finish_open`, `files.rs`, `create_ui.rs`), not after `reload_view`. Reload now carries both display settings over and rebuilds the renderer with them. Layer choices are not touched.

**Evidence**
- **[code]** `reload` calls `self.open(…)`, and `open` builds the config as `RenderConfig { password, ..Default::default() }` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, `build_document`). The file watcher's `reload_view` (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_watch.rs:411`) calls `session.reload` and `document_replaced`, but not `set_reading_colors`.
- **[test]** A temporary kittest probe on `main` @ `43550c44` (not committed) used `file_watch`'s own `harness` and `find_new_version`. Before the reload, the app preference and the document setting were `(true, true)`. After it they were `(true, false)`: the preference was still on, but the document's renderer was back to the file's colours. That matches the reporter's "toggling the preference off and on restores it". The same probe found that a plain in-place Save keeps `(true, true)`, so saving alone does not reset the setting.
- **[inference]** On macOS the reporter sees the revert right after saving. The watcher's Unix `Stamp` includes `ctime` (`file_watch.rs:46`). A metadata-only change made after PdfCraft's own write would make the saved file look like a new version and trigger a reload. Examples are an extended attribute written by Finder, Spotlight or a sync client. I have not verified this on macOS.

title: Tests: the parser-cancel test guards against a hang, not a 2 s limit (#1970)
author: Faabyy
body:
`waiting_worker_can_cancel_before_initializer_returns` gave its threads 2 s to start, and a busy FreeBSD VM in CI took longer. Its waits only guard against a hang: the initializer is held until the end of the test, so a waiter that can't cancel never returns, however long the guard is. They now allow 600 s, like the hang guard in `page_contents_and_nested_forms_share_one_budget` (#2812), which already covers the second test named in the issue. The test polls with a 1 ms sleep instead of `yield_now`, and the held initializer no longer panics a second time when the test fails.

Checked by hand: with a 3 s delay at both threads' start the old test fails at its deadline and the new one passes; with the waiter's condvar wait made untimed (a real stall) the new test fails at its guard. `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render`, `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` pass. Not run on FreeBSD.

A real stall now takes 10 minutes to fail instead of 2 s. Other 2 s deadlines in `raster.rs` (around lines 2110-2229) could fail the same way on a slow machine; I left them alone.

title: fix(ui): a saved file whose metadata alone changes is not a new version (#3443)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3443, fixes #3755 (the same cause, reported from macOS), together with #3452. This PR removes the trigger: the reload after every save on macOS. #3452 makes a reload keep the reading colours.

**What the reporter measured on macOS** (#3443):
- **Before and after:** `stat` right after a save in PdfCraft, then again 5 s later.
- **Result:** inode, size and `mtime` were identical, but `ctime` had moved by about 1.57 s.
- **What did it:** the system rewrites the file's extended attributes (`com.apple.macl`, `com.apple.metadata:kMDItemWhereFroms`, `com.apple.provenance`).

**[code] Why PdfCraft reacted:**
- **The Unix stamp includes `ctime`.** `Stamp` (`crates/ui-egui/src/file_watch.rs:46`) uses it to tell versions apart. So PdfCraft took its own save for another program's change.
- **Reload on:** it reloaded the document, which dropped the undo history and, without #3452, the reading colours.
- **Reload off:** every save asked "Save over the changed file?" (`disk_differs`, #2166). The reporter confirmed both behaviours.

**Now, a file that still holds the bytes the document came from is the same version.** "The bytes the document came from" is `Document::saved_bytes`, the file as last opened, reloaded or saved.
- **Watcher** (`file_changed`): it already has the file's bytes. When they equal the saved bytes, it adopts the new stamp as the document's version and doesn't reload.
- **Save** (`disk_differs`, now given the saved bytes): a stamp that differs from the basis is a change only if the length differs or the contents do. The file is read only when its length matches the saved bytes, so the read is never larger than what is already in memory.
- **A file with other bytes is a change as before,** whatever its stamp says.

An earlier draft first required "only `ctime` moved" before comparing contents. A mutation run showed that gate changed no outcome. Identical bytes need neither a reload nor a prompt, whatever moved in the metadata, so the …

## What this changes

**Measure objects: set the plan scale as an architect's ratio (1:N), applied at once.**

Fixes #2752. The reporter had to enter "1:17.5" to measure a 1:50 plan correctly. The calculation is fine. The cause is the scale fields: they read `pt [72] = [value] [unit]`, and the left field is in **PDF points** (1/72 in = 0.3528 mm), not millimetres of paper (`crates/ui-egui/src/measure_ui.rs` on `main`: the `DragValue` with prefix `"pt "` around line 356, divided out in `Scale::calibrate(…, real_distance / drawing_points, …)` around line 413).

- `1 = 50 mm` reads 2.835 × too long;
- `1 = 17.5 mm` reads within 1 %;

1. **Plan scale as 1:N.** The panel offers the usual scales (1:1 to 1:1000) and a free `1:N` field (it also accepts `1/N`, `N` and comma decimals), with the unit (m, cm, mm) and the decimals beside it.

title: fix(edit): keep a superscript footnote marker in its paragraph's row (#3252)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3252. A footnote marker drawn with `Ts` (text rise) and a smaller `Tf` size sits on the same visual row as the body text around it, but the row-joining baseline tolerance in `group_layout` (`crates/edit/src/text_regions.rs`) was scaled by the *smaller* of the two runs' sizes (20% of it) — far tighter than a typical superscript's rise, which runs up to about half the body size. The fix scales the tolerance by the larger of the two sizes instead. Ordinary next-line leading (about 1.2× the font size) stays well outside it, so paragraph lines that are genuinely stacked still start new rows as before — only a same-row, raised-or-lowered, smaller-or-larger run (a super/subscript) is now tolerated.

title: fix(forms): draw fields the file leaves to the viewer, for display only (#3470)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3470. A filled form whose writer left the appearances to the viewer showed its text fields empty in PdfCraft. Acrobat, Firefox and MuPDF show the values.

**[spec]** ISO 32000-2, Table 224 (printed p.529), `NeedAppearances`: "A flag specifying whether to construct appearance streams and appearance dictionaries for all widget annotations in the document … A PDF writer shall include this key, with a value of true, if it has not provided appearance streams for all visible widget annotations present in the document." It is deprecated in PDF 2.0, but files that rely on it are common.

**[code] Why the fields were empty**
- `pdfcraft_forms::need_appearances` was only used when *writing*.
- The engine's display copy draws missing appearances in memory (`display_bytes` → `pdfcraft_annot::with_missing_appearances_cached`). It skips `Widget` annotations.
- So nothing drew a text field from its `/V`. Check boxes looked right only because they use the appearance states already in the file.

**The fix**
- **New function:** `pdfcraft_forms::with_field_appearances(doc) -> Option<Document>` returns a copy in which text, combo and list widgets are drawn from their values. It uses the same generator a typed value uses (`appearance::field_appearance_drawn`, as in `redraw`).
- **Which widgets:**
  - When the form sets `/NeedAppearances true`, every such widget is redrawn, since the flag says the file's appearances aren't to be trusted.
  - Otherwise only widgets with no `/AP /N` are drawn. An appearance the file has, even an empty one, stays the file's.
  - Buttons keep their states.
- **Engine:** the display copy applies it after the comment appearances, in both `display_bytes` (page view, page images, Print as Image) and `display_bytes_for` (CLI render).
- **Saving:** the document itself is not changed, so saving writes the file as it was. Editing a field already writes a real appearance.

**[test] The reporter's repro.** Ink insid…

body:
## What this changes

PdfCraft can now be built for 32-bit Windows 7 (`i686-win7-windows-msvc`), and it runs and draws correctly on an old OpenGL 2.1 laptop. Three problems stood in the way. Each is fixed by a small patch to a vendored crate, described in `vendor/README.md`:

1. **The exe wouldn't load on Windows 7** (`4b2211b0`). It statically imported `combase.dll`, `api-ms-win-core-path-l1-1-0.dll`, `api-ms-win-core-winrt-l1-1-0.dll` and `windows.data.pdf.dll`, which are all Windows 8+.
   - `windows-link`: on x86, `CoTaskMem*` and `CoCreateFreeThreadedMarshaler` now come from `ole32.dll`. The fix has to live here because x86 import symbols collide across DLLs.
   - `windows-core`: `RoGetActivationFactory` and `CoIncrementMTAUsage` are looked up at run time and return `E_NOTIMPL` where they're missing.
   - `arboard`: `PathCchStripPrefix` is replaced with a small Rust function, with unit tests.
   - `winprint`: `PdfCreateRenderer` is looked up when printing starts.
2. **No OpenGL context on OpenGL 2.1 drivers** (`9db7ea7b`). wgpu needs GL 3.3. eframe's glow fallback asks glutin for an unversioned context, which WGL turns into a 3.3 core request, so the driver refused it. `glutin` now falls back to the legacy `wglCreateContext` when `WGL_ARB_create_context` refuses a desktop GL context.
3. **Garbled drawing on that driver** (`5a7327ca`). Every mesh came out as slivers and stray triangles: no menus, no text, no page. `egui_glow` now draws each mesh on GL 2.x from its own buffers, which are never refilled and are freed on the next frame. Refilling one shared buffer per mesh made the Intel driver draw with other meshes' vertices. 16-bit indices, fixed attribute locations and emulated VAOs are kept as well; they were tried first and didn't fix it on their own.

Behaviour on Windows 8+ and on GL 3.3+ drivers is unchanged. `PDFCRAFT_GL_LEGACY=1` makes any driver take the GL 2.x path, which is useful for testing it.

The test machine was an HP Eli…

title: Text: tracked glyphs retain their word boundaries
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Preserve word boundaries when extracting letter-spaced text.

## What this changes

`text_paragraphs` and `object_list` treated every gap in tracked (letter-spaced) text as a word break, so "TEST WORD" came out as "T E S T W O R D". Extraction now tells repeated glyph tracking apart from real word gaps. It handles TJ adjustments and separately positioned glyphs without counting character spacing twice, and accounts for horizontal scaling.

Adds three synthetic regressions and updates the progress notes.

## How you verified it

- Without the fix, the three new tests fail (`"T E S T W O R D"` instead of `"TEST WORD"`); with it, they pass.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

## Never-crash and provenance

No new panic shortcuts, unsafe code, dependencies, fonts or binary fixtures. Tests generate synthetic documents. No third-party implementation code or Adobe-derived assets were added.

## Security and reach

Existing headless tools exercise the fix. Root confinement, opt-in MCP, the control channel and network behaviour are unchanged.

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

Tracking inference is heuristic and needs at least three letter-gap samples. Larger-gap and ordinary word-run checks guard against merging real words.

title: M6: Prepare a form ▸ Text field table: rows and columns of text fields as one edit
author: Piohrun
body:
## What this changes

Adds **Prepare a form ▸ Text field table**: drag out an area on a page and it becomes rows and columns of named text fields, added as **one undoable edit** ("Undo Add text field table"). This is useful for order forms, line items and timesheets, which otherwise take dozens of fields placed by hand.

The tool opens a movable window to set up the table, with the table previewed on the page as it changes:
- rows, columns, row and column spacing, and the first row number;
- column widths: draggable dividers, or the arrow keys once a divider has focus;
- a name pattern per column: `N` or `{row}` is the row number, `{col}` the column number and `{seq}` the cell number. With none of them, the row number goes at the end (`price_N` → `price_1`, `price_2`, …). An `N` inside a word (`Name_N`, `NET_N`) is left alone. Default names use the first free `TableK` (`Table1_N`, `Table1_c2_N`, …), so a second table never collides with the first.

The table is either added whole or refused, with the reason shown in the window and nothing added. It is refused if a cell would be under 4 pt (checked after mapping onto the page, so `/Rotate` and `/UserUnit` count) or if a name would contain a period, appear twice, or already exist in the form.

Where it lives:
- **forms** (`table`): layout, naming and validation, total on every input. The 4-point minimum used in three places in `author.rs` is now one constant, `MIN_FIELD_SIDE`.
- **engine** (`field_table::edit`): maps the cells from view space onto the page and builds the batch. Rows run down the page *as displayed*, including on rotated pages.
- **automation**: a new `form_add_field_table` tool does the same headlessly (AGENTS.md §3).
- **ui-egui**: the window, the tool, the page preview and catalogue entries in all 22 languages.

## How you verified it

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`pdfcraft-forms`, `pdfcraft-engine`, `pdfcraft-automation`, `pdfcraft-ui-egui`, all…

title: M14: drag a tab out into its own window, and onto another window (#1683, #2848)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Several windows (parity `view.multiple-windows`, now `partial`; #1683, #2848, and the drag half that #1768 asked for):

- **Drag a tab out.** A document tab dragged more than 40 pt above or below the strip, or past the window's sides, opens in a window of its own when released: placed so the tab sits under the pointer, with the source window's size, mode and panels. While it is held there the drop marker disappears and a badge at the pointer (window icon + name) says what releasing does. Escape cancels, as for reordering (#2848).
- **Drag a tab in.** A tab dragged onto another PdfCraft window joins it: at the gap under the pointer when the pointer is over that window's strip (which marks the gap), after the last tab when it is elsewhere in the window. A window left without tabs closes.
- **Menus.** The tab's context menu gets Move to new window and Move to window ▸ (the other windows by name). A new Window menu has `window.move_tab_new` (Move tab to new window), `window.merge_all` (Merge all windows) and `window.close` (Close window), translated in all 22 catalogues.
- **Closing and quitting.** Closing a window closes its tabs, asking about unsaved changes first (new `CloseRequest::Window`). Closing the main window quits: every window's unsaved documents gather in the main window first, so the existing save-prompt chain asks about each. The last session remembers every window's files (reopened in one window). The file watcher (#431) serves documents in every window.
- **Control channel.** `ui.state` gains `window_id` and `windows` (each window's `id`, `title`, `focused`, `tabs`); the `ui.*` methods act on the focused window.

One `PdfCraftApp` draws every window: each extra window is an egui viewport drawn inside the main window's pass (`show_viewport_immediate`). title: M5: copy and paste comments between documents, select several at once, finish connected lines from the menu
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Three things a reviewer working with comments across documents needs (parity `comment.copy-paste` and `comment.multi-select`, both new and `shipped`; `comment.export-selected` to `partial`; `comment.polyline` notes):

title: fix(forms): write each /DR font as its own object, so Acrobat keeps typed text (#3441)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3441. A text field added by PdfCraft showed its typed text in Adobe Acrobat only while the field had focus. As soon as the user clicked elsewhere the text vanished, though it was still stored and printed. This happens in Acrobat 2026.002.22031 (the reporter's), on a field added to a blank page as well as to a Word export. PDF-XChange Editor and PDFgear show it correctly.

**How the cause was found (black-box, synthetic files only)**
- **[test] The same field, two writers.** A big text field written by PdfCraft (`main` @ `43550c44`) and the same field written by MuPDF were each typed into and blurred in Acrobat, PDF-XChange Editor and PDFgear. Only PdfCraft's file in Acrobat lost the text.
- **[test] Bisection in Acrobat.** Seven copies of PdfCraft's file each changed one thing:

  | variant | text kept in Acrobat |
  |---|---|
  | unchanged (rewritten by MuPDF) | no |
  | `/DR` fonts as objects | **yes** |
  | no `/DR` | **yes** |
  | appearance stream also drawn inside `/Tx BMC` | no |
  | appearance and `/DR` share one font object | **yes** |
  | no `/P` | no |
  | `/DA` 12 instead of 0 | no |

  Every variant that keeps the text has no font dictionary written inline in `/DR`.
- **[code]** `ensure_form` (`crates/forms/src/author.rs`) wrote Helv, TiRo and Cour as dictionaries inline in `/DR /Font`. The XFA-to-AcroForm writer (`crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs`) did the same.
- **[test]** A file written by this branch, with `/DR` fonts as objects, keeps the typed text in Acrobat.

**[spec] / [inference]** ISO 32000-2 doesn't require resource fonts to be indirect. This works around how Acrobat redraws a field, and is what Acrobat itself writes.

**The fix**
- `ensure_form` adds the standard fonts as objects.
- Fonts an earlier save wrote inline become objects too, with the same dictionaries, so files PdfCraft 0.9 and earlier already made are repaired by the next field edit.

title: Signatures: one content type and one message digest in the signed attributes
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

RFC 5652 allows one content-type and one message-digest attribute in a signer's signed attributes, each with one value (§11.1, §11.2). `parse_signer` kept the last attribute of each kind and the first value of each attribute, so a CMS with two of either could mean one thing in PdfCraft and another in a different reader. Such a CMS is now not read.

The content-type attribute must also name the type of the encapsulated content (§11.1). The signature covers the attribute but not `eContentType`, so `eContentType` can be changed after signing without breaking the signature. A CMS where the two differ is now not read either.

Both cases go through the existing parse-error path, so a PDF signature like this shows "The signature could not be read (CMS: ...)" and is invalid. No new user-facing text, so no catalog changes.

These are the two points CodeRabbit raised on #2559 that I kept out of it. This PR is independent of #2559: it touches `crates/sign/src/cms.rs`, a new `crates/sign/tests/cms.rs` and the sign README, none of which #2559 changes.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-sign --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign -j 2`: all pass, including the RFC 3161 timestamp tests and the 52 PDF signature tests
- [ ] `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`: not run, no crate boundary or asset touched

**Tests.** New `crates/sign/tests/cms.rs` builds each CMS the way the signer does, signed with the `rsa-aes.p12` test identity, so a case differs from a valid one only in its attributes or `eContentType`:

- `signed_attributes_hold_one_content_type_and_one_message_digest`: the valid set is read and its signature verifies; a repeated content type or message digest (same value or another), two values, or none are refused.
- `the_signed_content_type_is_the_type_of_the_encapsulated_content`: data in both places and TSTInfo in both (an RFC 3161 token) are read; …

title: M7: break Thai rows between dictionary words
author: rutthawitc
body:
## What this changes

Thai is written without spaces between words. Until now:

- **Rewrapping existing text** (`text.rs` `wrap`, `text_regions.rs`) treated a whole Thai run as one word, so it never wrapped and overflowed the box.
- **Add text** (`added.rs` `thai_lines`) broke rows at any shaped cluster, splitting words mid-word. Before this change, a 90 pt box gave rows like `…ให้บริก` / `ารน้ำประปาที่ส` / `ะอาด…` (บริการ and สะอาด cut in half).

Now rows end between words, found with ICU4X's dictionary line segmenter (`icu_segmenter` 2.3, compiled dictionary data, no LSTM model, Unicode-3.0). `linebreak::breaks` returns every place a row may end inside a run without spaces: the existing Chinese and Japanese rule plus the dictionary's breaks next to Thai.

Rules applied on top of the dictionary, whatever it says:

- a row never starts with a following vowel (ะ า ำ ิ …), a tone or other mark, Mai Yamok (ๆ) or Paiyannoi (ฯ), or a closing bracket
- a row never ends with a leading vowel (เ แ โ ใ ไ) or an opening bracket
- the CJK pair rule honours the same Thai marks (found by the property test: `の` followed by a stray Thai mark was split)

Per call site:

- `text.rs` `wrap`: unchanged; `linebreak::pieces` now cuts Thai too.
- `text_regions.rs`: breaks are computed once per run of non-space characters instead of pair by pair, because Thai needs the whole run.
- `added.rs` `thai_lines`: clusters are grouped into words and whole words wrap. Only a word wider than the row is broken between clusters, as before (`กิ่กิ่กิ่` in a 16 pt box still gives `กิ่` / `กิ่` / `กิ่`). The spaces where a row ends are dropped, as in the Latin wrapper.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-edit -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit -j 2`: 192 passed (Thai face embedded, so the Thai Add text tests ran rather than skipped)
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: OK, 37 crates; `cargo xtas…

title: M2: Type 0 fonts with /ToUnicode /Identity-H read their codes as Unicode
author: Lcoding15
body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing to PdfCraft.

Base this on `main` — it is the only integration branch. `main` moves fast (it took
396 commits in the three days to 2026-10-12), so a PR that sits for a day usually needs
a rebase. Rebasing the same day you are asked keeps the work from dying of conflicts.
Delete any section below that does not apply.
-->

## What this changes

Some producers (seen in PDFs exported by WSCAD, an electrical CAD tool) write /ToUnicode /Identity-H on Type 0 fonts: a name, not a CMap stream. The identity CMap that name resolves to maps codes to CIDs, not to Unicode, so PdfCraft found no text on such pages: nothing could be selected, copied, searched or edited. Acrobat reads the two-byte codes as UTF-16 code units, and the text comes out right.

Why it matters: WSCAD is widely used for electrical schematics and wiring diagrams, and its PDF exports are what electricians, panel builders and maintenance teams open every day. On these files PdfCraft showed the drawing correctly but behaved as if it were a scan: no text selection, no copy of device tags or wire numbers, no search, and no text editing. Acrobat handles the same files normally, so this is a visible parity gap on a whole class of technical documents, and the fix is small and confined to fonts whose /ToUnicode is that exact name.

After this PR:

    Rendering / text layer (vendored hayro-interpret, patch 44 in vendor/README.md): a Type 0 font whose /ToUnicode is the name /Identity-H or /Identity-V reads each code as its Unicode value (Type0Font::identity_to_unicode). Control characters (C0, DEL, C1) and lone surrogates map to nothing.
    Editing (crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs): the same font is reused for text edits with an identity ToUnicode map built in (one bfrange per high byte, so no range crosses a last-byte boundary, §9.10.3).
    A simple (non-Type 0) font with that name is unchanged: the name is not treated as a ToUnicode map there.

This was split out of #3222 so it can be reviewed …

title: i18n: add Central Kurdish (Sorani) as an interface language
author: Nyanpasuwu
body:
## What this changes

Adds Central Kurdish (Sorani, `ckb`) as an interface language.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/ckb.tsv` — 2,670 entries in logical order, clean-room from the
  meaning of the English labels. The `(context, source)` key set is identical to `ar.tsv`.
- `LANGUAGES` — one row: `ckb`, `کوردیی ناوەندی`, `plural_one_other`, `rtl: true`.
- `DATE_LANGUAGES` — one row with Kurdish month and weekday names, plus `CKB_MONTHS` and
  `CKB_DAYS`. Required because `date_languages_are_the_interface_languages` keeps both
  registries in step.
- `ATTRIBUTION.toml` entry; `ATTRIBUTION.md` regenerated by `cargo xtask assets --write`.
- `docs/localization.md` — native name in the language list, `ckb` in both `ui.set` code lists,
  a paragraph in the RTL section, Kurdish in the coverage sentence.

RTL reuses the Arabic path. The catalog is written in logical (typing) order and `rtl: true`
runs every entry through `bidi::display_rtl` when the catalog loads. No new layout or bidi
code: the four limits `docs/localization.md` lists for Arabic (layout not mirrored, wrapped
paragraphs break at the wrong end, typed text not reordered, labels assembled in code keep
left-to-right order) apply unchanged. Bidirectional layout remains separate work.

Counts use the two [CLDR `ckb` forms](https://www.unicode.org/cldr/charts/48/supplemental/language_plural_rules.html#ckb)
(`one`, `other`). Sorani keeps the noun singular after a numeral, so the 13 `@plural` rows
usually read the same in both forms; this is intended. Locale tags `ckb`, `ckb-IQ`, `ckb-IR`
and `ckb_IQ.UTF-8` resolve through the existing candidate walk.

## How this was verified

title: M12: XFA text honors its horizontal font scale
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA text now honors its horizontal font scale. `<font fontHorizontalScale="85%">`, and `xfa-font-horizontal-scale:90%` in a rich-text span's style, condense the glyphs to that share of their designed width. On `main` both are ignored, so condensed labels are laid out at full width. Labels a form designer narrowed to fit their box then overflow into the next box, or wrap and break mid-word.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. It condenses 37 of its labels (85% to 97%) and 27 rich-text spans (mostly 90%). On `main`:
- the date hints in 10b and 10c break as "(YYYYMMD" / "D)";
- "13. APPROVING AUTHORITY NAME" runs into the TITLE box beside it;
- "a. NUMBER DAYS" and "b. DATE APPROVED" in 15 overlap the boxes after them.

No existing issue (searched for fontHorizontalScale, horizontal scale and condensed).

### Fix

- **Model:** `FontSpec` and `Font` gain a horizontal scale (`h_scale`, a fraction, 1.0 by default), and rich-text `Run`s carry their own. `Font::apply` and `Face::with_run` inherit it like the other font properties.
- **Parsing:** `fontHorizontalScale` and the `xfa-font-horizontal-scale` style are read by one `scale` helper. It takes a percentage, and a bare number counts as one. The result is clamped to 1%–1000%, and anything that isn't a positive number is ignored.
- **Measuring:** `Face::width` multiplies by the scale. Line fitting, wrapping, underlines, caption reserves and content heights all measure through it, so they follow without further change.
- **Drawing:** a condensed span is written with `Tz`, inside a `q … Q` of its own. Horizontal scaling is text state, and text state outlives a text object (ISO 32000-1, 9.3.1), so a bare `Tz` would also condense every span after it. Unscaled spans are written as before.
- **Field values keep full width.** The forms layer draws a field's value from its `/DA` and appearance stream, and neither has horizontal sc…

title: M5: a stamp grows and shrinks with its handles before release (#3518)
author: jay-tau
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3518.

While a handle of a Fill & Sign line was dragged, only the blue selection frame followed the pointer. The line kept its old length until release, so a growing frame ran past the end of the line and a shrinking one had the old line sticking out of it. Check, cross and dot marks, typed signatures and comment stamps behaved the same, when moved as well as when resized. Image signatures already had a live layer (#355). Now every stamp has one.

Resizing a stamp only changes its `/Rect`, and its appearance is stretched to fit (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.5, Algorithm 8.1). So the preview lays two read-only layers over the page: the page without the stamp, and the stamp drawn alone on a transparent page, whose pixels are stretched with the frame. The preview is what the release produces.

- **render:** `RenderConfig.transparent` clears the page to transparent instead of white (or the reading-colours background). `render_page` now takes the `&RenderConfig` instead of two of its fields.
- **annot:** `isolate_annotation` leaves a copy of a page showing one annotation alone: no content, no other annotations. It returns `false` when the annotation has no `/AP /N` to draw.
- **engine:** `Document::stamp_preview(page, index)` builds the two layers from COS clones, like `image_signature_preview`. Nothing in the document, its dirty flag or undo history changes. The page beneath gets the appearances PdfCraft draws on screen for comments that have none, so such comments don't vanish while a stamp is dragged.
- **ui-egui:** `signature_drag.rs` covers every unlocked stamp. Image signatures keep their own path (embedded image, aspect ratio). Other stamps get a stamp layer, rendered as a tile around the stamp at the current zoom (at most 2048 px a side), so it stays sharp. title: M12: a space at the end of a line doesn't count when fitting XFA text
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A space at the end of a line no longer counts when XFA text is fitted into its box. `words` (`crates/xfa/src/text.rs`) keeps the space after each word as part of it ("DATE "). The line-fit test in `layout` compared the full width, space included, with the room left on the line. A space at the end of a line is never drawn, so a label that fits its box exactly but is written with a trailing space wrapped its last word onto a second line.

Forms are often written that way: designers type labels like "a. DATE " and size the box to the drawn text. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. Its "a. DATE " and "b. TIME " labels in sections 14 and 16 are 0.002 pt too wide only because of their trailing space. So "DATE" and "TIME" wrap onto a second line, which lands on top of the field below.

Alignment had half of this already: centered and right-aligned lines ignored one trailing space. They now ignore every trailing space, including words that are only spaces.

No existing issue (searched for trailing space, wrap and line fit).

### Fix

- `ink_width(w)`: a word's width without the spaces it ends with, which is what it takes at the end of a line.
- **Fitting:** a word fits when `line.width + ink_width(w)` fits, and the "a word longer than a line" check uses the same width. The line's running width still adds the full width, space included, so the next word starts after the space as before.
- **Alignment:** the trailing amount is the trailing spaces of the last word that has ink, plus any space-only words after it, instead of a single space width.

|---|---|
| ![Before: each label wraps its last word because of a trailing space](https://github.com/EricKaden/pdfcraft/blob/pr-evidence/xfa-trailing-space-before.png?raw=true) | ![After: each label fits its box on one line](https://github.com/EricKaden/pdfcraft/blob/pr-evidence/xfa-trailing-space-after.png?r…

title: fix(edit): unlink unused image resources on delete
author: skylartaylor
body:
## Summary

Deleting or replacing an image placement now performs a bounded document-wide resource census before optional cleanup. It follows page and inherited resources, Forms, Type3 glyphs selected through fonts or ExtGState, soft masks, tiling patterns, annotation appearance states, and image mask/alternate dependencies. Resources still used elsewhere remain intact.

When nonuse is established, cleanup stages removal of unused image aliases and stale optional mask/alternate edges so a full rewrite can release the old payload. Incomplete, malformed, unsupported, or over-budget cases skip optional pruning while the requested placement edit still succeeds. Failed traversal or rewriting abandons all staged cleanup mutations.

Blank pages without an explicit or inherited Resources dictionary are treated as having empty resources; present malformed values still stop optional cleanup. The rewrite uses a separate document-wide budget: 500,000 inspected entries, at most 100,000 entries per container, 16 MiB of inspected dictionary keys, depth 64, and at most 255 staged objects. Scalar entries count toward the work limit without recursive calls, so ordinary font width tables do not consume the executable-content visit budget.

## Validation

Implementation-session results, not rerun during publication:

- 217 edit tests passed.

title: M12: a negative XFA text indent hangs the first line
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A negative `textIndent` on an XFA paragraph now makes a hanging indent: the first line starts left of the lines after it. On `main`, `layout` (`crates/xfa/src/text.rs`) clamps the indent to 0, so a hanging indent is lost and every line starts at the left margin.

Form designers use hanging indents for numbered labels in narrow boxes: the item number sits at the edge and the wrapped words line up after it. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. It uses `textIndent` of -11, -14 and -18 pt in 10 places. The visible one is 10a, a 58 pt box holding "10a. ACCRUED LEAVE (CR BAL)" with `textIndent="-18pt"` and no left margin. Another viewer lays it out as "10a. ACCRUED" / "LEAVE" / "(CR BAL)", with the second and third lines 18 pt in. On `main`, PdfCraft starts all four of its lines at the edge.

No existing issue (searched for textIndent, hanging indent and negative indent).

### Fix

- **The first line never starts left of the box.** With a negative indent, the left margin used for the lines is `max(marginLeft, -textIndent)`, so the other lines move in to make room. The first line starts `textIndent` from them, which is never left of the box's edge. This matches the other viewer (black-box): with no left margin, the first line sits at the edge and the rest are indented by the hang.
- **With a left margin wider than the hang,** the lines follow the margin as written: the first line starts at `marginLeft + textIndent` and the rest at `marginLeft`, as CSS lays out `text-indent` against `margin-left`.
- **A positive indent is unchanged:** it still moves only the first line in.
- **Width and alignment follow:** each line's available width and its alignment offset are taken from where it starts, so a hanging first line has the extra room and the indented lines have less.

title: Text: paragraphs respect typography and filled panels
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Separate paragraphs at real style and container boundaries.

## What this changes

`text_paragraphs` and `object_list` merged rows that only looked like one paragraph: a heading over body text, a label over a different font, or text in two filled panels side by side. Grouping now separates rows on:

- a large row-size change;
- a change of dominant font family (subset prefixes and weight and style suffixes are ignored, including stacked ones such as `TimesNewRomanPS-BoldMT`). A row in one of PdfCraft's generated fallback faces (Inter for Cyrillic, Hebrew, Japanese) is not a family change: the edit chose that face for characters the paragraph's font lacks;
- a filled-panel boundary: rows inside different filled rectangles, or one inside and one outside. A rectangle counts as a panel for a run only when it is at least 15% taller than the run's line box, so a highlight or inline shading drawn to the height of the glyphs doesn't split its paragraph. Along one line, a box that holds only part of the text and is under 1.75 times its height is a highlight for all of that text, however padded; a panel's edge between two labels on one line still separates them. The same holds when one `Tj` draws the whole line: a highlight-sized box that does not reach across the text is a highlight for it.

A rectangle is a panel only for text drawn after it, in the page's drawing order through the forms that draw it. A box painted over text afterwards is a cover (a redaction), so it does not split the line it covers. A panel repainted behind each of its rows, under any matrix, is one panel: boxes that are the same on the page share an identity.

Panel identity is page-wide. It holds across content streams, a rectangle and its fill in separate streams, and transformed forms. A panel drawn on the page that contains form text still counts as the same panel. Stroked-only or clip-only rectangles are not panels. Compatible multiline text and inline style changes (bold, italic, a size bump within…

title: M12: XFA labels and buttons without a size grow to their content
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA text labels and buttons without an explicit size are now as large as their content. On `main`, `measure` (`crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`) gives a draw or a field without `w` all the width available. A button without `h` is also sized like a text field in its field font, with text-field padding. That means:

- A right-aligned label slides to the far side of its subform, away from the field it labels.
- A button spreads across whatever lies beside it, and stands taller than its caption.

This PR makes three changes, one commit each:

1. **A label or button without a width is as wide as its text.** A draw holding text, or rich text, takes its text's unwrapped width (`text::natural_width`, the longest paragraph with its margins and first-line indent) plus its margins. A button takes its caption's width. Both stay within what is available and are clamped to `minW`/`maxW`, the same rule containers without a width already follow.
2. **A button without a height is as tall as its caption,** in the caption's own font, never below `minH`. It no longer uses the field font's line plus the 4 pt padding that text fields reserve.
3. **A button's box is its whole field.** Its widget rectangle was its content area, inside its margins, but a button's border belongs to the field, so a top margin made the button shorter than the box it is meant to fill. The margins now pad the caption only.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. It has 420 text labels without a width, and its Instructions button has only `minW` and `minH`. On `main`:

- The Instructions button stretches across the form's header, over "1. CONTROL NUMBER". It covers the "Form issues? Send an Email to: …" line beside it, and stands about 17 pt tall where 10.5 pt is asked for.
- The right-aligned "PERSONNEL/FINANCE ONLY: … from date (YYYYMMDD):" label slides into the "to date" label after it, and the two overlap.
- "APD AEM v1.…

## What this changes

A push button's caption is now drawn in the font, size and color its `/DA` asks for.

On `main`, `button_appearance` (`crates/forms/src/author.rs`) ignores the `/DA`. It always writes regular Helvetica in black, sized from the button's height (`(height - 4) × 0.6`, clamped to 4–14 pt). A button asking for 9 pt bold in a 10.5 pt box therefore gets a 4 pt regular caption.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. Its "Attachments Menu" (`/HeBo 9 Tf`) and "DA Form 31 - Instructions" (`/HeBo 8 Tf`) buttons come out tiny and regular-weight.

No existing issue (searched for button caption, DA font and caption size).

### Fix

**`appearance::button_caption`** draws a caption in the font its `/DA` names, from the form's `/DR` (the same `dr_font` text fields use), falling back to Helvetica. It uses the `/DA` size, or the old height-based size when the `/DA` asks for an automatic size (0), and the `/DA`'s color operator. `button_appearance` takes the widget's `/DA`, else the field's own or inherited one, as `field_appearance_drawn` does.

### Centering, and #2900

The caption is centered by `FontText::width`, which on `main` measures every simple font with Helvetica's widths. A bold caption is wider than that, so on this branch alone it sits a little right of center.

An earlier version of this PR also changed `FontText::width` to measure each font with its own widths. #2900 (@marcoarnulfo) makes the same change, and more: it also handles fonts that remap codes through `/Differences`. It was opened first, so I dropped mine. Merged locally, the two combine cleanly, and the bold captions center: the centering assertion I dropped from this PR's test passes with #2900.

title: M5: snap to drawing for the drawing tools (object snap), F3
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Commenting on drawings (plans, schematics, CAD exports) asks for the points of a connected line or a polygon to sit *on* the drawing, as CAD's object snap does. The measuring tools already snap to the page's vector paths; the drawing tools now do the same (parity `comment.snap-to-drawing`, new, `shipped`; beyond Acrobat):

- **Snap to drawing** (F3, or the `circle-dot` button on the drawing tools' quick bar; remembered across starts) makes the points of connected lines, polygons, clouds, lines, arrows, rectangles and ovals land on the page's own paths: endpoints, midpoints, intersections and the paths themselves, within 6 screen points of the pointer, with the measuring tools' green ring and the target's name under the pointer while drawing. Freehand drawing and text markup don't snap. (Shift's hold while drawing, level or plumb, is its own PR, #4285.)
- **The comments already drawn snap too:** lines and arrows, connected lines, polygons and clouds, rectangles and ovals give their ends and corners, the middles of their sides, the centres of closed ones and the lines themselves, so lines join end to end. A comment being moved, resized or reshaped is left out (it would cling to where it was); hidden comments don't snap. They are a second, small geometry beside the page's (`measure::snap::{comment_outlines, outline_geometry}`, `Document::comment_paths`), rebuilt per edit without extracting the page's paths again; candidates from both are merged points first, then the nearest path.
- **Headless:** `comment_add` takes `snap: true` (page paths and the comments already drawn) (and `snap_tolerance`, in points on the displayed page, 6 by default) and reports how many points moved (`snapped`), so a script placing a polyline from measured coordinates gets the same corners a hand would.

title: Save commits the open Edit Text boxes before writing the file (#3496)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3496.

## What this changes

Save (and every save path that goes through `save_then`) already commits what is typed in a form field and the Fill & Sign type box before the bytes are taken (`commit_typing_in`). The Edit a PDF ▸ Text tool was missing from that list, so a save while its box was still open wrote the pre-edit file and reported success, as the issue describes. The text only reached the document when the box committed on click-away.

`commit_typing_in` now also commits, the same way click-away does:

- a new text box (`content.draft`), through `ContentView::finish_draft`, as the canvas does when the user clicks elsewhere;
- a paragraph open in the editor (`line_editor`) when it has changes, through `edit_text_ui::finished_edit`, as `put_down_edit_text` and the click-to-another-paragraph path (#2022) do. Clicking a page with the Text tool reaches either box, so both are covered.

For a tab that is not the active one (a save panel answering later, Close All), an open draft or a changed paragraph now counts as typing, so the tab is brought forward before the commit, like the other kinds of typing. A draft the standard fonts can't draw is still held open with its warning, as before (that check runs first).

## How you verified it

No local toolchain for this change; CI runs fmt, clippy and the tests. Two new unit tests, each fails without the fix (the box is left open and nothing is added to the document):

- `editing::tests::save_commits_the_open_text_box`: a new text box open at save time ends up as an added item, and the box is closed.
- `edit_text_ui::tests::save_applies_the_paragraph_open_in_the_editor`: a paragraph retyped in the editor is in the document after the save, and the editor is closed.

## Never-crash

No new `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing in non-test code; the commit returns `true` (nothing to do) when the document or tab is gone, like `commit_open_fill_text`.

title: Search: centre the active match in the viewport (#3530)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3530.

Moving to a search match (next/previous, Enter/Shift+Enter, a click in the Search panel, and the first match found as you type) scrolled the view so the match sat about 60 pt below the top of the window, and kept the horizontal scroll. On a zoomed-in page the match could end up off to one side, out of view.

`flash_match`, which every one of those paths goes through, now also sets `goto_point` to put the centre of the whole match at the centre of the window, as Acrobat does. It is the same mechanism and the same window-centre offset that a `/FitR` destination already uses (`go_to_dest`). The point is turned by the view rotation the same way `PageInfo::dest_fraction` does it, so it still lands on the match after View ▸ Rotate View. The scroll is clamped to the content as before, so a match near a page edge scrolls as far as it can.

To get the horizontal fraction, `DocView::page_heights` became `page_sizes` (width, height). It is only used for this.

Tests:
- `explicit_search_jumps_record_history_and_keep_match_destination` now checks that all three explicit paths (`go_to_match`, `find_step` forward and back) aim the match centre at the window centre. Without the fix `goto_point` is `None` and the test fails.
- New `search_centres_the_match_on_a_rotated_view` covers view rotations of 90°, 180° and 270°.

title: M6: util.scand reads dates as another viewer does
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

`util.scand(cFormat, cDate)` now exists, in both AcroForm and XFA scripts. It turns typed text into a `Date` by a `util.printd` format, and forms use it to check typed dates and to count days between two of them. On `main` it is missing, so a script that calls it throws `TypeError: not a callable function` and stops there.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. It calls `util.scand` 60 times, in the exit scripts of ten date fields on its emergency-leave page. Each script tries six formats in turn (`yyyymmdd`, `yymmdd`, `yyyymdd`, `yyyymmd`, `yyyymd`, `yymd`), so a date typed as 20261018, 261018, 2026118 or 2618 is rewritten as YYYYMMDD. Anything else gets "Invalid date entered".

No existing issue (searched for scand, util.scand and date parsing).

### How it reads dates

The public JavaScript API reference for PDF forms gives `util.scand`'s format letters (those of `util.printd`), the two-digit-year rule and `null` on failure. It doesn't say how lenient the function is. So I measured that black-box: a synthetic file (its script is below) runs 51 cases, plus that form's six-format check, in another viewer. This branch gives the same answer for all 59. What they showed:

- **Separators:** fields may be separated by anything but digits and letters, whether or not the format separates them. So `yyyymmdd` reads "2026-10-18" and "2026 10 18", and `mm/dd/yyyy` reads "10-18-2026". But nothing may come before the first field or after the last: " 20261018 ", "20261018x" and "x20261018" are `null`.
- **Digits typed together** fill the fields the format writes together, each with exactly as many digits as it has letters. `yyyymdd` reads "2026118" as January 18, `yyyymmd` reads it as November 8, and `yyyymd` refuses it. A run of digits for one field alone may have one or two digits (`mm/dd/yyyy` reads "1/5/2026"), except a four-digit year (`yyyy` refuses "26").
