title: fix(render): hit-test selection against the glyph quad, not its bounding box (#3693)
author: MatrixMagician
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3693.

`PageText::nearest` measured the distance from the pointer to each glyph's axis-aligned bounding box. In sheared (synthetic italic) or turned text that box is wider than the glyph and overlaps its neighbours, so a pointer on a letter was also inside the box of the letter before it, at distance 0, and the earlier glyph won. A drag ending on the last letter of a word or line then ended one or two letters short, and Copy missed it.

Now a glyph whose drawn em box (`quad`) holds the point wins, the one with the nearest centre if several do. If no quad holds the point, the bounding-box distance still decides, so pointers past a line end or between lines behave as before; a tie there goes to the nearer glyph centre rather than the first glyph. Upright and 90° text are unaffected.

title: fix(text): character spacing is not a word gap in Chinese (#3713)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3713.

A label spread to the width of a longer one (分散對齊, as on Taiwanese forms and 公文) is one show with character spacing, so **every gap inside it is the same**, while the value beside it has none. The line's typical gap is therefore the value's zero, and from half a line height upwards each of the label's gaps read as a word gap.

Measured on the reporter's fixture, all nine `Tc` steps:

```
before   Tc 0.1 – 0.4 em   受文者如正本
         Tc 0.5 – 1.0 em   受 文 者 如正本        text_find 受文者: 6 of 9 lines
after    every step        受文者如正本           text_find 受文者: 9 of 9 lines
```

### Why repetition, and not width

`Tc` is added after every glyph of a string (ISO 32000-2 §9.3.2), so spread text repeats one gap. A gap that repeats between consecutive CJK characters is therefore spacing **at any width**, and a gap that stands on its own is read as spacing only below one line height (it was half of one).

Width alone cannot tell the two apart: two cells of a row two character widths apart look exactly like two characters spread by two ems. The run structure would tell them apart, but it isn't in the glyph list — `TextGlyph` carries text, box, quad and direction, and the "runs" in `arrange` are geometric groupings, not shows — so the repetition is what is left to measure.

### What this keeps, and what it gives up

Measured on a fixture of the same shape (`姓名` and `王小明` on one line):

| gap between two cells | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 20 character widths | two segments: `姓名` / `王小明` | unchanged |
| 2 character widths | `姓名 王小明` | `姓名 王小明` |

So a row's cells keep their space, and a column gap wider than about three line heights was already a separate segment.

What it gives up is a row of **evenly spaced single characters**, whose gaps repeat like a spread label's and so now join. Taking word gaps from the content's own space characters on a tagged page — the report's second direction, which §14.8.2.6.2 NOTE 1 invites — would settle that case properly, and is a …

title: Redact: count shared outline items once so the walk ends
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

Counting the bookmarks of a hostile outline no longer takes unbounded time. The count behind the bookmarks category (used by Remove Hidden Information, Sanitize and the scan report) followed `/First` and `/Next` with no record of what it had visited, so an outline whose items share children was walked along every path: 60 levels of two shared items is about 2^60 steps and the count never returned. The scan runs the count before anything is removed, so Remove Hidden Information and Sanitize hung on such a file too.

`outline_len` in `crates/redact/src/sanitize.rs` now keeps the set of items it has reached. An item that two others name is counted once, and a level stops at an item that was already counted. A total budget of 100,000 items bounds the count. The per-level cap and the depth limit of 64 are unchanged. Ordinary outlines count exactly as before. Removing the outline itself does not walk it, so the count is the only walk that needed bounding.

title: Join /Contents pieces with a space in measure snap
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3570

**Cause.** `measure_snap` joined the `/Contents` array pieces with a newline. A trailing comment at the end of one piece therefore ended at the piece boundary, and the next piece's first line was read as live geometry. title: Give a redacted or sanitized copy a new file identifier
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

A redacted or sanitized copy no longer keeps the `/ID` of the file it came from. Applying redactions and running Sanitize now make the saved copy write a fresh trailer `/ID` pair. Before, the previous revision was dropped, but the identifier still linked the copy to its original.

This is a design choice, not something the specification requires: ISO 32000-2 (section 14.4) defines `/ID[0]` as a permanent identifier that survives incremental updates of the same document. A redacted or sanitized copy is a new document derived from the original, so this PR gives it new strings in both positions. If you would rather keep `/ID[0]` and change only `/ID[1]`, that is a one-line change; tell me which you prefer.

- `pdfcraft-cos`: `Document::require_full_save_with_new_id()` and `Document::new_id_required()`. A flagged full save regenerates both `/ID` strings. An encrypted file keeps `/ID[0]`, which its file key is derived from (the empty string when the file had no usable first entry), and gets a new `/ID[1]`. `SaveOptions` gains `id_entropy: Option<[u8; 16]>`: when it is given, the new identifier depends only on that entropy and the written bytes, so tests can pin output.
- `pdfcraft-redact`: `apply` and `sanitize()` request the new identifier. `sanitize()` does so whether or not it removed anything.
- Ordinary saves are unchanged. They write the same bytes as before (checked below).

Deliberately not changed: `remove_hidden`, the per-category removal used by the remove-hidden edit and by the optimizer's discard option, still keeps the identifier. No engine, automation, UI or dependency change.

title: M2: structure /ActualText reaches form XObjects with their own /StructParents (#3732)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
> **Stacked on #3689.** This changes the vendor patch (53) that #3689 adds, so the branch is built on top of it. Until #3689 merges, this PR also shows its nine commits. **Review only the last commit, 17a4cff3.** I'll rebase onto `main` once #3689 lands.

## What this changes

Fixes #3732 (follow-up to #3660 / #3689, from @mtlcl410's test report).

A form XObject that has its own `/StructParents` is structured content (ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.4). Its MCIDs index the structural parent tree under that key, the same way the page's MCIDs index the entry under the page's key. #3689 only applied structure-element `/ActualText` to the page's own content (nesting depth 0), so a paragraph in a tagged form still read its glyphs (`f0rm`, not `form`). Tagged generators often put whole paragraphs in forms.

- **vendor/hayro-interpret, patch (53):** the depth-0 test is replaced by a parent tree key carried in `Context`.
  - `interpret_page` enters structured content under the page's `/StructParents`.
  - `draw_form_xobject` gives a form its own `/StructParents` while it is drawn from structured content, or no key when it has none. Annotation appearances and forms inside forms are included.
  - Soft masks, patterns and Type 3 glyphs build fresh contexts that are never structured, so what they draw stays outside.
  - The hook is now `Device::structure_marked_content(key, mcid)` (was `page_marked_content(mcid)`).
- **crates/render/src/text/replacements.rs:** replacements are resolved lazily, one key at a time, as the content reaches it. Elements, texts and all budgets are shared over the page. There is a new page-wide budget for parent tree reads (nodes, `/Nums` pairs, `/Kids` and MCID items), so a page drawing many keyed forms can't make it reread a large tree once per form.
- A page whose own content has no marked content needs no `/StructParents`. The forms it draws are structured all the same.

title: fix: terminate inline images at their known data length
author: WhatSupQuebec
body:
## What this changes

An inline image whose dictionary states its data length now ends at exactly that many bytes. A `/L` (or `/Length`, PDF 2.0 Table 91) states the encoded length outright — filtered images included; otherwise an uncompressed image's length is computed from `/W`, `/H`, `/BPC` and `/CS` (full key names included, and an image mask's optional `/BPC` defaulting to 1 per Table 87). An `EI` found strictly inside that many bytes is part of a binary scan and is skipped; the `EI` at the exact end (one whitespace byte aside) is accepted without the look-ahead heuristics, which binary content after the image can fool. Filtered images without `/L` and unknown colour spaces keep the existing heuristics, and the length arithmetic is checked.

This was split out of #3683 at review request: it changes how every content stream's inline images are parsed, so it deserves its own description and review.

title: Refuse an OCR batch whose inputs would write one output file
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

Two inputs to the batch OCR tool `ocr_recognize_files` that would write the same output file no longer overwrite each other. Before, each input's searchable copy went into the output folder under its own file name, so `one/scan.pdf` and `two/scan.pdf` both wrote `out/scan.pdf`. The second copy replaced the first while both results reported success.

Now the whole batch is refused before anything happens: the output folder is not created, no input is read, and the OCR engines are not loaded. The error names the colliding file names and says what to do. A request without collisions runs exactly as before.

Names are compared the way the default filesystem compares them: without regard to case on Windows and macOS (`scan.pdf` and `Scan.PDF` are one file there), exactly elsewhere, and on Windows a trailing dot or space is not part of a name (`scan.pdf.` is `scan.pdf`). The compared name is the one the output is written under, after the separator replacement the writer already applies. The tool description says so.

Not changed here: the batch dialog in the desktop app writes its outputs the same way (`crates/ui-egui/src/ocr_ui.rs`, `ocr_files_into`). It needs its own change.

## What this changes

title: M9: empty signature fields show a Sign tab, sized to the field
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

Each empty signature field a click would sign now carries a small **Sign** tab in its top-left corner, so whoever has to sign can see where. On `main`, clicking an empty signature field already starts signing for it, but nothing marks the field. It looks like any other box, and a field without a drawn appearance isn't visible at all until fields are highlighted.

- **Which fields.** The fields a click would sign: an unsigned, visible field on this page, with a rectangle that passes the screen-space guard the validation badges already use. The document must allow filling (`allows_form_filling`, the check `forms_ui::page_input` makes). The form field of that name must be a signature field that isn't read-only, with a shown widget at that rectangle.
- **When.** With the Select tool, and not while preparing a form: the same condition as the field hit test, so the tab only appears where a click signs.
- **Look.** A chip in the theme's accent color with the Lucide `signature` icon and "Sign" in white, the way the app's primary buttons are drawn. The label is `tl!("Sign")`, which every catalog already translates, so no catalog changes.
- **Size.** The tab is sized to its field: 0.4 of the field's height on screen, from 10 to 18 pt. The inset, icon, padding, label and corners scale with it. It shows "Sign" from 14 pt up, when the whole tab fits in half the field's width, and the icon alone otherwise. A field too small for the 10 pt icon chip, or one whose rectangle isn't finite, gets no tab.
- **Click.** Over the tab the pointer turns into a hand, and a click opens signing for that field. The tab is drawn over every field, so a click on it goes to its own field, even where another field overlaps it and comes first in the form (which takes the click everywhere else). Where tabs overlap, the one painted last (on top) takes the click. A field that straddles the page's edge gets its tab in the part on the page, since fields take clicks on the page only, or…

title: fix(ui): a metadata-only change on disk is not a new version (#3755)
author: kekeandzeyu
body:
## What this changes

Fixes the false-positive half of #3755: on macOS, saving a document makes PdfCraft report a few moments later that the file "changed on disk". When the document had no unsaved changes, it also reloads silently, which drops the undo history.

**Cause.** Since #2218, `file_watch::Stamp` on Unix includes the change time (`ctime`/`ctime_nsec`). That is deliberate: it catches a rebuild that keeps the length and mtime. Shortly after PdfCraft writes a file, macOS adds extended attributes to it (`com.apple.macl`, `com.apple.provenance`, …). That moves the ctime and leaves the bytes alone. Both stamp comparisons then take it for a new version:
- the watcher (`file_changed`) reloads a clean document, losing undo, or shows the "changed on disk" notice on a dirty one;
- Save (`disk_differs`) shows the "file changed, overwrite?" dialog.

**Fix.** `ctime` stays in the stamp, so #2218's detection is unchanged. A changed stamp is now a hint, confirmed against the content before anything happens:
- `file_changed`: the watcher has already read the new bytes. If they equal `Document::saved_bytes()` (the file the document came from), the stamp is recorded in `known` and `basis`, and nothing else happens: no reload, no notice, and the next Save doesn't ask.
- `disk_differs`: when the stamp differs, the new `holds()` compares the file with `saved_bytes()`. A different length means a different version with no read. Same length means one read and a byte comparison. Equal bytes are not a conflict. A file that can't be read still counts as a difference, so Save still asks.

A real external rewrite still reloads or asks as before, including one that keeps the length (covered by a test).

**Not in this PR:** keeping the undo history across a *real* external change. A reload replaces the whole document, and that needs a separate design discussion (the bot suggested splitting the issue).

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-e…

title: fix(render): an isolated DeviceCMYK transparency group blends in CMYK (#3776)
author: jpeskov
body: ## What this changes Fixes #3776. Refs #2145 (Ghent PDF Output Suite 5.0, patch 16.2). The elements of an **isolated** transparency group whose colour space is `DeviceCMYK` now blend in CMYK, as ISO 32000-2 requires. Before this change, PdfCraft converted each colour to RGB and blended in RGB. Ghent patch 16.2 then showed an X in almost every cell. Now no clear X shows. Three cells keep a faint X (see "How you verified it"). *Top: `main`. Bottom: this PR. The fixture is the script from #3776.* **The rules.** Blending occurs in the group's colour space (§11.3.4). For a subtractive space, each component is complemented before the blend function and complemented again after it. For the nonseparable modes, C, M and Y blend as their complements R, G and B, and K is not blended (§11.3.5.3). K comes from the backdrop for Hue, Saturation and Color, and from the source for Luminosity. **The method.** An isolated group starts from a transparent backdrop of its own (§11.4.7). Thus the renderer can calculate its contents apart from the page. Two vendored patches do this: - **hayro-interpret patch (45)** - `CmykGroup` records the group at `Do`: the state after `/Matrix`, the root transform and the interpreter cache. It is similar to `SoftMask`. - `Device::draw_isolated_cmyk_group` is a new device hook. Its default returns `false`, so other devices do not change. - `draw_form_xobject` sends a group to the hook when the group is isolated, is not knockout, has `/CS /DeviceCMYK` and has a layer of its own. When the hook returns `false`, the contents are drawn as before, through `interpret_form_contents` (now a function of its own). - `Color::ink_tints` gives the process tints of a colour: `DeviceCMYK` as it is, and `DeviceGray` as black only (§10.4.2.2)…

title: M6: XFA calculations rerun only when what they read changed
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

After any change (a typed value, a click, a field's change script), PdfCraft reran every calculate script in an XFA form, in document order. Another viewer reruns only the calculations whose inputs changed. The difference shows on real forms: when a form carries a hidden second copy of a section whose calculation writes the visible copy's field, rerunning everything lets the hidden copy write last.

- **Reads are recorded.** Each script run reports the fields and exclusion groups whose value it read, once each, capped at 4,096 per run (`XfaOutcome::reads` and `reads_cut`). That covers `rawValue`, `value`, `formattedValue`, `isNull` and a field's text through `toString`/`valueOf`. In FormCalc it covers references, function arguments and `isNull`. Writes and other properties (presence, access) are not reads.
- **The engine keeps them per document** (`CalcDeps`): what each calculation read when it last ran, with a reverse index from fields to the calculations that read them.
- **What runs after a change:**
  - the calculations that read the changed field, or any field bound to the same data node;
  - the field's own calculation, when anything else wrote it;
  - any calculation that has never run (a new row's).

  These run round after round, in document order, until nothing is due. A user's or script's write wakes the readers even when the value is the same. A calculation's own write wakes them only when it changed the value, so calculations that agree don't keep waking each other.
- **Still every calculation:** opening, a reset, `xfa.form.recalculate()`, added or removed rows, and imported data, as on `main`.
- **Undo, redo and revert** give the document a fresh record, so the next change runs every calculation once and learns again. An edit that runs the form's scripts works on a copy of the record and keeps it only when it succeeds; an edit that runs none copies nothing. When opening can't keep what its scripts changed, it drops what they read …

title: Fill & Sign marks stay upright on rotated pages (#2392)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fill & Sign marks (check, cross, dot, line) on a page with `/Rotate` were drawn in the page's own axes. Typed text and rubber stamps already record the page rotation (`PCTextRotate`, `PCStampRotate`) and draw upright in their displayed box; marks did neither. On a page turned 180° the checkmark came out upside down (the report: scanned pages are often stored that way), and on 90°/270° it lay on its side and a line stood on end. The cross and dot only looked right because they are symmetric.

Reproduced with `pdfcraft-cli` on `main`: a checkmark and typed text on blank pages turned 0/90/180/270. The text was upright on all four; the checkmark rendered as ✓, ‹, ^, ›.

- **`annot` / `lib.rs`:** `Shape::Mark` records `PCStampRotate` on a turned page (marks are `/Stamp` annotations, like the rubber stamps that already use it).
- **`annot` / `appearance.rs`:** the turned-box and `/Matrix` code the rubber stamps had is moved ahead of the stamp `match` and shared, so marks are drawn upright in their displayed box and mapped into `/Rect` the same way. Unturned marks are drawn exactly as before.
- **`FillMark::rect_at(at, rotation)`:** the mark's box, sized in displayed axes (a line is 36 × 4 pt *as displayed*). It replaces two copies of the size arithmetic in the Fill & Sign tool (`ui-egui/src/fill_sign.rs`) and `fill_sign_add` (`automation/src/comments.rs`), which both sized the box in the page's own axes.

Marks placed before this keep their old appearance (no rotation was recorded for them).

On the comment that a **date** stamp is also upside down: dates are Fill & Sign *text*, which already carries `PCTextRotate`; in the reproduction above typed text was upright on every rotation, so this PR doesn't change it.

Fixes #2392

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-annot -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-automation -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-annot` (45), …

title: M6: XFA formattedValue shows a date in the field's display picture
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

In XFA scripts, a date field's `formattedValue` now gives the value as the field's display picture (`<format><picture>`) shows it, as another viewer does. On `main` it gave the raw value, the ISO date, so a script doing date arithmetic on `formattedValue` read `2026-10-20` where it expected `20261020`.

- **The template keeps the display picture.** `Field::display_picture` is parsed from `<format><picture>`, apart from the edit picture (`<ui>…<picture>`).
- **`formatted_value(picture, raw)`** shows an ISO date in a `date{…}` picture, using the first of several alternatives (`date{YYYYMMDD}` turns `2026-10-20` into `20261020`). It reuses `date_pattern` and `iso_to_pattern`. It returns `None`, so the raw value stands, for:
  - other kinds of picture (`num`, `text`, `time`);
  - a clause it can't read;
  - a value that isn't an ISO date.
- **The script snapshot carries it.** The live form keeps each field's display picture, and the engine works out the formatted text when it builds the snapshot, so a value refreshed in place is never shown stale.
- **JavaScript and FormCalc** read `formattedValue` from it. A script that sets the value in the same run then reads the raw value, since the formatted text it started with is out of date.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. Its "10b TO" calculation adds the days requested to 10b FROM by reading `FROM.formattedValue` as `YYYYMMDD` (`substr(0,4)`, `substr(4,2)`, `substr(6,2)`). On `main` that read the ISO date and gave `NaNNaNNaN`. With this branch and #3397 together, FROM `20261020` with 3 days gives TO `20261022`, as in another viewer. #3397 is needed too because the same calculation also checks that `rawValue` is the 10-character ISO date, and on that branch's data pictures scripts read `20261020` until its latest commit.

No existing issue (searched for formattedValue, display picture and format picture).

title: M4: a file stamped anew with the same bytes is still the document's version
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Sync clients set a file's times again after uploading it. One of them rewrites the modification time to the whole second about ten seconds after a save (which also moves the change time); Nextcloud and Dropbox do similar things. The file watcher (#431) and Save's check (#2166) compare the file's stamp (length, times, inode), so for a document in a synced folder:

- a clean document **reloaded** silently ten seconds after every save, which threw its undo history away;
- with changes made since, the **"This file changed on disk"** notice came up about nothing;
- the next **Save asked "Save over the changed file?"** although the file on disk was exactly what PdfCraft had written.

Now the bytes decide when only the stamp moved:

- The watcher reads a changed file anyway; when its bytes are the ones the document was opened from or last saved as (`Document::saved_bytes`), the new stamp is recorded as the document's version (`known` and `basis`) and nothing else happens.
- Save (`save_doc_to_then`) asks `disk_is_another_version`: the stamp first, as before; only when it differs and the length is the same is the file read and compared with `saved_bytes` (and its stamp checked again afterwards, so a write in between still counts). Same bytes: written at once, and the new stamp is the document's from then on.

Parity `core.reload-changed-files`: notes and evidence updated.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test reload` (13), `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib file_watch`, `cargo xtask parity`

**Tests** (`crates/ui-egui/tests/reload.rs`): `a_file_stamped_anew_with_the_same_bytes_is_still_the_documents_version`: after a save, the file's modification time is set again without changing a byte; the document is not reloaded (its undo history is still there), changes made since get no notice, Save writes at once; a real new version aft…

title: M5: the arrow keys move the selected comment
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

With a comment selected, the arrow keys scrolled the view (↑ ↓) or turned the page (← →), so a text box, rectangle or line could only be placed with the mouse. Now:

- an arrow key moves the selected comment **one screen pixel**, and **⌘/Ctrl or Shift and an arrow ten**, as Edit text already nudges objects (#1520);
- up is up on screen whatever the zoom, the page's `/Rotate` and the view's rotation (the step is one screen pixel mapped to user space, so it follows the zoom: fine steps when zoomed in, visible ones on a zoomed-out A0 plan);
- each press is one undo step (`Edit::MoveAnnotation`, "Move comment");
- the keys are taken before the view's navigation, which has them back as soon as nothing is selected (Escape);
- text markup stays with its text, a locked comment where it is, and nothing moves while a text field has the keyboard.

New parity entry `comment.keyboard-nudge` (P2, shipped; headless through `comment_edit move`), `docs/ui-parity.md` row extended.

title: Alt+Left / Alt+Right go back and forward through the view history (#3632)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

- **Alt+← / Alt+→ (⌥ on macOS) go back and forward through the view history**, as in Acrobat and browsers. Following a link already records where it was followed from (`go_to_dest` → `go_to_page` pushes the history); Previous view / Next view only had ⌘[ / ⌘] (Ctrl elsewhere), and Alt+← turned the page because `canvas::shortcuts` reads ← / → whatever the modifiers. The new bindings are consumed in `canvas::shortcuts` before the arrows turn the page.
- **Nudging a selection no longer takes Alt+arrows.** In Edit text & images, `object_ui::nudge_keys` runs before `canvas::shortcuts`, and its `consume_key(Modifiers::NONE / SHIFT, arrow)` also matched a press with Alt (egui's logical matching ignores extra Alt), so with a picture or objects selected Alt+← nudged the selection and dirtied the document. It now takes only arrows pressed alone or with Shift, **judged by each key event's own modifiers** rather than the frame's, so Alt released within the same frame as Alt+← can't turn it into a nudge (and a plain arrow pressed before Alt goes down still nudges). Ctrl/⌘+arrows were already left to the page turn and still are.
- **Help ▸ Keyboard shortcuts** lists `Alt+← / Alt+→` (`⌥← / ⌥→` on macOS) as "Previous view / Next view", reusing the existing translated labels: no catalogue changes.

Fixes #3632

title: docs(windows): register the portable copy as a PDF handler for the current user (#3758)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3758 (and the cause found in #625). The portable zip registers nothing with Windows, so choosing `pdfcraft.exe` under "Open with" often doesn't stick: double-clicking a PDF then never starts PdfCraft, and the log isn't touched. The MSI registers a `PdfCraft.Document` ProgID, `.pdf\OpenWithProgids`, `Applications\pdfcraft.exe` and Default Programs capabilities (`packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs`). The portable copy, by design, writes nothing outside its folder.

This is docs only:
- `packaging/windows/portable.txt`, which every portable copy ships with and which only marks portable mode by being there (`crates/ui-egui/src/portable.rs`: the contents aren't read), gets a section "Opening PDF files with this copy". It has PowerShell lines that register the copy for the current user only (`HKEY_CURRENT_USER`). They add a ProgID (`PdfCraft.Portable`, so it never collides with the MSI's `PdfCraft.Document` on a PC that has both), list it under `.pdf\OpenWithProgids`, and write Default Programs `Capabilities` (name, description, `FileAssociations\.pdf`) registered under `RegisteredApplications`, the same shape the MSI writes for all users. It then points to Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Default apps. The undo lines say to choose another `.pdf` default first, so Windows isn't left pointing at a removed ProgID.
- The README's portable paragraph says where to find it.

It doesn't add a "make default" button, the other suggestion in #3758. That would make the portable build write to the registry itself, which is a decision for the maintainers. Windows also doesn't let an app set the default; the user always picks it in Settings.

title: fix(organize): imports find the objects they added when new numbers fill gaps
author: petarlaf
body:
## What this changes

`import_pages_with` and `insert_file_pages`, which Duplicate, Replace and Insert Pages go through, took every object numbered above the destination's highest number before the import for one the import added. That only holds while new objects get higher numbers. Once no number is left above the highest, `Document::add` fills free numbers below it (`allocate_num`). That happens when:

- the trailer's `/Size` is exhausted (4294967295 or more; cos already logs "exhausted trailer /Size"), or
- the document holds object 4294967295. An edit to an object of that number creates it: for a damaged file whose catalog is object 4294967295, Recover Page Tree writes the catalog there.

In those documents:

- the imported copies skipped resource sharing, so each import stored its fonts and images again;
- a refused import (a source too deep to follow, #1800) left the objects it had added in the destination;
- with object 4294967295, `n + 1` overflowed. Debug builds panic (`import.rs:243: attempt to add with overflow`). In release it wraps to 0, so every object in the document counts as added: a refused import frees them all, and a successful one runs resource sharing over the whole document.

Both functions now record the object numbers before the import and treat the numbers present afterwards but not before as the import's (`added_objects`). A `HashSet` keeps this independent of the order `object_numbers` returns.

`saturating_add(1)` would stop the panic but not the rest. With object 4294967295, the rollback would then free that object, which the document already had, and keep the objects the import added (see the sabotage runs below).

In the app the engine edits a working copy and discards it on error, so the refusal path never cost a user their document there. The functions still broke their own contract, and the missed resource sharing reached saved files.

Found by a local mutation fuzzer that drives the organize operations on mutated files in a debug…

title: Allow Ctrl+wheel zoom in an unfocused window (#3736)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #3736.

Plain wheel scrolling already works in a visible PDFcraft window while another application has focus, but Ctrl+wheel zoom did nothing until you clicked the window first. The cause is in `document_area`: the wheel/pinch zoom branch was gated on `navigation_enabled`, and that also required `ui.input(|i| i.focused)`.

The zoom branch now uses its own `zoom_enabled` gate. It is the same check minus the focus requirement, so an open dialog, the close prompt, the command palette or disabled UI still block zoom. `navigation_enabled`, which the other page gestures use (wheel glide, the selection-drag wheel and so on), still requires focus as before, so the change covers only what the issue asks for. It is in the shared egui path, not limited to Windows, because the existing unfocused scrolling also works on every platform.

Test: `ctrl_wheel_zooms_an_unfocused_window` opens a document in an `egui_kittest` harness, marks the window unfocused, and sends a Ctrl+wheel notch over the page. It checks that the command palette still blocks the zoom, and that the zoom happens once the palette is closed. Without the fix the zoom stays unchanged and the second assertion fails.

title: fix(text): vertical CJK written without a vertical font reads down the column (#3712)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #3712.

Vertical text is often written with a *horizontal* font: each character upright, placed on its own, top to bottom, columns right to left — what OCR text layers over scans of vertical books and some converters produce. Every row across the columns is one baseline, so the rows became the lines.

Measured on the reporter's fixture, through `pdfcraft-cli text`:

```
before   遊山春 / 客上天 / 慢開來 / 慢滿得 / 上櫻很 / 山花早 / 。。，
after    春天來得很早， / 山上開滿櫻花。 / 遊客慢慢上山。
```

### What the fix is

A run of upright CJK glyphs that touch down one centre is marked as what it is: text whose **writing direction is down** although each outline is upright. It then goes into the quarter turn that reads down and right to left — where a vertical font's text already goes (`to_upright(.., 1, ..)`) — so nothing new decides the reading order, and `Identity-V` pages are untouched.

Marking the direction is also what makes **Copy** keep the columns apart. `column_text` reads the direction to tell a column of text from a row of cells, so with the layout change alone it still gave

```
遊客慢慢上山。	山上開滿櫻花。	春天來得很早，
```

— the three columns joined by tabs, left to right. It now gives them as lines, right to left, which is the issue's expected text for step 4.

### Why three glyphs, and why CJK only

Two characters below each other happen in ordinary horizontal text (a one-character line above another), so two is not a column; three in a row, each touching the one above on the same centre, are. The test is also limited to CJK, which is what is written vertically — stacked Latin is more often a narrow table cell than a column of text.

### Tests

`upright_glyphs_stacked_down_a_column_read_as_vertical_text` builds the reporter's page through the real text pipeline (`extract_page`) and pins:

- the columns read right to left at **18, 24, 36 and 48 pt** apart (the issue reports all four);
- a search inside one column stays in it, with a highlight taller than it is wide — that is what a drag follows;
- Copy …

title: fix(xfdf): a field name full of periods no longer overflows the stack on export
author: petarlaf
body:
## What this changes

The XFDF export (`export_xfdf`, which `Session::export_data` calls for XFDF) splits each field's full name on periods and nests one `<field>` element per part. That assumes the parts match the field tree's levels. A `/T` can hold periods of its own: ISO 32000-1 §12.7.3.2 says a partial name shall not contain one, but nothing stops a file from having one, and `pdfcraft_forms::fields` keeps `/T` as it is. A name can then split into far more parts than any tree has levels, and the export goes wrong at three sizes:

- From 65 parts, the export writes a file our own import refuses: `walk_xfdf` stops at `MAX_DEPTH` and the error is "XFDF fields nest more than 64 deep".
- Past about 1,020 parts, the 1,024-level XML check refuses it as well.
- By 100,000 parts (50,000 still exported), `write_node` recurses once per level until the main thread's 8 MiB stack overflows: `fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting`. That is an abort, so the engine's `guard` cannot catch it. The PDF that does this is 1.3 KB after `write_full`, because the repeated name compresses well. Dropping the nested `Node` tree recursed just as deep.

The export now nests at most `MAX_DEPTH` levels, the most the import reads back (`splitn(MAX_DEPTH, '.')`). The parts past the last level stay together in the deepest element's `name`. The import joins that onto the prefix with a period, so the same full name comes back. Names of 64 parts or fewer export exactly as before.

Found by a static read of the XFDF exporters, then reproduced in a debug build.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf -j 2`: 53 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-xfdf -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings
- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-xfdf -- --check`: clean

Two new tests:

- `field_names_with_more_parts_than_the_import_reads_still_round_trip`: names of 1 to 1,000 parts, including 63 to 66 around the limit, export and read back with the same name and value, through both `data_valu…

title: fix(annot): a comment listed many times gets one display appearance
author: petarlaf
body:
## What this changes

`with_missing_appearances_cached` builds the copy the engine displays: on open and after every edit (`display_bytes`), and for the CLI (`display_bytes_for`). It gives every annotation without `/AP /N` an appearance. It made that check against the source document, which never gets the appearance, so an annotation that `/Annots` lists many times went through once per listing. The first listing built the stream. Every repeat took it from the cache and added another stream object to the copy, and the engine writes the copy out with `write_incremental`, so the display bytes grew with the number of listings.

A local probe used one Ink annotation with 2,000 points, listed 20,000 times in one page's `/Annots`:

- before: a 136 KB file (6.3 KB gzipped) gave a 428 MB display copy with 20,004 objects, in 2.2 s and 864 MB peak memory. The cache saves the drawing but not the copies, so every edit paid this again;
- after: 173 KB, 0.02 s, 6.4 MB.

Each annotation reference is now handled once per call, across all pages. The repeats pointed at the same dictionary, so the copy shows the same thing as before, with one stream instead of one per listing.

title: Split multi-column TJ rows into separate editable cells (#3744)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
When a PDF table row is emitted as a single `TJ` operator with large negative positioning numbers between cells (such as `[(Labor) -6713 (Remove Cabinets) -26768 (150.00) -5751 (150.00)] TJ`), `interpret` treated the entire array as one continuous `Shown` run, collapsing all columns into a single `TextLine` and `TextBlock` so editing one cell shifted or collapsed the remaining columns. Segment `TJ` arrays at intra-`BT` column jumps (`>= 3 em`, `>= 0.6 em` for invisible OCR text, or `<= -1 em` backwards) and patch only the edited cell's operand slice on replace, clear, rewrite, and group move so sibling columns keep their exact horizontal positions.

Fixes #3744

## What this changes

- **`crates/edit/src/text.rs` (`tj_segments`, `is_column_jump`, `interpret`, `TextLine`, `Shown`):** Splits `TJ` operand arrays into per-column segments whenever the horizontal gap between non-blank strings meets or exceeds the intra-`BT` line-join threshold (`3 em` of font size, `0.6 em` for rendering mode `3`, or `-1 em` backwards, accounting for horizontal scaling `Tz` and letter tracking). Each segmented `Shown` run and `TextLine` records its `TjSlice` range and equivalent thousandths-of-an-em advance adjustment.
- **`crates/edit/src/text.rs` & `crates/edit/src/text_regions.rs` (`patch_tj_slices`, `drop_and_patch`, `splice_rewrite`, `replace_line`, `clear_block`, `rewrite_block`, `rewrite_styled_block`, `move_text_blocks`, `text_edit_layout`):** Replaces or clears only the targeted `TJ` operand slice(s) with their numeric advance adjustments (and compensating delta before trailing slices in `replace_line`), keeping unselected columns in the same `TJ` operator at their original coordinates.
- **`crates/audit/src/lib.rs` (`audit_lines`):** Joins consecutive `TextLine` segments originating from the same `TJ` operator (`paint_pos()`) back into a single line box during redaction auditing so covers spanning a wide `TJ` gap and part of the following value are still measured against the who…

title: Edit text: a table row written as one TJ array is a row of cells
author: muraa-p
body:
## What this changes

`Fixes #3744`

Edit text read a `TJ` array as one line, so a table row written as one array showed as a single line of text ("Labor Remove Cabinets 150.00 150.00"), and editing one word rewrote the whole row: the other cells were dropped from the page.

A `TJ` array now splits into runs wherever one adjustment moves the pen further than the reach that joins separate runs of one text object (3 em forward, 1 em back). That is the reach `Pen::continues` uses, so each cell is a run of its own, exactly as two separate runs of the same text object would be, and each keeps its own box, position and text matrix. A jump within that reach keeps today's single space, so kerned and justified lines stay one line.

Editing a cell rewrites the array around it: the operands before the cell, the new text, and the operands after it with the text matrix of the cell that follows. The other cells keep their places. A `Tm` sets the line matrix as well, so the rebuild puts the line matrix back and the rows after the edited one stay where they were.

The paragraph editor (`rewrite_block`) and the styled-block edit rewrites the array the same way.

**A line that continues a split array keeps the array's other cells.** A `Tj` after an array's last cell continues the line, and a run before the array joins it, so such a line carries several operators. Each line keeps the parts of the `TJ` arrays it covers (`TextLine.parts`, one entry per array: the range of the array's operands it drew, and the text matrix the following operands continue from). Every rewrite that drops a line's operators rebuilds each array the line covers around the operands the line drew, and the array's remaining operands go back with the matrix of the run that follows them. On an earlier head, a joined line dropped its `TjPart` and editing it deleted the whole array — the text loss found in review. With `parts`, both paths keep every cell, and the two new tests cover both shapes.

**Two views of the s…

title: fix(edit): substitute a visible font when editing glyphless OCR text
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Description

Scanned PDFs produced by Tesseract / PDFium (`Glyphless` / `GlyphlessFont`) or Adobe (`HiddenHorzOCR` / `HiddenVertOCR`) place an invisible OCR text layer (`3 Tr`) over the page image using a placeholder font that carries `/ToUnicode` mappings and `/W` advances for text selection, while its embedded TrueType `FontFile2` only defines a single rectangle glyph (`.notdef` + `GID 1`) mapped across every character via `/CIDToGIDMap`.

When an OCR paragraph is edited in `pdfcraft-edit`, the replacement text is emitted visibly (`0 Tr`). Because `Metrics::encode` previously accepted `/Glyphless` (its `/ToUnicode` and `/W` tables look populated), `rewrite_block`, `rewrite_styled_block`, and `replace_line` reused the `/Glyphless` font resource for the visible replacement text, causing every character to render and print as a solid black rectangle once editing finished. In addition, `embedded_sfnt` exposed the 2-glyph rectangle `FontFile2` to the inline text editor, and `rewrite_styled_block` calibrated run horizontal scaling (`Tz`) against `source.font` even when `source.font` could not encode the run's words.

This change:
1. Detects OCR placeholder fonts in `pdfcraft-fonts::pdf` (`is_glyphless`) by checking `/BaseFont`, descendant `/BaseFont`, and `/FontDescriptor` `/FontName` (after stripping any `ABCDEF+` subset prefix) for `Glyphless*`, `HiddenHorzOCR*`, and `HiddenVertOCR*`, and gating structural detection on `CIDFontType2` fonts whose 1-outline TrueType `FontFile2` has at least 64 non-zero CIDs all mapped to that single GID in `/CIDToGIDMap` (keeping valid whitespace-only subsets and 1-glyph subsets with intentional `cmap`/`CIDToGIDMap` aliases usable).
2. Prevents glyphless fonts from encoding visible replacement text (`Metrics::has_glyph` and `Metrics::encode` return `false`/`None`, and `embedded_sfnt` returns `None`) while preserving `Metrics::decode`, `Metrics::text_of`, `Metrics::codes`, and `Metrics::width` so the original invisible OCR layer still…

title: cli: the argument bugs photocraft#7071 lists are live here too
author: Hamza0101
body:
PhotoCraft's [#7071](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues/7071) lists the argument bugs a hand-written parser produces, each fixed on its own there. **Three of them are live in `pdfcraft-cli`.** Measured on `main`:

```
$ pdfcraft-cli extract f.pdf --pages 1 --out --password
$ ls
--password                 # exit 0, and the PDF is in a file called --password

$ pdfcraft-cli combine a.pdf b.pdf --out --nonsense
$ ls
--nonsense                 # --nonsense is not even an option here, and nothing said so

$ pdfcraft-cli check-one --edit f.pdf
pdfcraft-cli: check-one: missing file

$ pdfcraft-cli info /tmp/café.pdf          # that é as one Latin-1 byte
thread 'main' panicked at library/std/src/env.rs:878:51:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "/tmp/caf\xE9.pdf"
```

### The fixes

**An option whose value is a file or folder refuses a value that is another option** — `--out`, `--out-dir`, `--json`, `--root`, `--control`, `--script` — and names the way out for a file that really does start with `-`: `./--name`, which `--root` already offered and `tests/root_arguments.rs` already pins. This also closes the gap the option walk left for those: `validate_options` skips a value option's operand, so an unknown option sitting in that position was skipped too, which is why `--out --nonsense` wrote a file instead of saying what `--nonsense` was.

**Only those options.** A password or a title can be any string, `--page` included: `an_option_shaped_password_is_not_parsed_as_a_page_flag` pins `text protected.pdf --password --page`, and I would have broken it — the test caught the first version of this patch, which applied the rule to every value. For `--page`, `--dpi` and the rest, a value that is another option is already reported by the command in its own terms ("bad --page: expected a positive page number"), so nothing there changes.

**`positional` asks the option table which tokens are values**, instead of skipping the one after every option. The token after …

title: fix(render): render JBIG2 stencil masks instead of dropping them (#2134)
author: Mawfyy
body:
Two fixes for a page that renders as a solid dark layer: a JBIG2 stencil mask that cannot be decoded is dropped, and the image it masks is then painted over the whole page.

A stencil mask says *where* an image is painted, not how opaque it is. When the mask's data could not be decoded, the mask was dropped and the image was drawn over the whole page — a different picture, and a silent one. Such an image is now left out, the way an image whose own data cannot be decoded is left out, and the failure is reported: a new `RenderWarning::ImageDecodeFailure`, which the CLI prints.

The other half is the vendored decoder. `vendor/hayro-jbig2` capped a text region at 10,000 symbol instances. The index page of a 296-page book places 10,870 of them, so the region was dropped, its stencil mask with it, and the page drew the book's dark layer over its light one. The cap is replaced by PDFium's heuristic, which upstream merged as LaurenzV/hayro#1278 and which this copy predates: a region may place as many instances as its data can hold. The pixels the placements write are capped as well, since every placement copies its symbol into the region and a limit on their number does not bound that.

**Evidence.** The book is a 296-page PDF whose pages carry a light raster layer and a dark one, with a JBIG2 stencil mask cutting the text out of the dark layer. 11 of its 295 pages were affected. Page 6 against `pdftoppm`: differing pixels 63.9% → 3.8%, the rest the font antialiasing that every other page shows too; the other 284 pages match Poppler at 1–6%.

**Relation to #2309.** The first commit is a backport of the same upstream change #2309 brings with the vendored refresh, so that refresh replaces it; it is kept here so the pages render correctly before the refresh lands (#2309 currently conflicts with main). The second commit touches `hayro-interpret` and does not conflict with it.

**Tests.** The vendored crate's own test (`decode::text::tests::a_text_region_with_more_than_ten_thous…

title: M2: scans stay sharp at screen size and smooth when zoomed (area-average shrink, bilinear enlarge)
author: Kronbii
body:
## What this changes

Scanned pages (office scanners, print-to-image drivers, conference proceedings run through Ghostscript) looked thin and broken at normal zoom, and blocky when zoomed in. Both come from how the vendored hayro renderer resamples images that don't set `/Interpolate`, which is most scans.

**At screen size, a scan is now shrunk by area averaging instead of nearest-neighbour.** Since #635 (the fix for #624), a non-interpolated image drawn below its resolution was pre-shrunk with nearest-neighbour. A 300 dpi scan shown at 100% (96 dpi) is shrunk about 3× per axis, so nearest-neighbour kept about one sample in ten and dropped most strokes of its text. The shrunk raster was then sampled again by the nearest sampler at a fractional offset, which dropped more.

![300 dpi scan at 100%: main draws letters at random weights with broken strokes; this PR keeps every stroke](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/compare-100.png)

**When zoomed in, a page-sized scan is now smoothed.** A non-interpolated image drawn above its resolution was sampled nearest-neighbour, so every scan sample became a block and text edges were staircases. Images of page-scan size (512 or more samples on the shorter side) are now drawn bilinearly when enlarged, the same filter already used for images that set `/Interpolate`. Icons, QR codes and pixel art keep their hard pixels.

![The same scan at 400%: staircase edges on main, smooth outlines with this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/compare-400.png)

The page, generator and README for these screenshots are on [`pr-assets`](https://github.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/tree/pr-assets). Everything there is synthetic: text written by PdfCraft, rendered at 300 dpi, thresholded to black and white, and placed back as image-only pages.

### How

Both are patches to `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`, recorded as patches (21) and (22) in `vendor/README.md`:

- **`area_shrink`** is a separable area-a…

title: M4: delete several bookmarks at once (#3853)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3853.

The Bookmarks panel could delete one bookmark at a time. Now several can be picked and deleted in one undoable step:

- **Pick:** Ctrl/⌘-click toggles a bookmark, ⇧-click picks the rows from the last-clicked one to this one (over the rows on screen, so collapsed children and search filters are respected). A plain click still goes to the bookmark's page and becomes the pick. Picking does not move the document. Picked rows share the accent fill the Pages panel uses.
- **Delete:** Delete or Backspace with the pointer over the panel, or **Delete N bookmarks** in the right-click menu. The menu's one-bookmark commands (Rename, Move, Indent, Outdent, Set to current page) are disabled while several are picked. Escape drops the pick; an inline rename keeps Delete and Escape for itself.
- **Parents and children:** a picked parent takes its subtree with it, so picking a parent and its child is the same as picking the parent. Unpicked bookmarks and their destinations are untouched.
- **Headless:** `bookmark_delete` takes `paths` (a list of paths, at most 10,000) as well as `path`.

Engine: `delete_bookmarks` (organize) reads every path against the outline as it is before the call, so order and overlap do not matter, and a path that names no bookmark (or an empty list) fails before anything changes. `Edit::DeleteBookmarks` gives one undo step labelled "Delete bookmarks" ("Delete bookmark" for one).

### A stale pick is dropped, not applied

Picked paths mean something else after any edit, undo or redo. The pick remembers the document's `edit_generation()` and is dropped when it changes. I first compared a hash of titles, pages and child counts; an internal review pointed out that two look-alike bookmarks (same title, same page) can swap places with no visible difference while every path changes meaning, so a Delete would remove a bookmark nobody picked. The test for that is below.

title: M10: scanned pages become selectable and searchable on their own (background, view-only OCR)
author: Kronbii
body:
## What this changes

A scanned PDF has no text layer, so in PdfCraft nothing on it could be selected, found or copied. Nothing said why, either: dragging over a scan simply did nothing. Browsers recognize scans on their own, and users who switch from Chrome expect the same. PdfCraft already has Scan & OCR ▸ Recognize text; this PR makes it reach the reader in two ways.

**1. Scans are recognized in the background, view-only.** When a page's text layer comes back empty, PdfCraft reads the document's pages that contain pictures, starting from the current page. Each page can be selected, found and copied as soon as it is read. Progress and **Cancel** sit at the bottom of the document area.

![Background recognition: "Recognizing text… page 1 of 3" with Cancel at the bottom of the document](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/app-progress.png)

![Recognized text selected across lines on a scan, with the usual selection actions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kronbii/pdfcraft/pr-assets/app-selected.png)

The recognized text belongs to the view and is never written into the document. The file is not marked modified, there is nothing to undo, and nothing is asked on closing. To keep the text in the file, Recognize text still adds it as an undoable edit, unchanged. A Preferences checkbox turns background recognition off ("Recognize the text of scanned pages in the background (the file is not changed)"). It is on by default on desktop and needs the OCR models (release packages ship them; source builds use `cargo xtask models`). The web build has no worker threads and skips it.

**2. Selecting where there is no text explains why.** If background recognition is off, missing its models, or found nothing, a selection drag or double-click on a page with an empty text layer shows a bar explaining that and offering **Recognize text…**. That opens the existing dialog set to that page.

title: M7: keep a word on its line when its spacing differs by less than a thousandth of an em
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Edit text joins the runs of a line only when their text state matches (`compatible_word`, `crates/edit/src/text.rs`). Character spacing (`Tc`) and word spacing (`Tw`) were compared to 1e-6.

Word documents exported through macOS Quartz (`Producer: macOS … Quartz PDFContext`, `Creator: Word`) write each word as its own text object, and some of them get `0.0001 Tc`. On a real proposal the title line `для компании AEROSOL` is four text objects with the same font, size and baseline. Only `EROSOL` has `0.0001 Tc` (with `50 0 0 50 … Tm` inside a `0.24` `cm`, that is 0.0012 pt per glyph). The line opened as two paragraphs, `для компании A` and `EROSOL`. Now character and word spacing are compared to a thousandth of an em (`Tfs / 1000`), the unit glyph widths are given in (ISO 32000-1 §9.7.4.3). A difference below that can't be seen.
- Horizontal scale and rise still have to match exactly.
- Visible spacing still keeps runs apart: `0.5 Tc` on the same word still makes two paragraphs, which the new test checks.
- The intent of #3215 (a run with its own `Tc` mustn't be redrawn in another run's state) holds: within this tolerance, redrawing in the first run's state moves a 100-glyph line by at most 0.1 em.

title: M7: keep an applied paragraph's look until its page is drawn again
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

When a paragraph is applied (⌘↩, clicking elsewhere, or switching to another paragraph), the edit rewrites the page in the same frame. The page raster on screen is only marked stale (`DocView::page_changed`) and stays up until the new one arrives. On the next frame `TextBackground::prepare` sees no editor and drops the textless background, and the editor itself is gone. So:
- for those frames the **old text** showed again;
- the paragraph outlines are already read from the new inventory, so the old text sat under the new outline;
- then the new raster arrived and the text jumped to its new layout (on a tiled page, tile by tile).

Edits to added items already avoid this with `MoveBackground.settling`, and pen strokes with the comment settling.

Now the paragraph editor does the same:
- **`TextBackground::remember`** records how the editor drew its text each frame: the TextEdit's galley, its position in the page's 0..1 coordinates, and the page width on screen.
- **`TextBackground::committed`** is called from `apply_edit` next to `MoveBackground::committed`. When the edit is the open paragraph's `EditTextBlock` and its textless background is ready, the background and that last look stay on screen.
- **`TextBackground::page_received`** ends this once the page is no longer drawn from before the edit. A new `DocView::page_out_of_date` tells: the whole-page raster (a tiled page's backdrop too) or any of its tiles is still stale. Both the page and the tile result paths call it, so whichever arrives last ends it.
- **Other endings.** Any other edit ends it. A zoom or a turn of the view since then stops drawing it, so the raster shows instead of rows at the wrong scale or place. Opening another editor replaces it, as before.

The look shown in between is the editor's own layout, the one the user typed into. If the saved layout differs, the text still moves once when the raster arrives. It no longer goes back to the old text first. Making the two layouts…

title: M7: keep a moved or resized page image in place until its page is drawn again
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

While a picture on the page is dragged by its frame or a corner in Edit text & images, its old place is blanked and the page raster's picture of it is stretched into the new frame (#1677). On release the edit is applied in the same frame and the drag state is cleared.

The page raster stays on screen until its replacement arrives (`page_changed` only marks it stale). So for those frames:
- the picture showed again at its **old** size and place;
- the selection frame and handles were already at the new one;
- then the picture jumped when the raster arrived (on a tiled page, tile by tile).

Resizing shows it most: the old, larger picture flashes around the new frame after every release.

Now the release keeps the move. `ImageSelection` records the old and new frames in the page's 0..1 coordinates. While the page is out of date, the selected image keeps being drawn the way the drag drew it: blanked at the old frame and stretched into the new one from the stale raster. A new `DocView::page_out_of_date` decides when to stop:
- the whole-page raster (a tiled page's backdrop too) is still `STALE_TAG`;
- or any of its tiles is still stale.

When the edit fails, the page never goes stale, so nothing is kept. A second drag before the page is drawn again takes the picture's pixels from where the raster still has it (the first edit's source frame), blanks that, and keeps it as the source on release. The drag preview's drawing moved into `stretched_picture` so both paths share it.

**Later commits on this branch:**
- **No outline where the picture was.** The dragged picture's faint inventory outline no longer trails at its old place during the drag.
- **Fresh pixels once the page raster is fresh** (from review). The old frame stays blanked while any tile is stale. Pixels come from the old frame only while the whole-page raster itself is stale (`DocView::page_raster_out_of_date`); after that they come from the destination.
- **No hover flash after a corner r…

title: M7: picture watermarks can have a fixed width in points (#3771)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3771 (the watermark half; see "Not in this PR").

A picture watermark was sized only as a fraction of the page, so the same watermark came out a different size on pages of different sizes. It can now be given a **fixed width in points**, the same on every page, with the height following the picture's shape.

- **Engine:** `Watermark::width` in points. `0` keeps the page-relative `scale`; otherwise it is 1 to `MAX_MARK_WIDTH` (20000, more than any page) and `scale` is ignored. Text watermarks already had an absolute size (`font_size`).
- **Tool:** `doc_watermark` takes `width`. A value outside 1 to 20000, or not a number, is an error rather than being clamped, because a size the caller asked for should not quietly change.
- **Dialog:** a **Width** checkbox with a points field in Add Watermark ▸ Source ▸ File (starts at 144 pt). The Scale slider is off while it is ticked. The value is remembered while the box is off and left out of the edit. It reuses the existing "Width" string, so there are no catalog changes.

### Hardening that came with it

The picture's size comes from the file the user picks, so it can be anything a file says. With a fixed width the height follows from the shape and could overflow, so `placement()` now works out where a picture lands and **refuses before anything is changed** (including before `replace` removes an existing mark) when:

- the picture's size is not finite (`NaN`, `±inf`), or
- at a fixed width, the picture would be taller than the limit (an overflow would otherwise write `inf` into the content stream).

The same up-front check now runs for **backgrounds**, which share `picture()`. Scale factors are written with `matrix_number` instead of 3 decimals: with 3 decimals a 612 pt source at "1 pt wide" drew 1.2 pt wide, and a 10 000 pt one rounded to `0` and drew nothing. At a fixed width the picture is exactly that wide, and the height limit allows for a rounding error, so a legitimate 20000 pt width is not…

title: Print: Japanese paper sizes (はがき・封筒・JIS B4/B5)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this adds

PdfCraft's Print dialog and the `doc_print` tool listed the US, ISO A, ARCH and ANSI sheets only, so a Japanese sheet had to be entered as a custom size — and there were no JIS B sheets at all. Japanese printing uses **JIS P 0138** B4 257 × 364 mm, B5 182 × 257 mm and B6 128 × 182 mm, which are not the ISO 216 sheets (250 × 353 mm and 176 × 250 mm), and its office and book papers are not in the list either. Reference: #3811 (a print paper size was requested).

- **Papers added** (`crates/print/src/lib.rs`, `PAPERS`; points at 72/25.4 from millimetres):
  - **JIS B4/B5/B6**: `B4 (JIS)` 728.50 × 1031.81 pt, `B5 (JIS)` 515.91 × 728.50 pt, `B6 (JIS)` 362.83 × 515.91 pt
  - **ISO B4/B5**: `B4` 250 × 353 mm and `B5` 176 × 250 mm. These were absent; they are added so a plain `B4`/`B5` means the ISO sheet, as PDFs use it, and the JIS sheets are clearly labelled.
  - **はがき** `Japanese Postcard` 100 × 148 mm, **往復はがき** `Japanese Double Postcard` 148 × 200 mm
  - **封筒 長形3号/長形4号** `Japanese Envelope #3` 120 × 235 mm, `Japanese Envelope #4` 90 × 205 mm (長形4号)
  - **角形2号/角形3号** `Kaku #2` 240 × 332 mm, `Kaku #3` 216 × 277 mm
  - **四六判** `Yonroku-ban` 127 × 188 mm
- **Name resolution** (`find_paper`, used by `doc_print`): a paper is named by its label, the name before its notes (`ARCH D` for `ARCH D (24 x 36 in)`, `4 x 6 in label`, `Letter` for `US Letter`), ignoring case, spaces and punctuation — `B5 (JIS)`, `b5 (jis)` and `b5jis` are the same sheet. title: M4: a new bookmark goes to where the reader is (#3865)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3865.

A bookmark made in the app always went to the top of the page, so two sections on one page could not be bookmarked apart. A new bookmark now records where the reader is:

- **Text selected:** the top-left of the selection, on the selection's page.
- **Nothing selected:** the top of the window, on the page showing there.

It is written as `/XYZ left top null`: the reader's zoom is kept, and when only the top is pinned the horizontal position is too (so a bookmark made while scrolled sideways does not snap the view back). Clicking it goes there, through the existing destination handling. With no layout yet (before the first frame) it goes to the page top, as before.

- **render:** `PageInfo::xyz_for_view`, the inverse of `dest_fraction`. It pins only the coordinates it is given. On a page turned a quarter, the displayed y decides the user `left` and the displayed x the user `top`.
- **organize:** `add_bookmark_at` (`add_bookmark` calls it with no position). A coordinate that is not finite is refused with `OutlineError::BadPosition` before anything changes.
- **engine:** `Edit::AddBookmark` takes `left` and `top` (both `None` is the page top, as before). Existing constructors are updated.

Applying a paragraph in Edit text & images takes the editor away (`view.line_editor.take()`) and queues the `EditTextBlock`. When that edit fails, `apply_edit` shows the error, and the typing goes with the editor.

title: M7: an added picture resized by a corner shows only at its new size
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

When an item added in this session is moved, `MoveBackground` (`content_ui.rs`, #1488) renders the page without it once per gesture. The item's own pixels then follow the pointer over that background, and stay in their new place after the release until the page is rendered again (`settling`).

A corner resize got none of this. `MoveBackground::prepare` keyed it on `Grab::Move` only:
- while the corner was dragged, only the outline and handles followed it (`paint_page`), and the picture stayed at its old size under them;
- after the release, the page raster still had the old size until the new one arrived.

So resizing an added picture always showed two sizes at once.

Now a picture's corner resize uses the same background:
- **During the drag,** its pixels are stretched from the box it had into the dragged box (`dragged`, which already keeps the aspect ratio for pictures).
- **After the release,** they are drawn into the applied box until the page is rendered again.
- **A move** is the same stretch with an unchanged size, so it is drawn as before.
- **Text resized by a corner** rewraps rather than stretches. It keeps the outline only, as before.

title: M5: Wayland tablet pens and pressure-sensitive ink
author: mgaux-dev
body:
## What this changes

On Wayland, winit 0.30 binds no tablet protocol, so compositors turn a graphics-tablet pen into a plain pointer and its pressure is lost. This PR makes the pressure reach the app, then uses it for ink.

### 1. Wayland tablet pens in the vendored winit (patch 14)

`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/seat/tablet/` binds `zwp_tablet_v2` and reports a pen the way winit 0.30 already does on Windows (`WM_POINTER` / `PT_PEN`):

- **Tip down:** `WindowEvent::Touch` whose `force` is the pen pressure (0–1). egui-winit turns it into the primary pointer, so every tool behaves as before.
- **Hovering:** `CursorEntered` / `CursorMoved` / `CursorLeft`.
- **Barrel buttons:** middle (`BTN_STYLUS`) and right (`BTN_STYLUS2`) clicks, as libinput desktops map them.
- **Cursor:** the pen's cursor is set through `wp_cursor_shape_v1`, follows the window's cursor and is hidden with it.
- **Opt-out:** `WINIT_WAYLAND_TABLET=0` leaves tablets to the compositor's pointer emulation.

### 2. Ink width follows pen pressure

A pen that reports pressure now draws thinner where it presses lightly, scaling linearly from 10% of the chosen width at no pressure to 100% at full pressure (`pdfcraft_annot::pressure_width`).

- **While drawing:** the Draw tool records a pressure for each point and paints the stroke at those widths. The stroke shown between release and the page re-render keeps them too. The pressure comes only from the touch that drives egui's pointer, claimed by egui-winit's rule: the first touch to start while none is down, until it lifts. A second contact, such as a hand on a screen that reports force or another pen, can't change a stroke's pressure or lend it to the next stroke.
- **Saved PDF:** `Shape::Ink` gains `pressure`, shaped like `strokes`, or empty for a mouse. The annotation stores it in a PdfCraft-only key, `/PCPressure`, parallel to `/InkList` (one number per point, 0–1, rounded to thousandths). The appearance stream strokes each curve segment a…

title: check: judge a file by a page budget and render every page when asked
author: Axiomatic47
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli check` judges each file by one wall-clock budget (`--timeout`, 20 s by default), so a long volume that renders steadily is reported as a timeout beside a page that truly stalls. In a rendering census of a 12,000-file law library at 36 dpi with a 30 s budget, 35 United States Reports volumes (vols. 158–224, 450–950 pages each) read as timeouts in one shelf, while every one of them renders whole: a 784-page volume takes 93 s. The child, `check-one`, also stops after 500 pages without saying so, so the rest of such a volume is never rendered.

After this change:

- `--page-timeout S` judges the file by its pages: it is killed only when no page completes within S seconds. Given alone it lifts the file bound; given with `--timeout`, both apply. The parent asks the child for one progress line per page (`check-one --progress` prints `{"page":n}` before its result) and reads the child's stdout on a thread while it polls, so the page clock resets as pages complete.
- `--max-pages N` sets how many pages `check-one` renders (500 as before; `0` means every page) and is passed through from `check`.
- Every report row carries `checked`, the number of pages that ran; a timeout row says how many pages completed before it.

Nothing changes without the new flags: no flags still means 20 s per file and the first 500 pages, and the existing JSON keys are unchanged. Two small things to know: the parent always asks the child for its page lines, so a timeout row's `checked` is right whichever budget ended it; and `--timeout` now accepts fractional seconds (`--timeout 2.5`) where it took whole seconds before.

Two things noticed in the same census, left for their own PRs: `check` reports a dangling file symlink as `crash` (the child's read fails and exits 1; 262 such rows in one folder of removed links), and a progress line could carry the page's render time for a per-page census.

title: M3: Find ignores accents by default, with an Accent-sensitive option (#3460)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3460. Also the Find half of #3841 (see "Anything a reviewer should look at first").

Find now **ignores accents by default**: `cafe` finds `café` and `CAFÉ`, `resume` finds `résumé`, and `s` finds `š`, `ș` and `ş`. The find bar has an **Accent-sensitive** checkbox in Find options (off by default) for when the exact spelling matters. It is independent of Case-sensitive and Whole words only. The options button lights up when any option is on.

`text_find` takes `accent_sensitive` (default `false`), so what an agent finds is what the reader sees. A continuation with `start_page` and `skip` keeps whatever the caller passes again.

### What counts as an accent

Only **Latin letters** fold. A precomposed letter whose canonical decomposition is an ASCII letter plus combining diacritical marks (U+0300–036F) matches its base letter, and so does such a mark drawn as a separate glyph after a Latin letter (decomposed text). Everything else stays distinct:

- letters with no decomposition (`ł`, `ø`, `đ`, `ß`), which are letters of their own;
- the kana (`が` is not `か`), whose voicing mark is outside that block;
- Cyrillic (`й` is not `и`) and Greek.

### Changes

- **render:** `fold_accents`, `FindOptions { case_sensitive, whole_words, accent_sensitive }` (derives `Default`: all off) and `PageText::find_options`. **The older `find`, `find_opts` and `find_opts_limited` still match accents as written**, so Search & Redact and every other caller are unchanged.
- **render, new dependency edge:** `unicode-normalization` is now a direct dependency of `pdfcraft-render`. It was already in the build (through the text shaping stack, locked at 0.1.25), so `Cargo.lock` changes by one dependency line and no new crate or version.
- **ui:** `Find.accent_sensitive` and the checkbox.
- **automation:** `text_find` option.
- **i18n:** "Accent-sensitive" in the 18 enforced catalogs, with `ATTRIBUTION.toml` hashes updated (`cargo xtask assets` passes).

title: Selection: vertical CJK placed one glyph per baseline copies in column order (#3712)
author: midasdf
body:
## What this fixes

**#3712:** vertical Chinese (and Japanese) written *without a vertical font* — one upright glyph placed on its own, top to bottom, columns right to left, the way OCR text layers and some converters write vertical text — is selected and copied **row by row across the columns** instead of column by column.

The issue's synthetic `stacked.pdf` has three 12 pt columns 18 pt apart reading 「春天來得很早，」「山上開滿櫻花。」「遊客慢慢上山。」. A drag down the right column copies `春 / 客上天 / 慢開來 / 慢滿得 / 上櫻很 / 山花早 / 。。，` instead of `春天來得很早，`.

**Cause.** Reading-order layout (`crates/render/src/text.rs::arrange`) groups glyphs by baseline: glyphs on one baseline form a segment, and segments on the same baseline that nearly touch are merged. The columns' rows are exactly such baselines, so the rows became lines. Nothing read a stack of single upright glyphs as a vertical line.

## The heuristic

- In reading-order layout, before horizontal segmentation, **consecutive upright CJK glyphs that stack** are grouped into a vertical column. A pair continues a stack when: both glyphs are kana/kanji or their punctuation (`is_cjk`), their boxes overlap horizontally by ≥ 60 % of the narrower box, their heights differ by < 35 %, and the lower box touches or nearly touches the upper one from below (`-0.5 h ≤ drop ≤ 0.6 h`). Two consecutive glyphs are enough, so short vertical labels work.
- A column is **one segment and one line**: it is excluded from the same-baseline merge (so the rows across columns cannot form), and its glyphs stay in content order, top to bottom (the existing x sort ties on x and falls back to content order).
- Block order takes a group of vertical columns **right to left**: the rightmost column of the group first (even if the content stream drew the columns left to right), then its nearest column on the left that shares vertical space. Horizontal text keeps the existing left-then-right column rule.

title: Deps: update rustls-webpki and webpki-root-certs (RUSTSEC-2026-0382/-0383)
author: midasdf
body:
## Background

`cargo-deny`'s **advisories** check has failed on main since **2026-10-21**, when two RustSec advisories were published for the emSign/emudhra certificate incident (private keys for several intermediates are now well known):

- **RUSTSEC-2026-0382** — *Certificate verification may accept distrusted intermediates* — `rustls-webpki 0.103.15` affected, fixed in **≥ 0.103.16**.
- **RUSTSEC-2026-0383** — *Bundled root certificates allow trust in distrusted emSign intermediates* — `webpki-root-certs 1.0.9` affected, fixed in **≥ 1.0.10**.

main's `Cargo.lock` pins exactly those two versions, so **every branch's `dependency licences and advisories` job fails**, including unrelated PRs: runs [39624013324](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/39624013324) (`fix/image-holds-until-redraw`), 39623789598 (`fix/editor-holds-until-redraw`), 39623757124 (`fix/editor-opens-without-fade`), 39623744308 (`fix/join-near-equal-spacing`) and 39623255159 (`fix/field-tooltip-3854`) all fail the same job with the same two advisories, and PRs #3869, #3886 and #3892 show green wasm32/ubuntu/windows jobs with only this deny job red. This PR fixes it once for main.

## Change

`Cargo.lock` only, two entries:

```
rustls-webpki    0.103.15 -> 0.103.16
webpki-root-certs 1.0.9   -> 1.0.10
```

No manifest change, no other package, version or dependency edge moves (`git diff --stat Cargo.lock` → 4 insertions, 4 deletions: the two `version` and two `checksum` lines). A plain `cargo update -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-root-certs` also repointed `windows-sys 0.52` edges on several unrelated crates while re-resolving, so the two entries were changed directly and the resulting lock was validated by the resolver.

- `cargo metadata --locked` accepts the lock (no re-resolution needed).
- `cargo tree --locked -i rustls-webpki` → `rustls-webpki v0.103.16` (via `rustls`/`ureq`; the reqwest/sigstore paths use the same entry).

title: M14: the Preferences OK button stays in reach below the scrolling settings (#3557)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3557.

The Preferences settings scroll when the window is short, but the **OK button was the last thing inside the scrolled content**. In a short window it was off screen until you scrolled to it, and the dialog was cut off partway through the Light/Dark theme cards, which is the layout the report describes ("the confirmation button needs to scroll to the bottom to display", "the height is not right, there is too little displayed content"). I reproduced it headlessly with the `shot` example in a 1000×560 window: the dialog ended mid theme cards with a fade and no OK.

- **OK is a row below the scroll area**, outside it, so it is always in reach however far the settings are scrolled.
- **The scroll area gets the height the window leaves**, at least 60 pt (`PREFERENCES_MIN_SCROLL`). The dialog around the settings takes about 80 pt more, so OK still fits the smallest window (820×520) at the largest interface size (300% leaves 173 pt). The old 200 pt floor did not: OK landed at y=180–208 in a 173 pt window.
- **The scrollbar has a gutter of its own** (a non-floating bar, for this dialog only). The app's floating bar lies over the right edge of full-width rows such as the theme cards.

### A regression this nearly introduced, and the fix

A scroll area starts from the room its modal offers it, and a modal offers more each frame for the first few. With OK inside the scroll that never showed, because the settings demanded far more than the offer. With OK outside, the dialog **opened small and stretched by about 45 pt a frame for ten frames**, and clicks in its first frames landed on controls that were still moving.
