title: fix(platform): a save on a Mac SMB share no longer hides the file
author: bulgariamitko
body:
## What this changes

On macOS, saving a PDF that lives on an SMB share (for example a Windows file server) could make the saved file **hidden**: invisible in Finder and in Windows Explorer, so it looked as if the save had deleted the document.

Cause: `write_atomically` (used by the desktop save and the automation tools) writes a dot-named staging file (`.{name}.pdfcraft-{suffix}.tmp` / `.{name}.{suffix}.pdfcraft-tmp`) and renames it over the target. macOS smbfs gives every new file whose name starts with a dot the server's "hidden" attribute, which shows up as `UF_HIDDEN` on the Mac, and the rename carries that flag over to the target.

Repro on a Mac with an SMB share mounted: create `.x.pdf.pdfcraft-0.tmp` (`ls -lO` shows `hidden`), write it, fsync, `rename()` it over an existing `x.pdf`; `ls -lO x.pdf` now shows `hidden`. We hit it with real 20–30 MB PDFs on a shared office folder.

Fix: before the rename, `staging::write_atomically_with` clears `UF_HIDDEN` on the staging file if it is set (macOS only, best effort: a failure is ignored and the save goes ahead as before). rustix has no `chflags` and the workspace forbids `unsafe`, so this adds `nix` (0.30, `fs` feature only, macOS-only target dependency) for its safe `chflags` wrapper; its dependencies (`libc`, `bitflags`, `cfg-if`, `cfg_aliases`) are already in the lock file.

Windows is unchanged: a leading dot does not set `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN` there.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked -p pdfcraft-platform -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test --locked -p pdfcraft-platform -j 2`: 17 passed
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: OK

title: M9: closing a half of a side-by-side comparison keeps the app running (#3915)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3915.

In a side-by-side comparison, drawing a half can close that half's own tab: a snapshot tab's notice bar **Close** sets `close_requested`, and `document_area` then calls `close_tab`. `compare_area` kept using the view indexes it was given, so:
- closing the **right** (new) half panicked at the scroll sync, `app.views[new]` (`compare_ui.rs:354`, as the issue describes);
- closing the **left** (old) half shifted the indexes, and the right half was then drawn with a stale index, which panicked inside `document_area` (`canvas.rs:2371`).

The frame isn't guarded (#3914), so either case closed the app and lost every unsaved tab.

Now `compare_area` takes the two halves' document ids on entry, and finds each half again by id before drawing it and before the scroll sync. When one is gone, the frame ends there. On the next frame `side_by_side` no longer finds the pair, and the remaining tab draws normally.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test compare`: 6 passed
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`: passes; no assets were touched

**Test.** `compare.rs::closing_either_half_of_a_side_by_side_comparison_keeps_the_app_running` compares two versions side by side, sets `close_requested` on one half's view (what the snapshot bar's Close does), and runs three frames. It checks that the tab closed and the app is still running, for each half in turn.
- Without the fix it fails at `compare_ui.rs:354`, the issue's line.
- Mutation check: going back to the stale index inside the loop alone fails the left-half case (`canvas.rs:2371`), and removing the lookup after the loop alone fails the right-half case. So each of the two lookups is pinned.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

title: M12: support zero-instance XFA subforms
author: nnamdiarimah
body:
## What this changes

Optional XFA subforms currently render at least one instance, and their instance managers cannot add a first row from zero or remove the last row. This implements that lifecycle for named subforms using default data binding.

- Distinguish a blank merge (`initial`) from a data merge constrained by `min`/`max`, including zero and optional singletons.
- Retain default definitions separately from live nodes, so JavaScript and FormCalc managers remain available at zero without exposing phantom fields or running their scripts.
- Preserve template defaults, sibling order, nested initial instances (including empty subforms), undo/redo, and save/reopen. Failed subtree cloning rolls back its allocations.
- Remove absent instances from geometry and page breaks. Intrinsic horizontal sections can still split after row removal shrinks them below a full page; explicit `keep intact` and fixed-height blocks retain their keep-together behavior.

- Measure repeated flowing containers and table rows using each instance’s data, including nested scopes, fixed containers, growing text fields, pagination and repeated headers.
- Cache manager counts and default descendant paths during effect replay, preserving add-then-fill operations and invalidating shifted child managers. Native deadlines and a cumulative native/WASM work budget reject excessive replay without publishing partial document state.
- Charge each rebuilt snapshot once and count actual manager-lookup visits, avoiding premature work-budget exhaustion across small script batches while retaining deadline and rollback guards.
- Document dormant definitions, occurrence semantics, cache invalidation, resource limits and regression intent. Distinguish supported horizontal `keep intact` behavior from broader keep rules still missing.

title: M7: a text editing session for one paragraph
author: komo1iddin
body:
First step of #2512.

## What this changes

Editing a paragraph calls into `pdfcraft-edit` once per keystroke (`text_edit_layout`) and once more to apply (`rewrite_block`). Each call reads the page again from whatever document it is given. Nothing ties the draft to the document state it was made against, so an edit queued from an older state can rewrite another paragraph (#2022, #2516).

This adds `pdfcraft_edit::TextSession`, a plain value with no threads:
- **`TextSession::open(doc, page, block)`** reads the page's lines once. It keeps them with the paragraph as it was, a clone of the document, and its `ReadState` (#2504).
- **`layout(text, style)`** lays a draft out with the same rewrite Apply runs, on a copy of the opened document. Every draft starts from the same page, so no draft sees another's output. It returns today's `TextEditLayout`.

title: M6: values typed into Password fields are written to no file (#3926)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3926.

A value typed into a text field with the **Password** flag was kept in the field's `/V` like any other value. Every file PdfCraft writes therefore held it in plain text: Save, a full rewrite (Save As ▸ optimized), Reduce File Size / Optimize PDF, and the recovery snapshots written by autosave.

**What the specification says** [spec]. ISO 32000-2:2020 §12.7.5.3, Table 231 "Field flags specific to text fields", bit 14 Password (p. 540):
- Normative: "Characters typed from the keyboard shall instead be echoed in some unreadable form, such as asterisks or bullet characters." PdfCraft already does this (`appearance.rs:447`).
- In a **note** to the same row: "To protect password confidentiality, it is imperative that PDF processors never store the value of the text field in the PDF file if this flag is set."

The second sentence is a note, so it's informative rather than a `shall`. But it is explicit and strongly worded, and this PR follows it.

**How.**
- `pdfcraft-forms` gains `has_password_values` and `clear_password_values`. The latter removes `/V` from every text field with the Password flag.
- `pdfcraft-engine` writes each file from `writable(&editor.cos)`: a copy without those values when there are any, otherwise the document itself, so there's no extra cost.
  - `save_bytes`, in both the appending and the rebased-on-last-save branches;
  - `save_full_bytes`;
  - `OptimizeJob::run`, which covers Reduce File Size and Optimize PDF;
  - `autosave_snapshots`. If the copy can't be made, no snapshot is written for that document, rather than writing the plain value.
- The open document keeps the value in memory, so scripts and the session still see it. The masked appearance (`*******`) is written as before.

- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-engine`: forms 92, engine 287 passed. `c…

title: M14: JPEG and TIFF export refuse a raster of the wrong length instead of panicking
author: Piohrun
body:
The follow-up promised on #2425, where FredApps found that a raster of the wrong length slipped through PNG export. JPEG and TIFF export had the same gap, and it turned out to be a panic as well.

## What this changes

`encode_jpeg` and `encode_tiff` composite the raster over white with `as_chunks::<4>()`, which drops a partial trailing pixel, and pass the result to encoders that trust its length. Running each case before this change:

| Raster for its size | JPEG | TIFF |
|---|---|---|
| a partial pixel at the end (1–3 bytes) | written as a valid image | written as a valid image |
| a pixel too many | **panic** | written as a valid image |
| a pixel short | **panic** | **panic** |
| empty | **panic** | error |
| a size whose byte count overflows | **panic** | error |

The JPEG panics come from `image`'s `JpegEncoder::encode`, which checks the buffer length with `assert_eq!`. The TIFF one comes from `tiff`'s `write_data`, which compares the buffer with the pixel count rather than the sample count, then slices it per strip.

The check `encode_png` gained in #2425 is now `check_raster`, and all three encoders call it first: a raster that is not exactly `width × height × 4` bytes (checked arithmetic), or has no pixels, is an error, in every format. Rendered pages are always the right size, so what Export ▸ Image, `pdfcraft-cli render` and `doc_export_images` write is unchanged; `encode_jpeg` and `encode_tiff` are public, so a caller passing a wrong buffer now gets an error instead of a crash.

## How you verified it

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-engine` (all targets)

**Tests (unit, `engine::export::raster_tests`).**

title: Reject rounded page rasters beyond the pixel budget
author: narain1
body:
## What this changes
`render_page` sizes the raster with `render_size`, which rounds each side up, but the pixel cap (`MAX_PIXELS`) was only applied to the unrounded scale. A page such as 8000.5 x 7999.5 pt rounded to 8001 x 8000 (64.008M pixels) and went on to `Pixels::zeroed`, allocating about 256 MB past the documented budget, in both normal and `reject_oversize` modes.

The final integer product is now checked against `MAX_PIXELS` before the allocation, using the existing error channel (`page N raster size WxH exceeds renderer pixel limit`). Exactly 8000 x 8000 is still allowed. Tiled requests for large pages are unaffected.

## How you verified it
- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-render`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib` (318 passed)

**Tests.** To avoid allocating hundreds of MB in a test, `Pixels::zeroed` has a `#[cfg(test)]` allocation probe that refuses and records the request. It is test-only, with no hook or counter in release code. The new tests cover: the rounded over-cap page never reaching the allocator in both modes; the exact cap still reaching it; small pages rendering with exact pixels and large pages still tiling; and invalid page or scale requests never reaching it.

I reverted the guard and confirmed `rounded_pixel_budget_rejects_before_actual_allocation` fails (`Attempts { calls: 1, first: Some((8001, 8000)) }`, expected no calls), then restored it.

title: M7: opening a paragraph leaves the page as it is until it changes
author: komo1iddin
body:
## What this changes

Clicking a paragraph in Edit text & images used to change how it looked at once:
- **Until the textless background was rendered,** the editor covered the paragraph with an opaque box, white or dark for pale text (#913). On a coloured banner or a shaded table row, the background flashed to the cover's colour and back.
- **The editor then drew the text again** in its own fonts and layout, over a textless page. So even an unchanged paragraph shifted or changed face the moment it was opened.

A screen recording on a real proposal (a table and banners) shows both, and a third case:
- **A quick click** (press and release in one frame) straight from one open paragraph into another switches editors inside `page_input`. In that frame:
  - the first paragraph's textless page had already been painted, so its text disappeared;
  - the new editor's frame took the first paragraph's measured draft extent (`draft_rect`) and spanned both paragraphs.

Now an unchanged paragraph is the page's own text:
- **Textless page deferred.** `TextBackground::paint` reserves a place under the page's later shapes for the textless page, instead of painting it. The editor fills that place (`TextBackground::reveal`) only once the paragraph has changed, after this frame's typing. Until then the page raster, with its own text, shows.
- **Text invisible while unchanged.** The editor lays the text out as before for the caret and the selection, but draws it in no colour while it equals what was opened (`unseen`).
- **Cover only when needed.** The opaque cover is drawn only for a changed paragraph whose background isn't ready yet, also in a place decided after the frame's typing.
- **Frame from its own paragraph.** The editor's frame uses `draft_rect` only when it was measured for the open paragraph (`TextBackground::draft_rect_for`).

Opening a paragraph therefore draws only its frame and caret. The first keystroke switches to the textless page and the editor's text, as before.

title: perf(render): read PDFCRAFT_TEXT_DEBUG once instead of per glyph
author: narain1
body:
## What this changes
`TextDevice::draw_glyph` calls `std::env::var_os("PDFCRAFT_TEXT_DEBUG")` twice for every glyph it draws. `getenv` scans the whole process environment under a lock, so text extraction pays that cost on each glyph. The variable is now read once into a `OnceLock`. Behaviour is unchanged when the variable is unset, and when it is set the same debug lines are printed.

One caveat: the value is now fixed at the first glyph of the process, so setting the variable later in the same process has no effect. It is a debug switch read from the shell, so I think that is fine, but say if you would rather keep it dynamic.

## How you verified it
- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-render`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render --lib` (313 passed)

**Measurement.** I found this by sampling all-page text extraction on a 391-page PDF (macOS arm64, release build): `getenv` was the single hottest leaf frame. With only this change, median all-page text extraction (15 runs, same machine, built against the revision I pin, `516caea`) went from 623 ms to 551 ms on that file (-12%), 24.0 to 20.2 ms on a 14-page file and 87.4 to 83.1 ms on a 65-page file. The extracted text and structured output were byte-identical (hashed) before and after on all three files.

**Tests.** There is no new test: this removes repeated work and does not change what is produced, and the flag is read once per process so a unit test cannot toggle it. The existing render tests cover the glyph path.

title: M14: the --control file is owner-only on Windows too, and the CLI checks it (#3922)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3922.

`pdfcraft --control FILE` writes the loopback port and a random token to `FILE`. `pdfcraft-cli ui` then reads it to drive the app: opening paths, saving, exporting, typing, taking screenshots. The doc comment, the README and AGENTS.md §3 promise an "owner-only file". On Unix that holds. On Windows it didn't:
- **App:** the staged file inherited its folder's access list. A new folder at a drive root, `C:\Users\Public` and `C:\ProgramData` let *Authenticated Users* or *Users* read what is created in them, so another signed-in user could read the token and drive the app.
- **CLI:** the owner and mode check was `#[cfg(unix)]`, so on Windows a file planted in a shared folder by another user was trusted. The CLI would then send commands, typed text included, to that user's listener.
- The README's `~/.pdfcraft-control.json` example doesn't work in cmd.exe, which doesn't expand `~`.

### How PdfCraft handles this on each system

| | macOS, Linux, FreeBSD (unchanged) | Windows (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Creating the file | Fresh staged file with a random name, `create_new`, **mode 0600**, renamed over `FILE` | Same staging. Before the token is written, the file gets an **access list of its own with only the current user and SYSTEM** (inheritance removed), and its **owner is set to that user**. If either step fails, nothing is written. |
| CLI before reading | Refuses a symlink or non-regular file. On the opened file, checks the **owner uid** and that the group/other mode bits are clear | Same symlink and regular-file checks. Then, **through the one handle the contents are read from**, reads the **owner and access list** (SDDL) and compares accounts **by SID**. Refuses a file owned by another account, or one that any account other than the user or SYSTEM may use. |
| Time of check vs. time of use | The check is on the opened file (`fstat`), and dev/inode must match the path | The handle is opened shared for reading only, so the file can't…

title: perf(render): look CFF glyph names up in a map (vendored hayro-interpret patch 44)
author: narain1
body:
## What this changes
`CffFontBlob::glyph_index_by_name` (vendored `hayro-interpret`) searched the whole CFF charset, with a string lookup per glyph, every time it was called. It is called for each character code of a font that maps by glyph name (`StandardKind::map_code`), and it already carried a `TODO: This is probably slow to do repeatedly?`. It now builds a name to glyph map the first time it is needed and shares it between clones of the blob.

The first glyph with a given name still wins, as it did when the charset was searched in order, so results are unchanged. This is vendored patch (44) for `hayro-interpret`, registered in `vendor/README.md` with its test.

It also checks that the map is not built until first use and that clones share one map. The new first-use and shared-map assertions pin the caching. The duplicate `Alpha` pins the ordering: with `names.insert(..)` in place of `names.entry(..).or_insert(..)` (last match wins) the test fails, because the duplicate resolves to glyph 2 instead of 1. title: fix(render): refuse Identity codes with no route to a glyph (#3529)
author: amoisttowe1
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3529.

A Type 0 font that loads, `/Encoding /Identity-H`, whose descendant CIDFont names no Adobe
character collection (`/Ordering (Identity)`, or `CIDSystemInfo` absent), and for which the file
carries no readable program: its two-byte codes number glyphs of the font named by `/BaseFont`,
and that font is not in the file. Substitution can give us a face to draw with — measured here,
the Helvetica-shaped standard stand-in — but not that font's glyph *numbering*, so such a code has
no route to any glyph. `map_code` previously fell through and used the number as a glyph index of
the stand-in, which is the mechanism behind the strings the report quotes (`AX:adeW`, `;HžMarkings`). Those
codes now draw `.notdef`, exactly as an unmapped CID in a font that is present.

The rule, not the appearance: whether anything is visible depends on what the stand-in's `.notdef`
looks like. All fourteen standard faces this build can substitute (`Helvetica` through `ZapfDingbats`,
measured) have an empty `.notdef` — a page of `<0000>` inks 0 pixels for every one of them — so the
runs come out blank, which is the "render nothing" outcome #3529 asks for. A substitute with a visible
`.notdef` would show boxes instead and still be correct by the rule.

Measured at base `606c560d` on macOS 26.6 (Apple silicon), built without craft-fonts,
every row in both states — guard present and guard removed; dark = an RGBA pixel with R, G
and B all below 128 on a 400×120 page at scale 1 (wide enough that nothing clips):

title: fix(engine): guard undo and redo refresh and roll back on failure (#3925)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
`Session::undo` and `Session::redo` swapped `editor.cos`, `editor.keys`, and the `undo`/`redo` stacks and then ran `Self::refresh_scoped(doc, scope)` outside `guard(...)`, without rolling back the swapped state on a panic or error. Wrap `Self::refresh_scoped` in `guard(...)` inside both `undo` and `redo`, and on any failure or panic swap `editor.cos`, `editor.keys`, and the `undo`/`redo` stacks back and re-run `Self::refresh(doc)` (falling back to `Self::show_released(doc)`) before returning the error.

### Problem
In `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, `Session::apply` wraps its refresh in `guard(...)` and rolls back `editor.cos`, `editor.keys`, and `editor.undo` if the refresh returns `Err` or panics. By contrast, `Session::undo` and `Session::redo` cleared `doc.edit_notices`, swapped `editor.cos` and `editor.keys`, pushed the previous entry onto `editor.redo` / `editor.undo`, and called `Self::refresh_scoped(doc, scope)` directly without `guard(...)`. If `refresh_scoped` panicked (for example after `release_working` replaced `doc.renderer` with an empty inline buffer) or returned `Err`, the editor state stayed swapped while `doc.info` and the renderer remained on the previous state or empty.

### Solution
- Wrap `Self::refresh_scoped(doc, scope)` in `guard(...)` in both `Session::undo` and `Session::redo`, converting any caught panic into `Err(EditError::Reopen(m))`.
- When `refreshed` is `Err(e)`, pop the pushed entry back from `ed.redo` (in `undo`) or `ed.undo` (in `redo`), restore `ed.cos` and `ed.keys`, push the entry back onto its original stack, call `Self::adopt_keys(doc)`, and run `guard(|| Self::refresh(doc))` with fallback to `Self::show_released(doc)` so `doc.info`, `doc.bytes`, `doc.display`, and `doc.renderer` stay consistent with `editor.cos`.
- Clear `doc.edit_notices`, update `doc.dirty`, and increment `doc.generation` only after the refresh succeeds.
- Add `tests::undo_and_redo_roll_back_on_a_refresh_panic_or_error` covering single-panic rollback, double…

title: M10: a symbolic TrueType font without an encoding reads its glyph names (#3962)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3962.

**The cause.** The file's body text is set in a symbolic TrueType subset with no `/Encoding` and no `/ToUnicode`. The codes are glyph positions in the Macintosh order, 29 below ASCII (`S` is 0x36), and the font's own `cmap` maps each code to the right glyph. So the page draws correctly, but both of our readers took the code itself as a character:
- **Extraction and Word export** (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/true_type.rs`, `EmbeddedKind::code_to_unicode_name`) read a code with no encoding as WinAnsi, so 0x36 became `6`.
- **The editor** (`crates/fonts/src/pdf.rs`, `unicode_map`) read it as StandardEncoding, the same `6`. Typing encoded back through that map, so it would have set the wrong glyphs too.

**What the specification says.** ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2 gives two ways to map a simple font's codes to Unicode: a ToUnicode CMap, or the glyph name the encoding selects, looked up in the Adobe Glyph List. When neither applies, "there is no way to determine what the character code represents", and the processor may choose. That is the case here.

**What this does.** Both readers now take the `post` table name of the glyph the code actually selects, through the same `cmap` lookup the renderer uses (the code, then 0xF000/0xF100/0xF200), when that name has a Unicode value. MuPDF reads this file's text the same way: on a synthetic copy of the structure below, it extracts `Solid state equipment has operational characteristics.` while pdftotext gives the shifted text.

The new reading applies only when all of these hold:
- the font is not flagged Nonsymbolic;
- it names no base encoding (a `/Differences` entry still wins for its code);
- its program is an embedded TrueType (`FontFile2`);

title: M3: resize and move the window again right after a resize or move (Wayland)
author: bmh129
body:
## What this changes

With PdfCraft's own title bar on GNOME/Wayland (#1530), a second resize by a window edge, or a second move by the empty tab strip, now works straight after the first. Before, nothing happened until you clicked inside the window.

**Cause.** `ViewportCommand::BeginResize` and `StartDrag` hand the pointer to the compositor. On Wayland the compositor keeps the button's release, and winit reports only that the pointer left (`Event::PointerGone`), which egui deliberately doesn't count as a release. egui therefore still thought the primary button was held, and the next press on an edge or the tab strip didn't start a drag (`drag_started()` never fired). A click inside the window delivered a real press and release and reset it.

**Fix.**
- `window_controls::desktop_grab` sends the command and notes the hand-over. Edge resizing (`resize_edges`) and moving by the tab strip (`chrome.rs`) now go through it.
- `window_controls::release_after_desktop_grab`, called first in `raw_input_hook`, adds the primary button's release to the next input: once, and only if that input doesn't already bring one.
- It doesn't check the backend. Where the real release does arrive (X11, macOS), egui sees a second "released" for a button that is already up, which does nothing.

Ported from the same fix in WordCraft (`1581c288`, `window_controls.rs` is shared code between the two apps). None of the vendored winit patches is involved; the change is on the egui side.

title: M3: hand the launcher's activation token back from the first window (Linux)
author: bmh129
body:
## What this changes

Opened from the menu or dock on Linux, PdfCraft now hands the launcher's activation token back from its first window. GNOME's busy cursor clears as soon as the window appears, instead of staying for about 15 seconds, and on Wayland the window opens with keyboard focus.

**Cause.** A launcher with `StartupNotify=true` (the packaged `ai.storyteller.pdfcraft.desktop`, the RPM's and the Flatpak's) puts an activation token in the environment: `XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN` on Wayland, `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID` on X11. It shows a busy cursor until a window hands the token back. winit only hands a token back if the window was created with one (`WindowAttributesExtStartupNotify::with_activation_token`), and eframe 0.36.2 never gives it one and offers no way to pass it in. So the token was never used: Mutter kept the busy cursor until its timeout, and the window didn't get focus.

**Fix.** This is vendored winit patch 14, in the new `vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/startup_token.rs`, called from `Window::new` in `platform_impl/linux/mod.rs`:
- The first window the process creates without a token takes the one in the environment. The variable it reads depends on the backend.
- Later windows never take it, since the token is spent once handed back. A token given explicitly still wins, and also counts as the first window.
- An empty token, or one over 1,024 bytes, is ignored. On X11 the token is written to a window property and sent to the window manager. A huge `DESKTOP_STARTUP_ID` could fail that request, and with it window creation, so PdfCraft wouldn't start.
- The variable is **left in the environment**, unlike winit's `reset_activation_token_env`. Changing the environment while other threads may read it is unsound on Linux, and PdfCraft starts threads before its first window. The cost is that processes PdfCraft starts inherit a spent token. That should be harmless: a compositor rejects a spent token, and a second X11 "remove" for the same ID does nothing.

title: M6: a document script that throws no longer stops the form's other scripts (#3940)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Part of #3940 (item 2, custom `/C` calculations left blank; items 1 and 3 are separate, see below).

`pdfcraft_js::run` evaluated the document-level scripts in one `?` chain before the field script (`crates/js/src/lib.rs`, `run_here`). If any document-level script threw at top level, the `?` returned before the field script ran, so **every** Calculate, Format, Validate and Keystroke script in the form failed, and `js_run` failed before reaching the user's script. The form in #3940 does exactly that: its document script defines the helpers the `/C` actions call, then copies a button icon with `buttonSetIcon(buttonGetIcon())`, which PdfCraft doesn't have, so all 132 calculated fields stayed blank.

Each document-level script is now evaluated on its own. One that throws stops where it failed (what it defined before the error stays defined), the others and the field script still run, and the error is collected in a new `Outcome::doc_errors` (`document script N: <error>`) instead of failing the field script:

- the engine reports those errors with the other script errors, **once** per run rather than once per field script (the document scripts run again before every field script, so a form with 132 calculations would otherwise repeat the same line 132 times);
- `js_run` returns them as `document_errors`, so an MCP client sees which document script failed and why, as the reporter asked.

Reproduced first with a synthetic form (text field `a`, calculated `c` whose `/C` calls a document-level helper, a document script that defines the helper and then calls `buttonSetIcon`): on `main` 88dad98d, `form_fill a=21` leaves `c` empty and `js_run` fails with `TypeError: not a callable function`; the same form without the `buttonSetIcon` line gives `c = 42`.

Not in this PR:
- `app.popUpMenuEx` (item 3): #2081 implements it.
- `Field.buttonGetIcon` / `buttonSetIcon` (item 1): still missing; with this PR their absence costs only the icon copy, not the whole form…

title: M6: calculations read their notation only from a comment, and a regex after a condition as a regex
author: Piohrun
body:
The follow-up promised on #3550, for the two findings CodeRabbit raised outside its diff there, plus a third from its review here. Each was reproduced before fixing.

## What this changes

`af.rs` reads Calculate scripts for two things: what the Calculate tab shows and the form calculates (`parse_calculate`), and where a script names fields, which a rename rewrites and the calculation order reads (`calculation_sites`, `calculation_reads`). Both readers took the wrong text in three cases.

1. **Notation markers outside a comment.** Both found `BVCALC` and `EVCALC` anywhere in the script. In `var s = "BVCALC a EVCALC"; event.value = …;`, the string read as the notation `a`: a rename of `a` rewrote the string, and the field calculated as `a` instead of running the script, which never ran. The lexer now keeps the text of each comment, and the notation is read only from the first comment that holds `BVCALC` and an `EVCALC` after it, as Acrobat writes it (`/** BVCALC a + b EVCALC **/`). A line comment counts, and a block comment that never ends still runs to the end of the script. Both readers use the same `notation_range`, so the Calculate tab and a rename still agree on what a script reads.
2. **A regular expression after a condition.** A `/` after any `)` was read as division. After the condition of `if`, `while`, `for` or `with`, it starts a regular expression. So in `if (flag) /getField("a")/.test(x)`, a rename of `a` rewrote the regex. Worse, in `if (flag) /"/.test(x)` the quote started a string that hid the script's real `getField` calls, and a rename left them stale. The lexer now notes which `(` opened such a condition, and a `/` after its `)` starts a regular expression. That includes the `while` that ends a `do` loop: the loop ends at its `)`, so a `/` after it starts the next statement. A method with one of those names (`o.if(x)`) doesn't count. After any other `)`, a `/` still divides.

title: fix(automation): guard MCP dispatch and bound line and file reads (#3924)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3924.

- **Guard all MCP methods in `McpServer::handle`:** `guarded_dispatch` now wraps `self.dispatch(method, &params)` for every JSON-RPC request method rather than only `tools/call`. Tool calls continue to report caught panics in the tool result (`isError: true`) via `guarded_tool`, while resource and protocol methods (`resources/read`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `initialize`, `tools/list`, `ping`, etc.) report a JSON-RPC internal error (`-32603`) so an unexpected panic in `doc_info` or `doc_inspect` cannot terminate the server or discard unsaved session edits.
- **Bound MCP request line reads and survive non-UTF-8 lines in `McpServer::serve`:** Replaces uncapped `BufRead::lines()` with `read_line_limited` capped at `MAX_LINE_BYTES` (16 MiB) and `drain_line` (which discards the remainder of an overlong line via `fill_buf`/`consume` without buffering it in memory). Overlong lines receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` (`-32600`) reply, undecodable non-UTF-8 lines receive a `PARSE_ERROR` (`-32700`) reply, oversized line buffers are shrunk back to 64 KiB, and the server continues serving subsequent requests.
- **Cap tool file reads at 512 MiB (`MAX_INPUT`):** Adds `read_input` / `read_input_bytes` in `crates/automation/src/lib.rs` (matching `doc_batch`'s 512 MiB cap via metadata pre-check and `take(MAX_INPUT + 1).read_to_end(...)`) and replaces uncapped `std::fs::read` calls across `lib.rs`, `a11y.rs`, `comments.rs`, `content.rs`, `forms.rs`, and `signing.rs`. Updates `file_access::tests::tools_do_not_touch_the_file_system_without_resolving_the_path` so every `read_input` caller is still verified to resolve its path first.

title: Clippy keeps rsa verification-only (RUSTSEC-2023-0071)
author: oracola91
body:
## What this changes

`deny.toml` ignores RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (Marvin: a timing side channel in RSA private-key operations, with no fixed `rsa` release). The ignore is safe only because `pdfcraft-sign` uses `rsa` to verify signatures and nothing else; private-key operations use aws-lc-rs (ADR-0009). Nothing checked that.

`clippy.toml` now disallows:

- the `rsa` types that hold a private key: `RsaPrivateKey`, the PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS signing keys, and the two decrypting keys. The wrapper types are listed because their `random()` constructors make a private key without naming `RsaPrivateKey`.
- the ways to make or use a private key without naming those types, for a key returned by another crate or used through a generic: the `RsaPrivateKey` constructors and its `decrypt`, `decrypt_blinded`, `sign` and `sign_with_rng`, the private-key methods of `rsa`'s own traits (`Decryptor::decrypt`, `RandomizedDecryptor::decrypt_with_rng`, `PaddingScheme::decrypt`, `SignatureScheme::sign`), and `rsa::hazmat::rsa_decrypt` and `rsa_decrypt_and_check`. The generic `signature` and `pkcs8` traits stay allowed, because the ECDSA keys use them too.

No code uses any of them today, and only `pdfcraft-sign` depends on `rsa`. #2772 signs RSA in the web build through Web Crypto for the same reason. If #629 ever moves signing to RustCrypto `rsa`, the ignore in `deny.toml` would have to go too, and this rule with it.

Split out of #2268, so each PR does one thing.

- `cargo clippy --locked -p pdfcraft-sign --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `main` (9a0ec645): clean. `pdfcraft-annot`, which has no `rsa` dependency, is also clean, so the paths don't warn in crates that can't resolve them.

title: fix: Issue #4017. Flattening removes empty fields it cannot draw
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #4017
 
**Bug.** `doc_flatten` with `fields: true` left text fields that had no value and no appearance stream in `/AcroForm /Fields` and on the page. The flattened file could therefore still be filled in.
 
**Why.** Flatten keeps every widget without an appearance so its value is not lost with nothing drawn in its place (#1794). A field with no value has nothing to lose but it was kept too.
 
**Fix.** A widget without an appearance now stays only when its field has a value. That is its `/V` or the nearest one inherited through `/Parent` (bounded walk with a seen-set). A missing value or an empty string or an empty array counts as no value. Comments and valued widgets behave as before.

End to end with `pdfcraft-cli run` on a synthetic file like the issue's (a filled field and an empty one with an appearance and two empty ones without): `doc_flatten` → full save → reopen → `form_fields` gives 0 fields (on `main`: `empty_no_ap_1`, `empty_no_ap_2`). title: M10: odd and even pages are page numbers, as Acrobat counts them (#3984)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3984: with the range `4–11` and **Even pages only**, printing started at page 5.

`print::range::narrow` kept the odd or even *places* in the chosen pages (the first one chosen counted as "odd"), and its doc comment said Acrobat does the same. Acrobat counts **page numbers**. Odd and even now keep the pages whose number is odd or even, for a typed range, picked thumbnails and the current page alike, in the order given; Reverse turns that round.

| Range, Even pages only | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `4–11` | 5, 7, 9, 11 | 4, 6, 8, 10 |
| `3–11` | 4, 6, 8, 10 | 4, 6, 8, 10 |
| `2, 7–10` (Acrobat's example) | 7, 9 | 2, 8, 10 |

### Basis

Adobe's published manuals, by title, the "Last updated" date printed on their pages, and printed page:

- *Adobe Acrobat DC Help* (last updated 11/28/2019), Printing ▸ Options in the Print dialog box ▸ Pages to Print, p. 515: "Odd Or Even Pages Choose which pages to print: All Pages In Range, Odd Pages Only, or Even Pages Only. For example, if you set the range to 2, 7–10 and choose Even Pages Only, only pages 2, 8, and 10 print."
- *Using Adobe Acrobat 9 Pro* (last updated 9/30/2011), Options in the Print dialog box, p. 413: "Selecting Odd Pages Only or Even Pages Only affects which pages in a range print. For example, in a range that includes 2, 7–10 with Even Pages Only selected, only pages 2, 8, and 10 will print."

The header/footer/watermark page ranges (`marks_ui`) and Extract's odd/even filter in #3729 already count page numbers, so this also makes the three agree.

Not in this PR: the issue says the section "appears to have multiple bugs"; only the odd/even one is described, and that is what this fixes.

title: M7: letters a TrueType subset dropped take another font, whatever its /Widths says
author: komo1iddin
body:
Fixes #4038.

## What this changes

For a simple font, `Metrics::has_glyph` took a nonzero `/Widths` entry as the glyph being there. Some producers write a subset TrueType font with a width for every code from 32 to 126, the dropped glyphs' too. An edit that added such a letter then encoded it in the subset (`Metrics::encode` succeeded, so `source_encodes` reused the font), and the letter drew as a `.notdef` box.

Composite subsets already ask their program (`cids_with_outlines`, #2153). Now simple subsets do too:
- **`codes_with_glyphs`** reads a subset simple font's embedded sfnt program (`FontFile2`, or an OpenType `FontFile3`) once. It marks each code (0–255) whose glyph the program has. The glyph is looked up the way the renderer does, and in a TrueType program it must have an outline, unless the code shows white space. A subsetter either drops a glyph or leaves it empty.
- **`simple_glyph`** is that lookup: the encoding's character in the Unicode cmap, else the code in a symbolic cmap. It is moved out of `embedded_widths`, which now shares it.
- **`has_glyph`** also needs the code's bit when the font has that set. A space (code 32) is kept as before.

Without a readable sfnt program (bare CFF, Type 1, none) nothing changes.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-fonts` and `pdfcraft-edit`, all targets

title: M9: remote (server-side) signing with an OTP — CSC API and Aruba ARSS
author: Emerald313
body:
## What this changes

Adds remote signing: the key stays at a signing service (a QTSP's "firma remota" / cloud
signature), authorised per signature with a one-time password. This is how most Italian and
many EU qualified signatures are used today, and it is what #2596 asks for. Proposed there
first: https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/2596#issuecomment-6314557696

- **Only a digest leaves the machine.** PdfCraft writes the PDF, the ByteRange and the CMS
  locally, as for every other digital ID. The service receives only the SHA-256/384 of the
  CMS signed attributes, through the existing `ExternalKey` trait (`crates/sign/src/remote/`).
  Every signature the service returns is checked against the certificate's key before it is
  embedded, so a wrong or foreign signature is never written.
- **Two protocols:**
  - the **Cloud Signature Consortium API**, v2 (2.0–2.2) with the v1 dialect tolerated:
    `info`, `auth/login` (HTTP Basic), `credentials/list|info`, `getChallenge`/`sendOTP`,
    `credentials/authorize` (with `authorizeCheck` polling), `signatures/signHash`,
    `auth/revoke`. Auth objects and `auth/expression` (AND/OR/XOR) are honoured;
  - **Aruba's ARSS** `signhash` (SOAP, public WSDL), which Aruba's remote signatures use
    instead of CSC.
- **Network stays opt-in and outside the libraries.** `sign`, `engine`, `automation` and
  `ui-egui` contain no network code. The transport is a trait the caller injects, like
  `TimestampAuthority`. The HTTPS implementation lives in `pdfcraft-platform` behind a new
  `https` feature, on the `ureq` + rustls + `rustls-native-certs` stack that Help ▸ Check
  for updates already uses (no new crates in `Cargo.lock`). Only the desktop app and
  `pdfcraft-cli run` wire it; `pdfcraft-cli mcp` only with `--remote-signing`; `batch` never.
  A connection is made only when the user adds a remote account or signs with one. HTTPS
  only (plain HTTP only to loopback), the OS's trusted roots, no redirects, responses
  capped …

title: fix: Small correctness items at issue #3929 which are the OCR size check, release model path & update link check
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Refs #3929 (three of its eight items. The UI items stay open)
 
**1. OCR size math.** `Ocr::recognize` compared the buffer length against `(width * height * 4) as usize` in `u32`. That panics in debug builds and wraps in release for large sizes. Now a small `is_rgba` helper does the check in `u64` with checked multiplication.
 
**2. OCR model path in release.** `Models::search_dirs` ended with `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../assets/models` so every release binary looked in the build machine's source tree. It is now under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`. Release packages ship the models beside the executable and `PDFCRAFT_MODELS` still works.
 
**3. Update URL check.** The check accepted any `html_url` that starts with `RELEASES_PAGE` + `/` so `releases/../../other/repo` (or `%2e%2e`) passed and a browser resolves that to another github.com page. The rest of the path must now be plain segments (no empty or `.` or `..` and only letters and digits and `._-+`). Anything else falls back to the releases list as before.

title: fix: Issue #4018, form_fill warns when a value does not fit its field (#4018)
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #4018
 
**Bug.** With a fixed font size in a text field's `/DA` the `form_fill` tool saved the whole value but the appearance cut it at the edge of the box. The result only said `"filled": n`. A person sees the cut but an agent filling forms through the CLI or MCP did not.
 
**Why.** The appearance builder laid the text out and clipped it but nothing reported it. `form_fill` already warns about characters the font cannot draw and a cut-off value is the same kind of silent loss.
 
**Fix.**
- The text appearance builder (`forms::appearance`) notes when the text it lays out does not fit. That means one line wider than the box or wrapped lines whose descent falls below it. It uses the same layout it draws with so nothing is measured twice. `field_appearance_drawn` keeps its signature and output.
- `forms::appearance::value_overflow` asks that for one widget and `engine::Document::field_overflow` asks it for a field by name.
- `form_fill` adds a `warnings` entry for each filled field that is cut off. For example `form field "single_12pt" (page 1): the value does not fit: 200.76 pt wide at 12 pt, room for 136 pt, so the box shows only part of it (the whole value is saved)`.
- Auto-sized fields (`0 Tf`) shrink to fit and are not reported unless they hit the 4 pt minimum and still do not fit.

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-forms`, `-engine` and `-automation`
- [x] tests pass: `pdfcraft-forms` (140) plus the form/field tests in `pdfcraft-engine` and `pdfcraft-automation`

- `a_value_wider_or_taller_than_its_box_is_reported` (`crates/forms`): fixed 12 pt single-line and multiline fields that are too small for the value. It also covers auto-size and wide and short controls.
- `form_fill_warns_when_a_value_does_not_fit` (`crates/automation`): one warning for the narrow field and none for the wide one or a short value. **Without the fix:** `left: 0, right: 1` with…

title: M10.5: print through the macOS system print dialog
author: fitb-greg
body:
## What this changes

On macOS, the Print dialog offers **System print dialog…** in the printer list, between the printers and Save as PDF. Print composes the print-ready PDF exactly as for a printer: pages, sizing, Multiple/Booklet/Poster/Label, comments and forms. It then hands that PDF to macOS's own print panel. From there the person reaches what PdfCraft's dialog does not offer: the PDF menu (PDF services such as fax workflows, Open in Preview, Save to iCloud; see #2157), presets, and the driver's own panes.

- **Dialog:** with the choice selected, Copies, Two-sided and Properties… are disabled, as for the browser's print dialog, and a hint says the system dialog chooses them. PdfCraft's dialog closes at once. The progress card shows "Waiting for the system print dialog…" until the panel closes, then a notice says *Printed through the system print dialog*, *Cancelled*, or the error.
- **How it opens the panel:** `crates/print/src/system_dialog.rs` writes the PDF to an owner-only (`0600`, `create_new`) temporary file. It runs `/usr/bin/osascript -` with a short AppleScriptObjC script on stdin, which uses PDFKit's `printOperationForPrintInfo:scalingMode:autoRotate:` with `kPDFPrintPageScaleNone` and `showsPrintPanel`. The temporary file is removed whatever happens. The answer (`printed` / `cancelled` / `error: …`) is read defensively: a non-zero exit is never success, and stderr is capped.
- **Automation:** `printers` now reports `system_dialog` (true on macOS), and `doc_print` accepts `printer: "system-dialog"`, returning `system_dialog: printed|cancelled`. The names match the Flatpak portal PR #3066 so the two compose.
- **Other platforms:** nothing changes; the choice is not offered.

Helps with #2157 (macOS PDF Services) without closing it: PDF services are reachable through the system dialog, not listed in PdfCraft's own printer list.

title: fix(comments): thread replies by their /IRT reference, count comments like Acrobat
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

Comment replies were filed under their parent by the parent's `/NM`, matched across the whole document. `/NM` need not be unique, and PyMuPDF names the first comment on every page `fitz-A0`. On a 48-page review written that way by PyMuPDF (28 comments, 16 replies), every reply landed under page 1's comment, and the other pages showed none.

The Comments header comment count also disagreed with Acrobat. It counted comments and replies together, 28 + 16 = 44, where Acrobat counts only the comments and says 28.

The attached PDF is the file that was used for the manual user testing. 
[EU_AI_Education_Guidelines_2026_annotated.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33819539/EU_AI_Education_Guidelines_2026_annotated.pdf)

**Comment Threading**
- A reply now finds its parent through `/IRT`, the reference that points at the parent object, instead of through the parent's name. The parent is stored as its page and its position in `/Annots`.
- Both places that read comments do this: `inspect`, when a file opens, and `pdfcraft_annot::summaries`, after each edit.
- Everything that shows threads uses the result: the Comments panel, comment properties, the canvas context menu, the engine's comment summary and `comment_list`.
- Replies to replies now show in the panel, under the comment the thread starts from. Before, the panel didn't show them at all (#806/#839 fixed this only for `comment_list`).
- Some `/IRT`s point at nothing usable: the annotation itself, a loop, a pop-up, or an object no page lists. Such an annotation now shows as a normal comment. Before, it was hidden everywhere but still counted.

**Header**

title: M9: visible signatures read upright on rotated pages
author: vjeko2404
body:
## What this changes

A visible digital signature (Digitally sign / Certify, the `sign_document` tool) placed on a page with `/Rotate` was drawn in user space, so its graphic and details turned with the page. Scanners often store pages landscape with `/Rotate 270` so they display portrait. On those, the signature (stamp image plus "Digitally signed by …") came out sideways, while the page itself looked correct. Stamps (#1398) and Fill & Sign marks (#2392) were already fixed for this. Digital signatures were not, and I found no existing issue or PR for it.

Now, in `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs`:

- **New signature field on a turned page:** the widget gets `/MK /R` equal to the page rotation (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.19). The rotation is read through `pdfcraft_model::pages`, so an inherited `/Rotate` counts too.
- **Appearance:** laid out in the box as displayed (sides swapped for a quarter turn), with a `/Matrix` from `pdfcraft_model::view_matrix_for`. That maps the box exactly onto `/Rect` (§12.5.5), the same convention `pdfcraft-forms` uses for `/MK /R`.
- **Existing field:** signing it follows that field's own `/MK /R`. A field without one is drawn exactly as before.
- **Pages that aren't turned:** the same appearance as before, with no `/MK` and no `/Matrix`.

One new dependency: `pdfcraft-sign` → `pdfcraft-model` (L4 → L2; `cargo xtask layers` passes).

title: fix(js): bound sandbox memory growth and check runtime-compiled source (#4001)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary

Hardens the JavaScript sandbox in `crates/js` (`lib.rs` and `xfa.rs`) against unbounded memory growth and unchecked runtime-compiled scripts:

- **Runtime-compiled source checks (`eval` / `Function`):** Installs `SandboxHooks` (`boa_engine::context::HostHooks`) on both AcroForm and XFA JavaScript contexts. `ensure_can_compile_strings` checks parameter and body lengths against `MAX_SCRIPT_BYTES` before converting to host strings and applies `refuse()` to each parameter, the function body, and the combined function signature + body.
- **Buffer and intrinsic string/array bounds:** Caps `HostHooks::max_buffer_size` to `16 MiB` (`MAX_BUFFER_BYTES`) and bounds `String.prototype.repeat`, `String.prototype.padStart`, `String.prototype.padEnd`, `Array.prototype.join`, and `Array.prototype.toLocaleString` to `MAX_STRING_UNITS` (`4 MiB` UTF-16 code units) and `MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH` (`1 << 20` elements) so oversized allocations throw `RangeError` before allocating.
- **Host-side copy bounds:** Bounds `text()` conversions to `MAX_STRING_UNITS` before allocating a Rust `String`, caps cumulative UTF-8 bytes in `strings()` to `MAX_HOST_BYTES` (`1 MiB`), and caps AcroForm `Host` (`alerts`, `console`, `requests`) and XFA `XHost` (`console`, `LaunchUrl`, `ResetData`) by item count, line length (`xfa::clip`), and total retained bytes (`MAX_HOST_BYTES`).

Closes #4001

## Verification

- Added unit and child-process regression tests (`runtime_compiled_source_and_host_copies_are_bounded` and `sandbox_memory_and_eval_limits_hold_in_child_process`) in `crates/js/src/tests.rs`.
- Verified `cargo test -p pdfcraft-js` (55 passed), `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-js --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.

title: A number set across a vertical column belongs to it (#3711)
author: Hamza0101
body:
Split out of #3812 at review request, and **stacked on it** — this needs that PR's column detection.

縱中橫 (tate-chu-yoko): a number in vertical CJK is usually set *across* the column — 「2026年10月21日」 — so its digits are horizontal glyphs among vertical ones. Split by writing direction, they became a flow of their own, written out before or after all the vertical text: a drag down the column missed them, and a drag that began on them selected another part of the page.

```
before   第12 頁        the number is a flow of its own, with a gap read as a space
after    第12頁
```

`across_in_columns` finds the horizontal runs that sit inside a column and gives each glyph a box in the column's own frame, so the run joins the column at its own height instead of becoming a flow. A run belongs to a column when it is centred on it, no wider than 2.5 of its width, no taller than 1.4, beside one of the column's own characters, and at most `MAX_ACROSS` (4) glyphs — two to four digits is what 縱中橫 is for, and a longer run beside a column is text of its own.

The slot the run is laid out in is the hole between the characters above and below it, so no gap is left at either end for the layout to read as a word space.

### Tests

`a_number_set_across_a_vertical_column_stays_in_it` builds the fixture through the real pipeline (`extract_page`) and pins:

- `2026年10月21日出版` and `第12頁共有三段` as the two columns, with a heading above them unaffected;
- a search across the join (`年10月`) matching once, with one highlight down the column;
- a drag over the page copying the columns right to left;
- and the negative case: `年\n月\n12` — a number centred in a *large* gap, which is not part of the column — stays three lines.

`cargo xtask ci`: all 8 steps passed.

### From the #3812 review

`placed` is a `HashMap` from glyph index to box, not a list scanned per glyph (`placed.iter().find`, `joined.contains`): a page can hold as many of these runs as it has columns.

fails before your fix** by reverting the fix and watching it go red. A test nobody has seen
fail is not evidence that it pins anything.

## Never-crash

Every PDF, script, MCP call, settings file and keystroke is untrusted input (`AGENTS.md` §4).

title: Build each crate's integration tests as one binary
author: aiongg
body:
Every `tests/*.rs` file builds into its own executable that links the whole crate graph, so a debug test build writes tens of GB. This moves each crate's integration tests into `tests/it/` as modules of one `tests/it/main.rs`.

- Nine crates get one `it` binary: pdfcraft, pdfcraft-cli, automation, cos, crypt, engine, render, sign, ui-egui. Crates with a single test file keep it as it is.
- Test executables: 150 → 52 (37 unit, 15 integration), 2.17 GB in total.
- ui-egui `perf.rs` keeps its own process: its frame-time budgets would be measured beside other tests.
- The GPU tests share one lock now that they run in one process. Five files had their own `static GPU` mutex. `the_drop_line_shows_in_front_of_the_first_tab` rendered without one.
- Path fixes the move needs: `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`/`#[path]` gain one `../`, `mod support` becomes `use crate::support`, and the Linux-only `winit_wayland_scroll` module that compiles vendored winit source lives in `main.rs`. Docs, READMEs and ATTRIBUTION name the new paths (`--test it <filter>`).

Testing: `cargo test --workspace` passes 4,445 tests with 16 ignored, the same per crate as CI on 80b7d2152. clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, `xtask parity` and `xtask assets` pass.

title: fix: Part of #3504, not "Fixes", Text extraction says when the content budget cut a page.
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Part of #3504 and not a full Fix.
 
**Bug.** When a page's content inflates past the renderer's budget (256 MiB or 64× the compressed size) the renderer stops reading it and reports `ContentTruncated`. `pdfcraft-cli render` prints that warning but text extraction threw it away. `pdfcraft-cli text` printed the text before the cut with no warning. The tools `text_extract` and `text_find` and the search-based `redact_mark` treated the partial text as the whole page. A search redaction could report success while the text past the cut was never marked. The editor and the redaction apply step still read that text.
 
**Fix.**
- `PageText` gets `truncated`. The renderer sets it (in `finish`) when the cut happened so the flag survives the automation page-text cache.
- `pdfcraft-cli text` prints the same warning as `render`.
- `text_extract` and `redact_mark` (find and words and pattern) add a warning naming the page. `text_find` counts the page in `warning_count` and is no longer `complete`.
- A page within budget is unchanged.
**Not covered.** This does not make the readers use one cap. The renderer stops at 256 MiB per page while the `cos` readers allow 1 GiB per stream and that is a design call. The app's Find and export and word count (`filtered_text`) and the engine's other text readers do not show the cut yet. The `parity/` note says so.
 
## How you verified it
 
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-render`, `-automation`, `-cli` and `-ui-egui`
- [x] tests pass on `pdfcraft-render`, `pdfcraft-automation` and `pdfcraft-cli`

title: Attachments: a saved attachment keeps the PDF's Mark-of-the-Web on Windows (#3990)
author: mmmaarian03-crypto
body:
Fixes #3990.

## The problem

Save in the attachments panel wrote the file with no `Zone.Identifier` stream. An embedded file from a PDF that arrived by email or from a browser became a trusted local file to SmartScreen, Office's Protected View and the internet-macro block.

## The change

- New `pdfcraft_platform::zone::mark_from(target, source)`: gives `target` the source PDF's own `Zone.Identifier` (copied as it is, up to 64 KiB, when it reads as a zone), or the Internet zone (`ZoneId=3`) when the PDF has none or isn't a file. It is a plain alternate-data-stream write with no `unsafe`, and a no-op off Windows.
- `attachment_action` calls it after the atomic write. Best effort: on a volume without alternate data streams (FAT32, exFAT, some network shares) the save still succeeds, unmarked, as before.
- Parity: `view.attachments-panel` cites the new test.

Not in this PR: macOS `com.apple.quarantine`, and Open on a PDF attachment, which opens it in a tab without writing a file.

## Checked (Windows 11 x64)

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-platform zone`: no zone, a copied zone, and a stream that isn't a zone or is too large.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test pickers attachment`: the new `a_saved_attachment_carries_the_documents_zone` (a PDF opened from a file with a zone, from a local file, and from bytes) fails without the change; the existing attachment tests still pass.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-platform -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask parity`.

title: fix: Issue #4076, pdfcraft --help prints usage instead of opening the app.
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #4076.
 
**Bug.** The desktop app's argument loop took `--help` as a view setting called `help` (and swallowed the next argument as its value) and took `-h` as a file to open. Both started the window so a scripted `pdfcraft --help` never returned.
 
**Fix.**
- `-h` and `--help` print a short usage and exit 0 before any window or log file is created. The usage points scripts to `pdfcraft-cli`.
- `--version` and `--help` write with `writeln!` instead of `println!`. The `println!` call panicked when standard output was full or closed. For example `pdfcraft --version > /dev/full` exited 101 on `main` and now exits 0.
**Not covered.** Release builds on Windows are GUI-subsystem programs. As with `--version` today the text shows when the output is piped or redirected and not in a plain console window. Attaching to the parent console would need `unsafe` Win32 calls.

title: M5: a callout's arrow point, knee and text box change on their own (#1152)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1152. A selected callout now has handles on its three parts, as the issue asks. The behaviour follows what Acrobat does, observed in Acrobat Pro DC (a 2021 Continuous release) with synthetic files (numbers below), and Acrobat DC Help (PDF edition, "Last updated 11/28/2019"), p. 357: "Callout text boxes have three parts: a text box, a knee line, and an end-point line. You can resize each part by dragging a handle. The knee line can be resized in one direction only".

- **Arrow point and knee handles.** Dragging the arrow point moves it alone. Dragging the knee moves it along its knee line only (level knee lines sideways, upright ones up and down). It can be lengthened, and it stops 12 pt from the box.
- **Text box resize handles.** The eight handles sit on the text box (`/Rect` inset by `/RD`), not on `/Rect`, which also holds the leader line. While the side the line meets stays where it is, the line doesn't change.
- **Moving.** Dragged from inside, the box moves alone: the arrow point stays and the knee comes along. Dragged by its leader line, the whole callout moves.
- **Laying the line out again.** When the side the line meets is moved, or the knee is dragged into the box, the line meets the middle of the side facing the arrow point, with a 12 pt knee line.
- **New callouts** get Acrobat's knee line: 12 pt, level, out from the middle of the side facing the arrow point. This applies to the Callout tool and to `comment_add` without `knee`.
- **Preview.** While a part is dragged, the line is drawn to where it will meet the box.
- **Engine and automation.** `set_points` (`Edit::ReshapeAnnotation`, `comment_edit` `points`) takes a callout's arrow point and optional knee. `comment_list` gives a callout's `points` and `text_box`. `comment_edit` `rect` resizes its text box. Each change is one undo step.

title: fix(print): M10 — Windows ya no cambia las letras de las fuentes TrueType incrustadas (#3132)
author: j7121994
body:
## Qué cambia

Al imprimir desde PdfCraft en Windows, el texto de las fuentes TrueType incrustadas como subconjunto salía con las letras cambiadas, aunque en pantalla y en el PDF de impresión todo estaba bien. Este PR lo corrige: antes de entregar el trabajo a la cola de Windows, cada programa TrueType u OpenType incrustado recibe un nombre que ninguna fuente instalada tiene. Fixes #3132.

### El error

Un subconjunto incrustado vuelve a numerar sus glifos. ReportLab, por ejemplo, numera los de Arial por orden de código: en el subconjunto normal el espacio es el glifo 11 y en el negrita el 8, mientras que en la Arial instalada es el 3. El camino de impresión de Windows (Windows.Data.Pdf dibujando en el print control de Direct2D, a través de craft-print) conserva los números de glifo del subconjunto, pero los dibuja con **la fuente instalada que se llama igual**. Cada letra sale entonces como el glifo de la Arial del sistema que tiene ese número:

| Texto (fuente) | Impreso |
|---|---|
| `Revisión de clientes,` (Arial Bold) | `Wj{nxn s%ij%hqnjsyjx1` |
| `insolvencias y fianzas` (Arial Bold) | `nsxtq{jshnfx%~%knfsÄfx` |
| `Conclusión: hay correcciones…` (Arial) | `Kwvkt}{q vBpiÇ(kwzzmkk…` |

Es un desplazamiento fijo por fuente: +8 en la normal y +5 en la negrita, la diferencia entre la posición del espacio en cada subconjunto y en Arial. Donde ese desplazamiento cae fuera del ASCII sale otro glifo de Arial: la `z` de «fianzas» es el glifo 98 del subconjunto negrita, y el 98 de Arial es `Ä`. La tabla sale de simular ese cruce (código → glifo del subconjunto → glifo de la Arial instalada con ese número) sobre un PDF real de ReportLab. Coincide letra por letra con la foto de la hoja impresa, con la `Ä` y la `Ç` en los mismos sitios, y con lo descrito en #3132 para las colas Brother y la impresora Adobe PDF.

title: fix(edit): setting a paragraph's width no longer panics on text larger than a page
author: Matoo125
body:
## What this changes

`rewrite_block` clamps a requested paragraph width between the text's size in user space (`size * k`) and the largest page PDF allows (14 400 pt), in `crates/edit/src/text.rs`. `f64::clamp` panics when its minimum is the larger, so text set above 14 400 pt crashed the app as soon as its paragraph was given a width. The size can come from the file (`/F 20000 Tf`, or `1 Tf` scaled up by `Tm`) or from the request (the automation tools pass `size` through).

The lower bound is now capped at 14 400 pt too: `w.clamp((size * k).min(14_400.0), 14_400.0)`. Such a paragraph gets the widest width allowed, and `f64::min` also turns a NaN size into the cap. Nothing else changes for text below 14 400 pt.

title: fix(cos): one decode budget per page walk, so repeated stream references cannot multiply decoding
author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

`MAX_DECODED` bounds one decode, but most page walks gave every `/Contents` entry and every form XObject occurrence a fresh allowance. A small file whose `/Contents` names one compressed stream thousands of times, or whose forms draw one form thousands of times, made these walks decode and keep gigabytes. Eleven findings across nine crates share this root cause, so this PR adds one shared bound and uses it everywhere.

**The shared bound.** `pdfcraft_cos::DecodeBudget` holds what one operation may still decode: a cumulative decoded-byte allowance, a form-entry counter and a seen-set of stream refs. Every decode in the operation is charged to it (`decode`, `decode_strict`, `decode_within(max)`, `decode_contents`). A decode that runs past the remaining allowance spends all of it, so a bomb referenced many times is inflated once. `DecodeBudget::page()` is 256 MiB decoded (`MAX_PAGE_DECODED`) and 50,000 form entries (`MAX_PAGE_FORMS`). Unit test: `budget::tests::repeated_references_share_one_allowance`.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| 733e38bfa | `DecodeBudget` |
| 92ab0e932 | A spent budget reports its whole allowance in the error |
| ea4939cd0 | `decode_strict`, charged to the budget |
| 735c80c6c | `decode_within(max)`: a per-stream bound inside the shared one |

title: test(sign): serialize the Keychain search-list tests
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

Before: `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign --test it keychain -- --ignored` ran the two Keychain tests in parallel. Each saves the user's keychain search list, changes it and restores what it saved, so one could undo the other's temporary keychain, or put back a keychain the other had already deleted (CodeRabbit's comment on #3716).

After: a shared lock runs them one at a time. With the lock alone, `keychain_identities_carry_their_issuers` still failed about one run in ten when it ran second. The Security framework caches the search list in the process and picks up `security list-keychains` asynchronously, so `keychain::find` did not see the new keychain yet. The test now waits up to five seconds for the identity to appear.

The issuer test also failed on every run after the first for a while: trustd remembers which keychain file it found an issuer in, and each run used a new path (with the process id) and deleted it, so the next run's evaluation looked in the deleted file and got an empty chain. The test keychain now lives at one fixed path, and a copy left by a killed run is deleted first.

The review fixes restore the search list before deleting the keychain and fail the test when restoring it doesn't succeed.

Only test code changes.

title: Fix: a pen on Wayland opens the window through Xwayland (#3650)
author: mgaux-dev
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3650.

winit 0.30 doesn't support the Wayland tablet protocol (`zwp_tablet_v2`), so the compositor decides what a pen does in the window. On KDE Plasma a hovering pen moves the cursor but its tip never clicks; on Hyprland (#3650) it does nothing at all. Xwayland supports the protocol itself and hands X clients the pen as a pointer, so through Xwayland the pen hovers, clicks and draws. PhotoCraft makes the same choice.

At startup (`apps/pdfcraft/src/pen_display.rs`), the event loop is built with winit's X11 backend (`EventLoopBuilderExtX11::with_x11` through eframe's `event_loop_builder`) only when all of these hold:

- winit would use Wayland (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_SOCKET` set);
- `PDFCRAFT_NATIVE_WAYLAND` is unset, empty or `0`;
- a pen is attached: `/proc/bus/input/devices` lists a device with `BTN_TOOL_PEN` **and** absolute X/Y axes (the key alone isn't enough, since a uinput virtual keyboard can claim every key code);
- `DISPLAY` is a local display (`:N` or `:N.S`) whose socket `/tmp/.X11-unix/XN` exists;
- the libraries winit loads for X11 are installed (looked for in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and the usual library directories, then in `ldconfig -p`).

The last two are checked because winit allows one event loop per process: an X11 start that failed couldn't fall back to Wayland, and the app wouldn't open at all. If they can't be confirmed, the window stays on Wayland, as before, and a warning is logged. The choice is made once, so the OpenGL retry opens on the same display server. Other platforms are unchanged.

Still missing: pen pressure (winit's X11 backend doesn't read it, so ink is a fixed width), and a pen plugged in after launch only takes effect at the next launch.

title: M5: review statuses are hidden, chain and show per reviewer, as in Acrobat (#4122)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4122.

Review statuses now follow ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.3: a state belongs to one user, a user's next change replies to their previous state reply, and PdfCraft shows one status per reviewer.

**Writing** (`crates/annot`):
- Status replies (`/StateModel /Review`) are written with the **Hidden** flag (`/F 30`, Table 167 bit 2). A state reply records a state, not a note (§12.5.6.3: "The state is not specified in the annotation itself but in a separate text annotation"), so it is not drawn as a note icon or listed as an ordinary reply.
- A reviewer's next change replies to **their previous state reply**, not to the comment. §12.5.6.3 requires this: "Additional state changes shall be made by adding text annotations in reply to the previous reply for a given user." Checkmarks (`/StateModel /Marked`) chain the same way. Another reviewer, or the other state model, starts its own chain on the comment.

**Reading** (`ReviewStates` in `crates/render`, used everywhere states are shown):
- A state reply belongs to the comment its `/IRT` chain reaches past earlier state replies. Loops and chains longer than 64 belong to nothing.
- `statuses(c)` gives each reviewer's latest status, in the order they first set one. A status set back to None stays listed: None is a state of its own (Table 174).
- `marked_by(c, author)` is that reviewer's own checkmark. `marked(c)` lists who has one on.

**Where it shows**:
- **Comments panel**: one badge per reviewer with their name, for example "Bob: Rejected", and a None badge for a status set back to None.
  - The status filter hides a comment only when every reviewer's status is hidden. A comment with no status counts as None.
  - The checkmark button, the "…" menu and the checkmark filter use the current author's checkmark (Preferences ▸ Commenting author), since Marked is a state of the user who set it (Table 174).
  - Status text stays searchable.
- **The comment's right-click menu** on the page uses the current au…

title: Accessibility: set a table's Summary and a header cell's Scope (#4103, #4104)
author: pat26-dotcom
body:
## What this changes

`accessibility_set_tag_property` takes two more properties:

- `summary` on Table tags: the table's `Summary` attribute (Fixes #4103).
- `scope` on TH tags: `Row`, `Column` or `Both` (Fixes #4104).

Both are Table attributes, so they are written into the tag's attribute object with `/O /Table`
in `/A`, not into the tag dictionary:

- An existing Table attribute object is edited in place in `/A`; other attribute objects (e.g.
  `/O /Layout`) and the revision numbers that follow them in an `/A` array stay as they are.
- Without one, a new `<< /O /Table … >>` is added (as `/A` itself, or appended to the array).
- An attribute object reached by reference is copied into the tag's own `/A` before it is edited,
  so other tags sharing that object keep their value.
- Clearing removes the key; an attribute object left with only `/O` goes, and so does an `/A`
  left empty.
- The tag's type is checked after the role map (a `/MyTable` mapped to `/Table` takes a summary).
  Wrong tag types and other scope values are rejected with an error.

`accessibility_tags` (and `pdfcraft_engine::a11y::tags`) now also lists `summary` and `scope`.
Undo works as for the other properties ("Change tag properties").

A correction to #4104 as I filed it: `table-headers` reports tables *without* header cells, which
is fixed by changing a cell's type to TH (already possible). `Scope` doesn't change that rule;
it tells assistive technology which cells a header applies to, which PDF/UA-1 expects of a TH
in a table that doesn't use `Headers`/`ID` (Matterhorn checkpoint 15-003).

title: fix(sign): judge a page's indirect /Annots array by the annotations it gains
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

When a page's `/Annots` is an object of its own (`/Annots 12 0 R`), adding a signature widget or a comment in a later revision updates that array in place and leaves the page dictionary unchanged. The validator classified the changed array as "other changes", so **countersigning such a document made every earlier signature show as invalid**.

This is common in real files: a multi-signer contract from a Brazilian signing service had 4 of its 9 signatures reported invalid, although each one's digest verifies and every later revision only adds a signature field. PdfCraft hits it on its own output too: sign a PDF whose page has an indirect `/Annots` twice, and the first signature turns invalid.

A changed array that was a signed page's `/Annots` is now judged like an inline `/Annots`, by the annotations it gained (signature, form fill or comments, via the existing `added_annots`), under the same DocMDP rules. It still has to have been that page's array in the signed revision, so a later revision cannot name some other object as `/Annots` to slip a change through.

I searched open and closed issues and PRs and found nothing on this. #3440 reworks the same function; I built its branch and it does not cover this case (the repro still reports the first signature invalid there). The change is small, so whichever lands first, the other rebases easily.

title: fix(sign): let an LTV update declare the ESIC extension in the catalog
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

PAdES LTV writers add the `/DSS` and, in the same revision, declare the ESIC developer extension in the catalog: `/Extensions << /ESIC << /BaseVersion /1.7 /ExtensionLevel 2 >> >>` (ISO 32000-2 §7.12). The validator only allowed a short list of catalog keys to change after signing, so this update counted as "document structure" and **the signature the LTV data protects showed as invalid**. I hit it on a notarial deed from a Brazilian e-notary service; poppler verifies its digest, and the only post-signing revision adds the DSS, XMP and `/Extensions`.

`/Extensions` may now gain declarations after signing. A declaration that was in the signed catalog may not change or disappear (that is still "document structure"). Developer extensions only declare what a file uses and do not change what a page shows.

I searched issues and PRs (DSS, LTV, Extensions, ESIC) and found nothing on this, and #3440 keeps the same catalog key list.

title: Search: keep the match in the middle while a zoom is still on (#3530, builds on #3547)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3530. **Builds on #3547** by @MarekSpodBiedry: its commit is included unchanged (cherry-picked, authorship kept). Once #3547 is merged, this PR is the single commit on top of it.

#3547 centres the match on a find step. Even with it, the match could still end up out of view after zooming, but only now and then. I reproduced two causes:

1. **A zoom pending in the same frame.** If a zoom anchor was pending (Ctrl+wheel, pinch, a zoom button or key), the layout took the anchor branch and put the step's `goto` off to the next frame. There, its page-top offset (60 pt below the window top, scaled by the zoom) undid the centring. At 600 % that puts the match below the window.
2. **The eased Ctrl+wheel zoom.** egui spreads a wheel notch over about a quarter of a second (`motion.rs` explains this). Every frame of that set a new zoom anchor at the pointer, so the rest of the zoom moved the match you had just stepped to away from the middle again. A step taken shortly after a Ctrl+wheel zoom often ended up off screen.

What happens now:

- A step whose match centre is known scrolls to that point alone (both axes in one frame) and drops any pending zoom anchor (`flash_match`).
- A zoom that happens before the step is laid out, or while a wheel zoom is still easing, anchors on the match at the window's centre instead of the pointer. This covers Ctrl+wheel, pinch, buttons and keys through `zoom_at`, and a fit zoom that changes. The view keeps anchoring on the match until the first frame with no zoom gesture after the step, or until any other jump (`go_to_page`).
- If a match centre is not finite (a hostile page's glyphs spanning −∞…∞; NaN survives `clamp`), the step falls back to the page jump instead of using a NaN scroll target or zoom anchor.
