title: M6: scripts see xfa_version, and xfa_installed in XFA forms
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

Form scripts now see two globals that XFA forms check before anything else:

- `xfa_version` (3.5) in every document;
- `xfa_installed` (`true`) only in documents with an XFA form.

On `main` neither exists, so an XFA form's version check decides the viewer is too old.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. One of its document-level scripts begins:

```js
if (typeof(xfa_installed) == "undefined" || typeof(xfa_version) == "undefined" || xfa_version < 2.8)
```

When that test is true, the script alerts that the form "requires a newer version" and then calls `app.findComponent`, which PdfCraft doesn't define. PdfCraft runs document-level scripts before every script. So on `main`, every script in this form, down to `1 + 1` in the `js_run` console, raises that alert and then fails with `TypeError: not a callable function`.

No existing issue or PR (searched for xfa_installed and xfa_version).

### Where the values come from

The values come from black-box measurement in another viewer, with two synthetic files: a plain AcroForm and a one-field XFA form. Each prints `typeof` and the value of both globals.

| | plain form | XFA form |
|---|---|---|
| `xfa_version` | number, 3.5 | number, 3.5 |
| `xfa_installed` | undefined | boolean, `true` |

This branch gives the same four answers. A document counts as an XFA form when its AcroForm has an `/XFA` entry (`pdfcraft_xfa::xfa_shape`), so a form whose XFA was stripped reads as a plain form again.

title: Reject non-hex characters in XFDF colour parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Found while testing `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs:236-243 (parse_hex)`. There is no existing issue.

**Cause:** `parse_hex` checked only that the text was 6 bytes long, then ran `u8::from_str_radix` on each 2-byte slice. `from_str_radix` accepts a leading '+', so a malformed colour such as `#+f+f+f` was read as a valid RGB value.

**Fix:** `parse_hex` now returns `None` unless all 6 bytes are ASCII hex digits, checked before any parsing.

## How you verified it

- Regression test `tests::a_colour_with_non_hex_digits_is_rejected` fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf --lib a_colour_with_non_hex_digits_is_rejected`). It covers '+' and '-' signs, a non-hex letter and a valid colour.

title: Comments: turn by a rotate handle (Tab: quarter turns)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Comments can be turned. A selected rectangle, oval, text box, typewriter text, line, arrow, connected lines, polygon, cloud or drawing gets a rotate handle above its frame: a round button with a turning arrow on a stem, which lights up under the pointer, says how it works in its tooltip and is named *Rotate* for screen readers.

- **Drag** turns the comment about its middle, showing its turned outline and the angle; **Shift** holds it to 15° steps.
- **Tab while dragging** sets quarter turns (Shift+Tab back), and the pointer stops turning it. Taken in `raw_input_hook` before egui moves the keyboard focus with it.
- The page's **right-click menu** turns the selected comment a quarter either way (*Rotate counterclockwise* / *Rotate clockwise*, existing labels).
- One undo step: `Edit::RotateAnnotation { page, index, degrees }` ("Rotate comment").

**How it is stored.** Lines, connected lines, polygons, clouds and drawings turn their points: plain PDF, the same in every viewer. PDF has no angle for rectangles, ovals and FreeText, so those keep their own box in `/PCBox` and the angle in `/PCAngle`; the appearance is drawn upright in that box and turned about its centre by the form's `/Matrix`, and `/Rect` is the turned box's upright hull. Viewers map the turned `/BBox` onto `/Rect` (§12.5.5), which is exactly that hull, so every viewer shows the comment turned and unscaled. A program that redraws the appearance from `/Rect` shows it upright again; I'd rather keep the comment's type than turn a rectangle into a polygon (and ovals have no such way out).

- Moving takes `/PCBox` along. A turned text box fits its own box and grows from its top edge as it reads (that edge stays put on the page); it is typed into through the comment card.
- A turned box is hit inside its turned outline (not in the corners of the hull) and shows that outline when selected. It has no resize handles yet.

title: M12: dynamic XFA forms tab in their template's traversal order
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A dynamic XFA form that PdfCraft lays out now tabs the way its template's `<traversal>` says. On `main` the traversal is ignored, so Tab follows the order the layout happened to write the widgets in, which is document order.

The template's `<traverse>` links are parsed: `next`, plus `first` on a container. The arrow-key operations are ignored. After layout, a new `traverse` module works out the order and writes each page's widgets in it. The laid-out pages have no `/Tabs`, so the forms crate (and other viewers) tab in annotation order, and nothing else needs to change.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while filling it. Its template has 947 `next` links and 22 `first` links, many of them through draws (`#draw[3]`). On `main`, Tab jumps around the page: Name → Rank → Date → DoD ID, then Organization before Leave Address, then the approval blocks out of order. With this branch it goes down the page block by block: Control Number, Name, DoD ID, Rank, Date, Leave Address, Organization, the type-of-absence boxes, blocks 9–10 (supervisor, then approver), then departure, extension and return, remarks, and the leave dates. Each row goes left to right.

No existing issue or PR (searched for xfa traversal, xfa tab order and tab order dynamic form; #3527 is AcroForm `setPageTabOrder`).

### How Tab follows the traversal

I measured this black-box in another viewer, with two synthetic forms. Each field's enter script appends its name to a protected log field, so the log records the order after a run of Tab presses. Both forms are now fixtures (`fixtures::traversal_template` and `fixtures::traversal_targets_template`), and this branch gives the same order for both:

- **Default order:** without links, a positioned container's children go in rows, top to bottom, then left to right (fields written A1 A2 A3 A4 but placed A2 A3 / A4 A1 tab A2 A3 A4 A1). A flowed container's children go in document …

title: M6: read-only form fields are Tab stops; protected XFA fields stay out of the order
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

Tab now stops on read-only form fields. A read-only field takes the focus and shows the focus frame, but nothing changes it: no editor opens, typing does nothing, Space doesn't tick a check box or pick a radio button, the arrows don't move a list box's selection, and a combo box opens no list. Shift+Tab goes back through the same stops. On `main`, Tab passes over every read-only field.

A laid-out XFA form's protected fields are still passed over. PdfCraft lays out both `access="readOnly"` and `access="protected"` fields as read-only AcroForm fields, so they now need telling apart. The layout marks a protected field's widget with a private `/PCXfaNoTab true`, next to the existing `PCSom`, `PCXfaClick` and `PCXfaImage` keys. The forms crate gives a marked widget no place in the tab order (`tab = usize::MAX`), and the widgets after it close up. The mark is on the widget, so a protected button in an exclusion group is passed over on its own. Stripping the XFA takes the mark out with the other private keys.

This follows storytold/pdfcraft#4149, which makes laid-out XFA forms tab in their template's `<traversal>` order. That order was measured black-box in another viewer, on a synthetic probe form (now `fixtures::traversal_template` in #4149). In that viewer, Tab stops on the read-only field D4 but not on the protected field D5, and Shift+Tab is the exact reverse. The public documentation of XFA's `access` attribute says the same: a read-only field stays in the tab order and a protected one leaves it, though the user can change neither. This was the one measured difference left after #4149. It matters on real forms such as DA Form 31 (a public Army leave form), whose leave-type check boxes are read-only.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched issues and PRs for read-only tab, readonly tab, tab skips read-only and protected field tab). #4149 touches the same `form.tab-order` parity entry (see below).

title: M4: a save prompt that opens in the background asks for the user's attention
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

When "Save changes?" opens while PdfCraft is in the background, PdfCraft now asks for the user's attention: on macOS the Dock icon bounces until PdfCraft is active again, on Windows the taskbar button flashes until the window comes to the front, and on X11 the window gets the urgency hint. When the user comes back, or the prompt is answered, the request is withdrawn.

This happens when the user quits from the Dock menu while another app is in front, or logs out (macOS sends the same quit event), or when an agent calls `ui.quit`. On `main`, PdfCraft correctly keeps the window open to ask about the unsaved work, but nothing tells the user. It looks as if PdfCraft simply didn't quit. I ran into this on macOS 27: PdfCraft had unsaved changes when I quit it, another app was in front, and I couldn't tell why PdfCraft hadn't quit.

How it works: `attend_save_prompt` runs last in `logic`. It sends `ViewportCommand::RequestUserAttention(Critical)` on the frame the prompt opens while the window isn't focused. It sends `Reset` once the window has focus again or the prompt has closed. It uses egui's own viewport command, so there is no `unsafe`, no new dependency, and nothing outside `ui-egui`.

**Why a critical request.** Apple's documentation for `NSApplication.requestUserAttention(_:)` says that when an inactive app presents a modal panel, AppKit makes this request itself, with `NSCriticalRequest`. A native app's "save changes?" alert therefore bounces until the user comes back. PdfCraft's prompt is drawn by egui, so AppKit never sees it, and PdfCraft has to ask itself. An informational request bounces the icon once, for one second. That is easy to miss, and the prompt is holding up the quit the user asked for. winit 0.30 maps `Critical` to `NSCriticalRequest` on macOS, `FLASHW_ALL | FLASHW_TIMERNOFG` on Windows, and the urgency hint on X11.

**When it doesn't ask.** A prompt that opens while PdfCraft is in front asks for nothing. Leaving with the promp…

title: M2: a symbolic TrueType font reads its (3, 0) cmap before its (1, 0) one (#4156)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4156.

A symbolic TrueType font now draws through its Windows (3, 0) `cmap` subtable before its Macintosh (1, 0) one, as ISO 32000-2 §9.6.5.4 prescribes:

> When the font has no Encoding entry, or the font descriptor's Symbolic flag is set … If the font contains a (3, 0) subtable, … [the codes] shall be used to select the associated glyph description from the subtable. Otherwise, if the font contains a (1, 0) subtable, single bytes from the string shall be used to look up the associated glyph descriptions from the subtable.

**Cause.** `EmbeddedKind::map_code` in the vendored `hayro-interpret` (the branch taken when the Nonsymbolic flag is not set) tried the cmap records in the order the font lists them, and kept the first match. Records are sorted by platform ID, so (1, 0) came before (3, 0). The #4156 sample was written by SAS 9.4. Its embedded `AlbanyAMT` subsets are symbolic (`/Flags 4`) with no `/Encoding`, and their (1, 0) table is wrong: code 43 maps to `V`, 49 to `glyph17408` and 56 to `p`. The (3, 0) table maps them to plus, one and eight, which agrees with the fonts' `/ToUnicode`. So "8" drew as "p", "+" as "V", and "1" and "%" not at all.

**Fix.** The Windows (3, 0)/(3, 1) records are tried first. The Macintosh and Unicode records still serve codes the (3, x) ones leave out, so a font whose (3, 0) table is incomplete loses nothing it drew before. The patch is marked `PdfCraft patch (#4156)` and listed in `vendor/README.md`.

With this branch, `pdfcraft-cli render` draws the #4156 sample the same as MuPDF, with every "1", "8", "+" and "%" in place.

No other open PR changes this branch of `map_code`. #2980 and #3969 touch TrueType cmaps, but only in the non-symbolic path and in text extraction.

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed

title: fix(linux): say why no file dialog opened, and keep the work that asked (#3988)
author: nicolasfalesy
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3988 (the first of the two parts the triage comment split out: tell the user when no file dialog can open, instead of dropping the work).

On Linux, when the desktop portal runs but the backend that draws its file chooser doesn't (#3988: `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` started without `DISPLAY` and died), every Open, Save and Reduce File Size dialog did nothing, said nothing, and threw away the work that asked for it.

**Why the app couldn't tell.** I reproduced it with the real `xdg-desktop-portal` 1.22 on a private bus whose GTK backend can't start. The portal still lists `org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser` (version 4) and accepts `OpenFile`, then answers the request with `Response` code 2. rfd 0.17 maps any non-zero code to an empty answer (`portal/mod.rs`, `parse_response`) and only falls back to zenity when the portal can't be reached at all, so a dead backend looks exactly like Cancel. A check of the portal alone (like PhotoCraft's `file_dialog_probe`) also says "fine" in this state.

**The fix.**
- `pdfcraft_platform::file_dialog_probe::why_empty()` runs on the picker's worker thread, only after an empty answer. It reads the `.portal` files the portal reads (`XDG_DESKTOP_PORTAL_DIR`, else `portals` under the user and system data folders), takes the backends that implement `org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser`, and asks the bus (`NameHasOwner`) whether any of them is running. A backend that just handled a request is still running, so "none is running" means the panel never showed. It only reads bus state: it never activates a backend, which would start every installed backend after every Cancel. With no portal it falls back to zenity's presence, as rfd does.
- Anything it can't tell counts as working, so a Cancel on a working desktop stays silent. Inside Flatpak and Snap it says nothing: the bus proxy and AppArmor hide or refuse the backend names, so a running backend would look missing. (That leaves the reporter's Snap case open. It …

title: fix(forms): ignore print requests from automatic field scripts
author: enriquemelzer-bit
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4088.

An AcroForm field's Keystroke, Validate, Calculate or Format script could open the print dialog just by calling `this.print()`, including on each recalculation. Filter `Request::Print` when collecting these automatic field-script outcomes and record a JavaScript console diagnostic. Preserve field values, alerts, other requests and script errors. Explicit button and console scripts can still produce Print requests at the engine and automation boundaries, including when they also trigger automatic calculations. UI limitations are documented below.

## How you verified it

Integrated with main `1dd2737b47a9c1c9562f0af563053d1bf510e4bf` on 2026-10-27. Main's automation module layout remains intact; the existing automation regression moved into `crates/automation/src/tests.rs`. The engine change and all three engine regressions are preserved. Main's ShowPanel/SaveAs filters and document-error provenance/deduplication remain intact, with tests exercising their interaction.

The four existing frontend dependencies use `acab34c0d8d84363ea3d05885f1a15601c233a19`, main's `edc41f68` plus the published one-line Cargo 1.95 manifest correction from [craft-libs #366](https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/pull/366). title: chore(sonar): exclude vendored crates and the spec-mandated MD5/RIPEMD-160 (SonarCloud rust:S4790)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## What this changes

Scopes SonarCloud's analysis in `sonar-project.properties`. No code changes.

**193 findings addressed:**

- **186 findings in `vendor/`** (every rule there: rust:S3776 52, rust:S2208 49, rust:S8863 30, rust:S1612 17, rust:S107 10, rust:S4790 9, rust:S8862 7, rust:S3329 4, rust:S4325 2, rust:S9045, rust:S7425, rust:S9168, rust:S7424, python:S3457, python:S1172 1 each). `vendor/` holds third-party crates (hayro*, lopdf, winit, vello_common, egui-wgpu) that we carry with small patches marked `PdfCraft patch:` and intend to drop once upstream releases the fix (`vendor/README.md`).   - `crates/crypt/src/lib.rs` (6): MD5 is the hash that ISO 32000 §7.6.4 mandates for the RC4 / AES-128 standard security handler (Algorithms 1–5). We cannot open or write those files without it.

Config only; the SonarCloud check on this PR shows the scoped result.

Whether you would rather keep `vendor/` in the analysis. If so, drop the `sonar.exclusions` line and those findings come back as upstream's to fix.

title: M4: bookmarks show and set their title colour and style (ISO 32000-2 Tables 151, 152)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Refs #3193 (point 2: "a button for setting the background color … so as to mark certain rarely-used chapters").

**The need.** Readers of long documents mark bookmarks to tell them apart, for example rarely used chapters or sections still to review. PDF already has a place for this:

- ISO 32000-2 §12.3.3 gives every outline item a title colour, `/C`. Table 151 defines it as "An array of three numbers in the range 0.0 to 1.0, representing the components in the DeviceRGB colour space", with black as the default.
- It also gives style flags, `/F`. Table 152 defines bit 1 as italic and bit 2 as bold, and the default is 0.

PdfCraft ignored both, so a file whose author coloured or emboldened its bookmarks showed every title alike, and nobody could set them.

- The Bookmarks panel draws bold titles in the semibold face, italic ones slanted, and each colour as given.
  - A colour is lightened towards the text colour only as far as it needs to reach 3:1 contrast on the panel (`theme::readable`). Dark blue stays readable in the dark theme, and red on white is unchanged.
- `bookmark_list` reports `color`, `bold` and `italic` where they differ from the defaults.

title: fix(ui): Ctrl+Z in an open paragraph undoes the document, not stale text
author: RiceDee
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4176.

`edit.undo` leaves Ctrl+Z to a focused text field, so with a paragraph open in Edit text it went to the paragraph editor's own `TextEdit` undo history. After a formatting change (which applies at once and refreshes the editor's text), that history still held the text from before it, so Ctrl+Z put it back into a box laid out for the page after the change, and the document kept the change. The box shares its id across paragraphs, so it could also put back another paragraph's text.

- **The box's history starts at what the page has** (`forget_typing_before`): on opening, and whenever formatting applies. Undo in the box takes back only typing done since. The same goes for the Add text box, which now has its own fixed id (`content_ui::input_id`).
- **Undo and Redo reach the document** from a focused page box once it holds no typing the page doesn't have (`commands::registry_shortcuts`); while it does, they stay the box's, as before.
- **An open box is applied and closed before an Undo or Redo step** (`close_text_editors`), as clicking away applies it, so it never shows a state the document has left. If its text can't be applied (text the standard fonts can't draw, a refused rewrite), the box stays open and the step doesn't run: nothing typed is lost.

Related to #2512, whose session design makes this one undo step per session; this keeps today's one-step-per-format-change behaviour and only stops Undo going to stale text.

title: M11: PDF Optimizer ▸ Clean Up stores LZW streams with Flate (optimize.flate-unencoded)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
The PDF Optimizer's Clean Up panel in Acrobat has two Flate options under "Object compression options": "Use Flate to encode streams that are not encoded" and "In streams that use LZW Encoding, use Flate instead", described as "Applies Flate compression to all content streams and images that use LZW encoding" ([Optimizing PDFs](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/optimizing-pdfs-acrobat-pro.html)). `optimize.flate-unencoded` had the first one; its note said "LZW not yet re-encoded". This adds the second as its own checkbox in Clean Up and as `lzw_to_flate` on `doc_optimize` (which now reports `lzw_streams`). It is on by default like the neighbouring Flate option: I couldn't find Adobe stating this checkbox's default, only that in Clean Up "By default, only elements that don't affect functionality are selected", which this one doesn't; happy to switch it off by default if you know otherwise.

For each stream with an LZW filter, the filters up to the last LZW one are decoded strictly, with its `EarlyChange` and predictor, and the result is Flate-encoded under the same predictor, so a predicted image stays predicted. `EarlyChange` goes away (it is LZW's alone), filters applied before the LZW one (an ASCII85 layer, say) go with it, and the ones after it keep their bytes: `[/LZWDecode /DCTDecode]` becomes `[/FlateDecode /DCTDecode]` with the same JPEG. The re-encoded stage is decoded once more and compared, so a predictor the encoder can't reproduce leaves the stream alone. Streams whose LZW data doesn't decode cleanly are left as they are, as are streams with `/Crypt`, an external `/F`, `/DecodeParms` that can't be read for certain (an indirect reference, an array of the wrong length), cross-reference and object streams (rewritten on save), and streams that decode past 256 MiB (`MAX_PAGE_DECODED`), since the data and its check are held together. The stream is converted whether or not it gets smaller, since the option is also how LZW is removed for PDF/A and PDF/X; hap…

title: M5: sticky notes draw the icon they name (ISO 32000-2 Table 175)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**The need.** A sticky note's icon is how readers tell notes apart on a page at a glance: a question, a key point, an insertion. PdfCraft broke this in two ways.

- **Its own icon choice did nothing.** The Properties dialog offers seven icons, but it drew only two shapes: Comment, and a page for everything else. Choosing Key, Help, Insert, New paragraph or Paragraph left the note looking the same.
- **Notes in received files lost their icons.** Notes that name other icons drew as the same page. That covers the standard names and further common ones such as Check or Star. Changing such a note's colour also redrew it as a page, so its icon was lost.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.4, Table 175 (`Name`) lists Comment, Key, Note, Help, NewParagraph, Paragraph and Insert, and says the viewer "shall provide predefined icon appearances for at least the following standard names", adding "Additional names may be supported as well".

**The change**
- `annot::appearance::note_icon` draws a shape of its own for each of the seven standard names. It also draws seven further names in common use: Check, Circle, Cross, CrossHairs, Star, RightArrow and UpArrow.
- The new icons are drawn the same way as the existing Comment and Note icons: simple geometric drawings in the appearance stream, filled in the note's colour with a dark outline. No image or icon files are involved.
- `NoteIcon` gains the further names, with `NoteIcon::ALL`. The Properties chooser and `comment_add` offer all fourteen; the chooser shows the PDF names, as before, so no new UI strings.
- A note keeps its icon when its colour changes.
- Any other name still draws as Note, the table's default.

title: M3: a Launch link that names a PDF opens it in PdfCraft (ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.6)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4168.

**The need.** Document sets often link their parts with Launch actions. The file in #4168 has 268 links such as `..\se\se_ST.pdf`, each meant to open a sibling PDF. PdfCraft follows no Launch action, so these links did nothing. Written as GoToR, the same link opens.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.6: a Launch action "launches an application or opens or prints a document". A document must not be able to start programs. Opening a PDF, though, is exactly what a remote Go-To already does, with its own checks.

**The change** (`render::inspect`, `launch_pdf`)
- **What counts.** A Launch action whose `/F` names a `.pdf` file, and that has no `/Win` launch parameters, is read as the remote Go-To to that file's first page. `/Win` (Table 208) names an application, an operation and arguments.
- **How it opens.** The link becomes `LinkTarget::RemoteGoTo { launch: true, … }` and goes through the same path as a GoToR link:
  - PDF files only;
  - `--root` confinement;
  - confirmation for absolute paths;
  - opened as a document in PdfCraft, never handed to the operating system.
- **Path separators.** Windows writers separate such paths with `\`, while §7.11.2.1 separates components with `/`. A Launch path that contains no `/` has its `\` read as `/`.
- **Everything else stays unfollowed:** any other Launch action, one with `/Win`, a URL file system, or a name that isn't `*.pdf`.
- **Reporting.** In `doc_info`, a remote link's target now says `"action": "Launch"` or `"GoToR"`.

title: M7: preserve paragraph frames when resizing upright and rotated text
author: enriquemelzer-bit
body:
## What this changes

Resizing an existing paragraph keeps its chosen width and height independently of glyph bounds, including text at arbitrary angles. A 30-degree paragraph can keep a 90 x 10 pt frame through typing, movement, undo/redo and save/reopen: words wrap along its baseline and remain visible outside the chosen height. Refs #3474.

Images inside reserved blank paragraph-frame space retain ordinary and modifier clicks. Dragging an image cannot move the surrounding selected paragraph. Text ink still takes precedence over background artwork, edge grips remain available, and marquee selection and dragging a selected mixed group retain the complete paragraph frame. Image priority respects placement and clipping; a quick drag is resolved from where it started.

Blank frame-space clicks follow the paragraph's orientation. A point in the outer corner of its axis-aligned bounds, outside both its ink box and oriented frame, can start a marquee and does not toggle the paragraph with Shift-click. Marquee intersection and dragging an existing selection retain their rectangular bounds.

The four UI edge handles follow the paragraph's orientation, including document/view rotation, shifted crop boxes and UserUnit. Dragging projects onto the selected text axis; moving the left edge moves the text along its baseline. Typing uses a readable horizontal editor and Apply preserves the PDF angle. Automation exposes `editing_quad` in displayed page coordinates, alongside the existing ink `rect` and frame AABB `editing_rect`; width/height use the paragraph's local axes, with height anchored at its local top edge.

Height-only edits change nonpainting metadata and preserve original operators, kerning, row breaks, colours and invisible OCR. Rotated reflow with mixed source fonts, colours or text states is refused before mutation rather than flattening formatting. Partial formatting and document-font selection for rotated paragraphs remain unsupported.

title: M9: sign with PKCS #11 smart cards and tokens; opt-in timestamps and LTV
author: MarAvFe
body:
Smart cards and USB tokens sign through the vendor's PKCS #11 module (cryptoki, Apache-2.0; native only). Certificates are listed without a PIN; signing logs in with a zeroized PIN (none on PIN-pad readers) and signs on the token (RSA PKCS #1 v1.5, ECDSA P-256/P-384). When a card holds an authentication and a signing certificate, only the nonRepudiation one is offered.

- Sign dialog: Configure New Digital ID > Use a smart card or token, module prefilled from known middleware locations; card PIN in Sign as. Card IDs list on every desktop platform. Named IDs sort before IDs named by a bare GUID.
- CLI and agent tools: sign_card_ids; sign_document takes a pkcs11: id. The module comes only from --card-module, the PIN only from a terminal prompt in pdfcraft-cli run; network only with --network.
- Long-term validation, opt-in (Preferences > Signatures): a timestamp server URL and an LTV switch. Signing then runs on a thread behind a cancellable modal: RFC 3161 signature timestamp, missing issuers from AIA, OCSP or CRL that verify and cover the signing time, /DSS, and a document timestamp (PAdES B-LTA). pdfcraft-sign stays transport-free (ltv::Fetch); HTTP lives in pdfcraft-platform::http.
- pkcs11_probe example: a stand-alone card check.
- docs/smart-card-signing.md.

title: M5: cloudy squares, circles and text boxes are drawn (ISO 32000-2 Table 169)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

**The need.** Reviewers mark areas of drawings and documents with cloudy rectangles, ellipses and text boxes. When a PDF carries such a comment without a stored appearance, PdfCraft drew none of them, so the marked area was simply invisible. A polygon whose cloudy border has intensity 0 (or no intensity) drew a cloud anyway. And PdfCraft's clouds had bumps about twice as large as reads naturally.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.5.4:
- Squares, circles and polygons (PDF 1.5), and text boxes (PDF 1.6), may have a border effect.
- Table 169 says `/BE /S /C` draws the border "as a series of convex curved line segments in a manner that simulates the appearance of a cloud", and that "the width and dash array specified by BS shall be honoured".
- Its intensity `/I` is "in the range 0 to 2. Default value: 0".
- Table 180's `/RD` gives the differences between "the left, top, right, and bottom coordinates of Rect and those of the square or circle".

**Commit 1: cloudy squares, circles and text boxes are drawn**
- `cloud_intensity` reads `/BE`. A border is cloudy only for `/S /C` with `/I` above 0; intensity 0, the default, draws a plain border.
- A cloudy square or circle draws its bumps around `/Rect` less `/RD`, in the order left, top, right, bottom. Without `/RD`, the bumps are inset by their own height so they stay inside `/Rect`. A circle's outline gets one point per bump.
- A cloudy text box draws its background and border as the cloud, with the text inside. A cloudy callout keeps its own appearance, as before.

**Commit 2: bumps half the size**
- The standard leaves the bump size open. The radius at intensity 1 was 6 + 1.5 × the line width, so a 2 pt border had 18 pt lobes. It is now 3 + 0.75 × the width, about 9 pt across at 2 pt, and intensity 2 still doubles it.
- The change applies both to PdfCraft's own Cloud tool and to clouds it draws for other PDFs. The Cloud tool's `/Rect` margin is derived from the same radius, so it follows.

title: fix(audit): covered_text reports the words under the cover, not the whole line
author: mercuryVM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4164.

**Problem.** A text line joins the runs painted on one baseline, and when a cover hid part of a line the audit reported the line's whole text in `covered_text`, including words painted beside the cover that stay visible. The issue's repro (a cover over `SECRET`, then `tail` at x 200, outside it) reported `["SECRETtail"]`.

**Fix.** As the issue suggests, the text now comes from `pdfcraft-edit`:

- `TextLine` keeps each joined run's text together with the end of its word boxes in `ink` (private field `runs`), exposed read-only as `TextLine::runs()` → `(&str, &[[f64; 4]], bool)` per run, in content order: its text, its word boxes, and whether joining put a space before it. No new public type.
- When the line's text is reordered for reading (right-to-left via `bidi::to_logical`, or visual-order Indic via `indic::to_logical`), the runs no longer read like the line, so they are cleared and `runs()` yields nothing. This covers both reorder sites (`text_lines_in` and the form-aware walker).
- `pdfcraft-audit`: `Budget::hidden_text` takes the cover's rectangle, and a new `covered_words` reports the runs whose word boxes the cover overlaps (positive-area intersection), joined as the line joins them (a word shown in two adjacent runs stays one word; a space where the line has one, or where uncovered runs were left out between them). It falls back to the whole line when the runs can't say: a line of one run, a reordered line, or a cover that matched on the line's box but overlaps none of its words. Same for filled-rectangle covers and annotation covers (`/Redact`, opaque `/Square`).

Which lines count as covered is unchanged (`is_cover` / `covers` are untouched); only the reported text gets narrower. The copy-permission and output bounds work as before: withheld text is still never assembled. The comparison bound now also counts runs (see Review).

title: fix(edit,fonts): draw Han text no Japanese face covers in a Chinese face
author: mailbyms
body:
## What this changes

Editing existing text in a Simplified Chinese PDF fails today with `the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+8054` (联): the only CJK faces in the fallback chain are Japanese ones, and none of them has the Simplified-only characters. Towards #2095.

- `crates/fonts`: **`document_chinese_fonts_for_style()`** — the `Hans` faces in style and weight order (serif with a serif source, sans with a sans one, the requested weight before Regular), mirroring `document_japanese_fonts_for_style()`. Empty when craft-fonts has no `Hans` face, which is every official build today (AGENTS.md §1.1 keeps Source Han and Noto CJK out), so nothing changes until craft-fonts carries one — #3908 proposes allowing the OFL typefaces.
- `crates/fonts`: **`covers_text()`** — whether one face can draw every character of a text (a cmap lookup and an advance per character, no outline), so a caller can keep a line in one face instead of discovering one character at a time that a face cannot draw it.
- `crates/edit`: **`type3_faces()`** — a Chinese face leads for Han text that no Japanese face can draw in full. Kana, and text the Japanese faces do cover, keep the Japanese faces, so Japanese, Cyrillic and Latin text is drawn exactly as before.
- `crates/edit`: **`source_family()`** — 宋体/Songti/Kai/FangSong source fonts now read as serif, so such a line asks for a serif stand-in rather than Mincho's Gothic counterpart.

No font file is added anywhere: the face has to come from craft-fonts.

title: M11: Convert to PDF/A needs the owner's permission on an encrypted document (#3921)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3921.

`check_permission` gated `Edit::ConvertPdfA` by `p.modify()` alone. But `pdfcraft_preflight::convert` starts by removing the encryption, since PDF/A forbids it. So a document opened with the user password, whose owner allowed changes but withheld printing and copying, could be converted and saved as an unencrypted copy with every restriction gone. That is a change of security, which the engine otherwise reserves for the owner.

`ConvertPdfA` now needs `unrestricted(p)`, the same rights as Protect and Remove security. Otherwise it is refused with `NotPermitted("removing the encryption, which PDF/A forbids")`, so the user sees why Save as PDF/A was refused.

- An unencrypted document has no permissions, so it converts as before.
- A batch containing the conversion is refused by the existing `Edit::Batch` recursion.
- The comment on #3921 said a fix already existed elsewhere. I checked: on `main` (`0dc77fe4`) the new test fails (output below).

**Every route goes through this check.** `Session::apply` is the only caller of `check_permission` and the only way into `run_edit`. The UI (`standards_ui.rs`), the `pdfa_convert` automation tool (`a11y.rs`) and actions (`actions.rs`) all call it. Undo and redo only swap snapshots that an earlier `apply` already allowed.

title: render: fall back to an installed Simplified Chinese face for non-embedded CID fonts (Windows)
author: qwe3084614
body:
## Problem

PDFs generated by Chinese government systems (customs declarations, invoices, tax forms) almost always set their Chinese text in a **composite (CID) font that is not embedded** — typically `STSong-Light` with `/Encoding /UniGB-UCS2-H` and `/CIDSystemInfo << /Registry (Adobe) /Ordering (GB1) /Supplement 2 >>`, exactly the shape of the fixture in `crates/render/src/inspect.rs`.

In current PdfCraft **all of that text draws nothing**: company names, field values, whole columns. Every other viewer the user is likely to have (Edge, Chrome, WPS, Adobe) renders the page, so this reads as a defect, and it makes an entire class of documents unusable for reading.

## Why it happens

- `crates/fonts/src/fallback.rs`, step 5 of the substitution chain: for the `GB1` / `CNS1` / `Korea1` orderings there is no licensed face, so the chain reports none and the caller draws nothing. That is the *right* answer for the bundling policy — but the user-visible result is missing text.
- `crates/render/src/raster.rs` (`japanese_fallback`) substitutes only for `Adobe-Japan1`; the comment explains why: the pinned craft-fonts' Chinese face is Noto CJK, which AGENTS.md §1.1 rules out (Source Han under another name).
- hayro's own substitutes for non-embedded fonts are the Latin standard 14, which hold no Han glyph.

For `UniGB-UCS2-H` documents this is easy to fix at runtime, though: the encoding *is* Unicode, so `Type0Font`'s existing `map_via_unicode` path ("Yay, Unicode worked!") accepts **any** Unicode font as the substitute — no CID-keyed CFF needed. The `.notdef` guard only fires when the Unicode mapping fails.

## What this PR does

On Windows only, wire one more step into `RenderConfig`'s `font_resolver`, between the Japanese craft-fonts substitute and hayro's standard resolver:

title: fix(optimize): keep a destination referenced only through an indirect /Dest
author: Matoo125
body:
## What this changes

Reduce File Size (Clean Up) removes named destinations that nothing refers to. `referenced_names` in `crates/optimize/src/links.rs` collected the used names by reading `/Dest` and a GoTo's `/D` **directly** with `dest_name`, which only recognises a string or name. When a link's `/Dest` is an *indirect reference* to the name string (valid PDF) rather than the string itself, the name was not counted, so the destination it still used was treated as unreferenced and deleted — silently breaking the link.

title: M2: text extraction finishes a column before the next one across a paragraph gap (#3658)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3658.

On a two-column page, text extraction and Find read the top of the left column, then the whole right column, and only then the rest of the left column. This happened whenever an ordinary paragraph gap separated the left column's blocks.

The cause is step 3 of `arrange` (`crates/render/src/text.rs`). It took the top-most unread block next. It preferred a block to its left only when the two overlapped vertically, which a block below a paragraph gap never does.

**The new rule.** The next block is the nearest unread block below the one just read that:
- overlaps it horizontally (by more than 30% of the narrower width), and
- starts at most 2.5 times the height of its last line below it.

That block is skipped when another unread block:
- **sits above it in its own span.** This is the rest of a column above a full-width heading or footnote.
- **is beside it on its left,** as before.
- **shares its first line.** The two first lines overlap by at least 30% of the taller one. That is a table or form row, which still reads across, including labels and values in different sizes or on shifted baselines. A line that only touches it, or a small footnote marker, is not a row.

When the rule declines, the old top-most rule applies unchanged, so the result is never worse than `main`'s. Footers, footnotes and captions further down keep their old place. Extraction, Find and copy share this order.

| `pdfcraft-cli text` on the issue's `columns.pdf` | |
|---|---|
| before | Two columns · A1 A2 A3 · B3 B4 · C1 C2 · B1 B2 |
| after | Two columns · A1 A2 A3 · B1 B2 · B3 B4 · C1 C2 |

`text_find` for "B2 second paragraph B3 second paragraph" now finds 1 match (was 0). The wrong join "C2 third paragraph B1 second paragraph" finds 0 (was 1).

**Known limit.** When a paragraph in the next column starts on the same line as the continuation (text on a baseline grid), it counts as a row. The top-most rule then applies, so the order of #3658 comes back. Telli…

title: M7: edited text keeps the spaces typed, except at the edges of a stretched justified row (#4199, #3797)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4199. Fixes #3797.

Editing a paragraph and saving collapsed every run of typed spaces to one, and dropped an indent or trailing spaces. "Hello     world   end" was saved as `(Hello world end) Tj`. Adding a space to a paragraph therefore did nothing after Apply, which is #3797.

**Cause.** `rewrite_block_from` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`) is the single-style paragraph rewrite behind `replace_block` and `Edit::EditTextBlock`. It split the typed text at any white space and joined the words with one space, and `wrap()` did the same. The single-line path (`replace_line`) and the styled region path (`rewrite_styled_block`) already kept spaces. Text extraction was not at fault: the saved content stream itself had lost them.

**Fix:**
- **The text is kept as typed.** CR and CRLF become line breaks, and any other white-space character becomes one space each.
- **`wrap()` keeps each run of spaces,** including an indent and trailing spaces. It drops only the spaces where a row soft-wraps.
- **Centred and right-aligned rows** are measured to their last word, so spaces typed after a title don't shift it. The editor's draft box is measured the same way, so the preview box equals what Apply draws.
- **A justified row that isn't the last one** still drops its indent and trailing spaces, exactly as on `main`, so word spacing reaches only the spaces between its words. Its output is byte-identical to `main`. Keeping an indent on a justified row is a possible follow-up; see below.
- **A paragraph at `0 Tz`** is not justified, which avoids an infinite `Tw`.

body:
## What this changes

The `dependency licences and advisories` check now fails on every PR. [RUSTSEC-2026-0385](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0385), published today, flags `ctutils` 0.4.2: its mask generation and `u128` comparisons are not constant-time. The fix is in 0.4.4.

`ctutils` comes in through `crypto-bigint`, which the signing crates use (`rsa`, `elliptic-curve`, `pdfcraft-sign`). This updates only that package, to 0.4.5. In `Cargo.lock`, one version and checksum pair changes. No manifests, dependency lists or other packages change.

Seen failing on #4217's `dependency licences and advisories` job: `advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo update -p ctutils` changes only the `ctutils` record, from 0.4.2 to 0.4.5, under the workspace's Rust 1.95.
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-sign`: 111 passed, 2 ignored
- [x] `cargo xtask assets`: ok

The advisory job on this PR is the regression check. I didn't run `cargo deny` locally.

title: fix(redact,cos): cleared redaction marks leave nothing behind
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

Adding redaction marks and then clearing them left traces behind in two ways: the page's original annotation list wasn't restored, and Save still wrote the cleared marks into the file even though nothing referred to them any more.

**Clear all didn't put the page back** (`fix(redact)`)
- `clear_marks` wrote `/Annots []` on a page that had no annotations before the marks.
- It replaced an indirect `/Annots` array with an inline copy.
- It left replies to a mark in place. Their `/IRT` kept the cleared mark in the document, and the comment list showed a reply to nothing.

`clear_marks` now writes the list through `pdfcraft_annot::set_annots` (now public), as deleting a comment does, and removes each mark's replies and pop-ups with it. The "what goes with a deleted comment" walk moves out of `delete_annotation` into `with_replies_and_popups`, which both use. It visits each annotation once, where the old loop swept the list again until nothing changed.

**Inline replies and pop-ups stayed behind** (`fix(annot,redact)`)
- `/Annots` may hold an annotation dictionary inline instead of a reference. The standard asks for references, but files do it and PdfCraft accepts them.
- Deleting a comment or clearing marks only matched referenced entries. An inline reply (`/IRT`) or pop-up (`/Parent`) of what went stayed behind, pointing at nothing, and so did the pop-up an inline reply or inline comment names (`/Popup`). This was already the case on `main`; CodeRabbit's review of this PR found it.

`goes_with` matches an entry against what is going, inline entries included, and `delete_annotation` and `clear_marks` both filter with it. The walk follows the pop-up an inline reply names, and deleting an inline comment takes the pop-up it names.

**A save wrote the cleared marks anyway** (`fix(cos,engine)`)
- An incremental save wrote every object added in the session, whether anything still referred to it or not.
- A mark added and then cleared therefore went into …

title: M7: paste added text boxes and images in the engine and through content_copy (#2636)
author: lev-n
body:
Part of #2636 (copy, cut and paste of text boxes and images). This is the engine and automation half. The desktop parts are stacked on it: #4264 (⌘X / ⌘C / ⌘V and the Edit menu) and #4268 (the item's right-click menu). #4258 is a separate small engine fix found along the way.

## What this changes

- **`Edit::PasteContent`:** pastes an added text box or image copied in this document or another, as it was, as one undo step ("Paste"). A text box keeps its font, size, colour, alignment and box. An image keeps its picture, box, turns, flips and crop.
- **Placement** (`pdfcraft_edit::added::paste_place` / `paste_rect`): a paste lands where the item was, 18 pt down and to the right past each copy of it already on the page, or at a given point. It always stays on the page.
- **`content_copy` tool:** `doc, page, index, to_doc, to_page, at` drives the same thing headlessly.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **Image storage:** a pasted image draws its picture from the copied image object while that is still the picture in the target (same document). Otherwise it reuses an added image there that already holds the picture, so a second paste into another document doesn't store a third copy. Only as a last resort is the file embedded.
- **Into another document:** the picture goes as its JPEG or JPEG 2000 file (Add Image keeps a JPEG 2000 picture as the file it was given), or else a PNG. A colour profile is dropped, and a CMYK picture stored losslessly turns to RGB. The parity entry and the tool description both say so.
- **Permissions:** `Document::added_image_file` refuses when the source doesn't allow copying, and `content_copy` checks copying before anything else. The paste itself needs the target's modification permission, like any content edit.
- **What counts as a copy:** for an image, the same box, turns, flips and crop, whichever object holds its picture. That's what lets the second paste into another document step past the first.

</details>

title: M5: stamp_custom places a picture fitted inside a rect (#4077)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4077.

`stamp_custom` could only centre a PDF page or image at its natural size, capped at 200 pt, and `page_add_image` takes raster images only. So a vector diagram couldn't be placed at, say, a text column's 483 pt width.

`stamp_custom` now takes **`rect` `[x0, y0, x1, y1]`** (displayed-page points from the top-left, like `at`) as an alternative to `at`. The picture is scaled to fit inside the box, keeping its shape, and centred in it. A PDF page stays a form XObject (`/PCPicture`, drawn with `/Pic Do`), so it remains vector and its text can still be extracted.

- **Engine.** `Edit::AddCustomStamp` with a non-point rect now *fits* the picture (`fit_picture`) instead of stretching it to the box.
  - A box that already has the picture's shape is kept exactly. Image signatures (`signature_image.rs`), the only in-tree caller that passes an explicit rect, are therefore unchanged.
  - On quarter-turned pages the displayed sides are swapped, as the natural-size path already does.
  - Non-finite or empty boxes reach the annotation's existing check and are refused.
- **Automation.** `rect` must be four finite numbers, with each side from 1 to 14400 pt (the largest PDF page, ISO 32000-2 Annex C).
  - Passing both `at` and `rect`, or neither, gives `InvalidArgs`.
  - Like `at`, `rect` isn't clipped to the page.
  - `path` still goes through the read root.
  - Without `rect`, behaviour is unchanged.
- **Schema and description** in `tools.rs`; the parity note and evidence for the custom-stamp entry.

The UI is unchanged: a click still places a stamp at its natural size, and the handles then resize it. Drag-to-size is #342.

title: M2: draw images past the pixel cap at a reduced size instead of skipping them (#4071)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4071.

An image over 2^28 pixels was skipped before decoding, so a page holding one rendered blank without a warning. The cap is `image_size_ok` in `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/x_object.rs`, mirrored by `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` in hayro. A 36×24 in plan scanned at 600 dpi (21600×14400, 311 Mpx, CCITT G4 or Flate) was one such page. Large-format scans pass 2^28 routinely. The cap came from a fuzz fix (ee254a91: a stencil with `/W 4294967295`), and that protection stays.

**Vendored patch (54)** draws such images at a reduced size. Memory is bounded by the output, not the source.

- **Size gate.**
  - Up to 2^28 px: unchanged.
  - 2^28 to 2^30 px: decoded reduced, if the image's *packed* samples are at most 512 MiB.
  - Over 2^30 px: refused before anything is decoded or allocated. `/W 4294967295` is still refused there, and `absurd_mask_and_fax_sizes_are_refused_before_decoding` passes unchanged.
- **Reduction** (new `reduce.rs`).
  - The filters produce full-size samples, packed as the stream holds them: 39 MB for the 311 Mpx 1-bit plan.
  - These are reduced row by row, by whole factors, before anything expands a sample. A full-size image never exists as bytes per pixel, RGB or RGBA.
  - Each block is averaged into 8 bits. Indexed images and colour-key masks take the block's middle pixel at their own depth. 1-bit images count set bits.
  - The reduced image reports its size through the existing `scale_factors`, so the renderer draws it over the same rectangle.
- **Factors.** The largest factors that keep the image at least the size it's drawn at, raised further if needed to stay within 32 MiB once converted and 2^15 px a side.
- **CCITT** keeps 1 bit per pixel past 2^28 px; it used to write a byte per pixel. `ccitt_size_ok` allows 2^30.
- **Flate limit.** For an over-cap image, Flate output stops at the samples plus one predictor byte per row, not twice the samples.
- **Cache.** `DecodedImageKey` gains `reduction` and `mask_reduction`, so a re…

author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4186.

The three `pdfcraft-ui-egui` integration tests listed in #4186 fail at random on busy Windows and FreeBSD runners, on PRs that don't touch what they test. Today alone they turned #4214, #4220 and #4235 red.

**Two of them waited a frame count, not a time.**
- `control_open_replies_pending_while_the_worker_opens_and_focuses_once_it_has` stepped 30 frames waiting for a worker-thread open.
- `mode_tabs_keep_the_hand_over_page_text_scrolled_under_them` ran 50 hover rounds waiting for page text.

title: fix(edit): leave Edit a PDF from its panel, and delete selected objects
author: simscorpbs
body:
## What this fixes

Two things in **Edit a PDF** that a user hit right away: editing could not be left from the panel,
and an object could not be deleted.

### Leaving Edit a PDF

Only the mode bar put Edit text & images down (`enter_mode` → `put_down_edit_text`). Every other
way out moved the panel or the tool and left editing on underneath, with every paragraph still
boxed:

| Way out | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| × on the Edit panel | closed the panel only | leaves Edit (All tools), as Acrobat's Close does |
| < (Back to all tools) | set `mode` directly | goes through `enter_mode` |
| Another tool (Other options, catalogue) | kept `EditText` under the new tool | puts it down (`select_tool`) |
| Select tool / V | switched the tool, left an open paragraph unapplied | applies it first (`put_down_edit_text`) |

A paragraph still open is applied in each case, as switching mode already did.

### Deleting objects

Objects selected in Edit a PDF (by a paragraph's frame, Shift-click or a marquee) could be moved
but not deleted: no key, no menu, and no engine edit to remove an existing paragraph.

- **Delete / Backspace** on an object selection now deletes it as one undo step ("Delete
  object(s)"), as in Acrobat. A lone selected image keeps its own Delete.
- **`Edit::DeleteObjects { page, objects }`** mirrors `MoveObjects`: targets resolve against the
  original inventories before any change, and a refusal leaves the document untouched.
- **`pdfcraft_edit::delete_objects`** deletes paragraphs with `text::delete_blocks`, then images
  (last index first) and added items (last first).
- **`delete_blocks`** turns each text-showing operation of the paragraph into a `TJ` that moves by
  the same advance. The text after it on the same line stays where it was, and the strings leave
  the content stream. Hiding them (`3 Tr`) would leave the text searchable and copyable, as a bad
  redaction does. Clipping text and vertical text are refused, as in `translate_blocks`.

title: Test that moving an image keeps its marked-content sequence intact
author: eliets2
body:
## What this changes

Adds one regression test, `moving_an_image_inside_marked_content_leaves_every_sequence_intact`, in `crates/edit/src/tests.rs`.

`translate_images` only changes the image's own `cm`; its `Do` stays where it was, so a moved image stays inside the `BDC ... EMC` sequence that tags it, whether that is a tagged-PDF element or an optional-content layer. Nothing pinned this: the image-move tests cover clips, transforms and repeated moves but not marked content.

The test moves an image inside `/P <</MCID 0>> BDC` and inside `/OC /L0 BDC` and checks that both sequences are still there, that the `Do` is still inside its own sequence, and that the other sequence gained no image.

An earlier version of this pull request added a guard to `translate_images` that refused such moves. The review pointed out that the guard refuses moves that work today, so it is dropped; this pull request now only adds the test. Arrange moving an image across sequences (#3145) is a separate change and is not touched here.

Refs #3145

## How you verified it

title: Accessibility: turn a layout table into Div and P tags in one call (#4105)
author: pat26-dotcom
body:
## What this changes

A new automation tool `accessibility_layout_table_to_blocks {doc, object, generation}` (engine edit
`Edit::LayoutTableToBlocks`, `pdfcraft_a11y::layout_table_to_blocks`) turns a table used only for
layout (label and value pairs, a letterhead grid) into plain blocks in one undoable step:

- the Table tag, its THead/TBody/TFoot and TR tags become `Div`;
- its TH, TD and Caption tags become `P`, or `Div` when they hold structure tags of their own;
- content (MCIDs, MCRs, OBJRs), reading order and the tags inside the cells stay as they are, and a
  table nested in a cell stays a table;

  converted tags; other attribute objects and their revision numbers are kept;
- direct (inline) rows and cells are converted in place in their parent's `/K`;
- the tag's type is checked after the role map; anything that isn't a table is refused, and the
  whole table is read before anything is written, so a refused table changes nothing.

Afterwards `table-summary` and `table-headers` no longer apply to it. Undo uses the existing
"Change tag properties" label, so no new wording is needed in the catalogues.

This covers the Div/P half of #4105 (so it doesn't close the issue on merge). The other half, marking a whole (decorative) table as

title: M7: a batch of content edits refreshes the added content and page marks
author: lev-n
body:
## What this changes

`Edit::Batch` whose parts are all content edits gets `Scope::Content`, so the engine takes the content-only refresh. That refresh re-reads `Document::added()` and `marks()` only when `content_refresh_lists` says the edit changes them, and that function never looked inside a batch. A batch of `AddText` / `DeleteContent` (or `AddWatermark`) edits therefore left both lists stale until the next full refresh or undo.

`content_refresh_lists` now answers for a batch's parts. It's a 7-line arm; the existing match is untouched.

No in-tree caller builds such a batch yet, so this is latent today. `Edit::Batch` is public engine API, though, and the cut/copy/paste work for #2636 (#4230) and any script batching added-content edits hit it.

title: M7: cut, copy and paste added text boxes and images with the keys and Edit menu (#2636)
author: lev-n
body:
Part of #2636. **Stacked on #4230**: review the last two commits, 127233c0 (the feature) and 4944e215 (review fixes). The first two commits are #4230 and drop out of this diff once it merges.

## What this changes

In Edit a PDF, **⌘X / ⌘C / ⌘V and Edit ▸ Cut, Copy and Paste** act on the selected added text box or image:
- A text box keeps its font, size, colour, alignment and box; an image keeps its picture, turns, flips and crop.
- It pastes into any open document, as one undo step.
- A document that doesn't allow copying, or changes, refuses Copy or Cut and says why. A refused Cut neither copies nor deletes.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- **System clipboard:** a copy also puts the box's text or the image's pixels on the system clipboard for other apps. Anything copied since wins on ⌘V: a picture (a screenshot, say) is pasted instead of the old item, and text copied since leaves ⌘V alone. PdfCraft tells whether its copy is still there by comparing the text, or the picture's size and 64 sampled pixels (`content_clip.rs`), because no portable clipboard change counter exists.
- **Newest selection wins:** selecting an added item (clicking it, starting to type in it, or a paste selecting it) drops page text and page-picture selections. ⌘C and ⌘X therefore act on what was selected last, and a page picture selected after an item is not shadowed by it.
- **One ⌘V path:** `paste_image_key` tries the copied item first, then the existing system-clipboard picture paste. Other paste features can hook in there rather than adding their own `Event::Paste` listener.
- ⌘C / ⌘X go through `execute("edit.copy" / "edit.cut")`, so the keys and the menu share one permission check and one set of messages. Cut needs copying allowed as well as changes.
- **Other copies replace it:** copying page text, a page picture or a snapshot in PdfCraft drops the copied item, also on the web, where no system clipboard can be read back.
- **No paste mid-drag:** ⌘V while an item is being dragge…

title: M7: added text takes character spacing from Format text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4245.

Character spacing in Format text now works for added text, not only for a paragraph being edited. Acrobat's Add new text help says to use the FORMAT TEXT options on new text, and Format text lists "Character spacing: Choose the amount of space between letters" ([add text](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/edit-documents/edit-text-in-pdfs/add-text.html), [format text](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/edit-documents/edit-text-in-pdfs/format-text.html); helpx answered 403 here, so I read the web.archive.org copies from Dec 2025 / Jan 2026).

`AddedText` gets a `char_spacing` in points. It is drawn as `Tc`, and the item keeps it under `/CharSpacing` in its `/PCAdded` dictionary, so it reopens with the spacing and stays editable. An item saved without the key reads 0, so older files don't change. The spacing counts in every width the layout uses: wrapping, alignment, justification, the shaped Arabic/Hebrew/Thai path and the editor's box width. It scales with `/UserUnit` the same way the size does. The in-place editor previews it. `page_add_text` and `content_update` take `char_spacing`, and `content_list` reports it. The panel field is the existing one with the same -5 to 50 pt range; the engine refuses anything non-finite or past ±500 pt.

What's left out: line spacing and horizontal scale for added text stay disabled. They need their own model and layout changes, so I kept this PR to the one control the issue asks about.

Choices you may want differently (happy to switch):
- Spacing is counted after every character, trailing one included, as `Tc` moves the pen. So right-aligned or justified text ends one spacing short of the box's right edge. I can measure alignment by the ink instead.
- Like the paragraph fields, dragging the value applies on every frame. Typing a value or picking one from the list is a single undo step.

title: test(automation): give sign_document a real digital ID and document in the hostile-arguments sweep
author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

`no_tool_panics_on_hostile_arguments` passes `"in.pdf"` for every required string argument. Earlier in the sweep, `sign_id_create` writes a digital ID to that path (when the hostile `password` is long enough), and `sign_document` then reads it as its `id`. Nearly every `sign_document` call failed to decrypt it, so the hostile value under test was never reached. The 600,000-round key derivation on each failed decrypt also took most of the test's time.

The sweep now:

- empties the root before each tool, so no tool sees files an earlier tool wrote. It does this through the root's canonical path, as the tools reach it: `form_merge_data` writes a file named `" "`, and on Windows the plain path drops the trailing space, so that entry names the root itself;
- gives `sign_document` a real ID (`crates/sign/tests/data/ec-p256.p12`, password `test`, 2,048 rounds) and a fresh blank document for each call, and closes the document afterwards so later tools' placeholder document ids don't find it open;
- asserts that at least one `sign_document` call signed, so a broken fixture fails the test.

The same 176 tools and 26,290 calls run with the same hostile values. `sign_id_create` and `form_merge_data` are the only tools that write into the root; no other tool's placeholder path reaches a file that changes which check fails first.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `sign_document` calls past the ID decrypt (of 440) | 1 | 370 |
| ...and past the document lookup | 0 | 340 |
| `sign_document` time | 85 s | 2.8 s |
| `no_tool_panics_on_hostile_arguments` time | 89 s | 7 s |

The 70 calls that still stop at the ID are the ones whose hostile value is the `id` or `password` itself, a null required argument, or a non-object argument list. The 30 more that stop at the document carry a hostile `doc`. No new panics were found.

title: M10: (n) names the page at position n, whatever its label, in page ranges and the page box (ISO 32000-2 §12.4.2)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4281.

**The need.** A token in a Pages to Print range is a page label first and a number only if no label matches. The page box in the navigation bar resolves what is typed the same way. On a labelled document that leaves no way to name a page by its position once its number belongs to a label. With front matter labelled i–iii and the body starting at 1, `1` is the fourth page, and the first page can only be reached by typing `i`. The same range parser also reads Combine files ranges.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.4.2: "Page labels and page indices need not coincide: the indices shall be fixed, running consecutively through the document starting from 0 for the first page, but the labels may be specified in any way that is appropriate for the particular document." A page therefore has two names, and input needs a spelling for each. The file format keeps them apart the same way: a reference XObject's `Page` is "a page index or page label", an integer or a text string (Table 95).

**The change**
- **`print::position`** (new): the 1-based position a token names in parentheses, `(1)` or `( 1 )`. Ranges and the page box both use it.
- **Page ranges** (`print::range::page_of`): after the label lookup, `(n)` is the page at position n. That covers Print, `doc_print` and Combine files. It works alone and at either end of a range, mixed with labels and numbers: `(1)-(3)`, `(9)-`, `-(2)`, `(2)-1`, `ii-(5)`.
  - `(0)` and `(11)` on a 10-page document are out of range.
  - Anything else in parentheses is "not a page number or label", as before.
- **The page box** (`DocView::go_to_typed`): a label first (case-insensitive, as before), then `(n)`, then a number. A position past the end leaves the view where it is.
- **Labels still win.** A label that is itself `(1)` keeps naming its own page.
- **Odd and even still count positions.** They now have a test on a labelled document, and the parity note no longer calls that case unknown: indices are fixed a…

title: Assets: don't hash translation catalogs in ATTRIBUTION.toml
author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3098.

`ATTRIBUTION.toml` pins a SHA-256 for each of the 33 translation catalogs (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/*.tsv`). Every PR that changes UI text has to edit those 33 lines, so any two such PRs conflict there. Of the 722 open PRs, 224 touch `ATTRIBUTION.toml`, 205 of them together with a catalog. title: M5: Shift holds lines level or plumb while drawing (ortho)
author: ohagmann
body:
## What this changes

Drawing a straight line on a plan with the mouse always came out a little crooked: the Line and Arrow tools had no constraint at all, and connected lines, polygons and clouds neither. With **Shift held**:

- a new **line or arrow** runs **level or plumb** from where it starts, whichever is nearer to the pointer — a CAD drawing's ortho mode. The end slides along that axis (it is projected onto it, not turned), so it still follows the pointer;
- each new side of **connected lines, a polygon or a cloud** is held the same way from the corner before, and the rubber band to the pointer shows where the click will put it;
- dragging an **end or corner** of a drawn line or polygon (comment.reshape) with Shift is held the same way. It turned to 45° steps before; one rule for all of them.

Acrobat holds lines to 45° steps. On drawings and plans, the level and plumb lines are the ones people draw over and over; a 45° line is rarely wanted, and when it is, it is drawn without Shift. The measuring tools keep their 45° steps (unchanged).

Engine: `measure::snap::ortho(last, point)` next to `constrain`. Headless: `comment_add` takes `ortho: true` for line, arrow, polygon, cloud and polyline (each end or corner held to the one before; refused for other types). New parity entry `comment.draw-ortho` (P1, shipped), `comment.reshape` notes, a `docs/ui-parity.md` row, ROADMAP log.

**With #3545 (snap to drawing):** #3545 used to hold lines to 45° with Shift while drawing; that part has been taken out of it, so Shift's hold lives here alone. Both touch the drawing tools' point handling: whichever lands second puts the snapped point through `held()` (`held(points.first(), cx.snapped(p).0, …)`), which keeps a snapped end on the level or plumb line — tested that way in a combined build.

title: M12: XFA text is measured at its standard-14 font's own widths
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA text is now measured in the standard-14 font it is drawn in, at that font's own widths (ISO 32000-2 Annex D), instead of as Helvetica times a factor. On `main`, `text::Face::width` scaled Helvetica widths: ×1.04 for bold, ×0.92 for Times, ×0.96 for Times bold. Courier was a flat 0.6 em per character. The exact widths were already in the fonts crate (`Std14::text_width`), and the layout already writes each run in its exact standard-14 face (`Family::base_font`). Measuring and drawing now agree.

The factors are off by different amounts for different letters. Times capitals are wider than 0.92 × Helvetica (an `A` is 722 against 0.92 × 667, about 614), and Times lowercase is narrower. Helvetica-Bold differs from 1.04 × Helvetica letter by letter. So bold and Times text could wrap a line too early or too late, or come out narrower or wider than the box measured for it. Two places show it most: labels in a box without a set width, and right-aligned or centered text.

DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, found while reading the layout code during work on that form. I laid its first page out with `main` and with this branch and compared every text run:
- No line wraps differently.
- 10 of its 110 runs move sideways, by 2 to 4.4 pt, and nothing moves vertically.
- Most of them are centered bold headings: *REQUEST AND AUTHORITY FOR LEAVE*, *PART I - REQUESTOR INFORMATION*, and the *DEPARTURE*, *EXTENSION*, *RETURN* and *REQUESTOR / SUPERVISOR / APPROVING AUTHORITY SIGNATURES* titles. On `main` the ×1.04 estimate made them wider than they are, so they sat left of center. *REQUESTOR / SUPERVISOR / APPROVING AUTHORITY SIGNATURES* sat 4.4 pt left.

The change is small on this form, but the rule is wrong for any form, and it costs nothing to get right.

`Family::std14(bold, italic)` now maps a family to its `Std14` face, and `Family::base_font` reads the name from that same `Std14`, so the face measure…

title: fix(automation): roots-only mode refuses other shares and devices by name
author: mercuryVM
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4003: its first point. The issue lists three; ticket-craft asked for them to be split, and this PR does only the first. The other two are listed at the end.

**Problem.** With only `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` set (no `--root`), `AutomationRoots::check_path` sent every path straight to `std::fs::canonicalize`. A path on another network share or in a device namespace was therefore resolved, contacting the host (an SMB or WebDAV lookup), before it was refused. The refusal also read differently: `cannot resolve \.\pipe\x: …` rather than `outside the read root`. `--root` mode already refuses these paths by name with `foreign_share`.

**Fix.**
- `foreign_share` moves from `lib.rs` to `file_access.rs` (`pub(crate)`, unchanged). `--root` mode keeps calling it.
- `check_path` makes the path absolute by name, which reads nothing. It then refuses a path on another share or device namespace than the root's with the same refusal as any other path outside the root, and only then follows links. A root on a share still accepts paths on that share.
- `resolve` is split into `absolute` (empty-path check, reserved device names, `std::path::absolute`) and `resolve` (links followed), so the share check sits between them. `…\out\NUL`, which becomes `\.\NUL` once made absolute, keeps its own `reserved device names` refusal.
- `docs/mcp.md` said UNC paths "are resolved like drive-letter ones", which is no longer true. It and the automation README now describe the refusal.

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.

title: M5: NoZoom comments and sticky notes keep their size on screen (ISO 32000-2 Table 167)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4278.

**The need.** Sticky notes, and any annotation a file marks NoZoom, are meant to keep the same size on the screen whatever the zoom. PdfCraft scaled every annotation with the page instead, so zooming in made notes grow over the text they comment on (#4278). The notes PdfCraft creates set the NoZoom flag (`FLAG_NO_ZOOM` in `pdfcraft-annot`), but nothing read it: no code in `crates/` or `vendor/` looked at bit 4.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.5.3 and §12.5.6.4:
- Table 167, bit 4 NoZoom: "If set, do not scale the annotation's appearance to match the magnification of the page. The location of the annotation on the page (defined by the upper-left corner of its annotation rectangle) shall remain fixed, regardless of the page magnification."
- The text after the table says such an annotation "shall always maintain the same fixed size on the screen and shall be unaffected by the magnification level at which the page itself is displayed". The processor moves the other three corners itself, but "shall not actually change the annotation's Rect entry".
- §12.5.6.4: "Text annotations shall not scale and rotate with the page; they shall behave as if the NoZoom and NoRotate annotation flags … were always set." So a note keeps its size even without the bit.

**1. The renderer** (vendored hayro-interpret, patch 51)
- `InterpreterSettings::magnification: Option<f32>` is the zoom the page is shown at on screen (1.0 = 100%).
- In `interpret_page`, once the appearance is mapped onto `/Rect` (Algorithm 8.1), it is scaled by 1/magnification about the upper-left corner of `/Rect` in default user space. This applies to an annotation with bit 4, and to every text annotation. `/Rect` itself never changes.
- Form fields and links are left in `/Rect`, even with the bit set.
- A magnification that isn't finite and greater than zero is ignored. A scaled transform that would not be finite falls back to the unscaled one.

title: Omit minus sign when FormCalc Format() rounds to zero
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2328-2330` (the "format" number-picture branch, `if num < 0.0 { text = format!("-{text}") }`). There is no existing issue.

FormCalc `Format()` printed a small negative number as "-0.0" (negative zero). The number-picture branch prepended `-` whenever the unrounded input was below zero, without checking the rounded digits. A small negative value under the picture `9.9`, such as -0.04, therefore printed as `-0.0`.

title: M12: XFA check boxes sit where their margins, caption and alignment put them
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA check boxes and radio buttons are drawn where their field's margins, caption and paragraph alignment put them. On `main` the box is always drawn at the left edge of the space the caption leaves, plus the box's own margin. Horizontal alignment, the right margin, and the size of a caption without a reserve all have no effect.

I measured another viewer on two synthetic forms with 56 check boxes and radio buttons that vary each of these. The rule they follow:

- **No caption** (or a hidden one): the box sits at the right of the field's content area, as if a caption on its left took the rest. Horizontal alignment has no room to act on. A right margin moves the box in, and vertical alignment and the top and bottom margins work as for text.
- **A caption with a reserve:** the box sits in the space the caption leaves, where the paragraph's alignment puts it (left by default).
- **A caption without a reserve:** the box keeps its own size on the far side, and the caption takes the rest of the field. A left caption puts the box at the right, a top caption puts it at the bottom, and so on. The caption's text starts right after the box.
- **An inline caption** on a check box has no text to run with. It isn't drawn, and the box sits as with no caption.
- **The box's own margin** (`<checkButton><margin/>`) doesn't move the box.

DD Form 2946 (*Department of Defense Telework Agreement*, a public blank form) is a real-world case, and where this was found. Its page 4 safety checklist has Yes and No boxes in 12.7 mm cells. The boxes are 4.94 mm, with a 3.556 mm right margin and no caption. That is the usual way to center a box in a table cell: no caption, then a right margin until it looks centered.
- On `main` every box sits against the left line of its cell.
- With this change each box sits 4.2 mm in, against its right margin, as the other viewer draws it.

title: M3: a link without a position keeps the reader's place (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.2)
author: Lcoding15
body:
Description:
## What this changes

A `/XYZ` destination with a null (or unusable) `left` or `top` went to the **top** of the target page. ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.2 says a null value keeps the current one. Acrobat Reader, observed black-box on a synthetic two-page fixture at 400 %, keeps the user-space point at the window's top-left on the new page, at the same zoom.

This matters for CAD exports. WSCAD writes every cross-reference ("/91.4" = sheet 91, column 4) as `[page /XYZ null null 0]`. Zoomed in, following one landed on the sheet's title row instead of where the reader was looking.

`go_to_dest` now reads the place at the window's top-left before the jump (`place_at_corner`) and uses it for the null coordinates, along each axis the page overflows the window. A page that fits keeps the layout's own placement (centred, or its top), so fit-page / fit-width jumps look as before. This also applies to bookmarks and remote destinations that use `go_to_dest`. `crates/organize/src/outline.rs` already documents a left-out coordinate as "keeps the reader's position".

Still missing (noted in `parity/`): a null `/FitH` top and `/FitV` left still go to the page edge.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --lib -- canvas::` (54 passed), `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test it -- view::` (75 passed)
- [x] `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask parity`
