title: M2: Type 3 text in rendering mode 7 is not rendered and adds no clip (ISO 32000-2 9.3.6)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4429.

**The need.** Text in a Type 3 font shown with `7 Tr` was painted, filled in the current fill colour (black by default). Clip-mode text is normally followed by a fill, so the glyphs showed wherever that fill didn't reach. In the issue's fixture that is a black bar beside a red box.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §9.3.6, after Table 104:
> Where text is drawn using a Type 3 font:
> • if text rendering mode is set to a value of 3 or 7, the text shall not be rendered.
> • if text rendering mode is set to a value other than 3 or 7, the text shall be rendered using the glyph descriptions in the Type 3 font.
> • If text rendering mode is set to a value of 4, 5, 6 or 7, nothing shall be added to the clipping path.

The same clause says that when "the only glyphs shown have no outlines … no clipping shall occur".

**The change** (vendored hayro-interpret patch 64, `interpret/text.rs`)
- **Mode 7.** `show_glyph` keeps mode 7 for a Type 3 glyph instead of turning it into a fill (patch 42 did that for every mode but 3). The glyph goes to the device as `GlyphDrawMode::Clip`: nothing is painted, and text extraction keeps it as clipping text, not as an invisible OCR layer.
- **The clip.** `clip_glyph`'s Type 3 arm is now a deliberate no-op citing §9.3.6. It used to log "not implemented". Text shown only in a Type 3 font leaves no clip at `ET`, and outline glyphs in the same text object still shape theirs.
- **Unchanged.** 0, 1, 2 and 4 to 6 render the glyph descriptions filled (patch 42), and 3 renders nothing.
- **Records.** Patch 64 is recorded in `vendor/README.md`, with patch 42's note and its renamed test. The `view.render-type3` notes in `parity/` now say how the modes apply.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed: `pdfcraft-render` (`--all-targets`) and `hayro-interpret` (`--lib --tests`)
- [x] tests pass on the crates I changed: `pdfcraft-render`, 385 unit and 23 …

title: M2: zero-area fills and clips mark the pixels they touch (ISO 32000-2 §10.7.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4432.

**The need.** A rectangle with no height or no width encloses no area, and the rasteriser marked no pixels for it.
- **As a clip.** `10 10 100 0 re W n` hid everything painted after it. A fill of the whole box through that clip left the page blank.
- **As a fill.** `10 10 100 0 re f` fell back to a thinnest-line stroke. On a pixel boundary that stroke half-covered two rows, a faint line where one solid row belongs. So the fill and the clip of the same rectangle marked different pixels.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §10.7.4, "Scan conversion rules":
- A shape paints "any pixel whose half-open square region intersects the shape, no matter how small the intersection is".
- Its example: "A zero-width or zero-height rectangle paints a line 1 pixel wide."
- And: "For clipping, the clipping region consists of the set of pixels that would be included by a fill operation."

**The change.** hayro-interpret patch (65), `degenerate_fill_area` in `interpret/path.rs`.
- **What counts.** A fill or clip path whose bounding box has no width or no height, but not both. "No" means the existing near-zero tolerance of 1/256 unit, the test the fill path already used for this case.
- **Along a device axis.** When the line lies less than a pixel across one device axis, it gets the run of whole device pixels it touches. That is the half-open rule: floor of the low end to ceiling of the high end, at least one pixel each way.
- **Rotated or skewed CTM.** Otherwise it gets a band one device pixel wide centred on the line, like the thinnest line of §8.4.3.2.
- **Fill rule.** The area is filled, or pushed as the clip, with the non-zero rule.
- **Unchanged.** A point (both sides zero) and any path with area, however thin, paint exactly as before.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p hayro-interpret -j 2 --lib --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo t…

title: M11: PDF Optimizer can discard links to other documents (optimize.discard-external-refs)
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

PDF Optimizer ▸ Discard User Data had no option for external cross-references (`optimize.discard-external-refs` was planned). The reference app's help page lists it in the Discard User Data panel: "Discard External Cross References: Removes links to other documents. Links that jump to other locations within the PDF are not removed." (https://web.archive.org/web/20221217175446/https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/optimizing-pdfs-acrobat-pro.html).

- Discard User Data has a new checkbox, "Discard external cross-references", off by default (`Settings::discard_external_refs`).
- It takes `GoToR`, `GoToE`, `Launch` and `ImportData` actions, and `Thread` actions with an `/F`, out of the `/A` entries of link annotations and bookmarks. The actions chained after a removed one through `/Next` take its place in the same order; entries there that are not actions (a null, or a reference to one) do not.
- The page names links, so only link annotations (`/Subtype /Link`, also when the name is stored as an indirect object) and bookmarks are changed. Other annotations, such as form fields, keep their actions.
- A link left with no action and no `/Dest` is removed from its page. When the link is an indirect object, that object is also rewritten without the action, so anything else that refers to it (the structure tree, for example) holds no action to another document. A bookmark keeps its title, its place and its children; bookmarks stored directly inside another bookmark are changed where they are.
- Links within the document (`/Dest`, `GoTo`) and web links (`URI`) stay. An indirect action that changes is written as a new indirect object, except the first action left at the head of an `/A`, which is copied into the `/A` directly when other actions follow it. Objects that use the old action keep it.

title: M9: a document timestamp lands in a signature field, where validators look
author: amoisttowe1
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4301.

`timestamp_document` appended its `/DocTimeStamp` dictionary with nothing pointing at it.
#4301 (from @alehel's review note on #4226): validators that discover signatures through
the AcroForm field tree may therefore miss a document timestamp. PdfCraft's timestamps
were such dictionaries. This makes us write the layout our validator has read since #621:

- The dictionary is stored as `/V` of a Sig field, reachable catalog → AcroForm `/Fields`
  → widget — the layout `sign()` writes for new fields. The field is its own widget:
  zero-area `/Rect`, `F 132` (Print|Locked), no `/AP` — a timestamp stamps the file, not a
  place on the page; page 1's `/Annots` gains it (redirected to a fresh array whenever
  the entry references one, rewritten inline otherwise) and AcroForm gains `/SigFlags 3`
  (SignaturesExist | AppendOnly), as `sign()` does. The name is `Timestamp_n`, counted
  past the names of existing named signature fields — `sign()`'s policy for `Signature{i}`.
  Basis: ISO 32000-2 §12.8.5, the document timestamp dictionary.
- A new Sig field is a form change: like `sign()`, linking requires permission bits 6 and
  4 (`check_signing_permissions`). Under a fill-forms-only `/P` the timestamp still

- Linking is also skipped when no first page resolves; `/AcroForm` is not a dictionary

title: M2: a Separation /All colour paints every colourant, gray 1 − tint on screen (ISO 32000-2 8.6.6.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4438.

**The need.** A Separation colour space whose colourant is the special name `/All` was drawn through its alternate space and tint transform, as if `All` were an ordinary spot ink. With `[/Separation /All /DeviceCMYK <</FunctionType 2 /Domain [0 1] /C0 [0 0 0 0] /C1 [1 0 0 0] /N 1>>]`, `0.5 scn` filled a box light cyan. `All` is the space registration targets and crop marks are drawn in, so they took whatever colour the writer's tint transform gave instead of the neutral "every ink" colour they stand for.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §8.6.6.4: the name All "shall refer collectively to all colourants available on an output device"; painting operators "shall apply tint values to all available colourants at once", and on an additive device such as a monitor the tint values "shall be complemented by subtracting from 1". So on screen a tint t is the gray 1 − t on R, G and B, whatever the alternate space and tint transform say. The same clause has `None` paint nothing.

**The change** (vendored `hayro-interpret` patch 66, `src/color.rs`)
- **Reading the space.** `Separation::new` notes when the colourant name is `All`. The vendored comment saying `All` was ignored is gone.
- **Converting.** `Separation::convert_f32` writes the gray 1 − t for each tint of an `All` space and never evaluates the tint transform. The tint is clamped to [0, 1] first, and a NaN tint becomes black through the existing saturating cast.
- **Reach.** Fills, strokes, images in the space and shadings in the space all convert through this function. The print path (`engine::print_raster`) renders an RGB raster through the same `PageRenderer`, so it follows too. There is no CMYK or separations output path on `main` to change.
- **Unchanged.**
  - `/None` still paints nothing.
  - Any other colourant name still goes through its alternate.
  - A DeviceN space that names `All` keeps its alternate: §8.6.6.4 gives the name this meaning for Separation spaces, and DeviceN's own…

author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

title: fix(forms): a multiline field rejects a glyph wider than the field
author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

`TextBox::fits` (crates/forms/src/appearance.rs) checked a multi-line value against the height only. Wrapping breaks long words by character, so the one way a wrapped line can be wider than the box is a single character wider than the box. title: Reject non-finite numbers in XFDF coordinate lists on import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

XFDF import no longer accepts non-finite coordinates. `csv()` in `crates/xfdf/src/lib.rs` (lines 274-276, used by `annot_from_xml` at 924-928) parses coordinate lists with `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts `nan`, `inf` and `infinity`. `annot_from_xml` only checked the list length, so these values reached `/Rect`, `/L`, `/CL`, `/Vertices`, `/QuadPoints` and `/InkList`. The writer prints a non-finite real as `0`, so a saved file held an invented 0 coordinate.

Fix: `csv()` now returns an empty list when any entry is non-finite, so the list is treated like any other unusable one. An annotation with a bad `rect` is skipped, as already happens for a malformed rect. A line, callout or vertex list with a bad value is left out. The annotation is still imported if its `rect` is valid. Import still succeeds, and other annotations in the file are imported normally.

No existing issue is linked for this change.

## How you verified it

- Regression tests `tests::import_skips_annotations_with_non_finite_coordinates` and `tests::import_drops_non_finite_numbers_from_every_coordinate_list` fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfdf non_finite`).

title: M6: an editable combo box takes a typed value (ISO 32000-2 Table 233 Edit)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4450.

**The need.** A combo box with the Edit flag (`/FT /Ch /Ff 393216`: Combo plus Edit) opened only its drop-down list on the page. There was no text box, so a value that isn't one of the options could not be typed, and keystrokes went nowhere. `form_fill` already took such a value headlessly, so only the page editor was missing.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:2020 §12.7.5.4: a combo box "may be accompanied by an editable text box in which the user can type a value other than the predefined choices, as directed by the value of the Edit bit in the Ff entry". Table 233, bit 19 Edit: "If set, the combo box shall include an editable text box as well as a drop-down list; if clear, it shall include only a drop-down list."

**The change** (`ui-egui::forms_ui`)
- **The text box.** An editable combo box opens a single-line text box over the field, styled like a text field's editor, as well as its list. The list works as before.
- **Committing.** Enter, Tab or a click away commits the typed text as `Edit::SetFieldValue` with `FieldValue::Choice`, which is the path `form_fill` and the list already use. Undo, field scripts and appearance regeneration therefore work as they do for any fill. A pick from the list still sets an option and discards the typing.
- **Shown text.** The text box starts on the shown text of the picked option, not its export value. Typing an option's shown text picks that option, because the engine maps it to the export value.
- **Without Edit,** a combo box is unchanged: a drop-down list only, and typing does nothing.
- `draft_text` (the editor's starting text) is also used where a re-opened draft is refreshed after an accepted edit (`editing.rs`), so the same field shows the same text either way.
- DoNotSpellCheck (bit 23) needs nothing, since the text box does no spell checking. CommitOnSelChange (bit 27) is already met, because a pick commits at once. MaxLen doesn't apply to choice fields.

title: M6: with NeedAppearances, check boxes and radio buttons draw their /MK caption (ISO 32000-2 Table 224)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4453.

**The need.** A form that sets `/NeedAppearances true` leaves its widgets' appearances to the viewer. PdfCraft already redraws text and choice fields for such forms (#3470), but check boxes and radio buttons kept the appearance streams the file carries. In the reported form, a check box whose `/MK /CA` is ZapfDingbats `4` (a check mark) has a filled square as its `/AP /N /Yes`. Checked, it showed the filled square, while most other readers show the check mark. A copy saved by PdfCraft looked the same.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 §12.7.3, Table 224, `NeedAppearances`: "A flag specifying whether to construct appearance streams and appearance dictionaries for all widget annotations in the document". It is deprecated in PDF 2.0, where appearance streams are required, but PDF 1.x forms still set it.
- Table 192, `/MK /CA`: "The widget annotation's normal caption, which shall be displayed when it is not interacting with the user". Unlike the other push-button entries, `CA` may be used with any type of button field, check boxes included.
- §12.7.5.2.3: the state is selected by `/AS` (or `/V`), and the standard example draws the on state as ZapfDingbats `(4) Tj`.

**The change** (`pdfcraft_forms::with_field_appearances_cached`, display copy only)
- **When.** When the form sets `/NeedAppearances`, every check box and radio button widget that has an `/MK` dictionary is drawn in its current state, whatever appearance the file gives it. This uses the `button_state_shown` path merged in #4368:
  - the `/MK /BG` background and `/MK /BC` border (in the `/BS` width and style);
  - when on, the `/MK /CA` character in ZapfDingbats (`4` check, `l` dot, `8` cross, `u` diamond, `n` square, `H` star; `4`, or `l` for a radio button, when there is none), in the `/DA` colour, at the `/DA` size or sized to the box.
- **When not.** A widget with no `/MK` keeps its own appearance, since nothing describes how to redraw it. Without `/NeedAppearances` nothing…

title: M7: opt-in grant for installed fonts that permit editable embedding
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

Refs #2077 (the engine and automation half of it).

A font the user selects only enters a PDF if its name table declares an open licence. That rules out the faces most office documents are set in (Arial, Calibri, Verdana…), even though their vendors declare editable embedding in OS/2 `fsType`, which `validate()` already enforces for every font. So a paragraph set in a subset of Calibri can't get a new character in Calibri, and bold/italic can't switch to the installed Calibri Bold.

This adds an explicit, opt-in grant instead of changing the default:

- `pdfcraft_fonts::embedding::FontGrant { OpenLicence (default), InstalledEmbeddable }`, re-exported from the engine.
- `validate_document_input(bytes, grant)`: under `InstalledEmbeddable` the open-licence declaration is not required. Everything else stays: the `fsType` gate in `validate()` (restricted 0x0002, preview & print 0x0004 and bitmap-only 0x0200 are refused), the excluded families and the Adobe-authored check apply under either grant.
- `Edit::RegisterTextFont { page, bytes, grant }`, `text::register_text_font(…, grant)` and `text_fonts::discover(roots, grant)` carry it through.
- Automation: `text_font_files` and `text_font_import` take `installed: true` (default false).
- The desktop app passes the default, so its behaviour is unchanged. The setting the issue proposes ("Allow installed fonts that permit embedding", off by default, with a one-time licence notice) and `.ttc` collections are left for a follow-up, so this PR stays reviewable and doesn't touch the i18n catalogues.

Nothing is bundled, shipped or committed: the font is read from the user's machine at the user's request, and the user answers for its licence when sharing the PDF (AGENTS.md §1.4).

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts -p pdfcraft-edit -p pdfcraft-engine -p pdfcraft-automation -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` on Rust 1.95: clean except two lints already…

title: M2: the standard 14 fonts fit the Euro to its standard width (WinAnsi 128; ISO 32000-2 §9.6.2.2)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4458.

**The need.** A standard 14 font named without embedding and without `/Widths` drew the € so wide that the next glyph ran into it. "€5", "€€" and "a€b" collided in Helvetica, and more in Times-Roman and Times-Bold. The advances were right. The € itself was drawn up to 722 units wide in a 500-unit advance.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §9.6.2.2: for the standard 14 fonts, `Widths` and `FontDescriptor` were optional in PDF 1.0 to 1.7, and a PDF processor "shall have these fonts, or their font metrics and suitable substitution fonts, available". So the substitute has to fit the standard metrics. Annex D, Table D.2: the Euro is WinAnsiEncoding code 200 (octal), that is 128. §9.2.4: the advance places the next glyph, so a glyph wider than its advance overlaps it.

**The change** (`vendor/hayro-interpret`, patch (67))
- **Root cause.** The metrics were never the problem: the renderer's standard metrics and the writer's `Std14` table both already give the Euro 556 (Helvetica family), 500 (Times) and 600 (Courier), and every other WinAnsi name has a width in both. The renderer fits a substitute glyph to the standard width only when it knows the substitute's own advance. For the bundled CFF substitutes, `StandardFontBlob::advance_width` returned `None`, so their glyphs were drawn at their own width whatever the metrics said. Their € is 667 to 722 units wide.
- **The fix.** `CffFontBlob::advance_width` reads a glyph's advance from its charstring (through the same `draw` call and scale as the outline, with a null pen). `StandardFontBlob::advance_width` uses it for CFF, as it already used `hmtx` for OpenType substitutes. Glyphs are now fitted to the standard width both ways, as the existing rule for an exact standard font already said.
- **Other glyphs this touches.** Logged on all codes 32 to 255 in the twelve text faces, the substitute advance differs from the metrics only for: € (Helvetica, -Bold, -Oblique, -BoldOblique, Times-Roman, -Bold, …

title: Add an Android app shell and a file-dialog seam
author: tzhazuma
body:
This adds `apps/printcraft-android`: a Gradle project that hosts the existing egui UI inside an `android-activity` window, plus one small seam in the shared UI crate — PrintCraft is the one Craft app whose file dialogs live *inside* `crates/ui-egui` instead of a host hook.

PrintCraft is pure Rust (the parser, interpreter, rasteriser and text extractor are its own crates), so the only platform code here is the Java picker bridge.

## What the shell does

- **Entry point** — builds as `libmain.so`, loaded with `System.loadLibrary`; `android_main` is the usual `android-activity` entry.
- **The shared-crate seam** — `rfd` 0.17 does not compile for Android at all (its platform traits go unimplemented there) and `arboard` has no Android backend. `crates/ui-egui/src/fd.rs` is a drop-in: on every platform `rfd` supports it re-exports `rfd`'s types unchanged, and on Android it is a lookalike with the same builder API that asks a `Host` the app shell installs. The call sites become `crate::fd::{FileDialog, AsyncFileDialog}` — mechanical and platform-neutral; `rfd` and `arboard` move behind `not(target_os = "android")`, and the two `arboard` calls get an Android twin that returns `None` (the app's own snapshot still pastes).
- **Pickers** — the Storage Access Framework answer: an open copies the picked document into `<filesDir>/import/`; a save reserves a path in `<filesDir>/export/` and a worker publishes the finished file to the `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT` destination once it stops growing. File ▸ Open uses the *asynchronous* dialog the UI already polls, so the answer arrives on a later frame and the app's own `process_picked → open_path` opens it — no dialog code was rewritten.
- **Phone start-up state** — Read mode with the left tool panel closed, 40 pt hit targets, no zoom, plus a command-palette long-press (top 9%, 500 ms) that runs the app's own commands.

title: M12: honor named-month XFA data pictures on read and write
author: wireless89
body:
## What this changes

An XFA field bound with `date{DD MMM YYYY}` currently leaves `18 Oct 2026` as the script's raw value and as the widget text, even when its edit picture is `MM/DD/YYYY`. Filling a new date then writes ISO text such as `2026-10-19` into the datasets instead of the declared `19 Oct 2026`.

`data_date_letters` recognizes only numeric month tokens when checking that a data picture contains a whole date. Accept the existing `MMM` and `MMMM` tokens too. The shared converter already reads and writes English month names; this connects those existing capabilities to data binding. A year and an original `D` or `DD` day-of-month token remain required. Check the original picture before normalization maps weekday `E`/`EE` to `d`/`dd`. Weekday-only and unsupported month runs do not qualify.

## How you verified it

Latest refresh: retained the new upstream OCR progress entry and placed the older XFA entries below it. Resolved only progress-log/status-line conflicts; the XFA source and tests are unchanged. All scoped checks below passed again on main `9e90b2a5`.

2026-10-27 integration: rebased onto main `9e90b2a5` after the XFA module split; all scoped checks below were repeated. The date change now lives in `crates/xfa/src/data/dates.rs`, preserving the upstream module split and public re-exports. Removed the introduced unquoted blank line in the roadmap status block.

title: M3: copied text keeps one line per baseline, reading order for turned lines, letters for ligatures
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4467.

**The need.** Copy and `text_extract` broke text into more lines than the page shows.
- **One baseline, several lines.** Runs drawn too far apart to merge, or in different sizes, or out of order each got a line of their own: `08` / `first` / `second` for a row that reads `08 first second`.
- **A turned line at the end.** A word set upwards in a row came out after the whole page.
- **The ligature character.** A glyph named `/fi` in the font's encoding came out as U+FB01, so a pasted `office` was not the word, and Find missed it.

**The basis.**
- **Ligatures.** ISO 32000-2 §9.10.3: its ToUnicode example maps the ff, fi and ffl ligature glyphs to "a Unicode scalar value for each character in the ligature: LATIN SMALL LETTER F (U+0066) LATIN SMALL LETTER I (U+0069) for f i". 4 of 5 other readers copy the letters.
- **Lines and turned text.** ISO 32000-2 does not say how untagged text forms lines (§14.8.2.6.2 leaves word and line finding to the processor), so this follows most other readers:
  - a baseline reads as one line, left to right (4 of 5);
  - columns stay apart (5 of 5);
  - a turned line reads in its place (4 of 5).

**The change** (`crates/render/src/text.rs`)
- **Ligature letters** (`draw_glyph`, `ligature_letters`). U+FB00–U+FB06 become their compatibility decomposition: ff, fi, fl, ffi, ffl, st, st. Nothing else is normalised, and the glyph keeps its one box.
- **One line per baseline** (`arrange`, step 4; `same_line`). The next block joins the line just read, with a space at the gap (more than `WORD_GAP` heights), when:
  - its first line's baseline is within a fifth of a height of that line's;
  - it starts to that line's right;
  - it is less than `SAME_LINE_GAP` = 8 heights of the taller run away.

  Baselines are compared as the em box bottom less a fifth of its height, so a 9 pt label and a 14 pt word on one baseline match.
- **What stays apart.**
  - Two columns: a column of several lines is read only after the c…

title: M3: Find matches ligatures and words split by a line-end hyphen
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4469.

**The need.** Find and `text_find` missed two kinds of words people search for:
- **Ligatures.** `office` was not found where the page draws `of` + an fi ligature glyph whose text is U+FB01. Fonts that name the glyph `/fi`, and ToUnicode maps or `/ActualText` that give U+FB00–U+FB06, all produce this.
- **Divided words.** `example` was not found where the line ends in `exam-` and the next starts with `ple`, and neither was `exam-ple`.

**The basis.**
- **Ligatures.** ISO 32000-2 §9.10.3 maps ligature glyphs to the letters they stand for ("a Unicode scalar value for each character in the ligature: LATIN SMALL LETTER F (U+0066) LATIN SMALL LETTER I (U+0069) for f i"). Every other reader I compared (5 of 5) finds `office`.
- **Divided words.** §14.8.2.3 has writers mark a hyphen that only divides a word as U+00AD, but untagged PDFs rarely do. ISO is silent on how search treats a U+002D at a line end, so this follows most other readers: 4 of 5 find `example`.

**The change** (`crates/render/src/text/search.rs`, used by Find, `text_find` and Search & Redact's word list)
- **Ligatures.** U+FB00–U+FB06 read as their letters (ff, fi, fl, ffi, ffl, st, st) in both the page and the query, before case folding and whether or not the search is case-sensitive.
  - Each letter stays owned by its glyph, so the highlight covers the ligature.
  - Nothing else is normalised (U+FB13, full-width letters and circled digits stay distinct).
- **What counts as a divided word.** A glyph divides a word when:
  - it ends its line with a hyphen (U+002D, U+00AD or U+2010);
  - a letter comes before the hyphen, in the same glyph or in the glyph before it on the line with no word gap;
  - the next line starts with a letter.
- **How it is searched.** When a page has such a glyph, it is searched in three readings:
  - as written, where the break is a space, as before;
  - joined, with no hyphen and no break: `example`;
  - kept, with the hyphen but no break: `exam…

title: M7: synthetic bold and italic per range in the text's own face
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

Bold and italic in a face that has no bold or italic variant. Today, a paragraph set in an embedded face can only become bold by switching to a standard family (`BlockStyle.bold` swaps the face to Helvetica/Times/Courier-Bold), and a range can't become bold or italic at all unless it is already in a standard family. Word processors solve this by drawing the variant synthetically; this does the same, per range or for the whole paragraph:

- `RangeStyle::synthetic_bold` / `synthetic_italic` and the same on `BlockStyle` (`Option<bool>`).
  - **Bold:** the run is filled, then stroked in its own fill colour, `SYNTHETIC_BOLD` = 1/30 em wide (`2 Tr`, round joins, no dash). Every fill colour space carries over (`g/rg/k/cs/sc/scn` → `G/RG/K/CS/SC/SCN`).
  - **Italic:** the text matrix's vertical axis is sheared along the baseline by `SYNTHETIC_SLANT` = tan 12° (`slanted()`).
  - The face, advances and wrapping stay as they were. `Some(false)` takes either away again, also where a word processor drew it (a stroke in the fill colour; an outline in another colour stays).
- Automation: `text_edit` takes `synthetic_bold` / `synthetic_italic` for the paragraph and in each `ranges` item.

Three reading fixes were needed so a slanted run survives the next edit. Each one also applies to word-processor PDFs that use sheared italic today:

1. **`same_plane` compares the vertical axis upright.** A sheared word was another "plane", so `Plain *words* here` fell apart into three paragraphs after one italic word.
2. **`upright_height`: a line's size and `k` come from the height square to its baseline**, not from the length of the slanted axis. A 12 pt slanted word read as 12.27 pt.
3. **A run's box (`rect`/`frame`) is its cell standing upright on the pen's path**, as an italic face's box is its advance. The rise still moves along the real axis (group moves use `Ts`).
   - The parallelogram's bounding box was wider by the slant. That made the next rewrite stretch the ru…

title: M3: web and email addresses written as page text open like links (#4207)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4207.

**The need.** Many PDFs, among them office exports and scans run through OCR, show web and email addresses as plain page text with no link annotation over them. In PdfCraft such an address did nothing: no link cursor on hover, nothing on a click (#4207). The reader expects it to open the way a link does.

**The basis.** No clause of ISO 32000-2 covers this. The standard defines link annotations (§12.5.6.5) and URI actions (§12.6.4.8), not reading addresses out of page text. The basis is the issue, and this follows the rules PdfCraft already applies to addresses that come from documents.

**The change**
- **Detection** (`engine::text_links`, new).
  - `find_text_links` runs the detector Create links from URLs already uses (`pdfcraft_annot::links::find_urls`) over a page's extracted text, through `PageText::find_with`. It returns each address with one view-space rectangle per line.
  - It finds `http://` and `https://` addresses, `www.` addresses (opened as `https://`; `find_urls` itself keeps `http://` for the links it writes into documents) and email addresses (`mailto:`).
  - Sentence punctuation (`.` `,` `;` `:` `!` `?`) and brackets around an address are left out. Text that only looks like an address (`example.com`, `https://x`, `user@localhost`, `a@b.c`) is not found.
  - Work is capped: at most 512 addresses per page, and nothing is searched on a page of more than 200,000 glyphs.
  - `TextLink::covered_by` tells when a link annotation lies over the address. The annotation is what the document asks for there, so it wins.

  - A click goes through `request_document_url` with `LinkOrigin::Link`. That is the same `links::document_url` check (http, https and mailto only, hidden characters, mail parameters, length) and the same confirmation as a link annotation.

title: M3: relative links resolve against the document's base URI, and a link is active only in its QuadPoints (ISO 32000-2 Tables 176, 211)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4473.

**The need.** Two kinds of link didn't work the way the document describes them:
- A URI action written as a relative address (`page.html`) in a document whose catalog gives `/URI << /Base (https://example.com/base/) >>` was refused as "the address isn't a complete web or email address".
- A link whose `/QuadPoints` cover only the first word of a line opened from anywhere in its `/Rect`.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.8, Table 211. `Base` is "the base URI that shall be used in resolving relative URI references. URI actions within the document may specify URIs in partial form, to be interpreted relative to this base address."
- ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.5, Table 176. `QuadPoints` are "n quadrilaterals in default user space that comprise the region in which the link should be activated". The region is `Rect` when the entry "is not present, or the PDF processor does not recognise it, or if any coordinates in the QuadPoints array lie outside the region specified by Rect".

**The change**
- **Base URI** (`render::link_area::resolve_uri`, used by `inspect`).
  - Inspection reads the catalog's `/URI /Base` (a string of at most 8 KiB) into `DocInfo::uri_base`.
  - A URI action without an RFC 3986 scheme is resolved against the base by RFC 3986 §5, through the `url` crate. It is already in the tree, and `engine::links` checks addresses with it. `LinkTarget::Uri` then carries the resolved address.
  - The base is used only when it is an `http`/`https` address that names its host as written (`https://host/…`). The result must keep the base's scheme.
  - An address that already has a scheme is never touched.
  - An address or base with control characters, or whitespace other than a space, is left as written. The URL rules would drop those characters and read `java\nscript:` as a scheme.
  - The resolved address then goes through the same `links::document_url` check and confirmation as before.

title: M7: a moved text box's drag preview shows the box alone (#4464)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4464.

**The need.** Add a text box over something on the page (a filled shape, a picture, other text), finish it, then drag it. The preview that follows the pointer carries a copy of whatever the box covered at its first place. It looks as if the page content is being moved, though on release only the text moves.

**The basis.** A pure display fix; no PDF semantics change. The cause: during a move (#1488), the moving pixels were cut from the page's own raster inside the item's box. That raster has the item *and* everything under it.

**The change**
- **`pdfcraft_edit::isolate_content`** (new). On a copy of the document, leaves item `index` alone on its page: `/Contents` becomes the item's own stream, `/Annots` goes. The item's stream already starts from the page's initial graphics state (`place_tagged` closes everything drawn before it), so it draws the same on its own.
- **`Document::added_content_alone`** (new). Renders that copy with `RenderConfig { transparent: true, .. }`. Read-only, like `added_content_preview`: working bytes, dirty state and undo history are untouched.
- **`MoveBackground`** (`ui-egui`). Renders both rasters per gesture: the page without the item (as before) and the item alone. The moving pixels now come from the item-alone raster, mapped from its first box onto the dragged one, so what it covered stays where it is. The preview shows once both rasters are in; until then, or if either render fails, the item stays put while dragged, as before. The same holds for a picture resized by a corner and for the frames after release while the page re-renders.

title: fix(sign): let a writer raise the catalog /Version after signing
author: akbartriasno
body:
## What this changes

A later revision that raises the catalog's `/Version` no longer makes an earlier signature show as invalid with "document structure". `/Version` may now be added or raised after signing. A signed version may not go back or be dropped, and one that does not read as a version may not change at all.

PAdES LTV writers add the `/DSS` and lift `/Version` in the same revision. ISO 32000-2 §7.7.2 provides the entry so a version can be raised by an incremental update. `/Version` was not in the catalog keys that may change after signing (`change_kind` in `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs`), so the signature the DSS protects was judged altered.

Follow-up to #4133, which let `/Extensions` gain declarations. That file shape still failed on `main` after #4133, and the only remaining cause was `/Version`.

I hit it on an invoice signed with VIDA (PAdES, ECDSA P-256) and then stamped with an Indonesian e-Meterai (second signature, `ETSI.CAdES.detached`). Its revisions are: the first signature; a DSS revision that adds `/DSS`, `/Extensions /ADBE` and `/Version /1.7`; the e-Meterai signature, whose revision also adds `/Extensions /ESIC`; and a last DSS update. poppler's `pdfsig` reports both signatures valid, and the PdfCraft 0.13.0 release flagged the first one. With this change the same file validates in a local build. I searched issues and PRs (DSS, LTV, Extensions, ESIC, signature, document structure) and found only #4133 and #3440; #3440 keeps the same catalog key list, so it does not cover this.

title: feat(ui): Ctrl+Shift+→ / ← open the next / previous PDF in the document's folder (#4267)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Ctrl+Shift+→ / ← (⇧⌘→ / ⇧⌘← on macOS) now open the next / previous PDF in the same folder as the open document, also under File ▸ Open next / previous PDF in folder.

Acrobat has no command like this, so it follows the request in #4267: only files ending in `.pdf` (any case) in the document's own folder, no subfolders, folders or files whose name starts with a dot (macOS `._name.pdf` resource files would otherwise show up on some drives). The order is natural rather than plain alphabetical, so `scan2.pdf` comes before `scan10.pdf`, which is what a folder of numbered invoices needs; happy to switch to plain alphabetical if you prefer. The file opens through the normal open path, in its own tab, so the document you came from keeps its tab and any unsaved changes, and a file that is already open just comes to the front. At the first or last PDF, or for a document that was never saved to a folder, nothing opens and a notice says why. Text fields keep the shortcut for extending the selection, and the web build has no folder, so the command is disabled there. The folder is read once per keypress. Before this, Ctrl+Shift+→ also turned the page (the canvas ignores the modifiers on the arrows); plain → and Ctrl+→ still do. Same with Ctrl+Shift+→ nudging a selected comment, which Ctrl+→ still does. If you'd rather keep these keys free, happy to switch the shortcut.

Left out: following the file manager's own sort order (each one keeps it differently) and toolbar buttons. Also open: whether stepping should replace the current tab instead of adding one; I kept the tab so nothing unsaved is ever at risk, but that piles up tabs on a long folder. A password-protected or unreadable PDF stops the stepping there, since stepping starts from the active tab; remembering the last file tried would get past it, if you want that.

title: fix(xfdf): a multi-select choice holding ", " survives Export/Import Data as XML, CSV or text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #4484.

XML, CSV and text keep a multi-select list's choices in one cell joined by ", ", and the import split that cell at every ", ", so an option with a comma in it ("Smith, John") came back as pieces that match nothing and the field was refused. The cell is still split at every ", " first, and if every piece is one of the field's options (export value or display text, as `set_value` accepts) that is the result, so every cell that was accepted before gives the same result as before. Only when some piece isn't an option is the cell read as a run of the field's own options separated by ", " (a small left-to-right pass over the cell, trying each option at each reachable position, comparing both the export value and the display text), which needs no change to the export format. If the cell isn't made of the field's options either, it is split as before, so what used to be refused is still refused.

title: M6: radio buttons sharing an on state are exclusive unless RadiosInUnison (ISO 32000-2 Table 229)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4488.

**The need.** A radio group can give several buttons the same on state, for example `Yes`, `Yes`, `No`. When its RadiosInUnison flag was clear, clicking one `Yes` turned on every `Yes`. Clicking the other `Yes` then changed nothing, so it could never be chosen on its own. The value model named only the on state, so `set_states` turned on every widget that had it, and the click decided "already selected" from `/V`, which is the same for both buttons.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- Table 229, RadiosInUnison: "If clear, the buttons are mutually exclusive (the same behaviour as HTML radio buttons)".
- §12.7.5.2.3, after EXAMPLE 2: "If it is not set, at most one radio button in a field shall be set at a time."
- §12.7.5.2.4: `/V` holds the on state of "whichever child field is currently in the on state", and where `/V` and `/AS` differ "the value of the AS key shall be used". With two `Yes` buttons, `/V` is `/Yes` whichever is on, and only the widgets' `/AS` tells them apart.
- Table 229, NoToggleToOff: if clear, "clicking the selected button deselects it".
- Table 230: with `/Opt`, on states may be positions (`/0`, `/1`, …) to tell buttons with the same export value apart. Those buttons already have distinct on states, so they are unaffected. The `/Opt` handling from #532 (`state_for`, `export_of`) is unchanged.

**The change** (`forms`, `ui-egui::forms_ui`, `automation`)
- **One button, not one state.** A new `FieldValue::Widget(i)` turns on widget `i` of a check box or radio group, as a click on it does. A click, Space and the arrow keys now send it.
- **Exclusive unless in unison.** In a radio group without RadiosInUnison, `set_states` turns on only that widget, and every other widget gets `/AS /Off`. A check box, or a radio group with RadiosInUnison, still turns on every widget that shares the state (§12.7.5.2.3 EXAMPLE 2).
- **Setting by name.** `FieldValue::Radio(Some("Yes"))` (form_fill with a string, reset, scripts, imported d…

title: M6: a check box's kids with different on states tick one at a time (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.2.3, Table 230)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4495.

**The need.** A check box field can have several widget kids with different on states, for example `A` and `B`. PdfCraft could only ever tick the first one. With `A` ticked, clicking `B` cleared the field, so `B`'s tick flashed and vanished. With nothing ticked, clicking `B` ticked `A`. There were two causes:
- The click sent `Check(f.value.is_empty())`, a field-wide toggle. Whichever kid was clicked, a field that was on turned off.
- `write_value` always turned on the first kid's on state, for `Check(true)` and also for a named state such as `"B"`.

Reset to `/DV`, script value changes and FDF/XFDF import all went through `Check(bool)`, so they ticked the first kid too.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- §12.7.5.2.3: a check box field "represents one or more check boxes". `V` "holds a name object representing the check box's appearance state", and where `V` and `AS` differ "the value of the AS key shall be used".
- Table 230: `/Opt` has an entry "for each widget annotation in the Kids array", so that check boxes can be "checked independently, even if they have the same export value".
- §12.7.5.2.3 EXAMPLE 2: kids that share an on state are checked together.

**The change** (`forms`, `ui-egui::forms_ui`, `xfdf`, `automation`)
- **Clicking a kid.** Clicking a kid that is off sends its on-state name, so that kid (and any kid sharing its state) turns on and the others turn off. Clicking a kid that is on clears the field. "On" is the kid's own `/AS`, read by the new `Field::widget_on(i)`. Space on a focused kid does the same.
- **Setting the value.** In `write_value`:
  - a name (`Text`/`Radio(Some)`, an on state or an `/Opt` export) ticks the kids with that state;
  - `Check(true)` keeps the kid that is on, else takes the first;
  - the yes/no words work as before.
- **Stored values.** The new `Field::check_box_value(Option<&str>)` maps a stored value (`/DV`, a script's value, imported data) to the state it names. Reset, `apply_script_ch…

title: M8: after Apply redactions, Save asks where and proposes the name with _Redacted (protect.redact-filename-suffix)
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

After Apply redactions, Save wrote the redacted document over the file it was opened from. The reference app's help page "Removing sensitive content from PDFs" (section "Redact sensitive content") says that after Apply: "The Save As dialog is displayed. Specify a filename and location. The suffix “_Redacted” is appended to the filename." (https://web.archive.org/web/20221231010434/https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/removing-sensitive-content-pdfs.html).

- The view counts the Apply redactions steps in effect (`DocView::redactions_applied`). While the count is above 0, Save on the desktop works as Save As: it asks where, and the dialog proposes `<stem>_Redacted.pdf` (for example `contract_Redacted.pdf`) in the document's folder. The `.pdf` extension is matched in any letter case. The web build downloads under that name, and a host page (`?host=parent`) receives the save as a Save As.
- Undo of an Apply redactions step takes one off the count and Redo adds it back. Revert, Reload and a successful desktop save set it to 0, so the next Save writes in place. The web build keeps the count after a download, so later downloads also carry the `_Redacted` name. A name that already ends in `_Redacted` keeps one suffix.
- Save after Apply redactions no longer writes over the opened file without asking. Sign's save proposes `{stem}_signed.pdf` the same way (`crates/ui-egui/src/sign_ui.rs`).
- The naming helper, `redacted_file_name`, is in `pdfcraft-redact` (re-exported by the engine). The `redact_apply` tool's result now carries the same name in `save_as`, for `doc_save`'s `path`. `doc_save` without `path` still writes in place.

title: M6: a value the validate action rejects is dropped and the field keeps its value
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4498.

**The need.** A text field whose validate action rejects the typed value (a range it is outside, or a script that sets `event.rc = false`) showed the message but kept the rejected text in its editor and pulled focus back to it on Tab or a click. The user could not move on to the next field without first fixing the text by hand. Every other reader tested (5 of 5) shows the message, puts the field back to its previous value and lets focus move on.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 Table 199: the `/V` action "shall be performed when the field's value is changed. This action may check the new value for validity." It doesn't say what a reader does with a rejected value, so this follows the behaviour all five other readers share. The engine already treated a rejection as no change: the edit runs on a copy, so the document and undo history were untouched. Only the interface held on to the text.

**The change**
- **`forms`:** a new `FormError::Rejected` tells a validate refusal apart from the others. It covers the range check and a custom validate script returning `event.rc` false; its message is the range's text or the script's alert. A keystroke (format) refusal stays `Invalid`/`Format`, since it is about the typing.
- **`engine`:** `EditError::is_rejected_value()`.
- **`ui-egui` (`editing.rs`):** `apply_edit` now wraps `try_apply_edit`, which returns the error. When typed text is rejected by the validate action, the draft is dropped instead of reopened. The field shows its kept value, and the editor that Tab or a click opened on the next field stays open. A format refusal still reopens the editor with the text (#166).
- **Unchanged:** the message still shows as the same notice ("Fill in G_range failed: …"), with the script's alert as its text. Alerts are notices throughout the app today, and #4306 is the place to change that. A Save, Print or Export pressed with the rejected text still stops after the message, so the user sees the field reve…

Follow-up to #3970, from CodeRabbit's last finding there, which came after the fix commit and was still open when the PR merged.

After PdfCraft's own title bar or edges hand a move or resize to the desktop, `release_after_desktop_grab` gives egui back the button release the compositor kept. body:

Part of #4340 (the viewer half). The headless half, `page_render` and `render_preview`, is #4494. The two PRs are independent and touch different files.

Although #3943 cleared the AcroForm `/V` (and masked `/AP /N`) of Password-flagged text fields when writing a document to disk, editing an XFA `<passwordEdit/>` field also mirrors the typed value into the XFA `datasets` stream (`xfa_sync_datasets`), and incremental updates could retain earlier edits' datasets or masked appearance streams in the document overlay. title: M9: name a laid-out XFA form's signature fields by their SOM path, so other viewers find the signature
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

A dynamic XFA form signed in PdfCraft showed no signature when opened in another viewer. That viewer listed the box as an unsigned field.

**Cause.** That viewer lays a dynamic form out again from its template. It then finds a signature by the field's SOM path, such as `form1[0].Page1[0].Approval[0].Signature[0]`. PdfCraft named its generated signature field by the short template name (`Signature`), so the signature it wrote was never found. `existing_fields` (formerly `signed_fields`) already reads other viewers' signatures by that path; this makes PdfCraft write its own the same way.

**The fix.**
- An unsigned signature box of a laid-out form is now written as a field hierarchy that spells its SOM path (`form1[0]` > `Page1[0]` > `Approval[0]` > `Signature[0]`).
- The parents are generated fields marked `/PCXfaNode` and shared by the boxes of one subform.
- A new layout (`rerender`) drops them along with the other generated fields, and `strip` removes the key.
- Other generated fields keep their short names.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and tests on `pdfcraft-xfa`, `pdfcraft-engine`, `pdfcraft-automation` and `pdfcraft-ui-egui`: 2,414 passed.
- **New tests**, each seen to fail with the fix reverted:

title: Fix FormCalc Round overflowing to infinity for large values
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

FormCalc `Round()` no longer returns infinity for large values with decimal places.

Cause: `Round` computes `(a * k).round() / k` with `k = 10^places`. When `a * k` exceeds f64::MAX, the product becomes infinity, so `Round(1e300, 12)` returned infinity instead of 1e300.

Fix: `Round` checks whether the scaled product is finite. If it is not, it returns `a` unchanged, since a value that large has no fractional digits to round. Ordinary rounding is unchanged.

title: Match email addresses followed directly by a hyphen
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

The email redaction pattern in `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs` (lines 216-221, `email`) missed an address followed directly by a hyphen.

**Cause:** The domain scan in `email` accepts `-` anywhere, including after the TLD. For `bob@example.com-`, the TLD check saw `com-`, which is not all alphabetic, so it rejected the address. In `bob@example.com-bob2@example.org`, the match started at `example.com-bob2@example.org` and left `bob@` unredacted.

**Fix:** After the domain scan, `email` ends the domain at a hyphen that directly follows the TLD letters of the last label. This happens in two cases: only hyphens follow (the domain ends there), or the scanned run is followed by `@` (the hyphen starts another address's local part). The tests cover the trailing-hyphen cases and `bob@example.co-uk`.

This PR has no linked issue (found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:216-221`).

title: M12: an XFA date field keeps what its patterns don't read as typed, and reads its own patterns first
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

An XFA date field refused much of what another viewer accepts. Typing `10/18/2016` into a field with only a display picture got "Invalid date/time ... should match format yyyy-mm-dd". So did `xyz`, and ISO dates typed into a field with a different edit picture. It also stored some dates wrongly: `18OCT16` in a `date{YYYYMMDD}|date{DDMMMYY}` field was taken by the generic lenient parse and kept as typed, where the field's own DDMMMYY pattern gives 2016-10-18.

On a synthetic form in another viewer, a typed value is:
- stored as an ISO date when one of the edit picture's patterns reads it;
- otherwise kept exactly as typed, with no error.

This is also XFA 3.3's rule: text that can't be canonicalized through the edit picture is taken as canonical and stored as entered (chapter 4, "Rule 2, Input Parsing a Data Value Using a Picture Clause", p. 163).

ISO text (`2016-10-18`, `20161018`) is kept as typed and shown through the display picture.

**The change:**
- The XFA layout marks generated date fields `/PCXfaDate true`.
- The forms layer (`af::Actions::keystroke` and `format_value`) never refuses text for such a field. It shows a date only for a value that already is one: in the field's pattern, or ISO. Anything else is shown as typed rather than read loosely into a date the data doesn't hold.
- The engine tries the edit picture's alternatives (#3552's `typed_date`) *before* the field's own format, not only after a refusal. A date one of its own patterns reads is therefore never mistaken for another.
- `strip` removes the key with the other private keys. Ordinary AcroForm date fields are unchanged.

Fixes #3466 (both parts the issue was split into: the right-click menu, and a double-click that opens).

title: edit: preserve gap-drawn spaces and indents in subset fonts via /ActualText (#4229)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Fixes #4229

## Summary
When editing text in a subset font that has no `' '` glyph (`metrics.encode(text)` returns `None` for strings containing `' '`), `source_show` emits each `' '` as a numeric `TJ` positioning adjustment (e.g. `[-330] TJ`) while painting non-space words with `(word) Tj`. Previously, reading the rewritten line back via `text_lines`, `text_blocks`, or `PageText` relied solely on inter-word horizontal gap inference, which collapsed multi-space runs (`"  "`) into a single `' '` and dropped leading/trailing space indents (`"  ab"`) because no glyph preceded or followed the `TJ` displacement.

## Changes
- **`crates/edit/src/text.rs`**:
  - `source_show`: When `metrics.encode(text)` is `None` and the emitted operators paint at least one glyph (`out.iter().any(|op| op.is("Tj"))`), wrap the emitted operators in `/Span << /ActualText (...) >> BDC ... EMC` carrying the logical text (`bidi::to_logical` after `indic::to_logical` when `metrics.visual_order`).
  - `interpret`: Retain numeric-only `TJ` operators inside an open `/ActualText` replacement (`actual.iter().any(Option::is_some)`) so leading/interior/trailing space adjustments inside the span are included in the merged `Shown`'s origin `tm`, `rect`, `frame`, and `extra_ops` (while `ink` remains restricted to the non-space words' glyph ink boxes), and filter out any zero-glyph non-`actual_text` entries before `positioned_tracking` in case an `/ActualText` `BDC` is unclosed.
  - `rewrite_block_from`: When `reuse && m.encode(" ").is_none()`, pass `tw + stretch` directly to a single `source_show` call per line rather than splitting the line at spaces into separate per-word calls.

  - `assign_subset_space_fonts` / `rewrite_styled_block`: Assign any space on a wrapped row whose font resource cannot encode `' '` to the nearest preceding or following glyph-bearing character on that row (copying both style index and font resource in two linear passes), so spaces betwee…

title: M12: run an XFA signature field's preSign scripts before it is signed and postSign after
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA signature fields' `preSign` and `postSign` scripts never ran. DA 31, for one, has a pair on each of its 35 signature boxes:
- **preSign** shows an "Electronic Signature Notice", sets the box's date field to today and makes it read-only.
- **postSign** clears and unlocks that date again if the box turns out unsigned.

Signed in PdfCraft, those boxes got no date and the date field stayed editable.

**The change:**
- `Session::run_sign_event(doc, field, SignEvent::Before | SignEvent::After)` runs a signature field's `preSign` or `postSign` scripts as one undoable step, through the existing `Edit::XfaEvent`. It returns `Ok(false)`, changing nothing, when there are none: not a laid-out XFA form, JavaScript off, no such field, or no such script. `clickable_som` becomes `scripted_som(…, activity)`, so both share the lookup.
- **What gets signed is what the signer saw.** A `preSign` script changes the form right before it's signed, so the signer has to see those changes first.
  - **In the app,** `preSign` runs as signing begins (`start_signing`): its message and what it changes show under the Sign dialog before the signer confirms. The step stays pending (`presign`). If signing ends without a signature (the dialog cancelled, the save picker cancelled, or signing failed and the dialog closed), it is taken back by `settle_presign`, checked every frame, provided it is still the last edit (`Document::undo_depth`). `postSign` runs once signed; its change comes after the signature, so it is left to save.
  - **Through `sign_document`,** the scripts run only when the caller asks (`run_form_scripts: true`): an agent hasn't seen the page. The result's `form_scripts` lists every field `preSign` changed (`changed`: field, value and read-only before and after), with `before_signing`, `after_signing`, the scripts' `alerts` and `errors`, and `unsaved_changes`. Not asked, the scripts don't run and `form_scripts.skipped` says the box has them.

title: M7.5: crop an added image by more than half from one side
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

An added image's crop was capped at 45 % **per side**, in three places:
- the Edit panel's 0–45 % drag values;
- `content_update` (`< 0.5`);
- the drawing matrix, which silently cut any larger value down to 0.45.

So keeping only the right third of a picture (70 % off the left) wasn't possible. `added_images_rotate_flip_and_crop_as_drawn` even set 0.5 and passed only because of that silent clamp.

The limit is now **per axis**: a side may trim up to 95 %, as long as left + right, and bottom + top, keep at least 5 % (`AddedImage::MIN_CROP_KEEP`).

- `AddedImage::crop_valid` is the rule for input. `content_update` refuses anything else, saying what is allowed, and its schema says so too.
- `AddedImage::clamp_crop` brings a crop read from a file (untrusted) into range. Non-finite or negative sides trim nothing. An axis that trims too much keeps its two sides' proportion. The matrix uses it, so it no longer needs its own `max(0.05)`.
- Edit panel: each side's drag value goes up to 95 % minus its opposite side. A new crop is still applied once, when the drag ends.

title: fix(forms): enforce mutual exclusion when RadiosInUnison is clear (#4488)
author: YusufMntm
body:
Fixes #4488

## What this changes

Resolves high-priority bug #4488 where clicking one of two radio buttons that share an on state turned both buttons on when `RadiosInUnison` was clear.

Per ISO 32000-2:
- **Table 229 (RadiosInUnison)**: "If clear, the buttons are mutually exclusive (the same behaviour as HTML radio buttons)."
- **§12.7.5.2.3**: "For radio buttons, the same behaviour shall occur only if the RadiosInUnison flag is set. If it is not set, at most one radio button in a field shall be set at a time."
- **§12.7.5.2.4**: Where `/V` and `/AS` differ, "the value of the AS key shall be used. The two `Yes` buttons share `/V /Yes`, and only their `/AS` tells them apart."

If a target widget is provided, only that widget is turned on; otherwise (headless/automation), prefer keeping the currently active widget or select the first matching widget. title: M3: links run Named, Hide and ResetForm actions and their /Next chains (ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.11, §12.6.4.12, §12.7.6.3, §12.6.2)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4524.

**The need.** A link annotation with a named action, a hide action or a reset-form action only showed "This PDF uses the unsupported {s} action." and did nothing. A link whose `/Next` chained more actions ran none of them. Push buttons already run all three, so a page-turn, show/hide or clear-form link did nothing while the same action on a button worked.

**The basis.**
- **Named actions:** ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.12, Tables 215–216. NextPage, PrevPage, FirstPage and LastPage are actions processors "shall support". For any other name, "if the viewer does not recognise the name, it shall take no action". The Table 215 NOTE also allows nonstandard named actions. GoBack and Print are supported because documents use them widely.
- **Hide:** §12.6.4.11, Table 214. `/T` is an annotation reference, a fully qualified field name, or an array of them. `/H` defaults to true.
- **ResetForm:** §12.7.6.3, Tables 241–242. It resets the listed `/Fields`, or all fields except them when bit 1 of `/Flags` (Include/Exclude) is set.
- **`/Next`:** §12.6.2, Table 196 and its Note 1. Chained actions run in order, "each followed in turn by any actions specified in its Next entry, and so on recursively".

**The change**
- **Reading** (`render::inspect`). `LinkTarget` gains `Named(name)`, `Hide { fields, hide }` and `ResetForm { fields, exclude }`. `Link` gains `next`, the chained actions in the order they run. The action parser was split out of `link()` so the head and each chained action are read the same way.
  - **Hide.** A widget or field reference names its field by the fully qualified name, built from `/T` up the `/Parent` chain (bounded, with a seen-set). A reference to an annotation that belongs to no field is skipped. If nothing is left, the action stays unsupported and the existing notice shows.
  - **ResetForm.** A field reference is read by its `/T`, exactly as push buttons read it today (`pdfcraft_forms::button_action`). An entry that names no f…

title: XFA: ready events run in the other viewer's order, and layout:ready again after a new layout
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #3589:** its commits (and a merge of `main`) are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

An XFA form's ready events now run when and in the order another viewer runs them. On a synthetic form, that viewer logged this on opening: the field's `initialize`, then the root subform's; the root's `form:ready`, then the field's; the root's `layout:ready`, then the field's; then `docReady`. When a click showed a hidden section that took the form to a second page, it ran `layout:ready` again for both objects, and the root's script read the new page count.

A second synthetic form, with a calculated field and two more fields, placed the calculations: they run once `initialize` has run, before `form:ready`, as XFA 3.3 orders them (the form ready event fires after the calculations and validations; p. 213, p. 388, pointed out by @mtlcl410). It also showed the siblings' order: `form:ready` runs in the exact reverse of `initialize`'s order (the root, then its fields last to first), while `layout:ready` runs the root and then its fields in document order.

Before this change, PdfCraft:
- ran `initialize` parents first, and `docReady` interleaved with `initialize`, before the form was laid out;
- never ran `form:ready` (`<event activity="ready" ref="$form">`);
- ran `layout:ready` once, on opening, so a form that reacts to its own layout (page numbers, sections that appear) saw only the first one;
- kept the open-time page count for a whole event, so `xfa.layout.pageCount()` read the old count after a re-layout.

Changes, all in `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`:
- `on_open` runs `initialize` children first (`children_first`, siblings and an object's own events keeping their order), then the calculations, then `form:ready` in the reverse of that order (`objects_reversed`, an object's own events keeping theirs), then `layout:ready` and `docReady` parents first. When a ready script wrote a value, the calculations run once more…

title: M3: a GoToE link opens the PDF embedded in the document at its destination (ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4529.

**The need.** A link with an embedded go-to action (`/S /GoToE`) only showed "This PDF uses the unsupported GoToE action." The PDF it pointed to was attached to the same document, and the Attachments panel could already open it in a tab. The link that goes to it did nothing.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.4, Tables 204–205:
- **The action.** A GoToE action is "similar to a remote go-to action but allows jumping to or from a PDF file that is embedded in another PDF file". `/T` is a target dictionary that locates the target relative to the source. `/D` is the destination in the target.
- **The target dictionary.** `/R /C` means the target is a child of the current document. It is named by `/N`, "the name of the file in the EmbeddedFiles name tree". For a file attachment annotation, `/P` gives the page (an integer, or a named destination) and `/A` the annotation (its index in `/Annots`, or its `/NM`).
- **PDF only.** "Embedded go-to actions work only for files of Type PDF."

**The change**
- **Reading** (`render::inspect`). A new `LinkTarget::EmbeddedGoTo { source, destination, new_window }`. `source` is the existing `AttachmentSource`: `Document { key }` for `/N`, or `Annotation { page, index }` for `/P` and `/A`.
  - **Keys.** `/N` is converted and spent from the text budget the same way the EmbeddedFiles keys in `DocInfo::attachments` are, so the two match exactly.
  - **Annotations.** `/P` can be a page number or a named destination of this document. `/A` can be an index or an `/NM`, which is looked up in that page's `/Annots`.
  - **Destination.** `/D` is read by the GoToR reader's destination code, now split out as `remote_destination`. A target document's explicit destination names its page by number.
  - **Not followed.** The parent (`/R /P`), a nested target path (`/T` inside `/T`), a target under another root document (`/F`) and any malformed target stay `Other("GoToE")`, so the existing notice shows.

title: M6: list boxes show and pick the option /I names, and a single-select list shows one value
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4531.

**The need.** Some list boxes highlight the wrong rows, and some picks don't survive a save:
- A list box with `/Opt [[(1) (One-A)] [(1) (One-B)] [(2) (Two)]]`, `/V (1)` and `/I [1]` highlighted both One-A and One-B. 5 of 5 other readers tested highlight One-B alone.
- Picking One-B wrote `/I [0]`, so the file reopened as One-A.
- A list box without MultiSelect but with `/V [(TW) (JP)]` highlighted two rows.

**The basis.**
- ISO 32000-2 Table 234, `/I`: it "shall be used when two or more elements in the Opt array have different names but the same export value", and "if the items identified by this entry differ from those in the V entry …, the V entry shall be used".
- Table 233, MultiSelect: "if clear, at most one item shall be selected". An array `/V` on a single-select list is therefore malformed. The other readers split on how to show it, with no majority, so the tie-break is the first value only.

**The change**
- **Two commits, one per fix.**
- **Which rows are selected** (`forms`): a new `Field::selected` holds the selected option positions.
  - `/I` is used when it is an array of integers, strictly ascending, in range, and names exactly `/V`'s export values.
  - Otherwise `/V` decides, and each value selects the **first** option with that export value. This is what the writer records when it is given only an export value, so a pick still shows the same row if another tool drops `/I`. A test pins it.
  - List appearances highlight by position, not by export value.
- **Picking** (`forms`, `ui-egui`):
  - `FieldValue::ChoiceIndices` picks options by position.
  - A value given as display text (`"One-B"`) now records that option's position in `/I` as well.
  - List-box clicks, Ctrl/Shift-clicks, the arrow keys and the unbaked overlay all work by position. A pick writes `/V (1)` with `/I [0]` or `/I [1]`, and it survives a save and reopen.

title: Tests: XFA calculation tests no longer fail when the machine is busy
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

`hundreds_of_xfa_calculations_run_in_one_engine_within_the_open_budget` (engine) and `hundreds_of_xfa_calculations_open_and_recalculate_within_their_budgets` (automation) fail at random under load. The scripts of an opening or a change share a 3 s wall-clock budget (`OPEN_BUDGET_MS` in `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`), and a click's scripts share 5 s (`EVENT_BUDGET_MS`). Each script has 1 s or 3 s (`timeout_for`), and the engine has 10 s to start (`ENGINE_START_LIMIT`). On a busy machine the tests go past one of these limits, and the calculations they check are skipped: "The form's scripts were stopped: the scripts took more than 3 seconds; 73 more were skipped". The tests now run with the time limits raised 100-fold, and the engine test also counts the script engines started (a per-thread counter, as `tint_transform_runs` in #2812). - `Session::with_xfa_time_scale(factor)` and `Automation::with_xfa_time_scale` multiply each of these limits for a test. The default is 1.
- `pdfcraft_js::xfa_session::engines_started()` counts the script engine threads started on the calling thread.
- Three more tests that failed the same way under load run with the limits raised: `repeated_xfa_print_buttons_work_through_tools_and_after_reopen` ("the script engine took longer than 10 s to start"), `xfa_scripts_run_for_buttons_and_field_changes_through_tools` and `xfa_data_import_adds_and_removes_rows_of_a_dynamic_form`.

title: XFA: a form saved with its pages is laid out when it requires dynamic rendering, unless signed
author: EricKaden
body:
Split out of #1566 by @EULArule, who asked for it to be taken over in two PRs. The other part, required fields, is #4537.

## What this changes

Some viewers save a dynamic XFA form with its pages drawn. They leave no `/NeedsRendering` and keep only the signature boxes as AcroForm fields. PdfCraft took such a file for a static form, because it has fields, and showed its pages as they were saved: nothing on them could be filled in, because the other fields live in the template.

Such a form is now laid out from its template when its configuration says `<dynamicRender>required</dynamicRender>`, as #1566 did. Designer writes that value for a dynamic form, as it writes `forbidden` for a static one (#3180).

**Signed forms are left as saved.** If one of the signature boxes is signed, the form opens exactly as before. Laying it out would replace the pages the signature covers. PdfCraft would then report that signature as broken, since the open-time layout is an appended revision. Another viewer would see changed pages after the signature too. #1566 noted this ("a signature made before the layout is reported as invalid because the pages changed"). Making a signed form fillable needs a save that keeps the signed revision's pages, the design question in #4309, so it is not attempted here.

The same rule is in both places that decide:
- `pdfcraft_render::inspect`, which sets `DocInfo::xfa`;
- `pdfcraft_xfa::is_dynamic`, which `render_into` checks.

The xfa crate reads only the configuration packet (`config/acrobat/acrobat7/dynamicRender`), never the same element in the template or data. It finds signed boxes by walking the AcroForm's fields, at most 32 levels deep and 10 000 fields.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and tests on `pdfcraft-xfa`, `pdfcraft-render` and `pdfcraft-engine`.
- New fixture `saved_with_pages_shell(render, signed)`: a form saved with its pages drawn, its signature box the only field, and the configuration's `dynamicRe…

body:
## What this changes

Comment Properties had one opacity for a whole comment: a text box's see-through background took its text and border with it, and a rectangle marking an area on a plan couldn't have an opaque line over a faint fill (a tester's request).

- **Comment Properties** shows an opacity per part where a comment has parts: a text box, typewriter text or callout its **Text**, **Border** and **Fill opacity**, a rectangle, oval, polygon or cloud its **Line** and **Fill opacity**. The rows stay put for the kind of comment; a part that isn't drawn (no fill, no border) is greyed. Lines, drawings and the rest keep one **Opacity**.

title: XFA: a field's change scripts run for every keystroke and may rewrite what it enters
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4359:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

Another viewer runs an XFA field's `change` scripts for every keystroke, before the value is committed. The script sees the keystroke and may rewrite what it enters. PdfCraft ran them only once, when the value was committed, so a field couldn't refuse a typed character. Forms rely on this: a day count that keeps only digits, or a date field that refuses typing and points to its picker.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form:
- Typing `a` then `b`: `change=[a] new=[a] prev=[] sel=0-0`, then `change=[b] new=[ab] prev=[a] sel=1-1`.
- A backspace: `change=[] new=[a] prev=[ab] sel=1-2`.
- Select-all and `q`: `change=[q] new=[q] prev=[a] sel=0-1`.
- A script that rewrites `xfa.event.change` changes what is entered: `toUpperCase` gives `ABC`, and stripping non-digits from `a1b2` gives `12`.

The change spans four crates:
- **js:** `XfaEvent` carries a keystroke's `change`, `selStart` and `selEnd` (`newText` and `prevText` as before). `XfaOutcome::change` is the `xfa.event.change` a change script ends with. FormCalc reads `$event.change`, `selStart` and `selEnd`, and may assign `$event.change`.
- **engine:**
  - `Session::field_keystroke(id, name, widget, &Keystroke)` runs the field's change scripts for one keystroke, through `xfa::keystroke`. Each script sees what the one before it entered. The call returns what the keystroke enters, or `None` when the field has no change scripts.
  - The scripts run on a copy of the document. Only what they enter, and what they show or ask for, is kept: message boxes and beeps go out as usual. Their other changes come when the value is committed, which runs the change scripts again as before. Nothing in the document changes per keystroke, so typing leaves no undo steps.
- **ui-egui:** the field editor reads each keystroke off its text before and after (`keystroke_between`: the shortest repl…

title: XFA scripts: the bare event is named as the field event, of type Field, and its target has numPages
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #3575:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

XFA scripts can use two event objects: `xfa.event` and the bare `event`. Until now PdfCraft named the bare `event` by the XFA activity (`click`, `change`, …), gave it no `type`, and its target (the document, from #3575) had only `exportDataObject`. Scripts that branch on `event.name` or `event.type`, or read `event.target.numPages`, took the wrong path.

After this PR the bare `event` in an XFA script has:

- **`event.name`**: the matching field event's name.
  - Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form: a click script sees `Mouse Up`, a change script `Keystroke`, an exit script `Blur`.
  - Taken from the event table in the public JavaScript API reference for PDF forms, not measured: enter → `Focus`, mouseDown → `Mouse Down`, mouseUp → `Mouse Up`, mouseEnter → `Mouse Enter`, mouseExit → `Mouse Exit`, calculate → `Calculate`, validate → `Validate`.
  - Activities with no field event in that table (initialize, ready, layoutReady, docReady, preSign, postSign, and the rest) keep their XFA name, as before.
- **`event.type`**: `Field` (measured) for the field events above. Activities that keep their XFA name have no `type`, as before.
- **`event.target.numPages`** (measured): the document's page count. It is a read-only getter that calls the same function as `xfa.layout.pageCount()`, so the two always agree. `exportDataObject` is unchanged.
