title: Forms: a script that fails says so in one notice per action, with a button to the JavaScript console
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4306:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

A form script that fails no longer fails silently. Before this, the error from a failing AcroForm JavaScript or XFA JavaScript/FormCalc script (a button whose click script throws, say) went only to the JavaScript console log. Nothing in the app said so, and the button just looked broken.

Now, when scripts run for something the user did (a button's click and the calculations it sets off, a field change, an XFA form's opening) and one or more of them failed, the toast shows one notice for that action: "A script in this form failed: <first error>". The error is clipped to its first line, at most 120 characters. Under it is a **JavaScript Console** button, which runs the existing `tools.js_console` command.

- **One notice per action.** Every script output the app is handed for one action goes through `handle_js` once, and the notice quotes the first error. A button's own outcome and what its changes then set off (calculations, validations) used to reach the app in two batches, one of them a frame later. They now arrive as one batch, so a click whose button and calculation both fail gives one notice. Failing again while the notice shows (clicking a broken button twice) restarts that notice; it doesn't queue a second one.
- **It waits its turn.** The notice joins #4306's queue after the action's own messages, since the error is what ended the script. At most one failure notice waits, and it is the latest action's. If another notice replaces it before its time, it is shown again once the toast is free, like #4306's left-out count.
- **It doesn't get in the way.** It is the existing non-modal toast. Its button takes focus only when clicked, so typing into a field goes on while the notice shows. It stays 6 seconds, longer than the toast's usual 3.5, because it has a button to reach, and it stays up while the pointer is over it. Clicking the bu…

title: fix(forms): respect /I when options share export values and single value on single-select (#4531)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4531

- **Respect /I when options share export values:** According to ISO 32000-2 Table 234 (/I Entry), when multiple options in Opt have the same export value or when choice field values are represented as an array, /I specifies the zero-based indices of the selected options. When /I is present and its export values match /V, /I determines the exact selected rows rather than highlighting every row sharing the export value. If /I is absent or differs from /V, /V takes precedence.
- **Lenient single-select list box array /V handling:** In single-select list boxes (without MultiSelect flag), if a malformed PDF specifies an array /V, lenient viewers highlight and keep only the first item (row) and on save write a single string /V.
- **Field indices & automation/UI parity:** Added indices: Vec<usize> to Field and FieldValue::ChoiceIndices(Vec<usize>). Both UI selection (click/drag, combo box dropdown, arrow key navigation) and headless automation ( orm_fields and  orm_fill) track and set exact option indices so duplicate export value options can be unambiguously inspected and manipulated headlessly and interactively.
- **Appearance generation:** Appearance stream generation for list boxes now highlights only the exact selected rows via resolved choice indices.

title: M14: a drag across checkboxes checks or unchecks them all (#1662)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #1662.

Press on a checkbox and drag over the ones next to it: each checkbox the pointer goes over takes the first one's new state, until the button is released. This is the behaviour VectorCraft (storytold/vectorcraft#1600) and PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#3521) use, and it follows their design: the first box toggles when the drag starts, its new state is kept in the egui context, and every box the drag crosses takes it.

- **One place.** The change is in `widgets::checkbox`, which every labelled checkbox goes through (clippy.toml disallows the others). Preferences, dialogs and panels all get it at once.
- **A click is unchanged.** It still toggles one box, through egui's own click.
- **The drag belongs to the checkbox.** The checkbox now senses drags as well as clicks (`Response::interact`). Without that, a drag in a scroll area (Preferences, most dialogs) would scroll the panel. A press that moves and comes back before the release toggles the box once, not also as a click.
- **`changed()` still works.** `interact` returns a new response, so the change a click made is carried over to it. Every box the drag sets is marked changed too, so callers that act on `changed()` (comment filters, field properties, the optimizer) see drag changes as they see clicks.
- **Left alone:** a disabled box, a box clipped out of view (rows scrolled under the OK row), and a box under another layer (a menu open over a dialog).
- **The drag ends with its own release.** The state counts only while the box the drag started on is still being dragged, so a release on a frame that draws no checkbox (a dialog closing) leaves nothing behind.
- **Not changed: the page checkbox on Organize Pages thumbnails** (`checkbox_without_text`). It keeps taking clicks only, because a drag that starts on it moves the page, as a drag on the rest of the thumbnail does. The issue also limits this feature to the interface's own checkboxes, not PDF form fields, which this doesn't t…

title: M14: Ctrl+Tab can go through the tabs most recently used first (#2063)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2063.

Next tab and Previous tab (Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab; ⌃Tab on macOS) can now follow the order the tabs were last shown in, as Windows' Alt+Tab does, instead of their order on screen. It is a choice in **Preferences ▸ Documents and view ▸ Next tab and Previous tab**: *In tab order* (the default, unchanged from #1551) or *Most recently used first*.

As the issue asks:
- **One press goes back to the tab shown before.** Switching between two of five open files is a single Ctrl+Tab each way.
- **While Ctrl is held, the order of the first press holds.** Tab again goes on to the tab shown before that one, and Shift+Tab steps back in the same order. Letting go of Ctrl makes the tab you landed on the most recent one.
- **Without Ctrl** (the command palette, `command_run`), each step is a cycle of its own, so Next tab goes back and forth between the two most recent tabs.

How it works:
- **The history is in a module of its own, `tab_cycle.rs`.** It is pure logic with unit tests, so the UI files only get small hooks.
  - `RecentTabs` keeps the open tabs most recently shown first, keyed by document id rather than position, so moving and closing tabs keep it right.
  - A tab closed during a cycle drops out of it, and one opened during it comes last.
  - A tab opened in the background, never shown, comes after every tab that was.
  - Home takes no part, as in tab order. From Home, Next tab goes to the most recent tab.
  - Combine files takes part like a document.
- **Every frame records the tab showing** (`note_shown_tab`, at the start of `shortcuts`, before the modal early returns), so a tab shown by a click or by opening a file counts. Ctrl held keeps the cycle going.
- **The choice is saved** as `tab_cycle` (`"tabs"` / `"recent"`) and can be set with `set tab_cycle recent` over the control channel.

title: refactor(ui): panel docking uses craft-ui's shared Workspace and DockCommand
author: aiongg
body:
## What this changes

Panel docking uses craft-ui's shared docking (`craft_ui::docking::Workspace`, `DockCommand`) instead of pdfcraft's own copy of the workspace model, its validation, its actions and the `ui.dock` parameter parser. craft-ui, craft-quit and craft-docpath are pinned to craft-libs 6e7f285, which includes the docking follow-ups. craft-print stays at 666c358.

- `Workspace` is `craft_ui::docking::Workspace<Panel>`. `ui.dock` parameters are parsed as `DockCommand<Panel>` and applied through it.
- App-side: `Panel`, `permissions`, the default layout, `tools_on_right`, `saved_split_path`, the bare docked Tools panel from #2244, the settings key and `persist`/`restore`. `validate` adds the document-view rules to craft-ui's checks. `set_visible` skips panels that already have the requested visibility.

- The layout stays a split tree, which `tools_on_right` and `saved_split_path` rely on: `new_dock_zones` is off and `validate` refuses any dock.
- pdfcraft has no panel lock, so `restore` clears a settings file's `locked` flag and saved arrangement before validating.
- craft-ui's group and floating-window labels go through `i18n::t` in sentence case, like the existing ones.

Behaviour users will notice comes from craft-ui: tab groups are dragged by their bar, floating windows have a title bar, double-click minimizes a group, and the group menu has more items. `ui.dock activate` on a hidden panel shows it. title: fix(links): support Named, Hide, ResetForm actions and /Next chaining (#4524)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4524

- **Named actions:** Links with `/S /Named` now support standard page navigation actions (`NextPage`, `PrevPage`, `FirstPage`, `LastPage`, matching push button support in `canvas.rs`). Unrecognized or non-navigation named actions (such as `Save`, `Print`) take no automated action without confirmation.
- **Hide actions:** Links with `/S /Hide` now show or hide the target fields (`/T`) and their children according to `/H` (default `true` hides, `false` shows). Targets can be field names, arrays of names/references, or indirect references (resolved by qualified name).
- **ResetForm actions:** Links with `/S /ResetForm` now reset the specified fields (`/Fields`) or all fields except the specified fields (`/Flags` bit 1 exclude flag). When `/Fields` is omitted or empty, all fields in the document are reset to their default values (`/DV`). When `/Fields` is present in include-mode but none of the targets resolve, no fields are reset.
- **`/Next` action chaining:** An action dictionary can chain subsequent actions through `/Next` (either a single action dictionary or an array of actions, per ISO 32000-2 §12.6.2 Table 196). Inspector parses and collects chains into `LinkTarget::Sequence(...)` up to `MAX_ACTION_CHAIN = 64` actions with cycle detection via `HashSet<ObjectId>`. Visited nodes are globally bounded by `MAX_ACTION_VISITS = 1024` to prevent exponential DAG fanout.
- **Headless automation and UI tooltips:** `doc_info` serialization exposes `Named`, `Hide`, `ResetForm`, and `Sequence` link targets. In the UI, hover labels display user-friendly translated tooltips for named, hide, and reset-form actions.

title: M4: Duplicate pages can give the copies' form fields names of their own (#2228)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2228.

When a page with form fields is duplicated, the copies keep the fields' names. Fields of one name are one field, so filling in a copy fills in the original too. The issue asks for an option that gives the copies names of their own, so a form can be extended page by page.

- **New command: *Duplicate pages with new field names*** (`page.duplicate_renaming_fields`), in the Pages menu, the command palette, and Organize pages ▸ Insert next to *Duplicate pages*. Every copied field gets the first free name, `Text1` → `Text1-1`, then `Text1-2`, and so on. That is the rule Combine files and Insert from file already use (`FieldConflicts::Rename`). Nested fields are renamed at the colliding node, so their children keep their names.
- **Plain *Duplicate pages* is unchanged.** It still keeps the names, as does a Ctrl-drag copy in the page grid. That stays the default because the copies are the document's own fields, and renaming them changes what the form exports.
- **Headless:** `page_duplicate` takes `field_conflicts: "merge" | "rename"`, defaulting to `merge`, so existing callers behave as before.
- **It says what it did**, like Insert from file:

  - the undo step is labelled *Duplicate pages — 1 field renamed* or *— fields renamed*, and it is one step.

Internally:
- `organize::duplicate_pages_with(doc, pages, at, FieldConflicts)` returns the renames. `duplicate_pages` is now its `Merge` wrapper.
- `Edit::DuplicatePages` carries `field_conflicts`, as `Edit::InsertPagesFrom` already does. Its existing call sites pass `Merge`.

An XFA button click through `run_javascript` (`js_run` with `field`) and the `form_set_script` tool returned `take_js_output`, the document's whole waiting script output, as their own. title: M2: an image whose data stops short keeps its height and lines up with its soft mask (#2780)
author: hazeliscoding
body:
## What this changes

An image or soft mask whose data stops short of its `/Height` now keeps that height. The rows present are drawn where they belong. The missing samples are raw zeros, decoded like the rest, the way 1-, 2- and 4-bit samples already were and the way Chrome draws them.

8-bit data was cut to the rows present (`fix_image_length` in vendored hayro-interpret, and a copy of the rule in `rgb_via_lookup`):

- A short image was drawn short. Its missing rows were left unpainted, and its `/SMask` was squeezed into the rows it had. On the scanned pages in #2780, the colour layer's data ended early, so the full-height text mask was squeezed with it and the text came out as a faint ghost.
- A short soft mask was stretched over the whole image.

Every path now pads the raw samples before `/Decode` and before any inversion: the 8-bit fast path, the per-pixel and colour-table paths, both mask paths, and the colour-key `/Mask`. `rgb_via_lookup` no longer keeps its own copy of the length rule.

**A sample cap, because padding expands data.** Every sample an image says it has is now padded and then expanded (to `u16`, then `f32`). `image_size_ok` caps only pixels, so a few bytes of a many-ink image could ask for a huge allocation: a 32-ink image of one byte took 4.2 GB and 11 seconds at 2^25 pixels, and would ask for 32 GiB at 2^28.

Images and masks are now also capped at 2^30 samples (`image_samples_ok`, four a pixel at the pixel limit). The cap is checked in `decode_context` before anything is expanded. An image over it is left out with `ImageDecodeFailure`. No gray, RGB or CMYK image within the pixel limit is affected.

Fixes #2780. The cause is the one @imamehoiho-oss found in the issue. Their file wasn't attached, so this is fixed and tested on synthetic images. `vendor/README.md` records this as hayro-interpret patch 67.

**What other viewers do.** I checked Chrome's PDF viewer (pdfium) as a black box, with synthetic 1 × 4 DeviceGray images whose data stops a…

author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4359:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the commit "M12: a radio group's own enter and exit scripts run when the focus enters or leaves the group".

## What this changes

An XFA exclusion group, a set of radio buttons, can have enter and exit scripts of its own, as each of its buttons can. #4359 runs a button's enter and exit whenever it gains or loses focus, but PdfCraft never ran the group's. A form that reacts to the focus entering or leaving the group as a whole, for example to show a hint or check a choice when leaving, did nothing.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form (exclusion group `grp`, buttons `r1` and `r2`, all logging their events):
- **Clicking into the group:** `grp enter` → `r1 enter`.
- **Moving to the other button:** `r1 exit` → `r2 enter`. The group's scripts don't run.
- **Leaving the group:** `r2 exit` → `grp exit`.

PdfCraft now does the same:
- **engine:** `Session::field_focus_crossing(id, name, widget, focus, crossing)`.
  - When `crossing`, a radio button's focus change also enters or leaves its group. Enter runs the group's enter before the button's; exit runs the group's exit after the button's.
  - A move between two buttons of one group passes `crossing = false`, so only the buttons' scripts run.
  - `Session::field_focus` keeps its meaning (the focus crosses the field) and now includes the group.
  - Each object's scripts are an edit of their own, so one that changes nothing still leaves no undo step. Which of them run is decided before any does, so an exit the value's change already ran is still skipped.
- **xfa:** `has_focus_scripts` counts a group's own enter and exit scripts, so a form whose only focus scripts are a group's still runs them.
- **ui-egui:** the app's focus tracking passes `crossing = false` when the focus moves between two widgets of the same radio field.

title: fix(automation): page_enhance_camera reports the XFA data it could not write
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Builds on #4559. Until #4559 merges, this diff also shows its commit.

## What this changes

`page_enhance_camera` applies its page replacement through `Session::enhance_camera_page_at`, outside the tool's edit helper. On a dynamic XFA form the edit writes the form's data, and the warnings for values it could not write ("XFA data not written for fields whose data node holds structured content: ...") went to the document's script output. - `command_run` with `ocr.enhance_camera` returns them the same way, because it calls the tool.

`command_batch` runs each step through `command_run`, so it reports what each step's tool reports. The engine's actions run in a session of their own (`actions::run_on`), so their output does not stay in the automation session.

title: M2: a 16-bit image with an odd byte count is drawn instead of crashing the page
author: hazeliscoding
body:
> **Stacked on #4561.** Both PRs add a numbered patch to the same line of `vendor/README.md`, so this one is based on #4561's branch to avoid a conflict there. Only the last two commits are new here. I'll rebase onto `main` once #4561 merges.

## What this changes

A 16-bit image whose data has an odd byte count crashed the page render. `get_components` (vendored hayro-interpret) paired the bytes with `chunks(2)` and read `v[1]`, which panics when the last chunk has a single byte:

```
panicked at vendor\hayro-interpret\src\x_object.rs:1171:48:
index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 1
pdfcraft-cli: renderer crashed on page 1
```

That's from the released 0.13.0 CLI. It happens in two cases:

- **Data cut short mid-sample:** 5 bytes for a 1 × 4 image.
- **A complete image followed by one stray byte:** for example a line end counted in `/Length`. A 1 × 1 image with 3 bytes is enough.

The samples are now read in whole pairs of bytes (`as_chunks::<2>()`, which needs no indexing). A last byte without its pair reads as a 0 sample, as an incomplete 1-, 2- or 4-bit sample already does (`BitReader::read` returns `None`, and `get_components` reads that as 0). So a half sample means the same thing at every bit depth:

- A stray byte after a complete image becomes one extra sample, which is dropped with the rest of the excess.
- An image whose only data is that one byte is still drawn, as a 1-bit image with any data is.

`vendor/README.md` records this as hayro-interpret patch 68. I found it while reading `get_components` for #4561, and no issue or PR mentions it.

title: M2: a colour-key mask keys the raw samples of an image with an inverted Decode
author: hazeliscoding
body:
> **Stacked on #4565, which is stacked on #4561.** All three add a numbered patch to the same line of `vendor/README.md` (67, 68, 69), so they form one chain to avoid conflicts there. Only the last commit is new here. I'll rebase onto `main` as the others merge.

## What this changes

A colour-key `/Mask` is now tested against an image's raw samples, as ISO 32000-2 §8.9.6.4 specifies, also when the image's `/Decode` is inverted.

The 8-bit fast path in vendored hayro-interpret inverts an image with an inverted default `/Decode` in place. `resolve_alpha` then tested the key against the inverted bytes, so it masked the wrong samples. This affects complete images, not only short ones.

I checked a 1 × 4 DeviceGray image with `/Decode [1 0]`, `/Mask [0 0]` and data `00 FF 00 FF` on a blue page:

| | rows |
|---|---|
| Chrome's PDF viewer (black box) | masked, black, masked, black |
| released 0.13.0 | white, masked, white, masked |
| this PR | masked, black, masked, black |

`decode_raster` now records whether the fast path inverted the data in place, and the colour key turns the data back into raw samples (255 − c) before comparing. There's no copy of the image. `vendor/README.md` records this as hayro-interpret patch 69.

CodeRabbit raised this on #4561. That PR is about short data, and this bug was already there for complete images, so it gets its own PR.

title: automation: compare canonical root components exactly and test roots-only escape confinement (#4003)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What & Why

Closes #4003 (completing the remaining two hardening items after `be0ec707` / #4289):

1. **Exact canonical component comparison in `file_access::same_component` (`crates/automation/src/file_access.rs`):**
   - Previously, `same_component` compared all path components on Windows with `a.to_lowercase() == b.to_lowercase()`. Because `Root::open` and `file_access::resolve` already canonicalize existing directories on disk via `std::fs::canonicalize`, normal path components inside an existing Windows directory already carry their exact on-disk casing, while `str::to_lowercase()` applies Unicode case-folding that NTFS does not (for example folding U+212A KELVIN SIGN `'K'` to `'k'`, allowing a sibling folder `inK` outside read root `ink` to pass the containment check on Windows) and ignores per-directory case sensitivity (`FILE_CS_FLAG_CASE_SENSITIVE_DIR`).
   - `same_component` now compares canonical `Component::Normal` components by exact `OsStr` equality (`a == b`) while keeping Windows `Prefix::Disk` and `Prefix::VerbatimDisk` drive letters ASCII case-insensitive (`u8::eq_ignore_ascii_case`), matching `std::path::Path::starts_with` in `--root` mode.
2. **Escape confinement loop under both `--root` and `AutomationRoots` (`crates/automation/tests/it/hostile_args.rs`):**
   - `no_tool_escapes_the_root` now runs its full tool/property/escape-vector sweep under both `--root` (`Automation::with_root`) and roots-only (`Automation::with_automation_roots`) confinement modes, including `..` and symlink traversal anchored at `root` as well as Windows device pipe paths.

title: XFA: check box and radio exit scripts wait for the focus to leave
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4563 (and so #4359) and #4369:** their commits are included here until they merge. This PR's own change is the commit "M12: check box and radio exit scripts wait for the focus to leave". The merge commit before it resolves #4359 against #4369 in `on_changes` (#4369's change and click order, with #4359's record of the exits that ran, per object), which whichever of the two merges second needs anyway.

## What this changes

A check box or radio button keeps the focus while it is clicked. Measured black-box in another viewer on synthetic forms, it runs its exit scripts once, when the focus leaves:
- **Check box (Q48):** `cb enter` → `cb change 1` → `cb click 1` → (second click) `cb change 0` → `cb click 0` → (focus to the next field) `cb exit 0`.
- **Radio group (Q49):** `grp enter` → `r1 enter` → `grp change 1` → `r1 change` → `grp click 1` → `r1 click` → (click r2) `r1 exit` → `r2 enter` → `grp change 2` → `r2 change` → `grp click 2` → `r2 click` → (focus out) `r2 exit` → `grp exit`.

PdfCraft ran the exit scripts with every click: the button's and then the group's, before the focus had gone anywhere. A form that checks a choice or moves on when the field is left did so after each click. In the app, a click on a check box also applied its value before the focus scripts, so its enter ran after its change and click.

- **engine:**
  - The session records which XFA object has the focus, as `field_focus` hears it: a field's widget, or a radio button.
  - A check box or radio group set while it has the focus (its widget, or any button of the group) runs no exit scripts with the change. `field_focus` runs them as the focus leaves, once.

title: M4: Document Properties reads a named opening destination's page, so choosing page 1 replaces it (ISO 32000-2 12.3.2.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4572.

**The need.** When a document opened at a named destination, Document Properties ▸ Initial View showed page 1 at the default magnification, wherever the name actually went. Choosing page 1 then changed nothing: the dialog counted it as "unchanged" and kept the named action, so the document still opened on, say, page 3. `doc_initial_view { "page": 1 }` did the same.

**The basis.** ISO 32000-2:
- §7.7.2, Table 29, `OpenAction`: "A value specifying a destination that shall be displayed or an action that shall be performed when the document is opened." With the entry absent, "the document shall be opened to the top of the first page at the default magnification factor."
- §12.3.2.4: "a destination may be referred to indirectly by means of a name object (PDF 1.1) or a byte string (PDF 1.2)". A named destination stands for the explicit destination it names.

**The change** (`organize::view`, plus a small helper in `organize::outline`)
- **Reading.** `initial_view` now resolves a named opening destination: a bare name or string as `/OpenAction`, or a GoTo action whose `/D` is a name or string. It is looked up in the `/Names /Dests` tree, then the catalog `/Dests`, with the resolver bookmarks already use (`explicit_dest`: destination depth 8, name tree depth 32 with a seen-set). The page and magnification shown are where the document really opens. A name that names nothing still reads as page 1.
- **Writing.** `set_initial_view` is unchanged in shape. It keeps the opening action when the page and magnification equal what `initial_view` reads, and otherwise writes an explicit destination (or, for page 1 at the default magnification, removes `/OpenAction`). Because the read is now right, choosing page 1 on a name that goes to page 3 is a change, and an explicit `[page1 /XYZ null null 2]` replaces it. The magnification the name had is kept unless the user changes it.

title: M14: pinned tabs open at every start (#2926)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2926.

**Pinned tabs**, as the issue asks: a pinned file is open every time PdfCraft starts.

- **A document tab's right-click menu** gets *Pin Tab*, or *Unpin Tab* on a pinned one. It's only offered for documents that have a file, since an unsaved new document has nothing to open again.
- **A pinned tab shows a pin** where the others show a page, and it moves to the end of the pinned tabs at the start of the strip.
- **At every start the pinned files open first**, in the order they were pinned. This happens whatever *Reopen the files that were open when PdfCraft last closed* says; with that preference on, the session's files follow and none opens twice. A file given on the command line isn't opened twice either. A pinned file that is missing at a start, such as one on a drive that isn't connected, is skipped but stays pinned.
- **Only *Unpin Tab* unpins.** Closing a pinned tab closes it for this session. That is deliberate: quitting with unsaved changes closes the tabs one by one as each is answered (`close_and_continue`), so unpinning on close would lose pins on every such quit.
- **The pins are saved** with the other settings as `pinned_tabs`, as absolute paths, so a file opened by a relative path matches. They are read back leniently: text entries only, each once, at most 64.

The changes are in `tab_context.rs` (the actions and the reading), `last_session.rs` (opening at start), `chrome.rs` (the menu item and the icon) and `lib.rs` (the field and its persistence). The `pin` icon is the bundled Lucide one, so there are no new assets. New strings: *Pin Tab*, *Unpin Tab*, and the notice when 64 are pinned.

title: proposal(redact): prevent retention of confidential vector paths behind clipping (F-008)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Fixes security finding **F-008** (CWE-200 / Sensitive Data Exposure): Partial vector redaction hides the covered area with clipping (`clip_out`, `W/W*`) but retains the complete original drawing instructions (`body`, painting operator).

### Root Cause
When a vector path intersected a redaction region but was not completely covered (`!scope.covered(b)`), `crates/redact/src/interp.rs` used `clip_out` to add an inverse clipping path around the redaction rectangle. However, it still emitted the full original drawing path (`body`) and painting operator. For paths with clipping flags, it additionally retained the path geometry via `ops.extend(body); ops.push(Op::new("n", vec![]));`. An adversary or recipient could extract confidential outlined text, signatures, or geometry from the PDF content stream despite the visual redaction overlay.

### Proposed Fix
- Remove vector paths that intersect redaction marks completely, whether fully or partially covered.
- Refuse partial clip retention so that no drawing geometry is retained in the content stream.
- Increment `scope.report.paths_removed` for partially covered paths that are removed.
- Add an integration test (`partially_covered_vector_paths_do_not_leak_drawing_commands`) verifying that vector drawing commands are stripped and do not leak into the content stream.
- Update `parity/acrobat-features.toml` notes accordingly.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact` passes (143 unit and integration tests).
- `cargo fmt --check` passes cleanly.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-redact -- -D warnings` passes with zero warnings.
- `cargo xtask parity` passes.

title: proposal(redact): unlink unused Type 3 glyph programs and fonts on redaction (F-011)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary

This proposal addresses finding **F-011** (CWE-212 / Sensitive Data Exposure) in `pdfcraft-redact`.

### Problem
Previously, when displayed Type 3 characters were removed during redaction or sanitization, their font dictionary in `/Resources` preserved the original glyph programs and graphical resources in `CharProcs` and `Resources`. When saved with a full save, those references kept confidential glyph geometry, embedded images, or vector payloads recoverable in the saved document even after all displayed uses were redacted.

### Changes
1. **Type 3 Font Analysis and Encoding Mapping**: Added `type3.rs` and `type3_tables.rs` to map character codes to glyph names across standard base encodings (`StandardEncoding`, `WinAnsiEncoding`, `MacRomanEncoding`, `MacExpertEncoding`) and `/Differences`.
2. **Surviving Glyph Tracking**: Implemented content stream inspection across all pages, page-tree resource holders, and reachable form XObjects to track active Type 3 font glyph usage in post-redaction content.
3. **Glyph Unlinking & Exclusive Resource Pruning**:
   - Unlinked unused glyph programs from `CharProcs`.
   - Pruned exclusive resources (`/XObject`, `/ColorSpace`, `/Pattern`, `/Shading`, `/ExtGState`, `/Font`, `/Properties`) from the Type 3 font's `/Resources` that were only used by removed glyphs.
   - Removed completely unused Type 3 fonts from resource dictionaries (`/Font`).

title: Forms: a field's Mouse Down, Mouse Enter, Mouse Exit, On Focus and On Blur actions run
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4359:** its commits are included here until it merges. This PR adds the AcroForm side to #4359's focus tracking (`run_focus_scripts`), so it builds on that rather than adding a second tracker. Its own change is the commit "M6: a field's mouse and focus actions run as the pointer and the focus move".

## What this changes

ISO 32000-2 §12.6.3, Table 197 gives a widget an action for each of six triggers: Mouse Up (`/A`, or `/AA /U`), and `/AA` D (Mouse Down), E (Mouse Enter), X (Mouse Exit), Fo (On Focus) and Bl (On Blur). PdfCraft lets you set all six in Field Properties ▸ Actions, but only a push button's Mouse Up ever ran. Forms use the others to show help text on hover, highlight the field being filled in, or check an entry when it is left. In PdfCraft those did nothing.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form (every trigger of two text fields, a push button and a check box logs `event.name` into a log field):
- **Hovering:** `a Mouse Enter`, then `a Mouse Exit`.
- **Clicking from a, after typing in it, into b:**
  - moving there: `a Mouse Exit`, `b Mouse Enter`;
  - the press: `b Mouse Down`, then `a Keystroke commit`, `a Validate`, `a Blur`, then `b Focus`;
  - the release: `b Mouse Up`.
- **Tab:** `b Blur`, then the next field's `Focus`. An unchanged field doesn't commit.
- **Clicking the field that has the focus:** `Mouse Down`, `Mouse Up`.
- **Push buttons and check boxes** take the focus on a click like a text field.

PdfCraft now does the same:
- **forms:**
  - `widget_action(doc, field, widget, trigger)` reads a widget's action for any trigger: the widget's own first, then the field's, since a field with one widget is often one dictionary.
  - Its action parser is the one a push button's Mouse Up already used, split out (`parse_action`).
  - `Trigger::event_name` gives `event.name`: Mouse Up, Mouse Down, Mouse Enter, Mouse Exit, Focus, Blur.

title: Reject '+' as a hex digit in FormCalc url Decode escapes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

FormCalc `Decode(..., "url")` no longer accepts a `+` sign as a hex digit in `%XX` escapes. Previously a malformed escape such as `%+f` was decoded as byte 0x0F. Now it is left as literal text, the same as `%zz`. Valid escapes such as `%2F` decode as before.

Found while testing `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs:2280-2284`. There is no existing issue, so there is no `Fixes #` line.

**Cause:** the url branch of Decode passed the two characters after `%` to `u8::from_str_radix(h, 16)`, which accepts a leading `+`.

title: fix(xfa): render lines without width as vertical and without height as horizontal
author: manurosado
body:
## What this changes

In dynamic and static XFA forms, vertical dividing lines frequently omit the `w` attribute and horizontal lines omit the `h` attribute, while template declarations may set `slope="/"`.

Previously, `Layouter::measure()` defaulted missing line widths to the full available container width (`avail_w`), and `Layouter::draw_draw()` drew diagonal strokes connecting opposite corners whenever `slope_up` was true. As a result, standard vertical table column separators and horizontal field boundaries were rendered as full-width diagonal slashes across table cells and forms.

This PR fixes line orientation by:
1. In `Layouter::measure()`: when `d.value` is a `Value::Line`, bounding its natural width to the edge thickness plus horizontal margin (`(edge.thickness.clamp(0.1, 20.0) + c.margin.horizontal()).min(avail_w)`) instead of expanding across `avail_w`.
2. In `Layouter::draw_draw()`:
   - If width `w` is omitted or `(d.common.h.is_some() && inner.w <= edge.thickness * 2.0)`, drawing a strict vertical segment from `(inner.x + inner.w/2, inner.y)` to `(inner.x + inner.w/2, inner.bottom())`.
   - If height `h` is omitted or `(d.common.w.is_some() && inner.h <= edge.thickness * 2.0)`, drawing a strict horizontal segment from `(inner.x, inner.y + inner.h/2)` to `(inner.right(), inner.y + inner.h/2)`.
   - Only drawing diagonal strokes when both width and height are explicitly positive and distinct from the edge stroke thickness.
3. Added docstring to `draw_draw` in `crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`.
4. Added unit test `xfa_line_without_width_is_vertical_and_without_height_is_horizontal` in `crates/xfa/src/tests.rs` covering lines without width (vertical), lines without height (horizontal), and narrow lines.

## How you verified it

Ran `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa` against `main`:
- 124 passed; 0 failed.
- Verified that axis-aligned lines in multi-page XFA forms render strictly horizontally or vertically without diagonal slashes.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] cli…

title: Forms: a push button takes the focus on a click and as a Tab stop
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4585 (and so #4359):** their commits are included here until they merge. This PR's own change is the commit "M6: a push button takes the focus on a click and as a Tab stop".

## What this changes

A push button took no focus in PdfCraft. Clicking one ran its action, but the focus didn't move to it, and Tab went past it. So a push button's On Focus and On Blur actions (#4585) never ran, and a keyboard user couldn't reach a button at all.

Measured black-box in another viewer on a synthetic form (every trigger logs `event.name`):
- **Tab from text field b reaches the button:** `b Blur`, then `btn Focus`.
- **A click on the button from text field a:** `btn Mouse Down`, then `a Blur`, then `btn Focus`, then `btn Mouse Up`.
- **A click on the button that has the focus:** `btn Mouse Down`, then `btn Mouse Up`.
- **From the button to a check box:** `cb Mouse Down`, then `btn Blur`, then `cb Focus`, then `cb Mouse Up`.

PdfCraft now does the same (ui-egui):
- **A click on a push button focuses it**, as a click on a check box does. The field it leaves commits and blurs first, then the button's Focus runs, then its action (Mouse Up), in #4585's order.
- **Tab and Shift+Tab stop at push buttons** (`takes_focus`: the fields that can be filled in, plus push buttons that aren't read-only), in the document's tab order.
- **On a focused push button:**
  - Space or Enter presses it (its action, as a click's release runs it);
  - Tab moves on;
  - Escape or a click elsewhere leaves it.
- **The keyboard holder is shared.** The invisible widget that keeps Space, Tab and the arrows from scrolling the page under a focused check box now serves push buttons too (`hold_keys`).
- **Laid-out XFA buttons** are push buttons as well, so they now run their XFA enter and exit scripts (#4359) when they gain and lose the focus.

title: M5: Import comments takes another PDF and copies its comments onto the same pages
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## What this changes

Import comments read XFDF, FDF, XML, XDP, CSV and text data files only, and `comment.import-from-pdf` was planned. The reference app's help page says "Comments can be imported from a PDF document", that "the comment positioning matches that of the file from which they were imported", and that importing from a ten-page document into a two-page one brings only the comments of the first two pages (Import and export comments, https://web.archive.org/web/20251226015046/https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/using/importing-exporting-comments.html).

A locked comment, or an annotation of that name that is not a comment (a link, a screen or 3D annotation, a redaction mark, a widget), stays, and the copy is added beside it without the name.
- The import is one undo step. A PDF without comments is refused with "nothing in the file matches this document", and a PDF that needs a password is refused.

Any other file goes to the data importer first, and is read as a PDF when that fails, `%PDF-` occurs in its first 1,024 bytes and the PDF reader opens it. `doc_import_data` takes a PDF the same way.

title: M5: review statuses are hidden, chain per reviewer and show per reviewer, by /IRT reference (#4122)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4122.

Supersedes #4126 (reworked on main's /IRT threading).

Review statuses now follow ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.3: a state belongs to one user, a user's next change replies to their previous state reply, and PdfCraft shows one status per reviewer.

**Writing** (`crates/annot`):
- Status replies (`/StateModel /Review`) are written with the **Hidden** flag (`/F 30`, Table 167 bit 2). A state reply records a state, not a note (§12.5.6.3: "The state is not specified in the annotation itself but in a separate text annotation"), so it is not drawn as a note icon or listed as an ordinary reply.
- A reviewer's next change replies to **their previous state reply**, not to the annotation. §12.5.6.3 requires this: "Additional state changes shall be made by adding text annotations in reply to the previous reply for a given user." Checkmarks (`/StateModel /Marked`) chain the same way. Another reviewer, or the other state model, starts its own chain on the annotation.
- A reply with a `/StateModel` but no `/State` has the model's default state (Table 175).

**Reading** (`ReviewStates` in `crates/render`, used everywhere states are shown):
- States are found by **object reference**, on main's settled `parent` links (#4061), not by `/NM`. A state reply sets the state of the first annotation up its `/IRT` chain that is not itself a state reply: §12.5.6.3 says its `/IRT` "shall refer to the original annotation", and later changes reply to the previous state reply. So a status set on a reply is that reply's, at any depth of the thread, and is never folded into the thread's comment; `comment_list` reports it on the reply, as main already does.
- A loop, or a chain to nothing listed, belongs to nothing.

title: M12: an XFA form laid out again by its scripts rebuilds its pages in the view (#4603)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4603.

**The need.** On a dynamic XFA form, a field change whose scripts lay the form out again (a check box's change script that shows a hidden section) writes new pages into the document, but the session kept the old page list. The new section's fields had no page rectangle, the field list kept its old length, and saving failed with "the edit changed the page count from 1 to 2", so the form could not be saved once the section was shown. A picture chosen for an XFA image field, and a reset whose calculations show or hide a section, took the same path.

**The basis.** XFA 3.3, chapter 30, config `dynamicRender` (p. 1300): the form may "re-render itself during the session to show or hide objects, instantiate pages, and so on". Chapter 7, "Basic Layout in Dynamic Forms" (pp. 269-270): content that no longer fits "moves on to the next available page within the page set". The page tree written must keep `/Count` equal to its page objects (ISO 32000-2, Table 30, p. 103), and the session's page list must match the file it saves, which the save check of #1698 enforces.

- `XfaRun` gains `relaid`. `Runner::relayout` sets it just before it calls `pdfcraft_xfa::rerender`, so a layout that fails part way, after it may have replaced fields, still counts.
- `EditCtx` gathers it from every script run inside an edit: `on_changes` (field changes and resets), `on_data_replaced` (pictures) and `on_event`.
- After the scripts, `apply` raises the edit's scope to `Scope::Full` when the form was laid out again, as the text-growth path of #2624 already does. title: M12: XFA repeating rows lay out past 50, and tables in positioned containers repeat their rows (#4607, #4615)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4607. Fixes #4615.

**The need.** On a dynamic XFA form, repeating rows were lost in two ways:
- **Past 50 (#4607).** A repeating subform laid out at most 50 instances, so rows 51 and on of a long list or table never appeared. That held whether the rows came from the data or from a button's `addInstance`. Calculations over the rows saw only those 50.
- **A table in positioned content (#4615).** A table (`layout="table"`, rows `layout="row"`) placed at its own position in a positioned subform laid out each row subform **once**, whatever the data or `occur` asked for: 5 data rows gave 1, `max="3"` gave 1, and no warning was recorded. The same table in a flowed subform repeated its rows. The table was also measured with one instance of each row, so what followed it in a top-to-bottom container sat right after that row.

**The basis.**
- XFA 3.3, chapter 17, "The occur element" (p. 786): `max` is "the maximum number of occurrences for the enclosing container, or -1 to set no upper boundary for occurrences". Chapter 9 (p. 336) says the same: -1 "means that the number of occurrences is unlimited", and pagination "is performed downstream by the layout process". A form's own `max` still stops the rows: "it can be copied at most twenty times into the Form DOM", and a row past it "would simply be ignored".
- Chapter 8, "Tables" (p. 327): "A table subform represents an entire table and contains everything in the table. A row subform represents one row of a table and contains everything in the row." Chapter 7, "Layout Strategies" (p. 265): "Dynamic forms may contain a mixture of objects laid out using different layout strategies"; "Repeating Elements using Occurrence Limits" (p. 263): `max` "Regardless of the data no more than this number of instances may be included". The count belongs to the row and its `occur`, not to the layout of the table's parent.

title: feat(edit): Esc in an open paragraph selects its box, so Delete removes it
author: meethere
body:
## What this changes

In **Edit text & images**, a click inside a paragraph opens it for typing. Selecting the whole box (to delete or move it) meant aiming for its thin frame; a press a few pixels inside put the caret in the text instead, which users found hard (#2203: "it many times selects individual character inside the box").

Now **Esc** in the inline editor leaves the text and selects the paragraph's box, as Acrobat does when Esc leaves a text box. **Esc then Delete** removes the paragraph (with #4111's object-selection delete), the arrow keys nudge it and its frame drags it. Esc still discards an unapplied draft, as before.

- `ObjectSelection::select_paragraph_next(page, block)`: the editor overlay has no document inventory, so it records the request.
- `ObjectSelection::prepare`, which has the document, selects that paragraph **after** its own Escape check. `prepare` runs before the overlay in the frame, so the Esc that closed the editor cannot clear what it selected.
- `clear()` drops a pending request, so a disabled tool or a cleared selection never selects later.

title: fix(ui): keep added image corner resize responsive and clip out-of-bounds drag preview (#4477, #3938)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4477
Fixes #3938

In **Edit a PDF** (`QuickTool::EditText`), resizing or moving an added image had four interacting issues:

1. **Corner handle presses hijacked by object marquee (`object_ui.rs`, `content_ui.rs`):** `paint_page` draws the four circular resize handles centered on `r.expand(1.0)` with radius `3.5` (reaching `4.5` px outside `r`), while `object_ui::page_input` ran before `content_ui::page_input` and only checked `r.expand(2.0).contains(p)` without checking `content_ui::select_grabs`. Pressing on the outer portion of a corner handle where the resize cursor is shown missed `hit`, called `leave_single(view)` (clearing `view.content.selected`), and started an object marquee that placed the image into `view.objects.selected` on release, preventing `content_ui::page_input` from responding again.
2. **Handles and items extending past the page edge (`content_ui.rs`):** `content_ui::page_input` and `select_grabs` filtered the pointer to `xf.rect` before checking `corner` and `hit`, so corner handles at or beyond the page boundary (or an image dragged partially out of bounds) stopped responding once the drag was released.
3. **Inward corner resize along one axis (`content_ui.rs`):** `dragged` computed the proportional scale factor with `.max(...)` across the two axes (`((w + dx) / w).max((h + dy) / h)`), which froze shrinking whenever the other axis did not also move inward. It now uses the axis with the larger relative pointer change, matching `edit_text_ui`.
4. **Out-of-bounds drag preview distortion (`content_ui.rs`):** `MoveBackground::paint` sampled `page_tex` across the full unclipped `r.expand(1.0)` quad and started a second drag during `settling` from `from` instead of the settled box. When an added image extended outside `xf.rect`, `xf.screen_to_norm` produced UV coordinates outside `0.0..=1.0`, clamping and smearing page-border texels across the out-of-bounds portion of the dragged image. `MoveBackground::paint` now clips t…

title: fix(comments): count comment drafts as unsaved work and post them on save (#3918)
author: adiraj66132
body:
## What this changes

A comment being typed lived in the app, not the file, and nothing counted it as work. Close, quit and
the auto-reload on an external change all went through `has_unsaved_work`, which listed form drafts,
the open text box and the paragraph editor but not the three places a comment is typed:

- the floating composer card (`comments.composer`) — a new note, text box, callout, caret or replacement;
- the reply box under the selected card (`comments.reply`);
- the "Add a comment" box at the top of the Comments panel (`comments.add_box`).

All three are now counted, so closing, quitting or reloading asks first; and **Save posts them as
annotations before writing**, the same way `save_then` already commits form typing and the open text
box. Nothing typed is ever dropped behind a save that the user chose.

What counts as unsaved and what gets posted now share one rule:

- `comments::can_post` — what the card's Post button allows (text, or an edit being cleared).
- `comments::composer_changed` — whether the card holds anything Post would post. An *edit* card is
  only work when its text differs from the comment's own, so opening Edit and closing the document
  no longer prompts or rewrites the comment.

`comments::submit_composer`, `submit_reply` and `submit_add_box` are the single place each edit is
built: the panel and the card call them, and so does Save. `new_comment` lost its `PageCx`
parameter (it only ever read `page` and `prefs`), which is what lets Save build a comment without a
live page transform.

`comments.editing` (the inline edit of a card's text) is deliberately **not** touched here: PR #3125
already counts it and commits it, and both changes edit the same expression. Whichever lands second
reconciles one adjacent line.

Fixes #3918

title: fix(forms): allow deleting individual radio buttons from a group (#4609)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4609.

In Prepare Form mode, deleting a single radio button previously deleted the entire radio group and all its buttons because `prepare::delete_selected` ignored widget indices and issued `Edit::DeleteField { name }`.

This change:
1. Adds `delete_widget` (and `delete_widget_object`) to `pdfcraft_forms::author`:
   - If the field has only one widget remaining, delegates to `delete_field`.
   - If the field has multiple widgets:
     - Removes the widget object from page `/Annots` arrays.
     - Removes the widget object from the field's `/Kids` array.
     - Removes the corresponding entry from `/Opt` if `/Opt` is present and matches the widget count.
     - Resets `/V` and `/DV` to `/Off` if the deleted widget was the actively selected choice.
     - Cleans up calculation order `/CO`.
     - Regenerates appearances for the remaining widgets via `redraw_field`.
2. Adds `Edit::DeleteWidget { name: String, widget: usize }` to `pdfcraft_engine` with full atomic undo/redo support.
3. Updates `prepare::delete_selected` in `ui-egui`:
   - Inspects the field's widget count using `form: &[FormField]`.
   - Emits `Edit::DeleteWidget` when a single widget from a multi-widget field is selected.
   - When all widgets of a field are selected (or for single-widget fields), emits `Edit::DeleteField`.
   - When multiple individual widgets or fields are selected, batches them atomically and deletes widgets in descending index order to avoid index shifting.
4. Adds support for an optional `widget` index parameter in the headless `form_delete_field` automation tool.
5. Adds comprehensive unit tests in `forms` and `engine`, a headless automation test in `automation`, and UI integration tests in `ui-egui`.

title: Reject non-hex characters in XFA image hash parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

XFA image hash parsing no longer accepts `+` as a hex digit. Before this change, `parse_hex32` (`crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs`) only checked the length and then called `u8::from_str_radix` on each byte pair. That function accepts a leading `+`, so a string like `+f000...` decoded as a valid hash with a first byte of 0x0F.

`parse_hex32` now returns `None` unless every byte is an ASCII hex digit, before it parses any pair. A regression test covers the `+`, `-` and space prefixes, and checks that mixed-case hex still parses.

No existing issue. Found while testing `crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs:50-52`.

## How you verified it

- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Never-crash

- [ ] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests, unless it is provably infallible with a comment saying why
- [ ] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions (`get`, and strings only at char boundaries); checked or saturating arithmetic; allocations sized by input are capped; recursion is bounded
- [ ] No `unsafe`

body:
## What this changes

Part of #2378: the half ticket-craft split out there, *"No warning naming the character that forced the substitution"*. The other half, keeping the source font for what it can show, is #2955. This PR is independent of it and does not touch that logic.

When an edit can't show a typed character in the text's own font, it sets the text in a standard font (not embedded) or in fallback outlines. `LineEdit::substituted` said so, but `Session::apply` dropped it, so neither the app nor the tools could tell the user. Now:

- **ui-egui:** a notice after Apply, e.g. *"The text's own font can't show c (U+0063), so the edited text is set in Helvetica."* The German catalog entry is included, other languages fall back to English.

author: Lcoding15

## What this changes

Fixes #4616.

Add Watermark (and Update Watermark) now has a **Saved Settings** row, like Acrobat's. Type a name and press **Save Settings** to keep the watermark as it stands. Settings are kept in the app settings, so they are there for every document and the next session. Choosing one from the list fills the dialog again; **Delete Settings** forgets the one shown.

- **A picture source.** The file may be gone by the time the setting is used. Save is off for File watermarks, with a tooltip saying why.
- **The page range.** It belongs to the document at hand.

Persistence follows the never-crash rules:
- Settings are stored under `watermark_settings`.
- Reading them back is lenient: unreadable entries and entries without a name are dropped, numbers are clamped to the dialog's ranges, non-finite values take the default, and a duplicate name is kept once.
- Sizes are capped: 64 settings, 100-character names and 4000-character texts.

title: M6: a static XFA form whose data fills thousands of fields opens in seconds (#4637)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4637.

**The need.** Opening a static XFA form gives its fields the values held in its XFA datasets. Each value went through `forms::set_value`, which reads the whole field tree to find the field and reads it again to recalculate. n values cost about 2n readings of n fields, so the open time grew with the square of the fields. A public 136-page form with about 6,000 fields took 261 s to open, and a 95-page one with about 4,000 took 112 s.

**The change**
- **`forms::set_values`** fills a batch as `set_value` fills each value in turn, but:
  - it reads the form once;
  - it recalculates once, after the last value. The calculation order (ISO 32000-2, Table 224, `/CO`) runs once over the final values.
- **Same results as one by one:**
  - Fields with the same fully qualified name (§12.7.4.2) still share the value.
  - A name the batch already wrote, or a twin of one, makes the form be read again first. That write then starts from what the earlier one left. For example, clearing a no-toggle-to-off radio group the batch just selected is still refused.
  - Each value reports its own result.
  - A failed recalculation fails the batch, as it fails `set_value`.
  - A batch where nothing is filled recalculates nothing.
- **`set_value_with`** now uses the same write path (`fill`), so the two cannot drift apart.
- **The engine** (`xfa_values_from_datasets`, on open and on an XFA data import) collects the changed values and fills them with `set_values`. It finds fields by name through a map, not a scan per value.

## How you verified it

- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-forms`, `pdfcraft-xfa` and `pdfcraft-engine` (`--all-targets`)

title: fix(edit): resizing an image under a shared clip scales its own clip too
author: meethere
body:
## What this changes

Resizing an existing image in **Edit text & images** grew the picture but left it showing only through its old box, with the rest cut off. Seen on a real lab-report PDF (not attached: it holds personal data). Its generator draws every picture as

```
q  x y w h re W n   (the picture's own clip, its size or a little wider)
   w 0 0 h x y cm  /Im Do
Q
```

inside an outer `q … re W n … Q` that the section's text shares. An invoice whose pictures have no clip resized fine.

`image_transform_scope` (#1049, #1269) only accepted a scope containing **every** active clip. Under the section's clip none does, so it fell back to transforming the `Do` alone: the picture's own clip stayed at the old size.

Now, when no scope contains every clip, the **outermost scope holding only the image** is used. It holds all of the image's private clips, which move with it; anything outside it is shared with other content and stays. The existing case of a clip shared with a caption inside the same scope (`cropped_image_resizing_moves_private_clips_and_keeps_shared_ones`) keeps its fixed clip. `crop_image` uses the same scope, so cropping such a picture replaces its own clip.

Related: #1022 / #1049 (the same bug without an outer clip).

title: Redaction: a pattern nothing paints with any more leaves the page (rebases #3680; @Hamza0101)
author: adiraj66132
body:
## What this changes

This is **@Hamza0101's [#3680](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/3680)** — a tiling pattern nothing paints with any more leaves the
page, so its cell (and the text under the mark that was in it) does not reach the saved file — carried onto current `main` and out of its
`CONFLICTING` state. **The work, the design and the measurements are theirs;** I rebased it, resolved four conflicts, dropped one commit whose
content is already upstream, and wrote one commit of my own that their change needs to coexist with `main`.

Fixes #3647.

Their approach, unchanged: redaction never enters a pattern cell. It notices that no surviving paint can reach the pattern — `cs`/`SCN` set
the fill and stroke pattern, `g`/`rg`/`k` clear the space, `q`/`Q` carry the graphics state — every painting operator that survives the
rewrite records which pattern it drew with, and a pattern the page selected but nothing uses any more leaves the resources. `Report` gains
`patterns_removed`. The case they singled out as the one a careless version breaks, two boxes from one pattern with only the first marked, is
covered and still keeps the entry.

## The four conflicts

`#3680` was **1,612 commits** behind `main` (CONFLICTING / DIRTY).

1. **`crates/redact/src/tests.rs`** — both sides inserted a test in front of the same closing brace. `main` had grown two tests there

title: M14: keyboard shortcuts can be changed, removed and reset (#4635)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4635.

Help ▸ Keyboard shortcuts was read-only. Now every registered command's key can be changed there:

- **Change** waits for the next key press, which becomes the command's shortcut. Escape on its own stops waiting without closing the dialog.
- **Remove** leaves the command without a key, and **Reset** gives it its default back.
- **Reset all shortcuts** puts every command back to its default.
- **Find a command** searches all registered commands, so a command without a key can get one. Without a search, the list shows the commands that have a key, as before.

What the dialog refuses, and what it does about conflicts:
- **One key runs one command.** Taking a key another command had takes it from that command, and a notice says so: "Ctrl+S was taken from “Save”, which now has no shortcut." Reset does the same if the default was given away meanwhile.
- **Refused with a reason:** Alt combinations (the `Shortcut` model has no Alt), Escape/Tab/Enter/Space/Backspace without Ctrl, and the keys the document view reads itself (Copy, the zoom and page keys, Find next/previous, Select all, Rotate view). The view reads those after the registered commands, so binding one would silently break it.
- **No typing hijack.** A key of the user's own without Ctrl (a letter, F5) doesn't fire while a text field has the keyboard, whatever the command normally allows, so it never takes over typing.

How the binding is shared:
- The changes are published to the egui context each frame (`custom_shortcuts::publish` / `effective`).
- The key handling (`registry_shortcuts`), the menus, the palette, the tooltips (Next/Previous view), the search field's key hint and the control channel's `commands` list all read the same binding.

Persistence follows the never-crash rules:
- Changes are kept in the settings under `shortcuts`, as `{ "command id": "cmd+shift+J" | null }`.
- Reading them back is lenient: unknown commands, unreadable keys and anything a press would be …

title: fix(platform): a saved file keeps its hidden and system attributes on Windows
author: FriedCerebrum
body:
## What this changes

Every save writes a staging file beside the target and renames it over the target. On Windows the renamed file keeps the *staging file's* attributes, not the replaced file's, so a hidden or system PDF came out of a save visible.

The staging file is now created with the replaced file's `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN` and `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM`, through std's `OpenOptionsExt::attributes` (no `unsafe`, no new dependency). A hidden target's staging file is hidden from its first moment, and a plain target's staging file is created explicitly plain. A new file gets neither attribute. Read-only targets are still refused before staging, as before. The archive bit is left to the system, as on any changed file.

The writer is shared, so the desktop save and the automation tools/CLI both get this.

Refs #4593. On local NTFS a plain file does **not** become hidden. I checked that with plain renames on Windows 11 26200, and the new test pins it. So I couldn't reproduce the report itself. My guess is that the reporter's file sits on an SMB/NAS share that hides dot-prefixed names (Samba's `hide dot files`). Staging names start with a dot. Asking the reporter where the file lives would settle it. If it is a share, this change at least asks for plain attributes on the staging file explicitly, but I haven't verified it against a share.

On Windows 11 (26200), Rust 1.99.1:

title: M8: Sanitize can remove or flatten a signed document's signatures (#4622)
author: Lcoding15
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4622: all three modes the issue proposes (`abort`, `remove`, `flatten`).

Sanitize Document on a signed file used to be refused, with no way forward. Refusing is still the default, but the signatures can now be given up explicitly. A sanitized rewrite invalidates them anyway, and their certificates, names and timestamps are hidden information too.

- **redact:** `sanitize::Signatures { Remove, Flatten }` and `sanitize::sanitize_signed(doc, how)`.
  - **Remove** (`sanitize_removing_signatures`): every signature field goes, signed or empty, document timestamps included. Its widgets, and with them how it looks on the page, are removed through `forms::delete_field_object`.
  - **Flatten** (`sanitize_flattening_signatures`): the signature fields stay through to Sanitize's form flattening, so each one's look becomes page content like any other field's. The signature dictionary with the certificates, the signer's name and the timestamp goes with the form: once `/Perms` is gone too, nothing reaches it. Whatever the appearance itself shows, such as "Digitally signed by …" and a date, stays visible, as the issue says.
  - **Both modes also remove** any signature widget a page lists that the form adopts no field for, found by walking `/FT` up the `/Parent` chain (bounded, cycle-safe), plus the catalog's `/Perms` (DocMDP, UR3) and `/DSS` and the form's `/SigFlags`.
  - Then the usual Sanitize runs, and the save is a full rewrite, so no earlier revision is left.
  - No signature validation is involved: valid, expired, untrusted or malformed signatures are all handled the same way.
- **engine:** `Edit::SanitizeSigned(SanitizeSignatures)`, labelled "Sanitize document and remove signatures" or "… and flatten signatures", and undoable until saved. It is the one full rewrite the signed-document guard lets through. `Edit::Sanitize` still returns `SignedRewrite`.

Extends `pdfcraft-ocr` from English-only to Western European Latin-script languages. Adds an extended alphabet (`LATIN_ALPHABET`, 182 characters), an optional custom alphabet file, a larger `LANGUAGES` list, and small model-discovery changes that make the search logic testable.

On `main`, the recognition alphabet is the 96-character ASCII + `€` set, and the docs say the models read "English and other languages written without accents". Scanned German, French, Spanish, etc. text therefore loses its accented letters. [Link issue: Fixes #NNN, if one exists.]

title: Keep the part of an email address before an apostrophe when redacting
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Email redaction no longer drops the part of an address before an apostrophe. The email scanner's `local` closure in `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs` did not accept an apostrophe in the local part. It treated `'` as a boundary and started the match after it, so for `o'brien@example.com` only `brien@example.com` matched. Search and Redact share that span, so the leading `o'` stayed visible.

The local part may now contain an apostrophe, but a match cannot start on one. `o'brien@example.com` and `'john'@example.com` are now matched as `o'brien@example.com` and `john'@example.com`. A quote around an address (`'john@example.com'`) stays outside the match.

No linked issue. Found while testing `crates/redact/src/patterns.rs:216` (email, `local` closure).

## How you verified it

- [ ] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Never-crash

- [ ] No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!` outside tests, unless it is provably infallible with a comment saying why
- [ ] No indexing or slicing with input-derived positions (`get`, and strings only at char boundaries); checked or saturating arithmetic; allocations sized by input are capped; recursion is bounded

title: feat(automation): doc_info reports every page's media, crop, bleed, trim and art boxes
author: acosimati
body:
## What this changes

`doc_info` listed only each page's displayed width and height, although the engine already
computes the five page boxes (`Document::page_boxes`, ISO 32000-2 §14.11.2) and `page_set_box`
can write them. A print workflow needs to read the trim and bleed boxes back, and an agent that
sets a box had no way to confirm what it set. Every entry of `pages` now carries
`boxes: { media, crop, bleed, trim, art }`, effective values (a missing box is its parent's),
in the tools' convention: points from the top-left of the displayed page, the same rect
`page_set_box` takes, so a rect written with `page_set_box` reads back unchanged. The crop box
is therefore `[0, 0, width, height]` and the media box may have negative coordinates when it
extends past the crop. `boxes_user` is the same five boxes in PDF user space (`[x0, y0, x1, y1]`,
y up, unrotated), as the file stores them, for prepress checks that want absolute values. Both
are `null` when the document can't be read for editing. The tool description names the two
fields and their conventions.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation` (41 unit + 270 integration tests, including the two new ones)
- `cargo xtask layers` / `cargo xtask assets` not run: no crate boundary or asset touched

Tests: `doc_info_reports_the_five_page_boxes` (a synthetic PDF whose TrimBox and BleedBox differ
from the MediaBox, upright and turned a quarter: the trim's left margin of 10 pt is reported at
the top in `boxes`, and unchanged in `boxes_user`), and new assertions in

title: fix(annot,ui-egui): guard comment edits against non-comments and stale state (#3916)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Closes #3916

## Root Cause
1. In `crates/annot/src/lib.rs`, `annot_ref`, `delete_annotation`, and `props` indexed directly into a page's `/Annots` array without verifying `is_comment_subtype`. As a result, passing a `/Annots` slot occupied by a non-comment annotation (`/Widget`, `/Link`, `/Popup`, `/Watermark`, etc.) allowed comment operations (`delete_annotation`, `set_contents`, `move_annotation`, `set_color`, `props`, etc.) to mutate or remove form widgets and links.
2. In `crates/ui-egui/src/comments.rs`, `CommentView` retained `selected`, `editing`, `composer` (`ComposerKind::Edit`), and `gesture` across document and page updates (`DocView::document_changed`, `apply_edit`) without checking whether the referenced `(page, index)` comment slot still existed in `DocumentInfo::annotations`, allowing stale selections or open edit composers to target a shifted or non-comment `/Annots` slot.

## Changes
- **`crates/annot/src/lib.rs`**:
  - Added `is_comment_dict` and enforced comment subtype checks in `annot_ref`, `delete_annotation`, and `props` so non-comment `/Annots` entries return `AnnotError::NoSuchAnnotation { page, index }` / `None`.
  - Replaced unchecked slice indexing in `delete_annotation` with `.get_mut(index)`.
- **`crates/annot/src/tests.rs`**:
  - Extended `non_markup_annotations_are_not_comments` to verify `delete_annotation`, `set_contents`, `move_annotation`, and `props` reject `Widget`, `Link`, `Popup`, and `Watermark` annotations and leave their `/Contents` intact.

title: M12: an XFA corner is a right angle unless its join is round, and is drawn with its own line
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

This corrects #4319, which rounded every XFA corner that has a `radius`. It never read the corner's `join`. In the XFA specification that defaults to `square`, a right angle; a radius rounds a corner only when `join="round"`. DA Form 31 (*Request and Authority for Leave*, a public blank form) draws its page frame as a `<rectangle>` with `<corner radius="5.08mm" thickness="0.441mm"/>` and no `join`. Since 0.14.0 PdfCraft drew that frame with round corners, and the curve ran across the fields at the frame's corners (block 1, Control Number, and the Personnel/Finance "to date" field). Another viewer draws the frame square.

How another viewer draws `<corner>`, measured on two synthetic forms (each case on a `<rectangle>` value and on a subform `<border>`):

- **The radius always trims the edges.** Each edge stops the radius short of each of its corners, whatever the corner's shape or presence, and the corner fills the gap.
- **Shape.** The default `square` is a right angle, `join="round"` a quarter circle. `inverted="1"` turns a square corner into a notch the radius deep, and a round one into a quarter circle centred on the box's corner.
- **Each corner has its own line.** It is drawn with the corner's `thickness`, `color` and `stroke` (0.5pt solid black by default), not the edge's. A hidden corner leaves a gap between the trimmed edges.
- **The fill follows the corners' shapes**, hidden corners included.
- **Plain rectangles.** A box whose corners are all right angles lined like its edges (thickness, colour and stroke, not presence) is drawn as a plain rectangle. Its edges meet whole at the corners, and when they are hidden the corners are too. DA Form 31's frame is one; so are its grey boxes, whose edges and corners are hidden.

Changes, all in `crates/xfa`:

- **`model.rs`, `parse.rs`.**
  - `Corner` gains `round` (from `join`) and `line`, its own presence, thickness, colour and stroke, read as an edge's.
  - `Border::radii` gives each corner's…

title: M10: preserve TIFF associated-alpha colors on import
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Translucent TIFF images with associated alpha no longer have their transparency applied twice when imported into a PDF.
For example, a premultiplied 8-bit pixel `[32, 64, 96, 128]` now becomes straight RGB `[64, 128, 191]` with alpha `128`, instead of keeping the dark premultiplied colors behind the same soft mask.
RGBA and explicitly tagged BlackIsZero grayscale-alpha work at 8 and 16 bits through Create PDF and Add Image, including files whose alpha metadata changes between TIFF directories.
Unassociation happens at source precision before the existing 16-bit high-byte reduction.
Zero alpha clears associated colors, and malformed associated colors greater than alpha are clamped.

The importer also refuses unsupported planar alpha and multiple-extra RGB layouts before reading pixels.
The pinned decoder's legacy `read_image` reads only the first plane of planar TIFFs and can compact multiple extra samples away, so treating those buffers as complete interleaved alpha data produced incorrect output.
Existing straight-alpha, unlabelled RGB and explicitly unspecified/unknown extra-sample compatibility behavior is retained.
Related to the TIFF/image semantics discussed in #1201; this does not resolve that broader audit.

## How you verified it

- Reproduced through a freshly built upstream `20eebc1c` CLI before production changes: associated RGBA colors are embedded premultiplied behind an additional alpha mask, while equivalent straight-alpha controls render correctly.
- Observed the original associated-color and GrayA regressions fail, then the planar-RGBA refusal regression fail at its intended runtime assertion.
- Independently byte-validated corrected five-sample TIFF controls, reproduced their lost extra/alpha meaning through 30 pure-main CLI calls, and observed the new native refusal regression fail before adding the layout guard.

title: fix(app): set Windows taskbar and Alt+Tab big icon (ICON_BIG) (#3818)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Closes #3818

## Root Cause
`native_options` in `apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs` sets the window icon with `ViewportBuilder::with_icon`, which `eframe` passes to `winit`'s `set_window_icon`. On Windows, `set_window_icon` only sets the small icon (`ICON_SMALL`, used by the title bar), leaving the big icon (`ICON_BIG`, used by the taskbar and Alt+Tab) unset so Windows displays a generic application icon.

## Changes
- **`apps/pdfcraft/Cargo.toml`**: Added `winit = { version = 0.30, default-features = false }` under `[target.'cfg(target_os = windows)'.dependencies]` (already in the lockfile via `eframe` and patched to `vendor/winit`).
- **`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs`**:
  - Added `taskbar_icon` and `set_taskbar_icon` on Windows to decode `APP_ICON_PNG` and set `ICON_BIG` via `winit::platform::windows::WindowExtWindows::set_taskbar_icon` on `cc.winit_window()` in `app_creator`.
  - Added unit test `the_window_and_windows_taskbar_icons_load_from_the_bundled_png` verifying `APP_ICON_PNG` decodes cleanly for both the viewport icon and the Windows `ICON_BIG` taskbar icon.

title: perf(ui): reloading waits for the system's change notifications instead of looking every 250 ms
author: ZJHeepfixer
body:
## What this changes

The worker that reloads a document when its file changes on disk (#431) looked at every open file's metadata every 250 ms for as long as a document with a file was open. That is four wakeups a second for the whole session, focused or not, whether anything changed or not, and it was most of PdfCraft's idle cost: on an M2 Max with a PDF open, the process woke 4.2 times a second, and `sample` showed only `pdfcraft-watch` in a timed wait. The parity entry already listed "OS change notifications (polling adds up to 250 ms)" as missing.

The worker now follows the folders of the open files through the system's change notifications (FSEvents on macOS, inotify on Linux, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows), through the `notify` crate, and looks only when one of them says something changed there:

- **What a notification means.** Any notification, or an error saying some were lost, is a reason to look. The stamps still decide what changed, exactly as before, so a path spelled differently in a notification (`/var` against `/private/var`, a case difference, a link) can't hide a change.
- **Bursts and busy folders.** A burst of notifications is one look. A folder that never stops changing (a build directory, Downloads) costs at most one look per `SETTLE` (40 ms), not one per change.
- **Unchanged.** Reading a changed file once it has settled and ends in `%%EOF`, epochs (#1802), PdfCraft's own saves, and the notice for unsaved changes all work as before.
- **Where it still looks every 250 ms.** In these cases a notification can't be trusted, so the worker keeps looking every 250 ms, as before:
  - files on a network or FUSE volume, which another computer (or the FUSE server) can rewrite without this one being told. `statfs` says which: `MNT_LOCAL` on macOS, the `f_type` magic numbers on Linux. ReadDirectoryChangesW does report changes on SMB shares, so Windows has no exception;
  - files whose folder is missing or couldn't be watched. The folder is followed ag…
