title: M12: XFA fields validate before they exit, and a list box validates and exits as the focus leaves it
author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4573:** its commits (and those of #4359, #4563 and #4369, which it builds on) are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

XFA fields now run their validate scripts before their exit scripts, each kind of field at the moment another viewer runs them. A list box now keeps the focus as items are picked in it, as a check box does. #4573 listed list and combo boxes as not covered.

Measured in another viewer on two synthetic forms, each field logging its enter, change, validate, exit and click scripts:
- **Text field:** typing runs change; leaving runs validate, then exit.
- **Check box:** a click runs validate, then change and click; exit waits for the focus to leave.
- **Drop-down:** picking an item runs change, validate and exit at once. The drop-down gives up the focus as the item is picked, so clicking away afterwards runs nothing more for it.
- **List box:** picking an item runs change and click. The list keeps the focus; validate and exit run as the focus leaves it.

Before this change, PdfCraft ran exit before validate for every field. A check box validated after its change scripts, and a list box validated and exited with every pick.

Changes:
- `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`, `on_changes`:
  - A check box or radio button runs its validate scripts first, before `TOGGLE_ORDER`.
  - Any other field runs them after its change scripts and before its exit scripts.
  - A list box with the focus keeps it, like a check box: its exit waits, and its SOM path goes into `FocusLeft::unvalidated`.
  - `FocusLeft` holds what is left for the focus to finish (the exits that ran, the list boxes still to validate), so `on_changes` keeps seven arguments.
- `Runner::validate`: one validate script, with the existing alert rule (a failing value shows its message, an empty one doesn't). It is shared by `on_changes` and `on_focus`.

author: EricKaden
body:
**Builds on #4589:** its commits (and #4585's, which it builds on) are included here until it merges. This PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

A click in the text field being edited now runs that field's Mouse Down and Mouse Up actions. Before, the open editor took the press, and the page never saw it, so neither ran.

The order comes from the synthetic form measured for #4585 in another viewer. A click on the field that has the focus runs only Mouse Down and Mouse Up: no Blur, no Focus. A press that drags to select text runs them too, the Mouse Up as the button comes up over the field.

title: perf(forms): an XFA redraw reads the form once, not once per field
author: MoriartyPuth
body:
## What this changes

Regenerating the widget appearances of **every** field of a form used to cost one
whole-form reading per field. A dynamic XFA form is laid out at open and its field
appearances are regenerated then (and again after every script event that lays it out
again), and such forms have thousands of fields — so opening one was **quadratic in the
field count**: this branch brings `pdfcraft-cli info` from 2.36 s at 1,000 field rows to
0.13 s, and 23.73 s at 4,000 to 0.63 s (8,000 fields went from about 12 minutes to
1.69 s, measured on an older build). After this PR, laying out a 4,000-field form reads
the form 2 times, not 4,001 times.

Concretely, on current `main` `engine::xfa_redraw` loops over the form's fields and calls
`pdfcraft_forms::redraw_field(name)` per field — and `redraw_field` starts by reading the
whole form to find its field by name (`author.rs`: `fields(doc).into_iter().find(…)`).
One full-form enumeration (page `/Annots` maps, inheritance, HashMaps) per field. The
widget-redraw loop body now lives in `redraw_field_at`, which takes a field that is
already resolved; `redraw_field` keeps the by-name lookup for its own callers (unchanged
behaviour), and the new `redraw_all_fields` reads the form once
(`fields_with_adopted`) and redraws every field from what it already knows. The engine's
`xfa_redraw` is now one call to it. A signed signature field still keeps the picture its
signer's application drew (the skip moves with the loop), and a field whose appearance
cannot be drawn still produces an error naming the field.

## How you verified it

Measured with a synthetic ladder (a one-page dynamic XFA form with K subform/field rows;
`pdfcraft-cli info`, release build, sums of three runs agreeing):

| K fields | `main` (`d764a8eb`) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 2.36 s | 0.13 s |
| 2,000 | 5.47 s | 0.26 s |
| 4,000 | 23.73 s | 0.63 s |
| 8,000 | 715 s (measured on `0b670caf`) | 1.69 s |

title: input: macOS nine-grid IMEs commit unmarked text, and their code keys no longer type digits (#4687)
author: andyau98
body:
## Summary

Nine-grid input methods such as 九方 (Q9 M9) never call `setMarkedText`: they swallow their code keys silently (no IME callback at all) and commit the chosen character from inside `keyDown:` with `insertText:replacementRange:` and `replacementRange = NSNotFound`. winit dropped that commit (no `pending_commit`), and it also sent the swallowed code key to the app as `KeyboardInput` text, so typing a character inserted its digits and the character never arrived — #4687.

- Track whether an IME callback ran for the key being handled by `keyDown:` (`ime_callback_fired`, set in `insertText:`, `setMarkedText:` and `doCommandBySelector:`).
- In `insertText:`, treat a commit inside `keyDown:` with no marked text, no pending commit and a string different from the event's characters as an unmarked commit: announce `Ime::Enabled` if the state is still `Disabled`, then emit `Ime::Commit`, mirroring the existing mouse-commit branch.
- In `keyDown:`, call `NSTextInputContext.handleEvent(&event)` (which reports whether the input context consumed the event) instead of `interpretKeyEvents`, and skip the `KeyboardInput` entirely for a key consumed with no callback and nothing forwarded by `doCommandBySelector:`. Clearing only `KeyEvent::text` was not enough: egui-winit falls back to `logical_key.to_text()`, which still types the digit.

The patch is confined to the vendored winit (`vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/macos/view.rs`, winit 0.30.13). If you would rather carry this as a winit upstream change first, the same logic can be proposed there (rust-windowing/winit#3617, rust-windowing/winit#4650).

## Testing

macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6, aarch64), Q9 M9, in PdfCraft 0.14.0 built from this branch:

- Keyboard: the nine-grid digit codes no longer appear, and the chosen character commits cleanly (keyboard and mouse candidate selection).
- Backspace, Enter and the arrow keys still reach the app; no Windows or Linux paths are touched.

title: fix(check): check dynamic XFA forms after they are laid out
author: MoriartyPuth
body:
## What this changes

`pdfcraft-cli check` never checked a dynamic XFA form's real pages. It took the page count
from the file's page tree and rendered those pages from the raw bytes — for a dynamic XFA
form, that is the one placeholder page the file still holds (the template is what layout
turns into pages at open). So `check` reported

```
{"file": … , "status": "ok", "pages": 1, "warnings": 0, "ms": 1, …}
```

for a synthetic 7 KB dynamic form the app lays out into two pages, and `ok / pages=1 /
0 warnings` for every larger dynamic form too (a 400-page laid-out form: `ms: 10`). This
contradicts the other file-reading verbs on the same file — `info` says `pages: 400`,
`pdf_pages: 1`; `text` reads a page 3 the placeholder tree does not have; `render --page 3`
draws a laid-out page. `tests/it/xfa.rs` states the rule those commands already follow
(#1645): **page commands must use the same dynamic XFA layout as the app and tools** —
`check` is the one command outside it.

Two consequences beyond the numbers:

- The ok verdict was about pages the app never shows. When the layout itself misbehaves,
  `check` cannot see it: any crash/hang/error that lives in opening a dynamic form
  (`Session::open` — template parse, script events, appearance generation for the laid-out
  pages) passes the sweep as long as the placeholder page renders.
- `cargo xtask fuzz` drives `check-one` on mutated seeds, which inherits the same blind
  spot: a mutation that only breaks the template still passes, because the layout pipeline
  never runs.

`check` now opens a dynamic XFA form the way `info`/`text`/`render` do, through
`Session::open`, and checks the laid-out copy: `pages` counts the laid-out pages (what
`info`'s `pages` reports), the pixels+text loop runs per laid-out page, and a failed open
is reported as the `open-error` a user would get opening it in the app. A form that cannot finish the layout
inside `--timeout` reports as `{"timeout": 1}` in the parent's summary, so large dynami…

title: fix(print): fall back to the lpoptions listing when the PPD is unreadable (#4699)
author: lordwotton29
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4699.

`cupsd` keeps `/etc/cups/ppd/<queue>.ppd` at `0640 root:cups` on Arch and similar setups, so an ordinary desktop user cannot open it. `printer_options_via_within` turned that permission error into `None`, and `Print ▸ Properties…` showed *"This printer offers no settings of its own."* — although `lpoptions -p <queue> -l` was returning every option, with its choices and default, to that same user.

When the PPD is missing, unreadable, or parses to no options, the list is now built from that `lpoptions -l` listing. Options Craft handles itself (`PageSize`, `PageRegion`, `Duplex`, `Collate`, `ImageableArea`, `PaperDimension`) are skipped to match `parse_ppd`; the starred choice becomes the default; keys and choice names pass the same conservative checks the PPD path uses; and the option list, the choices per option and the labels are capped at the same numbers `parse_ppd` uses (400, 400, 256).

Where an option's value has to be typed, CUPS prints `Custom`, `Custom.<TYPE>` (`Custom.PASSCODE`, `Custom.STRING`) or `Custom.WIDTHxHEIGHT` in place of the choices. The dialog collects no such value, so those templates are dropped instead of offered as selectable text; an option whose choices are *all* templates disappears with them, and a starred template never becomes the default.

`localize` now runs after the fallback, so a readable PPD that produced no options still lends its `*ll.Translation` lines to the list the fallback built. It leaves options it cannot translate untouched, so the PPD path is unchanged.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-print`, then `rustfmt --check --edition 2024` on the two touched files — clean with the repository's `rustfmt.toml`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-print -j 2` — 53 passed, 0 failed

title: fix(ui): the page sets its cursor once, from the top claim the tool reaches
author: alehel
body:
## In short

The cursor's shape is a promise about what a click will do: a hand follows a link, an I-beam selects text, a four-way arrow moves something. Until now about twenty parts of the page view each set the cursor, and whichever ran last in a frame won, whatever a click would actually do. So with the stamp tool over a link you saw the link's hand but a click placed a stamp, and with the Select tool over a comment lying on text you saw the I-beam but a drag moved the comment.

With this PR each part instead asks for a cursor, with a rank (an open editor outranks a resize handle, which outranks a comment, which outranks a link, and so on), and the page picks the highest-ranked request the current tool cares about, once per frame. A link counts only for the tools that follow or edit links, so the stamp keeps its crosshair. A link's tooltip shows only with its hand, because it says where a click goes; a comment's tooltip shows with any tool beside that tool's cursor, because it is only information, as in Acrobat.

The cursor now tells the truth, a new tool declares what it wants instead of patching one pair of tools at a time, and a test fails if any page code sets the cursor directly again. PR 3 makes the click use the same answer, so the cursor and the click can't disagree at all.

## Why

This is PR 2 of three for the page pointer router, after #2685 (merged).

Bugs about "what the cursor registered" kept coming back in the page view, and each fix only covered one pair of tools. A review on 15 October found the cause: the page view had no single place that decided what was under the pointer. All pages are one egui widget, and about twenty tool modules each tested the pointer themselves and **set the cursor themselves**. egui keeps the last cursor set in a frame, so the order of the per-page chain decided the cursor, while a separate set of booleans decided who acts on a press. Nothing made the two agree, and the cursor promised one thing while a press did anoth…

title: fix(ui): Update previews the page without the marks it replaces
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

**Update Background**, **Update Watermark** and **Update Header and Footer** previewed the new marks on the page's thumbnail. That thumbnail still has the marks Update is about to replace:

- A background colour is previewed as a tint multiplied onto the page. Update the default pale yellow to light blue and the preview shows a muddy teal, which is the blue multiplied onto the yellow.
- A new watermark or header was drawn over the old one, so both showed.

OK applied the right result. Only the preview was wrong.

In Update, the preview now draws the page without its marks of that kind:

- **Engine.** `Document::page_without_marks(page, kind)` removes the marks with the same `remove_marks` that Update uses, on a copy of the document. It is read-only, like `text_edit_preview` and `added_content_preview`. It returns `None` when the page has no marks of that kind, so its thumbnail already is the right page, and it skips the copy when the document has none at all.
- **Dialog.** In Update, `marks_ui` renders that page off the UI thread at the preview's size. It renders once per page shown, and again only after an edit. A blank sheet shows until the render arrives. If the page can't be prepared or rendered, the preview falls back to the thumbnail, as before. Add, and pages without marks of that kind, still use the thumbnail. The render is released when the dialog closes.

Other kinds of mark stay in the preview: Update Watermark still shows the background, and Update Background still shows the watermark.

No new strings.

title: fix(comments): delete or edit one reply from its own menu, keeping the thread
author: alehel
body:
## What this changes

In the Comments panel a reply had no menu. The only **Delete** was on the comment card's **…**, and it deletes the whole thread (`DeleteAnnotation` on the comment, which takes every reply with it). A reviewer couldn't remove one wrong reply without losing the comment and everyone else's replies. Headlessly, `comment_delete` with a reply's id or page and index already deleted just that reply, so the app and the tools disagreed.

Now, on the selected card, **each reply has its own "…"** ("Options for this reply"), with:

- **Edit**: opens the panel's inline editor on that reply, in place of its text. Save changes the reply's `/Contents`, not the comment's.
- **Copy text**: copies the reply's text.
- **Delete**: deletes that reply alone. The comment, its other replies and its status stay, as one undo step ("Delete comment").

This follows Adobe's public help, which says to delete a reply from that reply's own options menu, and to edit a comment from its options menu ([Reply to comments](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/share-and-review-documents/manage-reviews/reply-comments.html), [Delete comments](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/share-and-review-documents/review-documents/delete-comments.html), [Edit comments](https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/desktop/share-and-review-documents/review-documents/edit-comments.html)). I read no Acrobat files.

Decisions:

- **A reply with replies of its own takes them along**, with its pop-up and any status or checkmark set on it. That is what `pdfcraft_annot::delete_annotation` already does for a comment and what `comment_delete` already did for a reply. Keeping them would leave `/IRT`s pointing at nothing. One undo brings them all back.
- **A locked reply's Delete is greyed out** (the engine refuses it anyway). Edit stays available, because the Locked flag doesn't restrict the contents (ISO 32000-2 Table 167), as on the card.
- **Status and checkmark replies stay badges**, with no menu. A Replace Te…

title: audit: detect image covers over extractable text (#3117)
author: robertobulltech
body:
## What this changes

Pasting a black image over extractable text currently passes the faux-redaction audit. Image XObjects, stencil image masks and inline images now produce `covered-text` findings through the engine, `doc_audit_redactions` and `pdfcraft-cli audit`.

Refs #3117 **(image cases only)**. This leaves Type 3 covers and path-fill colour/clipping changes separate from #3155; the original issue has not been edited.

- Decode lossless DeviceGray/RGB/CMYK samples, Decode arrays and stencil polarity. Measure the union of painted sample regions, excluding unpainted stencil bits and nonopaque soft-mask samples.

- Retain each text run's showing operator to distinguish text painted before and after an image, even when those runs join one line. Preserve the existing contrast and translucent-cover policy.
- Return an incomplete-audit error for unreadable/ambiguous content, unsupported image analysis, unaudited form text combined with images, or exhausted image/decode/comparison bounds. A partial walk cannot become a clean result.

The issue's exact synthetic generator was run on unmodified main `86a4120a`: only page 6 was reported. After the fix, **pages 1, 2, 3 and 6** are reported by both CLI and automation. Poppler still extracts `secret` on each page; Poppler and PdfCraft renders show it covered on pages 1–3. Pages 4–5 remain outside this image-only change.

title: M10: preserve hard line breaks in RTF export
author: KyleKassen

Previously, an extracted block containing `First line`, `Second line`, `Third line`, and `Fourth line` separated by LF, CRLF, and CR was exported successfully, but RTF readers joined the text into `First lineSecond lineThird lineFourth line`.

title: feat(web): page host mode, so a page can host PdfCraft in its own document (#4731)
author: helenkwok
body:
Closes #4731.

A page that loads the PdfCraft module into its own document can now opt into the host bridge with `data-host="page"` on `<canvas id="pdfcraft">`. The messages are the `?host=parent` ones, carried as non-bubbling DOM `CustomEvent`s on the canvas: PdfCraft dispatches `pdfcraft:ready`, `pdfcraft:save` (`name`, `saveAs`, `bytes`), `pdfcraft:dirty` and `pdfcraft:failed` with the message fields as `detail`, and the page dispatches `pdfcraft:open`.

**Design.** `host::Bridge` now holds a `Transport` (`Parent` or `Page`) with one `send`, and the two differ only in how an event goes out and how `open` comes in; save, dirty, ready and failure reporting are shared. `?host=parent` is checked first and behaves as before, including no bridge for an unframed page or a cross-origin parent (#2167). Only the exact attribute value `page` opts in (`page_host_enabled`, unit-tested). `packaging/web/README.md` documents it with a host-page example that adds its listeners before `init`. No `parity/` entry or automation tool: this is a second transport for the existing embedding surface, which has neither.

**Checks.** On Linux: fmt and clippy (`-D warnings`) pass; the workspace tests (no fail-fast) 5057 passed, 2 failed (`links::about_dialog_has_contributors_and_models_tabs` and `control::simplified_chinese_about_tabs_and_credit_controls`, which fail the same way on unchanged `main` in my container and pass on this branch when run alone). In a browser, with a release build of this branch: a page with `data-host="page"` received `pdfcraft:ready`, opened a six-page PDF it dispatched, and on Ctrl+S received `pdfcraft:save` (`saveAs: false`) with the document instead of a download.

title: perf(render): cache bounded derived image pixels
author: ishveet
body:
# perf(render): cache bounded derived image pixels

## What this changes

Repeated draws of the same large PDF image currently repeat decoding and resampling when the decoded source exceeds the existing 64 MiB source-cache limit. This adds a bounded cache of eligible final-size pixels in the Hayro renderer, using the existing decode, filtering and image-sampling behavior. It avoids retaining the large decoded source solely for reuse.

The cache is limited to ordinary device Gray/RGB raster XObjects with complete resource/settings identity. Masks, soft masks, stencils, inline images, JPX, transfer functions, Type3 rendering, patterns and knockout groups remain on the existing path. FIFO eviction is deterministic; retained pixel payload is capped at 16 MiB and bookkeeping at 512 entries per `RenderCache`.

This is a follow-up to [#2436](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2436), whose discussion left scaled-image caching for follow-up. Coordinate with [#2068](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2068), which is still migrating rendering to shared `craft-pdf`; if that migration lands first, port the backend change there rather than duplicating it in the app adapter.

## Measurements

Three fresh processes per binary/workload, three renders per process. Cold is the first render with an empty renderer cache; warm is the median of the six subsequent renders. Peak is median Windows process peak working set, sampled every 10 ms.

Reproduction argument sets (run each executable in three fresh processes; the example writes its fixture and first RGBA output under the process working directory):

title: M14: cargo xtask perf, performance budgets for large documents (gap 13)
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
## What

`cargo xtask perf` adds performance budgets for large documents (gap 13, `misc.performance-budgets`).

- It generates deterministic synthetic PDFs in a temporary directory (never committed): 10 pages, 1,000 pages, and 10,000 pages plus 64 MiB of filler (about 97 MiB).
- For each size it runs the release `pdfcraft-cli` once per phase, in its own process: open, scroll (render the first 10 pages at 72 dpi), edit (set a title, rotate a page), incremental save, full save.
- It records wall time and, on Linux, peak resident memory (`VmHWM`), keeps the fastest time and highest peak of `--runs` (default 3), writes JSON to `target/perf/results.json`, and compares against the committed `xtask/perf-budgets.json`. It exits non-zero when a budget is exceeded or a phase has no budget.
- `.github/workflows/perf.yml` runs it nightly, on demand, and on changes to the benchmark. It is **not** a required check.
- Updates `docs/gaps.md` gap 13, `docs/roadmap.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, the README command list and the `misc.performance-budgets` parity entry (now `partial`).

## Why

Gap 13 lists budgets as missing; memory and timing so far were one-off manual measurements. This makes them repeatable and checkable.

## How the numbers were chosen

Measured on a GitHub `ubuntu-latest` runner: the slowest `large` phase took 1.3 s and peaked at 347 MiB; open was 0.4 s at 145 MiB. Budgets are at least eight times the measured time and 2.5 to 4 times the measured peak (for example `large` saves: 20 s, 1000 MiB). They catch an order-of-magnitude regression such as an extra copy of the file, not a few percent. Times for a phase include the open, since each phase is its own process.

## Verification

- Unit tests: budget comparison (within, over time, over memory, unreadable peak, missing budget, unknown fields), the committed budgets covering every size and phase, generator determinism, page count (parsed with `lopdf`), filler size, and phase scripts.
- The Performance workflow passed and produ…

title: M7: an added text box or picture dragged onto another page moves there (#4655)
author: x-labb
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4655. Dragging an added text box (or an added picture) from one page and releasing it over another used to make it vanish: the release was read in the page the drag began on, so the item was saved far outside its own page (text dragged up from page 2 of a 400-pt page was saved at y=610).

Now, released over another page:

- the item is pasted onto that page, with its box where the pointer left it, kept whole inside the page's edges, and deleted from its own page, as **one undo step** ("Edit content"). It's the existing `PasteContent` and `DeleteContent` edits in one `Batch`, so there is no engine change; a picture is drawn from the same image object, not a second copy;

Same-page moves, resizes and releases over the gap between pages behave as before.

One thing worth a look: a page below the item's own is not yet in `screen_xforms` when the item's page reads the pointer (pages are registered as they are painted), so while an item is moved `document_area` builds every visible page's frame first (`page_frames`) and passes it to `content_ui::page_input`.

This overlaps the draft #1861 (images and attached pictures between pages, #787), which has conflicted with `main` since mid-October and where the author reported a bug on 10-14. title: M2: a non-symbolic TrueType font finds its glyphs by standard post names
author: exploded
body:
## What this changes

A non-symbolic TrueType font now finds its glyphs by name when its version 2.0 `post` table uses only standard Macintosh glyph names.

**Symptom.** PDFs printed from Chrome (`/Producer (PDFium)`) render every character as a box, while text extraction and search work. In the file that prompted this, the embedded `Helvetica` and `Helvetica-Bold` subsets are TrueType, `/Flags 32` (Nonsymbolic), `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding`.

**Cause.** Those subsets have:

- a single `cmap` subtable, platform 0 encoding 3 (Unicode BMP), and no (3, 1) or (1, 0) subtable, and
- a version 2.0 `post` table in which every glyph takes a standard Macintosh name (all indices < 258), so the table ends after the index array and has no string data.

`EmbeddedKind::map_code` looks codes up through (3, 1) and (1, 0), then falls back to the font's glyph names. read-fonts gives the empty string data as `None`, and `OpenTypeFontBlob::glyph_names` returned early on `None`, dropping all names, including standard ones that need no string data. With no route left, every code mapped to `.notdef`.

**Fix.** In `OpenTypeFontBlob::glyph_names`, missing string data reads as an empty list of custom names, so standard names still resolve. This is vendored `hayro-interpret` patch (67), marked `PdfCraft patch:` and listed in `vendor/README.md`.

**Relation to #2980.** #2980 also probes (0, x) Unicode `cmap` subtables on the non-symbolic path, which would fix these Chrome files by a different route. It doesn't touch `glyph_names`, so the two are independent. This PR covers fonts whose only route is the `post` names, for example a (0, 3) table that misses a code. The test is built so #2980's change doesn't make it pass on its own: its one `cmap` subtable maps nothing.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` (`pdfcraft-render`. The `blob.rs` hunk matches default rustfmt style, like the rest of the vendored file.)
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed (`cargo clippy -…

title: M6: LaTeX animate animations play: page actions, timers and one script context per document (#169)
author: pyatsysh
body:
## What this changes

PDFs made with the LaTeX `animate` package now play, with each of its three methods (`widget`, `icon`, which is the default, and `ocg`). Fixes #169. It closes the three gaps described there:

- **Page actions.** When the page being read changes, the old page's close actions and the new page's open actions run: the page's own `/AA /O` and `/C`, and its annotations' `/PO`, `/PV`, `/PC` and `/PI` (`pdfcraft_forms::page_scripts`, `Session::show_page`).
- **Timers.** `app.setInterval` and `app.setTimeOut` are kept per document and fire when they fall due; the app pumps them from `logic()` every frame (`Session::run_timers`, and `next_timer` for `request_repaint_after`). They are bounded: 10 ms is the shortest period, a document keeps at most 64, one call runs at most 16, and a timer's alerts and requests go to the console instead of the screen. `clearInterval` and `clearTimeOut` take the returned object; a function may stand for the expression.
- **One context per document.** `pdfcraft_js::session::ScriptSession` keeps one boa context on a thread of its own (with the script stack and a run limit, as `XfaSession` does). Document-level scripts run once (one added later runs before the next script), and buttons, the console, page actions and timers share the context, so the player's state persists. This is the button and console part of #269; field scripts (format, keystroke, validate, calculate) keep their fresh context, and a laid-out XFA form keeps its own path. Refs #269, where #344 also works on persistent form state.

`animate` also needs:

- `buttonGetIcon` and `buttonSetIcon` (the default method shows a frame by giving the player button that frame's icon), and `this.getOCGs()` with `name`, `state` and `initState` (the `ocg` method).

Fixes #4741.

A redaction mark only outlines what it covers until it is applied with **Redact all**. Saving a document with marks that haven't been applied left the text and images under them in the file, where anyone can read or copy them, and nothing in the app said so. In #4741 the reporter saw the marks on the page (filled while the pointer is over them) and took the saved file to be redacted. It wasn't.

Saving now asks first, when the document has redaction marks that aren't applied:

> **Apply the redaction marks before saving?**
> "form.pdf" has a redaction mark that isn't applied yet. Until it is, the text and images under it stay in the file, where anyone can read or copy them.
> Redact all removes that content for good. Save with marks keeps them to apply later.
>
> [Cancel] [Save with marks] [**Redact all and save**]

- **Redact all and save** applies every mark, the same edit as Redact all (one undo step), then goes on with the save. If the apply is refused (for example, text the redaction can't remove yet), nothing is saved and the reason shows as for Redact all.
- **Save with marks** writes them as marks, to apply later (another person reviews them, say). The same document isn't asked about again until it changes, so saving twice in a row asks once. The next edit, such as a new mark, asks again.
- **Cancel**, or dismissing the dialog, writes nothing.

Every save goes through the question: Save, Save As, and the save in the "save changes?" prompt when closing a tab or quitting. A cancelled save there keeps the tab open, as a cancelled Save As already does. The question comes before Save As asks where to save, and the save's own questions (where to save, overwriting a file that changed on disk) still follow.

Headless: `doc_save` reports the marks that aren't applied as `redaction_marks_pending` plus a `warnings` entry ("1 redaction mark isn't applied, so the text and images under it are still in the saved file; redact_apply remove…

author: mtlcl410
body:
> **Draft. Depends on #3575 (event.target as the document object); this PR adds getField, signatureInfo, signatureValidate and resetForm on it. It will be rebased onto main once #3575 merges.** Until then #3575's commits are included through one merge commit; this PR's own change is the last commit.

## What this changes

Fixes #4761
Related #4743

In a dynamic XFA form's JavaScript, the bare `event`'s target is the document (#3575). Forms ask that document for a field, and for a signature field's state. On `main` there is no such method, so these scripts stop with `TypeError: not a callable function` and the rest of the script doesn't run. In a scan of 82 public XFA forms:

| call | forms |
|---|---|
| `event.target.getField(<full SOM name>)` | 9 |
| `getField(...).signatureInfo().status` | 2 (one of them is the form in #4743) |
| `getField(...).signatureValidate()` | 7 |
| `event.target.resetForm(<name or array>)` | 2 |

After this PR:

- **`event.target.getField(name)`** finds a laid-out field by the SOM expression of its XFA field with every index written (`form1[0].sbfrmFooter[0].SignatureField1[0]`). title: xtask: interop suite opens every kind of output in MuPDF and Poppler (gap 12)
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Part of gap 12 (`docs/gaps.md`): the interop suite that opens every kind of output we write in other readers. It does not close the gap: pdf.js, Acrobat and real-world files are not covered.

## What it adds
`cargo xtask interop [--out DIR]` writes one small deterministic file per kind of output by running `pdfcraft-cli` on a script, then opens each in MuPDF (`mutool`) and Poppler (`pdfinfo`, `pdftoppm`), every reader a separate process:

| Case | Output |
|---|---|
| plain-save | new document, full rewrite |
| incremental-save | saved, reopened, changed, saved in place (also checked to have appended a second `%%EOF`) |
| encrypted-aes-256, -aes-128, -rc4-128, -rc4-40 | open and permissions passwords |
| signed | visible signature, self-signed P-256 ID |
| form-filled | text field, check box, combo box, filled |
| annotated | highlight, note, rectangle, text box |
| page-edited | page deleted, blank inserted, all rotated |

Per reader a file passes when it opens, reports the page count we wrote, and renders every page without an error on stderr. An encrypted file must also open with the owner password and refuse a wrong password and no password (the refusal has to be about the password, so a reader failing for another reason does not pass). A reader that is not installed is a declared skip; with `PDFCRAFT_ORACLES_REQUIRED` set it is a failure, as everywhere else the oracle crate is used. Output is a table on stdout and `interop.json` in the output directory.

A new `interop` workflow (Ubuntu 24.04, installs `mupdf-tools` and `poppler-utils`, sets `PDFCRAFT_ORACLES_REQUIRED`) runs it on changes to the writers and `xtask`, posts the table to the job summary and uploads the files. It is a separate workflow, so it is not part of the required gate. `crates/oracle` gains `mutool()` and `pdfinfo()` probes.

title: Edit text: spaces the source font can't encode read back as typed (#4229)
author: muraa-p
body:
## What this changes

`Fixes #4229`

Follow-up from #4217: replacement text written in the paragraph's own font keeps its width when the font has no encodable space by drawing each typed space as a positioning `TJ` gap of the font's space width. The width rounds, but the *text* doesn't: the reader takes a gap for at most one space, and takes nothing in front of the run's first glyph, so `  ab  ba   ab` read back (in `text_lines`, copy, Find and export) as `ab ba ab`, and the next edit started from that collapsed text.

When the typed spacing can't round-trip through the gaps — a run of two or more spaces, or spaces at the start or end of the run — the run is now marked with its exact text in `/ActualText` (`/Span << /ActualText (the typed text) >> BDC … EMC`, ISO 32000-2 Table 374), which extraction takes over the glyphs it spans: `text_lines` reads it back exactly as typed. The width still comes from the gaps, so nothing the reader of the page draws changes. Single spaces need no mark: one gap and one space round-trip by themselves, so every replacement the source font can encode verbatim keeps drawing as before.

The mark carries the text with `PdfString::text`, the same way the added-text and styled-block paths write `/ActualText` they already read. Rewriting a marked run replaces the whole span and takes its wrappers with it, so marks don't pile up over successive edits.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-edit` (`--all-targets`)
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-edit`: 285 passed, 0 failed

Tests in `crates/edit/src/tests.rs`, on the subset without a space glyph that #4219's width test uses:

- `typed_spaces_in_a_subset_without_a_space_glyph_read_back_exactly` — editing to `  ab  ba   ab` reads back exactly that through `text_lines`, keeps all 7 gaps (the width) and one `BDC`/`EMC` pair.
- `a_single_space_in_a_subset_without_a_space_glyph_reads_back_one` — editing to `ab ba` reads back `ab ba` with no `BDC` …

title: fix(render): treat combined fill-and-stroke operators as a knockout group (#3229)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary

Under ISO 32000-2 §11.7.4.4 (*Special considerations for stroking*), when a single operator both fills and strokes a path (`B`, `B*`, `b`, `b*`) or shows a glyph in text rendering mode 2 (`FillStroke`) or 6 (`FillAndStrokeAndClip`), the fill and stroke are treated as if they were contained in an implicit non-isolated knockout transparency group (`K = true`): the stroke replaces the fill where they overlap, and the combined result is composited once with the backdrop using the current soft mask and blend mode.

Previously, `fill_stroke_path` (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/path.rs`) and `show_glyph` (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/interpret/text.rs`) painted the fill and then painted the stroke directly over the fill as two separate compositing operations. Whenever stroke opacity was below 1.0, a non-Normal blend mode was active, or a soft mask was installed, the inner half of the stroke composited with the object's own fill before the backdrop.

This change introduces `with_fill_stroke_group`, which wraps combined fill-and-stroke path operators and text rendering modes 2 and 6 in a knockout transparency group (`device.push_transparency_group(1.0, soft_mask, blend_mode)` + `device.set_knockout()`) whenever transparency, a soft mask, a non-Normal blend mode, or a pattern paint is active and the device is not already inside a knockout group.

Closes #3229

title: M12: a dynamic XFA form runs all its opening scripts and is laid out once, so a save no longer keeps a half-initialized form (#4790)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4790

On opening a dynamic XFA form, PdfCraft runs the form's initialize, docReady and calculate scripts within a 3 s budget. On large forms that budget ran out after a few scripts, and the half-initialized form was what saving kept. This PR makes the opening scripts cheap enough to finish, in two commits:

1. **Lay the form out once after the opening scripts**, not after every script that shows or hides something (`crates/engine/src/xfa.rs`). One layout of a large form costs about 0.6 s.
2. **Start every script from one shared copy of the form** (`crates/js`, `crates/engine`). Each script used to copy the whole form twice before it ran. Now the engine sends the scripts of one event the same tree until the live form changes, and the script thread keeps the flattened form it built from it. Each script starts from a copy whose text is shared (`Arc<str>`), and still gets its own copy, so nothing one script changes reaches the next except through the engine. Resets in a row in one script's effects (`xfa.host.resetData` once per subform) are applied as one reset, each name once (kept in a set, so merging stays linear in the names).

**Real forms**, from a round-trip and fill run over 243 public blank XFA forms (sources in #4790):

title: Word count: key structure exclusions by parent tree, not page (#4228)
author: muraa-p
body:
## What this changes

`Fixes #4228`

Word count's structure exclusions (`TextFilter.mcids`, `crates/render/src/text.rs`) were a set of MCIDs per page. `TextFilter::excludes` matched a marked-content sequence's MCID against that set wherever the sequence is drawn: the page's own content, a form XObject with its own `/StructParents`, or an annotation appearance.

MCIDs are local to their content stream (ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.4). A form with its own `/StructParents` numbers its sequences under its own parent-tree key, so a sequence in such a form — or in an annotation appearance — that reuses an MCID the page excludes was dropped from the count, and an excluded element whose content lives in a form was never matched at all.

Now `TextFilter.mcids` is keyed by the parent-tree key (`/StructParents`) of the stream the content is drawn in: `HashMap<i32, HashSet<i32>>`. `excludes` takes that key and matches only when the structure element and the drawn sequence share it; content in a stream with no `/StructParents` (patterns, Type 3 glyph streams, soft masks, forms without the entry) matches nothing.

`crates/engine/src/word_count.rs` builds the set keyed by parent-tree key, resolving both `/Pg` (page) and `/Stm` (content stream) references: an element whose content lives in a form references it through `/Stm`, so its MCIDs land under the form's own key. The form's MCIDs are excluded while the page's same-numbered MCIDs are retained. The `page_has_form_xobject` caution block is gone.

Vendor patch 64 threads the key through `hayro-interpret`: `Context.struct_key` (default `None`), set from the page's `/StructParents` in `interpret_page` and saved/restored around a form in `draw_form_xobject`; `Device::begin_marked_content` now takes the key. The render device passes it to `filter.excludes`.

Fixtures now carry valid `/StructParents`, per ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.4.

title: M6: document-level scripts run when the document opens, so a field they hide is not drawn
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4797

ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.17 (p. 527) says the document-level ECMAScript actions in the name dictionary's `JavaScript` tree "shall be executed" when the document is opened. PdfCraft ran them only as a preamble to some other script, such as a calculation or a console or button script. Nothing ran them on opening.

Three public German municipal forms by one form vendor (form-solutions.de) use a document script to hide a plain AcroForm text field: a yellow bar on page 1 that says the viewer may not be compatible. In PdfCraft the bar stayed on screen and in print. These are the Baden-Württemberg Elterngeld application (copy published by Gemeinde Lauchringen), the Stadt Schmallenberg residence registration and the Gemeinde Ihringen landlord's confirmation. The renderer was never at fault: it skips Hidden and NoView annotations (Table 167). The script that hides the field simply never ran.

After this PR, opening a document:

- Runs its document-level scripts once, after the XFA open scripts, with JavaScript on (Preferences ▸ JavaScript), and when XFA layout is not active, as before.
- Applies the field changes they make, as button and console scripts already do. `display` and `hidden` become the widgets' `/F` bits: Hidden (bit 2), Print (bit 3) and NoView (bit 6). Values, read-only and required also apply. Calculations rerun only when a value changed, so hiding a field leaves every calculated value as saved.

title: Edit text: don't offer paragraphs drawn as a clipping path (#4786)
author: mmmaarian03-crypto
body:
Fixes #4786.

## What this changes

Since #3447, rewriting, clearing or moving text drawn in a clipping mode (`4 Tr` to `7 Tr`) is refused, because its glyphs are a mask for the artwork behind them. Edit text still outlined those paragraphs and opened them on a click, so the refusal came only afterwards. In a Photoshop export every text object is a mask, so nothing the editor offered could be edited.

- `TextBlock` gets `clips`, set when any of its lines draws in a clipping mode (the same rule `refuse_clipping_text` uses: one clipping run is enough).
- Edit text gives such a paragraph no box (`Rect::NOTHING`, as unplaced images already get): it is not outlined, opened or dragged. In Add text it no longer counts as source text under the pointer.
- `text_paragraphs` lists it with `clipping: true` (the key is only present when true), and the tool description says so.

This is a different case from #4708 (#3877), which flags text drawn *under* a `W`/`W*` path clip. The two touch neighbouring lines in `TextBlock` and `text_regions.rs`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

title: fix(ui,engine): cap Find-and-Redact matches and avoid quadratic OCR page checks (#3920)
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## Summary
Addresses two UI-thread work items reported in #3920:

1. **Cap Find-and-Redact search matches (`crates/ui-egui/src/redact_ui.rs`):**

title: M9: filling honours the fields a signature locks (/Lock, FieldMDP)
author: Hagma2023
body:
## What this changes

Once a signature field is signed, changing a field its lock names invalidates that signature (ISO 32000-1 §12.7.4.5, Table 233 `/Lock`; §12.8.2.4 FieldMDP). Acrobat marks those fields read-only when it signs; files from other signers often don't, and PdfCraft filled them, silently breaking the signature.

- **forms:** `signature_locks(doc, &fields)` reads the locks of *signed* signature fields: the field's `/Lock` and the FieldMDP transform in its signature value's `/Reference` (Acrobat writes both, other signers one of them). `All`, `Include`, `Exclude`; a listed name also covers the fields below it (`address` → `address.city`). Result: locked field → the signature field that locks it.
- Filling a locked field fails with the new `FormError::Locked { field, signature }`.
- `reset` leaves locked fields as they are, `recalculate_with` leaves a locked calculated field at its signed value, and `apply_changes` (button scripts, side effects of field scripts) skips locked fields.
- A lock on an *unsigned* signature field has no effect yet.
- `parity/acrobat-features.toml`: `sign.field-mdp` → `partial`, with what is still missing.

Out of scope (noted in parity): writing a lock when signing (`sign.lock-after-signing`), marking locked fields in the UI / `form_fields`, reporting a locked field's change in changes-after-signing.

title: fix(optimize): merge side-by-side and grid-tiled image fragments
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
Some PDF producers and printer drivers split a page picture into vertical strips placed side by side or into a 2D grid of rectangular tiles (`q ... cm /Im Do Q`), which `crates/optimize/src/fragments.rs` previously left unmerged because `stacked` only recognized 1D horizontal strips sharing the same left and right edges. Group fragments into horizontal rows (`same_y`), validate edge-to-edge tiling both horizontally within each row and vertically across rows, follow row-by-row and horizontal strip runs in `drawn_in_sequence`, and assemble the merged image at the finest horizontal and vertical pixel density.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-optimize -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-optimize -j 2` (7 unit tests, 5 JPEG transform tests, and 36 integration tests pass)
- Added unit tests in `crates/optimize/src/fragments.rs` covering out-of-order side-by-side vertical strips with mixed horizontal resolutions, out-of-order 2?3 tile grids, sequential side-by-side runs separated by a horizontal gap (left-to-right and right-to-left), partial trailing row truncation on a 2?2 grid, horizontal `u32` overflow refusal before allocation, and rejection of overlapping or mismatched rows.

## Never-crash

- Production code in `crates/optimize/src/fragments.rs` uses zero `.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, `panic!()`, `unreachable!()`, or `unsafe`.
- All slice accesses (`ops.get`, `out.get_mut`, `px.get`, `run.first`, `run.last`, `row.first`, `row.last`) use checked indexing and `?`.
- Merged dimensions `width` and `height` are verified to be finite and within `1.0..=f64::from(u32::MAX)` before casting to `u32`, `u64::from(width) * u64::from(height) <= MAX_PIXELS` is enforced before allocation, and buffer strides/offsets use `checked_mul`.

## Provenance

- Clean-room implementation based on ISO 32000-2 ?8.3 / ?8.9 coordinate transformations and image XObject dictionaries. No external code, fonts, or assets added.

title: fix(redact): `Q` inside a text object restores the text matrices, as the renderer does
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Inside `BT … ET`, `q`/`Q` save and restore the text matrix and text line
matrix as well as the graphics state. That is ISO 32000-2 §9.4.1 as
corrected by the PDF Association's errata (`pdf-association/pdf-issues`
#368); §8.4.2 points to it. Acrobat does the same: on a synthetic PDF 2.0
page, Acrobat 26.2 draws the text after `Q` at the pen from before `q`.

The renderer on `main` already does this. The redactor's own content
interpreter (`crates/redact/src/interp.rs`) did not: it kept Tm and Tlm
across `Q`. In

```
BT /F1 12 Tf 72 700 Td (AAAA) Tj q /F2 24 Tf (B) Tj Q (SECRET) Tj ET
```

the renderer draws SECRET at the pen from before `q`, over the B, and
`redact_mark find` takes its boxes from there. The redactor measured SECRET
after the B instead. The boxes missed the glyphs it measured, so
`redact_apply` found residue and refused: text after such a `Q` could not
be redacted.

The redactor's state stack now holds Tm and Tlm with each saved `Gs`, and
`Q` restores all three. Outside a text object the next `BT` resets both
matrices, so restoring them there changes nothing. Like the renderer, the
redactor applies the rule whatever the file's version (`q` inside `BT` is
only allowed from PDF 2.0).

No existing issue or PR covers this. I searched issues and PRs here
(`--state all`, several phrasings).

Not in this PR: the text-editing rewriter (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`) also
keeps Tm and Tlm across `Q`. I can follow up separately.

Earlier revisions of this PR changed the renderer the other way. @jpeskov
pointed out the erratum; the renderer patch and its tests are gone and
`vendor/` matches `main`.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-redact` and `pdfcraft-automation`, `--all-targets`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact`, plus `cargo test -p pdfcraft-automation --test it redact_text_after_q`

title: fix(view): touchpad motion sent in lines scrolls 1:1, not eased or boosted (#3665, #3234)
author: 0xPyAI
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3665. Fixes #3234.

Both reports have one cause. Touchpads send **line-unit** wheel events on two platforms: winit reports X11 smooth scrolling as `LineDelta((x - position) / increment)`, and Windows `WM_MOUSEWHEEL` as `delta / WHEEL_DELTA`. So a Windows precision touchpad, its inertia, and an X11 touchpad all arrive as fractions of a line, about once a frame, and never as points. Off macOS, egui reports the source of these events as `Unknown`.

- **#3665 (jumps ahead).** #1094 (commit 4db6ac4) accelerates line events by how fast they arrive. A touchpad stream looks like a fast wheel spin, so it was multiplied up to 6x, with the surplus added outside egui's smoothing. Measured in the new view test: 30 events of 0.2 lines moved the page **2924 points instead of 600** on `main`.
- **#3234 (stutters and stops short).** As mtlcl410 found on the issue, those events never reached the 1:1 touchpad path from #868, which takes only `Point` deltas. egui eased each one over the next ~100 ms, so the tail of a fling arrived as short eased steps and then a stop.

**Fix (in `wheel_boost::accumulate`).** A line event is touchpad motion when its delta is not a whole number of lines, or when egui reports it as `Trackpad` or `Momentum`. Touchpad motion now goes to `precise`, at the same distance (`lines × line_scroll_speed`), and is applied 1:1 through the existing un-eased path. The precise path also hides egui's eased copy of the event, as it already does for pixel deltas. `line` again holds only whole wheel notches, which keep egui's easing and the #1094 acceleration unchanged.

## How you verified it

On Windows 11:

- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p pdfcraft-ui-egui`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-ui-egui -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: fix(render): a form's stray `Q` no longer pops the page's saved states
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

A form XObject or annotation appearance whose content has more `Q` than `q`
popped graphics states that the content drawing it had saved. On `main`, in

```
page: q 1 0 0 1 20 -100 cm 0 0 200 400 re W n
      BT /F1 12 Tf 72 300 Td (AA) Tj ET /X Do
      BT /F1 12 Tf 72 280 Td (SECRET) Tj ET 0 0 1 rg 0 0 400 50 re f Q
form: BT /F1 12 Tf 200 0 Td ET Q Q
```

the form's two `Q`s, together with the restore `draw_form_xobject` does on
exit, pop the page's `q`. "SECRET" loses the page's `cm` (drawn, extracted
and found at 72,110 rather than 92,210), and the fill loses the page's clip.
Search redaction then fails closed: `redact_mark find` takes its boxes from
the render text layer, while the redactor measures the glyphs where they
really are. `redact_apply` reports "redaction could not be verified ... so
nothing was changed", so the text cannot be redacted at all.

A content stream balances its own `q` and `Q` (ISO 32000-2 §8.4.2, §8.10.1).
This PR adds patch (68) to the vendored hayro-interpret. `interpret()`, which
runs every form and appearance stream, records the state depth at which its
stream starts (`Context::enter_stream`), and puts the outer stream's floor
back on exit. A `Q` at that floor has no `q` of its own stream to match, so
it is ignored with a `warn!`. Balanced `q … Q` inside a form is unchanged.

This is the separate bug that #4831 mentions in its last paragraph. The two
PRs do not depend on each other. Both append to the hayro-interpret row of
`vendor/README.md` and add a `mod` line to the same two test `main.rs` files,
so whichever merges second needs a small rebase, which I will do the same day.

No existing issue or PR covers this. I searched issues and PRs here
(`--state all`: "unbalanced Q", "stray Q", "extra Q form", "restore state
underflow", "graphics state stack form", "q Q balance").

title: fix(ocr): copied OCR text keeps the spaces between words (#2306)
author: 0xPyAI
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #2306.

After Recognize text, copied text ran words together. The issue describes words copying as separate pieces instead of one paragraph. On current `main` the same cause shows as missing spaces. A synthetic 300 dpi scan of two paragraphs, run through `ocr_recognize` and then `text_extract`, gave:

```
Thequick brown foxjumps overthelazy dogwhilethecommittee reviews theannual budget
```

**Cause.** `pdfcraft_ocr::text_layer` places each recognised word with its own `Tm`, stretched to its box, and writes no spaces. A copy must then guess word breaks from the gaps between glyphs (`render::text`: a gap over `0.15 × line height` above the typical letter gap). OCR word boxes are tight around the ink, so many real word gaps fall under that limit.

**Fix.** Between neighbours on a line, the layer now writes a space glyph, as scanned PDFs from other programs do. Two words are neighbours when they read the same way, sit on about the same baseline (within 0.6 word heights), and are less than 1.5 word heights apart. The space is a sliver (0.01 word height) at the end of the first word, on its baseline, so the word's box stays the scanned word's. Search highlights and the OCR edit path (which keeps each word's width) do not change. Words on other lines, and table cells farther apart, get no space, so the edit grouping of phrases and table cells stays the same.

After the fix, the same scan copies as:

```
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while the committee reviews the annual budget
report for the coming fiscal year and discusses several proposals.
Second paragraph: scanned documents should copy as continuous text, with words joined by
spaces on each line instead of one word per line.
```

title: fix(edit): Tab in an open paragraph adds space and keeps the keyboard (#3881)
author: 0xPyAI
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3881 (the Tab key part).

In Edit text, pressing Tab in an open paragraph did not add space. The paragraph's text box (`edit_text_ui.rs`, `TextEdit::multiline`) did not lock focus, so egui's focus order took the key: the keyboard moved to the next control, typing stopped there, and the paragraph closed on the next key. That is the "opens a new window instead of adding space" in the report.

Now Tab puts a tab stop of four spaces at the caret (replacing the selection, if any), and the paragraph keeps the keyboard. The key is consumed before the text box sees it, and the box locks focus, so neither egui's `'\t'` insertion nor its focus order runs. Shift+Tab is consumed and does nothing: a paragraph has no indentation to remove.

Spaces rather than a tab character, on purpose: no PDF font has a tab glyph. `source_encodes` would fail on a `'\t'`, so the paragraph would be rewritten in a substitute face, and the draft would show a gap the page cannot have.

title: fix(filters): preserve partial output from raw Flate fallback
author: Lucenx9
body:
## What this changes

A truncated raw deflate stream can begin with bytes that resemble a zlib header. When the zlib interpretation fails without output, the raw retry recovers a prefix and then reports truncation. The fallback previously discarded that prefix in favor of the original empty failure.

```diff
 raw retry reports corrupt data
- return the original empty failure
+ retain the retry's recovered prefix and decoded-byte count

title: fix(app): Issue #4851 A file name that isn't UTF-8 is skipped instead of crashing at launch
author: Ridzzz0Alam
body:
Fixes #4851

## The issue
The desktop app crashes (exit 101) before opening a window when an argument isn't UTF-8, such as a Latin-1 or Shift-JIS file name on Linux.

## Why it happened
`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs` read its arguments with `std::env::args()`, which panics on such an argument. #3849 fixed this in `pdfcraft-cli` only.

## The fix
- Read the arguments with `args_os`. One that isn't UTF-8 can't be opened (the app opens paths as `str`), so it is logged and skipped, and the app opens as usual.
- It keeps its place: `--control <name> report.pdf` must not make the PDF the control file.

## Tests
- `an_argument_that_is_not_utf8_is_skipped_not_a_crash` (`apps/pdfcraft/tests/help.rs`) runs the binary with `caf\xe9.pdf --version` and `--control caf\xe9.pdf --version`. On `main` it fails with exit 101. A fix that drops the argument instead fails the second case: the app takes `--version` as the control file and opens its window.
- Checked in the app on Linux: launched with the bad name and a valid PDF, the window opens on the PDF and the log says what was skipped.
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings` and tests on `pdfcraft`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`

## Not covered
Opening such a file. The app's open path, recent files and single-instance handoff are all `str`.

title: Forms: auto-sized single-line text fields fill their height, not 12 pt
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

An auto-sized (`0 Tf`) single-line text field was drawn at no more than 12 pt, however tall the field was. A 30 pt-tall field showed 12 pt text in the bottom half of the box, where Acrobat Reader fills it.

`auto_text_size_by` already computes the size from the height (`height / 1.15`, then shrinks to fit the width). This drops only the 12 pt upper limit for single-line text, so a 30 pt field (24 pt inside the border and padding) gets about 20.9 pt text. The 4 pt floor and the width shrink are unchanged. As a sanity bound the height is capped at 14,400 (`MAX_AUTO_HEIGHT`, the largest page side ISO 32000-1 Annex C recommends), so a hostile rect can't produce an absurd `Tf`.

ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.3 leaves the auto size implementation-defined (ISO 32000-1 §12.7.3.3 tied it to the rectangle's height), so the behaviour here follows Acrobat. Black-box check: a synthetic form with auto-size fields 30 pt and 60 pt tall, plus a fixed 12 pt field, opened in Acrobat Reader. The auto fields draw much larger than the fixed 12 pt one, and the 60 pt field draws larger than the 30 pt one.

**Not changed:** multiline and comb auto-size keep their 12 pt cap. I haven't checked those against Acrobat, so this PR doesn't guess.

The on-screen editor shares this function (`field_auto_text_size_by`), so what you type matches the page. It already caps its own size at 300.

author: Harrison-Booth

Refs #1619.

**Help ▸ Report an Issue…** opens a new GitHub issue with the version, OS and the open document's file type already filled in. Nothing is created until the user submits it. Nothing but those facts goes in the address: never a file name, path or contents.

title: perf(cos): keep a running total of the scan reader's cache size
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4867

## What this changes

`ObjectReader::try_get` (the reader behind `scan_objects`, `write_full` and the other whole-document walks) measured every parsed object in its cache, up to 128 of them, after each object it read, only to check the 8 MiB byte budget. It now keeps a running total: when a read parsed exactly one new object, that object's size is added; the whole cache is measured again only when something else changed it (a failed read, a read that inserted more or fewer than one object, which includes a nested load that made the editor cache evict, or a cache changed from outside). Inserts are counted, because cache length and pointer equality alone cannot tell a read that replaced entries from a plain hit. The cache is still cleared at the same moments as before, so which objects are parsed again, and every output, is unchanged.

Only `ObjectReader` (two new fields, `try_get`, the constructor) is touched. One existing test inserted a replacement into the reader's cache from outside and relied on the next read noticing it; it now inserts a new entry, which is the case the reader still detects. Added a test that the running total equals a fresh measurement after every read, including misses, hits and dangling references, and one for the review finding: a cached object, then a read of a string over the editor cache's 32 MiB limit leaves the cache length unchanged; it failed before the fix (the string stayed cached) and passes now.

## Measured

Synthetic PDF of 120,001 objects (40,000 pages, each with a page dictionary, a Flate content stream and a font dictionary; 18 MB), release build, `taskset -c 15`, rebased on current `main` (re-measured after the review), `perf stat -e instructions:u`, three runs each (counts repeat within 0.1%):

| whole-document walk | before | after | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| scan_objects (serialise every object) | 4.10 G | 1.62 G | -60% |
| write_full, object streams | 9.68 G | 4.72 G | -51% |
| write_full, classic table…

title: perf(cos): rebuild a damaged cross-reference index without parsing every object
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4868

## What this changes

Opening a file whose cross-reference data is damaged rebuilds the index from the object headers (`Document::reconstruct`). That rebuild was slow on large files. Three things change, all in `crates/cos/src/document.rs`:

- An object is parsed for the object-stream check only if its dictionary contains `ObjStm` or a `#`. The end of the dictionary is found by reading it the way the parser does (strings with nesting and escapes, hex strings, comments, nested dictionaries), so text inside a string, such as `9 0 obj` or `>>` + `stream`, is not taken for syntax. When the end is not certain (unterminated, a bad hex digit, `>>` inside an array, longer than 1 MiB) the object counts as a candidate and is parsed as before. A name can hide its letters as `#xx`, so `/Obj#53tm` still counts. Before, every object in the file was parsed once for this check.
- The positions of `/XRef` are found in one pass over the file instead of a 1,024-byte search after every object header.
- `find` looks for the rarest byte of the needle first (a block-wise byte scan) and compares the rest only there. It is also faster for the `trailer` scan and the other callers. The result is the same as before.

The set of objects, the trailer and the repair log are the same as before. The diff stays in the reconstruct region plus the helper functions next to it, to keep clear of #4738 and #4805.

## Why

Open of a damaged file was dominated by parsing every object and by byte-by-byte searches.

## Numbers

Synthetic PDF, 40,000 pages (page dictionary, Flate content stream, font dictionary: 120,005 objects, 23 MB), re-measured on current `main` after the review,, `startxref` pointed at a wrong offset. | open | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| damaged file | 3,169 M instr | 808 M instr (-74 %) |
| intact file (no reconstruct) | 73 M | 73 M |

title: perf(cos): write_full keeps the objects it parsed while numbering
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4869

**Stacked on #4873.** This branch is based on the #4867 branch (`perf/objreader-owned-bytes-running-total`), so until #4873 is merged this PR also shows its commits (the branch merges it). Once #4873 is merged this shrinks to this PR's own changes.

## What this changes

`write_full` walked the object graph to number the objects, kept only each reference, and then read every object a second time when writing it, because the reader cache holds 128 objects. It now keeps the parsed object from the walk and writes that, within a budget of 64 MiB of owned bytes (streams read from the file are views and cost only their dictionary) and 2,000,000 tree nodes. Past the budget an object is read again exactly as before, so memory stays bounded and the "read differently while saving" check still applies to those objects. Kept objects are the very ones that were numbered, so they cannot differ.

Touches `write_full` and helpers in `writer.rs`, and makes `owned_bytes` `pub(crate)`. After review, `owned_bytes` also counts name bytes and dictionary-key bytes (keys twice in a dictionary that indexes them), so the 64 MiB budget now covers a huge name or key; before, a name of 64 MiB + 1 byte was admitted with 0 bytes counted. Adds unit tests for the budget, including that case.

## Measured

Same synthetic PDF as in #4873 (120,001 objects, 18 MB), release build, `taskset -c 15`, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, three runs each (repeat within 0.01%). Whole-run totals:

| full save | main | #4873 only | this PR on top |
|---|---|---|---|
| classic table | 8.77 G | 3.90 G | 2.63 G (-33% vs #4873, -70% vs main) |
| object streams | 9.68 G | 4.72 G | 3.45 G (-27% vs #4873, -64% vs main) |

Cost: peak memory of the object-stream save on this file rises from 43 MB to 158 MB (the parsed trees are held until written); the node cap bounds this for larger files, which fall back to the old second read.

title: perf(cos): write hex strings, integers and references without the formatter
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #4870

## What this changes

`serialize` in `crates/cos/src/writer.rs` formatted every byte of a hex string, every integer and every object number of a reference through `write!`. It now uses a hex lookup table and a small digit loop (`write_digits`, `write_int`, `hex_pair`). Hex strings reserve their output size first. The octal escape in literal strings and the `#xx` escape in names use the same helpers. Whole-number reals also go through the integer writer. The bytes written are the same as before; only `writer.rs` changes in the library code.

## Why

Hex output is common: strings of encrypted documents are binary and are written as hex, as are `/ID` and many binary strings. Large arrays and many references also spend most of their save time in the formatter.

## Numbers

One object serialized in a probe, release build, `taskset -c 10`, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, three runs each (identical every run). The counts include building the test object, so the real saving in `serialize` is larger than shown.

| content | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 8 MB hex string | 2,247 M instr | 253 M (-89 %) |
| 1M integers | 373 M | 249 M (-33 %) |
| 1M references `N G R` | 668 M | 343 M (-49 %) |
| 1M names with escapes | 1,637 M | 597 M (-64 %) |
| 1M reals | 1,294 M | 1,293 M (unchanged: float formatting dominates) |

## How verified

- Output of the old and new build compared with `cmp` on 1M-element arrays of integers, references, reals and names, and on an 8 MB hex string and an 8 MB binary literal string: identical.
- A synthetic PDF with 40,000 pages (120,005 objects): the dump of every object and a full save (classic table and object-stream variants) are byte for byte identical with the old build.
- New integration tests in `tests/it/serialize_format.rs` compare against the standard formatter: proptests for integers (all of `i64`), whole reals, references, hex strings and literal/binary strings (octal escapes), plus unit tests for `i64::MIN/MAX`, every power…

title: fix(xfa): draw Romanian and Polish letters in XFA-to-static output instead of '?'
author: GigiG1
body:
Refs #3833 (Romanian character support).

## What

`xfa_to_static` lays XFA text out in the standard-14 fonts with `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding`, and `win_ansi()` turns every other character into `?`. Romanian (ă Ă ș Ș ț Ț ş Ş ţ Ţ) and Polish (ą Ą ę Ę ł Ł ś Ś ż Ż ź Ź ć Ć ń Ń) forms therefore lose those letters in labels, field values and the extracted text. Romanian ANAF tax declarations (dynamic LiveCycle XFA) come out as "DECLARA?IE PRIVIND OBLIGA?IILE DE PLAT?", while their layout and values are otherwise excellent.

## How

- `pdfcraft_fonts::LATIN_EXTRA`: 26 letters at control codes WinAnsiEncoding leaves undefined: 0x01–0x08, 0x0B, 0x0E–0x1F. It never uses 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C or 0x0D: an unescaped CR in a literal string reads as LF, and the text export separates pages with form feed.
- `win_ansi_extra()` maps those letters to their codes and everything else exactly as `win_ansi()` does.
- `Std14::text_width_extra()` measures them as their base letter (abreve = a, scommaaccent = s, lslash = l in the Core14 metrics), so `std14_metrics.rs` and its attested hash are untouched.
- In `crates/xfa/src/pdf.rs`, `standard_font` writes `/Encoding << /Type /Encoding /BaseEncoding /WinAnsiEncoding /Differences [code /name …] >>`, the span writer uses `win_ansi_extra`, and `Face::width` uses `text_width_extra`.
- ț and Ț are named `uni021B` and `uni021A`. The glyph list maps `tcommaaccent`/`Tcommaaccent` to U+0163/U+0162 (cedilla), so extraction would otherwise read them back as ţ Ţ.
- Field values need no change in `forms`, because `/DR` fonts already go through `Metrics::from_dict`, which reads `/BaseEncoding` and `/Differences`.

## Checks

These ran on `d28d047`. The four touched files and `crates/forms/src/appearance.rs` are byte-identical at `f94668f`, the base of this branch.

- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-fonts -p pdfcraft-xfa --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-fonts -p pdfcraft-xfa --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-fonts`: 94 passed. …

title: fix(render): a non-isolated knockout group blends its elements with the page under it
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4886.

A non-isolated knockout group (`/I false /K true`) starts from the backdrop
under it (ISO 32000-2 §11.4.7, §11.4.8): each element blends with that
backdrop in its own blend mode, and replaces the group's earlier elements
under its shape. The renderer drew such a group into a layer of its own that
starts transparent, so a blend mode inside it had nothing to blend with.
White drawn with `/BM /Difference` over magenta stayed white instead of
turning green.

When the group is entered plainly (full opacity, no soft mask, Normal
blending, and not itself an element of another knockout group), it is now
drawn in passes, one per blend mode its elements use:

- each pass is a knockout layer (patch 39's `Compose::Copy` behaviour)
  composited onto the backdrop with that pass's blend mode;
- in a pass, only elements of that blend mode paint. Every other element
  clears what is under its shape, as it would replace it (a path, glyph or
  shading through `set_paint`, where a shading that paints nothing, such as
  a mesh off the page, clears nothing; an image or nested group's layer
  composites with `Compose::DestOut`, which clears its coverage, a masked
  image's or stencil's mask included);
- the Normal pass records which other modes appear, so a group without
  blend modes still takes one pass, as before.

Each pixel's last covering element is then present in exactly one pass, and
that pass composites it with the backdrop in the element's own mode. That is
§11.4.8's result, up to anti-aliased edges (tested opaque, and at 50 %
for Normal and Difference). There are at most 16 passes, one per blend
mode. Each pass starts from the same marked-content state, so a stream that
leaves a `BDC` open doesn't hide the next pass.

In its own pass, a masked image or stencil mask still doesn't clear the
same-mode elements under it, the approximation patch 39 makes for those in
knockout groups (exact where the mask is opaque or transparent over a
different-…

title: edit: a variation selector after existing text draws the base glyph instead of failing the edit
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The Type 3 fallback collected one glyph per scalar, and no face has an outline for U+FE0F, so any edit of text containing a variation selector failed with the reported error. The fallback now treats U+FE00..U+FE0F the way the CID renderer treats them: the base character before the selector draws its nominal glyph, and the selector itself takes no glyph and no advance — `1` + U+FE0F and ➡ + U+FE0F edit and save where they used to refuse. A lone selector encodes to nothing rather than failing.

One scope note: the generated Type 3 font maps codes to base characters, so extracted text keeps the base character; the selector itself has no code to carry in that font. Full sequence round-tripping needs a complete embedded font (as the issue's DejaVu workaround shows) — this change makes the automatic path work instead of refusing.

New test: `variation_selectors_take_no_glyph_and_no_advance`.

Fixes #4861

title: Keep the outline intact when move_bookmark gets an invalid target

## What this changes

Found while testing `crates/organize/src/outline.rs:689-712`. There is no existing issue for this.

`move_bookmark` deleted the bookmark when the target parent path was invalid. It unlinked the bookmark from its old parent and relinked that parent before it resolved the target parent path. If the target did not exist, the function returned an error after the bookmark had already been removed from the outline, so it was lost.

title: fix(edit, a11y): `Q` inside a text object restores the text matrices, as the renderer does
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Follow-up offered in #4831, same bug class. Inside a text object, `q`/`Q` save and restore
the text matrix and the text line matrix as well (ISO 32000-2 §9.4.1, referenced from
§8.4.2, as corrected by the PDF Association's erratum, pdf-association/pdf-issues #368).
The renderer already does this: hayro's saved state holds both matrices. Two more
interpreters carried the matrices across `Q` and so disagreed with what is drawn:

- **Text editing** (`crates/edit/src/text/interp.rs`). Text after `Q` was listed at the
  position set inside `q … Q`, and editing it moved it there. The saved stack, including the
  part carried from one content stream to the next, now holds `(Ts, Tm, Tlm)`.
- **Heading detection** (`crates/a11y/src/headings.rs`). A word continued after `Q` was
  split ("Chap ter One"), because its next glyph looked like it started elsewhere. The saved
  stack now holds `(TextState, Tm, Tlm)`; the `MAX_SAVED` cap is unchanged.

Both restore on every `Q`, as the renderer does. The redactor gets the same change in #4831.

  `Td` inside `q … Q`, a `Tm` inside it, and a `Td` inside it followed by `T*`. Each checks the
  line's baseline, then edits the line and checks it hasn't moved.
- `pdfcraft-a11y` `tests::q_inside_a_text_object_restores_the_text_matrices`. Two headings

title: M7: Add text can have a background fill of its own (#4789)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4789.

Text added with **Edit a PDF ▸ Text** can now have a background fill of its own, apart from the text colour.

- **Format text panel:** a **Fill colour** swatch (in the bold/italic row) opens the palette, with **No fill** to take it off. It shows for added text only, not for the paragraphs of the page.
- **File:** the fill is the item's `/Background` parameter and is drawn as a filled rectangle under the text, over the text box. It is read back after save and reopen, so the item stays editable. Items written before this have no fill.
- **Headless:** `page_add_text` and `content_update` take `background` (`#RRGGBB` or a name; `none` removes it); `content_list` reports it. A bad colour is an error and changes nothing.
- **Editor:** while the text is typed or reopened, the editor draws the fill itself (the page's copy of the item is left out of the preview) and picks the caret from it, so white text on a dark fill stays readable.

### Hardening

`/Background` is read as exactly three finite numbers, each possibly an indirect object. A wrong length or a non-number drops the whole colour rather than reading it as another one (a second reviewer found that the first version read `[1 /Bad 0 0]` as red and lost a colour made of indirect numbers). A non-finite colour is refused by the edit.
