title: fix(render): a stroke whose outline comes back with NaN is drawn, not dropped
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4907.

The missing shapes in the report are white-filled outlines with a thin black stroke. The fill
draws; the stroke does not. One subpath of about 950 segments contains a cubic whose three
control points are equal and 0.001 pt from its start:

```
73.763 -0.536 l 73.764 -0.536 73.764 -0.536 73.764 -0.536 c
```

kurbo's stroker (0.13.1, through peniko) treats that curve as degenerate, finds a spurious cusp
at t ≈ 1 from rounding, and joins with a zero tangent, which puts NaN into the stroke outline.
vello_common's `flatten::fill` then drops any path containing NaN ("A path contains NaN,
ignoring it."), so the whole outline disappears, not just the tiny curve. The trigger depends
on the exact coordinates: the same shape a few ulps away strokes fine. kurbo knows this class
of bug (linebender/kurbo#617, #519; the fix in linebender/kurbo#610 is not released).

This adds patch (2) to the vendored `vello_common`: when `flatten::stroke` gets a non-finite
outline back from kurbo, it strokes the path again with every quadratic or cubic whose control
points all lie within the stroke tolerance of its chord replaced by a line to its end point, and
fills that. That replacement is one element out per element in, so the fallback's size is the
path's own. Outlines that come back finite (every path that drew before) take the old path
unchanged; the cost for them is one `is_finite` pass over the outline. A path whose input is
itself non-finite is still dropped, as before. `stroke` and
`StripGenerator::generate_stroked_path` now take a `Clone` path so it can be walked twice;
vello_cpu passes `&BezPath` or a copied slice iterator, and both are `Clone`. The changes carry
`PdfCraft patch:` markers and the `vendor/README.md` row records the patch and its tests.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` (workspace), and default rustfmt on the patched vendored file
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on `pdfcraft-render`, `--all-targets`; on `vendor/vello…

title: M7: arrange added text and images in the drawing order (#3798)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3798 for the content PdfCraft added (the issue's context menu and the page's own images are not covered; see the limits below).

An added text box or image can be moved in the drawing order of the page's added items:

- **Keys, in Edit a PDF with an item selected:** Ctrl/Cmd+Up and Down move it one step over or under the next added item; with Shift, all the way to the front or the back. The item stays selected where it lands, and at either end nothing happens and no history step is made.
- **Headless:** `content_arrange` (`doc`, `page`, `index`, `to`: `front`, `forward`, `backward`, `back`); its result gives the item's new index, and `content_list` follows the new order.
- **Engine:** `Edit::ArrangeContent`, one undo step named for the direction ("Bring to front", "Bring forward", "Send backward", "Send to back"); `pdfcraft_edit::added::arrange_content`.

Every added item is its own content stream and draws from the initial graphics state, so items trade places freely: only the streams the items sit in are rearranged, and whatever else the page's contents hold (the page's own streams, the wrappers around them, other tools' streams) stays where it is. A stream the contents name twice holds two places.

### Limits (also in the parity note)

- Only items PdfCraft added take part. An item cannot be sent behind the page's own content (a watermark under a figure still needs Watermark or Background), and the page's own images are not arranged.
- No context-menu entry yet, only the keys and the tool.
- Several selected items are not moved together.

author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #3900.

E and B swap the Draw tool and the Eraser, as the issue asks:

- **Tap E** (held under 0.35 s) switches to the Eraser and stays.
- **Tap E again, or tap B**, goes back to the Draw tool.
- **Hold E**: the Eraser only while the key is down; letting go gives the Draw tool back.

The keys act only from the Draw tool or the Eraser, so E means nothing to any other tool, and they are plain letters: not with a modifier, and not while a text field, a form field, a dialog or the palette has the keyboard. The quick bar follows every switch: its Draw group shows the tool that is active.

### The edge cases (each has a test)

- The release of E is settled every frame, **even with a dialog open**: a tap stays a tap however long the dialog stays, and a long hold gives Draw back as soon as the key comes up.
- **Choosing a tool while E is held ends the hold**: from the bar, a menu or a command, including choosing the Eraser itself. A late release then takes nothing back.
- **Space's temporary Hand on top of a held E** unwinds to Draw whichever key comes up first.

A second reviewer (Codex) found these in four rounds; all are fixed and tested.

title: M7: per-cluster ActualText and per-glyph ToUnicode for edited shaped lines (#4919)
author: bomu-bomu
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4919. Refs #1384.

After **Edit text** reshapes a left-to-right line (Thai, or Latin with combining marks), the saved line can be selected, found and copied word by word again, as the source line could:

- **One `/ActualText` span per cluster of several glyphs** (`ที่`, `ดิ`, `น้ำ`, `กิ่`, `ผู้`, `ช้`, `q́`) instead of one around the whole line. That's how Chrome writes such text, and PdfCraft's reader already handles it (`crates/render/src/text/device.rs`).
- **Each glyph carries its own character in `/ToUnicode`** where the cluster has as many glyphs as characters. That holds when every glyph is its character's own glyph in the face's cmap, or when the cluster is Thai, whose shaping substitutes mark forms one for one and never reorders them. This replaces the `<cid> <>` entries, so Foxit, which ignores ActualText, no longer pastes blanks.
- **The move to the next cluster stays inside the span.** A mark set back over its letter otherwise leaves a large `TJ` move after the span, which PdfCraft's reader counted as a word space (`ñ̄  Cafe`).
- **Right-to-left runs are unchanged.** They're drawn in visual order and keep one span in typing order.

Code: `crates/fonts/src/source_shaping.rs` (`ShapedGlyph::span`, `ShapedRun::rtl`, `split_clusters`) and the shaped-run writer in `crates/edit/src/text_regions/styled.rs`.

Checked on the edited line `ที่ดิน น้ำ กิ่ ผู้ใช้` (embedded static Sarabun):

| Reader | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| PdfCraft: Find `น้ำ` | whole line, x 40→194 | just the word, x 91→118 |
| PdfCraft: extract | correct | correct |
| Poppler: one word cropped | whole line | only the clusters inside the crop |
| MuPDF, with the ActualText removed | `�` after each cluster | correct |
| macOS Preview (PDFKit): whole line and one word | correct | correct |

title: M7: Thai document font from craft-fonts' Thai manifest (Sarabun)
author: bomu-bomu
body:
## What this changes

Refs #1384 (its first item: an open-licence document font for Thai, Sarabun). It's the PdfCraft side of storytold/craft-fonts#53, which adds Sarabun (OFL-1.1) to craft-fonts in a separate, opt-in `fonts/thai-manifest.txt`.

Thai text written into a PDF by **Add Text** (and `page_add_text`) uses **Sarabun Regular**, a looped Thai face suited to documents (the Thai document-style face), when the craft-fonts checkout has that manifest. Otherwise it falls back to **Noto Sans Thai**, the loopless interface face, which is today's behaviour. The interface keeps Noto Sans Thai.

- `crates/fonts/build.rs` reads `fonts/thai-manifest.txt` into a separate generated static, `CRAFT_DOCUMENT_FONTS`:
  - native builds only, and never on wasm, so the web build doesn't grow;
  - optional even under `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1` when the file is absent. A manifest that exists but is broken fails a required build.
- `document_thai_font()` (`crates/fonts/src/craft.rs`) prefers that manifest's Regular face, then the interface Thai face, then any document Thai face.
- **Document faces are never interface fallbacks.** They're kept out of `CRAFT_FONTS` and every `ui_*` list, and `ui_thai_fonts()` is unchanged.

**Works before craft-fonts#53 merges.** CI and releases pin craft-fonts at `b076417`, which has no Thai manifest. Those builds behave exactly as today (Noto Sans Thai). Release builds switch to Sarabun only when that pin is bumped after craft-fonts#53, in a separate PR.

Also in this PR, as its own commit: my entry in `contributors/people.toml`.

## How you verified it

With the Sarabun checkout (`CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts`, its branch from craft-fonts#53, `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1`), and again against a worktree of the pinned `b076417`:

title: feat(ui-egui): flash destination indicator after following an internal link (#4787)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Closes #4787

When a user clicks an internal link (`GoTo` / `LinkTarget::Page`), PdfCraft now briefly flashes a 2pt black rectangle around the destination region on the target page (blinking 3 times over 1.5 seconds at 0.25s intervals), matching Adobe Acrobat's destination indicator.

- **Destination flash indicator (`DocView::dest_flash`):** Adds `pub dest_flash: Option<(usize, [f32; 4], f64)>` to `DocView` (initialized to `None` in `DocView::new` and cleared in `DocView::document_changed`) to store the target page, normalized displayed-page rectangle `[x0, y0, x1, y1]`, and animation start timestamp when following an internal document link (`LinkTarget::Page(p, dest)`).
- **Destination indicator geometry (`DocView::dest_indicator_rect`):** Computes the normalized `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` indicator rectangle (`0.0..=1.0` of the displayed page, respecting crop box, `/Rotate`, and view rotation via `PageInfo::dest_fraction`) for all `DestView` variants (`Top`, `Fit`, `FitH`, `FitV`, `Xyz`, and `FitR`), including quarter-turn axis swapping for `FitH` and `FitV`.
- **Blinking black border on canvas:** While `view.dest_flash` is active (`0.0..1.5` seconds, blinking 3 times at `0.25` second intervals), paints the target rectangle in screen coordinates with `Stroke::new(2.0, Color32::BLACK)` and schedules repaints via `ui.ctx().request_repaint_after(...)` until the animation completes and resets `view.dest_flash = None`.

title: Reject '+' sign in print page ranges
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## What this changes

Print page ranges no longer accept a leading `+` sign as a page number. Before this change, ranges such as `+3` and `+2-4` were treated as valid pages.

Found while testing `crates/print/src/range.rs:20 (page_of)`. There is no existing issue for this.

**Cause.** `page_of` parsed each range token with `str::parse::<usize>()`, which accepts a leading `+`.

**Fix.** `page_of` now requires every character of a token to be an ASCII digit before parsing. Any other token returns `PrintError::NotAPage`, the same as other non-numeric text. A regression test covers `+3`, `+2-4` and `2-+4`.

title: fix(xfa, create): read a BMP's pixels from after its headers when its offset points into them
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4937.

The BMPs in the report give the pixel data's offset (`bfOffBits`, bytes 10..14) as 0. image
0.25 seeks to that offset as given, so it reads the pixels from the `BM` signature onwards. The
picture is drawn shifted by the header bytes and wrapped around. image's `main` now clamps an
offset that lands between the file header and the end of the info header, but 0 is still taken
as given there.

`pdfcraft_xfa::image::bmp_with_pixel_offset` returns the file unchanged (borrowed, not copied)
unless the declared offset lies inside the headers. In that case it computes where the pixels
start and returns a copy with that offset written in:

- the end of the info header;
- plus 12 or 16 bytes of masks for `BI_BITFIELDS` / `BI_ALPHABITFIELDS` in a 40-byte header;
- plus the colour table (`biClrUsed` entries, or `1 << bpp` for 1-8 bit; 3-byte entries for a
  12-byte core header).

If the computed offset falls past the end of the file, the input is returned unchanged and
image reports the error as it does today. This is what the reporter suggested.

Two places use it: XFA pictures (`size` and `decode`) and `create::embed`. The second is
reached from `create::from_images` and also, through `image_xobject` and the engine's
`embed_image`, from Add Image, Replace Image, image fields and file-backed watermarks and
backgrounds, so all of those get the repair. Because of the `create` call, pdfcraft-create now depends on
pdfcraft-xfa (L4 → L3, which `cargo xtask layers` allows). The other choice was a second copy
of the helper.

author: hikashop-nicolas
body:

A dynamic XFA form whose data has a bare `&` was never laid out. Example: the filled IRCC form IMM 1344 (the `xfa_filled_imm1344e.pdf` sample in the pdf.js test corpus) has `Humanitarian & Compassionate` in its data. title: M12: an XFA form's scripts can call the script objects of their subform
author: hikashop-nicolas
body:
## What this changes

An XFA form can keep named JavaScripts under a subform's `<variables>`: `<script name="LOVUtils" contentType="application/x-javascript">`. Its scripts call them by name (`LOVUtils.check(x)`). The template parser ignored `<variables>`, so every such call failed with `ReferenceError: LOVUtils is not defined`, and with it the form's initialize and calculate scripts. In the pdf.js XFA test corpus the failing names include `LOVUtils`, `validator`, `FormInit`, `myfunctions`, `layoutUtils`, `messages`, `Block` and `ColorFieldsValidation`.

- The parser now reads them (JavaScript only) into `Subform::script_objects`.
- `script_objects_for` returns the JavaScript that defines the ones a script at a given SOM path can see: those of its subform and the subforms above it, an inner object hiding an outer one of the same name. Only the objects the script names, and those they name in turn, are defined, since every script runs in a fresh context.
- Each object becomes `var Name = (function () { …text…; return { fn: fn, v: v, … }; })();`; the names come from reading the object's code without its comments and strings.
- The objects are run by the script engine before the script (`Script::prelude`) and are bounded by `MAX_PRELUDE_BYTES` (2 MiB) and by nesting, not by the size a script may have (256 KiB): they are part of the form, not the script being sized up.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-xfa -p pdfcraft-js -p pdfcraft-engine`

title: fix(optimize): size objects in compressed object streams by their compressed share
author: jonathanwxh-cell
body:
## What this changes

Previously, `audit_space` (`crates/optimize/src/audit.rs`) sized every claimed object via `size(doc, num)` (`pdfcraft_cos::serialize(&obj).len() + 20 + 20`) ? as if each object were written as an uncompressed standalone indirect object with its own `obj`/`endobj` wrapper and 20-byte ASCII cross-reference table entry. When non-stream objects (such as bookmarks, structure tree elements, form fields, annotations, or font dictionaries) were packed into compressed object streams (`/Type /ObjStm`, `XrefEntry::InStream { stream, .. }`), their categories counted much larger than the compressed object stream actually takes on disk, shrinking `DocumentOverhead` (`total - counted`) down to `0` and inflating the total reported byte count beyond `file_len` (the remaining gap noted under `optimize.audit-space`).

Now, unedited objects packed in an unedited compressed object stream share that object stream's compressed payload (`stm.raw.len()`) in proportion to their uncompressed serialized size (`serialized_len(doc, num) + 1`):
- All live members of each object stream (both claimed and unclaimed, such as `/Catalog`, `/Pages`, and `/Page`) contribute to the stream's uncompressed total `total_u`, so unclaimed members leave their proportional share of `stm.raw.len()` in `DocumentOverhead`.
- When some members of an object stream have been freed (`doc.free`) or edited in memory (`count < declared_n`), `total_u` is bounded below by the decoded object stream body length (`decoded.len().saturating_sub(first)`), so dead/superseded member bytes inside the object stream on disk become `DocumentOverhead` rather than inflating the surviving members' shares.
- Edited objects (`doc.is_edited(num)`) and members of edited object streams (`doc.is_edited(stream)`) continue to be sized as standalone objects.
- Category shares within an object stream are apportioned deterministically via cumulative rounding (`(acc * raw_len) / total_u`) in `SpaceCategory::ALL` order so no bytes…

title: Linux: sign with PKCS #11 token identities (p11-kit)
author: Bra1nZ
body:
## What

Signing with keys that live on PKCS #11 tokens — Rutoken, JaCarta and the software tokens Linux deployments actually use — through the same digital-id flow the macOS Keychain and the Windows CNG store already plug into:

- **Discovery**: the p11-kit proxy (`p11-kit-proxy.so`), the system-wide aggregate every major distro configures, with `PDFCRAFT_PKCS11_MODULE` as the escape hatch (colon-separated, like `p11-kit`'s own conventions).
- **`sign::pkcs11::list()`**: every certificate whose token holds a matching private key. Tokens with `CKF_LOGIN_REQUIRED` list their certificates too — the keys hide behind the PIN (`CKA_PRIVATE`), so the pairing is proven at sign time instead.
- **`find_with_pin()`**: signs in before the search and maps the PIN errors a UI can act on (`the PIN is incorrect`, `the token is locked`).
- **Signing**: RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 and ECDSA (raw `r‖s` from the token converted to DER) through `ExternalKey`; GOST keys enumerate but wait for the GOST algorithm work.
- **UI**: a "PKCS #11 token" section in the Sign dialog, the token's label as the display name, a Token PIN field for authenticating tokens. No module → nothing listed, no notice.

The C API is reached through the [`cryptoki`](https://crates.io/crates/cryptoki) wrapper (RustCrypto), so the workspace's `unsafe_code = "forbid"` holds unmodified — same spirit as `rustls-cng` (Windows) and `security-framework` (macOS).

## Testing

- Integration tests (`crates/sign/tests/it/pkcs11.rs`) run against a real module: SoftHSM 2 with an RSA key + certificate imported under `CKA_ID AABB`. They cover list → sign → verify, finding by `pkcs11:` reference and by common name, and refuse unknown references without panicking. title: fix(render): match words hyphenated across line breaks in search (#4950)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## Summary
When words are hyphenated across line breaks in PDF documents (e.g., `docu-` on line 1, `ment` on line 2), searching for `document` previously failed because the character stream preserved the hyphen and inserted an inter-line whitespace gap (`docu- ment`).

This PR addresses #4950 by:
- Detecting hyphen characters (`-`, `\u{00AD}`, `\u{2010}`, `\u{2011}`) connecting words at line breaks when extracting character streams for search.
- Dehyphenating line breaks connecting two alphanumeric words and skipping the inter-line space gap so that searching for `document` matches seamlessly across the line boundary.
- Preserving original glyph ranges and ownership (`first..last`) across line breaks so matching highlights both lines correctly.
- Falling back to non-dehyphenated search if no match is found, ensuring explicit literal searches (e.g., searching for `docu-ment`) continue to work.

Closes #4950

## Test Plan
- Added unit tests in `crates/render/tests/it/search.rs` (`search_matches_words_hyphenated_across_line_breaks`) testing both single multi-char glyphs and single-char glyph streams.
- Ran reference comparison tests `search_matches_reference_for_unicode_gaps_limits_and_word_boundaries`.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes with zero warnings.
- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` (400 unit tests + 44 integration tests) passes cleanly.
- `cargo xtask layers` passes with no violations.

title: fix(forms): renaming a radio button to an existing group's name joins that group
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

Part of #4949: the group name.

Today, renaming a radio button in Properties to a name another radio group already has is
refused as a duplicate. So two buttons placed separately can never become one group. In a PDF,
a radio group is one field whose widgets are its buttons (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.2.4). Two fields
with one button each are two groups, so naming one after the other has to move its buttons
into the other field.

`set_props` now does that when both the renamed field and the field it is named after are radio
groups. In `author/join.rs`:

- the renamed field leaves the form, together with its own value and field-level properties;
  the target group keeps its own;
- each of its buttons is re-parented under the target and appended to the target's `/Kids`;
- a button whose export value (its on-state, the non-`Off` key of `/AP /N`) is already taken in
  the target is renamed to the first free `ChoiceN` in `/N`, `/D` and `/R`. This is the name
  "join the selected group" already gives a new button. Buttons of the joining field that
  shared a value (one repeated on another page) share the new one, so they stay in unison;
- a moved button shows as selected only if its value is the target's current value and one of
  the target's own buttons has it, so the group never ends up with two buttons on;
- a field that is its own widget is handled on both sides. The joining one sheds its field
  keys. A target that is its own only button is first split into a field plus a widget. That
  split is the one `duplicate_field` already did; it is now a shared `split_merged`, and the new
  widget now takes the button's `/A` and its widget triggers in `/AA` (`E X D U Fo Bl PO PC PV
  PI`), while the field keeps `K F V C`.

Refused with an error (the engine keeps the edit only when it succeeds):

- either group lists its export values in `/Opt`, because the button values are indices into it;
- either field has no button;
- the target is locked.

title: M4: interleave the pages of two or more files, like pdftk shuffle (#4922)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4922.

Interleaves ("shuffles") the pages of two or more files, as `pdftk A.pdf B.pdf shuffle` does: page 1 of each file in turn, then page 2 of each, and so on. A file that runs out drops out and the longer ones carry on, so five fronts and five backs of a two-pass duplex scan come out in reading order, and `A1 A2 A3` with `B1` gives `A1 B1 A2 A3`.

- **Combine files tab:** an **Interleave pages** button beside Combine. It uses the list's order. A file is the pages its Pages field and its parts give it, in the order shown (a part whose Pages is cleared is the whole file at that place, several cleared parts are the file once each), so what was chosen in the grid is what is interleaved. It is disabled with a reason when there are fewer than two files or one can't be read.
- **Headless:** `doc_shuffle` takes two or more `paths` (images and text files are made into PDFs first, as Combine does), optional `pages` (each file's pages, in the range's order, so a descending range like `5-1` reverses a back side scanned last page first), `passwords` by position, and `out`/`open` as Combine. Colliding form field names are renamed and reported as `renamed_fields`, as `doc_combine` does.
- **Engine:** `Session::shuffle` and a new `pdfcraft_organize::reorder_pages` (a permutation of the page order, refused before anything changes unless it lists every page once). Each file keeps one bookmark, at its first page. At most 100,000 pages in all.

### How it is built, and why

The first version made one Combine entry per page and was quadratic (two 2,000-page files took 19 s). The files are now combined once, with their ranges, and the pages are moved once into their shuffled places: two 10,000-page files take about half a second. The order is built from a list of the files that still have pages, so the work follows the pages written, not the files times the longest file.

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-orga…

title: fix(cos): read startxref when data follows the final %%EOF
author: tsw2k
body:
## What this changes

A PDF with more than 4 KiB of data after its final `%%EOF` opened as damaged:

```
cross-reference data unreadable (syntax error at byte N: no startxref); rebuilding from object headers
rebuilt cross-reference index from 19 object headers
```

Its own cross-reference table was intact. The reader only looked for `startxref` in the last
4096 bytes, and here it sat about 25 KB before the end. I hit this on a sales proposal produced by
Telerik Reporting 17.0: the web server that served it appended its HTML print-preview page
(`<!DOCTYPE html>…</html>`) after `%%EOF`. qpdf reports the same file as damaged with "startxref
was more than 1024 bytes before end of file"; poppler opens it without a note.

`find_startxref` (`crates/cos/src/document/reader.rs`), now used by both the compact and the
materialized xref readers:

- searches the last 4 KiB first, exactly as before;
- otherwise searches the whole file backwards. The **last** `startxref` still wins, so an earlier,
  superseded revision is never read instead;
- when object headers follow that `startxref` (an update cut short before its cross-reference
  section, or a second file glued on), returns an error, and the table is rebuilt from object
  headers as before. The note now says why: "startxref is N bytes before the end of the file and
  objects follow it". This keeps `reconstruction_takes_the_trailer_from_a_cross_reference_stream`
  and `reconstruction_skips_a_trailer_whose_root_is_not_the_catalog` (#2365) unchanged.

The trailing bytes stay in the file, and an incremental save is appended after them.

Also adds my own entry to `contributors/people.toml` (`[people.tsw2k]`, real and display name
"Ilya Balashov"), committed as me, per `AGENTS.md` (Contributor credits).

title: M7: Remove watermark also removes watermarks other editors marked as artifacts (#4957)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4957 for removal: **Remove watermark** now also removes watermarks that other editors (Acrobat and the rest) wrote as artifacts, not only the ones PdfCraft added. Updating such a watermark and reading its settings back into the dialog are not part of this PR (see the limits).

A watermark written by another editor is page content marked `/Artifact <</Subtype /Watermark /Type /Pagination>> BDC … EMC` (ISO 32000-2 §14.8.2.2), with the properties inline or a name in the page's `/Properties` (the dictionary and its `/Subtype` may be indirect objects; names may use `#` escapes). Removing one cuts exactly those bytes out of the page content; everything else is copied as it was.

- **Edit ▸ Remove watermark** is offered for a document whose only watermark was made by another editor, and it stops being offered once it is removed (undo brings both back). The detection is cached per document revision and reset when content changes; a document over 5,000 pages, or with a page that can't be read, is offered the command without being checked.
- **Headless:** `doc_remove_marks` with `kind: "watermark"` goes through the same edit; its description says so.
- **Engine:** `pdfcraft_edit::remove_foreign_watermarks`, called by `Edit::RemoveMarks { kind: Watermark }` after PdfCraft's own marks, and `foreign_watermarks_present`.

### When a watermark is *not* cut out

Marked content does not save and restore the graphics state, so cutting one out can change how everything after it is drawn. A watermark is cut only when nothing it does can reach what follows:

- every state change inside it (`cm w J j M d ri i gs`, colour operators, `W W*`, `Tc Tw Tz TL Tf Tr Ts TD "`) sits inside its own `q … Q`;
- it does not sit inside, open or close a text object or a path that the content around it owns (cutting a `Tj` moves the text after it; `q … Q` restores neither the text matrix nor the current path);
- its `q`/`Q` balance, and the page's marked-content scopes pair u…

title: fix(forms): editing or sorting a list's items keeps its selected indices on the same items
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

A list box or combo box stores its selection twice: as values in `/V` and as positions in
`/Opt` in `/I` (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.5.4). `set_value` keeps both in step. But `set_props`,
which rewrites `/Opt` when the items are edited (Properties → Options, or `form_set_props
options`) or sorted ("Sort items"), left `/I` as it was. So `/I` pointed at whatever now
sits at the old positions.

Example: `/Opt [A B C]`, `/V [B C]`, `/I [1 2]`, then remove A. `/I` stays `[1 2]`, which now
means C and the new item D. A reader that uses `/I` to tell which items are selected then shows
the wrong ones.

After `/Opt` is rewritten, `set_props` now re-points the field's selection at the new list:

- `/I` lists the new positions of the selected values still offered, sorted and deduplicated.
  It is removed when none of them is offered any more. This is the same rule `set_value` uses.
- For a list box, `/TI` (the first visible row) follows the same `ListRows::top_showing` rule
  `set_value` uses: it stays put while the selected rows are still visible, otherwise it
  scrolls to them, clamped to the last full page. The field's `/TI` is updated, and every
  widget that carries its own scrolls by its own row and size (a widget's `/TI` is read first,
  and one past the end draws no options). `set_value` now scrolls such widgets the same way.

`/V` itself is not touched. A selected value that is no longer an item stays in `/V`, as it
does today.

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-forms -p pdfcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p pdfcraft-forms` and the new `pdfcraft-automation` test

title: fix(forms): clearing a field's default leaves it with none, not its parent field's
author: KenM76
body:
## What this changes

`/DV`, a field's default value, is inheritable (ISO 32000-2 §12.7.4.1). A field under a parent
field takes the parent's `/DV` when it has none of its own.

Clearing a field's default in Properties, or through `form_set_props` with `"default": ""`,
removed the field's own `/DV`. For a field with a parent that has a `/DV`, that brought the
parent's back. Example: `address` has default `Main St` and its kid `address.city` has
default `Elm`. Clearing the city's default left `Main St` as the city's default, so Reset
Form filled the city with `Main St`.

`set_props` now checks whether an ancestor sets `/DV` (new `tree::ancestor_sets`, cycle-safe
and capped like `inherited`). If one does, clearing writes an empty default of the field's own
instead of removing the key: `/Off` for a check box or radio button, and `()` otherwise.
Without such an ancestor the key is removed, as before.

`/V` is inheritable too, and clearing a value had the same shape: a kid field cleared by
`set_value` or Reset Form lost its own `/V` and showed its parent's. When an ancestor sets `/V`,
clearing a text or choice field now writes an empty value of its own (`()`, which reads as no
value). Check boxes and radio buttons already write `/Off`.

title: M10: preserve device JPEG Decode during image export
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

A DeviceGray JPEG with `/Decode [1 0]` can render as gray 191 on the page while Export all images and Save Image As write the original gray-64 JPEG.
These export paths now apply valid per-component Decode intervals for named DeviceGray/DeviceRGB JPEGs and produce PNG when the mapping changes their samples.
Default and identity mappings retain the original JPEG bytes when no other conversion is needed.

The mapping accepts indirect color-space names, arrays and endpoints, preserves supported soft/stencil/color-key masks, compares color keys against raw samples, and applies Matte after color mapping.
Required conversions report corrupt data, inconsistent dimensions/components, excessive pixel counts, explicit ColorTransform overrides and uninspectable DCT parameters instead of silently writing the wrong JPEG.
JPEG dimensions are checked before allocating a decoded raster.

Related #1201 (partial).
This does not close that audit: arbitrary CMYK JPEG Decode, ICC/calibrated color conversion, unsupported codecs and existing 16-bit precision limits remain.
The scope does not duplicate #3023 or #3053, whose JPEG paths still bypass per-component Decode.

## How you verified it

- Reproduced through `pdfcraft-cli run` on current main's engine, using contributor-original Gray/RGB JPEG fixtures, page_render and both export paths.
  Poppler ran only as an external oracle.
  On the exact PR head, both export paths for default/inverted/scaled Gray and inverted RGB (including three-component APP14) match PdfCraft and Poppler center pixels.
  Exported bytes stay identical after save/reopen; the default control stays byte-for-byte JPEG.
- Observed the new `jpeg_decode_inversion_changes_exported_pixels` regression fail before the fix (`jpg` instead of `png`).
- Added 13 create regressions and two automation regressions covering intervals, indirect names/aliases, malformed maps, finite endpoint extremes, alpha/Matte/raw color keys, APP14 RGB, conversion failures, …

title: fix(ui): arrow keys select in the Organize Pages grid, and a click between pages clears the selection (#3436)
author: tylamb1
body:
What this changes
Part of #3436 (the Organize Pages selection items).

title: M9: import certificates to trust from the Signatures panel
author: ffishman
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"ffishman"} -->
_Requested by **Rodrigo**_

## What this changes

Before: a certificate could only be trusted from the app by pressing "Add to trusted certificates" on a signer the open document already showed. Importing a CA certificate or a `.p7b` bundle was possible only through the `sign_trust` automation tool. So a signature whose PDF embeds only the signer's certificate stayed *Unknown*. Many Brazilian (ICP-Brasil) signatures are like this.

After: the Signatures panel has **Import certificates…** next to Validate all.
- It reads `.cer`/`.crt`/`.pem`/`.der` files and `.p7b`/`.p7c` bundles, with the same parser `sign_trust` uses (#3561).
- Several files can be picked at once, because ITI publishes the ICP-Brasil CAs as a ZIP with one `.crt` per authority.
- A dialog lists each certificate once, with its issuer, validity, CA or end entity and full SHA-256 fingerprint, and a note to compare the fingerprint with the one the authority publishes.
- Nothing is trusted until the user confirms. Certificate authorities start ticked and end-entity certificates don't, so confirming a whole bundle never trusts an individual signer by accident. Only the ticked certificates that aren't trusted yet are added, in one revalidation, and certificates already trusted are shown disabled.
- Before anything is read: a path that isn't a regular file (folder, pipe, device), a file over 8 MiB, more than 2000 files, or more than 32 MiB in all is refused. Each read also stops at the per-file limit. One unreadable file refuses the whole import and names that file. Fingerprints are computed once when the list is read.

How: `CertImport` in `tools/sign_ui/panel.rs` holds what was read and what is ticked. `import_dialog` draws the dialog. `PdfCraftApp::trust_certificates` adds a batch and revalidates once, and `trust_certificate` now goes through it. The button is left out of the web build, which has no file to read.

title: M10: preserve unitless image pixel aspect ratios
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #5008.

Create PDF and Add image previously treated unitless PNG pHYs and JPEG JFIF densities as square pixels.

For unitless density pairs, imports now preserve the declared pixel aspect by normalizing the denser axis to 72 dpi and expanding the other axis without resampling.

Proportional density pairs produce the same natural dimensions, and explicit DPI continues to override both axes.

JPEG EXIF correction retains unitless JFIF density and swaps its axes for quarter turns.

The JFIF scanner handles marker-fill bytes, validates segment boundaries, and stops at image data.

Page placement uses canonical PDF real serialization so a small positive dimension is not rounded to zero by fixed three-decimal formatting.
Natural Add image placement also accepts positive finite sub-point boxes and retains precise clipping and image transforms.
Image bounds returned by listing and copying retain their numeric precision for reuse as input.
Zero or non-finite sizes and non-finite composed transforms are refused before writing page content.

For TIFF, ResolutionUnit=1 uses paired positive X/Y rational densities as aspect-only metadata under the same normalization policy.

TIFF ratios below one are preserved; missing, malformed, zero, or zero-denominator pairs fall back to the existing square-pixel behavior.

TIFF inch and centimeter resolutions retain their absolute-size behavior, and explicit DPI remains the override.

Ordinary PNG and JPEG samples remain unchanged; ordinary JPEG bytes remain unchanged.

This policy interprets aspect-only metadata for natural placement and does not claim that it establishes physical size.

PNG viewers may ignore optional pHYs metadata, so this is an import-fidelity improvement rather than a mandatory conformance claim.

The existing JPEG orientation decode limit and separate ICC-profile limitation (#4669) remain.

title: M3: select text across pages (view.text-select)
author: TheSuperStew
body:
## What this changes

Text selection can now run across pages. Until now a selection could only belong to the page it started on: the drag extended it only while the pointer was over that page, and `Selection` held a single page (the #721 test even pinned "the selection stays on its own page (a selection can't span pages yet)").

A reading-order selection now goes from its anchor glyph to a head glyph on any page (`Span::Run` gains `head_page`). It covers the rest of the first page, the pages in between whole, and the last page up to the pointer.

- **Drag** onto another page extends the selection, including with the edge and wheel scrolling of #721/#1670. A quick drag that is already off its page (in the gap or on the next page) when egui reports the drag start now still starts the selection at the press. Before, it started nothing.
- **⇧-click** on another page extends the selection there, keeping its anchor.
- **Copy** puts each page's part on a line of its own, as Select All of the document does. It waits until every page the selection covers has its text read, so it never copies short. Those pages' text layers are queued and kept while the selection lasts.
- **Highlight, underline, strikethrough and Redact** (from the floating bar, from dragging with the tool, or from picking the tool after selecting) put one mark on each page, as a single `Edit::Batch` undo step named like one mark ("Add highlight"). That wording is already in `EDIT_LABELS`, so the catalogues translate it. A batch made only of added annotations refreshes just its pages, as a single added annotation does.
- **Add comment** and **Replace text** each sit on one page, so they are greyed out for a selection across pages.
- **Related fix:** the Redact and area-highlight box now starts only on the page the button went down on. A quick drag from one page's text that was already over the next page used to start a stray box there.

title: M10: Windows prints each page at the driver's resolution, not ~96 dpi
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

On Windows, PdfCraft hands the print-ready PDF to craft-print, which draws it with `Windows.Data.Pdf` into the XPS print API. At the pinned winprint revision (`5f80b9b`) each page was rendered at its size in DIPs, so pictures reached the paper at about **96 dpi**, whatever the source resolution or the driver's quality setting. A large scan fitted to small paper suffers most: an A0 drawing on A3 is about 35 % of its size, and every pixel the renderer drew is visible. That is why:

- "Microsoft Print to PDF" output is as jagged as the paper, so the loss happens before the driver,
- "Print as image" does not help: the sheet it builds goes through the same renderer.

This bumps `craft-print` to storytold/craft-libs#396, which pins winprint to storytold/winprint.rs#7 (upstream ArcticLampyrid/winprint.rs `a4da89b`, `5d49639`). Pages are now rendered at the resolution in the ticket's DEVMODE, and negative `DMRES_*` values are no longer passed as a raster DPI. No pdfcraft code changes. `Cargo.lock` loses winprint's pdfium build dependencies (reqwest, sigstore …), which #7 makes on-demand. It gains `roxmltree 0.21`, which craft-print moved to on its `main`.

Fixes #4941
Also addresses #4446 and #4769, and the cause reported in #3514. Unrelated to #4800, where 1-bit stencils are nearest-sampled in PdfCraft's own renderer.

**Draft until the chain is merged:** winprint.rs#7, then craft-libs#396. After that, re-pin `craft-print` to the merge commit of #396.

title: perf(engine): export page images on worker threads (about 80% less wall time)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## Summary

Export ▸ Image (PNG, JPEG, TIFF) was spent almost entirely in the image encoders, one page after another on one thread. On the benchmark document, drawing all 55 pages at 150 dpi took about 0.34 s, while encoding them took 1.1 s (PNG), 2.0 s (JPEG) and 1.8 s (TIFF). The encoders belong to the `png`, `image` and `tiff` crates and were already tuned (#2425). This PR draws and encodes several pages at once instead, so the same files are written in about a fifth of the time. Every file is byte-identical to before.

## What changed

- `pdfcraft_engine::export::Exporter::images(pages, dpi, format, sink)` exports a list of pages and hands each file to `sink` in page order. Worker threads each get their own `PageRenderer` (the same pattern as `automation::pages::extract_parallel`), using one worker per core minus one, up to 8.
  - Memory stays bounded. A worker draws at most one page ahead of `sink`, and fewer workers run when 1 GiB can't hold that many of the largest page (raster, RGB copy and encoded file).
  - The first page error, or the first error `sink` returns, stops the export and is returned. Every page before it has been handed to `sink` and none after it, as before.
  - A panic while drawing a page becomes that page's error. A panicking `sink` stops the workers instead of leaving them waiting.
  - With one page, one core, or on wasm, it runs the existing per-page loop on the calling thread.
- `Exporter::image` and the workers share one `draw_image` helper, so both paths draw and encode a page the same way.
- Export ▸ Image (`export_ui.rs`) and the `doc_export_images` automation tool now call `images`. Progress still shows "Exporting… n of m", where n is now the number of pages written. In the tool, a write error is still returned as it was, not as a page error.
- `crates/engine/examples/export_bench.rs` is the benchmark.

## Benchmark

```
cargo run --release -p pdfcraft-engine --example export_bench -- FILE [DPI] [png|jpeg|tiff] [RUNS]
```

title: M10: Word, HTML and RTF export mark right-to-left text (#4653, direction half)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Addresses the **direction half** of #4653 (Arabic in PDF conversion). The other half, getting the characters out of the PDF in logical rather than visual order, is the text extraction's and is not changed here (see the limits).

The Word, HTML and RTF exporters had no right-to-left handling at all: an Arabic or Hebrew paragraph came out as left to right, so it was aligned and ordered as if it were English. Now a paragraph, heading, table cell or text box that reads right to left is marked so:

- **Which text:** its first strong character, by its **Unicode bidi class** (R and AL are right to left, L is left to right; digits, punctuation and spaces decide nothing), the same rule as HTML `dir="auto"`. So an LRM mark before Arabic makes it left to right, and the Hebrew maqaf, though it is punctuation, starts a right-to-left text. Across a paragraph's runs, the first strong character of the paragraph decides.
- **Word:** `<w:bidi/>` on the paragraph (after `w:pStyle`, before `w:spacing`, the order the schema requires), including table cells and positioned text boxes; on the runs `<w:rtl/>`, and the complex-script bold, italic and size (`bCs`, `iCs`, `szCs`) on every run.
- **HTML:** `dir="rtl"` on `p`, `h1`–`h6` and `td`. **RTF:** `\rtlpar` on paragraphs and cells.
- **Mixed text in one run** (the common single-run case) is cut into runs so that only text that is right to left for certain is marked `w:rtl`: the strong Arabic or Hebrew characters, the combining marks and joiners attached to them, and the spaces and punctuation strictly between two of them. Latin letters, digits and weak characters, and the punctuation and brackets at the edges, are left in runs **without** `w:rtl`: Word treats every neutral and weak character in a `w:rtl` run as right to left, which would reverse numbers and misplace paired brackets. A mark after skipped neutrals stays pending with them until a real strong character commits it.

New dependency edge: `pdfcraft-export`…

title: M3: a file named with open parameters opens at their destination (#3425)
author: hazeliscoding
body:
## What this changes

Help systems start a PDF reader with open parameters after the file name, such as `manual.pdf#nameddest=Intro` or `manual.pdf#page=12`. PdfCraft read the whole string as the file name and failed with "os error 2" (#3425). A path that names no file, but whose part before a `#` does, now opens that file at the named destination or page:

- at launch,
- when another launch hands the file to the running app, at the place asked for last if it's asked twice before it has opened,
- and in its tab when the file is already open.

`page` (1-based) and `nameddest` are read, plus a bare `#Intro` as a destination name, as browsers' PDF viewers do. Other parameters (`zoom`, `view`, `pagemode`, `search`…) are ignored, and the file still opens. A path that names a file is never split, so a `#` in a real file or folder name still works.

The named destination is looked up in the target's `/Names /Dests` tree or catalog `/Dests` (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.4). In the running app the lookup runs off the UI thread, because a large manual's name tree takes a noticeable moment to read. The same lookup now applies a GoToR link's named destination, in the app and in `link_open`, instead of opening the file at its default view with a warning.

Headlessly, `doc_open` reads the same open parameters, through the parser in `pdfcraft_engine::open_parameters` that the app uses. It reports the destination the way `link_open` does.

Fixes #3425

title: fix(ui): prevent mouse wheel scrolling from triggering kinetic fling jumps (#4917)
author: YusufMntm
body:
## What this changes

Closes #4917.

Prevents discrete mouse wheel scrolling from triggering unexpected kinetic fling momentum and animation jumping:
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas/fling.rs`, restricts fling momentum calculation exclusively to genuine touchpad gestures that began with `TouchPhase::Start` and continuous `MouseWheelUnit::Point` input. Movement without a preceding `TouchPhase::Start` is ignored, and any discrete wheel step (`MouseWheelUnit::Line` / `MouseWheelUnit::Page`) immediately stops and resets gesture tracking.
- In `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, whenever discrete wheel steps occur in a frame (`line_base`, `boost_extra`, `input.line`, or `has_page`), any in-progress fling is halted and its gesture state reset, preventing kinetic drift from compounding with mouse wheel notches. Also resets fling state when resetting coarse viewport state.
- Added headless integration tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/it/canvas.rs` simulating rapid discrete wheel scrolling and active glide interruption.
- Added unit tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas/fling.rs` ensuring discrete wheel notches and unstarted gestures never glide.

title: M10: Recognize text no longer clips the first and last letters of a line
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

Recognize text dropped the first and last letters of many lines on 300 dpi scans: "The" came out as "he", "and" as "an", and closing full stops went missing. On clean synthetic pages that was about 4 % of the words, while Tesseract and PaddleOCR read the same pages without errors.

**Cause.** ocrs grows each detected word box by a fixed 3 pixels before it cuts the line image out for recognition. At 300 dpi that is less than one pixel of its 800 x 600 detection input, so the line images clip the edge letters. Because the margin is fixed in pixels, it gets worse as the resolution rises:

| synthetic pages | 150 dpi | 200 dpi | 300 dpi | 400 dpi |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| word errors before (text A / B) | 0.7 / 1.9 % | 0.8 / 3.1 % | 4.3 / 4.0 % | 8.4 / 6.9 % |
| word errors after | 0.1 / 0.4 % | 0.1 / 0.2 % | 0.05 / 0.2 % | 0.3 / 1.2 % |

**Fix (`pdfcraft-ocr`).**
- After `find_text_lines`, each line is widened by fractions of its median word height: 0.15 above and below every word, and 0.1 before the first and after the last word. Line finding itself is unchanged; widening before line finding merged lines.
- The recognised word boxes are clipped back to the line's original box, so `text_layer` sizes the invisible text exactly as before.
- Boxes lying on their side (up axis horizontal) are handled.

The factors come from a sweep over two texts at 150, 200, 300 and 400 dpi. The neighbouring values (0.12–0.18 across, 0.05–0.15 along) all land at 0.30–0.41 % word errors, so this is a plateau and not a lucky point. Mean over the 8 sets: character errors 0.59 % → 0.06 %, word errors 3.78 % → 0.30 %.

## What this changes

- `store::params` and `store::parse` persist and restore `FontResource` in `/PCAdded` stream dictionaries across saves.
- `format_section` passes available page font sources (`text_editor_fonts`) to `added_text_format` and updates active text style, drafts, and selected added items when picking custom/installed fonts or loading font files.
- `use_files` applies newly loaded fonts (`FilePurpose::TextFont`) to the current text style, active draft, or selected added text item.

title: fix(redact): an image too large to count its pixels is removed, not a panic
author: lowtide-lab
body:
## What this changes

Redaction clears the covered pixels of an image in place when it can decode it (`image::decode_and_clear`). Before decoding, it refuses images over `MAX_PIXELS` with `(w as u64) * (h as u64) > MAX_PIXELS`. `/Width` and `/Height` come straight from the file as `i64`, so two dimensions of 2^32 or more make that product overflow `u64`. In a debug or test build that panics with `attempt to multiply with overflow` at `crates/redact/src/image.rs:64`, reached from `apply` through the content interpreter's `Do` for any image a redaction mark overlaps. Release builds wrap instead, and the `checked_mul` chain further down then refuses the image, so this is a debug-only panic, not a release crash.

The size check now uses `checked_mul`, and an overflowing product counts as too large. The image is then removed whole, which is what release already did. Images within `MAX_PIXELS` are cleared exactly as before.

Found by a static read of the redact crate, then reproduced in a debug build.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-redact -j 2`: 151 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored

With `image.rs` reverted it fails on `main`: `panicked at crates/redact/src/image.rs:64:28: attempt to multiply with overflow`.

body:
## What this changes

When an image is exported (Export Images, Save Image As, Copy Image, and the automation `extract_images` tool), a soft mask or stencil `/Mask` of a different size is scaled to the image with `image::imageops::resize` in `gray_plane` (`crates/create/src/extract.rs`). `resize` scales the height first, into an `Rgba32F` buffer of the mask's width × the image's height, at 16 bytes a pixel. `size` caps the mask and the image at `MAX_PIXELS` each, but not that product. A mask that is wide where its image is tall makes the product huge: a 1 × 1,000,000 image with a 1,000,000 × 1 mask asks for 16 TB, the allocation fails, and the process aborts (`memory allocation of 16000000000000 bytes failed`, SIGABRT). That happens in release builds too, and `catch_unwind` cannot catch it. The PDF needs about 2 MB of samples, less once compressed.

When the mask's width × the image's height is over `MAX_PIXELS`, the mask is now scaled to the image's width first and then to its height. The two buffers are then the mask's own size and the image's own size, both at most `MAX_PIXELS`. Every mask under that bound is scaled exactly as before.

Found by a static read of the create crate, then reproduced in a debug build.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-create -j 2`: 49 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p pdfcraft-create -j 2 --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings
- `cargo fmt -p pdfcraft-create -- --check`: clean

New test `a_soft_mask_shaped_across_its_image_is_scaled_without_a_huge_buffer`: a 1 × 1,000,000 grey image with a 1,000,000 × 1 transparent soft mask, and then with a stencil `/Mask` that hides every sample, exports with 1,000,000 alpha values, all 0. Each case finishes in about 0.2 s.

- On `main` it aborts the test binary: `memory allocation of 16000000000000 bytes failed`, SIGABRT.
- Refusing such a mask (`return None`) instead fails the test, because the export then loses its transparency.

title: fix(render): read a precomposed Latin ligature as its own letters in Find
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4469 (the ligature-matching half of it; the hyphen-at-line-end
half is a separate, independent problem in the same file).

A font's ToUnicode CMap, or the Adobe Glyph List fallback for a glyph
literally named `fi`, can give one glyph the precomposed ligature
scalar (`U+FB00`–`U+FB06`) instead of decomposing it into separate
letters itself — the Adobe Glyph List maps the glyph name `fi` to
`U+FB01` (`crates/fonts/src/encodings.rs:163`), which is correct per
spec for that one glyph. `Find` compared characters one for one, so a
query like `office` never matched a page whose `fi` glyph carries
`U+FB01`, even though the page visibly draws "office".

`crates/render/src/text/search.rs` expands the eight Latin ligature
scalars into their own letters, on both the page's characters and the
query, before the literal match runs. This is the one place `Find`,
the `text_find` automation tool and Search & Redact's word search
(`redact_mark` with `find`/`words`) all go through, so all three are
fixed together.

Out of scope: the hyphen-divided-word half of #4469 (`exam-` / `ple`
across a line break), which the issue's own first comment asks to be
tracked separately from this one.

## How you verified it

- `cargo test -p pdfcraft-render` — 313 unit tests + 4 search
  integration tests, including the existing 2000-case differential
  fuzz test (`search_matches_reference_for_unicode_gaps_limits_and_word_boundaries`)
  that compares `find` against an independent reference implementation
  — unaffected, since its alphabet uses the already-decomposed `"ffi"`
  string, not the precomposed scalar.
- Proved the regression first: reverted the `search.rs` change,

title: M10, #2285: opt-in GPU text recognition (crates/ml)
author: huppiflupp
body:
## What this changes

This adds opt-in GPU text recognition for #2285. Nothing changes unless `PDFCRAFT_OCR_GPU=1` is set.

**This branch builds on #5058** (line padding). Its first commit is that PR; please merge #5058 first. Only the second commit is new here.

- **New `pdfcraft-ml` (L3, the slot `xtask/src/layers.rs` already reserves).** With feature `gpu` (native only) it runs both ocrs models in wgpu compute shaders, read from the same `.onnx` files rten loads:
  - a convolutional graph executor (implicit-GEMM, depthwise and single-channel convolutions, ConvTranspose, pooling, Slice, Concat),
  - the bidirectional GRU in one dispatch per layer for all lines, each line at its own length,
  - the detector's grey/resize/threshold steps on the GPU.

  Without the feature the crate is empty.
- **`pdfcraft-ocr` gets a `gpu` feature.** The desktop app and CLI enable it through `pdfcraft-engine/ocr-gpu`. The GPU is used only if all of these hold:
  - `PDFCRAFT_OCR_GPU=1` is set,
  - the models are ONNX,
  - a **self-check against rten** at load passes: a synthetic page and line, mask and best classes compared.

  Any GPU error sends that call, and every later one, to the CPU. `Ocr::backend()` says where recognition runs and why the GPU is not used.
- **The GPU path keeps the CPU pipeline's steps.** ocrs prepares the image and finds the lines, the lines are padded as in #5058, and ocrs cuts the line images. Only the two model runs move to the GPU, and characters get their boxes from their CTC steps as ocrs places them.

`xtask layers` lists `wgpu*` as a UI crate (L7+). This PR adds a narrow exemption, `GPU_COMPUTE = ["ml"]`: only `ml`, only `wgpu`, compute only (no window or surface). A test pins that `ml` still may not use egui/winit/eframe and that no other crate below L7 may use wgpu.

title: M12: XFA date pictures read a two-digit year with the century split of 30
author: EricKaden
body:
## What this changes

XFA picture clauses read a two-digit year (`YY`) with a century split of 30 by default. The XFA 3.3 specification, chapter 26 (Picture Clause Reference), p. 1171, gives a "century split option ... set by default to 30". PdfCraft split at 50, so `30` to `49` came out 100 years late (`450101` read as 2045-01-01, not 1945-01-01). This came up in review of #4511 and #4522, but the window predates both, so it gets its own PR.

Both XFA picture readers now use the spec's default (`CENTURY_SPLIT = 30`): `00` to `29` are 2000 to 2029, and `30` to `99` are 1930 to 1999.
- `crates/xfa/src/data/dates.rs` `pattern_to_iso`: the datasets reader and writer, scripts' `rawValue` and typed edit-picture alternatives. Because `iso_to_data` only writes a date in a two-digit data picture when it reads back unchanged, that picture now holds 1930 to 2029. 2030 and 1929 stay ISO, where 2050 and 1949 did before.
- `crates/js/src/formcalc/dates.rs` `parse_date`: FormCalc's `Date2Num` and `Parse` with a `YY` picture.

The other two-digit-year readers keep 1950 to 2049, because they follow other specifications:
- `crates/forms/src/af/format.rs` and `crates/js/src/format.rs` (`AFDate_*`, `util.scand`/`printd`) follow the AcroForm JavaScript API, not XFA picture clauses.
- `crates/sign/src/der.rs` reads UTCTime, where RFC 5280 §4.1.2.5.1 fixes 1950 to 2049.

## How you verified it

The local gate (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, `cargo xtask parity`) passes on `pdfcraft-xfa` and `pdfcraft-js`.

New and updated tests, at the boundaries `29`, `30`, `49` and `50`:
- `xfa::tests::a_two_digit_year_splits_its_century_at_30` covers `pattern_to_iso` and `data_to_iso` with `yymmdd`.
- `xfa::tests::a_date_its_data_picture_cant_hold_is_written_as_iso` now pins 1930 to 2029 as written in `yymmdd` and 2030, 1929 and 2050 as kept in ISO. Before, it pinned 2050 and 1949.

title: fix(edit): Office export respects a form XObject's own /BBox clip
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## What this changes

Addresses the Office-export part of #3503, left open by #3628.

A form XObject's `/BBox` clips its content (ISO 32000-2, the form
dictionary's `BBox` entry: "these boundaries shall be used to clip the
form XObject"), and the renderer already honours it. Export to
Word/HTML/PowerPoint/RTF reads a page's text through
`reading_lines`/`reading_blocks` (`crates/edit/src/text/lines.rs`),
which walks form XObjects with no notion of a clip at all, so text a
form's `/BBox` clips away -- never drawn -- was still read and
exported.

`form_call` now also resolves a form's `/BBox`, transformed into page
space by the same matrix it already computes for the form's `ctm`.
`reading_lines` keeps a stack of the active forms' boxes; a text run
whose box falls outside any of them is left out of the page's lines,
the same way a run from a different stream already starts a new line.
Each active box is checked independently rather than intersected,
which is equivalent for deciding whether a run is outside at least one
of them, and avoids reimplementing rectangle intersection.

**Scope.** This is a form's own `/BBox` only -- not an arbitrary
`re W n` page clip, and not a curved or rotated-into-a-quadrilateral
one (the AABB of the transformed box is used, which is exact for an
unrotated/unskewed matrix and otherwise a conservative over-approximation).
That matches the scope #3628 itself drew for the renderer's own
extraction device ("arbitrary curved clips... remain separate"), and
`crates/edit/src/images.rs` already computes a form's bbox this same
way (`form.ctm.bbox(...)`) for image extraction's own clip handling, so
this follows an existing, reviewed pattern rather than introducing a
new one.

**Out of scope**, left for later: `redact`'s own content-stream reader
has an independent interpreter and isn't touched by this; the
extraction/Find path is #3628's.

## How you verified it

- Proved the regression first: a synthetic one-page PDF drawing a form
  `/Fm` with `/…

title: sign: refuse to sign a document certified with no changes allowed
author: Harrison-Booth
body:
Signing a document certified with DocMDP /P 1 (ISO 32000-2 §12.8.2.2, Table 257) used to succeed silently and produce a document that reads as modified. `sign` and `sign_with_timestamp` now refuse it with a clear error; `sign_document` returns it as a failed call and writes no file. P 2, P 3 and approval signatures are unaffected, and document timestamps are untouched.

This is only the signing-side guard. The validation-side fix (a second signature after P 1 reported as a modification) is in storytold/pdfcraft#4576 and #3440 and is not duplicated here.

Tests: sign crate test (fails with the guard removed, checked) and an automation test. Ran locally on Linux: full pdfcraft-sign suite (119 + 24 pass) and the new automation test; cargo fmt --check clean. Not run: clippy, the rest of the automation suite, Windows/macOS, qpdf/veraPDF.

## What this changes

title: fix(render): cap a JPEG 2000 codestream's SIZ size at 2^28 pixels (#5078)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

A JPEG 2000 image is now refused when its codestream's SIZ marker declares more than 2^28 pixels, the same cap `image_size_ok` applies to `/Width` × `/Height`. The check runs in `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/filter/jpx.rs` on the header read at full resolution, before `Image::decode` (which makes the infallible allocation), and fails the same way as other undecodable images. It uses the full-resolution size because a `target_resolution` shrinks the reported `width()`/`height()` but each tile's coefficient buffers are still allocated at full size (review on this PR); the header is then re-read at the target resolution only when one is set. Logged as hayro-syntax patch (29) in `vendor/README.md`.

Fixes #5078

## How you verified it

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [ ] tests pass on the crates I changed

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

- No regression test yet. `vendor/README.md` says so in the patch's Test column, against that file's rule that every patch has one. A minimal codestream whose SIZ declares about 2^31 pixels should make `decode` return `None`.
- `MAX_PIXELS` is a local constant. The shared `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` lives in `hayro`, which hayro-syntax can't depend on.
- rustfmt wasn't run over `jpx.rs`, because it would reformat older blocks in the file. The new lines are already formatted.

title: fix(js): count every bracket in the nesting guard so a regex literal can't hide depth (#5079)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

`refuse()` in `crates/js/src/run.rs` now counts opening brackets `(` `[` `{` everywhere, including inside the strings and comments its scan skips, while closing brackets count only where the scan sees code. Before, a regex such as `/'/` was read as the start of a string, which hid every bracket after it on that line from the depth guard, and boa's unbounded recursive parser then overflowed the script thread's stack on open. Counting closers everywhere too (this PR's first version) let `((((/* )))) */` cancel real nesting, so closers inside comments and strings don't count. The trade-off: a script with more than 64 unbalanced opening brackets inside strings is refused, and the existing `ordinary_nesting_still_runs` test now expects that.

Every path that hands source to boa (AcroForm, XFA, `CheckedCodeFromStrings`) already goes through `refuse()`.

Fixes #5079

## How you verified it

`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean on `pdfcraft-js`, including the review fixes. Tests not run yet; CI runs them.

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] clippy with `-D warnings` on the crates I changed
- [ ] tests pass on the crates I changed

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

- No regression test yet. The issue suggests `/'/` + `(` × N on both the XFA-open and console paths.
- **This blocks the reported reproduction but is not a complete fix.** The guard is a byte scan, not a lexer, so it can't tell a regex from a division. A quote inside a regex can still make a later string's closing brackets look like code: `/'/((((')))) '` repeated per line ends each line at depth 0 for the guard but 4 levels deeper for boa. The same misreading hides the prefix-run (`!~+-`) and conditional (`?`) checks. Closing this needs a real lexer or a depth limit in the parser, which is a follow-up issue.

title: fix(cos): cap the total entries a materialized xref-stream chain merges (#5082)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

`read_xref_chain_materialized` in `crates/cos/src/document/reader.rs` keeps a running total of rows merged across the chain. Past `MAX_XREF_OBJECTS` it returns `CosError::Syntax`, and the open path rebuilds the index from object headers and logs the repair. That's the same escalation as a single section decoding past the cap. Before, the per-section cap and the 10,000-section chain cap multiplied with no overall bound.

It counts rows merged (including rows set aside, which are kept for the whole chain) rather than the map's size, because a chain that relists the same objects costs as much to merge. A section's rows never outnumber what the compact reader counts for it, and the compact reader stops at 2,000,000 rows, so no chain within its limit is refused here.

Fixes #5082

## Anything a reviewer should look at first

- No regression test yet: a chain whose sections are each under the per-section cap but exceed it together.

title: fix(render): bound the objects lopdf's fallback parses from object streams and arrays (#5083)
author: Higgs32584
body:
## What this changes

lopdf's fallback loader (used by `inspect` when the lazy reader fails, and always by `attachment_data`) parsed every object stream eagerly, capping only decoded bytes. A stream of `0 0 0 …` inside the 256 MiB limit built ~120M `Object`s (10+ GB) and aborted. This bounds what it builds:

- **Per top-level object:** at most 4,194,304 objects (`parser::MAX_OBJECT_NODES`, the same as cos's `MAX_NODES`), counting every array element and dictionary value at any depth. One budget is threaded through `array` / `_dictionary` / `_direct_object`. An object is charged once it is built, so failed `alt` branches cost nothing, and an exhausted budget is a nom `Failure`.
- **Per object stream:** at most 1,000,000 index entries (cos's `/N` clamp), and the index list is no longer allocated from the whole block.
- **Per load:** at most 8,388,608 objects across all object streams, in an atomic `NodeBudget` shared by rayon workers. A member reserves up to its own byte length (every object takes at least one byte) and refunds what it doesn't use, so parallel members can't hold the budget between them. Once the budget is spent, the remaining members are skipped with a warning.
- **`convert` in `crates/render/src/structure.rs`:** the depth limit is now 128, one level per array or dictionary, matching cos's parser. Before, it was 100 with two levels per dictionary, so ~51 nested dictionaries alone forced the lopdf fallback.

Logged as lopdf patch (7) in `vendor/README.md`.

Fixes #5083

title: M3: text selected on a page becomes the primary selection on Linux (#4821)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4821.

On Linux and the BSDs, text selected on a page now becomes the **primary selection**, so a middle click in another application pastes it. This is the X11 convention, and Wayland's `primary-selection` protocol carries the same behaviour.

- The text is written once the page selection has held still for a frame, so a drag doesn't write it on every frame. If the frame after a change isn't otherwise drawn, the app asks for a repaint so the selection still settles.
- egui only writes the regular clipboard, so this goes through `arboard` (`LinuxClipboardKind::Primary`). arboard uses the compositor's data-control protocol where it is offered (niri, sway, KDE…) and X11 otherwise, Xwayland included. `wayland-data-control` was already enabled through egui-winit; `crates/ui-egui/Cargo.toml` now declares it explicitly for these targets. `Cargo.lock` is unchanged.
- A `primary-selection` worker thread owns the clipboard. Connecting and setting both make round trips to the compositor or X server, so they never run on a frame. The thread takes the newest pending text from a single replaceable slot, so a stalled display holds at most one string. Owning the clipboard also keeps the selection served on X11.
- The regular clipboard is untouched; Ctrl+C works as before.
- Whole-document Select All (continuous scrolling, #2639) is not read just for this: its pages are read only when copied.
- A document whose security refuses copying (Table 22, bit 5) gives no primary selection, and says nothing about it, because the user only selected text.
- When the selection clears, the last text stays in the primary selection, as on X11. Selecting the same text again takes the primary selection back from whichever application took it in the meantime, even after a one-frame clear.
- On macOS, Windows, Android and the web build, nothing changes.

Not part of this: middle-click paste *into* PdfCraft's own text fields, and selections inside Edit text.

Related to #5081.
A CLI/MCP `page_extract` request with `separate: true` currently creates its output folder before the engine can refuse source extraction.
A protected document opened without assembly permission therefore leaves an empty folder even though no page was exported.

Use the shared atomic writer's existing parent-directory creation after extraction succeeds.
A source refusal now leaves missing output folders absent and preserves source pages and history, including with `delete: true`.
Successful separate exports retain their file naming and per-file atomic writes.
Later extraction or filesystem failures can still leave earlier completed outputs.

## How you verified it

- [x] Actual MCP baseline reproduced the empty folder for both `delete: false` and `delete: true`; owner, assembly-enabled and unprotected controls exported readable PDFs.
- [x] Observed the new regression fail at the missing-directory assertion before changing production code.
- [x] `cargo test --locked -p pdfcraft-automation -j 2`: 316 passed, none ignored, on functional implementation `c0df30f5`.
- [x] The test-only review update adds `delete: true` to the refusal regression; the focused regression, formatting, scoped Clippy and required gates passed again.
  Production code is unchanged from the full-suite and actual-CLI acceptance state.
- [x] Scoped all-target Clippy with `-D warnings`, formatting, layers, assets, parity, native CLI build, and automation/web WASM checks passed on Rust 1.98.1.
- [x] Actual rebuilt CLI acceptance passed 12 cases: missing nested folders on refusal, existing sentinel preservation, successful nested exports and reopened outputs, owner/user controls, invalid selections, root/symlink confinement, and a first-write error with `delete: true`.
  All 149 source hashes, fixture hashes and the CLI hash remained unchanged; MCP exited successfully.

title: M7: a justified row keeps the indent typed at its start (#4487)
author: AdrianTM
body:
## What this changes

Fixes #4487.

When you edit a justified paragraph, spaces typed at the start of a stretched row (any row but the last) are now kept as an indent. Before, they were dropped on save. The row still ends at the margin, reads back with its indent, and survives a second edit.

**Writing a stretched row** (`crates/edit/src/text/rewrite.rs`)
- The leading spaces are drawn at their own width, in the row's text object and under the row's `Tw`. A `TJ` adjustment then takes back the word spacing `Tw` added to them.
- The indent and the words go out as one `TJ` (`one_show`), for example `18.32 Tw [(    ) 6106.67 (Pack my box…)] TJ`. Two things depend on this:
  - The reader only keeps the spaces when they share one text-showing operator with the words. A spaces-only `Tj` before the words is dropped.
  - The row's line keeps the one word spacing it is stretched with. Drawing the indent at `0 Tw` first would make the reopened row read as `0 Tw`. That is approach 2 in the issue, and it ended with `200 Tz` on the next edit.
- The words are stretched over the width less the indent. The row starts at the paragraph's left edge, its first word starts after the indent, and its last word ends at the margin.
- Spaces after a stretched row's last word are still left out, as before.

**Editing it again through the styled path** (`crates/edit/src/text_regions/styled.rs`)
- The spaces a row starts with are measured and drawn without word spacing (`indent_len`, `same_run`, `row_widths`). Before, each one took the source row's stretched `Tw` (about 111 pt here), so the indent alone overflowed the width and the paragraph broke before its first word.
- When a run of the same source and font follows the indent (and neither is shaped), the indent is carried into that run's text object. It is shown there the same way as above (`indent_show`, `plain_show`), so the row still reads back as one line.

title: M13: preserve render warnings in MCP image resources
author: KyleKassen
body:
## What this changes

Refs #4340, limited to MCP page-image resources.

`resources/read` returned a PNG even when the renderer reported an approximate or incomplete picture.
For example, a failed DeviceN tint transform painted its fallback colour without exposing that diagnostic to the resource consumer.
Warned image reads now return the PNG first, followed by same-URI `application/json` text containing the one-based page and warning sentences.
Clean image reads retain their single PNG part.

A private shared renderer keeps the existing tool validation, preview handling and fatal errors in one place.
The existing tool response and public pixel API remain compatible.
This complements #4494 for tool warnings and #4501 for viewer warnings; #4494 explicitly leaves image resources selecting only the PNG.

## How you verified it

- Reproduced through the actual CLI and newline-delimited stdio MCP on official main `20eebc1c`: direct rendering reports a colour fallback, while two reads of the same image resource return only the PNG.
  The clean tint-transform control paints correctly, and both source PDFs remain unchanged.
- Observed two new resource regressions fail on the missing diagnostic while the invalid-request control passed; all three passed after the fix.
- The source-built fixtures check literal red, blue, fallback-black and control-green pixels, repeat reads, unchanged tool output, document state, incremental/full save and reopen, and invalid document/page/DPI/URI errors.

- [x] Rebuilt CLI: 27 stdio MCP requests, including 8 image-resource cases, 5 fatal-error controls and 4 other resource types.

title: M12: an XFA caption beside its field wraps in its reserve (XFA 3.3 p. 645)
author: mtlcl410
body: ## What this changes A field without a fixed height now measures a caption at its left or right in the caption's `reserve`, the width `draw_field` draws it in. Before, it was measured in what the reserve leaves to the widget. A long caption beside a check box then wrapped a word or two per line, and the field grew as tall as a page. XFA 3.3 p. 645 (`caption`, the `reserve` property): "When the caption is placed at the left or right the reserve property specifies the width of the caption region." Fixes #5108 **Real form:** USPTO PTO/AIA/14, Application Data Sheet (https://www.uspto.gov/sites/default/files/documents/aia0014.pdf). - Each of the two opt-out check boxes under "2. Opt-Out of Authorizations…" is 190.5mm wide, with a right-hand caption reserving 174.36mm. Main measures the caption in the remaining ~7mm. - On main, box A sits alone on page 5 and box B on page 6, and the form has 9 pages. - With this change, both boxes sit at the bottom of page 4, and the form has 8 pages, its reference count. **Before** (main, pages 4–6): box A alone on page 5, box B on page 6. **After** (with the fix, pages 4–5): both boxes at the foot of page 4. ## Change - `crates/xfa/src/layout/measure.rs` (`field_height`): a left or right caption with a reserve is measured in `reserve.min(inner_w)` instead of `inner_w - reserve`. A check box caption without a reserve keeps its existing rule (all the width the box leaves). - New test `a_caption_beside_a_check_box_wraps_in_its_reserve`: a 7.5in check box with a 6.5in right-hand caption of two lines. - With the fix, the field after it starts within an inch. - With the fix reverted, the check box takes 253pt and the test fails. ## How I …
